intro.heading: The in-home option, priced honestly, and then the alternative
paragraphs: Jumeirah 1 is one of the older coastal districts of Dubai, running inland from Jumeirah Beach Road through Al Bada'a and Al Hudaiba, with Pearl Jumeira and La Mer on the reclaimed waterfront and City Walk just behind. It is largely villas and low-rise apartments, which is why families here search for an IB home tutor rather than for a tuition centre: the house is the obvious place for a lesson, and a tutor arriving at the gate is the model most parents grew up with.

So this page starts by taking that option seriously rather than dismissing it. In-home one-to-one tutoring across Dubai is quoted in published rate tables at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, against roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor working online. The gap between those two bands is not a quality gap. It is a car. Somebody is driving along Jumeirah Beach Road at 16:30, parking, teaching for sixty minutes and driving back, and the price of that journey is inside your invoice whether it is itemised or not.

What the journey buys is real and worth naming: a familiar room, no technology to fail, a parent who can hear the session from the next room, and a younger child who settles faster with a person present. What it costs is also real. It limits the tutor pool to people willing to make that drive at that hour, which for a Diploma student means the pool is selected for geography rather than for whether anybody in it has taught Chemistry at Higher Level or supervised a History Internal Assessment. That is a poor way to pick a specialist.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, and no sentence on this site will promise a tutor at a UAE address. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For UAE families, lessons are one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, the student's own work on screen and written feedback between sessions. That is a deliberate trade rather than a limitation we are dressing up, and the rest of this page sets out the arithmetic behind it.

The other half of the page is a comparison, because that is the decision a Jumeirah 1 family is actually making. It compares this district with Jumeirah 2, Jumeirah 3, Al Safa, Al Wasl, Umm Suqeim and Pearl Jumeira on the things that genuinely differ, shows why the answer converges anyway, lists the permit categories so you can check any tutor who offers to visit, and sets the provider models side by side on price, replacement policy and what happens when a match does not work.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.programmesIntro: An IB household in Jumeirah 1 may be anywhere in the continuum, and the programme decides what in-home versus online actually changes. These are the programmes families here ask about, with what each one demands of a tutor.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Assessment is mostly timed external examinations with internal assessments marked against subject-specific criteria. This is the programme where the tutor pool question bites hardest, because a Higher Level specialist in a particular subject is a narrow requirement and a driving radius is a blunt filter.
programmes.countryNote: No UAE Ministry of Education equivalency points figure for the IB Diploma is published that this page can cite, so none appears here. The Ministry's British-track rule is sourced and different: five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at grade E or grade 3 or better, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. Check any IB figure on the Ministry's own site.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked one to eight, with a Personal Project in the final year. Support here is usually short and targeted at a criterion rather than weekly and open-ended, which makes the economics of a home visit worse: four sessions of criterion work does not justify setting up a standing drive across the district.
programmes.countryNote: Most MYP provision reachable from Jumeirah 1 sits in Al Safa, Umm Al Sheif and the Al Barsha campuses rather than inside the district itself. That is a fifteen to thirty-five minute afternoon run depending on which road is used, and it is why families here are often comparing a tutor who drives to them with one their child could have reached anyway.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The inquiry-led primary programme, reported descriptively rather than by level. This is the one group where a person in the room has a genuine developmental advantage, and we say so: a seven-year-old is not well served by an hour of video. Our UAE delivery is online across the board, so for the youngest learners a local arrangement may simply suit you better.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai continuum schools run PYP on a separate campus from their secondary provision, so a Jumeirah 1 family can have two children in the same school group with two different commutes. That changes the practical shape of an afternoon more than most tutoring pages acknowledge.

programmes.name: IGCSE inside IB households
programmes.description: Common in Jumeirah 1, where British-curriculum and IB schools sit within a few kilometres of each other and siblings are often split between them. A household can be comparing tutors for a Diploma student and an IGCSE student at once, and a single visiting tutor for both is a logistics saving rather than a teaching one.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. If one child is on Cambridge papers, ask the exams officer for the zone, the syllabus codes and the tier.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.subjectsIntro: The subject is where the in-home versus online argument is settled, because Diploma subjects at Higher Level are narrow requirements. These are the courses Jumeirah 1 families ask for most, with what each one needs from a tutor.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic route, with proof, calculus and a heavy non-calculator component at Standard Level. Higher Level adds a third paper and real depth. Marks are lost to unjustified steps and to exploration write-ups that describe a method rather than developing mathematics. A tutor who has taught the Higher Level version is a genuinely scarce requirement.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route, with the graphic display calculator used throughout. Students choose it expecting an easier course and meet statistical reasoning that punishes imprecision. Higher Level is demanding in its own direction, and some UAE and overseas engineering courses still expect Analysis and Approaches, so the route choice deserves checking early.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The classic Higher Level bottleneck for medicine and engineering applicants. Organic mechanisms, energetics, equilibrium and the data-based questions carry most of the lost marks, and the scientific investigation needs supervision rather than production. One teacher covering Higher Level Chemistry in a small school year is the commonest reason families here look outside the school.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Formula discipline, graph interpretation and the willingness to write units. Higher Level adds depth in fields, induction and quantum physics. Students who reached the Diploma on fluent arithmetic but weak algebra find Physics the subject where that shows first, usually in the second term of DP1 rather than at the end.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume plus precision. The content load is large and the marks turn on command terms: outline, explain, distinguish and evaluate all want different things. Higher Level adds substantial additional topics. Extended response questions reward structured, linked reasoning rather than a list of recalled facts in any order.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation. Most lost marks come from diagrams drawn without labelled axes or shifted curves, and from evaluation that asserts rather than weighs. The internal assessment commentaries are a structured task where the mark scheme is explicit, which makes them highly coachable without any line being crossed.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, the individual oral and the Higher Level essay. The individual oral is the component students in Dubai most often underprepare, because it is spoken and therefore feels less formal. It is marked against criteria like everything else and rewards rehearsed structure.

subjects.name: Arabic and modern languages
subjects.description: Arabic appears in Jumeirah 1 households both as a Diploma language and as a KHDA-mandated school subject, and the two are not the same job. Mandatory Arabic follows prescribed Ministry content, while Diploma Arabic follows the IB's own course. A tutor needs to know which one the family is asking about before quoting anything.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A short exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, both marked against criteria and both unlike anything students have written before. Support here is conceptual coaching and feedback on drafts the student has written. It is also one of the components most often outsourced, which makes stating the boundary worth the sentence.

subjects.name: Extended Essay supervision support
subjects.description: Four thousand words of independent research alongside six subjects. Almost all the avoidable damage happens in the first month, when the research question is set too broadly. A tutor narrows the question, holds the timeline and gives feedback on written drafts. The school supervisor remains the formal supervisor and no part of the essay is produced by anybody else.

sections.heading: What the phrase IB home tutor in Jumeirah 1 actually returns
paragraphs: Type it into a search box and you get three kinds of result. Agencies that will arrange a visit and quote on enquiry. Classified listings from individuals, some of whom name a rate. And platforms that advertise online tuition against the same phrase because they know what parents type. The first two are genuinely offering a tutor who drives to a villa in this district. The third is answering a different question and often not admitting it.

This page is in the third category and says so in the first paragraph. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. We target this phrase because it is the phrase parents use, and the useful thing we can do with it is tell you what the in-home market actually costs, who in it is permitted to charge, and what you would and would not gain by choosing it.

The reason the distinction matters is that the two models fail differently. An in-home arrangement fails when the tutor's schedule changes, when a drive becomes impractical, or when the person who was available turns out not to know the Higher Level course. An online arrangement fails when the technology is treated as the lesson, when nobody marks the written work, or when a provider matches a student to a generalist and calls it a specialist. Knowing which failure you are exposed to lets you ask the right questions up front.

So the question to put to any provider, in either model, is narrow: who specifically will teach my child, what have they taught before at this exact level, and what happens if it is not working after two sessions. A provider who answers those three clearly is worth considering whichever way the lesson is delivered. A provider who answers with a promise about outcomes is telling you something else.

sections.heading: Jumeirah 1 against the next district over
paragraphs: Families here compare districts constantly, usually because somebody at the school gate in Jumeirah 3 has a tutor who drives and somebody in Al Safa does not. The comparison is worth making properly, because some of it is real and some of it is noise. What is real is the school mix, the road you use in the afternoon and the depth of the local teacher population. What is noise is the idea that published tutoring rates vary by Dubai postcode. They do not.

The table below compares the districts in that conversation on the things that actually differ. Read the last column carefully, because it is where the comparison resolves. In every district the local in-home pool is selected by who will drive there at 16:30, and in every district the requirement for a Diploma student is a specific subject at a specific level. Those two facts do not meet, and they fail to meet in the same way in Jumeirah 1, Jumeirah 3, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim alike.

There is one genuine district difference worth knowing. Districts with more schools inside them have slightly deeper local teacher populations, because teachers tend to live near where they work. Jumeirah 2 and Jumeirah 3 hold more schools than Jumeirah 1, so an in-home search there returns more names. That makes the in-home option more available, not more specialised: more names from the same selection criterion is still a selection by distance.

The practical consequence is that a family moving within this strip, from Jumeirah 1 to Umm Suqeim or out to Pearl Jumeira, should not have to change tutor at all. If a move breaks the tutoring arrangement, the arrangement was built on geography. That is the clearest single test of whether a tutoring decision was made on the right basis, and it is worth applying before you commit rather than after you move.

sections.heading: The travel premium, and what the gap between the bands buys
paragraphs: Put the two bands next to each other and the premium is the whole story. In-home one-to-one tutoring across Dubai is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table giving AED 180 to 350 and individual home tutor listings reaching AED 200 to 500, all read in October 2026. A qualified subject tutor working online is published in a band of AED 150 to 300. At the specialist end the online figure rises to AED 200 to 450 and above, with a UK agency operating in the Gulf publishing AED 270 and a named-tutor service publishing AED 650.

Strip the overlap away and the in-home premium for comparable teaching is roughly AED 30 to 200 an hour. That is a car on Jumeirah Beach Road at 16:30, a parking space, and the twenty to forty minutes a tutor cannot sell to anybody else. It is a fair charge for a real cost. What it is not is a payment for better teaching, more marking or a scarcer specialism, and it is sometimes a payment for less of all three, because the pool it draws from was filtered by distance first.

The monthly view makes the decision concrete. Bestimate's estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 for budget support, AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Market packages seen in October 2026 include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Note what that second package is: eight hours a month for roughly twice the price of eight shorter online sessions.

None of these figures is an IB Gram price and this page publishes none; the free trial lesson and the consultation are where our own fees are discussed. Two context points are worth having in mind while you decide. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. And budget online tutoring advertised from AED 33 to 65 an hour exists for a reason: it is a different product, usually homework supervision rather than Higher Level subject teaching, and buying it for a DP2 student in February is the commonest false economy in this market.

sections.heading: Who is actually permitted to charge for private lessons in Dubai
paragraphs: If somebody is going to teach your child, in a villa or anywhere else, it is reasonable to know whether they may legally be paid for it. The UAE answer is specific. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Eligibility is broader than most parents expect and that is the useful part. Teachers registered in government or private schools may hold the permit. So may employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone providing private tutoring without the permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure appears on this page, and a site quoting a specific amount is quoting something that could not be verified.

Two conditions matter for a Jumeirah 1 family in particular. The permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school. So the arrangement some parents quietly want, your child's own teacher privately in the evening, is the one arrangement the rules are written to prevent. Treat that as press-reported for Abu Dhabi and verify the current ADEK document before relying on the exact wording.

The other condition concerns organisations rather than individuals. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is why no individual is KHDA approved, and why the phrase KHDA-approved tutor should make you ask for a document number. IB Gram holds no such permit, because it operates no premises in the UAE.

sections.heading: What actually happens in a home session, and what it means online
paragraphs: The practical texture of a home visit is rarely discussed and it shapes the decision. A tutor arrives at a villa in Jumeirah 1, usually between 16:00 and 18:00. The session happens at a dining table, in a study or in a majlis, with the household audible around it. Younger siblings pass through. Food is offered. A parent is somewhere nearby, intentionally or not. For a primary-aged child all of that is helpful. For a sixteen-year-old working on a Chemistry Higher Level data question, most of it is interruption.

Online sessions have the opposite texture and their own failure modes. The student sits with a laptop, a headset and the work on screen. There is no social overhead and no arrival time, which is why sessions start when they say they will. What goes wrong is less dramatic and more insidious: a camera off, a student half-present, a tutor talking while nobody writes. The fix is structural rather than technological, and it is marking. A session that begins with last week's corrected work and ends with a question set for next week cannot be passively attended.

Safeguarding is worth saying out loud because almost nobody in this market does. For a session in a home with a visiting adult, the sensible arrangement is a room with the door open and another adult in the house, and a parent should feel free to insist on that without apology. For online sessions, the equivalents are a shared household device in a shared room, sessions that are logged, and no private side channels between tutor and student. Any provider should be able to tell you its position on all three in one email.

Data is the other quiet issue. Lead forms on tutoring sites collect information about minors, often including the school, the year group, recent grades and sometimes a photograph. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection sits behind this, and the practical standard a parent should expect is simple: a stated purpose for every field, a privacy link on every page and a way to ask for the record to be deleted. If a form asks for your child's school and grades without saying why, that is a reasonable thing to refuse.

sections.heading: Why the answer does not change street by street
paragraphs: Here is the part of the comparison that resolves it. A Diploma student does not need a tutor. They need a tutor in Chemistry at Higher Level, or in Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or in History with a particular prescribed subject. Those are narrow requirements, and the narrower the requirement the less likely it is to be satisfied inside a driving radius, whichever district the radius is drawn around.

Work the arithmetic through. A school year group of ninety Diploma students might contain twelve taking Higher Level Chemistry, taught by one or two teachers. In the surrounding district, the number of people who have taught that course, are free at 17:00, and are willing to drive to a villa in Jumeirah 1 is a small number and sometimes zero. It is also a small number in Jumeirah 3, in Al Safa and in Umm Suqeim, because the constraint is the subject rather than the street.

Online delivery changes the constraint rather than the price. The pool becomes everybody who teaches that course and can work in a Gulf Standard Time evening slot, which is a different order of magnitude. That is the whole argument, and it is strongest exactly where families are most worried: the scarce Higher Level subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay in an unusual discipline, and the subject a small school year covers thinly.

It is weakest, honestly, at the other end. For a seven-year-old needing reading support, a person in the room is better and we do not pretend otherwise; our UAE delivery is online across the board, so a local arrangement may genuinely suit you better there. For a student who needs supervision rather than teaching, a visiting tutor at the kitchen table is a reasonable product. Those are the cases where the in-home market deserves the sale, and saying so is more useful to you than claiming online is better at everything.

sections.heading: Comparing provider models on the things that go wrong
paragraphs: Price comparisons dominate this market and they are the least useful comparison available, because the published rates overlap heavily. What differs between provider models is what happens when something goes wrong: the tutor leaves, the match is poor, a session is cancelled, the student's subject changes, or the promised specialist turns out to be a generalist. Those are the events that decide whether a year of tutoring was worth the money.

The table below compares the models rather than named brands, which is deliberate. Comparing against named competitors on quality or legality is neither fair nor useful, and competitor rates are quoted here only where they are published, with the month they were read. What the comparison shows is that the models differ most on replacement, verification and transparency rather than on hourly price.

Two columns deserve attention. Replacement policy is the one most families never ask about and most need: if the tutor becomes unavailable in February of DP2, what happens? And rate transparency is a genuine signal. In a researched set of competitor pages for these queries, three of six published no price at all, one published a schema price that contradicted its own visible text, and two quoted US dollars to UAE families. A provider that will not put a number anywhere is making a choice.

The last row is us, described without decoration. Online only in the UAE, one free trial lesson in one subject before any paid block, a stated replacement route if the match is wrong, no published price list on this page and no in-home service anywhere in the Emirates. sections.heading: Where the Diploma hours actually go, and the honesty line
paragraphs: Families who buy IB tutoring by the subject often discover that the hours were needed somewhere else. The Diploma's load is not evenly distributed. Six subjects run in parallel with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, and the internal assessments across those six subjects cluster in the same months of DP2. A student who is fine in lessons and drowning in deadlines needs a different kind of support from one who cannot do the chemistry.

In practice the hours go to four places. Timed examination technique, because Diploma papers reward command-term precision and pace. The internal assessments, which are structured, criterion-marked and therefore highly coachable. The Extended Essay, where almost all the avoidable damage happens in the first month when the research question is set too wide. And Theory of Knowledge, which asks for a genre of writing nobody has previously required and which students often leave until it is urgent.

The honesty line in all four is the same and worth stating because some providers in this market cross it openly. A tutor may teach, set practice, mark written work, explain what a criterion rewards, narrow a research question and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write any part of an internal assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay, and nobody at IB Gram will. One competitor in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price; that is an academic-honesty breach whose consequences fall on the student.

The same applies to materials. Official syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and subject guides belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson, so this page cites and links them rather than hosting them. And IB examination and results dates are not stated anywhere on this page, because the IB's own site could not be verified by automated checking for this project. Confirm every IB date with your child's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org, and treat any page that states them confidently without a source with appropriate caution.

sections.heading: Regulators, equivalency and what a Jumeirah 1 parent should verify
paragraphs: Dubai families often assume the rules they know are national, and they are not. Private schools in Dubai are overseen by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the regulator's role varies by emirate as well as its name.

This matters to a Jumeirah 1 family mainly when they move, which in this city happens often. A family relocating to Abu Dhabi moves from KHDA's framework to ADEK's, with different inspection arrangements and different professional-ethics rules for school staff. The tutoring arrangement does not need to change, but the assumptions about what the school and its teachers may do does. Of the competitor pages researched for these queries, ADEK was named by none at all.

Equivalency is the other thing worth knowing before it is urgent. The Ministry of Education's published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from those five, plus proof of one accredited A Level at grade E or two AS Levels at the same grade. On the American track, English proficiency requires IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Maths. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong.

No IB Diploma points threshold for equivalency appears on this page, because none could be read on the Ministry's own pages, and publishing an unsourced figure across a set of pages this size would be a liability rather than a service. Equivalency is performed by the Ministry and the emirate's attestation authority, not by any tutoring provider, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. Verify your own case through the official channel before planning around anything you read on a tutoring website, including this one.

process.title: Name the subject and the level first
process.description: Not the school, not the postcode. Chemistry at Higher Level, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level, History with its prescribed subject. That single line is what makes a shortlist possible, and it is the line most enquiries leave out in favour of a description of the problem.

process.title: Ask us who specifically will teach
process.description: You should know what your child's tutor has taught at that exact level before any money changes hands, and you should be able to ask about their permit status and get an answer in writing. A provider who will not answer either question is asking you to buy on trust alone.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One trial lesson, one subject, before any paid block is booked. It is a working session: a recent piece of marked work read against the criteria, the two highest-yield fixes named, and a plan for the first month. Then decide, including deciding against us.

process.title: Set the slot from the real arrival time
process.description: Jumeirah Beach Road in the afternoon is slower than the distance suggests, and a session that starts fifteen minutes late every week loses a session a term. Pick the slot from when your child is genuinely at the desk, which for most of this district means after 16:45 on a weekday.

process.title: Mark, correct, re-test
process.description: Written work is annotated between sessions and the next lesson starts from the corrections. That cycle is what moves marks, and it is also what makes an online session impossible to attend passively. Two sessions a week means two cycles, which matters more in a run-up than two extra hours would.

process.title: Say so after two sessions if it is wrong
process.description: A tutor who suits one student will not suit another, and being polite about a poor match costs a term. Tell us after two sessions and we move your child, carrying the diagnostic notes across so the new tutor does not start again from the beginning.

whyPoints.title: The in-home market priced, not dismissed
whyPoints.description: This page publishes what visiting tutors in Dubai actually charge, with sources and the month the figures were read, and names what the travel premium buys. You can weigh the option properly instead of being told online is better and left to guess at the numbers.

whyPoints.title: Permit categories you can check yourself
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition permit, who may hold it, what it costs, how long it lasts and the conditions attached are all set out here. One competitor in this market touches licensing in a single heading. A parent should be able to verify the person teaching their child.

whyPoints.title: A subject at a level, not a tutor nearby
whyPoints.description: Higher Level Chemistry, Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Theory of Knowledge, an Extended Essay in an unusual discipline: these are narrow requirements. Online delivery is what lets the shortlist be built from the requirement rather than from a driving radius around Jumeirah 1.

whyPoints.title: Replacement stated before you need it
whyPoints.description: If the match is wrong, tell us after two sessions and we move your child with the notes carried over. Most families discover their provider's position on this in February of DP2, which is the worst possible moment to find out it does not have one.

whyPoints.title: Safeguarding and data positions in writing
whyPoints.description: Shared device, shared room, logged sessions, no private side channels, and a stated purpose for every field on any form that asks about your child. UAE data protection law sits behind that, and we will answer all of it in an email rather than in a brochure.

whyPoints.title: Plain about the limits
whyPoints.description: We run no office, centre or in-home service anywhere in the UAE, we publish no IB examination dates we cannot source, and we say when a person in the room would serve a young child better. Knowing the limits before you enquire is worth more than a friendly form.

faqs.question: Is in-home IB tutoring in Jumeirah 1 cheaper or dearer than in Jumeirah 3?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rate bands do not vary by district, and nothing in the figures read in October 2026 suggests a Jumeirah 1 address is priced differently from a Jumeirah 3 one. In-home one-to-one is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour across the city, with AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table and individual listings reaching AED 500. What does vary slightly is availability: districts with more schools inside them have more teachers living nearby, so a search in Jumeirah 2 or Jumeirah 3 returns more names than one in Jumeirah 1.

faqs.question: What is the travel premium on a home visit actually paying for?
faqs.answer: A journey. Set the in-home band of AED 180 to 500 an hour against the published online band of AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor and the premium for comparable teaching is roughly AED 30 to 200 an hour. That covers the drive along Beach Road, the parking, and the twenty to forty minutes the tutor cannot sell to anybody else. It is a fair charge for a real cost. It is not a payment for deeper subject knowledge, more marking or a scarcer specialism, and the pool it draws on was filtered by distance before anything else.

faqs.question: Which categories of person are legally allowed to tutor privately in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Anyone holding the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Providing private tutoring without the permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so be wary of any site quoting an amount.

faqs.question: How can I check that a tutor who comes to the house holds a valid permit?
faqs.answer: Ask them directly, and ask for the detail rather than the assurance: which permit, issued by whom, valid until when. The private tuition permit is a MoHRE document, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, and it is free, so there is no cost reason for anybody not to hold one. Also ask whether your child attends the school where the tutor teaches, because the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and Abu Dhabi's ethics rules carry a similar bar for school staff.

faqs.question: Should an adult be in the room while a tutor works with my child?
faqs.answer: For a session in a home with a visiting adult, the sensible arrangement is an open door and another adult in the house, and you should feel entitled to insist on that without explaining yourself. For online sessions, the equivalent safeguards are a shared household device in a shared room, sessions that are logged, and no private side channels between tutor and student outside the platform. Any provider should be able to state its position on all three in one email, and a provider that treats the question as unusual has told you something useful.

faqs.question: What personal information about my child should a tutoring provider be collecting?
faqs.answer: Only what it can justify, with the purpose stated. Tutoring lead forms routinely ask for a child's school, year group, recent grades and sometimes a photograph, and UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection sits behind how that is handled. The standard to expect is a stated purpose for each field, a privacy link on every page and a route to ask for the record to be deleted. A form that asks for your child's school and grades without saying why is one you are entitled to refuse to complete.

faqs.question: Does a tuition centre group class work out better value than a home visit?
faqs.answer: For some purposes, yes. A group class at a centre spreads the cost and suits revision of common content, and centres publish their prices more often than agencies do. It is poor value for a narrow requirement, because a group moves at the pace of the group and a Higher Level student with one specific weakness gets no time on it. Note that a tutoring operation with premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, so a centre is one of the few places where asking for a permit number is straightforward.

faqs.question: We are moving from Jumeirah 1 to Umm Suqeim. Do we need to find a new tutor?
faqs.answer: Only if the tutor was chosen for proximity, which is the point. A move of a few kilometres along the coast changes nothing about your child's subject, level or internal assessment deadlines, so a tutoring arrangement built on the requirement rather than on the driving distance survives it untouched. If a house move breaks the arrangement, the arrangement was built on geography. It is worth applying that test before committing rather than after the removal van arrives.

faqs.question: My child's school offers Chemistry Higher Level with one teacher. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is the single most common reason Jumeirah 1 families look outside the school, and it is not a criticism of the teacher. A year group of ninety Diploma students might contain a dozen taking Higher Level Chemistry, which supports one or two teachers and no redundancy. If that teacher's style does not suit your child, or they are absent for a term, there is no internal alternative. An outside specialist is insurance against a structural single point of failure rather than a verdict on anybody's teaching.

faqs.question: Which Diploma components actually absorb tutoring hours?
faqs.answer: Four, and they are not evenly spread. Timed examination technique, because Diploma papers reward command-term precision and pace rather than knowledge alone. The internal assessments, which are criterion-marked and therefore genuinely coachable. The Extended Essay, where almost all avoidable damage happens in the first month when the research question is set too wide. And Theory of Knowledge, which demands a kind of writing nobody has previously required. A student who is fine in lessons and drowning in deadlines needs these rather than more subject teaching.

faqs.question: How do I compare an agency, a marketplace and a freelance tutor fairly?
faqs.answer: Not on price, because the published bands overlap heavily. Compare them on what happens when something goes wrong: who replaces the tutor if they become unavailable in February, what the position is if the match is poor after two sessions, how a cancelled session is treated, and whether the person who teaches is the person you were shown. Then compare rate transparency, which is a real signal. In a researched set of competitor pages for these queries, three of six published no price at all and two quoted US dollars to UAE families.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor we are matched with is not right for my child?
faqs.answer: Say so after two sessions. A tutor who is excellent for one student is sometimes wrong for another, and being polite about a poor match is the most expensive thing a family can do, because it usually costs a term before anybody admits it. We move your child and carry the diagnostic notes across so the new tutor does not start from the beginning. Ask any provider for its position on this before you commit, because the moment you need it is rarely a calm one.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in each emirate, and why should a parent care?
faqs.answer: Dubai schools fall under KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education covers Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah also approve fees, curricula and assessment methods. It matters when you move, because the rules on what school staff may do privately differ between emirates.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Diploma student in Jumeirah 1 usually start with?
faqs.answer: One, in the subject that is actually limiting the points total rather than the one with the lowest grade. One weekly hour plus marked written work between sessions is enough to establish whether the diagnosis was right, and it leaves room in a week that already contains six subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Two sessions a week is the normal pattern inside the final eight weeks before examinations, because it doubles the number of marking cycles rather than simply adding hours.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two Diploma subjects for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth being careful about. Mathematics and Physics, or Chemistry and Biology, are pairs where one well-qualified tutor can genuinely teach both at Standard Level and often at Higher Level. Pairs that cross the sciences and the humanities almost never work, however confident the offer. Ask which of the two subjects the tutor has actually taught at your child's level, and treat a yes to everything as a reason to ask the question again more precisely.

faqs.question: Is there any advantage left to a tutor who arrives in person?
faqs.answer: Yes, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. For a primary-aged child, a person in the room holds attention better than a screen and there is no technology to fail. For a student who needs supervision rather than teaching, a visiting tutor at the table is a reasonable product. For a household where screen time is already a battle, the social presence is worth something. Our UAE delivery is online across the board, so in those cases a local arrangement may suit you better than we would, and we would rather say it.

intro.heading: What the search is actually asking, and the honest answer to it
paragraphs: A parent typing IB home tutor into a search box in Jumeirah 2 is rarely asking for a specific delivery method. They are asking a harder question: is there anybody within reach who actually understands the course my child is sitting? The honest answer is that it depends entirely on the course, because an IB Diploma student is not a generic student. They are a combination of six subjects at two different levels, plus Theory of Knowledge, an Extended Essay and CAS, and the combination is what has to be matched.

That is why distance is the wrong filter. A Jumeirah 2 villa sits a short drive from the Umm Suqeim schools and a longer one from Al Barsha, so a radius of twenty minutes feels generous. Applied to a Diploma student it is not. A radius selects for people who are willing to drive at six in the evening. It does not select for people who have taught Higher Level Economics, marked a Chemistry investigation against criterion D, or seen what a Paper 1 unseen commentary in English A Language and Literature is marked against.

The second thing the search cannot see is the difference between a subject and a level. Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra homework; it has additional content, longer papers and extended-response questions that reward sustained reasoning. A tutor comfortable at Standard Level may be out of their depth two months into the Higher Level course, and that becomes apparent in February rather than in October. Matching on subject alone produces exactly this failure, and it is the commonest complaint families bring from a previous arrangement.

There is a straightforward structural reason the local pool is thin. Dubai had 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools in 2024-25 offering seventeen curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7. A minority programme produces a minority teaching workforce, and that workforce is concentrated around the schools that run it. Spread that across six subject groups and two levels and the number of people in any one neighbourhood who can teach any one combination is small.

So this page does three things. It sets out, group by group, what a generalist gets wrong in a Diploma subject, so a parent can judge a candidate rather than hope. It gives a verification routine for somebody you have not met: the permit, the qualification, the examiner claim and the reference, with what a straight answer sounds like. And it describes what an in-home arrangement in Jumeirah 2 actually involves, in minutes and dirhams, against the online alternative.

The delivery position is stated plainly up front. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Jumeirah 2 address, or to any address in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons here run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. That is not a limitation dressed as a feature. It is the thing that allows the match to be made on the syllabus, because the pool stops being everybody who will drive to Jumeirah and becomes everybody who teaches the course.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.programmesIntro: The IB runs as a continuum, and which stage a Jumeirah 2 student is at changes what matching means. A Primary Years pupil needs a good teacher; a Diploma student in the second year of three Higher Levels needs a named specialist in a named course. The four stages below are set out with what that difference looks like in practice.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.ageRange: Ages 3-12 · PYP Early Years to Year 6
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry organised around units rather than subjects, with no external examinations and no subject specialism to match. Support at this stage is about literacy, numeracy and the habits of independent work, and a strong primary teacher is a better match than a subject specialist. The exhibition in the final year is the first piece of extended independent work most students meet.
programmes.countryNote: Matching is easy at this stage and families in Jumeirah 2 rarely struggle to find help, which is why the frustration described on this page tends to arrive later. A parent who found a good primary tutor through a neighbour in Jumeirah 2 reasonably expects the same route to work for a Higher Level Diploma subject, and it does not, for reasons that have nothing to do with the neighbour.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, with task-specific clarifications written by the teacher. Matching now needs a tutor who understands criterion marking, because an MYP grade is produced by criteria rather than by a percentage, and a tutor who teaches content well but cannot read a criterion rubric will not move the reported grade.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP students at the Umm Suqeim and Al Barsha continuum schools reach Year 5 with strong investigation skills and uneven content coverage, which is a predictable curriculum seam rather than a failure. It is also the point at which a Jumeirah 2 family starts needing a tutor who knows the programme rather than one who knows the subject.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, one from each of the first five groups plus a sixth, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, all graded 1 to 7. Added to that are Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, with up to three points available from the first two. The maximum is 45. This is the stage where matching becomes a combination problem rather than a subject problem.
programmes.countryNote: Jumeirah 2 Diploma students commute to Raffles World Academy or Emirates International School in the Umm Suqeim cluster, to Jumeirah Baccalaureate School on the next road but one, or inland to Dubai International Academy and Dubai American Academy. Each school runs its own option blocks, so two neighbours in the same street can have combinations that need entirely different tutors.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses taken alongside a career-related study, a reflective project, a personal and professional skills course, service learning and language development. Offered by a small number of schools, and when it is, the Diploma subjects inside it are marked exactly as they are in the full Diploma, so subject matching works the same way.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is run by very few Dubai schools, which makes a student taking it the hardest of all to match locally. It is also the case where naming the exact Diploma courses inside the programme matters most, because those are the components a tutor can genuinely support and the rest is school-supervised.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.subjectsIntro: This is the list a Jumeirah 2 household is actually choosing from, grouped the way the Diploma groups it. The description on each is what a tutor has to understand about the assessment, because that is the difference between a subject graduate and somebody who can move a Diploma grade.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen textual analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, the individual oral, and an additional HL essay. A tutor has to know the assessment criteria and the learner portfolio, because Paper 1 is a timed skill rather than a body of revisable content.

subjects.name: French, Spanish and Arabic B
subjects.description: Productive, receptive and interactive skills, with a written assignment and an individual oral built on a stimulus. The marks turn on range and accuracy under the published descriptors, so a fluent speaker without the criteria is not yet a tutor for it.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, plus three internal assessment commentaries on published news articles. The commentary is where most of the recoverable marks sit, and the diagram conventions are specific and examined.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Business organisation, human resources, finance, marketing and operations, with a research project at Higher Level. The quantitative tools are examined precisely, and students lose marks applying a tool correctly to the wrong kind of decision.

subjects.name: History and Geography
subjects.description: Source-based paper work, essay papers and the historical investigation or fieldwork report. The marks reward argument structure and the handling of sources, both of which are learnable and neither of which is content knowledge.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure 1-3 and Reactivity 1-3, Paper 1 at 36 per cent, Paper 2 at 44, and a 24-mark scientific investigation. The data booklet is supplied in the examination, which changes what has to be memorised and what has to be found fast.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes with Higher Level extensions, the same assessment shape, and a scientific investigation. Uncertainty arithmetic and command-term discipline account for more lost marks here than any content gap does.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, continuity and change. The lightest calculation load of the three sciences and the heaviest demand on precise use of describe, explain and suggest.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Calculus, trigonometry, proof and algebra, with a mathematical exploration. Higher Level is a substantial step and the unstructured questions, where nothing signals which tool is wanted, are where the grade is decided.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led solutions, with the same exploration. A different course rather than an easier one, and the statistics at Higher Level surprises students who chose it to avoid calculus.

subjects.name: Visual Arts and Music
subjects.description: Portfolio, exhibition or performance work assessed against published criteria, with substantial coursework components. These are the hardest subjects to match locally and the ones where a school's own department does most of the work.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Up to three points on the diploma total. Support is process coaching only: framing a knowledge question, narrowing a research question until it can be answered, and reading a draft to ask what the evidence has not yet established.

sections.heading: Why the answer depends on the combination, not the subject
paragraphs: The Diploma is structured as six subjects taken from groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, with grades from 1 to 7, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The subject grades give a maximum of 42 and the core adds up to 3, for the familiar total of 45. A tutor is therefore never matched to a student; they are matched to one cell in that structure, and the cell has two coordinates, subject and level.

This matters because schools build option blocks, and option blocks differ. One Dubai school may run Higher Level Economics against Higher Level Chemistry, so a student cannot take both; another may not. The consequence is that two Diploma students living in the same Jumeirah 2 street can hold combinations with almost nothing in common, and a tutor who was excellent for one neighbour's child may be entirely wrong for the next. Recommendations passed between families fail for this reason far more often than for any failure of the tutor.

The level coordinate is the one that gets lost. Higher Level in most subjects adds content, lengthens the papers and introduces extended-response questions that are marked for sustained reasoning rather than for a single correct statement. Somebody who is genuinely comfortable at Standard Level can teach for two months before the difference shows, and what a parent then sees is not a mismatch but a student who seems to have stopped improving.

What follows from all of this is a practical instruction. Before any arrangement is made, write down the six subjects with their levels, the school, and which component is currently losing marks. Then ask a candidate about that specific component. Asking whether somebody teaches chemistry is nearly useless; asking what criterion D of the scientific investigation actually rewards is close to decisive, and takes about ninety seconds to evaluate.

sections.heading: What a generalist gets wrong, group by group
paragraphs: A subject graduate who has never taught the Diploma does not fail because of weak subject knowledge. They fail in a specific, predictable way: they teach the content and miss the assessment. Each Diploma group has its own version of this, and knowing them turns a vague worry into a question a parent can actually ask.

In group 1 the failure is treating English as literature appreciation. Paper 1 is an unseen commentary marked against criteria that reward analysis of how a text produces its effects, and a tutor who discusses themes without the criteria produces confident essays that score in the middle. In group 2 the failure is fluency: a native speaker without the descriptors will correct a student's French and never mention that the individual oral is marked on interaction as a distinct strand.

Group 3 fails on the internal assessment. The Economics commentaries have specific requirements about article date, diagram use and word limit, and a tutor who has not read them will coach good economics into a piece that loses marks on compliance. In group 4 the failure is the scientific investigation and the data question: a chemist who has never marked against criteria A to D will not spot that a research question cannot be answered with the apparatus available.

Group 5 fails on the exploration and on unstructured questions, where no part (a) tells the student which tool to reach for. Group 6 is the hardest of all to support externally, because portfolio and performance work is assessed against criteria the school's own department interprets. In each case the question to ask is about the assessment artefact, not the content, and the table below is the version we work from.

sections.heading: The third Higher Level is the one that needs the specialist
paragraphs: In almost every Diploma timetable there is one subject the school teaches thinly. It is usually the third Higher Level: the one with the smallest cohort, sometimes taught in a combined class with Standard Level students, occasionally taught by a teacher covering outside their main specialism. This is not a criticism of Dubai schools. It is arithmetic. A school with seven Diploma students taking Higher Level Economics cannot staff it the way it staffs Higher Level Mathematics.

That subject is where tutoring produces the clearest return, and it is also the hardest to match locally, for the same reason it is thinly taught: there are few people nearby who teach it. A parent who approaches the problem by distance will find somebody for the subjects the school already teaches well and nobody for the one that matters. That inversion is the single most useful thing on this page.

Identifying the thin subject is usually easy once a family looks. The signals are consistent: a combined class with another level, a teacher who also teaches a different subject, a cohort small enough to name, no past-paper programme, or a report that is noticeably less specific than the others. Any one of those is worth a question to the school, and the school will generally answer it straightforwardly.

The honest caveat belongs here too. A thinly taught subject is thinly taught everywhere, which means availability is genuinely constrained rather than rhetorically constrained. Where no UAE-based specialist is free in a household's slot, what we offer is an IB specialist teaching the same syllabus from elsewhere, on Gulf Standard Time, and we say so before anything is booked. The alternative, which several providers choose, is to accept the booking and send a generalist, and that costs a term before anybody notices.

sections.heading: What a distance filter actually selects for
paragraphs: It is worth being specific about what a twenty-minute radius around Jumeirah 2 contains and excludes, because the filter feels like it selects for convenience and in fact selects for something else entirely. Inside the radius are the Jumeirah strip, Al Safa, Al Wasl, Umm Suqeim and the edge of Al Sufouh. That is a substantial teaching population, and most of it works in British-curriculum and primary schools, because that is what the strip is made of.

So the people the filter returns are disproportionately excellent IGCSE and A Level teachers, primary specialists, and university students living nearby. The people it excludes are Diploma teachers at the inland campuses, anybody whose evening commute makes a 17:00 start impossible, and every specialist who happens to live in Sharjah or on the far side of the city. For a Diploma combination, the exclusion list is where the matches were.

The second thing a distance filter selects for is willingness rather than ability. A tutor prepared to drive forty minutes each way for a single hour is making an economic choice, and the rate has to carry the unpaid eighty minutes. That is precisely why the Dubai in-home band sits at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 online in published rate tables. The premium is travel, and it buys presence rather than expertise.

None of this argues that in-home tutoring is bad. It argues that distance is a filter applied to the wrong axis. The table below sets out what each available filter actually selects for, which is the practical way to decide which one a family should use. For a Primary Years pupil, proximity is a perfectly reasonable filter. For a third Higher Level in the second Diploma year, it is close to the worst available.

sections.heading: Verifying somebody you have not met
paragraphs: Online delivery means a parent in Jumeirah 2 is making a judgement about a person they will never be in a room with, and that deserves a routine rather than an instinct. Four claims are worth checking, and each has a verifiable version and a vague version. The difference between them is usually audible in the first two minutes.

The permit is the easiest. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation smart app, website or e-services under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Because it is free and fast, there is no good reason for a UAE-based tutor not to hold one. Tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no schedule of amounts has been published.

Qualifications and experience should be stated as specifics: which subject, which level, which syllabus, how many cohorts, which components they have marked. Examiner status deserves particular care. A claim to be a current examiner for the IB, Cambridge or Pearson is a specific factual claim about a current appointment, and it should be evidenced rather than accepted. It also should not be used to imply access to mark schemes, grade boundaries or paper content, because it does not confer that.

Finally, there are two claims nobody can substantiate and which should end a conversation. Any promise of a specific grade or a guaranteed improvement is not a service, it is a sales line, and any accreditation claim involving KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson should be met with a request for the permit or centre number. KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises; that is a real document with a real reference, and a provider who holds one can produce it.

sections.heading: What an in-home arrangement in Jumeirah 2 actually involves
paragraphs: Describing in-home tutoring honestly is more useful than arguing against it, so here is what the arrangement involves for a villa in Jumeirah 2. A tutor driving from Al Barsha arrives between 17:30 and 18:15 depending on Sheikh Zayed Road, parks on the street, and teaches for sixty or ninety minutes. Minimum session lengths are common in this market precisely because a sixty-minute visit is not economic once travel is counted. Published monthly in-home packages in Dubai run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions.

What the family gets is real. Somebody can see the desk, the phone, the lighting and whether the student is actually working between sessions. For a younger child, or for a student with attention difficulties, physical presence genuinely helps, and no amount of video replaces an adult in the room. These are reasons families choose it and they should be respected rather than argued down.

What the family pays, beyond the rate, is the candidate pool. Only people willing to make that drive at that hour are available, which for a third Higher Level in a small-cohort subject is frequently nobody at all. Families then accept a generalist because they are the one who will come, and the mismatch surfaces in February. The travel premium in the published bands is paying for the journey, not for Diploma experience.

IB Gram does not sell in-home tuition anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons for a Jumeirah 2 household are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the student's marked script and a shared whiteboard on screen and the option to rewatch the session. sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: The gap between the in-home and online bands is the most informative number in this market, so start there. Published Dubai rate tables read in October 2026 put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject teacher working online. The premium is somewhere between thirty and seventy per cent depending on where in each band a family lands, and every dirham of it is the journey.

That premium buys three things, and it is worth naming them so a family can decide whether they want them. It buys presence, which matters for younger students. It buys visibility of the working environment. And it buys the removal of a technology dependency, which is a real consideration for a household with unreliable connectivity. What it does not buy is a better teacher, and in a small-cohort subject it actively reduces the chance of getting one.

The rest of the market, for context. Budget online tutoring, typically university students, is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, which is about AED 240 to 600 a month on one weekly session. The IB and IGCSE specialist band runs about AED 200 to 450 and above, with monthly estimates for exam-year specialist support around AED 1,000 to 2,000 and more on two sessions a week. Premium named or examiner-led tutors are advertised at AED 500 to 650 and above. All of these are market figures, not an IB Gram price list.

One piece of context from the regulator is worth knowing while budgeting. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. And on VAT, the only figure any provider can honestly speak to is whether its own quoted price includes it; the general treatment of tuition fees should be checked with the Federal Tax Authority rather than taken from a tutoring page.

sections.heading: Where a tutor's help on Diploma coursework has to stop
paragraphs: Every Diploma student carries assessed work that must be their own: a scientific investigation in each science, a mathematical exploration, internal assessment commentaries in Economics, a historical investigation, an Extended Essay and a Theory of Knowledge essay. Each is supervised by a teacher at the school who confirms the work is the student's. That confirmation is why the boundary around a tutor's help is firm rather than a matter of style.

On the permitted side, a tutor may narrow a research question until it can be answered with the resources available, point out that a chosen variable is not controllable or that a chosen article does not meet the commentary requirements, explain what each criterion rewards and what it does not, teach the underlying content, and read a draft in order to ask questions about it. Questions are the instrument: which claim does your data not support, where is the counter-argument, why is this a correlation rather than a cause.

On the prohibited side, a tutor does not supply the research question as a finished product, process the data, write or rewrite any section, or return a corrected draft repeatedly until it is right. The student makes every change themselves. The research behind these pages found a site in this market selling completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, which is not a cheaper form of tutoring but a route to a candidate losing their diploma under IB academic-honesty rules.

The same principle covers materials. Syllabus guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the property of the IB, Cambridge and Pearson. The right behaviour is to reference them and link to the official source, and to work in sessions from material the student or their school already has legitimate access to. A provider offering to send a library of papers and mark schemes is offering something they are not entitled to distribute, which is worth noticing for what it says about everything else.

sections.heading: Expat turnover: what happens when the local tutor leaves Dubai
paragraphs: There is a risk specific to this market that nobody writes about. Dubai's teaching workforce is mobile. Contracts end in June, families relocate, and a tutor who has worked with a student for a year can be gone by August. For a two-year Diploma that lands in the worst possible place: a student loses continuity between DP1 and DP2, which is exactly the junction where predicted grades and investigation deadlines arrive.

A family that has solved the matching problem locally has usually solved it with one person, and that is a single point of failure. The person was hard to find, is now familiar with the student's weaknesses and their school's scheme of work, and none of that is written down anywhere. When they leave, the search starts again from zero and the new tutor spends four sessions rediscovering what the previous one knew.

The practical defence is a written record rather than a different person. From the first session there should be a short running document: the components losing marks, the diagnosis of why, the topics rebuilt and the evidence they held, the school's deadline dates, and what the student does and does not do independently. It takes a few minutes per session and it means a handover is a handover rather than a restart. A parent is entitled to ask for this and to have a copy.

Platform delivery changes the shape of this risk rather than removing it. Tutors still move on, but a match is made from a pool rather than from a neighbourhood, so a replacement is a scheduling problem instead of a search. Where a replacement cannot be found at the same level in the same slot, the honest thing is to say so and offer the specific alternative available, which is what we do. No provider can promise continuity of a particular person, and any provider who does is promising something outside their control.
