process.title: Write down all six subjects and their levels
process.description: Before approaching anybody, list the six Diploma subjects with Higher or Standard marked against each, the school, and the year group. This single sheet is what makes a match possible, and it is what distinguishes a conversation about your child from a conversation about tutoring in general.

process.title: Name the component that is losing marks
process.description: Not the subject, the component: Paper 1, the investigation, the commentary, the oral. A marked script is the best evidence and a photograph is enough. Families who can name the component get a usable answer in the first call; families who cannot spend the first three sessions finding out.

process.title: A short call to confirm the match is possible
process.description: Twenty minutes to establish the subject, the level, the school's scheme of work and the slot. If no specialist is available at that level in that window, that is said in the call rather than discovered later, and the specific alternative is named.

process.title: A free trial lesson on the student's own work
process.description: One lesson, nothing payable, no card details, built around a question or a draft the student has already been marked on. It shows whether the tutor knows the assessment rather than the subject. If the answer is no, a different tutor is proposed rather than the same one defended.

process.title: A written diagnosis after the trial
process.description: A short note naming the component, the cause of the losses, the first two priorities and the evidence that will show whether they moved. It is deliberately brief so that in four weeks it can be checked against results instead of reinterpreted.

process.title: A running record kept from session one
process.description: A few lines per session: what was taught, what was set, what the marked work showed. It costs minutes and it means that if a tutor leaves Dubai, or a second subject is added, the next person starts from the record rather than from the beginning.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject and level, in writing
whyPoints.description: A Diploma student is a combination, not a subject, and the level is half the match. The named subject and level are confirmed before booking, and if no specialist is free at that level in that slot it is said in the first call rather than discovered in February.

whyPoints.title: The thin subject gets the attention
whyPoints.description: In most Diploma timetables one subject, usually the third Higher Level, is taught in a small or combined class. That is where tutoring produces the clearest return and where local supply is thinnest, so it is the first thing we ask about rather than the last.

whyPoints.title: Verification you can actually perform
whyPoints.description: The permit, the qualification, the examiner claim and the component question are all checkable, and this page sets out what a straight answer sounds like. We would rather a parent interrogate a match than take one on trust, including a match we have proposed.

whyPoints.title: A boundary on assessed work, stated first
whyPoints.description: A tutor coaches the process around an investigation, exploration, commentary or Extended Essay and asks questions about drafts. A tutor does not write, process or correct them to completion. The school supervisor authenticates the work and the candidate carries the risk.

whyPoints.title: Honest about availability
whyPoints.description: Where no UAE-based specialist covers a combination in a household's slot, the alternative offered is an IB specialist teaching the same syllabus from elsewhere on Gulf Standard Time, and it is disclosed before booking. Accepting the booking and sending a generalist costs a term.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what IB Gram is not
whyPoints.description: An independent tutor-matching platform with no accreditation from the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK or the Ministry of Education, no UAE office, no school partnerships, and no in-home service anywhere in the UAE. Each of those is checkable, which is the point.

faqs.question: Is there an IB home tutor actually living in Jumeirah 2?
faqs.answer: Possibly, for some subjects, and that is the wrong question to start from. Jumeirah 2 has no Diploma school inside it, and the teaching population on the Jumeirah strip works largely in British-curriculum and primary schools. So a local search returns excellent IGCSE and A Level teachers and very few people with IB assessment experience. The more useful question is whether anybody at all teaches your child's named subject at their named level on a compatible timetable, which is a question about the whole pool rather than about one district. For a Primary Years pupil, proximity is a reasonable filter. For a third Higher Level, it is close to the worst one available.

faqs.question: Why does my child's subject combination make matching harder?
faqs.answer: Because a tutor is matched to one cell in a structure with two coordinates, subject and level, and schools build option blocks differently. One Dubai school may run Higher Level Economics against Higher Level Chemistry so a student cannot take both; another may not. The result is that two Diploma students in the same Jumeirah 2 street can hold combinations with almost nothing in common. A tutor who was excellent for one neighbour's child may be entirely wrong for the next, and recommendations passed between families fail for this structural reason far more often than because of anything the tutor did.

faqs.question: Which of the six Diploma subjects is hardest to find locally?
faqs.answer: Usually the third Higher Level, and for the same reason the school teaches it thinly: the cohort is small. A Dubai school with seven students taking Higher Level Economics cannot staff it as it staffs Higher Level Mathematics, and the people nearby who teach it are equally few. Group 6 subjects are harder again, because portfolio and performance work is assessed against criteria the school's own department interprets. The practical consequence is an inversion worth remembering: a distance-based search finds help for the subjects that need it least and nobody for the one that needs it most.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two of my child's Higher Levels?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking about specifically, because it halves the scheduling problem. The pairings that genuinely work are the adjacent ones: Physics with Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, Chemistry with Biology, Economics with Business Management. What matters is whether the person has taught both at Higher Level rather than whether they are confident in both subjects. A tutor who teaches one at Higher Level and the other at Standard will be fine for two terms and then will not. Ask the component question about each subject separately before agreeing to a combined arrangement.

faqs.question: What does a generalist tutor get wrong in a Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: The assessment rather than the content. In English they discuss themes without the Paper 1 criteria, producing confident essays that score in the middle. In a language they correct accuracy and never mention that interaction is a separately assessed strand of the individual oral. In Economics they coach good economics into a commentary that loses marks on article date or word limit. In a science they miss what criterion D of the investigation rewards. In each case the content teaching is fine and the marks do not move, which is why a parent sees a student who seems to have stopped improving rather than an obvious mismatch.

faqs.question: How do I check a tutor's qualifications if we have never met?
faqs.answer: Ask for specifics rather than adjectives: which subject, which level, which syllabus version, how many cohorts taught, which components marked. Then ask one assessment question about the component your child is losing marks on, and listen to the shape of the answer. Somebody who names criteria by letter with their mark allocations has taught the course; somebody who describes the subject has not. Ask separately whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free, takes two working days and therefore has no good reason to be absent for a UAE-based tutor.

faqs.question: Should I trust a tutor described as an IB examiner?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a specific factual claim about a current appointment and ask for the board, the component and the session. Examiner experience is genuinely valuable, because somebody who has marked a component knows what the scheme credits. What it does not confer is access to mark schemes before release, grade boundaries or paper content, and any suggestion otherwise should end the conversation. Our own position is that we do not describe a tutor as an examiner unless their current status can be evidenced, because the claim is common in this market and frequently unverifiable.

faqs.question: What does a twenty-minute radius around Jumeirah 2 actually exclude?
faqs.answer: Diploma teachers at the inland Al Barsha and Al Sufouh campuses, anybody whose own evening commute makes a 17:00 start impossible, and every specialist living on the far side of the city or in another emirate. For a Diploma combination, that exclusion list is where most of the real matches were. What the radius includes is a large teaching population working mainly in British-curriculum and primary schools, plus university students living nearby. The filter feels like it selects for convenience and in fact selects for willingness to drive in evening traffic.

faqs.question: What would an in-home arrangement in Jumeirah 2 involve in practice?
faqs.answer: A tutor driving from Al Barsha arrives between 17:30 and 18:15 depending on Sheikh Zayed Road, parks on the street and teaches for sixty or ninety minutes. Minimum session lengths are common in this market because a sixty-minute visit is not economic once travel is counted, and published monthly packages run about AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. What a family gains is presence and sight of the working environment, which genuinely helps younger students. What it costs beyond the rate is the candidate pool, because only drive-willing tutors are available.

faqs.question: Why is the in-home rate in Dubai higher if the teaching is the same?
faqs.answer: Because the rate is carrying the journey. Published Dubai bands read in October 2026 put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject teacher online, and the gap is travel time that nobody can teach during. A tutor crossing the city at six in the evening loses perhaps eighty unpaid minutes around a single hour, and the rate reflects that. The premium buys presence, sight of the desk and independence from a video connection. It does not buy Diploma experience, and in a small-cohort subject it narrows the choice rather than widening it.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to a Jumeirah 2 villa?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not sell in-home tuition anywhere in the UAE, because home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons for a Jumeirah 2 household run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own marked script and a shared whiteboard on screen, and the session available to rewatch before a mock or a deadline. That is the reason a match can be made on the syllabus: the pool is everybody who teaches the course rather than everybody prepared to drive to Jumeirah at six in the evening.

faqs.question: What happens if our tutor leaves Dubai mid-course?
faqs.answer: It is a real risk in this market rather than a hypothetical one, because teaching contracts commonly end in June and families relocate over the summer. For a two-year Diploma the damage lands at the DP1 to DP2 junction, where predicted grades and investigation deadlines arrive together. The defence is a written record rather than a promise about a person: a few lines per session recording the components losing marks, the diagnosis, the topics rebuilt and the evidence they held. With that, a change of tutor is a handover. Without it, the next person spends four sessions rediscovering what the last one knew.

faqs.question: How is a handover between tutors managed?
faqs.answer: From the running record, and the parent should hold a copy. A usable handover note names the six subjects and levels, the school and its scheme of work, the components that were losing marks and why, the topics rebuilt with the evidence that they held, the school's own deadline dates, and what the student does and does not do independently between sessions. A new tutor who reads that starts at session five rather than session one. Asking a provider whether such a record exists is also a reasonable way to judge how organised the arrangement is before committing to a term of it.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with an Internal Assessment or Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Narrow the research question until it can be answered with the resources available, point out that a variable is not controllable or an article does not meet the requirements, explain what each criterion rewards, teach the underlying content, and read a draft in order to ask questions about it. What a tutor must not do is supply the question as a finished product, process the data, write or rewrite any section, or return a corrected draft until it is right. The school supervisor authenticates the work as the student's own, and offers to produce assessed work put the candidate's diploma at risk under IB academic-honesty rules.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with a Jumeirah 2 family need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Anybody providing private tutoring in the UAE does. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. It is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation smart app, website or e-services, under Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day turnaround. Operating without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts has been published.

faqs.question: What time can a session start in a Jumeirah 2 household with two school runs?
faqs.answer: Most Diploma students living in Jumeirah 2 commute to Umm Suqeim, Al Sufouh or Al Barsha and are home between 15:45 and 16:45, with a younger sibling often arriving on a different bus. That makes 16:00 unrealistic, 17:00 workable on good days, and 18:30 the slot that survives a late bus and a second pick-up. Because lessons are online there is no travel attached to either end, so the booked hour is the taught hour. Over two Diploma years, a fixed slot that actually happens every week is worth more than an earlier one that gets rescheduled twice and then lapses.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.closingHeading: Send the six subjects and their levels, and we will tell you honestly
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB tutor from a Jumeirah 2 address, the useful first message is a list: the six subjects with Higher or Standard marked against each, the school, and the component that is currently losing marks. From that it is possible to say whether a specialist is available at that level in your slot, or whether the honest answer is that nobody is, in which case the specific alternative gets named rather than glossed. Take the free trial lesson on your child's own marked work, with nothing payable and no card details, and a short written diagnosis follows before any term is booked. Lessons run online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are offered only in India.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the IB Diploma Programme and the Middle Years Programme to students in Jumeirah 3 and along the Jumeirah coast. Matching is done by subject, level and the point you are at in the year: a DP2 student eight weeks from mocks needs a different session plan from a DP1 student opening an Internal Assessment.

intro.heading: What the next eight weeks have to achieve
paragraphs: Parents in Jumeirah 3 rarely start looking for an IB home tutor in January or in September. The search happens in the weeks after a report, after a mock paper comes back three marks under a predicted grade, or after a DP coordinator uses the phrase "at risk of not meeting the deadline". By then the question is not really about tutoring in the abstract. It is about a fixed calendar: the school's internal deadline for an Internal Assessment draft, the mock window in the new year, and the written papers of the May session, which Dubai Diploma candidates normally sit. Every one of those dates is already set. The only variable left is how the weeks in between are used.

That is how this page is organised. Rather than listing subjects and inviting you to enquire, it counts the IB year backwards from the examination room, so you can see which weeks are load-bearing and which are not. A DP1 student in October has nineteen months and almost no deadline pressure, which is exactly why the Internal Assessment work that gets left until DP2 is the single most common cause of a grade collapsing in the spring. A DP2 student in October has roughly one term before mocks and two before the papers, and in that window the work that moves a grade is narrow and specific: past papers under timing, command-term discipline, and finishing the coursework so that revision is not competing with it.

The phrase you typed matters too. An IB home tutor in Jumeirah 3 is what parents search because that is how home tutoring has worked in this city for twenty years: someone drives along Al Wasl Road or Jumeirah Beach Road, sits at the dining table for ninety minutes, and leaves. That model has real strengths and one structural weakness, which is that the tutor pool shrinks to whoever can reach your address during the school-run window. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; our tutors do not travel to UAE addresses, and that service exists only in India. What a Jumeirah 3 family gets instead is one-to-one online IB tutoring with a subject specialist, chosen because they teach Physics HL or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at the level your child sits, not because they happen to live within a twenty-minute drive of Umm Suqeim.

The practical consequence is scheduling. A tutor crossing Dubai in the 4pm to 6pm window loses between forty and ninety minutes to traffic, and that cost is either paid in the hourly rate or paid in the start time. Market rates published by Dubai providers in 2026 bear this out: online one-to-one sits roughly in the AED 150 to 300 band for a qualified subject tutor, while in-home one-to-one quotes run from about AED 180 to 500 once travel is absorbed. Online removes the drive entirely, which is why a 7:30pm or 8:00pm session on Gulf Standard Time is routine for Jumeirah 3 families with two children at different schools and one car.

What follows is the calendar in detail: the Diploma milestones and who sets each one, an eight-week term plan with the evidence a parent should be able to see at each stage, the Ramadan and school-holiday constraints that reshape a schedule every spring, and the academic-honesty boundary that decides what a tutor may legitimately do with an Internal Assessment or an Extended Essay. Where a figure appears it is attributed to its source and dated, because an unsourced number on a tutoring page is worth nothing to you.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.programmesIntro: Jumeirah 3 children sit in three different IB structures depending on their school and year group, and each one has a different relationship with the calendar. The notes below say what each programme assesses and where the term pressure actually falls for a family living on this stretch of the coast.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations, so nothing in it is driven by an exam session. Assessment is continuous and transdisciplinary, built around units of inquiry and finishing with the Year 6 Exhibition. Tutoring at this stage is about securing the mechanics - number fluency, reading stamina, writing structure in English - that the MYP will later assume are already in place.
programmes.countryNote: For a Jumeirah 3 family the PYP question is usually a transition one, because the local school mix means a child may move from a British primary into an IB Middle Years cohort at Year 7. A term of structured number work before that move costs far less time than repairing it in MYP 3.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, with the Personal Project in MYP 5 and optional eAssessments at the end. The criteria are published and specific, which makes the MYP unusually diagnosable: a child who scores well on Criterion A and badly on Criterion D has a presentation problem, not a knowledge problem.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 5 is the year where a Jumeirah 3 timetable gets crowded, because the Personal Project runs alongside the subject criteria and the mandatory Dubai subjects. Families who book a weekly slot in the autumn term of MYP 5 are usually protecting the Personal Project from the February crush.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth a published share of the final grade, and the written papers for most subjects carry the rest. The Diploma is scored out of 45, with three further points available from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the calendar bites hardest in Dubai. A DP2 student in Jumeirah 3 is carrying coursework deadlines set by the school, mocks in the new year, and papers in the May session. Tutoring that ignores the school's own deadline list simply adds a third workstream to a student already running two.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs at least two DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools rather than the mainstream, and the DP subjects inside it are assessed exactly as they are in the full Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Jumeirah 3 student is on the CP, the DP courses inside it still sit to the same session timetable, so the planning in this page applies unchanged to those components. The reflective project has its own school-set deadline, which is the one most often missed.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.subjectsIntro: Requests from this part of Dubai concentrate on the Group 4 sciences, both mathematics routes and Group 1 English, with Economics and Business Management close behind. The descriptions below name the component where marks are most often lost rather than restating the syllabus heading.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency and proof carry this course. Most lost marks are not conceptual: they come from unjustified steps, dropped working, and answers not given to three significant figures. HL adds Paper 3, an extended problem-solving paper that rewards students who have practised reading an unfamiliar context slowly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use dominate. The calculator is assumed throughout, which means marks go missing when students cannot justify the model they chose or interpret a correlation in context. The HL course adds substantially more statistics and matrix work than families expect.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Definitions and derivations are where the grade is decided. Students who can solve numerical questions often lose Paper 2 marks on explanation questions because they describe what happens rather than why. Uncertainty treatment in the Internal Assessment is a second predictable loss point.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics generate the most tutoring requests on this coast. The recurring problem is partial answers: a mechanism drawn without curly arrows, or an enthalpy calculation missing a sign. HL extends into additional organic and analytical content that cannot be compressed into a revision fortnight.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content masks the real issue, which is command-term precision. Outline, explain, distinguish and evaluate each want a different shape of answer, and a student who writes the same paragraph for all four caps out around a 5. Statistical treatment in the Internal Assessment needs separate attention.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is an unseen guided analysis and Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied works. The Individual Oral is internally assessed and globally moderated. Marks are lost when a student narrates the text instead of analysing how meaning is constructed, and HL adds the written essay on a non-studied body of work.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and real-world application decide the grade. The Internal Assessment is a set of commentaries built on recent news articles, and most mark loss there is procedural: wrong article date, missing diagram, or evaluation that restates the theory rather than weighing it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-based answers reward structure: a student who can deploy an Ansoff matrix or a break-even calculation correctly and then evaluate the limits of the tool scores well. The research project at HL is where time management fails, because data collection is slower than students plan for.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode discipline and algorithmic reasoning are examined more tightly than most students assume, and the Internal Assessment requires a documented solution developed for a real client. Sessions usually split between examination technique and keeping the project on the school's deadline.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: TOK produces an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, which together contribute to the three bonus points alongside the Extended Essay. The essay fails when it becomes an argument about the world rather than an argument about knowledge, and that framing is teachable in a handful of sessions.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.regionsIntro: Jumeirah 3 sits between Al Wasl Road and Jumeirah Beach Road, and the practical difference between it and the communities either side is measured in minutes of school-run traffic rather than in kilometres. The notes below record what that does to a weekday session start.

regions.name: Jumeirah 3
regions.note: Villa plots between Al Wasl Road and the beach, with several school gates inside a ten-minute drive. Pick-up traffic clears later here than inland, so a 5pm start is often optimistic and a 7:30pm online slot holds much more reliably through the term.

regions.name: Jumeirah 2
regions.note: Immediately north-east and almost identical in school access. Families here often run two different drop-offs, which is why a fixed online slot in the evening survives the week better than an afternoon appointment that moves whenever a bus is late.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1
regions.note: Closer to the City Walk and La Mer side of the coast. Evening traffic on Al Wasl Road and Jumeirah Beach Road in the DP2 mock season is the main reason parents here end up abandoning in-home arrangements mid-term.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: South along the same coastal strip, with its own cluster of school gates. A tutor driving between Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah 3 in the afternoon is paying for the distance twice, once in time and once in the quoted rate.

regions.name: Al Safa
regions.note: Inland of Jumeirah 3 and tightly bound to the same school run. Al Safa families often need a slot after a sports fixture or an after-school club, which is why a schedule agreed in September needs one planned revision by mid-term.

regions.name: Al Wasl
regions.note: The corridor between Jumeirah and Al Safa. Short distances here disguise long journey times at 4pm, and a session that depends on a car arriving on time is the first thing to break in a week with a mock examination in it.

regions.name: Al Manara
regions.note: A quieter inland pocket with good access to Sheikh Zayed Road. Students here commonly attend schools in Al Barsha and Al Sufouh, which lengthens the afternoon and pushes realistic tutoring to after 7pm.

regions.name: Pearl Jumeira and La Mer
regions.note: Newer coastal addresses with limited school provision inside the community itself. Nearly every family commutes out of the community for school, so a tutoring slot that does not require a second journey is the only one that survives exam term.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah and Al Safa
schoolClusters.note: The school gates closest to Jumeirah 3 are mostly British-curriculum, which is why many students here meet the IB only at Diploma level after IGCSEs. Students we support attend schools across this cluster; we are an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to any of them.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: The nearest concentration of IB World Schools running the full Diploma sits a short drive inland and south of Jumeirah 3. Diploma students from this coast commonly travel into this cluster each morning, which is what makes their afternoons so short.

schoolClusters.city: Across Dubai, for niche Diploma subjects
schoolClusters.note: Where a subject combination is rare - Higher Level Computer Science with Economics, say - the specialist teaching it may sit outside this part of the city entirely. Online delivery is what makes that irrelevant to a Jumeirah 3 family's schedule.

modes.description: A fixed slot each week with the same tutor, running alongside school teaching rather than duplicating it. This is the format that handles coursework deadlines properly, because the tutor sees the draft at the stage the school sees it and can plan backwards from the internal deadline instead of reacting to it.

sections.heading: What a Jumeirah 3 parent is actually asking in late October
paragraphs: The literal question behind the search is short: can someone experienced in the IB work with my child this term, and how soon. The honest answer for a Jumeirah 3 family is that a specialist can usually be matched within a few working days once the subject, the level and the preferred evening slot are known, and that the first lesson is a free trial with that matched tutor so you can judge the teaching before a schedule is agreed. What a Jumeirah 3 family cannot book through IB Gram is a tutor who drives to the villa, because home visits in the UAE are not a service we sell at all.

That distinction is worth taking seriously rather than treating as a caveat. The reason home tutoring dominated this city for two decades is convenience, not pedagogy, and the price of that convenience is a tutor pool defined by geography. If your child needs Chemistry HL specifically, the question is whether the person teaching it has taught that syllabus to examination, not whether they live within reach of Al Wasl Road at 4:30pm. Dubai's private sector contains 227 schools licensed across 17 curricula, according to figures published by the Dubai Media Office in January 2025, and the Diploma accounts for a small share of that enrolment. The pool of genuine Higher Level specialists in any one subject is therefore thin, and narrowing it by postcode thins it further.

The second half of the question is timing, and that is where the calendar comes in. A family searching in late October is roughly one term from mock examinations and two from the written papers of the May session. That is enough time for a measurable change in a specific component and not enough for a wholesale rebuild of two years of content, which is why the first session is spent deciding what the available weeks will be spent on. The sections that follow set out those weeks explicitly, with the milestones, the people who set them, and the evidence a parent should be able to see at each stage.

sections.heading: The Diploma calendar, counted backwards from the examination room
paragraphs: Almost every piece of Diploma pressure a Jumeirah 3 family feels traces back to a date somebody else controls. Some belong to the school: Internal Assessment titles, draft deadlines, mock windows and the internal cut-offs that let teachers mark and moderate before uploading. Some belong to the IB: the submission windows for internally assessed work and the written examination timetable itself. Confusing the two is the most common planning error we see, because a family that treats a school deadline as soft discovers in April that it was the only deadline that mattered.

The table below lays the Diploma out in that order, from the earliest decision to the last paper. Note what is missing from it: specific dates for the IB session. The IB publishes its own examination schedule and results dates, and the only reliable source for them is the IB or your child's Diploma coordinator. Secondary sites circulate versions of these dates that are sometimes a year out of step, so this page names the session - May, which Dubai cohorts normally sit - and sends you to the coordinator for the precise window. Cambridge and Pearson dates, by contrast, are published openly and are quoted on our IGCSE pages with their sources.

Read the table from the bottom upwards if your child is in DP2 and from the top downwards if they are in DP1. The difference in how the two years should be used is stark. A DP1 student has the luxury of fixing the mechanics - working shown properly, command terms understood, a research question chosen with care - at a point where no deadline is pressing. A DP2 student has to triage, which means choosing two or three components where effort converts into marks and deliberately not spending evenings on the rest.

sections.heading: An eight-week term plan that a parent can actually audit
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the block most Jumeirah 3 families start with, usually because it reaches from a report to a mock or from a mock to a coursework deadline. The value of a fixed block is that it can be audited. An open-ended arrangement that runs for a term without a stated target is how families end up paying for company rather than for teaching, and it is the single most common complaint we hear about previous tutors.

The structure below is what a well-run eight weeks looks like for a DP2 student in one subject. The first fortnight is diagnostic and deliberately slow, because a tutor who starts teaching in lesson one is teaching a guess. Weeks three to six are where content gaps are closed and examination technique is drilled against the published criteria. The last fortnight is almost entirely timed practice, because timing is the skill that collapses first under pressure and the one that recovers fastest with rehearsal.

What matters for a parent is the evidence column. You should not need to take a tutor's word for progress: a marked past paper with a mark breakdown, an error log that shows the same mistake appearing less often, and a session note that names the next target are all checkable without any subject knowledge of your own. Ask for them from the first week. A tutor who cannot produce them after a month is not keeping records, and a block without records cannot be audited at the end of it.

sections.heading: What the Jumeirah 3 school run does to a 4pm session
paragraphs: The hidden variable in every in-home tutoring arrangement on this coast is the car. Jumeirah 3 has school gates within a few minutes in several directions, but many Diploma students travel inland to Al Barsha, Al Sufouh or Umm Suqeim, and the return journey lands squarely in the afternoon peak. A tutor booked for 4:30pm is therefore booked against the least reliable hour of the day for both parties, and the usual outcome is a session that starts twenty minutes late and ends on time because the next appointment is somewhere else.

Online delivery removes the journey from the arithmetic on both sides. That is not a marketing point so much as a scheduling one: a 7:30pm or 8:00pm start becomes possible, the lesson begins when it is supposed to, and a cancelled session can be moved to another evening in the same week rather than written off. For families with two children in different year groups it also means two different specialists can teach on the same evening, which no single visiting tutor can do.

The comparison table sets both options out honestly, including the places where a tutor at the table has a genuine advantage. Younger children who need someone physically turning pages are better served in person, and a student who will not keep a camera on is harder to teach remotely than a parent might assume. The AED figures are market figures published by Dubai providers during 2026 and are quoted as a range, not as our price list; IB Gram's own model starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation rather than a published hourly rate.

sections.heading: Ramadan, winter break and the rest of the UAE year
paragraphs: A tutoring schedule agreed in October will meet at least three predictable disruptions before the May papers, and planning for them in advance is the difference between a block that finishes and one that quietly stops. The winter break removes a fortnight at exactly the point where DP2 students most need consolidation before mocks. The spring break lands close to the final coursework and upload period. Ramadan reshapes the whole working day for several weeks, with school hours shortened and family routines moving later into the evening.

Ramadan is the one that most often derails an in-home arrangement and the one online delivery handles most easily. Sessions can move to a post-Iftar slot, run shorter and more frequently, or pause for a fortnight and resume with a revised plan. None of that requires anyone to drive anywhere at a time when the roads around Jumeirah and Al Wasl are at their least predictable. Families who tell us at the start of a block that Ramadan matters to their schedule get a plan that assumes it rather than a plan that is rescued in the middle.

The holidays themselves are a resource rather than an obstacle for a student who is behind. A fortnight with no school timetable is the only period in the DP2 year when a student can work on one subject for several consecutive days, and an intensive block across a break often achieves more than six weeks of single sessions competing with homework. The reverse is also true: a student who is on track should rest, and a tutor who insists on holiday sessions regardless of where the student stands is selling hours rather than teaching.

sections.heading: The academic-honesty boundary, written out plainly
paragraphs: Internally assessed work carries a published share of the Diploma grade, which is exactly why it attracts services that should be avoided. The research for this project found a competitor selling finished Internal Assessments outright. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller: a malpractice finding can cost the Diploma entirely. No amount of convenience justifies that risk, and any provider offering it is telling you something important about how it treats the rest of its service.

The legitimate boundary is not vague. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each assessment criterion is asking for, discuss whether a research question is answerable in the word limit, help a student plan a method, read the student's own draft and ask questions about it, point out where an argument is unsupported, and teach referencing properly. A tutor may not write, rewrite, draft or edit-to-completion any part of the submitted work, may not supply text for the student to adopt, and may not produce the data. Every piece of writing that reaches the school must be the student's own.

In practice that boundary makes feedback more useful rather than less. A returned draft covered in questions - what does this evidence actually show, which criterion does this paragraph serve, why this method and not the obvious alternative - teaches a student to see their own work the way a moderator will. A draft returned already fixed teaches nothing and leaves the student unable to defend it in a supervision meeting. Our tutors work the first way, and your child's school will recognise the difference immediately.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory Dubai subjects and the timetable they occupy
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. For a parent, KHDA matters in two concrete ways: it inspects schools and publishes the outcome on a six-band scale, and it sets requirements that sit on top of whichever international curriculum a school is licensed to teach. Neither of those things gives a tutoring provider any status with the authority, and a company that describes itself as carrying KHDA approval is describing something it almost certainly does not hold.

The requirement most Diploma families underestimate is the mandatory subject set. KHDA's published guidance requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with those requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. The guidance also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, states that combined classes for both groups are prohibited, and sets instructional time against a 40-minute lesson unit. It further requires that teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects.

The practical effect on a Jumeirah 3 Diploma student is timetable arithmetic. Those lessons occupy periods that would otherwise be free, which compresses the school day and pushes private study later. It also means Arabic is a live subject for a student who may have arrived in the UAE recently, and the KHDA guidance is explicit that different or additional content for the mandatory subjects needs prior permission from the Ministry of Education - so any tutoring in those subjects has to work within the school's own scheme rather than a parallel syllabus of its own.

sections.heading: If you are six weeks out, and if nobody is free
paragraphs: Families sometimes arrive at this page with six weeks until a mock or a paper, which prompts the honest version of the question: is it too late. It is not too late to change a grade boundary outcome in one or two components, and it is too late to rebuild two years of content. In six weeks a student can learn to read a structured question properly, show working that earns method marks, finish papers inside the time, and secure two or three topics that have never been solid. That is a realistic and often decisive list. Anything presented as more than that, from any provider, should be treated with real scepticism.

The second honest answer concerns availability. Specialist Higher Level cover in a narrow subject is not infinite, and there are weeks in the year - the fortnight before mocks, the run-up to the May session - when the right tutor for a particular subject and level has no slot left. When that happens we say so and offer the alternatives: a different evening with the same specialist, a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same syllabus on Gulf Standard Time, or a later start date with the work resequenced. What we will not do is put a generalist in front of a Higher Level student and let the family find out in week three.

Starting is deliberately low-commitment for exactly this reason. Tell us the subject, the level, the year group and the evenings that work; we match a specialist and run a free trial lesson with that tutor; you decide afterwards whether to book a block. If the match is wrong, say so and we will change the tutor rather than ask you to persist with it. Six weeks is short enough that a bad match cannot be allowed to consume two of them.

process.title: Review against the calendar, not the clock
process.description: At the end of the block you get a summary of what changed, measured against the deadline it was aimed at. If the next milestone needs different work - coursework rather than papers, or timing rather than content - the plan changes accordingly rather than repeating itself.

whyPoints.description: Sessions are sequenced against your school's deadline list and the session your child is entered for, so coursework support happens while a draft can still change and timed practice happens when timing is the binding constraint. faqs.question: My child is in DP2 with mocks eight weeks away - is it too late to start tutoring in Jumeirah 3?
faqs.answer: No, but the target has to be narrow. In eight weeks a DP2 student can realistically fix examination timing, learn to show working that earns method marks, rehearse command-term responses, and secure two or three topics that have never been solid. That is often enough to change the outcome of a mock and to make the spring term usable. What eight weeks cannot do is rebuild two years of content, and any provider suggesting otherwise is selling hours. The first session is diagnostic: a paper sat cold, marked, and used to choose what the remaining weeks actually spend their time on.

faqs.question: Which IB session do Dubai schools enter, and would the November series ever apply to my child?
faqs.answer: Dubai Diploma cohorts normally sit the May session, which is why school calendars here build mocks into January and February. A November series does exist in the IB's schedule, but for a UAE student it is unusual as a first sitting and typically arises for a retake or for a student who has moved between hemispheres. The precise examination and results dates for either session should come from the IB or from your school's Diploma coordinator. Third-party sites publish versions of those dates that are sometimes a year out of step, which is why this page names the session rather than printing a window.

faqs.question: When should a DP1 student in Jumeirah 3 actually begin work on an Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families expect, and the reason is structural rather than motivational. Internal Assessment titles are usually agreed in the spring of DP1 or the first weeks of DP2, and the work that follows needs a research question narrow enough to answer inside the word limit. A question that is too broad is the most common cause of a weak coursework mark, and it is diagnosable in a single session before any writing starts. Students who settle the question in DP1 spend DP2 revising; students who leave it find coursework and revision competing in the same weeks.

faqs.question: During Ramadan, does the weekly Diploma slot move later in the evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the places where online delivery is simply easier to manage. School hours shorten during Ramadan and family routines move later, so a schedule built for a 5pm start stops working almost immediately. Sessions can shift to a post-Iftar slot, run shorter and more often, or pause for a fortnight and resume on a revised plan. Tell us at the start of a block that Ramadan matters to your timetable and the plan will assume it rather than being patched halfway through. No part of the arrangement depends on anyone driving anywhere at a difficult hour.

faqs.question: How late can a weekday session realistically start for a family on this stretch of the coast?
faqs.answer: Most Jumeirah 3 families settle on 7:30pm or 8:00pm on Gulf Standard Time, and that choice is driven by the school run rather than by preference. Diploma students here often travel inland to Al Barsha or Al Sufouh, so the return journey lands in the afternoon peak and an earlier appointment starts late more often than it starts on time. An evening slot begins when it is supposed to, finishes at a predictable hour, and leaves the homework window intact. For younger MYP students a 5pm or 6pm slot usually works better.

faqs.question: What happens to our schedule across the Dubai winter and spring breaks?
faqs.answer: It depends on where the student stands. For a DP2 student who is behind, a break is the only period in the year when several consecutive days can go to one subject, and an intensive block across it often achieves more than six weeks of single sessions competing with homework. For a student on track, rest is the better use of the fortnight and we will say so. The spring break matters more than the winter one, because it sits close to the final coursework and upload period, so plans around it are made with the school's internal deadlines in front of us.

faqs.question: How quickly can a specialist be matched once we have chosen a subject?
faqs.answer: For mainstream Diploma subjects, usually within a few working days of knowing the subject, the level, the year group and the evenings that work. Narrow Higher Level combinations take longer, and the fortnight before mocks and the weeks before the May session are the tightest periods in the year. If the right specialist has no slot, we tell you rather than filling the gap with a generalist, and we offer the alternatives: a different evening with the same tutor, a specialist based outside the UAE teaching the same syllabus on Gulf Standard Time, or a later start with the work resequenced.

faqs.question: Can we pause lessons during the examination weeks themselves?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most students that is the right call. Once the papers begin, the useful work is rest, light recall and paper-specific timing rather than new teaching, and some families keep a single short session a week purely to walk through the next paper's structure. Others stop entirely. Because sessions are booked as blocks with a stated target rather than as an open-ended subscription, pausing is a scheduling conversation rather than a contractual one. What we would discourage is introducing a new tutor or a new topic in the final fortnight, which adds load at the point where load is the problem.

faqs.question: What does the free trial lesson actually involve before we commit to anything?
faqs.answer: It is one lesson with the tutor we have matched to your child's subject and level, taught on a real topic rather than spent on introductions, so you can hear how they explain something and your child can judge whether the pace suits them. Nothing is booked beforehand and no schedule is agreed until after it. If the match is wrong, tell us and we will change the tutor rather than asking you to persist. The point of the trial is to move the risk of a bad match off your family and onto us, which is where it belongs.

faqs.question: Does searching for an IB home tutor in Jumeirah 3 mean somebody comes to the villa?
faqs.answer: Not with IB Gram. The phrase is how parents in this city have searched for twenty years, so we target it honestly, but our tutors do not travel to UAE addresses and home visits in Dubai are not a service we sell; that service exists only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. What you gain is a tutor chosen for the syllabus your child sits rather than for being within driving distance of Al Wasl Road, and an evening start time that holds through the term instead of competing with afternoon traffic.

faqs.question: How does a tutor work with my child's own school deadlines rather than against them?
faqs.answer: By starting from them. In the first session we ask for the school's deadline list - draft dates, internal cut-offs, the mock window - and sequence the work backwards from the nearest one. That way coursework feedback arrives while the draft can still change, and timed practice happens in the weeks when timing is the binding constraint. Tutoring that ignores the school calendar becomes a third workstream for a student already running two, which is the usual reason a weekly arrangement quietly collapses in February. Your child's teachers set those dates; we plan around them.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay without crossing the academic-honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is specific enough to state. A tutor may discuss whether a research question is answerable, teach the subject content behind it, explain what each assessment criterion rewards, help plan a method, read the student's own draft and respond with questions, and teach referencing properly. A tutor may not write, rewrite or edit any part of the essay to completion, supply text to be adopted, or produce data. Everything submitted must be the student's own work. A draft returned full of questions teaches a student to see it as a moderator will; a draft returned already fixed teaches nothing.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and how would a parent verify one?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. The permit route is MoHRE's own service page, and a parent is entitled to ask any individual tutor directly whether they hold one.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do Diploma families along the Jumeirah coast usually start with?
faqs.answer: One session a week per subject is the normal starting point through the term, moving to two or three a week during an intensive block before mocks or papers. More than that is rarely useful for a student still attending school full time, because the limiting factor is the time available to do the work between sessions rather than the teaching itself. Where a family is considering two subjects at once, we would usually suggest starting with the one where the next deadline falls soonest, auditing the result after a month, and adding the second only if the schedule genuinely has room.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.closingHeading: Start from the date that matters most
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.closingBody: If your child is in DP2, the nearest fixed point is probably a coursework deadline or the January mock window; if they are in DP1, it is the Internal Assessment question that has not been settled yet. Either way, that date is where a sensible plan begins. Tell us the subject, the level, the year group and the evenings that work for a Jumeirah 3 schedule, and we will match a specialist and arrange a free trial lesson so you can judge the teaching before anything is booked. Lessons run one-to-one online on Gulf Standard Time, with session notes you can read against your school's own deadline list.

intro.heading: The honest answer to "is there an IB tutor near me in Jumeirah Golf Estates?"
paragraphs: Jumeirah Golf Estates is a low-density community of villas and townhouses wrapped around two championship courses, sitting between Dubai Sports City, Jumeirah Park and the Al Khail Road corridor. It is a comfortable place to live and a difficult place to find a subject specialist on foot. The population inside the gates is a few thousand households. The number of adults within a ten-minute drive who have taught IB Diploma Chemistry Higher Level to an examination standard, or who can read a Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Internal Assessment against the five assessment criteria and tell you which one is costing marks, is very small. That is not a criticism of the neighbourhood. It is arithmetic.

So when a parent types "IB home tutor in Jumeirah Golf Estates" into Google, two different things are being asked at once. The first is practical: can someone come to the villa. The second, and the one that actually determines whether the grade moves, is whether that someone knows the specific course. Those two requirements pull in opposite directions. The tighter you draw the geographic circle, the shallower the pool of genuine subject expertise inside it. Draw a circle around Jumeirah Golf Estates and you may find a capable general maths tutor. Draw it around the whole of Dubai and you may find three people who have marked Physics Paper 3. Draw it wider still and you find the person who teaches that paper every year.

IB Gram resolves the conflict by removing the driving. Lessons for families in Jumeirah Golf Estates are delivered one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, from a specialist in the exact subject and level your child sits. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. We say that plainly rather than burying it, because the alternative is a parent waiting at 5pm for a car that was never coming.

What that buys you is specificity. A Jumeirah Golf Estates student taking Chemistry HL, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL and English A Language and Literature SL does not need one tutor who is adequate at all three. They need a chemist for the organic mechanisms, a mathematician for the proof and calculus, and somebody who can mark an Individual Oral against the criteria. Online matching makes that routine. Geographic matching makes it a lottery.

The rest of this page does four things. It sets out what home tutoring actually costs in this part of Dubai and what the travel premium pays for, using published market rates rather than invented ones. It explains the permit position, because every private tutor working in the UAE needs one and most parents have never asked. It names the schools Jumeirah Golf Estates children actually attend and what that cluster is short of. And it states the academic-honesty boundary, because the Internal Assessment is where families get into trouble and where a certain kind of provider in this market is happy to help them.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-golf-est.programmesIntro: Jumeirah Golf Estates children sit in three different IB programmes depending on their age and school, and each one fails in a different way. The Primary Years Programme rarely needs tuition at all. The Middle Years Programme needs criteria coaching. The Diploma needs examination technique. Here is what each involves and what tuition looks like for a family in this community.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment marked by the teacher and moderated externally. Points run to 45, with the core contributing up to three. The Diploma is where tuition demand concentrates, because the examination is unforgiving about command terms and about showing method rather than answers.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, and Dubai Diploma candidates from the Jumeirah Golf Estates cluster typically attend schools in Al Barsha South, Jumeirah Park, Arabian Ranches or Emirates Hills. Confirm every session and results date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org rather than with any tutoring provider, including us. For UAE university entry, Ministry of Education equivalency is a separate process handled by the ministry, not by a tutor.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, lettered A to D, with task-specific clarifications written by the teacher. There is no external paper in most schools, so the grade is built entirely from classroom tasks. Students lose marks for not answering the criterion in front of them, which is a skill rather than a knowledge gap, and it is highly coachable.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving the Jumeirah Golf Estates and Dubai Sports City belt run MYP to Year 11 while others switch to Cambridge IGCSE at 14, so a family moving between communities inside Dubai can find the assessment model changes entirely. Dubai private schools also run Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the MYP under KHDA requirements, which is additional timetable load the brochure does not mention.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry with no external examination and a Year 6 Exhibition. Tuition at this stage should be narrow and short: a specific reading fluency gap, number bonds, or written fluency in English for a child who has arrived from a different language of instruction. Long-running PYP tuition is usually a sign that the problem has been misdiagnosed.
programmes.countryNote: Jumeirah Golf Estates sits near several primary-only campuses, which means a family here often has a primary child five minutes away and a Diploma child thirty-five minutes away in a different community. That split is the practical reason online scheduling works better than a tutor driving between two addresses in the same evening.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study, plus a reflective project and personal and professional skills. Very few UAE schools offer it, so most Jumeirah Golf Estates families will never meet it. Where it is offered, tuition usually supports the Diploma course components rather than the career-related study itself.
programmes.countryNote: Because Career-related Programme provision in Dubai is thin, families who want a vocational-leaning post-16 route more often look at BTEC at a Dubai centre or at A Level. If your child's school has floated the Career-related Programme, ask the coordinator which Diploma courses sit inside it, because that is what determines examination load.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-golf-est.subjectsIntro: Demand from the Jumeirah Golf Estates and Victory Heights side of New Dubai is dominated by the sciences and mathematics at Higher Level, with English A support rising in the second year as the Individual Oral and Paper 2 come into view. These are the courses we are asked for most often from this postcode.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus, complex numbers and the Paper 3 extended investigation at Higher Level. Marks go on method lines that are never written down, on radians slipping back into degrees, and on candidates answering "show that" questions by quoting the result instead of deriving it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling, financial mathematics and graph theory at Higher Level. The common failure is technology use: students who can run a regression on the calculator but cannot state what the coefficient means in the context the question describes.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity across the reorganised syllabus, with organic mechanisms and energetics carrying the most lost marks. Paper 2 extended response rewards correct use of state symbols, significant figures and the data booklet, and penalises vague language about bond strength.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields, waves and the Higher Level extensions into rotational dynamics and quantum physics. Students lose marks for unit errors, for omitting the direction of a vector, and for describing an experiment without naming the controlled variable in the data-analysis paper.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The syllabus is now organised around unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and continuity. Command terms matter more here than in any other science: "outline" and "explain" carry different mark allocations and students routinely answer the wrong one.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, the Individual Oral on a global issue and, at Higher Level, the HL Essay. The Individual Oral is where coaching pays fastest, because it is a structured 15-minute performance with a published mark scheme.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: For students whose stronger language is not English, which is common across New Dubai's international intake. Writing tasks are assessed on text type as much as on language, so a student who writes a beautiful essay when a blog was asked for loses marks for a reason nobody explained.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and the three-commentary Internal Assessment portfolio. Diagrams must be labelled fully and referred to in the prose; a correct diagram that the answer never mentions earns very little.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools such as Ansoff, Porter and cash-flow forecasting, assessed through structured response and the research project. The weakness is almost always application: tools recited correctly but never applied to the stimulus organisation in front of the candidate.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Systems fundamentals, computational thinking, and the solution development for the Internal Assessment. Students arrive able to code and unable to document a design, and the documentation is where the criteria sit.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must run Arabic alongside the licensed curriculum under KHDA requirements, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and with teachers who hold the regulator's sign-off for those subjects. Support here is about keeping the mandatory subject from damaging the overall report.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay

These are the areas we are asked about alongside Jumeirah Golf Estates.

sections.heading: What a Jumeirah Golf Estates parent is actually asking
paragraphs: The search phrase is "IB home tutor in Jumeirah Golf Estates" but the question underneath it is narrower: is there a person near this villa who knows my child's specific course well enough to be worth the money. The honest answer is that proximity and subject depth rarely coexist in a community of a few thousand homes. Jumeirah Golf Estates has roughly the residential density of a small town and the subject-specialist supply to match.

Think about what the requirement really is. A Diploma student sitting Chemistry at Higher Level needs somebody who has read the current syllabus, knows which sub-topics sit in which paper, and can mark an extended response the way a moderator does. That is a working subject teacher or examiner, not a generalist. The chance that such a person happens to live within a short drive of one specific gated community, and happens to be free at the one hour your child is not at football or in a car, is low. Parents discover this after two or three disappointing trials.

IB Gram's position is that the geographic constraint is the thing to drop, not the specialism. Your child's lesson happens over live video at a fixed time in Gulf Standard Time, with a tutor selected because they teach that subject at that level. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, in Jumeirah Golf Estates or anywhere else. The trade you are making is a car arriving in the driveway in exchange for a tutor, teaching online, who knows Paper 3.
The sections below put numbers on that trade: what the Dubai market charges for each format, what the travel premium actually buys, and what you can verify before you commit a single dirham.
bullets: Density, not willingness, is why local IB specialists are scarce in villa communities
Subject-level matching matters more than the physical distance to the tutor

sections.heading: How many IB specialists are genuinely available near this community
paragraphs: It helps to think about tutor supply the way a school thinks about staffing. A secondary school needs one Chemistry teacher per few hundred students, and only some of those teachers have taught the Diploma rather than A Level or the national curriculum. Scale that down to the catchment of a single villa community and the expected count for any one Higher Level subject is often less than one. For the less common courses it is reliably zero.

That has a practical consequence parents should hear before they start calling agencies. If a provider tells you they have a Jumeirah Golf Estates based tutor for every subject you name, be sceptical and ask which school they teach at and which papers they have marked. Research across this market found providers listing dozens of schools as clients with no relationship at all, so the claim costs them nothing to make.

Our own answer is to disclose coverage rather than imply it is universal. The table below sets out, by subject and level, how the match usually resolves for a family in this part of Dubai, and what we do when nobody appropriate is free. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit, which is precisely why it is worth printing.

Read the table as a staffing forecast rather than a promise. The left column is the course, the middle columns describe how the match has typically resolved for families in the Jumeirah Golf Estates and Dubai Sports City belt, and the right column is what you are told when the answer is no. The pattern is consistent: the more specific the Higher Level course, the more certain it is that the right teacher is not within driving distance of this community, and the less that matters once the lesson happens over video.

sections.heading: What home tutoring costs around Jumeirah Golf Estates, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because that is the number that actually lands on a family budget. A weekly one-hour session with a qualified subject tutor sits in a band that published Dubai rate surveys put at roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month for mid-tier provision, rising to AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year support. Budget provision, typically a university student working online, is quoted from around AED 240 to AED 600 a month.

Now look at the hourly rates underneath those monthly numbers, because the gap between formats is where the money goes. Market research conducted in October 2026 across published UAE provider pages found budget online tuition advertised from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, qualified online subject tutors from AED 150 to AED 300, in-home one-to-one visits including travel from AED 180 to AED 500, IB and IGCSE specialists from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and premium named or examiner-led tuition quoted as high as AED 650. One provider published monthly packages of AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

The important observation for a Jumeirah Golf Estates family is what the in-home premium is actually paying for. It is not more teaching. A tutor driving from Al Barsha to a villa off the Fire course and back spends something close to an hour in a car for a sixty-minute lesson, and that hour is priced into the rate whether or not the invoice itemises it. You are buying the travel, and the travel narrows the pool of people willing to make it. These are market figures from the sources named, not IB Gram prices; our own fee is quoted after the free trial lesson.

The one cost nobody tables is the family's own travel. If the alternative to a tutor visiting is driving a child to a learning centre in Motor City or Al Barsha at 5pm, add that to the comparison honestly.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against a tutor in the villa: the comparison on its merits
paragraphs: A fair comparison does not pretend the in-home option has no advantages. A tutor sitting at the kitchen table can see a younger child's handwriting, can be supervised by a parent walking past, and removes the small friction of getting a teenager to a laptop on time. For a Primary Years child those things matter and we would say so.

For a Diploma student they matter much less than who is teaching. From Year 10 upwards the binding constraint is whether the tutor knows the paper. A student working through Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Paper 3 needs a shared screen with a worked solution building line by line, the same mark scheme open on both sides, and a recording to go back to. That is a better teaching environment than a notebook on a dining table, not a worse one.

Then there is the scheduling reality of this community. Jumeirah Golf Estates children are frequently at clubs in Sports City until 6pm, and a tutor who has to drive in afterwards is arriving at the point where a fourteen-year-old has stopped being able to concentrate. Online, the same slot starts at 7.15pm with no travel on either side, and can move to a weekend morning in a heavy coursework week or shift after Iftar during Ramadan without anyone renegotiating a round trip.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is the question almost no Dubai parent asks and the one with the clearest answer. Private tutoring in the UAE sits under a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits, administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no honest page can quote an amount and we will not.

The eligible categories are broader than most parents expect. They include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service, listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

There is one boundary worth knowing if your child attends school in Abu Dhabi or has a teacher who does. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. That has been reported in the regional press; verify it against the current ADEK policy document before relying on the exact wording. The practical point is simple: never ask for your child's own classroom teacher as a paid private tutor.

A separate thing entirely is a tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai, which needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no such permit, has no UAE centre or office, and is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge. A provider implying that its individual tutors carry KHDA sign-off is describing something the regulator does not issue to individuals at all.

sections.heading: The schools this neighbourhood feeds, and what the cluster is short of
paragraphs: Dubai's private sector had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, US at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. Those proportions explain the experience of a Jumeirah Golf Estates IB family precisely. You are in the 7 per cent, surrounded by provision built for the 37 per cent.

On the ground that means the nearest campuses to the Jumeirah Golf Estates gates are mostly British curriculum, teaching Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE at 16, while the IB continuum schools sit a little further out towards Al Barsha South, JVT, Arabian Ranches and Emirates Hills. A family with a Diploma student is therefore driving past three schools that do not teach their child's course to reach the one that does, and the pool of nearby adults who understand that course is thinner than the school count suggests.

The cluster is specifically short of Higher Level science and mathematics support, and of anybody who works on Internal Assessment criteria rather than content. That is consistent with what we are asked for from this postcode. Dubai's sector is also still growing: the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. More IB places near this belt will eventually change the picture.

One cost note while you are planning. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a family budgeting tuition against school fees, that is a stable baseline rather than a moving one.
