sections.heading: The exam calendar, counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Most families start tuition too late, and the reason is that the calendar is usually described forwards. Counted backwards it is obvious. The examination is a fixed point. The Internal Assessment deadlines sit months in front of it and are set by the school, not the board. Entry deadlines sit months in front of those. By the time a parent feels the panic, several of the levers have already been pulled.

For Cambridge candidates, the first thing to get right is which series applies. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate sits June, with November as the resit route. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Ask your school's examinations officer which zone your centre sits in.

For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, examinations are available in May/June and in November. As a checkable example of how far ahead the machinery runs: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, so always work from the live official timetable rather than from any figure restated on a tutoring page.

For the IB Diploma, UAE schools sit the May session. We are not publishing an IB examination or results date on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and we will not put a date in front of a parent that we have not read at source. Get your session and results dates from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org directly. What we can tell you is what the eight weeks before each milestone should contain, which is in the table.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may and may not do with an IA or Extended Essay
paragraphs: This matters more in this market than parents realise, because there are providers in the UAE search results selling completed Internal Assessments outright. One was found advertising finished IAs at AED 3,750. Buying one is not a shortcut; it is academic malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not on the seller.

The boundary is straightforward once stated. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain the assessment criteria, interrogate a research question, point out that a method will not produce analysable data, mark a draft against the criteria and say which criterion is losing marks and why, and teach citation and referencing properly. A tutor may not write any part of the work, rewrite sentences into their own prose, supply a research question as a finished product, provide data the student has not collected, or edit a draft to completion. IB Gram tutors work to that line and will decline a request that crosses it. We would rather lose the booking.

There is a related rule about materials. We do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. Tutors reference them and link to the official source, which is both the lawful position and the one that teaches a student where to look. Anyone offering you a folder of everything should prompt a question about what else they are relaxed about.

One more thing worth doing: keep the written notes the tutor sends after each session. If the authenticity of a piece of coursework is ever questioned, a dated record showing that the advice given was feedback on the student's own drafts is the student's best protection, and it costs nothing to retain.

sections.heading: Mandatory UAE subjects running alongside the IB
paragraphs: A detail that catches new arrivals in Jumeirah Golf Estates: your child's IB timetable is not the whole timetable. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April. The federal baseline behind this is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

The organisation of those classes is prescribed in some detail. KHDA requires separate classes by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both Arab and non-Arab groups are strictly prohibited because of different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

Two practical consequences. First, instructional time for the mandatory subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes; that is real timetable space competing with your child's Higher Levels. Second, for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so tutoring in these subjects has to follow the school's own material rather than an outside scheme. We will tell you when the school is the better route.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency for IB students, described accurately
paragraphs: If your child may apply to a UAE university, equivalency of the school-leaving certificate is a Ministry of Education process and it has specific requirements by curriculum. For the British track the published position is that students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One provider ranking in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the published rule says.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying.

For the IB there is a figure circulating on tutoring sites and we are not going to repeat it, because we have not read it on a Ministry of Education source. If somebody quotes you an IB points threshold for equivalency, ask where on moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority it appears. Equivalency is also something IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. Describe it, verify it at the authority, and do it through the official channel.

sections.heading: Getting started from Jumeirah Golf Estates, including what goes wrong
paragraphs: The useful version of this is not a four-step graphic. Send us three things: the subject and level, the school and what the last report or mock said, and the two or three time windows that actually work once the Sports City run and the Al Khail traffic are accounted for. With those three, matching is usually quick. Without the third, we will propose a slot nobody can keep.

Then there is a free trial lesson with the proposed specialist, which exists so that you can test the one thing you cannot test from a profile: whether this person can explain your child's specific confusion. Give the tutor a real problem beforehand, ideally a question from the last mock that was lost. A trial spent on introductions tells you nothing.

What goes wrong, honestly. Sometimes no specialist in the exact subject and level is free at the hours a family needs, particularly for Computer Science, Higher Level Physics in the weeks before the May session, and some language B combinations. When that happens we tell you the wait and where the available tutor is based, rather than offering a generalist and hoping. Sometimes the match is simply wrong on personality, in which case we change the tutor and do not argue about it. And sometimes the diagnosis is wrong: a student described as weak in mathematics turns out to be losing marks on reading the question, which is a different piece of work entirely.

Nothing on this page should be read as a promise about a grade. We do not guarantee outcomes, we publish no satisfaction statistics we cannot evidence with a sample size and a method, and we would be sceptical of anyone in this market who does.

process.title: Tell us the course, not just the subject
process.description: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is a different staffing problem from Applications and Interpretation Standard Level. Give us the exact course title, the year group, and the school, and the shortlist narrows immediately. If you are not sure which Mathematics route your child is on, the school's subject choice form will say.

process.title: Share the evidence of what is wrong
process.description: The most useful thing you can send is a marked mock paper or the last report with the subject teacher's comment. It usually shows the problem is narrower than it feels: three topics, or a recurring technique error, rather than a whole syllabus. That changes both the tutor we propose and the number of sessions.

process.title: Give us two or three realistic windows
process.description: Jumeirah Golf Estates evenings are shaped by the school run and by clubs in Sports City, so the slot that looks free on paper often is not. Two or three windows in Gulf Standard Time, with your preference marked, lets us hold a consistent weekly time rather than reshuffling every fortnight.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: You meet the specific tutor, over live video, and so does your child. Hand them a real problem from the last assessment. Afterwards you get the tutor's own read on what is going on and a proposed plan with a session count, and you decide. No payment is required to reach this point.

process.title: Lock a weekly slot and a stop date
process.description: Continuity with one tutor is what moves grades, so we book a recurring time rather than session by session. We also agree when the engagement ends, usually at study leave or after a specific deadline, so tuition does not quietly become a permanent expense nobody reviewed.

process.title: Review against the next assessment
process.description: After each session you get written notes on what was covered. At the next school assessment we look at whether the specific errors the plan targeted have gone. If they have not, we change the approach or the tutor; continuing unchanged for a second term is the most common waste of money in this market.

A Jumeirah Golf Estates family gets a Chemistry Higher Level teacher because that is what their child sits, not because that teacher happens to live near the Earth course. In a community of this density, that distinction is the difference between help and company.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is explicit
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question, mark against the published criteria and give feedback on the student's own work. They do not write, rewrite or complete an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay, and they will decline if asked. In a market where completed IAs are openly sold, this is worth stating rather than assuming.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that survives a Dubai term
whyPoints.description: A fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, movable within the week when coursework or a tournament collides, shiftable to post-Iftar during Ramadan, and pausable around examinations. No round trip has to be renegotiated to make any of that happen.

whyPoints.description: For some subjects there is no UAE-based specialist free, and for a few there rarely is. We name the wait and say where the available tutor is based rather than substituting a generalist. Disclosing a coverage limit costs us bookings and is the reason the ones we take tend to work.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor who comes to our villa in Jumeirah Golf Estates?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We deliver one-to-one IB tuition to Jumeirah Golf Estates families over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and we do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE — in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. Independent in-home tutors do work in this part of Dubai, and published market rates for an in-home one-to-one visit including travel run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour. What you gain by dropping the visit is the ability to pick a tutor by subject and level rather than by who is willing to drive to the Fire course.

faqs.question: Is there actually anyone near Jumeirah Golf Estates who knows the IB syllabus my child is sitting?
faqs.answer: For common Standard Level courses, sometimes. For Higher Level Chemistry, Physics or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, rarely, and for Computer Science almost never. A villa community of a few thousand households simply does not contain many adults who teach a specific Diploma course to examination standard. That is why we match online: the pool becomes every specialist in the subject instead of the handful inside a twenty-minute drive. If a provider claims a local tutor for every subject you name, ask which school they teach at and which papers they have marked.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay for IB tuition in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Think monthly first. Published Dubai rate surveys put a weekly one-hour session with a mid-tier tutor at roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month, and specialist examination-year support at AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above. Hourly, market research in October 2026 found qualified online subject tutors advertised at AED 150 to AED 300, IB specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and premium examiner-led tuition quoted as high as AED 650. Those are market figures from the providers named on this page, not IB Gram's prices; ours are quoted after the free trial.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with Jumeirah Golf Estates families need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Ask any tutor directly whether they hold the permit and under which category. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: My child is at a British-curriculum school near Jumeirah Golf Estates but moving to the IB Diploma. What changes?
faqs.answer: Three things, and none of them is content. Assessment becomes continuous: every subject carries an Internal Assessment that is marked by the teacher and moderated externally, so the grade is being built from the first term. Command terms become load-bearing, because "outline" and "explain" carry different mark allocations. And the core arrives — Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service, together worth up to three points. Students who struggled with IGCSE because of pace usually cope; students who struggled with extended writing need support early, not in the second year.

faqs.question: Which IB schools do Jumeirah Golf Estates families generally use?
faqs.answer: The campuses closest to the gates are mostly British curriculum, so IB families typically travel: towards Al Barsha South and JVT, where several IB continuum schools sit, or towards Arabian Ranches, the Meadows and Emirates Hills. That is consistent with Dubai's overall mix, where the International Baccalaureate accounts for about 7 per cent of private-school enrolment against 37 per cent for the UK curriculum. Named schools on this page are context for the neighbourhood only; IB Gram is not affiliated with, endorsed by or a partner of any of them.

faqs.question: What time can lessons realistically start for a child living in Jumeirah Golf Estates?
faqs.answer: Later than most families first suggest. The school run out of this community commonly runs twenty to thirty-five minutes each way, and clubs in Dubai Sports City keep secondary students out until around 6pm. In practice, consistent slots land between 6.30pm and 8.15pm on weekdays, with weekend mornings working well for Internal Assessment and Extended Essay blocks. Online removes the travel on the tutor's side, which is what makes a 7.15pm start possible at all; a tutor driving in afterwards arrives when concentration has already gone.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Internal Assessment without crossing an academic-honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor can teach the subject content, explain each assessment criterion, interrogate and narrow a research question, point out that a method will not generate analysable data, mark a draft against the criteria and explain which criterion is losing marks, and teach referencing properly. A tutor cannot write or rewrite any part of the work, supply a finished research question, provide data the student has not collected, or edit a draft to completion. Our tutors decline requests that cross that line. There are providers in this market selling completed IAs; that is malpractice and the student carries the consequence.

faqs.question: Which IB exam session do students in Dubai sit, and when should tuition start?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the May session. We are deliberately not publishing an IB examination or results date here, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and we will not put an unverified date in front of a parent — get yours from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org. On timing, work backwards instead: Internal Assessment deadlines are set by the school and sit a term or more before the papers, mocks sit roughly a term ahead, and the final eight weeks should be past papers under timed conditions. Starting tuition after the mocks means several levers have already been pulled.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Diploma student in this community usually start with?
faqs.answer: One weekly session per subject is the normal starting point, and for most students it is enough. Two or three a week makes sense in two situations: an examination-term intensive where the student knows the content and is losing marks on technique, or a genuine content backlog in a Higher Level science. More is rarely better, because a student needs time between sessions to attempt problems unaided — that attempt is where the learning happens. We would rather propose eight well-used sessions with a stop date than an open-ended weekly commitment nobody reviews.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring genuinely as effective for a Diploma student as somebody sitting at the table?
faqs.answer: For a Diploma student, the tutor's subject knowledge matters far more than the room. A shared screen with a worked solution building line by line, the same mark scheme open on both sides and a recording to revisit is a better teaching environment than a notebook on a dining table. For a Primary Years child the in-person advantages are real and we would say so. From Year 10 upwards the binding constraint is whether the tutor knows the paper, and online matching is what makes it possible to pick someone who does.

faqs.question: Does my child have to study Arabic as well as their IB subjects in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, with Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Arabic as a first language and for Islamic Education for Arab students. Instructional time is built on a 40-minute lesson unit. Because outside content for these subjects needs Ministry of Education permission, tutoring here has to follow the school's own material.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is available for my child's subject?
faqs.answer: We tell you. For some courses — Computer Science, Higher Level Physics close to the May session, some language B combinations — there may be no appropriate tutor free at the hours you need. In that case you get the realistic wait, the option of a shorter diagnostic block in the meantime, and, where the available specialist is based outside the UAE, we say so before you pay anything. What we do not do is put a generalist in front of a Higher Level student and hope. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit, which is exactly why we publish ours.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan or around school examinations?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the clearest practical advantages of online delivery. Sessions can shift to post-Iftar timing through Ramadan, move within the week when a coursework deadline or a tournament collides, and pause entirely during mock or final examination weeks. None of that requires a tutor's round trip to be renegotiated, so it can usually be arranged in the same week. We also agree a stop date at the start, typically study leave or a specific deadline, so the schedule has a defined end rather than running on by default.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram hold any KHDA or IB accreditation I should look for?
faqs.answer: No, and you should treat that claim as a warning sign wherever you see it. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed by or partnered with KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We hold no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is the specific permit issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, and we have no UAE office or centre. We name those regulators on this page to explain what each one governs, which is a different thing from implying any of them endorses us.

faqs.question: How do I tell a genuine IB specialist from a general tutor during the trial?
faqs.answer: Ask three concrete questions. Which papers does the subject have, and what is each worth at your child's level? What are the assessment criteria for this subject's Internal Assessment, by letter? And can you mark this specific lost question from the last mock and tell me what the mark scheme wanted? A specialist answers the first two without hesitating and the third with a mark scheme in hand. A generalist talks about confidence and study skills. The free trial exists for exactly this test, so use it on a real problem.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-golf-est.closingHeading: Start with the subject, not the postcode
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-golf-est.closingBody: If you have been searching for an IB home tutor in Jumeirah Golf Estates, the thing standing between your child and a better grade is almost certainly not distance. It is whether the person teaching them knows the course well enough to read a mark scheme out loud. Tell us the exact subject and level, send the last marked paper, and give us two or three evening windows that genuinely work once the Sports City run is done. We will propose a specialist, you will meet them in a free trial lesson over live video, and you will decide afterwards. No home visit, no promised grade, and no figure on this page that we cannot attribute.

intro.heading: What 'knows the IB' actually means
paragraphs: Jumeirah Islands is a gated community of villas built around man-made lakes, with no school inside the gates. Every school-age child here travels out, most often to Jumeirah Village, Al Barsha, The Meadows or Emirates Hills. So when a parent here searches for an IB home tutor, the underlying question is rarely about convenience alone. It is whether anyone reachable understands the programme their child is actually sitting.

That question deserves a real answer rather than reassurance, so here is what IB-specific knowledge consists of. It is command terms, and how an answer to 'evaluate' differs from an answer to 'outline'. It is criterion-based marking, where a mark comes from a descriptor rather than from a total of correct points. It is paper structures and their weightings. It is how internal assessment is marked and moderated. And it is the core: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS.

None of that is implied by being an excellent teacher of the same subject in another system. A strong A Level chemist knows the chemistry and may not know what Paper 3 contains or which criterion rewards what in an internal investigation. A capable Key Stage 3 mathematician may not know that the Diploma's Analysis and Approaches has a non-calculator paper that changes how algebra must be taught.

This matters more in the IB than in most systems because so much of the grade is not a written paper. Internal assessment, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are all marked against published criteria, with deadlines set by your child's school rather than by the IB. A tutor who has never read a criterion descriptor cannot help with the part of the Diploma that students most consistently mishandle.

Supply is the other half of the honest answer. The International Baccalaureate accounts for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment against 37 per cent on the UK curriculum, so IB families are a minority of a large market. Narrow that to one subject at Higher Level, within driving distance of a gated community off Sheikh Zayed Road, available at six in the evening, and the list is very short.

One more thing worth knowing before the detail: a great deal of the Diploma is decided by deadlines your child's school sets rather than by the IB. Internal assessment milestones, Extended Essay checkpoints and mock windows cluster, and a student with four of them in one fortnight has a planning problem that no amount of subject teaching addresses. A tutor who asks for the school's assessment calendar in the first conversation is telling you they know this.

IB Gram's answer is to drop the distance condition and keep the rest. Your child is matched to a subject and level specialist who teaches live online, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. We target the home-tutor phrase because it is what parents type, and we would rather tell you now than let you find out after a deposit.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-islands.subjectsIntro: What a genuine specialist in each IB subject must know, beyond the subject itself. Use these as the test; a specialist produces the answer without hesitating.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: A specialist knows that Paper 1 permits no calculator, which makes exact algebraic manipulation a trained skill rather than a by-product, and that Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers, series and vector geometry. They also know the exploration carries roughly a fifth of the grade across five criteria.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: A specialist knows this is calculator-active throughout and statistics-led, with graph theory at Higher Level, and that marks are lost in interpretation rather than calculation. They also know which quantitative degrees expect Analysis and Approaches instead, which is a conversation for the first Diploma year.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: A specialist can tell you what the data-based and extended-response components demand, that unit and significant-figure discipline costs more marks than physics errors, and that Higher Level separates at fields and induction. They know the investigation's four criteria and that design carries as much weight as analysis.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: A specialist teaches organic chemistry as electron movement rather than memorised products, because examiners use unfamiliar molecules deliberately. They know that mole reliability rather than comprehension decides calculation marks, and that spectroscopic identification arrives late and is under-revised.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A specialist knows the marks are lost to command terms rather than recall, and can distinguish what outline, explain, evaluate and distinguish each require. Examiner reports repeat this every session. They also know the statistics the investigation expects, which students meet nowhere else in the course.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A specialist knows the internal assessment is three commentaries of 800 words on published news articles, and that article choice is half the mark because a poorly chosen article cannot carry a diagram. They know Higher Level adds quantitative work and a further paper.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: A specialist can describe the Individual Oral precisely: a global issue, two texts, a sustained argument rather than a summary. They know Paper 1 is unseen analysis and Paper 2 comparative, and that students lose marks by summarising rather than analysing how meaning is constructed.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A specialist knows which parts catch out strong writers, namely investment appraisal and cash-flow forecasting, and that the research project needs a real organisation with a question narrow enough to answer inside the word limit. They know Higher Level adds extension topics.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A specialist knows the internal assessment fails on scope rather than ambition, that the written papers want pseudocode rather than a favourite language, and that Higher Level adds abstract data structures and resource management. They can say what a documented client brief has to contain.

subjects.name: TOK, the Extended Essay and IA coaching
subjects.description: A specialist can explain what each component is assessed on and, above all, what a tutor may and may not do: teaching research question design, argument structure and referencing, with feedback on the student's own drafts, and never writing any part of it. Any other answer ends the conversation.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Jumeirah Islands means in practice
paragraphs: Locally the phrase means one-to-one IB teaching arranged for a child who lives in this community, without the family having to drive to a centre after school. Jumeirah Islands has no school inside the gates and no tuition centre, so everything already involves a car. The appeal of a home tutor is removing one more journey from an evening that already has two.

IB Gram removes it differently. Lessons are live online, one tutor to one student, with a shared whiteboard and the past paper on screen for both. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all; our in-person service exists only in India, and there is no office or centre here either. Nothing on this site will suggest otherwise.

The trade is worth setting out plainly. Insisting on a tutor at your door means choosing from people who hold a Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition permit, teach your child's subject at your child's level, have a free slot in your window, and will drive into a gated community off Sheikh Zayed Road at 17:30. Those four conditions intersect in very few people.

Choosing live video removes the fourth condition and keeps the three that affect the grade. For a mainstream Standard Level subject the practical difference is modest. For Chemistry at Higher Level, Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or Computer Science, it is the difference between a tutor who has taught the course to a May session and a capable generalist.

Where in-person provision genuinely wins, we will say so. A younger child who needs an adult beside them to stay on task, a household with nowhere quiet in the early evening, or hands-on practical equipment coaching are all better served face to face. If that is your situation, hire locally and expect the travel premium the market charges for it.

sections.heading: Six things an IB specialist knows that a good teacher may not
paragraphs: This is the substance of the question behind the search, so here it is as a list you can use. None of these is obscure within the programme, and all of them are invisible from outside it, which is why a parent cannot judge expertise from a CV.

Command terms come first. The IB uses a defined vocabulary of instructions, and 'outline', 'explain', 'evaluate' and 'distinguish' each demand a different answer shape. A student who writes a good answer to the wrong command term scores poorly, and examiner reports repeat this every session. A tutor who treats these as interchangeable will not fix it.

Second, criterion-based marking: in the Middle Years Programme and in all Diploma internal assessment, marks come from descriptors rather than from a count of correct points. Third, paper structures and weightings, including which components exist at Higher Level and not at Standard. Fourth, how internal assessment is marked and moderated, and what the school's role in that is.

Fifth, the core. Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS are where Diploma students lose points they cannot recover, because the deadlines are internal and the work is independent. Sixth, the academic honesty boundary: exactly what a tutor may and may not do with a student's assessed work, which is both an ethical and a practical question.

The table sets each out with the question to ask and what a weak answer sounds like. It works on us as readily as on anyone else, and we would rather you used it and chose someone else than hired a confident generalist for a Higher Level course.

paragraphs: A fair page about this search should describe the thing being searched for rather than only the alternative. In-home tutoring in Dubai is a real and well-established market. Published figures put in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's survey, and independent home tutors at AED 200-500. Monthly in-home packages of around AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visits are advertised.

What the premium pays for is travel and presence. For a gated community reached from Sheikh Zayed Road or Al Khail Road, a tutor coming from Al Barsha or Business Bay in the 17:30 peak is adding forty to ninety minutes of round-trip driving to your hour. That cost appears either in the rate or in the tutor's willingness to still be doing it in week eleven.

Presence has genuine value for some students, and it is worth being honest about who. A child who will not remain in the chair without an adult present. A household with no quiet room at six in the evening. Practical equipment handling. In those cases a home visit is the better service and the premium is justified.

What the premium does not buy is subject depth. The tutor willing to make that drive at that hour for that rate is drawn from a smaller and generally less specialised pool, because an in-demand Higher Level specialist has no reason to spend ninety minutes in traffic. That is the trade, stated plainly, and the table lays it out so you can judge it against your own household.
IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so if you decide presence matters more than depth, you need a local in-home provider and the published rates above are the market you will be buying in.

sections.heading: Why hiring locally does not reduce the price
paragraphs: Parents often expect a neighbourhood tutor to be cheaper than a specialist, and in this market the published figures do not support that. The budget end is online: Tutopiya advertises from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65. The in-home end is the most expensive band for equivalent teaching, because travel is inside the rate.

In the middle, Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, which is roughly where a qualified subject tutor sits. Above that, TutorChase quotes around AED 270 for specialist work and Bestimate's survey puts specialist IB and IGCSE tuition at AED 200-450 or more. BartyED's premium examiner-led tier reaches AED 650.

So the structure of the market is that proximity costs more and buys less specialisation, while the cheapest option is online supervision that does not teach the programme. The band that moves IB grades is the qualified-to-specialist range, and it is available without a travel premium.

Treat examiner claims carefully wherever they appear. Current examiner status is hard to verify and must never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. If a provider's price rests on it, ask what evidences the claim before paying for it.

sections.heading: The core: where Diploma students lose points nobody warned them about
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS are the parts of the Diploma that generalist tutors handle least well, and they are where avoidable points go. Each is independent work against published criteria with deadlines set by your child's school, usually a long way before the written papers, and none of them responds to content teaching.

The Extended Essay fails on the research question more often than on the research. A question too broad to answer in 4,000 words produces a descriptive essay, and that is decided in the first fortnight rather than in the final draft. A tutor can teach question design, argument structure and referencing, and can read and comment on the student's own drafts, which is where the value is.

Theory of Knowledge is an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, and students struggle because it asks for argument about knowledge rather than knowledge itself. Students who write what they believe rather than constructing and testing a claim lose marks consist. That too is teachable, and it is rarely taught outside the school.

CAS is the component families forget until it becomes urgent. It is not graded, but it must be completed and evidenced, and the Diploma is not awarded without it. A tutor cannot do CAS for a student. What a tutor can do is point out in September that the reflection record is part of the requirement rather than an afterthought.

The sequencing point is the practical one. Internal assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay milestones and mock examinations tend to cluster, and a student with four deadlines in one fortnight needs a plan rather than more teaching. That planning conversation is often the single most useful hour a Diploma family buys.

sections.heading: The academic honesty boundary, stated plainly
paragraphs: This is the shortest section with the highest stakes. A tutor may teach content, explain assessment criteria, help a student design a research question, teach referencing and academic conventions, and read and comment on work the student has written themselves. That is the whole legitimate scope, and it is genuinely effective.

A tutor may not write, part-write, rewrite to completion or supply any portion of an internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project. Submitting work that is not the student's own is a malpractice matter handled by the IB, and the consequence can reach the loss of the Diploma. The risk falls on your child, not on the tutor.

There are operators in this SERP selling completed internal assessments outright at four-figure prices. A Jumeirah Islands parent comparing quotes should treat that offer as a disqualification rather than a service, and should ask every provider the same question: what will you do with my child's draft?

The right answer is unglamorous. The tutor reads the draft with the published descriptors open, states which band the work currently meets and why, and names the specific thing missing: no evaluation of method, an uncertainty never propagated, a conclusion that does not answer the research question. The student then fixes it, and learns to do it again.

We also do not reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. They are cited and linked; your child's school holds licensed access to what it needs.

sections.heading: Scheduling from a gated community with no school inside
paragraphs: This is a real operational difference between Jumeirah Islands and the villa communities that have a school at their centre. Every child here leaves the community for school, so nobody gets the early arrival home that an in-community school allows. Dubai schools finish between roughly 14:30 and 15:30, and the return journey puts most students here home between 15:40 and 16:50.

The practical consequence is that 16:30 is optimistic and 17:00 to 17:30 is dependable. Second-year Diploma students frequently do better at 19:30, after dinner, particularly for Theory of Knowledge, essay work or anything requiring sustained argument rather than quick recall. Booking the wrong hour is the commonest reason an arrangement quietly ends in week five.

Jumeirah Islands does have one transport advantage over the communities further inland: the Red Line station on the edge of Jumeirah Lakes Towers is a short drive away. That helps a teenager with an after-school activity and does nothing for a tutoring timetable, because the session happens at home either way.

Use the weekend for long work. A Saturday morning slot is the only place in the week where a full timed paper or a proper Extended Essay drafting session genuinely fits, and Sunday afternoon is the natural time to review what came out of it.

During Ramadan, school hours shorten and households run later; a post-Iftar session or a late-morning weekend slot works better than anything at five in the afternoon. We reschedule rather than cancel, and because nobody travels a reschedule is a slot swap rather than a negotiation.

sections.heading: Regulators, permits and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by any of them, nor by the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is the specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. We explain what these bodies do because parents ask, not because any of them endorses us, and any provider implying a regulator has vetted its tutors is worth questioning closely.

On the tutor side, individuals providing private lessons in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years and applied for through MoHRE's app, website or e-services, with a two-working-day completion time.

u.ae states that individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount quoted to you with suspicion. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules also bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school.

There is one timetable fact worth adding, because it affects every Dubai family's week. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA calculating instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit. In a Diploma week already carrying six subjects and the core, that is real pressure.

faqs.question: Six questions aside, what single answer tells us a tutor is the real thing?
faqs.answer: Ask six things: how an 'evaluate' answer differs from an 'outline' answer, which criteria the relevant assessment uses and what each rewards, the components and weightings at your child's level, how internal assessment is marked and moderated, when the Extended Essay question should be agreed, and what they will do with your child's draft. A specialist answers all six without hesitating. A subject-only tutor hedges on criteria and offers to improve the writing, which is the answer that matters most.

faqs.question: Do your tutors come to houses inside Jumeirah Islands?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; our in-person service runs in India only, and there is no office or centre here either. Lessons for Jumeirah Islands families are live online, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time. We target the home-tutor search phrase because that is what parents type, and then say plainly what the service is. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180-500 an hour including travel if presence in the room is essential.

faqs.question: Are there many IB-trained tutors living in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Fewer than you would expect, and the reason is arithmetic rather than geography. The International Baccalaureate accounts for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment against 37 per cent on the UK curriculum, so IB families are a minority of a large market. Narrow it to one subject at Higher Level, available at six in the evening, and willing to drive into a gated community off Sheikh Zayed Road, and the pool is very small indeed.

faqs.question: Can a tutor who teaches A Level handle an IB course instead?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but it should be tested rather than assumed. The content overlaps substantially; the assessment does not. IB courses carry criterion-marked internal assessment, specific command-term expectations, and component structures that differ between Higher and Standard Level. A strong A Level teacher who has never read an internal assessment descriptor will teach the subject well and the assessment badly. Ask what they will do with an internal assessment draft and whether they can name the criteria.

faqs.question: Why does the Extended Essay go wrong so often?
faqs.answer: Because the research question is usually the problem and it is settled in the first fortnight. A question too broad to answer in 4,000 words produces description rather than argument, and no amount of later drafting rescues it. A tutor can legitimately teach question design, argument structure and referencing, and give feedback on the student's own drafts. A tutor cannot write any part of it. If a provider offers to, that tells you what else they are willing to do.

faqs.question: What time should sessions start for a family here?
faqs.answer: Plan for 17:00 to 17:30 on weekdays. Because no school sits inside Jumeirah Islands, every child travels out and comes back later than peers in communities with a school at the centre, typically arriving home between 15:40 and 16:50 depending on the school and route. Second-year Diploma students often work better at 19:30, after dinner, especially for Theory of Knowledge and essay work. Keep Saturday morning for a full timed paper.

faqs.question: Does the metro station near Jumeirah Lakes Towers help with tutoring?
faqs.answer: Not really, and it is worth saying so because it looks like it should. The Red Line station on the edge of Jumeirah Lakes Towers is a short drive from Jumeirah Islands and is genuinely useful for after-school activities and for an older teenager's independence. It makes no difference to a tutoring timetable, because online lessons happen at home and an in-home tutor arrives by car in the same traffic everyone else is in.

faqs.question: What does a tutor do about Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Teach the thing students find hardest, which is constructing and testing a claim about knowledge rather than stating what they believe. TOK is assessed through an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, and the failure mode is sincere opinion rather than argument. A tutor can teach argument structure, counter-claim handling and the use of examples, and can comment on the student's own drafts. A tutor cannot write any of it, and we will not.

faqs.question: Should we book a single diagnostic session before committing?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and some families find it is all they need. One session with a specialist, working from your child's own marked work, establishes where they actually sit against the level they are entered for and what the first six weeks would target. You get a written read and no obligation. It is also the cheapest way to test whether the tutor is the specialist they appear to be, using the six questions above.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest to find a specialist for?
faqs.answer: Physics at Higher Level, Chemistry at Higher Level, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and Computer Science. These are the subjects where a generalist runs out of depth about four weeks in, and the ones where a home-visit requirement hurts most, because almost nobody who can teach them has a spare evening and a willingness to drive. In the spring term there can be a wait even online, and we quote a date rather than a hope.

faqs.question: Is online teaching a problem for a student who is already struggling?
faqs.answer: It depends on why they are struggling. If the cause is a gap in understanding or weak exam technique, the format is irrelevant and the tutor's expertise is everything. If the cause is that they will not start work without an adult in the room, the format matters a great deal and a local in-home tutor may genuinely be the better answer. Tell us which it is at the consultation; we would rather say so than take the booking.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in the UAE need a licence?
faqs.answer: Yes. Individuals providing private lessons need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years and applied for through MoHRE's app, website or e-services, with a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Which IB schools do children from Jumeirah Islands usually attend?
faqs.answer: There is no school inside the community, so families travel. The schools named most often by households here are Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills and Emirates International School Meadows nearby, Nord Anglia International School Dubai and GEMS World Academy Dubai in Al Barsha, Dubai International Academy Al Barsha, Raffles World Academy in Umm Suqeim and Sunmarke School in Jumeirah Village Triangle. We have no affiliation with any of them; confirm current programmes on KHDA's own school listing.

faqs.question: Can sessions follow us when we travel?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided we know the week before. Lessons follow whichever time zone you are in, and because nobody has to drive anywhere a change is a slot swap rather than a renegotiation. Many families in this community travel during school breaks and either pause entirely or use a short intensive block, which is particularly useful in the summer before the first Diploma year. The weekly slot is held either way.

faqs.question: What happens if we are not satisfied after a few sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we change the tutor rather than asking your child to persist. The free trial exists so the pairing is tested before you pay for a term, and fit failures are usually not about competence: a tutor who talks for fifty minutes can be entirely expert and wrong for a student who needs to be made to work. Judge the sessions on whether your child spoke, and on whether the tutor diagnosed rather than lectured.

intro.heading: The real question behind an IB home tutor search in Jumeirah Park
paragraphs: Jumeirah Park sits between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road, a villa grid of nine districts with Dubai British School Jumeirah Park inside the community itself and a ring of larger international schools within fifteen minutes of the gates. That geography shapes the tutoring question completely. A family in District 4 is not short of qualified teachers in the city; they are short of a half-hour window between the bus arriving and homework collapsing into argument.

So the search for an IB home tutor in Jumeirah Park is really three questions stacked on top of each other. Who actually knows this syllabus at the level my child is sitting it? When can they realistically teach, given a school day that ends at 15:00 and a parent who gets back from Business Bay at 18:30? And what does the market charge before anyone starts quoting me packages?

This page answers all three in order, with the numbers attributed. The answer to the first is that IB subject depth is scarce and geographically random: there is no reason the Chemistry HL specialist who understands criterion-based IA marking happens to live in Al Furjan rather than Al Barsha. The answer to the second is that a live online lesson removes the only variable you cannot control, which is Dubai traffic between 16:00 and 19:00. The answer to the third is a table further down, drawn from published competitor rates and Bestimate's Dubai rate survey.

Be clear on one point before you read further. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only. Online IB tutoring in Jumeirah Park is what we actually deliver: one tutor, one student, live video, screen-shared past-paper questions and a shared whiteboard, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We target the phrase because it is what parents type; we are not going to pretend a car is coming.

One more piece of context before the detail. Dubai's private school sector held 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the British curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment and the IB at 7 per cent. That means IB families in any given Dubai neighbourhood are a minority of a large market, and the tutoring supply reflects it: plenty of generalists, far fewer people who have taught a specific HL course through to a May session.

What you get instead is a wider pool. A villa in Jumeirah Park that insists on a tutor who can drive to the door is choosing from whoever is free, permitted and within a twenty-minute radius on a weekday evening. A family that accepts live video is choosing from every IB Diploma Programme tutor in Dubai and beyond who teaches that subject at that level. For a mainstream subject the difference is modest. For Physics HL, Chemistry HL or Maths AA HL it is the whole difference between a tutor who knows the course and a tutor who read the guide last week.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-park.programmesIntro: Jumeirah Park children are spread across three IB programmes depending on which school the family chose and when they moved to Dubai. Each programme fails in a different way, and each needs a different kind of weekly session.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around transdisciplinary units rather than subject syllabuses, so a parent often cannot tell from the report whether number fluency or reading stamina is the gap. Tutoring at this stage is diagnostic first: a tutor establishes where arithmetic automaticity, place value or written inference actually sits against age expectation, then builds twenty-minute practice blocks that do not look like more school.
programmes.countryNote: Jumeirah Park primary pupils often attend a British-curriculum school in the community and move to an IB continuum school later, which means an arrival into MYP from a Year 6 that never used criterion marking. Sessions in the final primary year are better spent on independent written explanation than on content.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP marks are awarded against four criteria per subject on a 1-8 scale, then converted to a 1-7 grade by a school-set boundary table. Students lose marks for process, not knowledge: an unlabelled graph, a missing evaluation of method, a conclusion that repeats the result. A tutor works criterion by criterion with the school's own task sheet in front of both of them.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-DP step is the sharpest transition in the Dubai system and it lands in Year 11. Jumeirah Park families who plan a move into Diploma at a school in Al Barsha or Jumeirah Village Triangle should use the final MYP year to build the algebraic fluency and lab-report discipline DP assumes on day one.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Final grades come from written papers sat in the May session for UAE schools, combined with internally assessed coursework. The workload problem is almost never one subject; it is four deadlines landing in the same fortnight with no revision plan behind them.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai DP candidates sit the May session, and the Internal Assessment deadlines set by the school typically fall a full year before that. A weekly session from the start of DP1 costs less in total than an emergency block in the spring of DP2, and it is the pattern most Jumeirah Park families settle into.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs at least two DP courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools and suits students who want a vocational spine with genuine IB subject rigour. Tutoring usually targets the DP courses inside it, plus the personal and professional skills portfolio, which students under-plan.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision in Dubai is thin and concentrated in a handful of schools, so a Jumeirah Park family on this route is often the only one in their street. That isolation is exactly where a specialist online tutor helps, because local word-of-mouth produces nobody who has taught the course.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-park.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects Jumeirah Park families ask for most often, with what each actually assesses. Levels are listed as the school teaches them, and a tutor is matched to the level, not to the subject in general.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most UAE engineering and economics applicants need. HL adds proof by induction, complex numbers in Cartesian and polar form, Maclaurin series and vector geometry. Marks go missing in Paper 1 where no calculator is available and algebraic manipulation has to be exact. An IB maths AA tutor in Dubai works Paper 1 under timed conditions from early DP1.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-active throughout, with statistics, regression, graph theory at HL and a modelling emphasis. Students who chose AI because AA looked harder still lose marks for the same reason: they describe a result rather than interpreting it in context. The IA here rewards a genuinely owned data set over a borrowed one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, waves, electricity and magnetism, atomic and nuclear physics, with HL extending into fields, induction and quantum phenomena. Paper 3 brings data analysis and an option topic. The commonest diagnosable failure is unit and significant-figure discipline in long-answer questions where the physics was actually right.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium, acids and bases, redox and organic chemistry, with HL adding spectroscopic identification and more quantitative equilibrium work. Organic mechanisms are where most students stall, because they memorise products instead of learning arrow-pushing. Practical data skills are assessed in Paper 3 and in the IA.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A content-heavy course where the mark is usually lost to command terms rather than recall. 'Outline', 'explain', 'evaluate' and 'distinguish' each demand a different answer shape, and examiner reports repeat this every session. Tutoring here is mostly answer construction against real mark schemes, plus statistics for the IA.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, with HL adding quantitative work and a longer paper. The Internal Assessment is three commentaries on published news articles, each 800 words, and students routinely pick articles that cannot carry a diagram. Choosing the article well is half the mark.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis, Paper 2 a comparative essay, plus the Individual Oral linking a global issue to two texts. HL adds the essay on a studied text. Students lose marks by summarising rather than analysing how meaning is constructed. Tutoring targets the thesis sentence and the line-level evidence.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Business organisation, human resource management, finance, marketing and operations, assessed partly through a research project. The quantitative sections, especially investment appraisal and cash-flow forecasting, catch out students who are strong writers. HL adds extension topics and a longer case study.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: System fundamentals, computer organisation, networks and computational thinking, with HL adding abstract data structures and resource management. The Internal Assessment is a working solution for a real client, and the commonest problem is scope: a project too ambitious to document properly in the word limit.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and IA support
subjects.description: TOK is an exhibition plus a prescribed-title essay; the Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent research piece with a supervisor. A tutor can teach research question design, argument structure and citation, and give feedback on the student's own drafts. A tutor cannot write any part of it, and we say so on the page.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Jumeirah Park actually means in practice
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Jumeirah Park, as the phrase is used locally, means one-to-one IB teaching arranged for a child who lives in this community rather than at a centre they have to be driven to. Most families who type it are not attached to the idea of someone in their living room; they are attached to the idea of not getting back into a car at 16:30. That distinction matters, because it is the whole reason online delivery works here.

IB Gram provides that one-to-one teaching as live online tutoring in Jumeirah Park. A tutor and a student meet on video at a fixed time, share a whiteboard and a past paper, and work. Nobody travels. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all; our in-person service exists only in India, and no page on this site will tell you otherwise.

The practical difference shows up in what you are choosing between. Hiring locally means choosing a tutor from the set of people who hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, teach your child's subject at your child's level, and can be at a villa in District 7 by 17:00 on a Tuesday. Those three conditions intersect in a very small number of people, and the intersection gets smaller the more specialised the subject. Choosing online removes the third condition entirely and leaves the two that affect the grade.

There is a second practical consequence, which is that the arrangement survives a house move, a change of school or a summer abroad without you having to start the search again. Jumeirah Park is a community people move within and out of, often at the end of an academic year, and an online tutor who already knows the student's weak topics is worth more in September than a new local tutor who has to begin again from nothing.

sections.heading: The Jumeirah Park school run, and when a session can realistically start
paragraphs: This is the part nobody publishes, and it is the single most useful thing on this page for a family here. Dubai private schools finish between roughly 14:30 and 15:30 depending on the school and the year group. What decides your tutoring slot is not the bell but the bus: a Jumeirah Park address on a route that also serves Al Barsha and Jumeirah Village adds twenty to forty minutes to that.

The table below sets out the pattern families in this community report, so you can see where your own household sits. Times are indicative and vary by route, year group and term, and your school's own transport office is the authority on your actual route. The useful column is the last one: the earliest slot at which a child is home, fed something and capable of thinking.

One detail worth knowing if you are new to the area: Jumeirah Park has no metro station inside it. The nearest Route 2020 stations are Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens, both of which require a car to reach, so public transport plays no part in a tutoring timetable here. Whatever happens after school happens by car or at home, which is why the afternoon window is as tight as it is.

The pattern that emerges is simple. Families whose children attend the school inside the community can genuinely hold a 16:00 slot. Everyone bussed outward is better off at 17:00 or 17:30, and Diploma students in DP2 often prefer 19:30 because they want to eat and decompress first. Booking the wrong slot is the commonest reason a tutoring arrangement quietly stops after five weeks.

sections.heading: Which schools this neighbourhood feeds, and what each implies for tutoring
paragraphs: Jumeirah Park is unusual in west Dubai because it has a school inside the gates, which skews the community towards the British curriculum in the primary and lower secondary years. The IB population here is largely secondary: students who moved into a continuum school in Al Barsha or Jumeirah Village, or who took IGCSE locally and then chose the Diploma over A Levels at sixteen.

That produces two distinct tutoring populations in the same postcode. One is MYP students needing criterion-based writing support in a system their parents never experienced. The other is DP1 and DP2 students needing HL subject depth and coursework discipline. They need different tutors, and a platform that treats both as 'IB tutoring' will match the wrong one.

The supply side is also moving. KHDA reported that Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. West Dubai absorbs a good share of that growth, so the school map around Jumeirah Park is not the one it was three years ago and will not be the one it is in three more.

Curriculum and programme information changes, and the regulator's own school listing is the place to confirm it before you enrol. sections.heading: What IB tutoring costs around Jumeirah Park, with the sources
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because that is the number that decides whether an arrangement survives a term. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring rate survey puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. A Jumeirah Park family taking two HL subjects at one session each is therefore planning for a four-figure monthly commitment, not a few hundred dirhams.

Working back to the hour, the published market in Dubai runs roughly as follows. EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52 at the budget online end. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270 for specialist work, Bestimate puts in-home visits at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at AED 200-500, and BartyED's premium examiner-led tier reaches AED 650. These are those providers' own published figures, read in October 2026.

None of these are IB Gram prices and this page does not publish one, because the right figure depends on subject, level and how many weeks are left. What we will say is where the money leaks: paying a travel premium for a generalist, buying a twenty-session package before testing the match, and starting Internal Assessment support three weeks before a deadline instead of three months. Begin with the free trial lesson and a consultation, then commit.

sections.heading: A home visit in Jumeirah Park versus the same hour online
paragraphs: Set the teaching aside for a moment and count what the two formats actually cost a household in this specific community. A tutor driving into Jumeirah Park from Al Barsha or Business Bay in the 17:00 peak is adding somewhere between forty and ninety minutes of round-trip travel to your hour. Somebody pays for that, either in the rate or in the tutor's willingness to keep the slot in week eleven.

The second cost is selection. Insisting on a home visit narrows the pool to tutors willing to make that drive, at that time, for that rate. In practice that means generalists, because a Physics HL specialist with full evenings has no reason to spend ninety minutes in traffic. The honest version of the trade-off is that a home visit buys you physical presence and costs you subject depth.

Against that, in-person has real advantages and it is worth naming them. A younger child who will not sit still on video genuinely does better with an adult in the room. Practical equipment handling is easier face to face. A household with no quiet room and no decent connection is not a good candidate for online lessons. The table below lays the comparison out so you can judge it against your own household rather than ours.

The third cost is continuity, and it is the one families underestimate. A home visit depends on the tutor's route still working in week twelve, after their own job changes or they take on a client in Mirdif. Slots held by travel tend to drift, then get cancelled, then quietly end. A slot held by nothing but a calendar entry is far harder to lose, and in exam term that reliability is worth more than the format debate.

sections.heading: The exam calendar counted backwards from a Jumeirah Park study desk
paragraphs: Dubai IB Diploma candidates sit the May session. Cambridge IGCSE and O Level candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. The February/March Cambridge series is offered to India only and is not an option for a UAE candidate, which matters because that mistake circulates widely in tutoring content.

The useful exercise is to count backwards. Nothing in the IB year is decided by the exam date; it is decided by the school's internal coursework deadlines, which sit roughly a year earlier. A DP2 student who has not chosen an Extended Essay research question by the autumn of DP1 is already behind, regardless of how good the revision plan looks in March.

Specific IB session and results dates are not published on this page. The IB's own site is the only authority and it blocks automated checking, so we will not restate a date that may have been revised. For Cambridge and Pearson the live official timetable is the reference, and your school's exams officer holds the zone-specific version. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong zone's timetable, so this is worth checking rather than assuming.

For an IGCSE sibling in the same household, the Pearson pattern is worth knowing as a worked example of how far ahead deadlines sit. The Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026. Entry deadlines sit months before any of that, and they are set by the school, not the board.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory UAE subjects, and the squeeze on the week
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Every Jumeirah Park family's school sits inside that system, is inspected on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and publishes its rating. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA and does not claim to be; we explain the regulator because parents ask, not because it endorses us.

The piece that affects your week is the mandatory-subject requirement. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required its current guidance to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject time on a forty-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that no mandatory lesson runs shorter than twenty-five minutes.

In an IB Diploma timetable that already carries six subjects, TOK, the Extended Essay and CAS, those additional periods are real pressure. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. For tutoring, the consequence is prioritisation: decide which subject the weekly hour goes to, and do not spread one hour across three.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what an IB tutor may and may not do
paragraphs: This is the shortest section with the highest stakes, so it is written plainly. A tutor may teach the content, explain the assessment criteria, help a student design a research question, teach referencing, and read and comment on work the student has written. A tutor may not write, part-write, rewrite to completion, or supply any portion of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, TOK essay or Personal Project.

That line exists because the consequence falls on the student, not the tutor. Submitting work that is not your own is a malpractice matter handled by the IB, and the outcome can reach the loss of the Diploma. There are operators in this market who sell completed Internal Assessments outright at four-figure prices. We will not, and a parent in Jumeirah Park comparing quotes should treat that offer as a warning rather than a service.

What good IA coaching looks like in practice is unglamorous. The tutor reads the student's draft with the published criterion descriptors open, says which descriptor band the work currently sits in and why, and names the specific thing missing: no evaluation of the method, an uncertainty never propagated, a conclusion that does not answer the research question. The student then goes and fixes it. That process produces both a better mark and a student who can do it again.

The same restraint applies to materials. We do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. A tutor will reference the official document and link to it, and your child's school already holds licensed access to the papers they need. Anyone offering you a drive full of exam material is offering you a copyright problem rather than a teaching advantage.

sections.heading: What happens when the right tutor is not free
paragraphs: Availability is the thing tutoring companies conceal, so here is ours. The scarce slots are weekday 17:00 to 19:00 GST in the spring term, and the scarce subjects are Physics HL, Chemistry HL, Maths AA HL and Computer Science. If you ask for all four conditions at once in March, there is a real chance the specialist you want has no free evening slot that week.

When that happens you get told, not managed. The options are a different time slot with the specialist you wanted, an immediate start with a strong generalist while the specialist's slot opens up, or a wait with a date attached. Some tutors covering UAE families are based outside the UAE and teach on Gulf Standard Time; where that applies we say so, because a parent is entitled to know who is teaching their child and from where.

The reason this is worth stating on a Jumeirah Park page specifically is that the local alternative has the same problem and hides it. A home-visit tutor who covers this community has a finite number of evening slots within driving distance, and when they are full the honest answer is also no. Online delivery does not abolish scarcity; it just means the constraint is the tutor's calendar rather than Al Khail Road.

If you are planning ahead, the way to avoid the problem entirely is to book the slot before you need it. Families who start a weekly session in September hold their 17:00 Tuesday for the whole year. Families who start in March take whatever is left. That is not a sales line; it is simply how a calendar of one-to-one slots fills, and it is the same for every provider in this market whether they admit it or not.
