process.title: Tell us the school, the subject and the level
process.description: The first conversation is short and specific. Which school, which year group, which subjects, HL or SL, and what the last report or mock actually said. A Jumeirah Park address tells us the likely bus timing; the school tells us the assessment calendar we will be working to.

process.title: Pick the slot that survives the school run
process.description: We set the weekly time around when your child is genuinely home and able to concentrate, using the arrival pattern in the table above. For most families here that is 16:30 or 17:30, and for DP2 students it is often after dinner. Getting this right is what makes the arrangement last.

process.description: One full session with the matched tutor before any payment. It is a real lesson on real material, not a sales call, and you get the tutor's written read of where your child actually is. If the match is wrong, say so and we change the tutor rather than asking you to persist.

process.description: After roughly six sessions there is enough evidence to judge. We look at marks on timed work rather than impressions, and decide whether to keep going weekly, add a second subject, shift to IA coaching, or stop. Stopping is a legitimate outcome and we would rather you did it deliberately.

faqs.question: Do your tutors come to homes in Jumeirah Park?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one IB tuition to Jumeirah Park families live online, over video, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; our in-person home-visit service runs in India only. We target the home-tutor phrase because it is what parents search, and we would rather tell you plainly than let you discover it after a deposit. If a tutor physically in the room is non-negotiable for your child, you need a local in-home provider and the market rate for that is roughly AED 180-500 per hour including travel.

faqs.question: What time can a session start if my child is bussed to Al Barsha?
faqs.answer: Plan for 17:00 at the earliest. Schools in Al Barsha and Al Barsha South typically finish between 15:00 and 15:30, and a bus route serving Jumeirah Park gets most children back between 16:00 and 16:40. Add time to eat and change and a 17:00 start is realistic, 17:30 more comfortable. Children at the school inside Jumeirah Park can genuinely hold a 16:00 slot. Diploma students in their second year often prefer 19:30, after dinner, because they concentrate better than they do at five o'clock. Your school's transport office has your actual route timings.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to spend per month on IB tutoring here?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Dubai rate survey puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Two HL subjects at one session each therefore sits in four figures monthly. Published hourly rates across the market run from AED 33-65 for budget online providers up to AED 650 at the premium examiner-led end. Those are other providers' figures, read in October 2026. faqs.question: Which IB schools do children from Jumeirah Park usually attend?
faqs.answer: Jumeirah Park has Dubai British School Jumeirah Park inside the community, which runs the British curriculum, so the local IB population is mostly secondary students who travel out. The nearby IB schools families most often name are Nord Anglia International School Dubai and Dubai Heights Academy in Al Barsha South, Dubai International Academy Al Barsha and GEMS World Academy Dubai in Al Barsha, Sunmarke School in Jumeirah Village Triangle, Emirates International School Meadows, and Raffles World Academy in Umm Suqeim. We have no affiliation with any of them; they are named as context. Confirm current programmes on KHDA's own school listing.

faqs.question: Is online IB tutoring actually as effective as having someone in the room?
faqs.answer: For Middle Years and Diploma students, in our experience it is at least as effective, because the thing that drives the grade is the tutor's command of the syllabus and the mark scheme rather than their physical presence. A shared screen with a past paper on it is arguably better than two people leaning over one sheet of paper. The honest exceptions are young children who cannot sustain attention on video, households with no quiet room, and equipment-heavy practical work. If your child is in one of those categories, say so at the consultation.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child with the IB Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can teach the assessment criteria, help narrow a research question, teach method and referencing, and read and comment on drafts your child has written. A tutor cannot write, part-write or rewrite any of it, and will not. Submitting work that is not the student's own is a malpractice matter the IB handles, and the consequences land on the student. Operators in this market do sell completed Internal Assessments; treat that as a reason to avoid them. Good IA coaching reads the student's draft against the published descriptors and names what is missing.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in the UAE need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. u.ae states that individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so be sceptical of any figure quoted to you.

faqs.question: When do IB and IGCSE students in Dubai actually sit their exams?
faqs.answer: Dubai IB Diploma candidates sit the May session. Cambridge IGCSE and O Level candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series; the February/March series is offered to India only and is not available here, which is a mistake you will see repeated in tutoring content. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Exact dates change and are zone-specific for Cambridge, so use the live official timetable and your school's exams officer rather than any date on a tutoring page, including this one.

faqs.question: My child is moving from MYP into the Diploma next year. What should we do now?
faqs.answer: Use the final MYP year for the two things the Diploma assumes on day one: algebraic fluency and disciplined written explanation. Content gaps are fixable in DP1; habits are not. For intended HL sciences that means lab reports with a real evaluation of method and propagated uncertainties. For Maths AA it means non-calculator algebra done fast and exactly, because Paper 1 allows no calculator. A term of weekly sessions through the summer before DP1 does more for the final grade than the same hours spent in the spring of DP2.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest to find a specialist for in this area?
faqs.answer: Physics HL, Chemistry HL, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL, and Computer Science. These are the subjects where a generalist tutor runs out of depth about four weeks in, and they are also the ones where a home-visit requirement hurts most, because the pool of people who can both teach them and drive to a Jumeirah Park villa at 17:00 is very small. Online matching removes the travel condition, which is why we can usually staff them. In the spring term even then there can be a wait, and we will tell you the length of it.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan or school holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families change them. During Ramadan school hours shorten and households often prefer a late-morning slot or a post-Iftar session, and we reschedule to whichever works. Over the summer and winter breaks families frequently either pause entirely or switch to a short intensive block, especially before the Diploma's second year. If you travel, sessions can follow you to another time zone as long as we know the week before. Rescheduling is a slot swap, not a renegotiation, because no tutor has to travel anywhere.

faqs.question: What exactly happens in the free trial session before we commit?
faqs.answer: It is a full-length session with the tutor who would actually teach your child, on material from their current course, with no card details taken. The tutor spends the first part finding out what the student can do rather than what they have covered, then teaches. Afterwards you get a short written read: where the student actually sits, what the first six weeks would target, and what frequency makes sense. If the match is wrong, we change the tutor. The point is to test the pairing before you commit to a term of it.

faqs.question: Does my child's school inspection rating tell me anything about tutoring needs?
faqs.answer: A little, but less than parents expect. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes the result, and a strong rating does tell you the school is well run. It tells you almost nothing about whether your particular child is secure in Chemistry HL equilibrium calculations. Use the published rating when choosing a school and use your child's own marked work when deciding about tutoring. We read the school report and the last timed paper, not the inspection band.

faqs.question: How do I know the tutor is any good before I pay?
faqs.answer: Judge three things in the trial lesson. Did the tutor diagnose rather than lecture, meaning did they find out what your child can actually do? Could they talk fluently about the mark scheme and where marks are lost in that specific subject at that specific level? Did your child talk, or just listen? A tutor who cannot name the paper weightings for the course they are teaching is not a specialist. Be wary of anyone promising a grade: nobody can guarantee an outcome, and the offer tells you something about the operator.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two of my child's IB subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking. Maths and Physics pair naturally, as do Chemistry and Biology at Standard Level, and a single tutor across two subjects gives you one person who sees the whole workload and can tell you which deadline to prioritise. At Higher Level we usually resist it, because genuine HL depth in two sciences is rare and a tutor stretched across both tends to be strong in one. For a Jumeirah Park family juggling slots, two tutors on two fixed evenings is usually easier than one tutor on a double.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-park.closingHeading: Start with the timetable, then the tutor
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-park.closingBody: If you are searching for an IB home tutor in Jumeirah Park, work out your real session window first. Find out when the bus actually reaches your district, decide whether your child works better at half past four or half past seven, and then look for the tutor who fits that slot and knows the syllabus at the level your child is sitting it. Take the free trial lesson before paying for anything, ask the tutor to name the paper weightings for the course, and tell us the school and the subject rather than just the year group. Lessons run live online, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: The same enquiry gets a different answer in September and in February
paragraphs: Jumeirah Village Circle generates more tuition enquiries than most Dubai communities, partly because of its size and partly because it is full of families who moved recently and are still working out how the Diploma behaves. The enquiry is almost always the same: my child needs an IB home tutor, what does it cost. The useful reply is a question back. Which term are we in, and what has already been submitted?

The reason is that the Diploma is a two-year machine with deadlines that mostly belong to the school rather than to the board. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment, marked by the teacher and externally moderated, and the school sets its drafting and submission dates months before the examinations. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, together worth up to three of the 45 available points, run on their own internal timelines. By the time the papers arrive, a large share of the grade is already fixed.

So a September enquiry and a February enquiry are different problems. In the first term of Year 12, almost everything is still available: subject and level choices, the Extended Essay research question, the Internal Assessment topic, and the habit of attempting problems unaided. By the second term of Year 13, the Internal Assessments are submitted or nearly so, the core is done, and what remains is examination technique on papers. That is still worth a great deal — technique genuinely moves grades in eight weeks — but it is a narrower job and it should be priced and planned as one.

Which brings in the second thing this page does. Your URL says home tutor, and that is what parents in Jumeirah Village Circle search, so it is answered honestly: what in-home tuition costs in this market, what the travel premium buys, and how families here actually choose. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE — in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. Stated here rather than after an invoice.

There is a supply consequence to all this that nobody mentions at the point of sale. Rates in Dubai do not move seasonally, but availability does. In the weeks before the May session every Diploma family in the emirate wants the same Higher Level specialists at the same two evening hours, so a family that books in September chooses its tutor and its slot, and a family that books in March accepts whatever is left. That is the strongest argument for acting early, and it has nothing to do with price.

The rest of the page is the calendar in usable form. The Diploma year counted backwards. What eight weeks, four weeks and two weeks can each still achieve. How Internal Assessment season behaves in a household with two children. Where Ramadan and the UAE term structure fall against revision. And what to do if you are reading this in February and worrying that you have left it too late.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-village-.programmesIntro: Jumeirah Village Circle families arrive with children in all three IB programmes, and the calendar pressure sits in a different place in each. Knowing which clock is running changes what the next month should contain.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher and Standard Level, each marked out of 7, plus up to three points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, to a maximum of 45. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment on the school's timetable. The calendar runs hardest here: the first term of Year 12 sets the Extended Essay question, the second sets Internal Assessment topics, and Year 13 is submission and examination technique.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. We publish no IB examination or results dates on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and an unchecked date in front of a parent is worse than none; get yours from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org. What governs your planning locally is the school's own Internal Assessment calendar, which is published and which most families never ask for.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria lettered A to D, with the Personal Project in the final year. There is no external paper in most schools, so the calendar is a rolling series of classroom tasks rather than a build towards one date. The implication is that help is useful at any point in the year, and that there is rarely a reason to rush.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Middle Years timetable also carries Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, mandatory in all private schools under KHDA requirements. For a Jumeirah Village Circle family that is real additional load, and it argues for short targeted blocks rather than standing weekly commitments across several subjects.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: Together worth up to three points, and run on school-set internal deadlines spread across both Diploma years. The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent piece with a school supervisor; Theory of Knowledge comprises an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay. Both are won at the question-framing stage, which happens far earlier than most families realise.
programmes.countryNote: The practical consequence for a Jumeirah Village Circle household is that a Year 12 student should be having the Extended Essay conversation in the first term, not the third. A badly framed research question is not rescuable in the final months, and that is the single most common reason core points are lost rather than earned.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-village-.subjectsIntro: Different subjects sit on different internal clocks, because their Internal Assessments take different amounts of calendar time. These are the courses Jumeirah Village Circle families ask about most, with a note on when the pressure arrives.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and the Higher Level Paper 3 investigation. The exploration is written over weeks rather than months, so its pressure arrives later than in the sciences, but Paper 3 preparation needs dedicated time in the second half of Year 13.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and, at Higher Level, graph theory. The exploration here depends on data the student must find or generate, which means the topic decision needs making earlier than students expect to avoid a scramble.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity, with the scientific investigation requiring laboratory access on the school's schedule. That dependency makes chemistry the subject where the calendar bites hardest: the design has to be right before the lab session, not after.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields, waves and quantum physics, with the same laboratory dependency as chemistry. Data analysis and uncertainty work can be done at any point in the year and is usually left far too late.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and continuity. Investigations often involve organisms or fieldwork, which adds seasonal and logistical constraints that students discover only when they try to collect data.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, the Individual Oral and, at Higher Level, the HL Essay. The Individual Oral is a scheduled performance, so it has a hard date in the school calendar and rewards rehearsal in the weeks before it.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A three-commentary Internal Assessment portfolio, each commentary tied to a news article from a specified window. That window is a genuine calendar constraint: students who leave it late cannot use the articles they wanted.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Structured response plus a research project requiring access to an organisation. The access is the bottleneck, and it has to be arranged weeks before the writing, which is why this project slips more often than any other.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay. Prescribed titles are released ahead of the session, so the essay has a fixed window, and the exhibition sits on a school-set date in Year 12 that families rarely see coming.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent piece with a school supervisor and a series of school-set reflection sessions. Won or lost at the question-framing stage in the first term of Year 12, and the hardest component to rescue late.

sections.heading: The Diploma year counted backwards
paragraphs: The calendar is almost always described forwards, which is why families act late. Counted backwards it is obvious what is still available. The examination is a fixed point. Internal Assessment submissions sit months in front of it, set by the school. Drafts sit weeks in front of those. Extended Essay reflection sessions sit across both years on the school's own schedule. Subject and level choices sit at the very start, and once made they are the hardest thing of all to change.

A Jumeirah Village Circle parent should therefore ask the school for one document: the published Internal Assessment and core deadline calendar for their child's cohort. Most schools produce it and most families never request it. It is the single most useful piece of paper in the Diploma, because it tells you exactly which months are already committed and which are free.

The second thing worth noting is that the board's own deadlines are invisible to you. Entry deadlines are handled by the school's examinations officer and sit months before the papers. We publish no IB examination or results dates on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and we will not put an unchecked date in front of a parent; take yours from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org directly.

The table below is the shape of the two years as a sequence of what-should-be-done-by-then rather than as dates. Find your current position in the left-hand column, and the rightmost column tells you what a tutor can realistically affect from here.

sections.heading: What eight weeks, four weeks and two weeks can each achieve
paragraphs: Families in Jumeirah Village Circle frequently ring with a specific number of weeks left and a reasonable question: is it worth it. The honest answer varies sharply with the number, and it is worth being precise rather than encouraging.

Eight weeks is a real window. It is enough to sit each paper under timed conditions more than once, mark it properly, and fix the three or four recurring technique errors that cost most students a grade boundary: missing method lines, command terms answered loosely, data-booklet or formula-booklet unfamiliarity, extended responses that tangle three creditable points into one sentence. Eight weeks is not enough to teach two missing Higher Level topics and polish technique at the same time, and a provider promising both is selling optimism.

Four weeks narrows it to technique alone, plus securing recallable marks — the qualitative analysis tests in chemistry, half-life calculations, genetics question shapes, the finite rule sets. That is genuinely useful and it should be priced as a short block, not as the start of a relationship.

Two weeks is triage. The useful work is paper-sitting under timed conditions with marking, so the student stops losing marks to process rather than knowledge, and a decision about which topics to abandon. Telling a student what not to revise is one of the more valuable things a specialist can do at that point, and it is rarely what a family expects to pay for.

Beyond twelve weeks the question stops being interesting, because almost nothing is out of reach. That is precisely why the early-year block is the one we push hardest and the one families almost never buy.

sections.heading: The home-tutor question, answered properly
paragraphs: Jumeirah Village Circle is dense and central, which makes it one of the easier Dubai communities for an in-home tutor to reach. So the honest version of this section is not that home tutoring is impractical here; it is that it costs more and narrows your choice of tutor, and that the second effect matters more than the first.

On cost: in-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are advertised at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, with a rate survey putting the band at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to AED 500. One provider publishes monthly packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions against AED 799 for eight online sessions. A qualified subject tutor working online is advertised at AED 150 to AED 300. Those are market figures from the providers named, researched in October 2026, not IB Gram prices.

On choice: the pool of tutors willing to drive to a specific address at a specific hour is far smaller than the pool who teach a specific course. For Standard Level subjects that may not matter. For Higher Level Chemistry, Physics or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, it matters a great deal, because the number of people who teach those courses to examination standard is small to begin with.

IB Gram resolves it by removing the travel entirely. Lessons are one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, and we do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. The calendar advantage is concrete: when an Internal Assessment deadline moves, or a mock week lands, a video session can be rearranged inside the same week without a round trip having to be renegotiated.

sections.heading: Internal Assessment season in a Jumeirah Village Circle household
paragraphs: There is a period, usually spanning the third term of Year 12 and the first term of Year 13, when every subject's Internal Assessment deadline arrives within a few weeks of every other. A student with six subjects faces six pieces of independent work, each with a school-set draft date, while also being taught new content. This is where households come apart, and it is entirely predictable from the school's own calendar.

The practical response is sequencing rather than more hours. Get the published deadline calendar, lay the six deadlines out, and identify which pieces depend on something outside the student's control: laboratory access for the sciences, an organisation for a Business Management project, articles from a specified window for Economics commentaries, data collection for a Mathematics exploration. Those are the ones to start first, because an external dependency that fails cannot be recovered by working harder.

Where a tutor helps most is at the front of each piece: interrogating the research question, checking that a method will generate analysable data, confirming the mathematics is at the level of the course. Three sessions spread across the right three weeks is worth more than ten in the fortnight before submission, and it costs less.

The boundary matters most in exactly this period, because the pressure is highest. A tutor may teach content, explain each criterion, question a research question, mark a draft against criteria and say which criterion is losing marks, and teach referencing. A tutor may not write any part of the work, rewrite prose, supply a finished question, provide data the student did not collect, or edit to completion. Our tutors decline requests that cross that line. One operator in this market was found advertising completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; buying one is malpractice and the consequence falls on the student.

sections.heading: Ramadan, terms and holidays against the revision calendar
paragraphs: The UAE academic year runs in three terms from late August to early July, with a winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break in the second half of the year. For a Diploma student those breaks are not neutral: the winter break sits close to Internal Assessment drafting for many subjects, and the spring break sits inside the run-up to the May session. How a family uses them makes a measurable difference.

Ramadan adds a second layer. School days shorten, evenings restructure around Iftar, and energy patterns change for the whole household, including for students who are not fasting. Because Ramadan moves earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, in the current period it falls in the part of the year when Diploma revision is at its most intense. Planning around it rather than being surprised by it is simply better practice.

What works, in our experience with Dubai families: shift sessions to post-Iftar, keep them shorter, and move the heaviest cognitive work — timed papers, Higher Level problem sets — to weekend mornings during that month. Online delivery makes all of that administratively trivial, because nothing has to be renegotiated with a driver or a travel schedule.

The holidays themselves are the most underused resource in the Diploma. A student who does four or five sessions across a winter break, working on an Internal Assessment draft or a weak topic, gains a term's worth of ground without competing with homework. Families almost never plan it, because holidays feel like time off, and then February arrives with the same gap still open.

sections.heading: What IB tuition costs, and when demand spikes
paragraphs: Rates in this market are published by format and tutor category rather than by season, but availability is seasonal and it affects what you can actually buy. Published Dubai rates for a qualified subject tutor working online run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level provision is quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, one UK-based agency publishing AED 270, and premium named or examiner-led provision as high as AED 650. Budget online tuition, typically a university student, is advertised from AED 45 to AED 150.

The seasonal effect is on supply, not price. In the eight weeks before the May session, every Diploma family in Dubai wants the same Higher Level specialists at the same two or three evening hours. A family that books in September has a choice of tutors and slots; a family that books in March takes what is free. That is the strongest practical argument for the early-year foundation block, and it has nothing to do with rates.

On monthly figures: independent estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. One provider publishes AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Every figure here was read from the provider's own published page in October 2026.

Our own fee is quoted after a free trial lesson, because the honest number depends on how many weeks are left and what the marked work shows. For budget context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion, so fees are the fixed line this year and tuition is the variable.

sections.heading: If you are reading this in February
paragraphs: This section exists because most people reach a page like this late, and a page that only addresses September enquiries is not much use. If you are in the second term of Year 13, here is the honest position. The Internal Assessments are submitted or nearly so, so roughly a fifth of each subject grade is already determined. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are done or close, so the core points are what they are. What remains is the external papers, and they are worth the large majority of the grade.

That is genuinely good news, because examination technique is the most improvable thing in the Diploma and the fastest to move. A student losing marks to missing method lines, loose command-term responses, formula-booklet unfamiliarity and tangled extended responses can recover a meaningful amount in eight weeks, and those four errors are visible in a single marked mock.

What will not work is attempting to teach missing content and improve technique simultaneously in the same eight weeks. If a Higher Level student is two topics behind, the choice is to secure the rest and accept a ceiling for this session, or to work on the missing topics and leave the technique errors in place. A specialist should tell you which trade they are making and why, and should be willing to say that one of the six subjects is beyond rescue this session.

The other thing available in February is the honest conversation about a November session or a university plan that does not depend on this specific points total. Neither is a failure, and both are better decided in February than in July. We will have that conversation rather than selling a schedule that was never going to fit.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to tutor, and what nobody is approved for
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own listing for issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no figure can honestly be quoted and we do not quote one.

A boundary that becomes tempting precisely when the calendar tightens: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. That is press-reported and should be verified against the current ADEK policy document before being relied on as exact wording. Whatever the precise text, do not approach your child's own teacher privately in Internal Assessment season.

And what nobody holds. A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs an Educational Services Permit for a training institute from KHDA. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE office or centre, and is not accredited, licensed, approved by or partnered with KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We also do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; tutors reference and link to the official source.

process.title: Tell us the date, not just the subject
process.description: Which term, what has been submitted, and when the next school deadline falls. A September enquiry and a February enquiry get different plans, different session counts and different prices, and a provider who does not ask is about to sell you the same package either way.

process.title: Get the school's deadline calendar
process.description: Most schools publish an Internal Assessment and core deadline schedule for each cohort and most families never request it. Send it to us. It shows which months are already committed and which are free, and it turns a vague worry into a sequence of dated tasks.

process.title: Send one marked paper or draft
process.description: A marked mock shows the technique errors in twenty minutes; a returned Internal Assessment draft with criterion feedback shows exactly which criterion is costing marks. Either is worth more than a conversation, and together they determine the realistic session count.

process.title: Take the free trial on a real problem
process.description: You and your child meet the proposed specialist over live video. Hand them the lost question or the criterion feedback. Afterwards you get their read, a plan sized to the weeks remaining, and the fee. No payment is needed to reach that point.

process.title: Set the stop date with the plan
process.description: Every block gets an end: a named deadline, a mock, or study leave. In a calendar-driven course that discipline matters more than in most, because an arrangement with no end quietly becomes a monthly cost nobody reviews while the deadlines that mattered pass anyway.

whyPoints.title: The plan is sized to the weeks remaining
whyPoints.description: Twelve weeks, eight weeks and two weeks are different jobs, and we will tell you plainly what each can and cannot achieve. A provider offering the same weekly package whatever the date is not planning; they are selling a subscription against a fixed deadline.

whyPoints.title: We ask for the school's deadline calendar
whyPoints.description: The real deadlines in the Diploma are set by the school, not the board, and most families have never seen their own cohort's schedule. Working from it is the difference between sequencing six Internal Assessments and discovering them one panic at a time.

whyPoints.title: Honest about late starts
whyPoints.description: If you are in February with two Higher Level topics missing, we will say that securing the rest and accepting a ceiling is the realistic plan, and that one subject may be beyond rescue this session. That conversation loses bookings and is more useful than a schedule that cannot work.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, stated before booking
whyPoints.description: Lessons are live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram makes no home visits in the UAE; in-person home tutoring exists only in our India service. The calendar benefit is real: a session moves inside the same week when a deadline shifts, with no round trip to renegotiate.

whyPoints.title: The coursework line holds under pressure
whyPoints.description: Internal Assessment season is when requests cross the line, and that is exactly when it matters. Tutors teach, question, mark against published criteria and give feedback on the student's own work. They never write, rewrite or complete it, and they will decline.

whyPoints.title: Attributed figures and no guarantees
whyPoints.description: Every AED rate here belongs to the provider or survey that published it, with the research date stated, and our fee follows the trial. No guaranteed grades, no satisfaction percentages without a sample size and method, and no self-asserted ratings.

faqs.question: Can an IB home tutor come to our apartment in Jumeirah Village Circle?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We teach Jumeirah Village Circle students one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, and we make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Independent in-home tutors do work here, and published market rates run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel. Dropping the visit widens the tutor pool from those willing to drive to the Circle at a given hour to everyone who teaches your child's exact course.

faqs.question: We are already in the second term of Year 13. Is it worth starting now?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a narrower aim. By that point the Internal Assessments are submitted or nearly so and the core is done, so roughly a fifth of each subject grade is fixed. What remains is the external papers, which carry the large majority of the grade and are the most improvable part of the Diploma. Eight weeks is enough to sit each paper timed, mark it properly, and fix the three or four recurring technique errors that cost a grade boundary. It is not enough to teach missing content as well.

faqs.question: What should I ask my child's school for before hiring anyone?
faqs.answer: The published Internal Assessment and core deadline calendar for your child's cohort. Most Dubai schools produce one and most families never request it. It shows when each subject's draft and final submissions fall, when the Theory of Knowledge exhibition sits, and when the Extended Essay reflection sessions happen. With that document a vague worry becomes a dated sequence, and you can see immediately which months are already committed and which are genuinely free for tuition.

faqs.question: Which Internal Assessments should my child start first?
faqs.answer: The ones that depend on something outside their control. Laboratory access for the sciences, because the school controls the timetable. An organisation for a Business Management research project, because access has to be arranged. Articles from a specified window for Economics commentaries, because late students cannot use the pieces they wanted. Data collection for a Mathematics exploration. Those dependencies cannot be recovered by working harder later, whereas a purely written component can be compressed if it has to be.

faqs.question: How early should the Extended Essay question be settled?
faqs.answer: In the first term of Year 12, before the first school reflection session if possible. The Extended Essay is won at the question-framing stage: a question narrow enough that available evidence can actually answer it makes the writing straightforward, and a badly framed one is the single most common reason core points are lost rather than earned. It is also the component that is hardest to rescue late, because the research has usually been done by the time anyone notices the question was wrong.

faqs.question: Do sessions need to stop during mock exam weeks?
faqs.answer: Usually pause rather than stop, and it should be planned rather than improvised. In mock weeks a student's time is better spent on the school's own schedule than on an extra session, with one exception: a single session spent marking a mock they have just sat, against the scheme, is often the most valuable hour of the term. After mocks is also the right moment to review the whole arrangement, because a marked set of six papers is the clearest diagnostic information you will get all year.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan affect a Diploma revision plan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: School days shorten, evenings restructure around Iftar, and the whole household's energy pattern changes, including for students who are not fasting. Because Ramadan moves earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, in the current period it falls in the part of the year when Diploma revision is heaviest. What works is shifting sessions to post-Iftar, keeping them shorter, and moving the heaviest work — timed papers and Higher Level problem sets — to weekend mornings for that month. Online delivery makes the rearrangement trivial.

faqs.question: Should we use the winter break for tuition?
faqs.answer: It is the most underused resource in the whole Diploma. Four or five sessions across a winter break, spent on an Internal Assessment draft or a specific weak topic, gains a term's worth of ground without competing with homework or school deadlines. Families rarely plan it because holidays feel like time off, and then February arrives with the same gap still open. The same applies to the spring break, which sits inside the run-up to the May session and is therefore even more valuable.

faqs.question: Does it cost more to book a tutor close to the exams?
faqs.answer: Not in rate, but it costs you in choice. Published Dubai rates do not move seasonally: a qualified subject tutor online is advertised at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour and specialist IB provision at AED 200 to AED 450 and above throughout the year. What changes is supply. In the eight weeks before the May session every Diploma family in Dubai wants the same Higher Level specialists at the same two evening hours, so a family booking in September chooses and a family booking in March accepts.

faqs.question: How many points can realistically move in one term?
faqs.answer: We will not put a number on that, and you should be wary of anyone who does. What can be said is where movement comes from: technique errors recovered on papers, one weak topic repaired, and criterion-level improvement on a draft that has not yet been submitted. What cannot move is a submitted Internal Assessment or a completed Extended Essay. Any provider promising a specific points gain is making a claim they cannot support, and grade guarantees are something we neither offer nor believe in.

faqs.question: Is it better to tutor one subject properly or three a bit?
faqs.answer: One, nearly always, and the reason is the calendar rather than the money. A student needs unaided practice between sessions, and that attempt is where the learning happens. With six Diploma subjects, Internal Assessment deadlines and academies in nearby Dubai Sports City, three weekly tuition slots leave no room for it. Pick the subject that most affects the overall total or the university plan, run a block, review at the next assessment, and then decide whether a second subject is needed.

faqs.question: What happens if a school deadline moves after we have booked?
faqs.answer: The session moves, usually inside the same week. This is the clearest practical advantage of video delivery for a calendar-driven course: nothing has to be renegotiated with a driver or a travel schedule, so when a draft deadline shifts or an unexpected mock appears, the week reshuffles. Schools in Dubai do adjust internal dates, particularly around Ramadan and the spring break, so an arrangement that can absorb that without lost sessions is worth more than it sounds in September.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an Internal Assessment draft that is already written?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a firm boundary, and less usefully than help at the start. A tutor can mark the draft against the published criteria, say which criterion is losing marks and why, point out that a conclusion is not supported by the data, and teach referencing properly. A tutor cannot rewrite the prose, write any new section, supply data the student did not collect, or edit it to completion. Our tutors decline requests that cross that line, and keeping the dated session notes protects the student if authenticity is ever queried.

faqs.question: What if no specialist is free in the weeks we need?
faqs.answer: You get the realistic wait and the specialist's location rather than a substitute. Availability is tightest in the eight weeks before the May session, which is when most families ring, and thinnest for Higher Level Physics, Computer Science and Theory of Knowledge support. In the meantime we can often run a useful adjacent block — data analysis, a marking session on a mock — with a different specialist. Where the available tutor is based outside the UAE, we say so, including the time zone, before any payment.

Add the school's published Internal Assessment schedule and one marked paper, and we will tell you what the remaining weeks can realistically achieve and what they cannot. Then you meet the proposed specialist in a free trial lesson over live video and decide. No home visits in the UAE, no promised points, and no figure on this page we cannot attribute to its source.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-village-.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects for students at schools around Jumeirah Village Triangle, Dubai Sports City and the Dubailand communities. Each one teaches a named syllabus rather than a general subject, and the first lesson is a free diagnostic session.

intro.heading: Start from the syllabus, not from the postcode
paragraphs: Jumeirah Village Triangle sits between Al Khail Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, a grid of villa clusters and low-rise apartments wrapped around three district parks. Families here send children to Sunmarke School and Arcadia Global School inside the community, and to JESS Arabian Ranches, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, GEMS Metropole and Fairgreen International School within a short drive. Several of those schools run the IB Diploma; several run IGCSE first and split at sixteen. That mix is why an IB home tutor in Jumeirah Village Triangle gets asked for so often, and why the request is almost never about the whole Diploma.

It is about one component. A Chemistry HL student is losing marks on Paper 2 extended response because they write mechanisms without curly arrows. A Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL student can differentiate but cannot read what Paper 1 is asking when the question says 'hence' rather than 'hence or otherwise'. A Biology student has a 12-page Internal Assessment and a Criterion D score of 2 out of 6 because the evaluation discusses human error instead of the limitations of the method. None of those problems are solved by a tutor who happens to live four minutes away in Jumeirah Village Circle. They are solved by somebody who has marked that component.

So this page is built the other way round from most tutoring pages. Rather than describing a neighbourhood, it sets out what the IB actually assesses: the papers, the percentages, the criterion letters, the word limits and the places where students in Dubai schools reliably lose marks. Where a figure appears, it carries the source it came from. Where something could not be verified — IB session dates, which ibo.org blocks automated checking of — the page says so instead of inventing one.

The delivery model is stated plainly at the top because it changes what you should expect. Tuition for UAE families runs one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and a recording the student keeps. IB Gram does not operate home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. The practical consequence is that a Triangle family is choosing from a pool of IB subject specialists rather than from the handful of tutors willing to drive into JVT at 17:30 on a weekday, and a Physics HL specialist is worth considerably more to a Year 13 student than geographical closeness.

What follows is the detail: subject-by-subject assessment structures, a mark-loss diagnosis table, the AED bands the Dubai market actually charges, a direct comparison between a home visit and an online session in this specific community, the Cambridge and Pearson examination calendar counted backwards from results day, the KHDA position on school inspection and mandatory subjects, and the academic-honesty line that separates teaching from malpractice. Fourteen questions at the end answer the things parents ask on the phone before booking anything.
If you want the short version: identify the component, not the subject. Then find somebody who knows that component's mark scheme. Everything else on this page is support for that one sentence.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-village-.programmesIntro: The IB runs as four separate programmes, and a Jumeirah Village Triangle parent usually needs only the one their child is in. The differences matter because the assessment model changes completely between them: PYP and MYP are internally assessed against published criteria, while the Diploma is externally examined.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around six transdisciplinary themes rather than subject timetables, and there are no external examinations. Assessment is teacher-led and continuous, ending in the Year 6 Exhibition — a student-driven inquiry presented to the school community. Tutoring at this stage is about underlying fluency: number bonds, written methods, reading stamina and the habit of explaining reasoning aloud. A tutor who tries to teach a PYP child content in exam-style blocks is working against the programme.
programmes.countryNote: Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City and Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park both run the PYP within reach of Jumeirah Village Triangle, and both are inspected by KHDA on the same six-band scale as every other Dubai private school. Parents in the Triangle often ask for PYP support in English writing, where the gap between spoken fluency and written structure is widest in a multilingual community.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses eight subject groups against four criteria each, lettered A to D, every one marked out of 8 and converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. In Mathematics the criteria are Knowing and understanding, Investigating patterns, Communicating, and Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Most mark loss in MYP is in Criterion C or D, where students solve the problem correctly and then fail to communicate or contextualise it. The programme ends with the Personal Project, assessed against its own criteria.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-Diploma transition is the most common reason a Jumeirah Village Triangle family calls in Year 11. MYP mathematics does not drill algebraic manipulation the way IGCSE does, so a student arriving in DP1 on Analysis and Approaches often has strong reasoning and weak fluency. That gap is closable in roughly eight to twelve sessions if it is identified before the first DP1 internal assessment, and considerably harder afterwards.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject is graded 1-7, with up to three bonus points from the TOK and EE combination, giving a 45-point maximum. Every subject carries an internally assessed component worth 20-25%, and the rest is externally examined. The grade is a weighted sum of components, which is why diagnosing the weak component matters more than general revision.
programmes.countryNote: JESS Arabian Ranches, Nord Anglia International School Dubai and North London Collegiate School Dubai all offer the Diploma within a reasonable drive of the Triangle, and Dubai added three new IB-curriculum private schools for the 2026-27 intake as part of 16,846 new places across seven openings. UAE candidates sit the May session; IB session and results dates are not published on this page because ibo.org blocks automated verification and a wrong date is worse than none.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a four-part core covering personal and professional skills, service learning and language development. It is far rarer than the Diploma in the UAE but appears in a small number of Dubai schools. Tutoring demand concentrates on the Diploma subjects taken within it and on the reflective project, which is marked against its own criteria rather than examined.
programmes.countryNote: Because CP cohorts in Dubai are small, a family in Jumeirah Village Triangle looking for CP support will almost never find a locally resident tutor who has taught that exact combination. This is the clearest case for online delivery: the pool that matters is the pool of people who have taught the course, not the pool within driving distance of Al Khail Road.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-village-.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects most requested by families around Jumeirah Village Triangle, with what each component actually tests and where the marks go missing. Weightings are from the published IB subject guides; levels are listed because the paper structure differs between them.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which is where most of the damage happens: students who rely on a GDC for sketching and solving lose marks on curve behaviour and exact values. HL adds Paper 3, a two-question extended investigation worth 20% of the grade and unlike anything in the textbook. The Exploration carries 20% at both levels.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-permitted throughout, statistics-heavy, and routinely underestimated. The common failure is treating AI as the easier route and then meeting hypothesis testing, chi-squared and regression with no statistical vocabulary. HL AI includes graph theory and matrices. Check the degree prerequisite before choosing: several engineering programmes specify AA.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 splits into multiple choice and data analysis; Paper 2 is extended response; HL Paper 3 covers experimental technique and an option topic. Marks are lost in explanation questions where students describe what happens instead of naming the law and applying it, and in uncertainty work, where propagation rules are half-remembered.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics carry the most lost marks. Examiners want curly arrows drawn from the correct electron source, lone pairs shown, and intermediates charged correctly. Bonding questions reward precise language about intermolecular forces. The Internal Assessment is 20%, and weak evaluations cost more than weak data.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem, not difficulty. Students who can recite a process often cannot answer a command term like 'distinguish' or 'outline' within the mark allocation. Data-based questions in Paper 2 reward reading the axes before the question. HL adds depth in plant biology, genetics and physiology.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks on their own: correctly labelled axes, shifted curves, and the new equilibrium marked. The three internally assessed commentaries use real published articles and are capped at 800 words each. HL adds quantitative Paper 3, where arithmetic slips cost more than theory gaps.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is guided textual analysis of unseen non-literary texts; Paper 2 is a comparative essay on studied works. HL adds the 1,200-1,500 word HL Essay. The Individual Oral links a global issue to one literary and one non-literary extract, and most students under-prepare the extract selection rather than the talking.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-based answers win marks: Ansoff, Boston Matrix, break-even and ratio analysis applied to the stimulus rather than described. HL Paper 3 responds to a social-enterprise case. The Internal Assessment differs by level, and students often pick a company they cannot get real data on.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper 1 covers systems fundamentals and computational thinking; Paper 2 is databases, modelling and simulation, or similar option content. The Solution — a working program with documented design — is internally assessed. Pseudocode conventions in the IB's own notation trip up students who only write Python.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Two assessed pieces: the exhibition of three objects with a 950-word maximum commentary, and a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title. TOK contributes up to three bonus points with the Extended Essay. Students lose marks by writing about the objects rather than about the knowledge question the objects illustrate.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-village-.modesIntro: Three ways a Jumeirah Village Triangle family can structure IB support. All three are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the right one depends on how far away the next assessment is.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the year
modes.description: A fixed slot, same tutor, same subject, running across both Diploma years. This is the format that moves a grade rather than rescuing a paper, because the tutor sees the student's own classwork week by week and can connect a Paper 2 weakness to the topic it came from. Most families start with one subject and add a second only if the first is working.
bullets: Same tutor for the full term, so no repeated diagnosis
Session recording and notes kept for revision

The honest answer to the search is that home tutoring in this part of Dubai is widely available and reasonably priced, and that its real constraint is not money but matching. A tutor who will drive into Jumeirah Village Triangle on a Tuesday at 17:00 is drawn from a radius of a few kilometres. Within that radius, the number of people who have taught IB Chemistry HL Paper 3, or marked a Mathematics AA Exploration against Criterion E, is small. For a general primary top-up that does not matter. For a DP2 student eight weeks out from a Group 4 paper, it is the whole question.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to Jumeirah Village Triangle families over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard the student can write on and a recording afterwards. What the online model buys is the specialist. A Triangle family gets the person who has taught that exact component, not the person who lives nearest to the second roundabout. The rest of this page is the detail of what that specialist actually works on.

sections.heading: Diploma assessment structure: where the percentages sit
paragraphs: A Diploma grade is a weighted sum of components, and almost every student who is stuck is stuck on one of them. Knowing which one changes what the tutoring does. A student at 4 in Chemistry HL with a solid Paper 1 and a collapsing Paper 2 needs extended-response technique, not more content. A student with a strong Paper 2 and a weak Internal Assessment needs criterion work, which is a completely different activity.

The table below sets out the components for the subjects most requested around Jumeirah Village Triangle. The figures are from the published IB subject guides. What it makes visible is the size of the internally assessed component: 20% in the sciences and in Mathematics, and in the sciences it is marked by the school and moderated by the IB. That 20% is the most controllable mark on the page, and it is the one students most often leave until the term it is due.

The second thing the table makes visible is HL Paper 3. In the sciences it is a distinct paper covering experimental technique and option content; in Mathematics AA and AI it is a two-question extended investigation worth a fifth of the grade. Students who have revised the syllabus thoroughly and never practised a Paper 3 walk into it unprepared, and Dubai school mock papers do not always include one.
Use the table diagnostically. Find the component your child's last report is weakest on, read what it tests, and start there.

sections.heading: Where IB students in Dubai schools actually lose marks
paragraphs: Mark loss is patterned, not random. After enough marked scripts the same half-dozen errors appear across every cohort, and they are specific enough to be fixed in a handful of sessions once named. This is the section that most tutoring pages replace with a sentence about building confidence.

The largest single category is command-term misreading. The IB publishes its command terms with defined meanings: 'state' wants no working, 'outline' wants a brief account, 'explain' wants reasons or causes, 'discuss' wants a balanced review, 'evaluate' wants judgement with evidence. A student who answers 'evaluate' with a description has written a correct paragraph and scored at the bottom of the band. The fix is mechanical — annotate the command term before writing — and it transfers across every subject.

The second is presentation of reasoning. In Mathematics, method marks exist and are awarded for visible steps; a correct answer with no working loses them. In Chemistry, a mechanism without curly arrows from the correct electron source scores nothing even when the product is right. In Physics, uncertainty propagation rules get half-applied. In Economics, an unlabelled diagram is worth less than a labelled one even where the analysis is identical.

The third is the Internal Assessment evaluation. Criterion D in the sciences asks for conclusion and evaluation, and students write about human error and time constraints when the criterion wants discussion of methodological limitations and specific, realistic improvements. It is 20% of the grade and it is the part a tutor can legitimately help with most — by teaching what the criterion rewards, while the student writes every word.

sections.heading: The examination calendar counted backwards
paragraphs: Dates are where tutoring plans fail. A family starts in March for a May sitting and discovers the Internal Assessment deadline passed in January. Counting backwards from results day rather than forwards from today is the fix, and it is worth doing on paper once at the start of each Diploma year.

For the IGCSE qualifications most Triangle students take before the Diploma, the series are concrete and published. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. One warning that matters: Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only, so no UAE candidate sits it. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

Published results timings give a sense of the lag. Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, which is exactly why a page like this should link the live official timetable rather than restate dates that can be revised.

For the IB itself, UAE candidates sit the May session. This page publishes no IB session or results date: ibo.org returns an error to automated checking, so nothing could be verified from the IB directly, and a date a parent plans around has to be right. Confirm it with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. The internal deadlines — IA submission, Extended Essay drafts, TOK exhibition — are set by your school and are the ones that actually bite first.

sections.heading: KHDA, inspection bands and the mandatory UAE subjects
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In 2024-25 that sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, with UK curricula at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and the IB at 7%. For a Jumeirah Village Triangle parent, that last figure is the practical one: IB schools are a minority of a very large market, which is why the IB-specialist tutor pool within any one neighbourhood is thin.

KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and publishes the reports. The band is useful but blunt. What is more useful to a tutoring decision is the subject-level commentary inside the report, which often names the exact weakness a cohort has — attainment in mathematics, or progress in Arabic as an additional language. Read that section before deciding which subject to fund.

The second KHDA point is one almost no tutoring page in this market mentions. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. KHDA also requires that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

Two consequences follow for tutoring. Mandatory-subject instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools free to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met and any mandatory-subject lesson advised to run at least 25 minutes — so the Arabic load on a Triangle timetable is fixed, not optional, and it competes with Diploma revision for the same evenings. And for those subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which constrains how any Arabic or Islamic Education support can be described. Note also that a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit; IB Gram holds no such permit and makes no claim to KHDA approval.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: This section exists because the market around it is not clean. At least one provider ranking for UAE IB searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Buying one is academic misconduct under IB rules, and the consequence lands on the student — not on the seller — up to and including loss of the Diploma. Any page offering to write your child's IA is offering to put their qualification at risk.

What a tutor may legitimately do with internally assessed work is substantial. They can explain what each criterion rewards, using the subject guide's own descriptors. They can help narrow a research question from something unmanageable to something a student can actually gather data on. They can look at a method and point out that it will not generate enough data points for the statistical treatment the student has planned. They can read a draft and say that Criterion D discusses human error where the descriptor asks for methodological limitations. They can teach citation and referencing. All of that is teaching.

What a tutor must not do is produce the work. Not write a paragraph for the student to insert. Not rewrite a conclusion so it reads better. Not supply a worked Exploration for adaptation. Not line-edit a draft into a different standard of English than the student can produce. The distinction is simple in practice: after the session, has the student written every word that will be submitted? If not, the line has been crossed.

The same holds for examination material. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright. We reference and link them at their official sources; we do not reproduce or distribute them. A tutor who hands over a folder of scanned mark schemes is creating a copyright problem, and in the case of unreleased material, a malpractice exposure.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency after the Diploma
paragraphs: Families in Jumeirah Village Triangle planning on a UAE university need to know about equivalency early, because it is a documentary process with subject-count rules, and discovering those rules in Year 13 is late. Equivalency is the Ministry of Education's recognition of a foreign secondary certificate, and it is required for admission to UAE institutions and for some employment routes.

For the British track the rules are published and specific. A student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects. That five-subject figure is worth holding on to: a competitor page ranking for UAE searches states that candidates must take six, which is wrong, and a parent who plans around it over-subscribes their child by a subject.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB, this page publishes no points threshold. The sourced article does not state one, and no figure has been read on moe.gov.ae, so inventing one would be exactly the error described above with a different number on it.

Two cautions. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency — it is a Ministry process and you deal with the Ministry or the emirate's attestation authority directly. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression. Anybody telling you otherwise is selling urgency.

sections.heading: Starting, and what happens when the specialist is busy
paragraphs: The process is short. You tell us the subject, the level, the component that is weak and the school. We ask for a marked piece of work — a mock script, a returned IA draft, a report with subject comments. A specialist runs a free diagnostic lesson, and within a day you get a written note saying what the error pattern is and how many sessions it plausibly takes. Then you decide. Nothing is charged before that note exists.

Availability deserves an honest paragraph, because no competitor in this market gives one. Common Diploma subjects — Mathematics AA and AI, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics, English A, Business Management — have deep cover for UAE evening slots, and a match usually takes one to three working days. Narrower courses are different. A rarely taken Group 2 language at HL, a specific Computer Science option, or a Career-related Programme reflective project may have no UAE-resident specialist free at all, in which case the match comes from our India-based IB faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and we tell you that before you book rather than after.

Scheduling around a Jumeirah Village Triangle week is usually straightforward. Term-time slots from 16:30 work for families whose children are at Sunmarke School or Arcadia Global School inside the community; families driving back from the Arabian Ranches or Dubai Hills schools generally want 17:30 or later. During Ramadan, sessions shift to post-Iftar timing, typically 20:30 to 22:00, and the schedule flexes again around school examination weeks when students need the evenings for their own revision.

One more honest note on permits, because parents ask. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure is quoted here. The application route is MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service, with no listed fee and a two-working-day completion time.

faqs.question: My child is a 4 in Chemistry HL. Which component should we work on first?
faqs.answer: Look at the component breakdown rather than the overall grade. Chemistry Paper 2 is 44% of the grade and Paper 1 is 36%, with the scientific investigation at 20%. A student weak on Paper 2 needs extended-response technique — naming the principle, then applying it, with mechanisms drawn properly. A student weak on Paper 1 usually needs data-analysis practice and faster recall. A student whose papers are fine but whose investigation scored poorly needs criterion work, which is a different activity entirely. Send the marked mock and the first diagnostic session identifies which of the three it is.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a JVT student usually need before a May sitting?
faqs.answer: For one named component with a diagnosed error pattern, six to ten weekly sessions is the normal range, and that holds whether the student is in Jumeirah Village Triangle or anywhere else. Fixing a whole subject from a 3 to a 6 is a two-term project, not an eight-week one. Internal Assessment coaching is usually four to six sessions spread across the drafting period rather than consecutive weeks. The written diagnosis after the free first lesson gives a specific number for your child's case, and if the honest answer is that the time remaining is not enough, it says that.

faqs.question: Is Mathematics Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation the safer choice?
faqs.answer: Neither is safer in the abstract; they fail different students. AA assesses algebraic fluency and proof, and its Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, so a student who leans on a graphing display calculator struggles. AI is calculator-permitted and statistics-heavy, and students who pick it expecting an easy route meet hypothesis testing and regression with no statistical vocabulary. The decision should be made on the degree prerequisite: several engineering and mathematics programmes specify AA, and some specify HL. Check the admissions pages of the universities on your child's list before the subject-choice form is signed.
