We explain what those bodies do; none of them endorses us.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match an IB tutor for a student in Jumeirah Village Triangle?
faqs.answer: For mainstream Diploma subjects — Mathematics AA and AI, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics, English A, Business Management — one to three working days for a UAE evening slot. Narrower courses take longer and sometimes cannot be filled from UAE-resident tutors at all: a rarely taken Group 2 language at HL, a specific Computer Science option, or a Career-related Programme reflective project. When that happens the match comes from our India-based IB faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and we tell you before you book. No competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit, which does not mean they do not have one.

faqs.question: What does a month of IB tutoring realistically cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Taking Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for one weekly hour: roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 for a mid-tier qualified tutor, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published package pricing in this market includes around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not ours. We quote against the actual subject, level and urgency after the free diagnostic lesson rather than publishing a rate that would be wrong for most cases.

faqs.question: Can Jumeirah Village Triangle sessions move during Ramadan or school examination weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and both are normal requests from Triangle families. During Ramadan sessions shift to post-Iftar timing, usually between 20:30 and 22:00 on Gulf Standard Time, and the length often shortens to 45 minutes. During a school's internal examination weeks most families pause entirely so the student owns their own evenings, then resume with a session spent reading the marked scripts. Because every session is recorded, a paused block does not lose anything: the student can revisit December's work in April without paying for it twice. Tell us the dates at the start of term and the slot is held.

faqs.question: My child is moving from MYP into DP1 next year. What should we fix over the summer?
faqs.answer: Algebraic fluency, almost always. MYP mathematics assesses against four criteria — Knowing and understanding, Investigating patterns, Communicating, and Applying mathematics in real-life contexts — and rewards reasoning and communication rather than drilled manipulation. A student arriving on Analysis and Approaches with strong MYP reasoning and weak fluency hits Paper 1, which is sat without a calculator, and stalls. Eight to twelve sessions of indices, surds, rearrangement, factorising and function notation before DP1 starts closes most of that gap. The same pattern appears in the sciences, where MYP Criterion-based practicals do not prepare a student for quantitative Paper 2 questions.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does Ministry of Education equivalency actually count?
faqs.answer: Five, not six. Equivalency is a documentary process run by the Ministry of Education and the emirate's attestation authority, and tutoring is not a requirement for it, for university admission or for school progression. Anybody implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency. What is worth knowing early is the British-track rule: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at no less than E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. A competitor page states six IGCSE subjects are needed; the published figure is five.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-village-.closingHeading: Find the component, then find the person who has marked it
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-jumeirah-village-.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, take the diagnostic habit. Open the last report and the last marked mock, and work out which component is losing the marks: Paper 1 or Paper 2, the extended response or the data analysis, the investigation or the examination. Then find somebody who has taught that component to the standard your child needs, and schedule them weekly rather than in a panic in April. For families in Jumeirah Village Triangle that means an online specialist on Gulf Standard Time rather than the nearest available tutor, and it means the first session is spent reading errors rather than selling. Send the marked script and book the free diagnostic lesson.

intro.heading: There is no such thing as an IB tutor - there are six of them
paragraphs: A Karama parent searching for an IB home tutor is usually imagining one person who can help across the board. The Diploma does not work that way. A student takes six subjects from six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, and each one has its own papers, its own weightings, its own command terms and its own internally assessed component. The word used for that component is often the same across groups and the thing itself is completely different. A History internal assessment is a historical investigation with a source evaluation section. A Mathematics internal assessment is a mathematical exploration. A Group 4 internal assessment is a scientific investigation with four criteria. A Language A internal assessment is an oral, recorded and marked by the teacher.

This matters because a generalist tutor working on the wrong model produces confident, plausible, useless advice. Being told to structure your investigation with a clear hypothesis is sensible for a science, irrelevant for an Economics commentary and actively misleading for a mathematical exploration. The useful first question is not how is your child doing in the IB. It is which subject, at which level, and which component - paper or internal assessment - is losing the marks.

The second thing worth understanding before buying anything is where the points come from. Six subjects at a maximum of 7 points each gives 42, and Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together contribute up to 3 more through a published matrix, for a total of 45. There are also conditions that can fail a candidate who has enough raw points, which is why the core is not an optional extra. A family focused entirely on subject grades and ignoring a Theory of Knowledge grade of E is looking at the wrong risk.

Karama's own situation shapes how this plays out. This is apartment living, often with siblings sharing a table and a device, and the Diploma student in the household is generally commuting out of the district to an IB school. That means the realistic session window is narrow and the room is shared, and both of those are planning problems rather than teaching problems. Families here are also, in our experience, unusually price-sensitive and unusually well informed, which is why this page publishes the market rates with their sources attached rather than asking anyone to take a figure on trust.

On delivery, plainly: the URL you clicked says home tutor because that is the phrase parents type, and we are going to answer the home-tutoring question honestly rather than pretend it was not asked. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every lesson for a Karama family is one-to-one over live video. The argument for that is made in a table further down, and the short version is that six subject groups need six specialists, and six specialists do not live within a twenty-minute drive of one Karama address.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-karama.programmesIntro: Where a Karama family usually sits when they start looking. The subject and the component matter more than the year, but the year changes what is still available to influence.

programmes.name: Diploma year one
programmes.description: Content is introduced across all six subjects, internal assessment work is planned and often begun, the Extended Essay process starts and Theory of Knowledge runs alongside. The highest-value tutoring in DP1 is on internally assessed components, because every one of them is still fully open and the design decisions that cap a mark have not yet been made.
programmes.countryNote: In a Dubai school, DP1 also carries mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. A DP1 student reporting that there is no time is usually right, and looking at the timetable before buying hours sometimes produces a better answer than buying them.

programmes.name: Diploma year two
programmes.description: Remaining content, internal assessment submission deadlines, the Extended Essay final submission, Theory of Knowledge components, mocks and then the papers. By the spring of DP2 most internally assessed marks are closed, so the remaining work is paper technique and the mechanical mark-losers that command terms and mark schemes punish.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the May session, with November as the alternative sitting. No IB session or results date appears on this page: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so any date should come from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org rather than from a tutoring website.

programmes.name: The three Higher Level subjects
programmes.description: Higher Level subjects carry additional content, longer papers and in several groups an extra component - a Higher Level essay in Language A, a third paper in the sciences, extended options in Individuals and Societies. The three Higher Levels are where a Diploma point total is usually won or lost, and where specialist teaching is most clearly worth more than general support.
programmes.countryNote: Karama families frequently choose Higher Level combinations with university entry in mind - two sciences plus Mathematics is common. That combination is heavy on time rather than on ability, and it is worth planning across two years rather than discovering the load in DP1 term two.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an exhibition and an essay and graded on a letter scale; the Extended Essay is an independent research piece with a 4,000 word limit, also letter-graded. Together they contribute up to 3 points through a published matrix, and there are conditions attached that can fail an otherwise sufficient candidate. Neither is optional and both are routinely under-prioritised.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai IB schools run internal Extended Essay deadlines that sit well before the IB submission date, and those internal dates are the ones that actually govern a student's spring. Ask the coordinator for them in writing at the start of DP1 rather than hearing about them in DP2.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-karama.subjectsIntro: The six groups and the core, with the internally assessed component for each and the place marks most reliably go. This is the list to work from when deciding which specialist you actually need.

subjects.name: Group 1: Language A, Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided textual analysis on an unseen text, Paper 2 comparative essay, an internally assessed individual oral, and at Higher Level an additional essay. The commonest loss is on Paper 1: students summarise the text rather than analysing how its choices create effect, and summary scores in the lowest bands however fluent the prose.

subjects.name: Group 1: Language A, Literature
subjects.description: The same assessment architecture applied to literary works only. The comparative Paper 2 essay is where structure decides the mark - a student who writes about two works in sequence rather than in comparison caps themselves. Comparison has to be the organising principle of each paragraph, not a concluding paragraph.

subjects.name: Group 2: Language B
subjects.description: A writing paper, a listening and reading paper, and an individually assessed oral carrying a substantial share of the grade. The oral is the component students prepare least and worry about most. Preparation is specific: the visual stimulus or extract, the structure of the response, and the ability to sustain an unscripted conversation about it.

subjects.name: Group 3: History
subjects.description: Source-based Paper 1, essay Paper 2, Higher Level regional Paper 3, and an internally assessed historical investigation. Paper 1 rewards evaluating sources for origin, purpose, value and limitation rather than describing them. Paper 2 essays fail on the absence of a sustained argument, not on a shortage of facts.

subjects.name: Group 3: Economics
subjects.description: Papers requiring diagram-led explanation, with an internal assessment built from commentaries on published news articles against syllabus units. Diagram accuracy and labelling is marked and routinely half-done. The commentaries are a different skill from the papers and need separate, timely teaching.

subjects.name: Group 3: Business Management and Psychology
subjects.description: Both run case-study or research-method heavy assessments with their own internal components. Business Management rewards applying a named tool to the stimulus rather than describing the tool; Psychology rewards methodological critique of named studies. Generic answers that could fit any stimulus score in the lower bands.

subjects.name: Group 4: Biology, Chemistry, Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 with a multiple-choice and a data-based section, Paper 2 extended response, and a scientific investigation worth 20 per cent across four criteria. The investigation closes months before the papers, so a DP2 student in the spring has only paper technique left. Uncertainty and graph work pays in both the papers and the investigation.

subjects.name: Group 5: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The more abstract route, with proof, calculus and algebraic technique emphasised, plus a mathematical exploration. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is the most demanding Group 5 option and the usual choice for engineering and mathematics applicants. Marks go on algebraic accuracy under time rather than on conceptual gaps.

subjects.name: Group 5: Mathematics Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route, with heavier technology use and the same exploration component. Choosing between the two routes is a decision with university consequences and should be checked against the specific courses a student may apply to, not against a general reputation.

subjects.name: Group 6 and the elective swap
subjects.description: Visual Arts, Music, Theatre and Film each run portfolio or performance-based assessment with substantial internally assessed weight. Many Dubai students swap Group 6 for a second subject from Groups 1 to 4, which is permitted and changes the balance of internal assessment deadlines in a year - worth mapping before DP1.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects against a prompt, and an essay on a prescribed title, letter-graded. Students treat it as unassessed background and then find it affecting their point total through the core matrix. The essay rewards engaging with the prescribed title precisely rather than writing generally about knowledge.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: An independent 4,000 word research piece in a subject, letter-graded, with supervisor meetings and reflections forming part of the assessment. The commonest failure is a research question too broad to answer in 4,000 words, and it is diagnosable in a single conversation months before the essay is written.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor search in Karama is actually asking for
paragraphs: The phrase home tutor carries two separate requests inside it, and separating them is the first useful thing to do. One is about delivery: somebody who comes to the flat, so there is no journey and the hour can be seen. The other is about the teaching: somebody who knows this subject at this level well enough to be worth paying. Families ask for both in one phrase, and in Karama specifically the second is far harder to satisfy than the first.

On delivery, the honest answer is short. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every lesson for a Karama family is one-to-one over live video, and we say it before anyone pays rather than after. Two providers ranking for these searches route UAE parents to overseas phone numbers without disclosing where the tutor sits, and a family should not find that out at the end of a month.

On the teaching, the Diploma makes the problem concrete. A student needs six subjects taught, three of them at Higher Level, each with its own internally assessed component. A household that insists on physical proximity is choosing from the people who can reach that address and are free in the right hour. For a single subject, that pool might be adequate. For Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches plus a Group 4 investigation plus an Extended Essay in Economics, it is not. The specialist you want for each of those three is a different person, and the chance that all three live near one Karama address is negligible.

There is also a market reality worth naming. The in-home rates published in Dubai run from AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, against AED 150 to AED 450 for online specialists. The amount above the online band is paying for a drive across the creek. For a household that may need two or three subjects supported over two years, that premium compounds into a real number, and it buys no additional subject expertise at all.

sections.heading: The six groups and their internal assessments, side by side
paragraphs: The single most useful table a Diploma parent can read is this one, because it shows that the internally assessed components across the six groups have almost nothing in common beyond being internally assessed. A tutor who understands one of them well does not thereby understand another, and advice that transfers between them is usually wrong.

Consider three of them. A Group 4 scientific investigation is assessed on four criteria - research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation - and its ceiling is set by whether the chosen variable can be measured precisely enough with school apparatus. A Group 3 History historical investigation requires a focused question, an evaluation of sources and a reflection on the methods of the historian, and its ceiling is set by whether sources on that question actually exist and are accessible. A Group 5 mathematical exploration is a piece of personal mathematical writing with its own criteria including personal engagement, and its ceiling is set by whether the student has mathematics of the right level to apply. Those are three different problems requiring three different conversations.

What they do share is timing. Almost every internally assessed component is submitted at a school deadline well before the papers, which means there is a point after which the mark is closed. For a family deciding where tutoring money goes, that is the governing fact: a DP1 student has every internal assessment open and a DP2 student in the spring has none of them. Spending in DP1 on internal assessment design and in DP2 on paper technique follows the architecture of the qualification rather than fighting it.

One more practical note, specific to Karama households with more than one Diploma student or a Diploma student and an IGCSE sibling. Internal assessment deadlines cluster, because schools set them to fit their own calendars, and several components can fall in the same fortnight. Asking the coordinator for the internal deadline list at the start of DP1 lets a family see the crunch and plan around it, and it costs nothing.

sections.heading: Command terms: the published vocabulary that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject publishes a list of command terms, grouped by the level of thinking they demand, and each term has an expected form of response. This is the most systematically ignored piece of free information in the whole qualification. A student who answers an evaluate question by describing has not made a mistake of knowledge; they have answered a different question, and the mark scheme has nothing to award.

The structure is consistent across subjects even where the vocabulary varies. The lowest tier asks for retrieval: state, list, define, identify. The middle tier asks for description or application: describe, outline, summarise, calculate, apply. The highest tier asks for judgement: analyse, evaluate, discuss, justify, compare and contrast, to what extent. Marks rise with the tier, and so does the structural demand on the answer. A to what extent question requires a position, evidence on both sides and a judgement; a describe question requires none of those and gains nothing by including them.

The second half of the skill is mark allocation. In most Diploma subjects a question's mark value tells you how many creditable points it wants. A six-mark question wants six distinct points, not one point expressed beautifully six ways. Students who write well are the most prone to this error, which is why strong writers sometimes underperform in the sciences and in Individuals and Societies while weaker writers who answer mechanically do better than expected.

Explicit command-term work is among the cheapest interventions in the Diploma and among the most transferable, because it applies across all six subjects at once rather than one. Two sessions early in DP1, followed by checking every past-paper answer against the command term before checking it against the content, moves marks in every subject the student takes. It is also something a family can do without buying anything: print the command term list for each subject from the school and read it with the student.

sections.heading: The oral components, and why Karama students prepare them last
paragraphs: Both language groups carry an internally assessed oral, and between them they account for a substantial share of two of a student's six subject grades. They are also, consistently, the components students prepare least and worry about most, which is an unusual combination and worth understanding.

In Group 1 Language A, the individual oral asks a student to examine how a global issue is presented in two works, one of them in translation, through two chosen extracts. The marks turn on the quality of the framing as much as on the analysis: a global issue chosen because it sounds impressive, rather than because the extracts genuinely support it, caps the whole component before a word is spoken. That decision is made weeks before the recording and is the right moment for a conversation.

In Group 2 Language B, the individual oral works from a stimulus and then opens into unscripted conversation. Students rehearse the prepared portion and then struggle in the follow-up, because the follow-up is the part that cannot be scripted. Preparation that works is specifically about handling the unprepared section - buying time in the target language, developing an answer rather than ending it, and having two or three reusable structures ready. That is coaching, it is practical, and it is quite different from language teaching.

For a Karama household there is a practical complication worth naming. Oral practice needs a quiet room and a working microphone, and in a flat with siblings sharing a table that is a scheduling problem rather than an academic one. It is also the one kind of session where the online format is unambiguously better than a tutor in the room, because the student practises speaking into exactly the setup the real recording will use. We would rather a student rehearse in the conditions of the assessment than in a conversation across a dining table.

sections.heading: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay: the three points nobody plans for
paragraphs: Six subjects at a maximum of 7 points gives 42. The remaining 3 points come from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay through a published matrix that combines their letter grades, and there are conditions attached that can fail a candidate who has otherwise accumulated enough. Families who treat the core as background are carrying a risk they have not priced.

The Extended Essay fails most often at the research question, and it fails there months before anyone writes anything. A question too broad to answer in 4,000 words produces an essay that surveys rather than argues, and surveys score in the lower bands. A question narrow enough to answer properly feels unambitious to a seventeen-year-old and scores well. That is a counter-intuitive trade and it needs explaining rather than asserting. The supervisor reflections are also part of the assessment, which students regularly discover late.

Theory of Knowledge has two components - an exhibition of three objects against a prompt, and an essay on a prescribed title - and the essay is where the marks concentrate. The recurring error is writing generally about knowledge rather than engaging with the precise wording of the prescribed title. The titles are deliberately specific, and a response that would fit three different titles fits none of them well. Reading the title closely, phrase by phrase, before any planning is the whole of the useful early work.

On where a tutor may help, the boundary is the same as everywhere else and worth restating because the core is where pressure peaks in DP2. A tutor can interrogate a research question, ask whether sources or data exist, read a prescribed title alongside a student and ask what each phrase commits them to, and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor does not write, co-write, edit to completion or supply any part of an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or an exhibition commentary. One provider in this market sells completed internally assessed work outright, which is an academic honesty breach whose consequence falls on the student who submits it.

sections.heading: What Diploma tutoring costs for a Karama household, by subject
paragraphs: Karama families tend to ask the cost question first and in detail, which is sensible, so here are the published numbers with their sources rather than a range we invented. All figures were read in October 2026 from each provider's own pages, and none of them are IB Gram prices.

Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end, which in practice buys homework supervision rather than Higher Level subject teaching. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table places IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. TutorChase publishes AED 270. BartyED sits at AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors. Monthly, Bestimate estimates a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work, with packages advertised around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

The number that matters for a Diploma household is the multiple. Supporting two subjects is twice the monthly figure; three is three times. A family in a Karama flat budgeting AED 800 a month for one subject is not budgeting AED 800 for the Diploma. This is why we push so hard on identifying the single component that is actually losing marks: one well-aimed subject engagement plus a short internal assessment block usually outperforms three vague standing hours at the same total cost.

For context on the household budget rather than the tutoring one, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Dubai's private sector was 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25. We publish no rate card on this page, hold no office or centre in the UAE, and claim no approval or accreditation from the International Baccalaureate, KHDA or anyone else.

sections.heading: A tutor in a Karama flat against one-to-one online, subject by subject
paragraphs: The in-home case in Karama is not a weak one and we are not going to straw-man it. In an apartment with younger children, a tutor arriving removes a journey and makes the hour visible. The parent can tell whether the time was worked. For a single subject with a generalist that can be a reasonable arrangement, and plenty of families here make it.

Where it breaks is at the subject level. The Diploma asks for six subjects taught, three at Higher Level, each with a differently shaped internally assessed component. The specialist who understands what caps a mathematical exploration is not the person who understands what caps a historical investigation, and neither is the person who can coach an unscripted Language B oral follow-up. A household choosing from whoever can reach a Karama address is choosing from a pool defined by geography rather than by subject, and for the harder components that pool is often empty.

The other practical consideration is the room. Karama study space is typically shared, and a tutor in the flat occupies the one quiet surface for the whole visit while other children also need it. An online session needs a device and headphones and can run in a bedroom. For oral practice in either language group it is strictly better, because the student rehearses into the same microphone-and-screen setup the real recording uses. These are small advantages individually and they add up across two years.

The cost difference is the least interesting argument and still worth stating plainly. In-home rates in this market run AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against AED 150 to 450 for online specialists. The premium above the online band pays for a drive across the creek. Over two years and two subjects that is a significant sum and it buys no additional subject knowledge. Our position remains the straightforward one: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, every lesson here is one-to-one over live video, and we tell families that before they pay.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and what the Diploma week has left
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. In 2024-25 the sector was 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of students, Indian at 26 per cent and US at 14 per cent. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places, after six opened in 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent.

The timetable facts are the ones that bite a Diploma student. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises a minimum of 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, since the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, and requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval.

Put those hours beside six Diploma subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, and a DP2 week has very little slack. A Karama student who says there is no time to do the Extended Essay properly is frequently making an accurate statement about the calendar rather than an excuse. Looking at the actual timetable before adding a tutoring hour sometimes produces a better answer than adding one, and we would rather say that than sell against a problem the timetable created.

On inspection bands, which families here read closely when comparing schools: a band is a judgement on a whole school across many measures. It does not tell you whether that school's Higher Level Chemistry teaching is strong, whether its internal assessment deadlines are set sensibly, or whether its Extended Essay supervision is attentive. Those are the questions that actually affect a point total, and the people who can answer them are other parents in the same year group and the IB coordinator.

sections.heading: Permits, accreditation claims and the dates we leave out
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit and a Karama parent can check it directly. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and states a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published officially, so no amount should be quoted to you by anybody.

A related rule: in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct likewise bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Anyone offering a Karama family their child's own subject teacher privately is proposing something that teacher should not be doing.

On IB Gram: we hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International or Pearson. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation for training institutes with premises in Dubai, involving initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry; we do not hold one. We have no office, centre or branch in the UAE. We publish no satisfaction percentage, star rating or tutor count, because none of those could carry a sample size, a date and a method.

And there is no IB examination or results date on this page. The IB's own site blocks automated fetching, which means any date we published would be unverified, and a wrong date in a Diploma plan is a date a family acts on. UAE candidates sit the May session with November as the alternative; for the specific dates, ask your school's IB coordinator or check ibo.org. We also do not publish or redistribute IB subject guides, assessment criteria documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads - we cite them and link out, because reproducing them is the IB's copyright rather than ours to share.

process.title: Name the subject, the level and the component
process.description: Not the IB in general, but Higher Level Chemistry Paper 2, or the Group 3 historical investigation, or the Language B oral. That is the question a specialist can answer and the question a generalist cannot, and getting it right saves the first paid hour.

process.title: Establish whether the component is still open
process.description: Internally assessed components close at a school deadline well before the papers. Ask the coordinator for the internal deadline list. A DP1 student has all of them open; a DP2 student in the spring has paper technique and nothing else, and the plan should reflect that.

process.title: A free trial with the right specialist
process.description: One session at no cost with the subject specialist you would continue with, spent on a marked script or a live internal assessment draft. You get a written note of what was found and what the component's descriptor actually asks for, whether or not you book anything further.

process.title: Check the command term before the content
process.description: In the first session we read the student's answers against the command term rather than against the content. A describe answer to an evaluate question is a structural problem, and fixing it moves marks in all six subjects rather than one.

process.title: Fix the hour against a shared Karama table
process.description: Pick a slot that accounts for siblings needing the same surface and for the real commute home. Al Mankhool and Oud Metha households can often hold 4.30pm; Karama around five; Deira-side and Al Nahda after six, and all of these shift during Ramadan. Times are Gulf Standard Time.

process.title: Measure, then end the block
process.description: Progress is the next assessment in that subject, not a tutor's impression. We report what moved and what did not, and if the pattern is flat we change the tutor or the approach rather than adding hours. When a component is submitted, that block is finished.

whyPoints.title: Specialists by subject, not Diploma generalists
whyPoints.description: Six groups with six differently shaped internal assessments cannot be covered well by one person. We match on the subject and the component rather than on availability, which is also why physical proximity is not a constraint we accept.

whyPoints.title: We tell you which component is closed
whyPoints.description: If an internal assessment has been submitted, no tutoring changes that mark and we will say so rather than booking hours against it. Knowing what is still open is the difference between spending usefully in DP1 and spending hopefully in DP2.

whyPoints.title: Command terms before content
whyPoints.description: A published list per subject sets the expected response, and answering an evaluate question by describing loses marks that content revision cannot recover. Two sessions on this transfers to all six subjects, and a family can do most of it for free with the school's own list.

whyPoints.title: A written boundary on assessed work
whyPoints.description: We interrogate research questions, teach technique and give feedback on the student's own drafts. We produce no part of an internal assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or an oral script. One provider in this market sells completed internal assessments; the consequence of that falls on the student.

whyPoints.title: Clear about where the tutor sits
whyPoints.description: The URL says home tutor because that is what parents search, and the honest answer is that IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Every lesson here is one-to-one over live video, stated before payment rather than discovered afterwards.

whyPoints.title: Figures attributed, claims absent, dates omitted
whyPoints.description: Every AED range names its publisher and the month it was read. We publish no rating or satisfaction figure, claim no IB or KHDA accreditation, hold no UAE premises, and print no IB examination date we have not been able to verify from the IB itself.

faqs.question: Can one IB tutor cover all my child's Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Realistically no. A Diploma student takes six subjects from six groups, three at Higher Level, and each has its own papers, weightings, command terms and internally assessed component. Those components are structurally different: a mathematical exploration, a historical investigation with source evaluation, a scientific investigation on four criteria and a recorded oral have almost nothing in common. A generalist who understands one of them will give confident advice about another that transfers wrongly. Match on the subject and the component instead.

faqs.question: How are the 45 IB Diploma points actually made up?
faqs.answer: Six subjects at a maximum of 7 points each gives 42. The remaining 3 come from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay combined, through a published matrix of their letter grades. There are also conditions attached that can fail a candidate who has accumulated enough raw points, which is why the core is not background. Families who focus entirely on subject grades and ignore a weak Theory of Knowledge grade are carrying a risk they have not priced.

faqs.question: Do you send an IB tutor to our flat in Karama?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every lesson for a Karama family is one-to-one over live video, and we say so before anyone pays. The reason this is not a compromise for the Diploma is arithmetical: six subject groups need six specialists, and the chance that all of them live within a twenty-minute drive of one Karama address and are free in the right hour is negligible.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the internal assessments in different IB subjects?
faqs.answer: Almost everything except the label. A Group 4 scientific investigation is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and its ceiling is whether the variable can be measured precisely enough. A History historical investigation needs a question that accessible sources can answer, plus source evaluation and a reflection on historical method. A mathematical exploration needs mathematics of the right level applied with personal engagement. An Economics internal assessment is commentaries on published articles against syllabus units. Four different problems, four different early conversations.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks when the content knowledge is there?
faqs.answer: Usually because of command terms and mark allocation. Every Diploma subject publishes a command term list, and each term has an expected response: state wants a fact, describe wants what happens, explain wants why, evaluate wants a position with evidence both ways and a judgement. Answering one with another loses marks that content revision cannot recover. The second half is mark allocation - a six-mark question wants six distinct creditable points, and strong writers are the most prone to making four points beautifully.

faqs.question: When should we start working on the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: In DP1, and the first piece of work is the research question rather than the reading. Extended Essays fail most often because the question is too broad to answer in 4,000 words, which produces a survey rather than an argument, and surveys score in the lower bands. A narrower question feels unambitious to a seventeen-year-old and scores better. The supervisor reflections also form part of the assessment, which students regularly discover late. Ask the coordinator for the school's internal deadlines in writing at the start of DP1.

faqs.question: How much help can a tutor legitimately give on an IB internal assessment?
faqs.answer: A tutor can interrogate a research question, ask whether sources or data exist and are accessible, teach technique such as uncertainty handling or source evaluation, explain what each criterion descriptor rewards, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write, co-write, edit to completion or supply any part of the submitted work. We put that boundary in writing before any internal assessment work starts, because under IB academic honesty rules the consequence of crossing it falls on the student rather than the tutor.

faqs.question: Why is the Language B oral so hard to prepare for?
faqs.answer: Because the part that carries the risk cannot be scripted. Students rehearse the prepared response to the stimulus and then struggle in the unscripted follow-up conversation, which is where the examiner probes. Useful preparation is specifically about that section: buying time in the target language, developing an answer rather than closing it, and having two or three reusable structures ready to deploy. That is coaching rather than language teaching, and practising it over video rehearses the actual recording conditions.

faqs.question: What should a Karama family budget for IB Diploma tutoring?
faqs.answer: Start from one subject and resist multiplying. Market rates read in October 2026: Unitors publishes IB from AED 200 an hour, Bestimate's Dubai table places specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and the budget end runs AED 33 to 65 with Tutopiya and EdFlik. Bestimate estimates a weekly hour at AED 600 to 1,200 a month mid-market. Two subjects doubles that and three triples it, which is why identifying the single component actually losing marks is the cheapest step available.

faqs.question: Is Theory of Knowledge really worth spending tutoring money on?
faqs.answer: A little, well timed, yes. It contributes to the core points alongside the Extended Essay and carries conditions that can fail a candidate. The essay is where the marks concentrate, and the recurring failure is writing generally about knowledge instead of engaging with the precise wording of a prescribed title. One or two sessions spent reading the title phrase by phrase, before any planning, is usually sufficient. Beyond that, Theory of Knowledge tutoring tends to produce elegant essays that answer a question nobody asked.

faqs.question: Which Mathematics route should my child take in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: It depends on what they intend to apply for, and it should be checked against specific courses rather than against a general reputation. Analysis and Approaches is the more abstract route, emphasising proof, calculus and algebraic technique, and is the usual expectation for engineering and mathematics. Applications and Interpretation emphasises modelling, statistics and technology use. Both carry the same mathematical exploration component. Confirm the requirement with the universities a student may actually apply to, because the two routes are treated differently by some courses.

faqs.question: My child is in DP2 and the internal assessments are submitted. What is left?
faqs.answer: Paper technique, and that is a real amount of grade. The mechanical losses are consistent across subjects: answering the wrong command term, making fewer creditable points than the marks available, abandoning a question rather than attempting it for partial credit, omitting units and working in the quantitative subjects, and running out of time through poor question triage. None of those are content problems. A full paper marked hard against the real scheme usually shows which of them is costing the most within a single session.

faqs.question: Does it matter that our Karama flat has no quiet study room?
faqs.answer: It matters for scheduling rather than for outcomes, and it is worth planning deliberately. Where siblings share a table and a device, staggered session times do more good than a better tutor at a worse hour. An online session needs a device and headphones and can run in a bedroom, which leaves the shared surface free. For oral components in either language group the online format is actually preferable, because the student practises into the same screen-and-microphone setup the real recording uses.

faqs.question: Do IB tutors in Dubai need a licence, and can we verify it?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and states a two-working-day completion time. Ask any prospective tutor directly. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties, and no official fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Why do so many Diploma internal assessment deadlines fall together?
faqs.answer: Because schools set their internal deadlines to fit their own calendars rather than coordinating across six subjects, so several components can land in the same fortnight. That crunch is visible in advance if you ask the IB coordinator for the internal deadline list at the start of DP1, and it costs nothing to ask. A student struggling in a crunch fortnight is often struggling with load rather than with any one subject, and seeing the clash early lets a household plan around it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help choose the extract for a Language A individual oral?
faqs.answer: A tutor can discuss it, and should, because the choice sets a ceiling on the whole component before a word is spoken. The marks turn on whether the global issue genuinely arises from the two chosen extracts rather than on whether it sounds impressive. A tutor can ask what each extract actually supports, test whether the framing holds, and give feedback on the student's own plan. The choice, the plan and the spoken response remain entirely the student's own work.

We do not send tutors to UAE homes - every lesson for a Karama family is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and we would rather tell you that now than after you have paid.

intro.heading: The honest answer to a home-tutor search in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: Parents in Dubai Knowledge Park type home tutor for sensible reasons. A tutor at the table means no screen to manage, a child who cannot wander off, and a visible sense that the hour is being used. Those are real advantages and it would be dishonest to pretend otherwise. What this page does is put a price on them, because in this market the price is unusually easy to establish and almost nobody publishes it.

Published Dubai figures put an in-home one-to-one visit at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once the tutor's journey is inside the fee, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. Monthly packages tell the same story: around AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, against about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are market figures from provider pages and the Bestimate Dubai rate table, not our prices. The difference between the two columns is almost entirely travel.

The second cost of in-home tuition is less visible and usually larger. A tutor who must drive to Al Sufouh is selected from the group willing to make that journey at that hour, which for a specific requirement is a short list. An IB Chemistry HL specialist, a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches tutor who has taught the course to examination, or someone who can coach a Physics investigation properly is not necessarily living within twenty minutes of Knowledge Park and free at 18:30. Families end up choosing on availability and calling it choice.

There is a third cost nobody quotes, which is reliability. An eight-week block with two sessions a week is sixteen appointments, and what a family actually buys is the number that take place. An arrangement that loses two a month to traffic, a late arrival or a rescheduled visit has quietly lost a quarter of the block, and that loss is larger than any plausible difference in teaching quality between two competent tutors. In this corner of Dubai, where the afternoon return from Al Barsha and the Marina coincides with the free zones emptying, it is the normal outcome rather than the unlucky one.

Dubai Knowledge Park sits in Al Sufouh between Dubai Internet City and Dubai Media City, a free zone built around universities, training institutes and corporate learning, with the Dubai Tram running along its edge and the Metro a short distance inland. The families who search from here live in Al Sufouh, The Greens, The Views, Barsha Heights, the Marina and JBR, and their children attend schools scattered across Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and the coastal corridor. Road journeys here are short in distance and unreliable in time, which is the practical half of the argument.

So the position on this page is plain. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family address is something we do only in India. We teach UAE students one-to-one, online, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. The rest of this page is the comparison that justifies that, including the places where in-home genuinely wins, and what we disclose about availability before a booking rather than after one.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-knowledge-park.programmesIntro: An IB enquiry from Knowledge Park can mean any of three programmes, and the support looks different enough in each that the word tutor means three different jobs.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at higher or standard level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and internal assessments in most subjects. Tutoring divides between subject content, command-term precision and coursework process coaching. This is where specialism matters most, because a higher level subject is a genuinely different course from its standard level version.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in this corridor attend schools in Al Sufouh and Al Barsha, and their internal deadlines for coursework usually bite harder on the term than the external session does. Ask the school for those dates in writing; they are what a sensible plan is built around.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked from zero to eight, combining into a grade from one to seven. Support is criterion-specific rather than general: a weak criterion points at a named skill, and working on the subject as a whole is the slowest possible route to a better grade.
programmes.countryNote: Parents new to this programme are usually puzzled by reports with no percentages on them. The quickest useful step is to lay out the four criterion levels for each subject side by side and look for the outlier, then ask the teacher which task produced it.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led and transdisciplinary, with no external examinations. Requests here are usually about securing the foundations a later programme will assume: reading fluency, number sense, written structure and the habit of explaining reasoning aloud. Short, frequent sessions work far better than long ones.
programmes.countryNote: Families in the apartment belt around the free zones often ask for primary support in the year before a transfer, either into an MYP school or into a British-curriculum one. The useful work is the same either way and it is unglamorous: fluency rather than enrichment.

programmes.name: Moving into or out of the IB
programmes.description: Students arriving from British, American, Indian or national systems, or leaving the IB for A Levels. The work starts with an audit of what was covered and to what depth, because transfers arrive unevenly rather than uniformly behind, and a general revision programme is the wrong purchase for them.
programmes.countryNote: The free zones in this district have a relocation rhythm, so mid-year arrivals are routine here rather than exceptional. One audit session produces a short written gap list, which is cheaper and more accurate than months of broad coverage.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-knowledge-park.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects most requested from this corridor, with a note on where the marks are decided in each. Availability is disclosed honestly later on this page.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most requested subject from this district. Higher level is a different course rather than a harder one, and proof, calculus fluency and the exploration are where marks concentrate.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use. Students who chose it expecting an easier route find the modelling questions demand clear written justification.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Command-term discipline and uncertainty handling decide the grade as much as content. The HL extensions within each theme are the most under-rehearsed material in the subject.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Notation carries marks: state symbols, charges and mechanism arrow origins are marked as right or wrong, not as tidy or untidy.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Terminology precision and long answers with enough distinct points. The investigation and its internal deadline usually matter more to the term than the content does.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, definitions and the internal assessment commentaries. Students lose marks by writing well rather than by writing to the criteria.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application to a real context rather than description of the tool. The written assignment is where structure matters most.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper-one guided analysis. Fluent writers often score poorly because fluency is not analysis of the text's construction.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Structural rather than content support: claim, counterclaim, the use of a real example and a genuine evaluation. It is the component most often left too late.

subjects.name: Extended Essay

sections.heading: What an in-home IB tutor costs in Dubai, and what the money is for
paragraphs: Start with the figures, because most pages in this market will not give them to you. Published Dubai rates put an in-home one-to-one visit at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with the tutor's travel inside that fee. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to 300. At the specialist end, published rates run from about AED 200 to 450 or more, and one premium provider publishes AED 650. Monthly packages in this market include about AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Those numbers come from provider pages and from the Bestimate Dubai tutoring-cost table, each attributed. They are the market and not our price list. The reason to publish them is that three of the six competitor pages examined for this project publish no figure at all, and one of them asks what tutoring costs in its own list of questions and then declines to answer. A parent who cannot tell whether a quote is ordinary is negotiating blind.

What the premium buys is worth being precise about. It buys a person in the room, which has genuine value for a young child, for a student who will not stay on task alone, and for a household that wants the hour to be visibly supervised. It also buys a car journey. In Al Sufouh at 18:00 that journey is unpredictable, and a tutor who is late has eaten the first ten minutes of a sixty-minute lesson that was paid for in full.

What it does not buy is a better tutor. There is no mechanism by which driving to Knowledge Park improves somebody's grasp of Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at higher level. The premium is a logistics charge, and the honest question for a family is whether the in-room benefit is worth that charge given this particular child and this particular subject. For a nine-year-old who needs company, often yes. For a seventeen-year-old six weeks from a Diploma paper who needs a specialist, usually not.

sections.heading: Four provider models, compared on the things that actually differ
paragraphs: Every provider in this market compares itself favourably to an unnamed other platforms. That is not useful. What is useful is a model-level comparison, because the four ways of buying tutoring in Dubai differ systematically on price, on tutor pool, on what happens when a tutor is unavailable, and on whether you can verify anything before paying.

The four are an in-home agency sending a tutor to your address, an independent freelance tutor found by referral or classified advertisement, a tuition centre running small groups on its premises, and an online one-to-one platform. Each has a defensible case. The in-home agency offers presence and a replacement policy. A freelance tutor is usually the cheapest and carries the most variable quality. A centre is the cheapest per hour for content coverage and the weakest for diagnosis, because a group cannot be diagnosed individually. An online platform offers the widest tutor pool and requires a screen to be managed.

The table sets these out with the figures attributed. Two columns in it deserve attention because almost nobody publishes them. The first is the replacement position: what happens if your tutor leaves Dubai in March, which happens often enough in this city to matter. The second is permit verification, which applies to any individual tutoring in the UAE and is a question a parent is entitled to ask of any model.

Read the table as a decision aid rather than as advocacy. There are rows in it where in-home is the better buy, and we have not hidden them. What we would say is that for a Diploma student needing a specific higher level subject, the tutor-pool column is the one that decides it, and that is the column where geography stops helping.

sections.heading: Knowledge Park against the neighbourhoods next to it: does the answer change?
paragraphs: It is a fair question whether this argument is really about Knowledge Park or about Dubai generally, so here is the local version. Knowledge Park, Internet City and Media City form one continuous free-zone district in Al Sufouh with the tram along its edge. The Greens, The Views and Barsha Heights sit immediately inland. The Marina and JBR sit along the coast to the south-west. Those six areas have noticeably different journey profiles and almost identical conclusions.

The reason the conclusion holds across all of them is that the binding constraint is not distance but the tutor pool. A family in Barsha Heights has a genuinely short run to the Al Barsha schools and could support an in-home arrangement with less friction than a Marina family could. That changes the reliability column and leaves the specialism column untouched. If the requirement is Chemistry at higher level with real mechanism depth, a fifteen-minute journey does not widen the list of people who can teach it.

Where the local picture does change things is in session timing. Students returning to Al Sufouh or Barsha Heights can realistically start at 17:00 on most days. Students returning to the Marina or JBR cannot, and a session booked before 17:30 for them will be rescheduled within a month. For a family deciding between formats, that is the practical difference: an online slot survives a bad traffic day because nobody has to travel through it.

sections.heading: Availability and fallback, disclosed before you book
paragraphs: No competitor page examined for this project discloses a coverage limit. Several route UAE parents to a phone number in another country without saying so. We think the opposite approach is both more useful and better business, so here is how availability actually works and what happens when the match is not there.

Mainstream requests are matched quickly: Mathematics at standard level, the Diploma sciences at standard level, English A, Economics, and MYP support across most subject groups. Narrower requests take longer. A higher level subject with a specific gap, a less commonly taught Diploma subject, a particular language, or a request tied to an unusual time slot all draw on a smaller group. When that happens, the honest options are a different time, a short wait for the right tutor, or a marking clinic in the meantime so the weeks still produce something.

Where a tutor is not based in the UAE, we say so before a booking rather than after one. This matters for two reasons. The practical one is scheduling: a tutor in another time zone can be excellent and still be awkward for a 17:30 Gulf Standard Time slot, and you should know that in advance. The honest one is simply that a parent choosing a service has a right to know where the person teaching their child is sitting.

sections.heading: The permit question, which applies whoever comes to the door
paragraphs: Anyone considering an in-home tutor in Dubai should know that private tutoring here is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and the application runs through its smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, which is why no figure appears on this page: a number circulating online could not be verified and publishing it would be guesswork presented as fact. What matters for a parent is that asking a tutor about their permit is an ordinary question with an ordinary answer, and a tutor who becomes evasive has told you something.

A second point applies specifically to the idea of hiring a child's own schoolteacher privately. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules have been reported as barring school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct pointing the same way. Treat that as press-reported rather than as a quotation from the policy document, and verify it with the school if it is relevant. The practical advice is simply not to pursue that arrangement.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: it requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal. IB Gram holds no such permit because it operates no premises in the UAE, and we will never describe ourselves as KHDA approved. Where this page names a regulator it is to explain what that body does and point you at its own pages.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line that matters more than the delivery format
paragraphs: Whichever format a family chooses, the more important question is what the tutor is allowed to do with assessed work, and in this market the answers vary dangerously. One provider examined for this project sells completed internal assessments at a published price. That is an academic-malpractice trigger under the International Baccalaureate's own rules, and the consequence lands on the student rather than on the seller.

Our position, on every page and in every session: a tutor teaches, explains, sets work, marks it, and gives feedback on the student's own writing. For an internal assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or an MYP Personal Project, that means coaching the process. Narrowing a research question until it is answerable. Planning. Teaching how sources are evaluated and cited. Reading a draft the student wrote and replying with the questions an examiner or supervisor would ask next.

What a tutor must never do is write, draft, complete or rewrite any part of the work, supply data, or hand over another student's work as a model to adapt. If a provider offers any of that, the offer itself is the warning. We would rather lose the enquiry, and we say so plainly because a parent cannot easily tell providers apart on quality and can tell them apart instantly on this.

The school is the authority on what support is permitted for a specific piece of work. Supervisors set internal rules, record support given, and in some cases require a declaration. Ask them rather than assuming, and ask early, because the answer sometimes changes what kind of help is useful. A tutor who is unwilling to have that conversation with a school is not the right tutor regardless of format.

sections.heading: How a Knowledge Park family should actually decide
paragraphs: Three questions settle it, and none of them is about format. The first is how specific the requirement is. A Year 4 child who needs reading fluency and company can be helped by many people, and proximity is a reasonable thing to optimise for. A Diploma student six weeks from a higher level paper who needs a particular gap closed can be helped by few, and specialism is the only thing worth optimising for. Most families know which of those they are and then choose as though they were the other.

The second is reliability over a term. An arrangement is only worth what actually happens, and sixteen sessions booked is not sixteen sessions delivered. Count honestly: a format that loses two sessions a month to traffic, travel and rescheduling has lost a quarter of the block. For a family in the Marina or returning from Al Barsha, that is the realistic arithmetic, and it is a bigger effect than any plausible difference in teaching quality.

The third is what you can verify before paying. You can verify what level a tutor has taught, for how long, and whether they are available in the slot you need. You can ask about the permit. You can ask where they are based. You can ask what they will and will not do with coursework. A provider that answers all five clearly is worth more than one that scores better on a single column in a table, and the willingness to answer is itself the signal.

Our own answer to those three questions is why this page exists in the form it does. We do not sell the format being searched for. We sell the one where the tutor pool is national rather than local, where sessions do not depend on a car, and where availability and limits are disclosed before money changes hands. Where in-home genuinely suits your child better, we would rather say so on this page than argue with you about it on a call.
