faqs.question: How much does an IB home tutor cost in Dubai Knowledge Park?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates put an in-home one-to-one visit at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with the tutor's travel inside the fee, and monthly packages at around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with specialists from about AED 200 to 450 or more and one premium provider publishing AED 650. Those figures come from provider pages and the Bestimate Dubai rate table. The gap between in-home and online is almost entirely travel rather than teaching quality.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send a tutor to our address in Dubai Knowledge Park?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family address is a service we run only in India. Every lesson for a Knowledge Park family is delivered one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The argument for that is on this page rather than hidden: you select from everyone who has taught the subject at that level instead of from those who can reach Al Sufouh at six in the evening, you do not pay a travel premium, and no session is lost to the road.

faqs.question: Is in-home tutoring ever the better choice for a Dubai family?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it would be dishonest to pretend otherwise. For a young child, presence in the room is genuinely valuable: a seven-year-old working on reading fluency benefits from an adult beside them in a way a screen does not fully replicate. The same applies to a student who will not stay on task alone, or a household that wants the hour visibly supervised. Where the requirement is a specific higher level Diploma subject with a named gap, the calculation reverses, because the pool of people who can teach that well is small and geography shrinks it further.

faqs.question: Why would a specialist tutor not live near the free zones?
faqs.answer: Because there is no reason they would. The number of people in Dubai who have taught a particular Diploma subject at higher level to examination is modest, and they are distributed across the emirate and beyond it according to where they live and work rather than according to where demand is. Requiring one to be within driving distance of Al Sufouh at a particular hour is an additional constraint that removes most of the list. Online matching drops that constraint and keeps the teaching-history requirement, which is the one that affects your child's grade.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor we are matched with leaves Dubai?
faqs.answer: In an online arrangement, far less than you would expect, because the match was never tied to geography in the first place: a replacement is selected on the same basis as the original. In-home arrangements are more exposed, and Dubai's turnover makes this a real risk rather than a hypothetical one. It is worth asking any provider what their replacement position is before you book, and treating a vague answer as an answer. We change tutor at no cost whenever a match turns out to be wrong, for whatever reason.

faqs.question: Does a tutor visiting a Knowledge Park home need a UAE permit, and can we check it?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any figure you read as unverified. Asking a tutor about their permit is an ordinary question; evasiveness is informative.

faqs.question: Can we hire our child's own teacher from their Dubai school privately?
faqs.answer: It is not an arrangement to pursue. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules have been reported as prohibiting school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct pointing in the same direction. Treat those as press-reported rather than as quotations from the policy documents, and check with the school if it matters in your case. Beyond the rules, it places a teacher in an awkward position with respect to their own assessment of your child.

faqs.question: How does a tuition centre group class compare with one-to-one?
faqs.answer: A centre is usually the cheapest route per hour and the weakest for diagnosis. In a group, nobody reads one student's script closely enough to notice that they are losing marks to command-term length rather than to content, which is the kind of finding that actually changes a grade. Centres work reasonably for content coverage where a student is simply behind on material, and they work poorly for a student who understands the subject and is not scoring it. If you use one, pair it with occasional one-to-one marking rather than with more group hours.

faqs.question: What should we ask any IB tutor before booking, whatever the format?
faqs.answer: Five questions. Which level of this subject have you taught, and for how long? Have you taken students through to examination in it? Where are you based, and in which time zone will you be teaching? Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? And what exactly will you do, and refuse to do, with an internal assessment or Extended Essay? Clear answers to all five are worth more than a better figure in any single column of a comparison, and the willingness to answer is itself the signal.

faqs.question: How many of the sessions we book will actually happen over a term?
faqs.answer: That is the right question and almost nobody asks it. An eight-week block with two sessions a week is sixteen appointments, and what matters is how many take place. In-home arrangements in this part of Dubai lose sessions to traffic, to tutor travel and to rescheduling, and for a family returning to the Marina the loss over a term is material. An online slot only has to survive the household rather than the road. Over a block that difference outweighs any plausible gap in teaching quality between two competent tutors.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects take longest to match for a family near the Al Sufouh free zones?
faqs.answer: Higher level requests with a specific gap, less commonly taught Diploma subjects, and particular languages. Standard level maths and sciences, English A, Economics and most MYP subject groups are matched quickly. Where a request is narrow we tell you the expected wait in writing before you book, and if we cannot cover it properly we say so rather than offering a generalist. No competitor page examined for this project discloses a coverage limit at all, which is why we put ours in a table on this page.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay or an internal assessment?
faqs.answer: With the process, yes; with the writing, never. A tutor can help your child narrow a research question until it is answerable, plan the work, learn how sources are evaluated and cited, and respond to the drafts your child wrote with the questions an examiner or supervisor would ask next. A tutor must not write, draft, complete or rewrite any part of it, or supply data or another student's work as a model. Your child's supervisor sets the rules for what support is permitted in their case, so ask them early rather than assuming.

faqs.question: What time can sessions start for a student living near the free zones?
faqs.answer: Around 17:00 for students returning to Al Sufouh, Barsha Heights, The Greens or The Views, and 17:30 or later for those coming back to the Marina or JBR. Those are not preferences but observations: slots booked earlier in optimism get rescheduled, and a rescheduled session in a sequential subject costs a week rather than an hour. Because nothing is delivered by car, the only thing the slot has to survive is the household's own evening, which is why fixed weekly times hold through a term here.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have an office in Dubai we can visit?
faqs.answer: No. We operate no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE, and we would not claim one. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education, and no page on this site will imply otherwise. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; we do not hold one because we have no premises. Where this page names a regulator, it is to explain what that body does and link its own site.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-knowledge-park.closingHeading: The comparison, and then the honest recommendation
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-knowledge-park.closingBody: If your child is young, needs company to stay on task, and the subject is general, an in-room arrangement is a reasonable buy and we are not the right provider for it. If your child is in the Diploma, needs a specific subject at a specific level, and has a term or eight weeks to use well, then the tutor pool is the only column that decides anything and geography is working against you. Tell us the programme, the subject, the level and what is actually going wrong, and we will tell you which of those two you are in, what the match time looks like, and where the tutor is based. Lessons run one-to-one, online, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Is there anyone near La Mer who really knows the IB?
paragraphs: Start with the honest version. La Mer is a low-rise beachfront district on the Jumeirah 1 shoreline, with a residential population measured in hundreds of households rather than thousands. Draw a twenty-minute driving radius around it and you capture Jumeirah 1, 2 and 3, Al Wasl, Al Safa, Umm Suqeim, City Walk and Pearl Jumeira. That is a wealthy, school-dense slice of Dubai. It is still a small catchment when the thing you need is a teacher who has marked a Physics HL paper or supervised a Mathematics exploration to the current criteria.

The reason is simple counting. International Baccalaureate programmes account for roughly 7 per cent of enrolment across Dubai's 227 private schools, against 37 per cent on UK curricula and 26 per cent on Indian ones, in KHDA's 2024-25 figures. Every one of those IB schools employs a handful of Diploma teachers per subject. Of those teachers, the ones free to tutor in the evening are fewer still, and Abu Dhabi's ADEK ethics rules and the MoHRE permit code of conduct both bar a teacher from taking paid work with students enrolled at their own school. A local search therefore returns agencies, generalists and university students far more often than it returns a subject specialist.

So when a parent in La Mer types the phrase into Google and gets a page promising a tutor at a Jumeirah address within forty-eight hours, the question worth asking is which subject, at which level, and who. A tutor who covers Maths, Physics, Chemistry and Economics across MYP and DP is a tutor who covers none of them to examiner depth. The Diploma is six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and an internal assessment in almost every course. Each of those has its own criteria and its own common failure modes.

IB Gram's answer is to stop treating the twenty-minute radius as the selection pool. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time and to your child's own school deadlines. That decouples the match from geography: a La Mer household can work with a Chemistry HL teacher who has supervised dozens of explorations, rather than with whoever happens to live two streets away and is willing to drive.

What follows is the detail a local search does not give you. How to test a tutor's syllabus knowledge in a single conversation. What the Dubai market actually charges, by tier, with each figure attributed. What the travel premium on a home visit is really buying. Which schools the Jumeirah coast feeds and what their timetables do to a 4pm start. What the permit rules say about the person teaching your child. And where the line sits between legitimate coursework teaching and academic malpractice.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-la-mer.programmesIntro: La Mer sits inside a cluster of IB continuum and dual-curriculum schools, so a family here may be dealing with any of three programmes at once: a younger child on PYP inquiry units, a middle child on MYP criteria, and a Diploma candidate counting down to the May session.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Six transdisciplinary themes, no formal external examination, and an exhibition in the final year. Reports describe approaches to learning rather than percentages, which is why parents often cannot tell whether a child is behind. Tutoring at this stage is diagnostic: number fluency, reading stamina, and the writing conventions a MYP teacher will assume are already in place.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, PYP runs alongside the KHDA mandatory subjects, so a Year 4 child in a Jumeirah school is also studying Arabic, Islamic Education where applicable, and Social Studies. Those lessons are built on a 40-minute unit and taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, which is often where a La Mer family first meets a language gap they did not expect.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked 0-8, converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. The personal project lands in the final year. Students who have never had the criteria explained to them tend to write good content that scores badly, because criterion wording rewards specific moves and penalises their absence.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools on the Jumeirah coast run MYP to Year 11 and then split into Diploma or A Level, while others switch to IGCSE at Year 10. A La Mer parent choosing between those routes is choosing between criterion-referenced internal assessment and terminal written papers, and the two demand different study habits from about Year 8 onward.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Marked out of 45. Internal assessment typically carries 20 to 25 per cent of a subject grade and is submitted long before the written papers, so the pressure peaks in DP1 summer and DP2 autumn rather than in the exam term.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the May session, which is the one Dubai schools timetable around. The November session exists as a resit and relocation route. Because the IB does not publish its calendar in a form we can verify automatically, treat your school's IB coordinator as the authority on every internal and upload deadline for your child's cohort.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more DP courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project, personal and professional skills, service learning and language development. Fewer Dubai schools offer it than offer the Diploma, so a family considering it usually needs help understanding how universities read the transcript.
programmes.countryNote: For a Dubai student, the practical question with CP is Ministry of Education equivalency, which is assessed on the certificate presented rather than on the programme's name. Verify the requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation channel before committing, because no IB points threshold has been published in a form worth repeating here.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-la-mer.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma and MYP courses La Mer and wider Jumeirah 1 families ask for most. Each note says what the course actually assesses and where marks go missing, because that is what determines how many hours of support a student needs.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency, with Paper 3 at Higher Level rewarding extended unseen problem-solving. Marks are lost in method communication rather than arithmetic: students who jump to an answer forfeit the working marks that make up most of a long question.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-assisted work. The graphic display calculator is assumed, not optional, and students who never learned its regression and distribution functions lose straightforward marks. HL adds matrices, graph theory and a heavier statistical load.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields, thermodynamics and the option topics, with multiple-choice, structured and data-analysis papers. Uncertainty handling and graph linearisation decide the data paper, and these are skills a school rarely has time to drill between other content.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. Organic reaction pathways and the reasoning behind equilibrium shifts are the standard pressure points, and the exploration needs a measurable, controllable variable chosen months before the write-up.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cell biology through to physiology and ecology, assessed heavily on command terms. Students who answer 'explain' questions as 'describe' questions cap themselves early, and statistical treatment of data in the exploration is where most marks are recoverable.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, with three commentaries drawn from published news articles. Diagram accuracy and explicit evaluation carry the paper; HL adds policy calculation questions that reward practised arithmetic.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisational structure, finance, marketing and operations, with a research project at Higher Level based on a real organisation. Tools applied mechanically score poorly; the marks sit in applying one framework to the specific firm in the case.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Non-literary and literary texts, with a Paper 1 guided analysis, a Paper 2 comparative essay and the individual oral on a global issue. Students lose marks by summarising rather than analysing how meaning is constructed.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: System fundamentals, computational thinking and a solution developed for a real client. The internal assessment stalls when the client and success criteria are vague, so the first support sessions are usually about scoping rather than code.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Receptive, productive and interactive skills on prescribed themes. For Dubai students this sits alongside the KHDA mandatory Arabic lessons, which follow Ministry content and cannot be supplemented with different material without prior ministry permission.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects with commentaries and a prescribed-title essay. Marks come from sustained argument about knowledge claims, not from examples; students who collect anecdotes without a thesis plateau in the middle band.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece in a chosen subject, supervised in school and assessed against five criteria. The research question is the whole game: too broad and the essay describes, too narrow and the evidence runs out.

sections.heading: What 'IB home tutor in La Mer' returns, and what it leaves out
paragraphs: Search that phrase from a La Mer address and you get three kinds of result. First, agency landing pages that name the neighbourhood in a heading and then describe a service identical to the one they describe for forty other neighbourhoods. Second, classified listings from individuals, most of whom teach a broad spread of subjects and levels. Third, tuition centres several kilometres inland that would require a drive each way. None of those results tells you the one thing that matters, which is whether a named person who knows your child's specific course at your child's specific level is available at a time your child can actually work.

That omission is not an accident. Proximity is the cheapest thing a tutoring page can claim and the hardest for a parent to verify. A page can say it serves La Mer without a single tutor living within ten kilometres, because the promise is about dispatch rather than residence. Of the competitor pages read in October 2026 for this market, three published no hourly figure at all, and the one page with a published rate contradicted its own structured data. Neighbourhood claims in that environment are worth very little.

The useful move is to invert the question. Instead of asking who is nearby, ask what the shortlist looks like when distance is removed. For a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level student at a Jumeirah school, the relevant pool is every teacher who has taught that course to examination, not every teacher who could reach Jumeirah 1 by 5pm. Those are very different lists, and only one of them is likely to contain somebody who can explain why a Paper 3 investigation question is structured the way it is.

IB Gram's position on the phrase is therefore plain. We target it because it is what parents type. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India. What a La Mer family gets instead is a subject specialist on live video, in a fixed weekly slot, with the travel time returned to the student.

sections.heading: The arithmetic of a local IB tutor pool around Jumeirah 1
paragraphs: Work the numbers that KHDA publishes and the shape of the problem becomes clear. Dubai had 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, taught across 17 different curricula. International Baccalaureate programmes held about 7 per cent of that enrolment. UK curricula held 37 per cent, Indian 26 per cent and US 14 per cent. The IB share is real but minority, and it is distributed across schools spread from Al Barsha to Nad Al Sheba rather than concentrated on the Jumeirah coast.

Now apply that to a single course. A school running the Diploma typically staffs each subject with two or three teachers, one of whom may be the coordinator with a reduced teaching load. For a less-populated Higher Level course, the whole emirate's teaching body for that course is small enough to fit in a seminar room. The subset available on a weekday evening, not barred by their employer's ethics policy from tutoring their own students, and living close enough to Jumeirah 1 to make a home visit viable, is smaller again.

This is why the travel-based model quietly substitutes availability for expertise. If the brief is 'Physics Higher Level, Thursday 5pm, within twenty minutes of La Mer', something has to give, and in practice what gives is the subject depth. The family ends up with a capable graduate who knows physics but has never read the current assessment criteria, or with a teacher stretched across four courses. Both can help a struggling student with basics. Neither reliably moves a 5 to a 7, because that movement depends on knowing exactly what the mark scheme rewards.

sections.heading: Six questions that test whether a tutor knows your child's syllabus
paragraphs: You do not need to be an IB teacher to tell a specialist from a generalist. You need six questions, asked in one conversation, and the confidence to end the conversation if the answers are vague. Every one of these has a concrete correct answer that a teacher of the course gives immediately and that somebody who has only read a textbook cannot fake.

Ask what the internal assessment in this subject is worth as a percentage of the final grade, and when the school's internal deadline usually falls relative to the written papers. Ask which paper carries the data-analysis or extended-response load and how long it runs. Ask what the command term in the student's last lost mark was asking for, and how the answer should have been structured. Ask which two topics in this course produce the most avoidable errors and why. Ask what a tutor is permitted to do with a draft under academic-honesty rules. Ask what the first session would cover and what evidence would show in four weeks.

The answers tell you three things. Whether the person has taught the course to examination, because assessment weightings and deadline rhythms are not memorable unless you have lived them. Whether they diagnose or deliver, because a teacher who asks about the last lost mark is reading the student rather than performing a lesson plan. And whether they understand the honesty boundary, which matters enormously once an exploration or an Extended Essay is in play, since a breach is the student's problem to carry, not the tutor's.
Run this test on anyone, including us. It is the fastest way to turn a proximity search into a competence check, and it costs one phone call.

sections.heading: What Dubai families pay, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Published rates for this market were read from providers' own pages in October 2026. At the bottom of the market, online sessions with university students or early-career tutors are advertised from AED 33 to 65 an hour by platform providers, with the broader budget band running to about AED 150. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between AED 150 and 300, with one agency listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors are quoted from AED 200 to 450 and above, with one UK-based agency listing AED 270. Premium named or examiner-badged tutors reach AED 500 to 650 and beyond.

In-home one-to-one visits, with travel included, are quoted between AED 180 and 500 an hour, with a cost comparison service putting the common band at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors reaching AED 500. Monthly packaging follows the same split: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, against AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. For a weekly one-hour habit, the same source estimates AED 240 to 600 a month at budget level, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support.

Read those two sets of numbers together and the travel premium is roughly AED 60 to 150 an hour. It is worth asking what that buys. It does not buy more teaching minutes, because the hour is the hour. It buys physical presence, which genuinely helps a younger child who will not sit still on a screen, and it buys the parent the ability to overhear the lesson. It costs the tutor forty to eighty minutes of unpaid driving per session, which is precisely why the travelling pool skews towards whoever lives nearby rather than whoever knows the course.

None of these figures is IB Gram's price list. They are the market, cited so a La Mer family can judge any quote they are given, including ours, against something external. For our own rates, the free trial lesson and the consultation that follows are the right place to ask.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against a tutor in the room, judged on this neighbourhood
paragraphs: The fair comparison is not online versus in-person in the abstract. It is online versus the in-person option actually available to a household on the Jumeirah 1 coast, at the time of day a school student can work, for the specific course in question. Framed that way, the trade-offs are concrete.

A tutor arriving in the room brings presence and removes the screen. For a Year 5 child who drifts, that is decisive. It also brings a hard scheduling floor: the tutor must leave somewhere else, cross Jumeirah Beach Road or Al Wasl in afternoon traffic, and arrive before the session can begin. A cancellation two hours out is common because one delayed journey collapses the evening. And the subject pool shrinks to people who will accept that drive for that fee.

Online one-to-one over live video removes the drive from both sides. A 4.15pm slot is genuinely 4.15pm. The tutor is selected for the course rather than the commute, so a Chemistry Higher Level student gets a Chemistry Higher Level teacher. Screen sharing puts a past paper, a mark scheme reference and the student's own exploration draft side by side, which is awkward on a dining table. Lessons can be recorded for the student's own revision, and a parent can read a written note afterwards instead of hovering. Against that, it asks more of the student's self-regulation, and it needs a quiet room with a stable connection.

sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child permitted to tutor in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is a permitted activity with a permit attached to it. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The service is listed as 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days.

Individuals offering private tutoring without that permit are, in the federal government's own wording, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any specific figure quoted to you about penalties should be treated as unverified. What matters for a parent is the simpler point: the permit exists, it is free, and there is no good reason for a working tutor not to hold one.

A second rule sits on top of it. A code of conduct attached to the permit bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and Abu Dhabi's ADEK has set professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff along the same lines. So a parent who arranges for their child's own classroom teacher to tutor them privately for a fee is pushing that teacher into a position their employer and the permit both prohibit. It feels like the obvious shortcut. It is the one arrangement to avoid.

A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai is a separate matter again: that requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE centre or office, and makes no claim of approval, accreditation or endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Any page telling you otherwise about itself is worth a second look.

sections.heading: Where the line sits on an exploration, an Extended Essay or a TOK task
paragraphs: This is the part of the market that carries real risk for the student rather than for the provider. Internal assessment work in the Diploma must be the student's own, authenticated by a supervising teacher at the school. A breach is handled as malpractice and the consequences land on the candidate's diploma, not on whoever helped.

So the boundary is worth stating precisely. A tutor may explain what each assessment criterion asks for and how marks are distributed across the criteria. A tutor may discuss whether a research question is answerable with the evidence available, or whether a chosen independent variable can actually be controlled in a school laboratory. A tutor may read what a student has written and say which criterion is underserved and why. A tutor may teach the statistical method, the referencing convention or the paragraph structure the student then applies themselves.

A tutor may not write any part of the submission. No tutor should draft the Extended Essay introduction, supply a worked exploration for a student to adapt, rewrite a TOK commentary into their own prose, or produce the Personal Project write-up. One provider in this market advertises completed internal assessments for sale at a four-figure AED price. That is not a cheaper version of tutoring; it is the thing that gets a diploma withdrawn. We will not supply it and will say so plainly to any family who asks.

The practical consequence is that coursework support has to start earlier than most families expect. If the only legitimate help is teaching and feedback on the student's own work, then there must be work to give feedback on, which means sessions in the scoping and first-draft weeks rather than the fortnight before the deadline. For a DP1 student in La Mer, that normally means beginning in the spring term rather than the autumn of DP2.
bullets: Legitimate: criteria explanation, question scoping, method teaching, feedback on the student's own text
Not legitimate: drafting, rewriting, supplying model answers to adapt, or producing the submission

sections.heading: The Diploma year counted backwards, and the IGCSE sessions around it
paragraphs: Most families plan forwards from today and run out of time. The useful exercise is to count backwards from the session, because every fixed date in the Diploma sits months before the written papers rather than next to them. UAE candidates sit the May session; the November session exists as a resit and relocation route. Because the IB's own calendar cannot be verified automatically for this page, every specific internal, upload and results date for your child's cohort should come from the school's IB coordinator, who holds the version that applies to them.

What can be stated with sources is the Cambridge and Pearson position, and it matters because most Jumeirah IB students sat IGCSEs first or have siblings sitting them now. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge is explicit that the correct zone timetable must be used and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Two scheduling realities in Dubai sit on top of the official calendar. Ramadan shortens the school day and shifts family routines, so revision that assumes a normal evening will not survive it; moving sessions to a post-iftar slot is routine and should be planned rather than improvised. And the long summer break falls directly between DP1 and DP2, which is the single best window for exploration and Extended Essay work because it is the only period with no competing school deadlines.

Always link to the live official timetable rather than relying on a restated date. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and they can be revised, which is exactly why a page like this one names months and sources rather than printing a future calendar.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory UAE subjects and the week they actually leave you
paragraphs: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and it publishes an inspection report for each school on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. That report is the document to read before you read anyone's marketing, including a school's own. Across the UAE the picture is federated: ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

For a La Mer family the KHDA rule with the biggest timetable consequence is the mandatory-subject requirement. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with the current requirements due to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, lesson length may vary provided the weekly total is met, and at least 25 minutes is advised for any mandatory-subject lesson.

Two things follow. The first is practical: those lessons occupy real timetable space, so an IB Diploma student in Dubai is carrying a slightly fuller week than the programme alone suggests, and a tutoring plan that ignores it over-books the evenings. The second is a constraint on what tutoring can legitimately do. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so support there has to be skills work on the school's own material rather than an alternative syllabus. Schools are also required to ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects, which is a credential a parent can ask about directly.

One more piece of context for budgeting. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For the same intake, seven new private schools, four on UK curricula and three on the International Baccalaureate, add 16,846 places; six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. A flat fee year and more IB places are both reasons to spend the tutoring budget on depth rather than on travel.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and what IB families should verify
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process that converts a foreign school certificate into something UAE authorities and universities can read. It is handled by the Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation channels, and it is not something a tutoring provider performs, arranges or guarantees. What a provider can usefully do is tell you the sourced parts and point you at the authority for the rest.

For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among the five required subjects. That last detail matters: one page ranking in this market tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published rule. For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics by at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

For the International Baccalaureate, no points threshold has been read on a ministry source for this page, so none is published here. Any figure you see quoted for IB equivalency should be checked against moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority before you plan around it. Tutoring is not required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory process.

The practical reading for a La Mer household is about subject choice in Year 11 and DP1. A student dropping to five Diploma subjects, or choosing a Mathematics route that a target university does not accept, creates a problem that no amount of later tutoring fixes. That conversation belongs with the school's counsellor and with the ministry's own published requirements, early, and a tutor's job is to make sure the chosen subjects are actually survivable at the chosen level.

faqs.question: Can IB Gram send an IB home tutor to a La Mer address?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition online, over live video, to families in La Mer and everywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. We target the home-tutor search because it is the phrase parents use, and we answer it honestly rather than promising a doorstep arrival we do not provide. What a La Mer family gets instead is a tutor chosen for the subject and level rather than for proximity, in a fixed slot that starts when the school run ends rather than after a cross-Jumeirah drive.

faqs.question: How many IB Diploma specialists realistically live within reach of La Mer?
faqs.answer: Fewer than the search results suggest. International Baccalaureate programmes carry about 7 per cent of enrolment across Dubai's 227 private schools, and each IB school staffs two or three teachers per Diploma subject. Narrow that to teachers free on a weekday evening, not barred by their employer's ethics policy from tutoring their own school's students, and living close enough to Jumeirah 1 for a visit to be viable, and the pool for a specific Higher Level course becomes very small. That is the structural reason an area-based search returns generalists and agencies more often than specialists.

faqs.question: What does an IB tutor cost per hour for a Jumeirah 1 family?
faqs.answer: Rates read from provider pages in October 2026 put budget online tutoring at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150 to 300, an IB or IGCSE specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, and premium named tutors at AED 500 to 650 or more. In-home visits with travel included are quoted from AED 180 to 500. Those are market figures, not our price list. For our own rates, start with the free trial lesson and ask during the consultation that follows.

faqs.question: Is the travel premium on a home visit in Jumeirah worth paying?
faqs.answer: It depends on the child's age. Comparing the published bands, roughly AED 60 to 150 of an in-home hourly rate is the journey rather than the teaching. For a primary-age child who will not settle in front of a screen, physical presence can be decisive and the premium is defensible. For a Diploma student working on an exploration or past papers, the same money buys more by going towards subject depth, because screen sharing handles document-heavy work better than a dining table does and the tutor can be chosen from a far wider pool.

faqs.question: How do I check whether a tutor actually knows my child's IB course?
faqs.answer: Ask six questions in one call. What is the internal assessment worth as a percentage, and when does the school deadline usually fall? Which paper carries the data or extended-response load, and how long is it? What was the command term in the last mark my child lost? Which two topics in this course cause the most avoidable errors? What may a tutor do with a draft under academic-honesty rules? What would session one cover? A teacher who has taught the course to examination answers all six without hesitating.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor working with a La Mer family need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit issued through MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The federal guidance states that individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. Since the permit costs nothing, there is no good reason for a working tutor not to hold one.

faqs.question: Can a La Mer child's own schoolteacher tutor them privately in the evening?
faqs.answer: That is the one arrangement to avoid. The code of conduct attached to the MoHRE private tuition permit bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and Abu Dhabi's ADEK has set professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff along the same lines. It looks like the obvious shortcut because the teacher already knows the class, but it puts them in conflict with both their employer and the permit. A specialist from outside the school carries no such conflict and can be chosen for the exact course and level.

faqs.question: Can an IB tutor help with the Mathematics exploration or the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can explain each assessment criterion and its mark allocation, discuss whether a research question is answerable with the available evidence, teach the statistical or referencing method, and give feedback on text the student has already produced. No tutor writes, redrafts or supplies any part of the submission, because internal assessment must be the student's own work and a breach is assessed against the candidate. In practice this means starting in the scoping weeks rather than the fortnight before the school deadline.

faqs.question: When do IB students in Dubai actually sit their examinations?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the May session, which is the one Dubai schools timetable around; the November session exists as a resit and relocation route. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on this page because the IB's own calendar could not be verified from its website for this project, and a wrong date is worse than no date. Your school's IB coordinator holds the version that applies to your child's cohort, including every internal and upload deadline, and that is the authority to plan from.

faqs.question: My child sits IGCSEs before the Diploma. Which series applies in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series; the February and March series is offered to India only, so it does not apply to a Dubai candidate. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and Cambridge states the correct zone timetable must be used, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Check the live official timetable, since provisional versions can be revised.

faqs.question: How does the KHDA mandatory-subject rule affect a tutoring timetable in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students and combined classes prohibited. Instructional time is built on a 40-minute lesson unit. Those lessons take real timetable space, so a Dubai student carries a slightly fuller week than the international programme alone implies. A tutoring plan that ignores it over-books the evenings, which is why we map sessions against the full school week rather than the subject list.

faqs.question: Can tutoring cover Arabic or Islamic Education alongside the IB?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the limit is worth knowing. KHDA requires that for mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so legitimate support is skills work on the school's own material rather than an alternative syllabus. Schools must also ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects, which is a credential you can ask your school about directly. Support therefore focuses on language skills, reading fluency and assessment technique.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for my child's subject and slot?
faqs.answer: You hear it at the shortlist stage rather than after paying. For thinly covered courses such as Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Physics at Higher Level or standalone Theory of Knowledge support, we name the fallback: a specialist matched outside the emirate in the same rate band, a coursework tutor paired with a content tutor, or a slot further into the week. No competitor page read for this market admits a coverage limit exists, which is precisely why we state ours in writing.

faqs.question: What time can an online session realistically start for a La Mer student?
faqs.answer: School days on the Jumeirah coast end between roughly 2.15pm and 3.15pm depending on year group, so 4.00 to 4.15pm is a realistic first slot once a child is home and has eaten. Because nobody has to drive, that slot holds. An in-home option in the same household usually cannot start before 5pm, since the tutor has to cross Jumeirah Beach Road or the Al Wasl junction between 4 and 6pm. Friday timetables finish earlier, which is why Friday evening slots fill first here.

faqs.question: Is online one-to-one tuition effective for a student who prefers a person in the room?
faqs.answer: For most Diploma and MYP students, yes, provided the format is used properly. A shared screen puts a past paper, a mark scheme reference and the student's own draft side by side, which is harder on a table. Sessions can be recorded for revision and a written note goes to the parent afterwards. The genuine trade-off is self-regulation: a younger child who drifts benefits more from physical presence. For those families we say so rather than selling the format that happens to be the one we deliver.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-living-legends.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are Diploma Programme and Middle Years Programme teachers working with families in Living Legends and the surrounding communities. Each one is listed by course and level, because a Biology HL brief and a Biology SL brief are not the same job.

intro.heading: One gated community, and almost no local Diploma specialists
paragraphs: Living Legends is a single master community rather than a district: villas and apartment towers arranged around a golf course, gated, sitting off Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road between Dubai Sports City, Motor City and Remraam. That compactness is pleasant to live in and unhelpful for finding a tutor, because tutor supply follows population density and road access, and a self-contained community of this size supports a handful of generalists at best. The chance that one of them has taught Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level recently is small.

The Diploma makes that scarcity matter more than it would for other curricula. Six subjects across two levels, three core components, internal assessments moderated against published criteria, and papers that differ between Higher and Standard Level in content, duration and weighting. The useful qualification in a tutor is not a degree in the subject but recent experience of this course at this level. A capable graduate can explain a topic and still miss that a student is losing marks to command-term misreading, which is where a large share of Diploma marks go.

There is a practical layer specific to gated communities that nobody writing about home tutoring mentions. A visiting tutor needs to be registered at the gate, or met, or given a pass. Parking has to be sorted. If the session is at six and the tutor arrives at ten past because security took five minutes, the family has paid for an hour and received fifty minutes. Twice a week, across a school year, that is a real quantity of lost teaching and a recurring small irritation that wears out an arrangement.

Then there is the permit question, which applies anywhere in the Emirates. Private tuition is regulated: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. A parent in a gated community is entitled to ask about it before letting somebody into the house, and the fact that the permit is free means there is no excuse for not holding one.

IB Gram's answer removes the gate, the drive and the radius from the problem at once. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, so the constraint becomes the subject and the level rather than who can reach the community at a usable hour. We do not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India, and saying so plainly matters more than a soft answer. The rest of this page covers what a visit actually involves here, how the formats compare, what the market charges, how the exam calendar works backwards, and where a tutor's role ends.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-living-legends.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes and one common alternative are in play for families here, often across siblings. These notes focus on what each one asks of a student in a community this size.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examinations. Progress comes through units of inquiry, a portfolio and the Year 6 Exhibition, a student-led project rather than a test. The habit that matters at this stage is explaining reasoning aloud, because the Middle Years Programme asks for written justification from the first term and children who were never asked to produce it stall in Year 7.
programmes.countryNote: Primary-age children here travel to schools in Motor City, Sports City or Remraam, so journeys are short and afternoon sessions are genuinely available. That is the one age group in Living Legends for which local timing is easy, and it is worth using while it lasts.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Each subject marked against four criteria, A to D, on a 0-8 scale against published descriptors, with the Personal Project in the final year. Marks go missing where a student answers the question but not the criterion, which is a diagnosable problem and a fixable one once somebody works from the rubric rather than a textbook.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Living Legends often meet the MYP after a move, because the surrounding communities mix British and IB provision within a few kilometres. A student arriving from a Year 9 International GCSE track into MYP 4 has the content and not the criterion habit, which is a term of work rather than a year.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher and three Standard, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked against published criteria and moderated by the IB. A plan built for the wrong level wastes hours on material the student will never be examined on.
programmes.countryNote: Candidates at UAE schools sit the May session, and the deadlines a student here actually works to are set by their own coordinator months earlier. Families in this community tend to arrive asking about internal assessment support a term later than the point at which it would have helped most.

programmes.name: A Levels as the local alternative
programmes.description: The surrounding school supply includes strong British-curriculum provision, so siblings in one Living Legends household are frequently split between the Diploma and A Levels. Cambridge International A Level runs in June and November series, which puts the two children on different annual rhythms.
programmes.countryNote: A household holding both routes needs two calendars respected in one week, and the peaks do not coincide. That is manageable when nothing has to travel and awkward when a visiting tutor is involved, which is one of the quieter reasons mixed-route families in this community end up working online.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-living-legends.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma courses families in and around Living Legends ask about most, with the level and the specific place marks are lost. A request that names the course and level is matched in hours; one that says IB science has to be unpicked first.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-dense and vocabulary-dependent. A student can recall a process accurately and score two of six because the answer is not structured as the markscheme reads it. Statistical treatment of internal assessment data is where otherwise strong candidates drop a band.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry underpins everything quantitative, and organic mechanisms decide the Higher Level grade. The standard loss is a describe answer where the command term asked for an explanation, and equations that balance without the state symbols required.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and electricity carry the marks and are taught early, so gaps compound for two years. Unit and significant-figure discipline costs marks on content the student understands, and Higher Level questions routinely combine two topics in one item.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, functions and calculus, with one paper sat without a graphical calculator. Marks are lost in method communication: a correct answer with no visible reasoning collects a fraction of what the question offers.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-led and calculator-active throughout, with modelling questions that must be answered in words as well as numbers. Students who chose it to avoid algebra are often surprised by the writing demand in the exploration.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides a large share of the marks: axes labelled, curves shifted correctly, the new equilibrium identified. The internal assessment commentaries depend on choosing usable published articles, and unusable choices are the common early error.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools must be applied to the case rather than described. Students who learned to define terms for International GCSE keep defining them and run out of time on the questions where the marks actually are.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two assessed orals and papers on unseen texts. The Individual Oral needs a global issue narrow enough to sustain for ten minutes, and students routinely choose one far too broad. Close analysis of how a text works is what lifts a grade.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition. Progress depends on discussion rather than drill, so the sessions need room to breathe. Short weekday slots rarely achieve much; a longer fortnightly block does more.

subjects.name: Arabic B and ab initio
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic regardless of licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students. Productive skills carry the assessment weight and benefit from short frequent practice.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-living-legends.regionsIntro: Living Legends sits among communities that supply its schools, its traffic and its tutor market. These notes are about what each one means operationally for a family inside the gates.

sections.heading: What a home visit to a gated community actually involves
paragraphs: Nobody selling in-home tutoring describes the logistics, so here they are. A visiting tutor coming to Living Legends has to get through a gate. Depending on the arrangement that means being pre-registered by the household, being met, collecting a pass, or waiting while security confirms the visit. Parking has to be found. None of this is onerous once, and all of it is a recurring friction twice a week for thirty-odd weeks.

The cost shows up as teaching minutes. A tutor booked for six o'clock who clears the gate at ten past has delivered fifty minutes of a sixty-minute lesson, and the family has paid for sixty. Over a school year at two sessions a week that is a substantial amount of tuition lost to administration. The second cost is reliability: a tutor who hits traffic on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and arrives at twenty past has effectively cancelled half the session, and this happens often enough to erode an arrangement by the second term.

The third cost is the one that shapes the market. Tutors price access. A specialist willing to drive from Al Barsha or the Marina to a gated community off a major arterial road, twice a week, at the hour everybody wants, is pricing the journey and the uncertainty into the fee. That is why in-home rates in Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The gap is logistics, not pedagogy.

None of this makes in-home tutoring wrong. For a child under about ten, or a student with significant attention difficulties, physical presence does real work and is worth paying for. For a Diploma student working on papers and data on a screen anyway, it is an expensive solution to a problem that no longer exists. The table below compares the two honestly, including where in-home wins.

sections.heading: Why a community this size cannot supply a Diploma specialist
paragraphs: This is arithmetic rather than opinion. Independent tutors build a diary from the families within reach, and the number of families within reach of a single gated community is small. Of those families, only some have Diploma students. Of those, only some need a particular subject, and only some of those need it at Higher Level. Follow that chain down and the local demand for, say, Chemistry Higher Level in one community is perhaps a household or two in a given year, which cannot sustain a specialist.

So specialists do not locate themselves by community; they locate themselves by access, and then they travel. The ones who travel to gated communities off arterial roads charge for it, and the ones who do not travel widen their subject range until the diary fills with whatever is nearby. Both are rational responses, and neither produces what a Living Legends family actually wants, which is somebody who has taught their child's exact course recently and is reliably available at a fixed hour.

There is a further scarcity that is often misread as a local problem. Higher Level cohorts at individual Dubai schools are often small, which means the number of teachers anywhere in the emirate who have taken a particular Higher Level course through to a final session recently is smaller than the number who teach the subject. That scarcity is city-wide. Narrowing the search by distance does not just reduce an already small pool; it filters on the one variable that has nothing to do with quality.

Removing distance inverts the question usefully. Instead of who is free and close, it becomes who has taught this course at this level and can take half past six on a Tuesday. That question has a real answer, and the answer is the same for a household inside the Living Legends gate as for one in Arabian Ranches. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, which is the honest version of this rather than a coverage area we could not actually serve.

sections.heading: What IB tutoring costs here, read from the monthly figure down
paragraphs: Most families decide on a monthly number rather than an hourly one, so start there. Bestimate's Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session put budget provision at AED 240 to 600 a month, mid-range at AED 600 to 1,200, and specialist examination-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward. Market packages include roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Read those two packages side by side: twice the money for half the number of contacts.

Translated into hours, the market has five identifiable bands. Budget online at AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing International GCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home visits at AED 180 to 500 including travel, with Bestimate at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors reaching 500. IB and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named provision at AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650.

For a Living Legends family the relevant comparison is between the qualified online band and the in-home band, because those are the two realistic options for a Diploma student. The difference buys a car journey and a gate pass. It does not buy better teaching, and in this community it actively costs teaching minutes for the reasons described above.

None of these figures is an IB Gram price list, and that distinction matters because three of the six most visible pages competing for these searches publish no price at all, while two of the three that do quote in US dollars. Each band above names who published it so a parent can check a quote rather than take it on faith. Our own answer to the price question is a free trial lesson and a conversation, since the only figure that predicts anything is whether this specialist moves this student.

sections.heading: The examination calendar, read backwards from the papers
paragraphs: No competitor page researched for this project names an examination series, a registration deadline or a results date. For a Diploma family that absence is strange, because the calendar is what a plan has to be built around, and the deadlines that matter most are not the examination dates at all.

Get the series right first. IB candidates at UAE schools sit the May session. For Cambridge qualifications, which many siblings in this community are taking, the UAE series are June and November; the February and March series is offered to India only, so any UAE page quoting a spring window is handing parents a date they cannot act on. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. This page publishes no specific IB examination or results date, because ibo.org returns an error to automated verification and an unsourced date that a family plans around is a genuine harm. Confirm IB dates with the school's coordinator.

The deadlines that actually shape a plan sit months earlier. Entry deadlines come well before the papers because centres submit candidate data and order materials. Internal assessment deadlines are set by the school rather than the board, typically several months before the board's submission window so that teachers can mark and the coordinator can moderate. A student who starts thinking about an internal assessment when the examination timetable appears has already passed the point where tutoring helps most.

Backward-looking anchors are worth citing because they can be checked. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those intervals, roughly ten weeks in summer and nine from the November series, are the real shape of the wait. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables that can be revised, so the official timetable is always the document to check.

sections.heading: The Diploma core, and where a tutor must stop
paragraphs: The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the internal assessments are the components most likely to be squeezed out of a week, because none of them has a weekly lesson defending its place. They also carry real weight and hard deadlines, set by the school months before the board's windows. A student who handles subject homework competently can still arrive at a submission date with nothing drafted.

The support that helps is shaped differently from subject tutoring. These components do not benefit from a short weekly slot; they need occasional longer sessions, spaced weeks apart, each with a clear deliverable. The research question tested for viability. The method agreed. A first section drafted and reviewed against the criteria. The argument checked for whether the conclusion follows from the evidence. Four well-placed sessions across a term achieve more than twelve fortnightly check-ins.

The boundary around this work is the thing that should decide which provider a family uses, and almost nobody writes it down. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments for a four-figure sum. That is not a competitive product; it is an IB malpractice trigger, and the consequence falls on the student, whose diploma can be withheld. So the line needs stating rather than left to inference.

What a tutor may do is substantial: teach the content, explain what each criterion asks for in the criterion's own language, test whether a research question will survive contact with real data, read a draft the student has written and say where it is losing marks, model an analysis on different material, and teach referencing properly. What a tutor must never do is produce the work. Not the exploration, not the Extended Essay, not the Theory of Knowledge essay, not a Personal Project, and not an edit so heavy the voice is no longer the student's. Nor may any provider supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables, which are the boards' copyright.

sections.heading: Who is legally permitted to tutor your child in the UAE
paragraphs: This question has a clear answer and most tutoring pages avoid it, which is itself informative. Private tuition in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and takes applications through the smart app, website and e-services system.

Two consequences follow. There is no reasonable explanation for a tutor not holding a permit that costs nothing and takes two working days. And individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published and a figure circulating online could not be verified, so treat any page quoting an amount with suspicion.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal. That requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. This is why the phrase approved tutors deserves scrutiny wherever it appears: the permit belongs to an institution with premises, and it is not a judgement about any individual's teaching.

For a household in a gated community there is a practical version of all this. Before the first paid session, ask three questions: do you hold a current MoHRE private tuition permit, which category of eligibility applies to you, and does my child attend your school? The last one matters because Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid tuition of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct does likewise. That reporting is press-sourced, so verify against the current ADEK text, but the principle is sound.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency for an IB or International GCSE student here
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process by which the UAE Ministry of Education recognises a foreign secondary certificate, and it sits between a school leaving certificate and a UAE university place. Several of the query clusters researched for this project contain no mention of it at all, and one ranking page publishes the wrong subject count for the British track. For a household with one child on International GCSE and another on the Diploma, getting it right early is more useful than any revision technique.

On the British track the published requirements are specific. Five accredited subjects in GCSE or International GCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. A competitor page claiming six subjects is wrong, and a family who planned an option block around that number has made a real mistake for free.

On the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the International Baccalaureate, no verified points threshold could be read on an official Ministry source for this project, so none is published here. Check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority directly.

Two limits worth stating. Equivalency is not something IB Gram performs, expedites or guarantees; it belongs to the family and the Ministry, and our role is to describe it and point to the official channel. And tutoring is not required for equivalency, for a university place or for school progression. Any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory process, which is both inaccurate and a poor way to treat a parent making a significant financial decision.

sections.heading: When no specialist is free at the hour you want
paragraphs: Every platform in this market writes as though a tutor is always available for every course at every level, and none of them discloses a coverage limit. That is not true of any provider, and pretending otherwise just moves the disappointment to the week after the enquiry. So here is the honest version for a household in Living Legends.

Common requests match quickly. Both Diploma mathematics routes, the three sciences at Higher and Standard Level, Economics, Business Management, English A and the International GCSE subjects have deep coverage, and a trial lesson can usually be arranged within a few days. Where a family wants the hour everybody else wants, between half past five and seven on a weekday, the limiting factor is the slot rather than the subject, and moving a session fifteen or twenty minutes often resolves it immediately.

Narrower requests behave differently. A rarely offered Group 2 language, Theory of Knowledge supervision at short notice, Computer Science Higher Level with a particular programming paradigm, or Career-related Programme reflective project support can all take longer, and sometimes the correct answer is that no suitable specialist is currently free. In that case we give a date rather than put a near-fit in front of a final-year Diploma student, which is the decision most likely to waste a family's money and term.

One further disclosure belongs on a UAE page. Lessons are delivered by specialists who may be based in the UAE or elsewhere, and the network includes experienced IB and Cambridge teachers outside the Emirates. That is how a household inside a gated community reaches a Higher Level specialist at a chosen hour at all. A parent should hear it at the outset rather than deduce it from a dialling code, and in no scenario does anyone arrive at a UAE address, because home visits are a service IB Gram operates only in India.

process.title: Name the course and the level precisely
process.description: Not IB science but Chemistry Higher Level, Year 12, losing marks on organic mechanisms. Name the school if you are willing to, because internal assessment calendars differ between schools and that changes how the first month is sequenced.

process.title: Give the real arrival-home time
process.description: Living Legends has no secondary provision inside the gates, so every Diploma student travels. Work out when they are actually home, fed and able to concentrate. A slot that looks fine and is twenty minutes too early fails every week.

process.title: Meet the specialist in a free trial
process.description: A full session, no charge, no card, with no gate pass to arrange. The test is diagnostic: the tutor should finish able to name the specific skill costing marks. If the fit is wrong, say so and we match again rather than asking anyone to persist.

process.title: Agree a plan with dates in it
process.description: A short written plan naming topics, cadence and checkpoints, anchored to the school's own assessment calendar. Core components get their own milestones, because those deadlines are set by the school months ahead of the board's windows.

process.title: Review at six sessions, then before the session
process.description: Six sessions is enough to see movement in method even where the grade has not shifted. Compare against the diagnostic rather than an impression, and pause cleanly for school examination weeks and travel.

whyPoints.title: No gate, no pass, no lost minutes
whyPoints.description: Sessions start on time because nothing has to clear security or find a parking space. In a gated community that is not a convenience point: over a school year at two sessions a week, gate access and traffic remove a real quantity of paid teaching.
