faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor to come inside Living Legends?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Home visits are a service we run only in India; everything we deliver to UAE families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Independent in-home tutors do work in this part of Dubai, and the market quotes them at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. In a gated community there is an additional hidden cost: gate registration, parking and traffic routinely remove five to fifteen minutes from a booked hour, and over a school year at two sessions a week that is a significant amount of paid teaching lost.

faqs.question: Why are there so few IB tutors based around Living Legends?
faqs.answer: Because local demand cannot sustain a specialist. Follow the chain: a single gated community holds a limited number of families, only some have Diploma students, only some of those need a particular subject, and only some need it at Higher Level. That leaves perhaps a household or two a year for any given specialism. Specialists therefore locate by road access and travel, charging for the journey, or widen their subject range until the diary fills with whoever is nearby. Neither produces what a family here wants, which is recent experience of their child's exact course.

faqs.question: Which schools do children from Living Legends attend?
faqs.answer: Primary and middle-years children mostly travel to nearby provision in Motor City, Sports City and Remraam: families name GEMS Metropole School, Victory Heights Primary School, Bradenton Preparatory Academy, South View School and GEMS FirstPoint School at The Villa. Diploma students generally travel further, to schools along the Al Khail Road corridor and in the Al Barsha and Jumeirah area, including GEMS Wellington Academy Al Khail, Fairgreen International School, Kent College Dubai and Jumeirah English Speaking School in Arabian Ranches. Schools are named as travel context only, with no affiliation implied.

faqs.question: What time can a Diploma session realistically start from this community?
faqs.answer: Later than the school bell suggests. There is no secondary provision inside Living Legends, so every Diploma student travels, usually toward Al Barsha South, Dubai Hills or the Al Khail corridor. School finishes between half past two and half past three, but the journey home in the afternoon plus thirty or forty minutes to eat and settle puts the first workable slot at around six. Online sessions can be pinned to that hour precisely, which is the main practical advantage over a visit depending on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road behaving.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a permit to work in a Dubai gated community?
faqs.answer: A tutor needs the same permit everywhere in the UAE, and the community makes no difference to it. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no schedule of amounts is published.

faqs.question: How much should a Living Legends family budget monthly for Diploma support?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session give AED 240 to 600 a month for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward for specialist examination-year support. Packages circulate at roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, which is twice the money for half the contacts. For Higher Level work the specialist band is the honest answer, and a free trial lesson is the sensible way to test the match before committing to it.

faqs.question: Is online tuition as effective as a tutor in the room for Diploma work?
faqs.answer: For secondary students, in most cases yes, and in some respects better. Diploma work is already screen-based: papers, data sets, graphing tools, annotated drafts. A shared document with both people writing on it does things a paper exercise book cannot, and the session leaves a record in notes rather than evaporating. The honest exception is children under roughly Year 5 and students with significant attention difficulties, where presence does real work. For a Diploma student here the limiting factor is the specialist's expertise, not the medium.

faqs.question: Can two children in one Living Legends household share a tutor?
faqs.answer: They can, and it is often better that they do not. A child in MYP 3 and a sibling in the second Diploma year need different things, and the person who gives excellent criterion feedback in the MYP is not automatically the right Physics Higher Level specialist. What works well is two consecutive slots with two specialists on the same evening, which costs nothing extra because nothing is travelling. With a visiting tutor the same arrangement means two journeys and two travel premiums, or one compromised session.

faqs.question: Which exam session will my child sit from a UAE school?
faqs.answer: IB candidates at UAE schools sit the May session. This page publishes no specific IB examination or results date, because ibo.org returns an error to automated verification and an unsourced date a family plans around is a real harm; confirm with the school's coordinator. For Cambridge qualifications a sibling may be taking, the UAE series are June and November, and the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with its November 2026 timetable running to 19 November 2026.

faqs.question: How far can a tutor go in helping with an Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: A long way, and the line is specific. A tutor may teach the content, explain what each criterion asks for in the criterion's own language, test whether a research question will survive contact with real data, read a draft the student has written and identify where marks are being lost, model an analysis on different material, and teach referencing properly. A tutor must never produce the work: not the exploration, not the Extended Essay, not the Theory of Knowledge essay. One page ranking in this market sells finished Internal Assessments, and the penalty for that lands on the student.

faqs.question: We have seven weeks before the papers. Is starting now sensible?
faqs.answer: Sensible, provided the plan changes shape. Seven weeks is a technique window rather than a content window. It starts with a diagnostic paper, then targets the two or three places marks are actually being lost, which at this stage is usually command-term reading, method communication and timing rather than missing knowledge. Expect two or three sessions a week with real work in between. What seven weeks cannot do is rebuild two years of a Higher Level course, and any provider promising a specific grade from here is selling something undeliverable.

faqs.question: How do Arabic and Islamic Education fit around a Diploma timetable?
faqs.answer: They are compulsory and they lengthen the week. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. A revision plan drawn from six Diploma subjects alone therefore overestimates how much free evening time a student in this community actually has.

faqs.question: Will you supply past papers for my child to practise on?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider offering a download library is showing you an unresolved problem rather than a benefit. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are the boards' copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. A tutor cites the official source, works from what the school has legitimately issued to the student, and writes equivalent practice questions in the same style and at the same difficulty, which produces the same preparation without the copyright problem.

faqs.question: If the first Living Legends match does not work, what then?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we match again. The trial lesson exists precisely to surface this before money changes hands, and the signal worth watching is not whether the session was pleasant but whether the tutor could name the specific skill costing marks by the end of it. The same applies if a fit fails later in the term. What we will not do is ask a final-year Diploma student to persist with a near-fit because the diary is full; where no suitable specialist is free, we give a date instead.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-living-legends.closingHeading: The gate is not the obstacle; the specialist is
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-living-legends.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB home tutor in Living Legends, the thing worth solving is not access but expertise. A gated community of this size cannot supply a Diploma specialist by local demand, and Higher Level scarcity is city-wide rather than local, so a radius search narrows the choice on the one variable that does not matter. Name the course, the level and the specific problem, then ask who has taught exactly that recently. Book a free trial lesson, judge it on whether the tutor names the skill costing marks, and decide from there. Nothing arrives at your address and no card is needed.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-meydan.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects to students across Mohammed Bin Rashid City and the Meydan corridor. Each is matched to a named subject and level, and the first conversation covers what a sensible number of sessions looks like before it covers anything else.

intro.heading: What a Meydan family is really asking about price
paragraphs: Parents in Meydan who go looking for a home tutor are rarely shopping for convenience alone. They are trying to work out what this costs, whether the number they have been quoted is reasonable, and what they are actually getting for it. That turns out to be remarkably hard to find out: of the six competitor pages measured for this project, three publish no price at all, two quote in US dollars, and one publishes an hourly figure that contradicts the price in its own structured data.

So this page leads with the money. Every AED figure on it is attributed to the competitor or rate table that published it and dated to when it was read, in October 2026. None of them is IB Gram's price list, and where our own pricing is relevant the honest answer is the free trial lesson and the consultation rather than a number invented for a web page. What the figures are for is giving you a reference point before you speak to anybody, including us.

The second half of the question is where the money goes wrong, and that is more useful than the rate. In this corridor the recurring patterns are identifiable: hours bought before any diagnosis, a flat monthly spend across two Diploma years when the need is concentrated in two terms, three subjects supported thinly instead of one properly, a travel premium paid weekly for two years, and a tutor retained past the point where the mark pattern stopped moving. Each of those costs thousands of dirhams and none of them is about the hourly rate.

Meydan itself shapes the arithmetic. The district sits around the racecourse inside Mohammed Bin Rashid City, with few schools inside its own boundaries, so almost every family drives out — commonly to Hartland International School or North London Collegiate School Dubai in Sobha Hartland, to Kings' School Nad Al Sheba, Repton School Dubai or GEMS Modern Academy next door, or further to Al Quoz and Al Jaddaf. A tutor driving in meets that traffic from the other direction, and somebody pays for the journey.

IB Gram delivers tuition to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE — home visits are a service we offer only in India. That is a pricing decision as much as an operational one: the market's in-home band sits AED 50 to 150 an hour above the equivalent online band, and what that buys is proximity rather than subject depth. The table further down sets both out side by side so you can judge it rather than take it on trust.

One instruction worth acting on before reading any further. Work out, in a single number, what you have spent on tutoring over the last twelve months. Most families in this corridor have never added it up, and the total is usually larger than the hourly rate suggested and arrived without a decision ever being taken to spend it. That number is the only honest starting point for the sections below, because every argument on this page is about where it goes rather than about how big it is.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-meydan.programmesIntro: Cost behaves differently at each stage of the IB, and a family planning a budget needs to know which stage they are funding. These are the four stages a Meydan family meets, described by what support actually costs at each.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The cheapest stage to buy support at and the one families buy least of, which is usually the right instinct. PYP has no terminal assessment, so there is no grade to protect, and the sensible purchase is short and diagnostic: whether number work and reading comprehension are secure enough for the next stage. A standing weekly commitment at this age is rarely good value.
programmes.countryNote: The exception in Dubai is Arabic. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and for a Meydan family arriving from outside the region Arabic from a standing start is the one PYP-stage request that reliably pays for itself, because it is far cheaper to begin here than in MYP.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Marked on four criteria out of 8 per subject, and the cost-efficient purchase is almost always one criterion rather than one subject. A student scoring well on three criteria and poorly on a fourth needs three or four sessions on the fourth, not a term of general subject work. The final-year Personal Project is the other point where short, scheduled support earns its fee.
programmes.countryNote: Meydan has a high share of families in their first or second UAE year, which produces a specific MYP pattern: a mid-programme arrival who needs the criteria explained before any teaching. That single conversation often removes the need for the weekly arrangement the family was about to buy, which is worth knowing before committing to one.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Where the money actually goes. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, three internal assessments, a 4,000-word Extended Essay and a 1,600-word Theory of Knowledge essay. Spend concentrates sensibly in two places: the term in which the internal assessments are drafted, and the six to eight weeks before papers. A flat monthly figure across two years overspends early and runs short late.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. No specific IB session or results date appears on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Confirm every one with your school's IB coordinator, because a budget built around an unverified date is a budget built on a guess.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses alongside a career-related study and a core including a reflective project. Provision in Dubai is thin, so families comparing it against the full Diploma are often doing so for load reasons rather than cost reasons. Where it is chosen, the tutoring budget narrows to the Diploma courses carried forward and the reflective project.
programmes.countryNote: Because CP availability is limited locally, families weighing it should settle the Ministry of Education equivalency question first. Equivalency rules are set by the Ministry and must be checked on moe.gov.ae for the specific qualification combination; no tutoring provider can decide it, and no page should imply that tutoring affects it.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-meydan.subjectsIntro: Subject choice drives cost more than most families expect, because the specialist bands apply unevenly. Below are the Diploma subjects Meydan students ask for, each with a note on where its support budget actually goes.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most expensive subject to support properly at Higher Level, because Paper 3 marking and exploration feedback are narrow specialisms. The cheap version — general maths revision — reliably fails here. Standard Level is more forgiving and sits comfortably in the mid band rather than the specialist one.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-assumed throughout, which makes the content more accessible to a competent generalist at Standard Level. The spend worth protecting is the exploration, marked on five criteria over 20 marks, where personal engagement and reflection are the criteria most often scored low and the cheapest to improve.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Often the wrong purchase. A large share of poor physics marks trace to the mathematics underneath rather than the physics, so four sessions on vectors, logarithms and rearrangement can be better value than a term of theme revision. Test the algebra before funding the physics.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Good value to support because the losses are precision rather than ignorance: enthalpy signs, missing state symbols, trends described instead of explained. Those are drillable in three or four sessions and apply to every paper, which is an unusually concentrated return.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-dense and command-term sensitive, which means the useful spend is on answer structure rather than on coverage. A six-mark extended answer written to a rehearsed template scores consistently; the same knowledge written as a list does not. Three sessions on structure often outperforms ten on content.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral is assessed on four criteria over 40 marks and is the most schedulable, most improvable component in the subject, which makes short scheduled support better value than a standing weekly hour. The HL essay's 1,200 to 1,500 word range is the other defined target.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are marked rather than decorative, so a short block on diagram discipline — labelled axes, shifted curves, new equilibrium marked — buys marks across every paper. The internal assessment is three commentaries with word limits, which makes it a defined and therefore efficient piece of work to support.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools are examined for application to the stimulus rather than for definition, so the efficient purchase is practice at reaching a judgement from a case. Students who can list the parts of a framework and never use it are the common pattern, and it is a technique fix rather than a content one.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on one of six prescribed titles, plus the exhibition. Short, scheduled support at the title-choice stage is disproportionately valuable, because a title chosen badly costs the whole essay. Weekly TOK tutoring across a year is rarely a good use of money.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words marked on five criteria over 34 marks, with the planning reflections contributing. The efficient spend is three or four scheduled feedback sessions on the student's own drafts rather than an ongoing arrangement. Nothing may be written or redrafted for the student at any point.

subjects.name: Internal assessments across the sciences
subjects.description: Four criteria, 24 marks, a 3,000-word limit. The highest-value single intervention in the whole Diploma is checking, before any data is collected, that the research question can actually be answered by the chosen method. That is one session and it saves six weeks.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Required in Dubai private schools under KHDA rules regardless of the licensed curriculum, so for many Meydan families this is a cost they did not plan for. Support works within the school's own approved material, because KHDA prohibits different or additional content for the mandatory subjects without Ministry permission.

regions.name: Meydan
regions.note: Low-rise and villa stock around the racecourse and Meydan One, with few schools inside the district itself. Almost every family drives out, so a visiting tutor would be entering the same pick-up traffic from the opposite direction.

regions.note: Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai sit inside the community, which makes it the one part of this block where a short school run is normal and an early session is easy to schedule.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: Repton School Dubai, Kings' School Nad Al Sheba and GEMS Modern Academy inside the district, either side of Dubai-Al Ain Road. Many Meydan children travel here, which sets the realistic session start at around 16:00.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Rashid City
regions.note: District One and the surrounding villa plots, with long internal roads and limited exits onto Al Khail. Twenty minutes disappears inside the community at pick-up, and a visiting tutor's travel time is billed to somebody.

regions.name: Al Quoz and Al Quoz 4
regions.note: Mixed residential and industrial with schools on the edges. Families travelling here start sessions after 17:00 on school days, which pushes a weekly arrangement into the least productive part of the evening.

regions.note: High-rise apartments and short commutes, with children mostly at Downtown and Al Jaddaf schools. Evening slots after 19:00 are common, and short focused sessions are better value than long ones at that hour.

regions.note: No school on site, so every family drives out and back. The narrow window between home and dinner argues for scheduled blocks around deadlines rather than a thin standing weekly hour.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf and Culture Village

regions.name: DIFC
regions.note: Few families, almost all apartments with long parental working days. Weekend sessions dominate here, and for a visiting tutor a weekend slot usually carries the same travel premium as a weekday one.

schoolClusters.note: The schools Meydan children most often attend, inside the neighbouring communities rather than the district itself. Between them they run the IB Diploma, a full continuum and British secondary routes, so two Meydan neighbours can be funding very different programmes.

schoolClusters.city: The corridor from Al Jaddaf to Al Barsha
schoolClusters.note: Schools a Meydan family will also have toured or shortlisted, several running the IB across more than one programme. Most remaining enquiries from this page come from students at this set.

modes.description: One tutor, one subject, one fixed weekly slot on Gulf Standard Time. The right purchase when a specific diagnosed gap needs rebuilding across a term, which is mostly DP1 rather than DP2. sections.heading: What IB tutoring actually costs in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: Here are the numbers, with their owners. Budget online tutoring, generally a university student, runs AED 45 to 150 an hour: EdFlik publishes from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist runs AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table giving 200 to 450 plus. In-home one-to-one, travel included, runs AED 180 to 500, Bestimate at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500. The premium end reaches AED 500 to 650 and above, BartyED publishing AED 650.

Monthly, the same sources give shape rather than precision. Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour session come out at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published packages in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Two readings of that spread matter for a Meydan family. The first is that the bands buy genuinely different things rather than the same thing at different prices: the bottom buys a confident undergraduate with no board marking experience, the middle buys a trained teacher who may not know your specific paper, the specialist band buys somebody who teaches one subject at one level all week. The top band buys reputation, which is sometimes a different lesson and sometimes not.

The second is that the in-home band sits above the online band by roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour, and that difference is travel. It is not a quality premium and nobody in the market claims it is. Paid weekly across two Diploma years in one subject, it comes to several thousand dirhams — which is itself a term of specialist support. That arithmetic is the reason the next sections exist.

sections.heading: Five ways a Meydan tutoring budget gets wasted
paragraphs: The hourly rate is the least important variable in what a family ends up spending. These five patterns cost far more, they recur across this corridor, and every one of them is avoidable with a decision taken before the money moves rather than after.

The first is buying hours before any diagnosis. A weekly subject hour purchased because a report was disappointing spends most of its time on material the student already has, because nobody established where the marks were actually going. A marked script and one diagnostic session answer that, and the answer frequently redirects the purchase entirely — most often towards technique, a single criterion, or the mathematics underneath a science.

The second is a flat monthly spend across two Diploma years. The need is concentrated in two places: the term in which internal assessments are drafted, and the six to eight weeks before papers. Spending the same amount in DP1 term two as in DP2 term four means overspending when nothing is urgent and running short when everything is. The third is supporting three subjects thinly rather than one properly; three thin passes move nothing and cost the same as one that works.

The fourth is the travel premium, paid weekly for two years, for proximity rather than depth. The fifth, and the most expensive, is keeping a tutor past the point where the mark pattern stopped moving. Six to eight sessions is enough to tell whether something is working. Carrying on because the slot is already in the calendar is how a term and several thousand dirhams disappear without anybody deciding to spend them.

sections.heading: The home-tutoring question, answered properly
paragraphs: A home tutor in Meydan is a real and reasonable thing to want, and the market supplies it. What it involves is worth setting out accurately, because the honest version is more useful than either a sales pitch or a dismissal.

What you get is presence. A parent can see the session happening. A thirteen-year-old cannot quietly open another tab. A tutor in the room notices a wandering attention sooner. For younger students and for students who need supervision as much as teaching, those are genuine advantages that no amount of argument about tutor pools dissolves. What it costs is the travel premium of roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour, a narrower pool of tutors — limited to those willing to drive to Mohammed Bin Rashid City — and a fixed slot that cannot move when the school adds a revision class.

The travel reality in Meydan specifically is worth stating. There are few schools inside the district, so children travel out and a visiting tutor travels in, both through the same afternoon congestion. District One's internal roads and limited exits onto Al Khail absorb twenty minutes before a car reaches a main road. A 16:00 in-home session in this part of Dubai is routinely a 16:40 session, and the tutor's lost time is priced into the rate whether or not it appears on the invoice.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. So this is not a comparison we are using to steer you — it is the reasoning behind a decision already taken, set out so you can test it against your own week. If after reading the table you conclude that presence matters more for your child than tutor choice does, that is a legitimate conclusion and the market will serve it. What we sell is the other side of the trade.

sections.heading: Two Diploma years, month by month
paragraphs: A tutoring budget for the Diploma should be lumpy, and most families make theirs flat. The need is genuinely concentrated: two periods do most of the work, two more are worth a modest standing arrangement, and two are worth very little at all. Knowing the shape in advance is worth more than negotiating the rate.

DP1 term one is the cheapest and most leveraged period. Content is being built rather than repaired, nothing is urgent, and a gap closed here costs a fraction of what the same gap costs eighteen months later. A single weekly session in the subject most likely to be taken at Higher Level is usually enough. DP1 term two is maintenance. DP1 term three is where exploration and internal assessment topics get chosen, and a short feedback block at that point is disproportionately valuable because a topic chosen badly costs six months.

DP2 term four is the expensive one and should be. Three internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay collide here while new Higher Level content is still arriving. This is where scheduled feedback blocks earn their fee, and where a family who spent flat through DP1 discovers they have less room than they thought. Term five is the mock cycle and the fortnight after it, which is the most informative data of the two years and has a short shelf life.

Term six is the final run: two or three shorter sessions a week on timed sections for a fixed number of weeks, then stop. Note what the table below does not contain: a recommendation to spend continuously. The honest shape of a Diploma tutoring budget has gaps in it, and a provider who proposes an unbroken two-year arrangement is proposing something that suits them.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: fees, the freeze and entry
paragraphs: A tutoring figure makes more sense beside the other education costs a Meydan family already carries. The most useful anchor is public and dated: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion out of AED 2.5 billion in total.

That matters because a family who had budgeted for a fee increase and did not receive one has headroom that did not exist a year earlier. The most common use of it in this corridor is one subject of weekly support in an examined year. It is worth spending deliberately rather than letting it drift, because a standing weekly hour bought without a diagnosis is the easiest money to waste in this market and the first of the five patterns above.

Supply context is also moving. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. The emirate's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25 offering seventeen curricula, with the IB at around 7% of enrolment. More IB places means more Diploma candidates, which over time thickens the local tutoring market rather than thinning it.

One cost families forget entirely until it arrives: examination entry for anybody sitting outside their school's normal process, and any retake arrangements. Those are the school's or the board's charges rather than a tutor's, and they are worth asking the exams officer about early. A tutoring budget set without them is a budget that will be revised in the spring.

sections.heading: Provider models compared, not brands
paragraphs: Comparing providers honestly means comparing models, because a brand comparison in this market quickly becomes a claim about somebody else's quality that nobody can evidence. The models differ in ways that affect cost directly, and the differences are structural rather than reputational.

A platform or agency sets the rate, vets the tutor and handles replacement; you pay for that layer and you get recourse if the match fails. An international marketplace is usually cheaper and puts the vetting on you, which is fine if you know what questions to ask and expensive if you do not. A freelance tutor found through a community group may be excellent and is entirely your own due diligence, including the permit question. A tuition centre adds structure and peers, charges less per student for a shared pace, and adds a commute at the end of a school day.

The question worth asking every model is what happens when it goes wrong. If the tutor is not the right fit, who absorbs that — you, or the provider? If a session is missed, who bears it? If the subject at the level you need is unavailable, are you told, or matched to somebody adjacent? Those three answers separate providers more reliably than the headline rate, and they are the questions least likely to be answered on a pricing page.

One caution about the market generally rather than any brand in it. The researched competitor set includes pages with contradictory prices between the body and the structured data, self-asserted star ratings, and in one case a school listed as a client that appears not to exist. A provider whose own figures disagree across two sections of its own website is telling you something about its record-keeping, and that is a legitimate thing to notice without naming anybody.

sections.heading: What a free trial lesson should actually tell you
paragraphs: A free trial is the only part of this market a parent can evaluate before paying, and most families use it badly. Treated as a sample lesson it tells you whether the tutor is pleasant. Treated as a diagnostic it tells you whether they know the paper, which is the thing you are actually buying.

Set it up to answer that. Send a marked script in advance and ask for the session to be spent on it: here is a question my child lost marks on, mark it with them against the official scheme and tell me what the pattern is. A specialist will do that comfortably and will talk in command terms, criteria letters, method marks and mark allocations. A generalist will drift towards re-teaching the topic, which is a perfectly good lesson and not the answer to your question.

Then ask two more things before the session ends. How many sessions does this pattern suggest, and what would you deliberately not work on? A tutor willing to name what they will leave alone is planning. A tutor who proposes an open-ended weekly arrangement for everything is selling. The second answer is more informative than the first.

On the word free: the trial is one lesson, with no payment and no card required, and that is the whole condition. It is worth asking any provider in this market to state the condition attached to their own free offer on the same screen as the word, because 'free' with an unstated condition is the oldest inefficiency in this business and it is still common.

sections.heading: Hidden extras, and what a quote should include
paragraphs: The quoted hourly rate is not the price, and the gap between them is where families in this corridor get caught. A quote worth comparing has to answer five questions, and in this market it frequently answers none of them on the page where the number appears.

First, session length: an hourly rate attached to 45-minute sessions is a different price from the same rate attached to 60 minutes, and both exist. Second, VAT: whether the quoted figure includes it. This page will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition as fact, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation nobody in this market provides — what a parent can reasonably demand is simply whether the number quoted to them is inclusive. Third, materials: whether anything is charged for separately.

Fourth, cancellation and no-shows: who bears a missed session, and with how much notice. Fifth, what happens to unused sessions if you stop. A package bought monthly and abandoned in week two is a real scenario and the answer should be written down before it happens, not negotiated afterwards.

One more, specific to in-home arrangements: whether travel is inside the rate or added, and whether it changes for Mohammed Bin Rashid City given the internal distances. The published in-home band of AED 180 to 500 is described as including travel, but that is the market's framing and an individual tutor's quote may not follow it. Ask, and get the answer in writing rather than in a conversation.

sections.heading: Is the person you are paying permitted to tutor here?
paragraphs: This is a cost question as well as a compliance one, because a tutor operating outside the permit system is a tutor with no recourse if the arrangement goes wrong. It also has a clean answer that almost nobody in this market publishes.

Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', listing no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two consequences for a Meydan parent. Anybody describing the permit as costly, optional or unavailable to them is either misinformed or not applying. And u.ae states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE will be subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, and Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the amounts, so no figure should be quoted to you by anybody.

There is also a conduct rule worth knowing before arranging anything convenient. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct similarly bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. However tempting it looks, do not arrange paid tutoring with your child's own classroom teacher. Separately, IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none.

sections.heading: When to stop paying
paragraphs: Almost nothing written about tutoring addresses the ending, which is why so much of it runs on indefinitely. A tutoring arrangement should have a point at which it stops, and deciding that point in advance is the single most effective cost control available to a Meydan family.

The review question is narrow and answerable: six to eight sessions in, has the mark pattern moved? Not the grade, which lags, and not the student's confidence, which can improve while nothing else does. The pattern — the categories in which marks are being lost — is the measurable thing. If it has shifted, the arrangement is working and should continue to its planned end. If it has not, either the diagnosis was wrong or the fit is wrong, and both are the provider's problem to fix rather than the family's to fund.

Scheduled blocks end naturally, which is part of why they are good value. A feedback block on an internal assessment finishes when the piece is submitted. A final-run paper block finishes a fixed number of weeks before papers. A criterion block in MYP finishes in three or four sessions. The format with no natural ending is the standing weekly hour, which is exactly the one most families buy first.

So the honest recommendation to end a page about cost is this: buy less than you think you need, buy it with a diagnosis in front of you, put a review date in the calendar on the day you start, and treat the absence of an ending as a warning sign rather than a convenience. The AED figures on this page are there so you can compare before you speak to anybody, and the free trial is there so the judgement about subject depth is made by you before any money moves.

faqs.question: Can we get an IB home tutor in Meydan through IB Gram?
faqs.answer: No, and it is better to say so plainly than to leave it ambiguous. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to UAE families over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE — home visits are a service we run only in India. The market does supply in-home tutoring in this corridor at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, which is roughly AED 50 to 150 above the equivalent online rate. That premium buys presence rather than subject depth.

faqs.question: What does a home visit actually add to the price?
faqs.answer: Roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour, based on figures read in October 2026. In-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to 500 including travel, with Bestimate's Dubai table giving 180 to 350 and independent home tutors 200 to 500, while a qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to 300. Monthly packages show the same gap: around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Across two Diploma years in one subject, that difference reaches several thousand dirhams.

faqs.question: Where does a tutoring budget in this area most often get wasted?
faqs.answer: Five patterns, in order of cost. Hours bought before any diagnosis, so most of a term is spent on material the student already has. A flat monthly spend across two Diploma years when the need is concentrated in two terms. Three subjects supported thinly rather than one properly. The travel premium paid weekly for two years. And keeping a tutor past the point where the mark pattern stopped moving, which is the most expensive of the five because nobody decides to do it.

faqs.question: How much should a Meydan family expect to pay per month?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates, for a weekly one-hour session, come out at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published packages elsewhere include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Expect the figure to be lumpy rather than flat: light in DP1 term one, heavy in DP2 term four when three internal assessments collide, and heavy again in the final weeks.

faqs.question: Is the cheapest tutor ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. Budget online tutoring at AED 45 to 150 an hour — EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 — buys a confident undergraduate, and for a single Standard Level topic gap with a parent keeping an eye on progress that can be exactly right. Where it reliably fails is Higher Level coursework feedback and anything requiring mark-scheme judgement, because that is experience rather than subject knowledge and the lower bands do not carry it.

faqs.question: What should be included in a tutoring quote before we pay?
faqs.answer: Five things, and in this market they are often absent from the page where the price appears. The session length behind the hourly figure, because 45 minutes and 60 minutes are different prices. Whether the number includes VAT. Whether materials are charged separately. Who bears a missed session and with how much notice. And what happens to unused sessions if you stop. Get those in writing rather than in conversation; they are worth more than a discount on the rate.

faqs.question: How do we judge a tutor in a single free session?
faqs.answer: Send a marked script in advance and ask for the session to be spent on it, marking it with your child against the official scheme rather than re-teaching the topic. A specialist talks in command terms, criteria letters, method marks and mark allocations. Then ask two questions: how many sessions does this pattern suggest, and what would you deliberately not work on. The willingness to name what they will leave alone is the clearest signal available that you are being planned for.

faqs.question: How do we know it is time to end a tutoring arrangement?
faqs.answer: Put a review date six to eight sessions ahead on the day you start, with one question against it: has the mark pattern moved? Not the grade, which lags, and not confidence, which can improve while nothing else does. If the pattern has shifted, continue to the planned end. If it has not, the diagnosis or the fit is wrong and changing costs nothing. An arrangement with no proposed ending at all should be treated as a warning rather than a convenience.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre cheaper than one-to-one for IB subjects?
faqs.answer: Per student, yes, because the attention is shared and the pace is fixed. Whether it is better value depends on whether your child's gaps match the group's. For a diagnosed specific weakness — one criterion, one component, one topic blocking everything built on it — a group moving through a set sequence cannot intervene at the line where the work breaks. Centres also add a commute at the end of a school day, which from Meydan lands in the same traffic that delays a visiting tutor.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start in Meydan?
faqs.answer: Around 16:00 for most families, because Meydan has few schools inside the district and children travel out — commonly to Sobha Hartland or Nad Al Sheba. Families whose school sits inside Sobha Hartland can manage 15:30. A visiting tutor driving in meets the same congestion from the other direction, and District One's internal roads absorb twenty minutes before a car reaches Al Khail, so an in-home 16:00 slot is routinely a 16:40 one in practice.

faqs.question: Do we need to check whether a tutor holds a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is quick. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone describing it as expensive or optional is misinformed. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, so there is no reasonable excuse for not holding one.

faqs.question: Can we hire our child's own teacher privately?
faqs.answer: Do not. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct similarly bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Beyond the rules, it is an awkward arrangement for the student if it goes badly. Treat press-reported policy as something to verify against the current ADEK document, and treat the general direction as settled.

faqs.question: Which part of the Diploma is the best value to pay for?
faqs.answer: Internal assessment feedback, and specifically one session before any data or drafting begins. The highest-value single intervention in the whole Diploma is checking that a research question can actually be answered by the chosen method, because a design fault is visible to a specialist in minutes and invisible to the student for six weeks. After that, the second-best purchase is a short block on command terms and timing, which transfers across every subject the student sits.

faqs.question: Does the school fee freeze change what we should budget for tutoring?
faqs.answer: It creates headroom for families who had budgeted for an increase. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. The most common use of that headroom in this corridor is one subject of weekly support in an examined year — worth spending on a diagnosed gap deliberately rather than letting it become a standing hour nobody reviews.

faqs.question: Will paying more get our child a better grade?
faqs.answer: Nobody can promise a grade and no honest provider will put a number on an outcome. What more money reliably buys is narrower expertise: somebody who teaches one subject at one level all week and has marked against the official scheme. That matters for Higher Level coursework feedback and mark-scheme judgement, and matters much less for Standard Level topic revision. Paying specialist rates for a task the mid band covers is one of the five waste patterns on this page.

faqs.question: Do you provide past papers or materials as part of the fee?
faqs.answer: No, and nothing is charged for them either. IB, Cambridge and Pearson materials are copyright, some unreleased, so we do not host, reproduce or distribute papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. Your school holds licensed access and the boards publish through their own platforms at ibo.org, cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com. Sessions work from the copies the school or board provides, and the paid time goes on marking rather than on sourcing documents.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-meydan.closingHeading: Buy less, with a diagnosis in front of you
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-meydan.closingBody: If you came here looking for an IB home tutor in Meydan, the honest answer is that IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition online rather than by home visit, and that the market's in-home premium of roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour buys presence rather than subject depth. Send the subject and level, the next three dates that matter, and the most recent marked script. The first lesson is a free diagnostic with no payment and no card, and it should end with two numbers: how many sessions the pattern suggests, and what the tutor would deliberately leave alone.

intro.heading: The syllabus is the thing, and it is the thing most local searches miss
paragraphs: A search for an IB home tutor in Mirdif is a search for proximity, but proximity is not what fixes a DP grade. What fixes a DP grade is somebody who knows that Mathematics HL Paper 3 is worth 20 per cent on its own, that the sciences now carry Paper 1 at 36 per cent and Paper 2 at 44 per cent with the internal assessment at 20, and that an English A Language and Literature HL candidate sits two papers plus an HL essay plus an individual oral. Those numbers decide where revision time goes. A tutor who does not know them will spend an hour on content your child has already met.

Mirdif sits in the eastern suburbs, ringed by Al Mizhar, Al Warqa, Al Khawaneej and Nad Al Hamar, with Dubai Festival City and Academic City within reach. The DP schools that families here use are spread across that arc rather than sitting inside Mirdif, so a tutor hired for being nearby is nearby to the villa and not to the school. More to the point, the DP is a six-subject programme and a struggling student is usually struggling in one or two specific components, not in a subject as a whole.

IB Gram delivers tuition to Mirdif as one-to-one lessons over live video. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to an address is a service offered only in India. The reason to prefer the online route here is not cost. It is that an HL Chemistry specialist who can mark a scientific investigation against the criteria does not have to live in Al Warqa for your child to work with them twice a week.

What this page does, then, is treat the search seriously on its own terms. The sections below set out what each DP component is worth, which command terms do the marking, the specific traps where Mirdif students lose marks in maths and the sciences, how past papers should be worked so they teach something, what the Dubai market charges for in-home and online tuition, and the line between coaching an internal assessment and writing it.

Scale is worth a sentence, because it explains the tutor market you are shopping in. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 offering seventeen curricula, and International Baccalaureate schools accounted for seven per cent of enrolment against thirty-seven per cent for UK-curriculum schools. A tutor advertising locally in the eastern suburbs is therefore far more likely to know GCSE and A Level than to know what an HL scientific investigation needs, and that is not a criticism of them so much as arithmetic.

Everything factual here is either from a named source or from the published subject structure, and the one thing deliberately absent is a date. The IB blocks automated checking of its own calendar, so no exam or results date appears on this page. UAE schools sit the May session; confirm every date with your child's IB coordinator rather than with a tutoring website, including ours.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-mirdif.programmesIntro: Mirdif families reach the Diploma Programme by several routes, and the route changes what tutoring is needed. The three programmes below are the ones requested from this part of Dubai.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Assessment is a mix of terminal written papers and internally assessed work, and the split differs by subject: 20 per cent internal in Maths and the sciences, 30 per cent in SL Economics, 30 per cent for the individual oral in SL English A Language and Literature.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai DP candidates sit the May session. Mirdif students most often need help with two components rather than two subjects: a Paper 3 and an internal assessment, or a Paper 2 essay and the Extended Essay. Diagnosing that before booking hours is the difference between six useful lessons and sixteen vague ones.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria lettered A to D and each marked out of 8. The programme rewards investigation, communication and reflection rather than terminal recall, which is why the step into DP assessment catches students who were comfortable all through MYP.
programmes.countryNote: The continuum schools serving the eastern suburbs run MYP into DP in the same building. Students who make that move without a deliberate change in habit frequently drop a grade in DP1 term one, and the cause is the mark scheme rather than the content.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: The core carries up to three points on the final 45 and swallows more student time than its weighting suggests. The Extended Essay is capped at 4,000 words, the TOK essay at 1,600 and the TOK exhibition commentary at 950. All three are the student's own work, and a tutor's role is questioning, structure teaching and feedback.
programmes.countryNote: Core support is the most common finite tutoring block booked from Mirdif, because it has a deadline rather than an exam. A dated series of lessons built backwards from the school's internal deadlines works; open-ended weekly lessons on an essay nobody has started do not.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: DP courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. A smaller cohort in Dubai than the DP, and support requests usually concern the DP courses taken inside it rather than the career-related component.
programmes.countryNote: Few eastern-suburbs schools offer it, so students on this route are often the only one in their year group needing help with a particular DP course. That is precisely the case where online matching beats a local search, because the local pool for one subject at one level may be empty.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-mirdif.subjectsIntro: Requests from Mirdif concentrate on the components with the highest marginal return: Paper 3 in HL maths and economics, Paper 2 in the sciences, and the internal assessments that sit at a fifth of the grade in most subjects.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: HL splits 30/30/20 across three papers with 20 per cent for the exploration; SL is 40/40/20. Paper 3 is the HL discriminator: two long, scaffolded investigations where students lose marks for abandoning part (b) rather than for not knowing the topic.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same weightings as AA. Technology use is assumed throughout, and marks go missing when a student computes a correct answer on the calculator and writes none of the reasoning the mark scheme wants to see.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 at 36 per cent combines multiple choice with a data-based section; Paper 2 at 44 per cent carries the extended response; the scientific investigation is 20 per cent with a 3,000-word ceiling. Uncertainty treatment and graph gradients are where the data section is won or lost.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same component structure as Physics. Organic mechanisms and equilibrium reasoning absorb the most tutoring time, and the single commonest Paper 2 loss is an explanation that states a trend without naming the cause the mark scheme requires.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Heavy on command-term precision: outline, explain, distinguish and evaluate all score differently for the same underlying knowledge. Students who revise content and not command terms plateau in the 4 to 5 range regardless of effort.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: HL weights Paper 1 at 20 per cent, Paper 2 at 30, Paper 3 at 30 and the portfolio of three commentaries at 20; SL is 30/40/30 with no Paper 3. HL Paper 3 is quantitative and is where unprepared HL candidates lose most.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: SL sits Paper 1 at 35 per cent, Paper 2 at 35 and the individual oral at 30. HL adds the HL essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words. Paper 1 unseen analysis improves fastest with weekly timed practice on unfamiliar text types.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Productive and receptive skills assessed separately, with text-type conventions carrying marks of their own. Students writing excellent prose in the wrong register for the task lose marks they never see explained.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with tool application assessed as a skill. The usual failure is describing a tool rather than applying it to the stimulus, which caps the response regardless of how accurate the description is.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A thin tutor pool in Dubai at HL, which makes it the clearest example of why matching by subject beats matching by district. Pseudocode discipline and the solution development documentation carry more marks than students expect.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Mirdif can and cannot be arranged
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Mirdif, in the sense of a qualified DP teacher who drives to a villa off Algeria Street, exists in this market. Independent tutors advertise in-home work across the eastern suburbs, and quoted rates for in-home one-to-one in Dubai run AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. The premium is real and so is the service. It is simply not the service IB Gram sells.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Sending a tutor to a family's address is something the business does only in India, and stating that plainly is more useful than hedging. For Mirdif the delivery is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with a screen shared both ways so the student writes and the tutor annotates.

The case for that is specific to the DP rather than general. A DP student needing HL Computer Science, HL Economics Paper 3 or Chemistry scientific investigation feedback is looking for one person in a small pool. Restricting that pool to tutors who will drive to Mirdif on a Tuesday at 16:30 removes most of it. Restricting it to nobody at all, which is what matching on subject and level does, leaves the pool intact.

The practical test of all this is the trial lesson, which costs nothing. Give the tutor a past-paper question your child got wrong and ask them to work it through against the published mark scheme. A specialist does that immediately and names the marks. Anyone else explains the topic. You will know inside fifteen minutes, and that is a far better test than a biography.

sections.heading: What each DP component is actually worth
paragraphs: Revision time should follow weighting, and most students allocate it by comfort instead. The table below sets out the published component structure for the subjects Mirdif families request most often. Read it next to your child's current marks and the misallocation is usually obvious within a minute: hours spent on Paper 1 recall in a subject where Paper 2 carries 44 per cent of the grade.

Two patterns are worth pulling out. First, the internal assessment is 20 per cent in Maths and in all three sciences. That is a fifth of the grade awarded for work done at a desk over weeks, with the criteria published in advance and no time pressure. It is the most recoverable fifth of any DP grade and the one students most often leave until it cannot be recovered.

Second, Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra content. In Mathematics, HL sits three papers at 30, 30 and 20 while SL sits two at 40 and 40, so the HL candidate has a whole additional assessment style to prepare. In Economics, HL Paper 3 carries 30 per cent and is quantitative in a way the SL course never asks for. A student moving from SL to HL in DP1 needs preparing for the format, not just the syllabus.

Weightings are published in each subject guide and are revised when a syllabus changes. sections.heading: Command terms are the mark scheme in disguise
paragraphs: The single most teachable thing in the DP is the difference between outline, describe, explain, analyse, evaluate, justify and discuss. Each has a defined expectation, and a question's marks are allocated against the term it uses. A student who writes a beautiful explanation in response to evaluate has answered a question nobody asked, and the mark scheme has no route to award the marks.

This is where plateaus come from. A Mirdif student revising Biology content for six weeks and staying at a 5 is usually not short of knowledge. They are answering every question the same way: recall, in sentences, at length. Explain wants a causal chain. Evaluate wants both sides and a judgement. Distinguish wants a stated point of contrast, not two separate descriptions. Outline wants brevity and gets penalised for padding by spending time the student needed elsewhere.

The fix is mechanical and fast. Take a marked paper, list the command term of every question that lost marks, and the pattern appears in one sitting. Then practise six questions using the same command term in a row rather than six questions on the same topic. Students find this dull and their marks move anyway, usually within three weeks, which is the shortest route to a visible change in any DP subject.

Mathematics has its own version: show that, hence, hence or otherwise, deduce, prove. Hence means the previous result must be used, and a correct answer reached another way loses method marks. Students lose these marks repeatedly and never learn why, because the lost mark looks like an arithmetic slip on the script.

sections.heading: The specific traps: maths, the sciences and the internal assessments
paragraphs: Mathematics HL Paper 3 is two long investigations, heavily scaffolded. The marks are distributed across the parts, which means a student who reads part (a), panics at part (c) and abandons the question loses the parts they could have done. The teachable habit is to attempt every part in order and to write the reasoning even where the final value is wrong, because method marks survive an arithmetic error and a blank does not.

In the sciences, Paper 1 now carries a data-based section as well as multiple choice, and that section is where uncertainty, gradient and intercept work is tested. Students who have never drawn a line of best fit by hand under time pressure lose marks that no amount of content revision recovers. Paper 2 extended response is lost to incomplete causal chains: the answer names the trend, names the result, and omits the mechanism in between, which is exactly the clause the mark scheme awards.

The internal assessments have their own failure modes. The maths exploration, recommended at 12 to 20 pages, fails on a topic too large to do personally rather than on mathematics; the strongest explorations are narrow. The scientific investigation, capped at 3,000 words, fails on a research question that cannot be answered with the data collected, and that fault is set in week one and cannot be repaired in week ten. Choosing the question properly is the highest-value hour of the whole process.

In English A, Paper 1 unseen analysis is the component that moves fastest with practice, because the skill being tested is responding to unfamiliar text types under time pressure. Weekly timed work on text types the student has not met is worth more than a term of studying texts they have.

sections.heading: Using past papers so they actually teach something
paragraphs: Most students use past papers as a mood check. They sit one, score it, feel either reassured or miserable, and sit another. That produces a graph of how they already perform and teaches almost nothing. Past papers teach when they are worked rather than sat.

The method that works is narrow and slightly tedious. Sit the paper under time. Mark it against the official mark scheme without mercy, awarding only what the scheme awards. Then separate the losses into three bins: did not know the content, knew it and answered the wrong command term, knew it and ran out of time. Those three have different remedies, and lumping them together is why revision plans fail. Content gaps need teaching. Command-term errors need the drill described above. Timing failures need a question-order strategy, not more knowledge.

A tutor earns their hour in the marking and the sorting, not in the sitting. A good lesson takes one marked paper and spends fifty minutes on the five questions where marks were lost for a reason the student cannot yet name. That is unglamorous, it is specific, and it is what changes a grade boundary.

On sourcing: official papers, mark schemes and subject guides belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson, and IB Gram neither reproduces nor supplies them. Your child's school holds the licensed access, and the subject teacher is the correct route. A tutor works from material the student already legitimately has.

sections.heading: The internal assessment boundary: what a tutor may touch
paragraphs: A fifth of a DP grade in most subjects is coursework the student must produce themselves, and this is where tutoring either earns its fee or destroys a candidacy. The IB's academic honesty rules make the exploration, the scientific investigation, the Extended Essay and the TOK essay the student's own work. A tutor who drafts any part of it creates a malpractice exposure for the student, and the consequence lands on the child, not the tutor.

The legitimate work is still substantial. A tutor may read the assessment criteria with the student rather than at them. They may interrogate a research question until it is answerable with the data available. They may teach referencing, structure and the conventions of a reflective paragraph. They may read a section the student has written and identify which criterion strand it does not yet meet and why. They may enforce a weekly schedule on a project that has no weekly pressure of its own.

What a tutor may not do is supply the question, supply the content, write, rewrite to completion, or edit the student's prose into their own voice. The working test is whether the student could explain, unprompted, why each paragraph is there. If they cannot, something has gone wrong regardless of who typed it. One ranking site in this market sells completed internal assessments outright; that is an integrity breach and an expulsion risk for the student, and declining to do it is not modesty, it is the only defensible position.

The same boundary covers the Extended Essay at 4,000 words, the TOK essay at 1,600 and the TOK exhibition commentary at 950. Coaching the process and giving feedback on the student's own text is the whole service, and families in Mirdif are told this before any money changes hands rather than after.

sections.heading: Timing a Mirdif session, and when to start
paragraphs: Secondary year groups in the eastern suburbs finish around 15:00 and reach Mirdif villas between roughly 15:30 and 16:45, depending on whether the route runs inside the community or comes back across Nad Al Hamar from Festival City. For most DP students that makes 17:30 the first reliable slot and 19:00 the most popular one, because DP1 and DP2 students also have school co-curriculars and are frequently not free at 16:30 on any day.

Start dates matter more than most families expect. A DP1 student who begins in October has time to change habits before anything is assessed externally. A DP2 student beginning after the first mock has roughly two terms, which is enough to fix component technique and an internal assessment but not enough to learn two years of HL content. Both are worth doing; they are different projects, and a tutor who does not say so is overselling.

Ramadan reshapes the week while it falls, and evening schedules shift accordingly. Post-iftar sessions are workable for DP students and are frequently more productive than a late-afternoon slot during fasting hours. Because lessons are over video, moving a slot by two hours for a month costs nothing and needs no renegotiation of anybody's drive.

The practical sequence is short. Tell us the subject, the level, the component that is weakest, and what time your child is genuinely free. Send one marked past paper or one returned internal assessment draft. Take the free trial lesson and judge it on whether the tutor could work your child's wrong answer against the mark scheme. Then fix a slot for the term, because consistency is worth more in this programme than intensity.

process.title: Name the component, not the subject
process.description: "HL Chemistry" is a brief nobody can act on. "Paper 2 extended response, losing the mechanism clause" is. If you do not know which component is weak, send the last marked paper and we will identify it before matching anybody.

process.title: Send one marked script
process.description: A past paper with the examiner's or teacher's marks on it tells us more in two minutes than a phone call does in twenty. It shows whether the losses are content, command term or timing, and those three need different tutors and different plans.

process.title: Free trial lesson over video
process.description: One lesson with the matched specialist, at no charge. Ask them to work your child's wrong answer against the official mark scheme and name where the marks sit. If they explain the topic instead, that is your answer and you are free to walk away.

process.title: Fix the slot and the target
process.description: Same tutor, same weekly time, held for the term, with one named component as the target. You get a short written note after each lesson saying what was worked and what the next target is, which is checkable against the next school assessment.

process.title: Review against real marks
process.description: At six weeks the question is whether the named component moved on a real piece of marked work. If it has not, the plan changes or the tutor does. We raise that ourselves rather than waiting to be asked, because a comfortable arrangement that is not working is the worst outcome for everyone.

whyPoints.title: Matched on level, not just subject
whyPoints.description: HL and SL are different assessments, not different amounts of the same one. HL Maths sits three papers at 30, 30 and 20; SL sits two at 40 and 40. Matching ignores that at your child's cost, so ours does not.

whyPoints.title: Work happens on real scripts
whyPoints.description: Lessons run on your child's own marked papers and the published mark schemes their school holds. We do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson material, and a tutor working from your child's actual losses needs none.

whyPoints.title: The pool is not limited to who will drive
whyPoints.description: A specialist in HL Computer Science or HL Economics Paper 3 does not have to live in the eastern suburbs for your child to work with them. Online delivery keeps that pool whole, which matters most in exactly the subjects where it is smallest.

whyPoints.title: Component-level written notes
whyPoints.description: After each lesson you get the component worked, the specific loss addressed and the next target, in writing. That is a claim you can check against the next marked paper rather than an impression of how the hour felt.

whyPoints.description: No IB exam or results date appears on this page, because the IB blocks automated verification and a wrong date is worse than no date. UAE schools sit the May session; your child's IB coordinator is the source for everything more specific.
