whyPoints.description: We coach, question and give feedback on internal assessments. We do not write, rewrite or supply them. That is said before payment, because the consequence of getting it wrong falls on your child rather than on us.

faqs.question: Will an IB tutor come to our house in Mirdif?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs home visits only in India, and tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video. In-home tutors do work in the eastern suburbs independently, and the market rate for in-home one-to-one in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel. If an adult in the room is what your child needs, that option exists elsewhere. What online delivery gives you instead is a specialist matched on subject and level rather than on willingness to drive to Mirdif at 16:30.

faqs.question: How much of my child's DP grade is the internal assessment?
faqs.answer: In Mathematics and in Physics, Chemistry and Biology it is 20 per cent. In SL Economics the portfolio is 30 per cent; in SL English A Language and Literature the individual oral is 30 per cent. That is a fifth to nearly a third of the grade, awarded for work done over weeks with the criteria published in advance and no exam pressure. It is the most recoverable part of any DP grade and the part most often left too late to recover. Confirm the exact figure in your child's subject guide.

faqs.question: What makes HL Mathematics Paper 3 so different from Papers 1 and 2?
faqs.answer: It is two long, heavily scaffolded investigations rather than a set of discrete questions, and it carries 20 per cent of the HL grade. Marks are spread across the parts, so the damaging habit is reading part (a), losing confidence at part (c) and abandoning the whole question. Attempting every part in order, and writing the reasoning even when the final value comes out wrong, preserves method marks that a blank cannot. It is a technique problem far more often than a content problem, which is why it responds quickly to targeted work.

faqs.question: Which schools in and around Mirdif offer the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: The eastern suburbs are served by an IB continuum school inside Mirdif itself and by several in the wider arc, with two IB schools in Dubai Festival City and British-curriculum schools out towards Academic City. Families here commonly use Uptown International School, Star International School Mirdif, Deira International School, Universal American School and Dubai English Speaking College among others. We name them as scheduling context only; IB Gram has no affiliation with, or endorsement from, any school mentioned on this page.

faqs.question: Why do command terms matter more than content for a plateaued student?
faqs.answer: Because marks are allocated against the term the question uses. Explain wants a causal chain; evaluate wants two sides and a judgement; distinguish wants a stated contrast rather than two descriptions; outline is penalised for padding. A student answering every question with recall at length will sit at a 4 or 5 whatever they revise. The fastest diagnostic is to list the command term of every question that lost marks on the last paper. The pattern usually appears in a single sitting, and three weeks of drilling one term moves it.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start tutoring in DP2?
faqs.answer: It depends what you are trying to fix, and an honest tutor will say which. Two terms is enough to change component technique, rebuild command-term discipline and get an internal assessment to a decent standard. It is not enough to learn two years of HL content that was never learned. Both situations are worth working on, but they are different projects with different realistic outcomes, and anyone promising the second in that time is selling rather than teaching. Send the mock script and we will tell you which one you have.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the maths exploration without writing it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the most valuable hour is the first one. The exploration, recommended at 12 to 20 pages, usually fails on topic choice rather than on mathematics: the subject is too broad to engage with personally. A tutor can interrogate the question until it is narrow and answerable, teach the criteria, and read what the student has written and say which criterion strand it does not yet meet. A tutor cannot supply the topic, the content or the sentences. Your child must be able to explain every page unprompted.

faqs.question: How should my child use past papers between now and the exams?
faqs.answer: Work them, do not just sit them. Sit under time, mark strictly against the official mark scheme, then sort every lost mark into three bins: content not known, wrong command term answered, ran out of time. Each has a different remedy, and mixing them is why revision plans stall. Content needs teaching, command terms need drilling, timing needs a question-order strategy. The school holds licensed access to papers and mark schemes; IB Gram does not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson material.

faqs.question: What time can lessons start for a Mirdif student?
faqs.answer: Secondary year groups reach Mirdif villas roughly between 15:30 and 16:45 depending on route, so 17:30 is the first reliably workable slot and 19:00 is the most requested. Children living in Al Khawaneej and the outer eastern areas arrive later and tend to book 18:00 or 19:00. Because lessons run over video there is no travel block on either side, so the booked minute is the start minute, and shifting a slot during Ramadan to a post-iftar time costs nothing to arrange.

faqs.question: Do you cover both HL and SL in the sciences?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we match differently for each. The component structure is shared, with Paper 1 at 36 per cent, Paper 2 at 44 and the scientific investigation at 20, but the depth and the extended-response expectations differ considerably. A tutor comfortable with SL Paper 2 is not automatically comfortable with HL. We ask which level before matching and we will say so if the specialist your child needs is not immediately free rather than filling the slot with whoever is.

faqs.question: What is the word limit on the Extended Essay and the TOK essay?
faqs.answer: The Extended Essay is capped at 4,000 words, the TOK essay at 1,600, and the TOK exhibition commentary at 950. Those ceilings are part of the assessment, and work that overruns is penalised, so planning the structure against the limit from the start matters more than editing down at the end. A tutor may teach structure, question the argument and give feedback on the student's own draft. Writing or rewriting any of it would be malpractice under the IB's academic honesty rules.

faqs.question: Are some HL subjects hard to staff for a family out in the eastern suburbs?
faqs.answer: At Higher Level, Computer Science, Economics Paper 3 and some Group 1 and Group 2 language combinations have the thinnest pools. That is the clearest practical argument for online matching: restricting the search to tutors willing to drive to the eastern suburbs on a weekday afternoon often leaves nobody on the list for those subjects. If no specialist is available for your child's exact subject and level, we say so rather than substituting a generalist, and we would rather lose the booking than fill it badly.

faqs.question: Does Dubai regulate private tutors, and what should I ask one?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask any independent tutor directly whether they hold one, and note that ADEK's ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid tutoring of their own students.

faqs.question: After six weeks of lessons, what should have changed on paper?
faqs.answer: By whether the named component moved on a real marked piece of work. Not by how the lessons felt, and not by a score on an internal test we set ourselves. At the outset one component is named as the target, the written note after each lesson records what was worked, and at six weeks that target is checked against the next school assessment. If it has not shifted, the plan changes or the tutor does, and we raise it first. No grade is promised anywhere on this page, because no tutor can honestly promise one.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two of my child's six DP subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and usually not at Higher Level. A tutor genuinely strong in HL Mathematics and HL Physics exists but is uncommon, and accepting a weaker second subject to keep one tutor costs a term you cannot get back. The honest arrangement for two sliding subjects is two specialists on two evenings, with a shared written log so revision does not double up. Because no travel is involved, consecutive slots on one evening are straightforward, and so are two siblings at two different levels.

intro.heading: Why the quotes to this address come back high, and what to do about it
paragraphs: Families in Mohammed Bin Rashid City notice something when they start ringing round for a Diploma tutor: the numbers are higher than the ones friends in Downtown or Business Bay were quoted for the same subject. It is not imagination and it is not a judgement about the district's ability to pay. It is geography priced into an hourly rate, and once you see the mechanism the decision becomes much easier to make.

The district is built around large plots and generous internal road layouts, with villa communities set back behind gated access and a limited number of entry points. For a tutor driving from Al Barsha or Jumeirah at four in the afternoon, the last two kilometres can take as long as the first twelve. Add the second visit of the evening somewhere else and the arithmetic is simple: a tutor working here fits fewer sessions into an evening than one working in a tower community, so the rate per session rises to compensate.

The Dubai market bands show the result. In-home one-to-one runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with travel inside the figure, and quotes to large-villa districts cluster towards the upper half of that range. Qualified subject tutors working online sit at about AED 150 to 300 an hour, specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, and budget online tutors are advertised from around AED 33 to 65. Monthly packages seen in the market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are other providers' published figures, read in October 2026, and they are market context rather than IB Gram's price list.

What matters is that the premium is paid for a drive rather than for teaching. There is no mechanism by which navigating District One's internal roads improves anyone's grasp of Higher Level Economics. Worse, the premium narrows the field: the tutors willing to make the journey are a small subset of those who could teach the subject, so a family here can pay the top of the band and still get a generalist. That is the trade this page sets out to make visible.

IB Gram delivers Diploma tuition to Mohammed Bin Rashid City as one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time, matched to the subject and level rather than to the postcode. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India, which is also why no travel component sits inside what you pay us. The sections below decode the quotes you will receive, cost a two-child household, and say where the money is wasted in a house this size.

These three contexts carry different cost profiles, and confusing them is why families here overspend in one year and underspend in the one that counted.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an internal assessment and the deadlines cluster rather than spreading evenly, so the weeks when one subject needs most attention are the weeks the student has least to give. This is the stage where the amounts are largest and where allocating a fixed budget well matters more than negotiating a rate.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision within reach of Mohammed Bin Rashid City is good, with IB schools in the district and immediately around it. The pool of tutors willing to drive into a gated villa community at four in the afternoon is a different matter, and that gap, rather than any shortage of teaching talent in Dubai, is what the local premium prices.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed rather than examined, with the Personal Project in the final year. This is the stage where tutoring is cheapest to make count and where most households spend nothing, then pay for it in DP1. A short block securing algebraic fluency or writing structure in Year 9 costs a fraction of the remedial work the same gap demands two years later under examination pressure.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving this district run MYP and then offer both the Diploma and A Levels, so the end of MYP is a genuine fork. One session testing readiness for a Higher Level subject, rather than a term of general support, prevents the most expensive misplacement available in the whole programme.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led and transdisciplinary, ending in the exhibition. The honest cost advice is to spend little and narrowly: a defined block on reading fluency or number facts, then stop. Weekly one-to-one tuition across a primary year is the least efficient purchase in this market and among the most commonly sold, particularly in districts where households can absorb it without noticing.
programmes.countryNote: Villa communities with young families attract a lot of local tutoring supply aimed at primary ages, often sold as ongoing support. We will tell a primary parent here that a four-session block is enough when it is, which costs us the recurring revenue and is the correct advice.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-rash.subjectsIntro: A Diploma budget is spent subject by subject, so allocation is the real question. These are the courses we cover for Mohammed Bin Rashid City families, each noted for where marks are genuinely lost, because that determines whether a session is worth a specialist rate.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Expensive to leave and cheap to fix early. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, exposing algebraic fluency, and Higher Level adds a third paper with its own style of extended problem that needs its own sessions.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling led, with calculator competence examinable. Losses sit in explaining output the student can generate, which is a technique problem and therefore among the cheaper things to correct.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Popular in this district and deceptively demanding at Higher Level. Diagram accuracy and evaluation depth separate the bands, and the internal assessment commentaries collide with other subjects' deadlines in DP1.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Frameworks are easy and evaluation is not. A student applying a tool without weighing it sits mid-band indefinitely, which is a technique loss and the cheapest category of problem to address.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Two papers plus an independent investigation worth a fifth of the grade. Equilibrium reasoning, organic mechanism detail and significant figures in the data-based section are the reliable losses.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Weak algebra costs Physics marks unrelated to physics, so a maths block can be charged against two grades. Uncertainty treatment is the least-taught and most-penalised area at both levels.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Terminology precision outweighs calculation. A fluent but imprecise writer plateaus, and command-term discipline moves the grade faster than additional content coverage.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Carries the Individual Oral and the Higher Level essay. Describing texts rather than analysing construction is the standard loss, and it responds to a short targeted block rather than a year of sessions.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Few tutors teach it, so it carries a scarcity cost rather than a difficulty cost. Support is structural: reading the prescribed title, building an argument, locating where the instrument awards marks.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of independent research. The best money spent is one early session narrowing the question, because a bad question cannot be rescued later by any number of paid hours.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-rash.regionsTitle: Mohammed Bin Rashid City and the districts around it
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-rash.regionsIntro: This district sits between Meydan and Al Quoz and contains several distinct communities. These notes are about what each does to a tutoring quote and to a session time, rather than about the architecture.

regions.name: District One
regions.note: Large plots, long internal roads and gated access, which is the single clearest driver of a high in-home quote in this part of Dubai. Online delivery removes the entire component.

regions.name: Sobha Hartland
regions.note: Denser towers and villas inside the wider district, with two schools on site. Quotes here are lower than District One's for the same work, purely because access is quicker.

regions.name: Meydan
regions.note: Immediately west and sharing schools with this district. A tutor already visiting Meydan may extend to here more cheaply, so it is worth asking whether they have existing clients nearby.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: Established IB provision a short drive south and one of the few nearby communities where teaching staff actually live, which occasionally produces a lower quote.

regions.name: Al Quoz
regions.note: The corridor's tuition-centre district, immediately north-west. Group classes there are the cheapest format reachable from here and reasonable for a shared topic gap.

regions.name: Business Bay
regions.note: Towers with short access times, which is why quotes there sit lower than here for identical teaching. Useful as the comparison that shows the premium is about access.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Shortest journeys in the corridor and the lowest in-home quotes nearby. Families who have moved here from Downtown usually notice the quote difference immediately.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Near the creek crossings with IB continuum provision, and a short run from this district outside peak hours. Relevant mainly for where the schools are rather than the tutors.

schoolClusters.city: Mohammed Bin Rashid City, Sobha Hartland and Meydan
schoolClusters.note: The schools inside or adjacent to the district cover IB Diploma provision and British-curriculum routes within minutes of one another. Two households paying the same rate may therefore be buying support for different qualifications entirely.

schoolClusters.city: Al Quoz, Al Barsha and Al Jaddaf
schoolClusters.note: The schools families from this district drive to for particular subject combinations. Several run an IB continuum and others run IGCSE before splitting into the Diploma or A Levels, which sets the subject-choice conversation a year earlier than most parents expect.

The lowest-cost format that reliably moves a Diploma grade, because it leaves room for practice between sessions and lets the tutor check whether the practice happened. Over two terms it costs less than most households here expect and more than they budget for in a single month, which is why the block total matters more than the rate.

sections.heading: What actually drives a quote to this district
paragraphs: A tutoring quote is built from components, and almost nobody itemises them. The table below does, with market figures attributed to the providers that published them. Read it to see which components apply to your household and which do not, because a quote that bundles everything together makes it impossible to tell what you are declining when you decline a visit.

The component that dominates in Mohammed Bin Rashid City is access time. A tutor's working evening is finite: between four and eight o'clock there are four hours, and a session plus a journey at each end consumes more of them here than in a tower community. A tutor who can fit three sessions into an evening in Business Bay and two here has to price accordingly, and that is a rational response rather than opportunism.

The second component is scarcity of willingness, which compounds the first. Subject specialists in short supply, such as Theory of Knowledge or Higher Level mathematics with Paper 3 experience, have no need to accept a long journey when nearer work exists. So the further a household sits from the city's teaching concentrations, the more likely it is that the in-home option delivers a generalist at a specialist price. That is the part a quote never itemises and the part worth knowing.

The third and smallest component is the one parents assume is largest: teaching skill. In this market price tracks delivery model and claimed credentials rather than observed outcomes, because outcomes are not visible at the point of purchase. The practical consequence is that comparing quotes tells you little, and comparing behaviour in a trial lesson tells you a great deal.

sections.heading: The four quotes you will get, and how to read each one
paragraphs: Ring round for a Diploma tutor from this district and you will receive roughly four shapes of quote. They are not comparable as printed, which is the problem, so here is how to normalise them before you decide. Each has a legitimate use and each conceals something different, and knowing which is which saves more than any negotiation.

The first is a plain hourly rate for a home visit, usually at the upper half of the band because of the access time described above. The second is a monthly in-home package, commonly around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits, which looks like a discount and is actually a commitment: ask what happens to a visit you cancel and whether unused visits carry forward. The third is a per-session online rate, which is the cleanest to compare because nothing is bundled into it.

The fourth is a monthly online package, advertised in this market around AED 799 for eight sessions. Note the unit carefully, because eight sessions is not eight hours unless the session length is stated, and that distinction accounts for most of the confusion in this market. Normalise everything to a cost per teaching hour, then ask what each quote includes by way of marked practice between sessions, written feedback, and replacement if the match fails.

One further warning specific to comparison shopping. A quote that will not state where the tutor is based should be treated with caution, not because teaching from outside the UAE is a problem but because concealing it is. Several providers ranking for Dubai queries present a local appearance while routing families elsewhere, sometimes behind a non-UAE phone number or a price in US dollars. Ask directly; a straight answer costs nothing to give.

sections.heading: Two children, one budget: the arithmetic nobody publishes
paragraphs: Villa districts tend to house families with more than one school-age child, and the tutoring market is priced per student rather than per household. That means the point at which tutoring stops being proportionate arrives sooner here than the per-hour figures suggest, and it arrives without anybody doing the sum.

Take a plausible case: one child in DP1 needing maths support and one in Year 10 needing science. At qualified-tutor online rates of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, two weekly sessions is eight to ten sessions a month and a figure in the low to middle four figures. At in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 with the district premium, the same arrangement moves into territory that competes with a term's school fees. The teaching has not changed; the number of journeys has doubled.

There are two sensible responses and one false economy. The first sensible response is sequencing: fund the child with the time-critical need now, usually the one closer to an examination session or an internal assessment deadline, and the other next term. The second is finding the shared cause, because siblings in the same household often have the same gap, and an algebra block can be charged against two children's grades in two different year groups.

The false economy is putting two children in one session to halve the cost. It sounds efficient and it rarely works: different year groups, different specifications, different weaknesses, and a session where each child is idle half the time. The exception is genuinely parallel need, such as two siblings in the same year group sitting the same specification with the same named gap, which does occur and is worth asking about rather than assuming.

sections.heading: Online against a home visit to a large-plot villa
paragraphs: With the components itemised, the comparison can be made properly rather than as advocacy. For a household in this district the decisive variables are access time, the breadth of the tutor pool, what happens when a session has to move, and whether a person in the room is genuinely required.

Access time favours online absolutely, and in this district by more than anywhere else in the corridor. The session starts when the student is ready rather than when a tutor has cleared the gate, which on a weekday afternoon can be the difference between a four o'clock start and a quarter past five. An alert student at four is worth more per dirham than a tired one at six, and that is a quality point rather than a convenience one.

Pool breadth favours online decisively, because the choice becomes every available specialist rather than those prepared to make the drive. Rescheduling favours online by a wide margin: a cancelled in-home visit wastes a journey and is often charged, while an online session moves inside the same week at no cost to anyone. Across a Diploma year containing mocks, travel, school trips and illness, that difference alone accounts for several sessions' worth of money.

The variable that genuinely favours a home visit is presence, and for a younger child or a teenager who will not work unless someone is physically there it can be decisive. We will not argue that away. To be unambiguous: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so the choice here is between our online delivery and a local arrangement you would make yourself, with this page's bands to judge it by.

sections.heading: Where the money goes to waste in a household like this one
paragraphs: Districts where tutoring is affordable without careful thought are districts where it is most often wasted, and that is a statement about budgets rather than about parents. When a monthly figure can be absorbed without noticing, the discipline that makes tutoring work tends to be absent, because nothing forces the question of whether it is working.

The largest waste is duration bought before diagnosis: weekly sessions booked after a disappointing report, continuing for two years, with nobody ever establishing what is actually losing marks. The second is paying a specialist rate for homework supervision, which is a genuine service and not a specialist one. The third is funding three subjects when one weakness underlies all three, typically algebra under maths and two sciences, or writing structure under two essay subjects.

The fourth is specific to this district: paying the access premium in subjects where presence changes nothing, which at Diploma level is nearly all of them. The fifth is the block that renews because stopping feels like a risk, long after its purpose was met. And the sixth is buying support for the child who complains loudest rather than the one with the time-critical deadline, which is understandable and still the wrong order.

What all six share is that none of them feels like waste while it is happening. A session that is attended and politely delivered looks like progress, because attendance is easy to observe and diagnosis is not. The remedy is mechanical: write down at the start what the block is for, and check at six weeks whether that specific thing has changed. If it has not, change the plan rather than extending it.

sections.heading: Counted backwards from the May session: when the money works
paragraphs: UAE IB schools sit the May examination session, and spending decisions make far more sense read backwards from it than forwards from today. The deadlines that constrain a Diploma student are set mostly by the school rather than by the IB, which surprises families who assume the opposite and then meet an internal assessment deadline months before anything the IB publishes.

Two cautions before using the table. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages. The IB holds those, and your child's Diploma coordinator holds the school's internal versions, which govern internal assessments, Extended Essay drafts and Theory of Knowledge submissions. Confirm every date with the coordinator rather than with a tutoring website, including this one, and treat an internal deadline as firm from the moment it is announced.

Read for spending, the calendar gives a simple rule. Spend small and early on anything irreversible, such as an internal assessment question or an Extended Essay focus. Spend moderately and steadily through DP1 on a diagnosed weakness. Spend heavily and briefly in the final window if the mock says you must, then stop. The pattern that fails is the inverse: nothing in DP1, panic in DP2, and a large open-ended commitment made in the month when there is least time for it to work.

One scheduling point worth asking about in advance. Internal assessment deadlines in different subjects cluster, and they cluster near the Extended Essay deadline, so the weeks when a subject most needs attention are the weeks the student has least to give. A coordinator can usually say where those collisions fall for a cohort. Knowing it in DP1 lets you move a block earlier rather than bidding for evenings that are already committed.

sections.heading: KHDA, the fee freeze and judging whether the spend is working
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Annual inspection runs on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, published school by school, and the departmental commentary inside a report is a free second opinion on whether a weak grade reflects the student or the provision.

The cost context this year is unusual. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places.

With the largest education line flat, a tutoring figure is more visible in a household budget than usual, so here is the test. At six weeks you should be able to see three things: a written statement of what was costing marks, marked practice showing that specific thing improving, and a mark or grade trend in the subject. If all three are absent, the spend is not working however agreeable the sessions are. The test requires no subject knowledge, which is exactly why it is the one to use.

On credentials, plainly: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or IB accredited, and does not claim to be. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. Any service describing its individual tutors with that phrase is referring to something else or saying something untrue.

sections.heading: What is not for sale here at any price
paragraphs: A page about cost has to name the place where the cheapest-looking option is the most expensive. At least one operator ranking for UAE IB queries sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. To a household under deadline pressure that can look like a solution with a known cost, which is precisely why it is dangerous. Submitting work that is not the student's own is academic misconduct under IB rules, the student bears the consequence, which can be the loss of the Diploma, and the website bears none of it.

What is legitimately for sale is substantial and good value. A tutor may explain the assessment criteria in the language the examiner uses, question a research question until it is answerable with the resources available, warn that a method will generate too little data, teach the underlying content, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. Those interventions sit at the top of this page's value ordering precisely because they are cheap relative to their effect.

What is not available from us at any rate is choosing the question, supplying the method or the data, writing any part of the text, or editing a draft into its final form, and nor will we hand over a worked example close enough to the student's own task that copying becomes the obvious next step. We state this to the student in the first session rather than in small print, because a sixteen-year-old under pressure deserves the boundary before they are standing on it.

We also do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, and we do not host them for download. We reference them and link to the official source. That costs nothing, is the lawful position, and is more useful anyway, because the official version is the current one while a stale file circulating in a parents' group is a reliable route to revising withdrawn content.

sections.heading: Getting started from Mohammed Bin Rashid City
paragraphs: Begin by naming a figure. Tell us what you are willing to spend monthly and for how long, alongside the subject, the level, the latest grade and the teacher's last comment quoted rather than summarised. A service that does not ask about the budget will recommend more sessions than you need, because recommending more is always the safer answer for them rather than for you.

If there are two children, say so at the outset and say which deadline is closer. Sequencing by time-criticality is usually the right answer with a fixed budget, and it is a decision best made before either child has started rather than halfway through a term when stopping one feels like a punishment.

We then propose a tutor and run a free trial lesson, which is a diagnosis rather than a sales call. Afterwards ask for a written statement of what is costing marks and what the block is for. If that statement is general, do not book at any rate, because without it there is nothing to check at six weeks and no way to tell a working arrangement from a comfortable one.

And the honest part. Availability is finite and some Diploma areas are thinner than others: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay supervision, Higher Level mathematics with Paper 3 experience, and second languages beyond the common ones. When the right tutor is not free at your preferred time we say so and offer a different slot, a short wait, or a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same syllabus to Gulf Standard Time. We will not substitute a related subject or level and charge the same rate.

process.description: The first session costs nothing. Ask for a written statement of what is costing marks and what the block is for. If the answer is general, do not book, whatever the hourly rate attached to it or however pleasant the lesson felt.

process.title: Sequence two children rather than halving a session
process.description: Two children in one session rarely works, because year groups, specifications and weaknesses differ. Funding the time-critical need now and the other next term usually produces two results instead of none.

process.title: Check the three signals at six weeks
process.description: A written diagnosis, marked practice showing that specific thing improving, and a mark trend. If all three are missing, the spend is not working, and the test applies at every price point in this market including ours.

whyPoints.description: We say plainly why quotes to a large-plot villa district come back high, itemise the components, and show which ones online delivery removes entirely. No other page in this market tells a household what it is actually being charged for.

whyPoints.description: Hourly in-home, monthly in-home package, hourly online, monthly online package. We show how to normalise each to a cost per teaching hour and name the question that exposes what each conceals, including unused-session terms.

whyPoints.title: Household arithmetic, not per-student arithmetic
whyPoints.description: The market prices per student and families budget per household. We publish the two-child sums and recommend sequencing by time-criticality, which usually produces two results rather than two half-finished arrangements.

whyPoints.description: A written diagnosis, marked practice on that specific thing, and a mark trend, all visible at six weeks. It needs no subject knowledge and it works at any price point, including on us.

faqs.question: Why are home tutor quotes to Mohammed Bin Rashid City higher than elsewhere in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Access time, mostly. The district is built around large plots with long internal roads and gated entry, so the last two kilometres can take as long as the previous twelve at four in the afternoon. A tutor who could fit three sessions into an evening in a tower community fits two here, and prices accordingly. The market band for in-home one-to-one in Dubai is roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, and quotes to villa districts cluster in the upper half of it.

faqs.question: Do your tutors come to homes in this district?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video throughout the UAE, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. We say so plainly because home tutor is the phrase parents search and leaving the impression open would be easy. Local in-home arrangements certainly exist here and this page gives you the bands to judge them by. What online delivery changes for a household in this district is the earliest possible start time and the breadth of the tutor pool.

faqs.question: What exactly am I paying extra for with a home visit?
faqs.answer: A car journey, a person in the room, and not having to set up a video call. Those are real and for a younger child presence can matter. What the premium does not buy is subject knowledge: there is no mechanism by which driving into a gated villa community improves anyone's grasp of Higher Level Economics. It also narrows the field to tutors willing to make a long evening journey, so a household here can pay the top of the band and still get a generalist.

faqs.question: We have two children who both need help. How should we budget?
faqs.answer: Sequence rather than double. At qualified online rates of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, two children with one weekly subject each is eight to ten sessions a month and a low-to-middle four-figure monthly total; at in-home rates with this district's premium it approaches a term's school fees. Fund the time-critical need first, usually the child closer to an examination session or an internal assessment deadline, and the other next term. Also look for a shared cause, because siblings often have the same underlying gap.

faqs.question: Can two siblings share one tutoring session to halve the cost?
faqs.answer: Usually not usefully. Different year groups, different specifications and different weaknesses mean each child is idle for half the session, and the saving buys a diluted hour rather than a cheaper one. The exception is genuinely parallel need: two siblings in the same year group, on the same specification, with the same named gap. That does happen and is worth asking about rather than assuming. Otherwise sequencing one child this term and the other next produces two results instead of two compromises.

faqs.question: How do I compare an in-home package against an online one?
faqs.answer: Convert both to a cost per teaching hour, which most quotes avoid making easy. A monthly in-home package of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits is eight contact hours. An online package advertised around AED 799 is eight sessions, which is only eight hours if a session is sixty minutes, so ask. Then ask what each includes beyond contact time: marked practice between sessions, written feedback, and replacement if the match fails. Those inclusions move the real value more than the headline figure does.

faqs.question: Where do households in districts like this one waste the most?
faqs.answer: Six places. Duration bought before diagnosis, with weekly sessions running for two years and nobody naming the problem. Specialist rates spent on homework supervision. Three subjects funded for one underlying weakness. The access premium paid where presence changes nothing. Blocks renewing because stopping feels risky. And funding the child who complains loudest ahead of the one with the closer deadline. None is solved by a lower rate; all are solved by a written purpose and a six-week check.

faqs.question: How do I know whether the tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: Three signals at six weeks. A written statement from the tutor of what was costing marks. Marked practice in that specific area showing movement. And a mark or grade trend in the subject. If all three are present the spend is working even if the grade has not moved yet; if all three are absent it is not working however pleasant the sessions are. The test needs no subject knowledge from you, and it applies identically at AED 60 an hour and AED 450 an hour.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects should we fund first if the budget is fixed?
faqs.answer: Start with anything irreversible: an internal assessment question or an Extended Essay focus, which is one or two sessions and cannot be bought back later at any price. Then the Higher Level subject chosen above the student's foundation, because that gap widens monthly and is cheapest to close in DP1. Then the transferable weakness under several subjects, usually algebra or writing structure, because one block moves two or three grades. The subject with the lowest grade is often a symptom of something higher in that order.

faqs.question: Is a group class in Al Quoz a reasonable alternative from here?
faqs.answer: For a named topic shared by several students, yes, and it is the cheapest format reachable from this district. It works poorly for internal assessment feedback, paper technique or anything personal, because an individual habit will not be noticed in a room of six. Note also that the journey is back, so the access problem reappears in a different form. The test is whether you can name the gap: if you can, a group class on that topic may be efficient, and if you cannot it is a cheap way of not solving the problem.

faqs.question: Are school fees rising in Dubai, and how should that change our thinking?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. With the largest education line flat, a tutoring figure is more visible in the household budget than usual. Practically, it makes this a good year to insist on a written purpose and a six-week check rather than absorbing an undifferentiated monthly payment into a general rise.

faqs.question: Does a tutor's permit affect what we should pay?
faqs.answer: It should not, because the permit costs them nothing. MoHRE issues a private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published, so disregard any specific amount quoted.

faqs.question: Can we pause sessions during Ramadan or the summer to control cost?
faqs.answer: Yes, and online delivery makes pausing cheap rather than disruptive. During Ramadan sessions commonly move to a post-Iftar slot, with no journey to renegotiate at either end, and a holiday pause costs nothing but a held slot. The exception is the eight weeks before the examination session, where pausing costs more than it saves. Agree a pause in advance so the slot is kept rather than released, and if the family is leaving the Gulf, agree which time zone the session is pinned to.

faqs.question: What if we start late in DP2 after a poor mock?
faqs.answer: It can still work, with a changed plan. With eight to twelve weeks of usable time the first session should mark the mock question by question, and the plan that follows should abandon some topics deliberately rather than attempting everything. Expect a high monthly figure for a short bounded block rather than a modest figure spread thin. What you should not buy at that stage is an open-ended arrangement, because the window closes before an open-ended plan has had time to work, and nobody can promise a grade inside it.

faqs.question: What happens if the specialist we want is fully booked?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than substituting quietly. Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay supervision and Higher Level mathematics with Paper 3 experience are genuinely thin, and the early-evening Gulf Standard Time slots this district wants after the school run fill first. The options are a different slot, a short wait, or a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same syllabus to Gulf Standard Time, disclosed as such. We will not substitute a related subject or level, and the trial lesson is free so asking costs nothing.

faqs.question: What should I send to get a recommendation that fits our budget?
faqs.answer: Five things. The monthly figure you are comfortable with and for how long. The subject and whether it is Higher or Standard Level, for each child. The latest grade, labelled as mock or classwork. The teacher's last written comment, quoted rather than paraphrased. And which deadline is closest across the household, because that decides the sequencing. A photograph of one marked paper beats all five, and with it we can usually propose a tutor the same day.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-rash.closingHeading: Price the teaching, not the journey
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-rash.closingBody: Quotes to this district come back high because of the drive, and the drive is the one component of a tutoring price that buys nothing academic. Normalise every quote you hold to a cost per teaching hour, ask what each includes beyond contact time, and set aside any that will not say where the tutor is based. Then send us the subject, the level, the monthly figure and which child's deadline is closest, and we will propose a tutor and run the first session at no cost. Check the three signals at six weeks.

intro.heading: The Diploma is a six-term project, not a revision sprint
paragraphs: Motor City sits between Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and the Dubai Autodrome, with GEMS Metropole School inside the community running a British curriculum through IGCSE. Diploma students from here commute out — to JESS Arabian Ranches, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Fairgreen International School or one of the other Dubailand-corridor schools — and come home into a queue of evening commitments. That shape matters, because the thing that actually determines a Diploma result is not how hard the final term is worked but whether the six terms before it were spent on the right things.

Most families searching for an IB home tutor in Motor City are at term five or six. The marks have come back short, the session is close, and the request is for intensive help. That is a legitimate request and it works for some components. But it is the dearest point on the curve, and the work it can do is limited by what has already closed: an Internal Assessment already submitted cannot be improved, an Extended Essay research question locked in DP1 cannot be rewritten, and a subject-level choice made at the start of DP1 cannot be revisited at all.

So this page is a calendar. It sets out what each of the six terms should produce, separates the deadlines your school controls from the ones the IB controls, shows where the Ramadan window falls against a Dubai academic year, and prices support term by term rather than by the hour. The aim is that a family at term one can plan, and a family at term five can at least see clearly what is still movable.

One honest caveat about dates, which this page observes throughout. UAE candidates sit the May session. No IB examination or results date appears here, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. A family reorganises travel and a revision plan around an examination date, so publishing an unverified one would be worse than publishing none. Your school's Diploma coordinator has the real calendar, and the deadlines that bind first are internal anyway.

Delivery is stated plainly because it changes what you should expect. Tuition for UAE families runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and a recording the student keeps. IB Gram does not operate home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. For a Motor City family the practical effect is scheduling: sessions can start at 17:30 after the drive home, run as short as 45 minutes, or sit at 20:30 after a fixture, none of which a visiting tutor can offer across this part of Dubailand.

sections.heading: The six terms, counted backwards from results day
paragraphs: A Diploma plan works backwards or it does not work. Counting forwards from today produces a revision timetable; counting backwards from results day shows which decisions close and when, and decisions closing is what actually limits a grade. The six terms of DP1 and DP2 each have a job, and a family that knows the job can tell at any point whether they are ahead or behind.

Term one of DP1 is about habits and choices. Subject and level selections are confirmed here and cannot be revisited meaningfully later, so a mismatch between a student and a course — Analysis and Approaches for someone who needed Applications and Interpretation, or a Higher Level science for someone carrying three of them — has to be identified now. It is also when non-calculator fluency, command-term discipline and the habit of showing method are cheapest to install.

Terms two and three of DP1 are about the internal assessments and the Extended Essay research question. Most schools set the EE subject and supervisor here, agree the research question, and run the first formal reflection. Science investigation methods are often approved in this window too. These are the dates families discover afterwards, and they are the ones a tutor can do most about if involved before them.

DP2 runs the other way: terms four and five are content completion plus the remaining internal deadlines and the TOK essay, and term six is examination technique and timed practice. By term six the only movable things are technique, timing, question selection and residual content. Everything internally assessed has closed. That is not a reason to skip term six — it is a reason not to let it be the only term you buy.

sections.heading: Which deadlines are your school's, and which are the IB's
paragraphs: Families routinely assume the IB sets every date. In practice almost every deadline a Diploma student actually meets is set by their school, working within the IB's submission windows, and the school's dates fall considerably earlier. That distinction is worth understanding because it changes who you ask and how much flexibility exists.

The school sets: the Extended Essay subject allocation, supervisor allocation, research question approval, reflection session dates, draft dates and final submission; internal assessment method approval and submission for every subject; the TOK exhibition and essay dates; mock examination windows; and the internal cut-off by which Higher Level content must be taught. These are the dates that constrain a student's year, and they are negotiable only in the sense that a school may grant an individual extension.

The IB sets the external session, the submission windows your school is working back from, and the results release. UAE candidates sit the May session. This page does not publish IB session or results dates because ibo.org blocks automated verification and no IB date in this project could be confirmed from the IB itself; your Diploma coordinator has them and ibo.org is authoritative.

The practical action is short and worth doing in the first fortnight of DP1. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the internal calendar in writing — every internal deadline for every subject plus the core — and put it on one page. Almost no family does this, and it is the single cheapest thing available: it converts a two-year programme from a vague pressure into a list of dates that can be planned against.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the UAE academic calendar and where revision actually fits
paragraphs: This is the part of planning that almost no tutoring page in this market addresses, and it is the part a Dubai family lives with. The UAE academic year carries its own rhythm — a long summer break, National Day, a winter break, a spring break and Ramadan — and the Ramadan period in particular reshapes a school day and a family evening at the same time as it falls in the run-up to summer examinations.

During Ramadan, school hours are shortened and the shape of the day changes: energy in the afternoon is lower, and the productive window for concentrated work moves to after Iftar. For a Diploma student in term five or six that is not a minor inconvenience, because it coincides with the period when timed paper practice should be at its most intense. A revision plan written in September that assumes thirty even weeks has not accounted for it.

What works in practice is to treat the Ramadan weeks as a different kind of work rather than as lost time. Short post-Iftar sessions, typically between 20:30 and 22:00, suit review, recall testing and marking a paper the student sat earlier. Full three-hour timed papers are better placed either side of the period. Recall-heavy work — definitions, formula lists, identification tables — fits well into short late sessions, and content teaching generally does not.

The planning consequence is to front-load. If Ramadan falls in the term before the session, the full-length timed paper practice has to start earlier than it otherwise would, and content completion has to be genuinely finished before it rather than running into it. A family that identifies this in term four has options; a family that meets it in term six has lost several weeks of their intended plan. Sessions can be rescheduled to post-Iftar timing on request, at no additional cost, and every session is recorded so a student working late can revisit it the next day.

sections.heading: What support costs term by term, not per hour
paragraphs: Hourly rates tell you very little about what a Diploma costs to support, because the need is uneven across six terms. A better unit is the term, and the pattern that actually works is heavier at the start, concentrated around each internal deadline, and heavier again at the end. Priced that way, the total is often lower than families expect and considerably lower than a constant weekly slot across two years.

The published Dubai bands, read in October 2026: Tutopiya from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the entry level; Unitors IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150; Bestimate's 2026 rate table at AED 150-300 for qualified online subject tutors, AED 180-350 for in-home one-to-one, and AED 200-450 or above for IB and IGCSE specialists, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500 once travel is included; TutorChase at AED 270; BartyED at AED 650 at the premium end. Monthly estimates from Bestimate for one weekly hour run roughly AED 240-600, AED 600-1,200 and AED 1,000-2,000 or above across the tiers.

Applied to a term of twelve weeks, the arithmetic is straightforward and the table below sets it out. The point of showing it this way is that it exposes the real decision, which is not whether to pay AED 250 or AED 300 an hour but which terms to buy. A family with a fixed budget almost always gets a better result spending it across term one, the internal assessment blocks and term six than spending all of it in term six.

IB Gram publishes no fixed hourly rate on this page because subject, level and urgency move it, and a quote follows the free diagnostic lesson rather than preceding it. One context figure: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. Fees are flat; tutoring is the variable line.

sections.heading: A Motor City evening, and why the format decides the schedule
paragraphs: Motor City has GEMS Metropole School inside it, which means primary and lower secondary families here have short school runs and real flexibility. Diploma families do not, because GEMS Metropole runs a British curriculum through IGCSE and Diploma students commute out across the Dubailand corridor. The drive back from Arabian Ranches, The Sustainable City or Dubai Investments Park in term-time afternoon traffic puts most students home between 16:30 and 17:30.

That makes about 18:00 the realistic earliest session start for a Diploma student in this postcode, and it makes two sessions a week across a whole term a scheduling question rather than a budget one. Online, two 45-minute sessions a week at 18:00 and 20:00 on different evenings is routine, and either can move later when a fixture or a music lesson already owns the slot.

A visiting tutor cannot offer that shape here. Forty to sixty minutes of travel each way means a two-hour minimum booking to justify the journey and a latest workable start of roughly 18:30, so the sixteen or twenty-four sessions a final-term plan needs become eight or twelve long ones at times that are hard on a student who has already done a school day and a commute. The published premium for that is AED 30-150 an hour over the equivalent online band.

Home visits remain a legitimate choice and for some students the right one: a younger child who cannot self-manage a screen, or a student whose written method needs correcting as it is produced. IB Gram does not offer them anywhere in the UAE — home visits are an India-only service for us — so the comparison below is offered to inform the decision rather than to argue a family out of something.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and why timing is the honest issue
paragraphs: Most academic-honesty failures in the Diploma are timing failures first. A student who starts an Extended Essay eight weeks before submission, or a science investigation three weeks before the deadline, is under a pressure that makes buying work look like a solution. At least one provider ranking for UAE IB searches sells completed Internal Assessments, and the people who buy them are rarely students who planned well and then decided to cheat. They are students who ran out of time.

Which makes the calendar a safeguarding issue as much as a performance one. A family that gets the internal deadlines on one page in DP1 term one, and schedules four to six sessions before each of them, is also removing the circumstances in which that temptation appears. That is a better argument for early planning than any marks-based one.

The boundary itself is clear and worth stating in full. A tutor may interrogate a research question until it is answerable, check that a method will generate data capable of supporting the planned analysis, explain what each criterion credits using the published descriptors, teach citation and referencing, and read a draft the student wrote and name where it fails a criterion. A tutor may not write, rewrite, restructure by rewriting, or edit prose into a standard the student cannot produce, and may not supply a completed assessment of any kind.

The same applies to examination material. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright. We reference and link them at their official sources and work from them on screen in session; we do not reproduce or distribute them, and a tutor offering a folder of scanned mark schemes is creating a copyright problem and, for unreleased material, something more serious.

sections.heading: Equivalency, university timing and the regulator footnotes
paragraphs: There is a second calendar running alongside the academic one, and it is the documentary one. Families planning on a UAE university need Ministry of Education equivalency, and the requirements have subject-count rules that are easier to satisfy if read in DP1 than discovered in DP2. Equivalency is the Ministry's recognition of a foreign secondary certificate and is required for admission to UAE institutions and some employment routes.

The published British-track rules are specific: one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, plus five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among those five. For the American track, English proficiency requires IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. For the IB, no points threshold appears on this page: the sourced material states none and no figure has been read on moe.gov.ae, so publishing one would be guesswork with a number attached.

Two boundaries. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency; it is a Ministry process and you deal with the Ministry or the emirate's attestation authority directly. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression — any implication otherwise is manufactured urgency.

The regulator footnotes that belong on every page here. Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, with Abu Dhabi and Al Ain under ADEK, Sharjah under SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. Private tutoring is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students; individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published so no amount appears here. IB Gram holds no regulator or awarding-body approval, no KHDA Educational Services Permit and no UAE office.

sections.heading: Starting at whichever term you are actually in
paragraphs: The first message should say which term the student is in, which subjects and levels, and what the school's internal calendar looks like. Send a marked piece of work if there is one. A specialist runs a free diagnostic lesson and sends a written note within a working day setting out what is still movable from where you are, with a session estimate against each item. Nothing is charged before you read it.

What that note says depends entirely on the term. At DP1 term one it will usually be about habits and subject fit, and it will be short, because that is the cheapest point on the curve and the honest answer is often one weekly slot in one subject. At DP2 term six it will be explicit about what has closed and what has not, and it will not pretend that an already-submitted internal assessment can be improved. A provider that gives the same answer at both points is not reading the calendar.

Availability is good for mainstream Diploma subjects at UAE evening slots — Mathematics AA and AI, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics, English A, Business Management, History — with a match normally inside one to three working days. Narrow courses are thinner: a minority Group 2 language at Higher Level, a specific Computer Science option, a Career-related Programme reflective project. Where no UAE-resident specialist is free, the match comes from our India-based IB faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and we say so before the booking.

One scheduling note specific to this community. Diploma slots from Motor City start around 18:00 because of the commute, and the 18:00 and 19:00 slots fill first across the whole corridor. A family booking in DP1 term one gets a choice of times; a family booking in term six takes what is left, which in a compressed window is a real cost rather than an inconvenience.
