process.title: Get the internal calendar on one page
process.description: Ask the Diploma coordinator in writing for every internal deadline across all six subjects plus the core: method approvals, draft dates, submissions, mocks. Almost no family does this and it is the cheapest useful thing available, because it turns two years of vague pressure into a list of dates.

process.title: Say which term you are in
process.description: The right purchase at DP1 term one is a weekly foundation slot. At DP1 term two it is Extended Essay question work. At DP2 term six it is technique and timed papers. Naming the term is what stops a family buying the final-term product in the first term, or the reverse.

process.title: Free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A full session at no charge spent on the student's own work. The output is a written note on what is still movable from where you are, with a session estimate against each item, which at term six includes an honest list of what has already closed.

process.title: Place blocks before deadlines, not after
process.description: Each internal assessment, the Extended Essay and the TOK essay gets four to six sessions scheduled before its school deadline. Placed after, the work is review with nothing to change. Placed before, the research question, the method and the criteria can all still be influenced.

process.title: Reschedule around the UAE year deliberately
process.description: Front-load timed paper practice if Ramadan falls in the term before the session, move sessions to post-Iftar slots between 20:30 and 22:00, and use the long summer break rather than treating it as time off. Every session is recorded, so a rescheduled week loses nothing.

whyPoints.title: The calendar treated as the product
whyPoints.description: We ask which of the six terms you are in before discussing subjects, because the right purchase differs completely between term one and term six and buying the wrong one is the most common waste in Diploma tutoring.

whyPoints.title: Internal deadlines separated from the IB's
whyPoints.description: Nearly every date a Diploma student meets is set by their school, well before the IB's windows. We tell you to get that calendar in writing in DP1 term one, because it is the information that makes planning possible at all.

whyPoints.title: Ramadan planned for, not around
whyPoints.description: Shortened school days and post-Iftar evenings change what work fits, and the period often falls just before the session. Short recall and review sessions between 20:30 and 22:00 work well; full timed papers belong either side of it, which means front-loading them.

whyPoints.title: Priced by term so the real decision is visible
whyPoints.description: The decision is not AED 250 against AED 300 an hour; it is which terms to buy. A fixed budget spread across term one, the internal assessment blocks and the final term beats the same money spent entirely in the final term.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what has closed
whyPoints.description: At term six a submitted internal assessment cannot be improved and an approved Extended Essay question cannot be rewritten. The written note says so rather than selling hours against work that is already finished.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for a Motor City commute
whyPoints.description: Diploma students here travel out of the community, so sessions start around 18:00 with slots to 21:00 and 45-minute lengths available. Two sessions a week across a full term is routine online and difficult with a visiting tutor's two-hour minimum.

faqs.question: Does an IB home tutor actually visit houses in Motor City?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors and agencies in Dubai do, priced at AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 rate table and up to about AED 500 for independent home tutors with travel included. IB Gram does not, anywhere in the UAE — home visits are an India-only service for us. For a Motor City Diploma family the online format also fits the calendar better: sessions from 18:00 once the commute home is done, 45-minute lengths, slots to 21:00, post-Iftar timing in Ramadan, and a recording of every session for later revision.

faqs.question: When in the two Diploma years should we start tutoring?
faqs.answer: DP1 term one is the cheapest and most effective point, and almost nobody uses it. Habits that decide a grade — non-calculator fluency, command-term discipline, writing method — install in weeks at that stage and take months later. Term one is also when subject and level mismatches can still be corrected, which no amount of later tutoring can do. Families who start in DP2 term six are buying the one product that cannot touch anything internally assessed, because all of it has already been submitted by then.

faqs.question: Which Diploma deadlines does our school set rather than the IB?
faqs.answer: Nearly all the ones your child actually meets. The school sets Extended Essay subject and supervisor allocation, research question approval, reflection sessions, drafts and final submission; internal assessment method approval and submission for every subject; the TOK exhibition and essay dates; mock windows; and the cut-off for Higher Level content being taught. The IB sets the external session and the submission windows the school works back from. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the internal calendar in writing during the first fortnight of DP1 and put it on one page.

faqs.question: How should a Dubai revision plan handle Ramadan?
faqs.answer: By front-loading and changing the kind of work rather than trying to carry on unchanged. School hours shorten, afternoon energy drops, and the productive window moves to after Iftar, which matters because the period often falls in the term before summer examinations. Short post-Iftar sessions between 20:30 and 22:00 suit recall testing, review and marking a paper sat earlier in the day. Full-length timed papers and new content belong either side of the period, which means scheduling them earlier than a plan written in September would have assumed.

faqs.question: Can anything about an Internal Assessment be changed in the final term?
faqs.answer: Not once it is submitted, and that is the single most important thing for a family arriving late to understand. The internally assessed component is worth 20-25% of every Diploma subject grade, it is marked in school and moderated by the IB, and it closes on the school's submission date. After that the only movable things are examination technique, timing, question selection and residual content. Which is why the written note after a diagnostic lesson at term six lists what has closed as well as what has not, rather than selling hours against finished work.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for Extended Essay help if the question is already approved?
faqs.answer: Less than before it was approved, which is exactly the point. A question that cannot be answered within the 4,000-word limit produces an essay that cannot score well however it is written, and the moment to fix that is before the school signs it off in DP1. After approval, useful support is still available: reflection sessions, structure, argument, referencing and criterion-referenced feedback on the student's own drafts. But the single highest-value intervention has passed, which is why the Extended Essay block belongs in DP1 term two rather than DP2.

faqs.question: Why does this page give no IB exam dates for the May session?
faqs.answer: Because none could be verified at source. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a family reorganises travel and a whole revision plan around an examination date. UAE candidates sit the May session; for the window, the results date and the candidate release time, ask your school's Diploma coordinator or read ibo.org directly. The dates that constrain a plan first are internal in any case, and your school holds all of those.

faqs.question: How much does a full two years of Diploma support cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends far more on which terms you buy than on the hourly rate. At published bands, a twelve-week weekly slot is roughly AED 1,800-3,600 at the AED 150-300 qualified band or AED 2,400-5,400 at the AED 200-450 specialist band, and a four-session block is AED 600-1,800. A sensible pattern is term one weekly, a block before each internal deadline, and the final term weekly — considerably less than a constant slot across six terms. Those are other providers' published figures read in October 2026; we quote after the free diagnostic lesson.

faqs.question: What time can a Diploma session realistically start from Motor City?
faqs.answer: About 18:00 for most families. GEMS Metropole School inside the community runs a British curriculum through IGCSE, so Diploma students commute out across the Dubailand corridor and are generally home between 16:30 and 17:30. Online sessions run to 21:00 on Gulf Standard Time, so a second weekly session can sit at 20:00 after a fixture without displacing it, and either can be 45 minutes rather than an hour. A visiting tutor's two-hour minimum and roughly 18:30 latest start make that pattern hard to arrange here.

faqs.question: Can we use the long summer break rather than term time?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most underused window in the whole Diploma. With no school commitments competing for the evening, the summer is the right place for non-calculator fluency work, for reading around an Extended Essay topic before the question is fixed, and for the procedural groundwork a student arriving from MYP needs before DP1 begins. Ten sessions in July and August routinely achieve more than twenty in October, because the student is not simultaneously trying to keep up with new content and a full school timetable.

faqs.question: Which schools do Motor City Diploma students usually attend?
faqs.answer: Not GEMS Metropole School, which is inside the community but runs a British curriculum through IGCSE. Diploma students from Motor City generally travel to JESS Arabian Ranches, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City, Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park, North London Collegiate School Dubai or GEMS Wellington Academy Al Khail. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three on the IB curriculum, creating 16,846 places. We name schools as market context and hold no relationship with any of them.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor start if we are already in the final term?
faqs.answer: One to three working days for a mainstream Diploma subject, though the binding constraint at that notice is usually the slot rather than the specialist. The 18:00 and 19:00 slots across this corridor fill first, so a family booking in the final term takes what is available, which in a compressed window is a genuine cost. Narrow courses may have no free UAE-resident specialist at all, in which case the tutor comes from our India-based IB faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and we tell you before you book.

faqs.question: Do we need to worry about Ministry equivalency during DP1?
faqs.answer: Read it in DP1 rather than acting on it then. Equivalency is the Ministry of Education's recognition of a foreign secondary certificate, required for UAE university admission and some employment routes, and the British-track rules are specific: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3 with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. No IB points figure appears here because none has been read on moe.gov.ae. Tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency.

faqs.question: What stops a student buying coursework when they run out of time?
faqs.answer: Mostly having not run out of time, which is a planning outcome rather than a character one. At least one provider ranking for UAE IB searches sells completed Internal Assessments, and submitting purchased work is academic misconduct with the consequence falling on the student. The families who avoid that situation are generally the ones who got the internal calendar in writing in DP1 and placed four to six sessions before each deadline. That is a stronger argument for early planning than any point about marks.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-motor-city.closingBody: The question that decides a Diploma result is which of the six terms got attention, not how many hours were bought in the last one. Get the internal calendar from your Diploma coordinator in the first fortnight of DP1 and put every deadline on one page. Place four to six sessions before each internal assessment, the Extended Essay question and the TOK essay. Front-load timed papers if Ramadan falls in the final term, and use the long summer break rather than treating it as time off. Tell us which term you are in, send a marked script, and take the free diagnostic lesson.

intro.heading: Mudon, Arabian Ranches 3, and the same answer twice
paragraphs: Mudon sits on the inland side of Al Qudra Road, a Dubai Properties community of villas and townhouses split into Al Salam, Rahat, Arabella, Naseem and Mudon Views. It has a central park, a community centre and no secondary school inside its own gates. That single fact shapes every tutoring decision a Mudon family makes, because the school run already goes outward, and so does the search for help.

Run the same exercise one community over. Arabian Ranches 3 shares the same stretch of Al Qudra Road and the same absence of an on-site Diploma school. Remraam, a few minutes further towards Emirates Road, is apartments rather than villas and a different price bracket entirely. Town Square sits beyond both. Ask each of those four sets of parents where they can find an IB specialist within a twenty-minute drive and the honest answer is the same: not reliably, and not in the subject you need.

This is why the comparison matters more than the geography. A tutor who lives in Motor City can be at a Mudon villa in fifteen minutes on a quiet evening and forty on a bad one. A tutor who has taught Chemistry HL for six Diploma cohorts might live in Mirdif, Sharjah, or outside the country altogether. Choosing by drive time means choosing from whoever happens to be nearby, and in a community this new that pool is thin in exactly the subjects where families need depth: Maths Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Physics HL, Chemistry HL, Economics HL.

IB Gram takes the other side of that trade. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, so a session can start at 4.30pm or 8.15pm without anyone sitting in traffic on the Al Qudra interchange. The tutor is picked for the subject and the level. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only, and no sentence on this page should be read as an offer to arrive at a Mudon door.

The second variable is money, and it behaves differently from the way parents expect. A visiting tutor's hourly quote has the drive built into it, which is why the in-home band in Dubai sits above the online one rather than beside it. From a Mudon address, off the main tutor corridors through Motor City and Dubai Sports City, that loading is larger than it would be for a family in Al Barsha. Nobody advertises it as a travel charge; it simply arrives inside the rate. Pricing the arrangement by the month rather than by the hour makes the difference visible, and the table further down this page does exactly that.

What follows is the comparison written out properly: what the Dubai market charges per hour and per month with sources attached, what the drive actually costs a family in Mudon against the neighbouring communities, what KHDA inspection bands mean for the schools your children attend, where IB marks are genuinely lost by subject group, and what a tutor is permitted to do with an Internal Assessment under IB academic-honesty rules. Every figure carries its origin, because an unsourced number is not information.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-mudon.programmesIntro: Mudon children are spread across all three IB programmes, usually at different schools, because the communities around Dubailand mix British primaries with IB continuum schools. Here is what each programme asks of a student and what that means for families living on this side of Al Qudra Road.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment worth 20 to 30 per cent of the final grade, which means a quarter of the Diploma is decided by coursework deadlines rather than by the exam fortnight. Students sit the May session at UAE schools.
programmes.countryNote: Mudon Diploma students mostly travel to Jumeirah English Speaking School in Arabian Ranches, GEMS International School Al Khail or Fairgreen International in The Sustainable City. None of those is a short walk, so a 4pm session at home is realistically a 5pm session once the car is parked, and that is the hour online lessons give back.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, A to D, marked out of eight and reported as a 1 to 7 grade through published grade boundaries. There are no public exams until the optional eRs. The difficulty for parents is that a criterion mark is not a percentage, so a 5 in Criterion C means something quite specific about inquiry skills rather than about effort.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Mudon and Arabian Ranches 3 often meet the MYP at Year 7 after a British-curriculum primary, and the first reporting cycle is where confusion starts. Tutoring here is usually about decoding the criteria and the command terms, not about content gaps, and that work transfers cleanly to a screen.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subjects, ending in the Year 6 Exhibition. Assessment is formative and portfolio-based, so there is no mark to improve in the way an older sibling has. Support at this stage is about reading fluency, number sense and the written communication the Exhibition will later demand.
programmes.countryNote: Mudon primary children often attend British-curriculum schools nearby and meet the IB only when they move up, which is why the parents asking about PYP in this community are usually planning a transfer rather than reacting to a report. Thirty-minute online sessions suit this age better than an hour with a visitor.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more DP courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Offered by a small number of UAE schools. Students take the same DP subject assessments as Diploma candidates, so the subject tutoring need is identical even though the overall qualification is not.
programmes.countryNote: Very few schools serving the Dubailand communities run the CP, so a Mudon family exploring it is usually comparing it against a two-A-Level route. The practical question is which DP courses are being taken, since those are the ones that carry external papers and therefore the ones tutoring targets.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-mudon.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Dubailand families request most for Diploma and Middle Years students. Each note says what the assessment actually rewards, because that is where tutoring hours earn their keep.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency. HL adds Maclaurin series, vectors in three dimensions and the harder differential equations. Marks go missing in Paper 1 because it is non-calculator and arithmetic slips compound; in Paper 2 because a graphing calculator is used to confirm rather than to explore.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and interpretation of data. The common failure is answering a modelling question mathematically and never writing the sentence that interprets the result in context, which is where the marks sit. HL adds matrices, graph theory and complex numbers.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, thermal physics, waves, fields and nuclear. Paper 2 extended response punishes students who calculate without stating assumptions. The HL extension in fields and induction is where grades split, and the practical scheme of work is where the Internal Assessment variable control is decided.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. Organic chemistry is the topic Dubailand parents ask about most. The fix is almost never more notes; it is mechanism drawing under timed conditions and curly-arrow discipline on every reaction type.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cell biology through to ecology, with data-based questions that reward careful reading of axes and units. Students lose marks writing descriptive answers where the command term asked them to explain, and in HL on the biochemistry detail that Standard Level does not reach.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and the three commentaries that make up the Internal Assessment. Diagram accuracy carries real marks: an unlabelled axis or a shifted curve without an explanation costs more than a weak evaluation paragraph.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided textual analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, the Individual Oral, and the HL Essay. The Individual Oral is where preparation pays most, because it is assessed on a global issue the student chooses and must defend with two extracts.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisational structure, marketing, finance and operations, with a research project at HL and a commentary at SL. Tools such as Ansoff and the BCG matrix earn marks only when applied to the named firm, not described in the abstract.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Reading comprehension, writing in registered text types and the oral assessments. Separate from the Arabic that KHDA requires all Dubai private schools to teach, which runs alongside the IB programme rather than inside it.

sections.heading: What a Mudon parent is actually comparing
paragraphs: The search phrase is an IB home tutor in Mudon, but the decision underneath it has two variables, not one. The first is convenience: can somebody be in the room at a time that works around the drive back from Arabian Ranches or Al Barsha South. The second is competence: does that somebody know what a Chemistry HL Paper 2 extended response is marked against. In a community with no secondary school inside its own boundary, those two variables pull in opposite directions.

Mudon's housing stock is villas and townhouses across Al Salam, Rahat, Arabella, Naseem and Mudon Views. The population skews towards families with school-age children, which is exactly the demand profile tutors chase. What it lacks is the density that makes a specialist viable locally. A tutor who teaches only Physics HL needs a catchment of several thousand Diploma students to fill a week; Mudon and Arabian Ranches 3 together do not supply that, so the people advertising locally are generalists covering four subjects at two levels.

Hold that against the alternative. A live video lesson removes the catchment problem entirely. The pool stops being people within a twenty-minute drive of Al Qudra Road and becomes people who teach that subject at that level, wherever they sit. For Maths Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level, which plenty of tutors can handle, the difference is modest. For Physics HL, Chemistry HL or Economics HL, it is the whole difference between a tutor who explains and a tutor who keeps pace.

The rest of this page sets out the comparison with numbers attached: the market rates, the drive-time arithmetic community by community, and what the two formats actually include once travel is priced in.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs across the Dubailand belt, with sources
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because that is the number a household budget actually meets. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those bands hold whether the family lives in Mudon or in Jumeirah; what changes is the travel loading.

Work back to the hour and the picture sharpens. University-student and budget online tutors advertise from around AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik publishing rates from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Named IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650.

The in-home band is the one that matters to this comparison. Visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate's range at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. Monthly packages seen in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. paragraphs: Put four Dubailand communities side by side and the pattern is immediate. Each has a slightly different housing type, a slightly different school run and a slightly different tutor supply, and in every case the Diploma specialist is somewhere else. Arabian Ranches 2 is the only one in the group with an IB Diploma school inside or immediately beside it, and places there are finite.

The operational number is the realistic start time for an evening session. A Mudon student finishing at Jumeirah English Speaking School in Arabian Ranches is home by about 3.45pm on a good day. A student at GEMS International School Al Khail or Nord Anglia in Al Barsha South is home closer to 4.30pm, and if there is an activity after school, closer to 5.30pm. A visiting tutor leaving Motor City at 5pm to reach Arabella is not in the room until 5.25pm at best, and the lesson then runs into dinner.

Online lessons collapse that. The session starts when the student sits down, which can be 4.15pm, 6pm or 8.30pm, and the same slot can move by thirty minutes during Ramadan without renegotiating a travel fee. For a family running two children on different timetables across two schools, this is the difference between two tutoring arrangements and one workable evening.

Group tuition behaves differently again. Online one-to-one is priced in the qualified-tutor band, carries no travel loading, and is the only format where subject match is independent of address. sections.heading: Where IB marks are genuinely lost, group by group
paragraphs: Diagnosis matters more than hours. A student at a 4 in Chemistry HL who should be at a 6 is usually not missing content; they are losing marks in a pattern, and the pattern is diagnosable from two marked papers. In the sciences, the recurring loss is in extended response: a calculation is produced correctly and the assumptions behind it are never stated, so the method marks arrive and the explanation marks do not.

In Mathematics, the split is between the two papers. Paper 1 is taken without a calculator, so an error in line two of an algebraic manipulation travels all the way to a wrong final answer, and follow-through marks only partially rescue it. Paper 2 rewards students who use the graphing calculator to confirm an answer they already reasoned towards, and punishes those who use it to search. The Internal Assessment, the mathematical exploration, loses marks most often on personal engagement and on reflection rather than on the mathematics itself.

In the humanities and language subjects, the losses are structural. An Economics commentary that describes a diagram instead of applying it to the named market caps itself. An English Paper 2 comparative essay that treats the two texts in sequence rather than in conversation loses on the criterion that asks for comparison. A Theory of Knowledge essay that answers the prescribed title generally, without areas of knowledge as the organising frame, is marked down regardless of how well it is written.

None of that requires a tutor in the room. It requires a tutor who can read a marked script, name the pattern and set the next fortnight's work against it, and that work happens just as well on a shared screen.

sections.heading: KHDA, inspection bands and what a Dubai school report tells you
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which the UAE government describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. Those five bodies are the complete regulator map, and most tutoring pages in this market name none of them.

The Dubai sector is large and it is growing. In 2024-25 it held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, American at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package. For the following intake, seven new private schools were announced, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places.

What the inspection report gives a Mudon parent is a reading of departments, not just a headline band. A school rated Good overall can hold an Outstanding mathematics department and an Acceptable science one, and that distinction is exactly what tells you where outside support is worth buying. Read the subject attainment and progress tables rather than the cover grade, and compare them against your own child's reports.

A regulator naming a school is not a regulator endorsing a tutor. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, no ADEK registration and no board affiliation, and says so plainly because several competitors in this market imply otherwise.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an Internal Assessment, and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay sit alongside them. Together they decide a large share of the final points total, and all of them must be the student's own work, authenticated by the subject teacher. An IB malpractice finding is not a mark penalty; it can cost the Diploma.

The boundary is clear once stated. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain what each criterion rewards, question a research question until it is answerable, critique a method, point out that a paragraph asserts rather than evidences, and mark a student's own draft against the published descriptors. A tutor may not draft, rewrite, edit to completion, supply text, or hand over a worked exploration for adaptation. One provider in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments for sale; that is the thing to walk away from.

In practice this makes coursework sessions look different from content sessions. The student arrives with their own draft and leaves with a list of their own decisions to make. Session notes record what was discussed rather than what was written, which is also what a school asks for if it queries authorship. Where a student needs to show process, the tutor's role is to make them keep a research log, not to produce one for them.

Nor may a tutor supply board material. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables stay with their publishers; sessions reference the official pages and link out to them rather than distributing copies.

sections.heading: Permits, equivalency and the paperwork behind a Mudon tutoring plan
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service listing is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

Two further constraints are worth knowing before you hire anyone locally. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar, so the arrangement some parents ask for first is the one to avoid. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different matter again: that needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which IB Gram does not hold and does not claim.

Looking further ahead, UAE university applications run through Ministry of Education equivalency. On the British track, a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One page currently ranking in this market states that UAE candidates need six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five. For the IB, no points threshold should be taken from a tutoring page, including this one, without being read on the Ministry's own site.
IB Gram does not perform equivalency or attestation and does not guarantee any outcome from it. The process belongs to the Ministry and the emirate authority, and the correct route is theirs.

sections.heading: The exam calendar, counted backwards from a Mudon desk
paragraphs: Tutoring plans fail on the calendar more often than on the teaching. Diploma students at UAE schools sit the May session, and the internal deadlines that decide a quarter of their points fall six to nine months earlier. Cambridge runs its IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series; the February and March series is offered in India only, so a UAE candidate who reads an Indian timetable is reading the wrong document. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November.

The checkable dates are the backward-looking ones. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which is the lag to plan around if a resit is in view. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school which zone it sits in rather than assuming.

Working backwards from a session gives a usable plan. Twelve months out, subject choices and Higher Level combinations are fixed. Nine months out, Internal Assessment topics are approved. Six months out, first drafts exist and mocks are sat. Three months out, the work is timed past papers rather than content. Six weeks out, it is error patterns from marked scripts. Ramadan falls inside that window in the current cycle, which is why evening sessions after Iftar are worth booking early rather than negotiating late.
IB session and results dates are not restated here. The IB's own site is the only place to confirm them, and a tutoring page quoting them without that check is a page that will eventually be wrong.

faqs.question: Which schools do Mudon students usually attend for the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Most travel outward. Jumeirah English Speaking School in Arabian Ranches runs the Diploma and anchors the school run for much of this belt. Further along Al Khail Road, GEMS International School Al Khail and Nord Anglia International School Dubai offer IB routes, and Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City runs the continuum. faqs.question: Does my child need a KHDA permit or anything similar to receive private tuition?
faqs.answer: No. The permit requirement falls on the person teaching, not on the family. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. faqs.question: Can a tutor help write my daughter's Economics Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone offering to is putting the Diploma at risk. The three Economics commentaries must be the student's own work, authenticated by the subject teacher. What a tutor can legitimately do is explain what each criterion rewards, question the choice of article and the economics being applied, check that diagrams are labelled and shifted correctly, point out where a paragraph asserts rather than evidences, and mark a draft the student has written against the published descriptors. The writing, the selection and the evaluation stay with your daughter. One provider in this market sells completed assessments; that is the service to refuse.

faqs.question: Is online tuition genuinely as effective for Higher Level sciences as sitting in the room?
faqs.answer: For the work that decides the grade, yes, and in one respect better. Extended-response technique, mechanism drawing, data analysis and marked-script repair all happen on a shared screen with annotation, and the student keeps the annotated copy. What online delivery cannot replace is the school laboratory, and it does not try to; practical work belongs to the school. Where it earns its place is the Internal Assessment around that practical: variable control, uncertainty treatment, graph choice and the evaluation paragraph. The trade you are making is a physical presence for a tutor who has actually taught the level.

faqs.question: Which exam series should a Mudon family be planning around?
faqs.answer: Diploma students at UAE schools sit the May session. For Cambridge, UAE candidates sit the June and November series; the February and March series is offered in India only, so an Indian timetable is the wrong document for a Dubai centre. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. As dated examples, Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Confirm IB dates on the IB's own site through your school's coordinator.

faqs.question: My son is at a 4 in Chemistry HL. What would the first month look like?
faqs.answer: It starts with two marked papers rather than a syllabus. A 4 at Higher Level is usually a pattern, not a content hole: calculations produced without stated assumptions, organic mechanisms drawn loosely, equilibrium questions answered qualitatively where the mark scheme wanted a quantitative line. The first session names the pattern. The next three attack it with timed questions from his own board, marked against the scheme, with the annotated scripts going back to him. Progress shows first in marks on individual questions, before it shows in a predicted grade, and the session notes track which questions moved.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Maths and Physics for the same Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking for. Maths Analysis and Approaches and Physics overlap in calculus, vectors and graph interpretation, so a tutor who holds both can use one to reinforce the other, particularly in mechanics and in fields. At Higher Level in both subjects simultaneously, the combination is less common and the honest answer may be two tutors. We would rather tell you that than stretch one person across a level they teach less confidently. Either way, the scheduling works the same way, because no travel has to be arranged between the two slots.

faqs.answer: Sessions move rather than stop. During Ramadan many Dubailand families prefer slots after Iftar, and because nobody is travelling, a time change costs nothing and can be arranged week by week. School holidays work the other way: they are the only blocks where a student can sit two or three sessions in a week without a timetable fighting back, which makes them the natural window for coursework catch-up or for the content repair a term could not absorb. Tell us which weeks you are travelling and the plan is built around them.

faqs.answer: Read past the cover grade. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and a school rated Good overall can hold an Outstanding mathematics department alongside an Acceptable science one. The subject-level attainment and progress tables are the useful part, because they tell you where outside support is likely to be worth buying. intro.heading: The question behind the search, answered plainly
paragraphs: When a parent in Muhaisnah types "IB home tutor near me" into Google, the question underneath is not really about travel. It is about competence. You want to know whether anybody within reach of Muhaisnah 1, 2, 3 or 4 actually understands how an IB Diploma grade is built, what a Mathematics exploration is marked against, or why a Chemistry student with sound notes can still land a 4. That is a fair question, and the honest answer in this part of Dubai is: fewer people than you would hope.

Muhaisnah sits in the older, denser half of Dubai, with Al Qusais on one side, Mirdif on the other and Al Nahda just over the Sharjah boundary. It is a neighbourhood of mid-rise apartment blocks and villa compounds, mostly families from India, Pakistan, the Philippines, Egypt, Jordan and Lebanon, and the schools closest to it lean heavily CBSE and British. IB Diploma provision clusters further out, towards Dubai Festival City, Nad Al Sheba and Mirdif. A family on an IB programme here is often commuting against the grain already.

That geography has a direct consequence for tutoring. The pool of private tutors who advertise locally is large, but it is dominated by CBSE and IGCSE generalists, because that is what the local demand looks like. An IB Physics HL specialist, an Economics HL examiner-trained teacher, a Visual Arts comparative study supervisor — these are not people who happen to live ten minutes from Muhaisnah Centre. They are scattered across the emirate and across the region, and the only reliable way to reach one is over video.

So this page does two things. It answers the home-tutoring question properly: what in-home IB tuition costs around eastern Dubai, what the travel premium actually buys, how the permit rules work, and how families here usually decide. Then it is straight with you about what IB Gram sells. We do not send tutors to addresses in Dubai. Home visiting is a service we run only in India. In the UAE every lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled to your child's week, and the reason we built it that way is precisely the supply problem described above.

The rest of the page is built to be useful even if you never contact us. There is a coverage table showing which IB subjects have local tutor availability in eastern Dubai and which do not. There is the market rate band in AED, attributed to its sources. There is the MoHRE permit position, which most tutoring sites in this market skip entirely. There is a plain statement of what a tutor may and may not do with an Internal Assessment under IB academic-honesty rules. And there is a short list of questions you can ask any tutor, local or online, in the first fifteen minutes, that will tell you whether they know the syllabus or are guessing.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-muhaisnah.programmesIntro: Muhaisnah families arrive on this page from three different places in the IB continuum, and the tutoring job is different in each. Here is what each programme assesses and what that means for a student living in eastern Dubai.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth of the grade, marked by the teacher against published criteria and moderated by the IB. The written papers carry the rest. A Diploma score out of 45 combines six subject grades out of 7 with up to three points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix.
programmes.countryNote: For a Muhaisnah student the DP is usually sat at a school some distance away, which makes the week tight before tutoring is even considered. The commonest request we see from this cluster is Higher Level support in one or two subjects rather than across the board, because the family has already worked out which two grades are blocking the total they need.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. There is no terminal exam unless the school opts into eAssessment. The Personal Project in the final year is assessed against its own criteria and supervised in school. Progress is judged on the most recent and most consistent evidence, not an average of everything.
programmes.countryNote: Several Mirdif and Festival City schools near Muhaisnah run the MYP, and parents moving in from a CBSE or British system find the absence of marks out of 100 disorienting. Tutoring here is largely about teaching the student to read a criterion descriptor and write to it, which is a skill no amount of extra content revision supplies.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subjects, with the Exhibition in the final year. Assessment is continuous and descriptive. Literacy and numeracy still sit underneath it, and a child can pass through the PYP with warm reports and a genuine gap in number fluency or written structure that only surfaces when the MYP starts awarding criterion marks.
programmes.countryNote: PYP requests from the Muhaisnah and Al Qusais area are almost always about reading fluency or number confidence rather than the programme itself. The useful intervention is short, frequent and diagnostic: twenty-five minute sessions twice a week beat a single ninety-minute block for a nine-year-old at the end of a long school day.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining at least two DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Fewer UAE schools offer it than offer the Diploma, and university recognition varies by destination, so the entry requirements of the target institution matter more here than on the DP route.
programmes.countryNote: CP enquiries from eastern Dubai are rare but they do come, usually from students who want two DP subjects taken seriously alongside a vocational strand. Tutoring on this route concentrates on those DP courses and on the reflective project's structure, with the career-related study handled by the school's own provider.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-muhaisnah.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects Muhaisnah enquiries most often name. Each line says what the course is actually assessed on, because that is where the tutoring hours go.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency under time pressure, calculus, and proof at Higher Level. Marks are lost on method presentation rather than final answers: unlabelled working, a derivative taken without stating the rule, a sketch without intercepts. The exploration adds a separate, criterion-marked piece of personal mathematics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-heavy problem solving. The common failure is calculator dependence without interpretation: a correct regression line and no sentence saying what it means in context. HL adds matrices, graph theory and more demanding modelling.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Conceptual definitions, graph interpretation and uncertainty handling decide grades more than algebra does. Students lose marks writing a correct equation while describing the physics wrongly, and on data questions that ask for a gradient's meaning rather than its value.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Bonding, energetics and organic mechanisms carry the load. The reliable pattern is a student who can recall structures but cannot explain a trend, and an investigation that collects data without a measurable, controllable variable chosen early enough.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term discipline matters here more than in any other science: outline, explain, distinguish and evaluate each want a different answer shape. Data-based questions on unfamiliar studies reward students who have practised reading a method, not memorising one.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy with full axis labels, then evaluation that weighs rather than lists. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on real news articles, and most lost marks come from an article that cannot support the required concept, chosen before the theory was understood.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application to an unseen case, and for HL a research project on a real organisation. Students lose marks applying a framework generically instead of to the stimulus, and on quantitative questions that look optional until the paper arrives.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen textual analysis, the individual oral built on a global issue, and for HL a comparative essay. The strongest gains come from teaching a student to write about how a text works rather than what it says, with quotations integrated into the sentence.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper questions on systems, networks and abstract data structures, plus a solution developed against a real client's requirements. The usual gap is a working program with thin documentation, because the write-up is what carries the criterion marks.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Named studies used precisely, with method and limitation, and essays structured to a command term. The experimental study replication is where a weak hypothesis or an untestable design costs marks that no amount of later writing recovers.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case-study recall with figures attached, map and graph skills, and for HL the global interactions core. Fieldwork write-ups lose marks on a question that was never geographically answerable and on data presentation that duplicates rather than develops.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic A
subjects.description: Two different courses, often confused. Arabic B is a language-acquisition route for non-native speakers; Arabic A is a literature or language-and-literature course for first-language students. Dubai schools must also run mandatory Arabic alongside the IB, which is a third, separate requirement.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-muhaisnah.regionsIntro: Muhaisnah is one of several eastern Dubai communities we take enquiries from, and the practical picture is similar across them: dense residential stock, long school runs, and IB provision concentrated elsewhere in the emirate.

regions.name: Muhaisnah
regions.note: Four numbered sub-communities off Al Awir Road, mixing apartment blocks, villa compounds and labour accommodation. Families here typically school in Al Qusais, Mirdif or Festival City rather than inside the neighbourhood.

regions.name: Al Qusais
regions.note: The nearest school-dense district, strong on CBSE and British provision and served by the Red Line. School end times here drive when a Muhaisnah family can realistically start an evening session.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: Villa communities east of Muhaisnah with IB continuum provision and several British schools. The Mirdif school run adds twenty to thirty minutes each way in the afternoon peak.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: On the Sharjah boundary, and the reason afternoon traffic on Al Ittihad Road behaves the way it does. Families living here but schooling in Dubai lose the most time to the commute.

regions.name: Al Mizhar
regions.note: Quieter villa district between Mirdif and Al Khawaneej, with a mix of British and American schools nearby and almost no in-neighbourhood tutoring supply.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City
regions.note: Home to two of the closest IB schools to Muhaisnah, one running the full continuum. Many of our eastern Dubai Diploma enquiries come from families schooling here.

regions.name: Al Warqa
regions.note: Large villa area south of Mirdif with substantial CBSE provision. Students transferring from CBSE into MYP or DP often arrive with strong content and unfamiliar assessment habits.

regions.name: Al Garhoud
regions.note: Older established district near the airport with long-standing schools and good road access to Festival City. Sessions after 6pm work better here than a 4.30pm start.

regions.name: International City
regions.note: Dense apartment district south-east of Muhaisnah. Families here are often price-sensitive and benefit most from the lower end of the online market rather than any in-home option.

regions.name: Nad Al Hamar
regions.note: Between Rashidiya and Mirdif, with quick access to Festival City schools. A practical catchment for the same IB schools Muhaisnah families use.

schoolClusters.city: Festival City, Garhoud and Rashidiya
schoolClusters.note: The closest cluster to Muhaisnah with genuine IB Diploma provision, reachable along Al Rebat Street and the Garhoud bridge approaches. Students we support in eastern Dubai frequently attend schools in this group.

schoolClusters.city: Al Qusais, Mirdif and Al Warqa
schoolClusters.note: The school-dense ring immediately around Muhaisnah, heavier on British and Indian curricula with IB continuum provision in Mirdif. School end times across this group set the earliest workable session slot for most families here.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-muhaisnah.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every Muhaisnah enquiry. All three run over live video; the difference is cadence and purpose, not delivery.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one subject support
modes.description: The default for a student carrying one or two subjects below where they want them. A fixed slot each week, built around the school's own assessment calendar, with work set between sessions and marked against the same criteria the school uses. Most families start with one subject and add a second only after they have seen the first move.

modes.title: Internal assessment and coursework coaching
modes.description: Structured sessions on an exploration, investigation, commentary or Extended Essay, run strictly as teaching and feedback on the student's own draft. The tutor questions the research design, points at a criterion descriptor the draft does not yet meet, and sends the student back to write. No part of the submitted work is produced by the tutor.

sections.heading: What "IB home tutor in Muhaisnah" actually returns, and why
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Muhaisnah, as the phrase is used in Dubai, means a private tutor who travels to a family's apartment or villa for one-to-one lessons in an IB subject. Market rates for that service in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour according to the published bands collected from Bestimate's 2026 tutoring-cost table and from independent home tutors advertising in the emirate. The rate includes the tutor's travel, which is why it sits above the online equivalent.

Search the phrase from Muhaisnah and you will get three kinds of result. First, directory listings that cover all of Dubai and sort by nothing useful. Second, agency pages that name every neighbourhood in the emirate in one paragraph and no school in any of them. Third, individual tutors, most of whom teach CBSE or IGCSE and list IB as a line item. What you will rarely get is a named person who teaches, say, Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and nothing else.

That is not an accident of search ranking. It reflects the actual supply. Muhaisnah's own catchment is dominated by CBSE and British schools, so the tutors who have built a local practice here teach those systems. IB Diploma enrolment across Dubai is about 7% of private-school pupils according to the emirate's 2024-25 figures, and it is concentrated in a handful of districts, none of them this one. A specialist follows demand, and the demand is not next door.

The useful conclusion is not that local tutoring is bad. It is that the constraint worth optimising is subject match, not distance. A student doing Economics HL needs somebody who has marked Paper 3 and knows why evaluation marks go missing. Whether that person is twenty minutes away or two thousand kilometres away changes nothing about the lesson, provided the lesson is live, one-to-one and on your child's clock. That is the trade this page is asking you to consider.

sections.heading: IB subject coverage in eastern Dubai: who is actually available
paragraphs: This is the table no tutoring site in this market publishes, because it exposes a limit. It sets out, for the IB subjects Muhaisnah families most often ask about, whether a UAE-based specialist is usually available, roughly how long a match takes, and what happens when nobody local covers the course. The fallback is always the same mechanism: a specialist elsewhere in our network, teaching over the same live video platform on Gulf Standard Time.

Read it as a planning document. If your child needs Mathematics or Chemistry support, the local pool is deep enough that you will have a choice of tutor and a trial lesson inside a few days. If the subject is Psychology, Computer Science, Visual Arts or a less common language, expect the specialist to be outside the UAE, and expect the match to take longer because we are looking for a particular person rather than any qualified teacher.

The second column is deliberately coarse. We are describing availability of a specialist who teaches that course at that level habitually, not of anyone willing to attempt it. Plenty of competent graduates will take an IB Psychology booking; far fewer can tell a student why their experimental study's hypothesis will cost them criterion marks before the data is collected. The distinction is the whole point of the table.

Where a subject shows limited UAE availability, nothing about the price changes. The rate is set by the tutor's specialism and experience, not by which time zone they sit in. What does change is scheduling flexibility, which usually improves, because a tutor teaching from a different time zone is often available in the early evening Gulf Standard Time slot that a UAE-based teacher with a day job cannot take.

sections.heading: What the travel premium buys, and what it costs in Muhaisnah
paragraphs: Start with the gap rather than the headline. The difference between a qualified online IB tutor and an in-home visit in Dubai is roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour at comparable experience levels. Over a two-session week across a thirty-week school year that gap is somewhere between AED 3,000 and AED 9,000. The question worth asking is what the extra buys, and from a Muhaisnah address the honest answer is: a shorter walk from the front door, and a smaller shortlist.

The underlying bands, taken from published competitor pricing and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, are set out below. Budget online provision, usually university students, starts around AED 45 and runs to AED 150. Qualified subject tutors working online sit roughly AED 150 to 300, with one Dubai agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 with travel included. IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, and a premium examiner-branded provider has published AED 650.

Those figures are the market, not our price list. IB Gram's own commercial position is set at the consultation, after the trial lesson, once the subject, level and cadence are known, because a weekly MYP Maths slot and an eight-week DP Physics exam block are not the same product. What we will say in public is that we sit in the qualified-specialist part of the market rather than the budget part, and that the trial lesson is free and carries no obligation.

One further Muhaisnah-specific point about the travel premium. A tutor driving to Muhaisnah 2 at 5pm from Jumeirah or Dubai Marina is pricing in the Al Ittihad Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road peak, and will quote accordingly or decline. The practical effect is that the in-home shortlist for this neighbourhood is drawn from tutors who already live on this side of the city, which tightens it further. The tutors who can reach you cheaply are the ones whose subject spread is widest, which is usually the opposite of what an IB student needs.

sections.heading: Online or in-home for a Muhaisnah household: the comparison that matters
paragraphs: Set the sentiment aside and compare the two formats on the things that change a grade. There are five: who you can actually hire, how much lesson time survives the logistics, what happens when a session has to move, what the student does between sessions, and what you pay. On four of those five an online lesson from a Muhaisnah apartment is either equal or ahead. The fifth, supervision of a young child who will not sit still without an adult in the room, is a real advantage for in-home work and the main reason PYP families choose it.

Lesson-time survival is the underrated one. A tutor arriving at Muhaisnah 4 at 5.15pm for a 5pm booking has lost fifteen minutes, and the family who waited is not getting them back. An online session starts when the clock says so. Over a term that difference compounds into several full lessons, which is more teaching time than most families gain from any change of tutor.

Rescheduling is the second. Dubai families move sessions constantly: a school trip, a late bus, Ramadan timings, a trip to see relatives over Eid. Moving an online slot is a message. Moving an in-home visit means re-planning somebody's drive across the city, which in practice means the session is cancelled rather than moved. Continuity is most of what tutoring delivers, and the format that survives disruption keeps more of it.

Against that, be clear about what online genuinely requires. A door that closes, a device with a working camera and a stylus or writing surface the tutor can see, and a parent willing to be in the house if the student is under twelve. Without the first of those, a lesson in a busy apartment with three siblings and a television becomes a worse lesson than an in-home one, and no platform fixes that.

sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is a checkable fact that most tutoring sites in the market never mention. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone offering private lessons without one is, in the ministry's own words, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws.

Eligibility is broader than people assume. Teachers registered in government or private schools can hold it, as can employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The application route is MoHRE's own service, listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, available through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days and no published fee.

No fine amount should be quoted to you, by us or anybody else. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source. If a tutoring site tells you the penalty is a specific number of dirhams, it is repeating something it cannot evidence.

There is a second rule worth knowing if your child is at school in Abu Dhabi rather than Dubai. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. So the apparently attractive idea of hiring your child's own subject teacher privately is, in several emirates, exactly the arrangement the rules are written to prevent. Ask any tutor whether they hold the permit. A professional will answer in one sentence.
bullets: Permit: MoHRE private tuition work permit, Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023
Cost: free of charge, valid two years
Route: MoHRE smart app, website or e-services; two working days stated
No fine schedule is published, so no amount can be quoted
