sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an IA, Extended Essay or TOK essay
paragraphs: This is the boundary that separates legitimate tutoring from a service that can get a student's diploma withheld. The IB's academic-honesty framework requires that work submitted for assessment is the student's own. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what a criterion descriptor is asking for, question a research design, point out that a paragraph does not do what the student thinks it does, and model the technique on a different example. A tutor may not write, draft, restructure or edit to completion any part of the submitted work.

In practice the line is easier to hold than it sounds, because it maps onto a simple test: after the session, who typed the sentences that will be marked? If the answer is the tutor, the work is not the student's. A good session on a Mathematics exploration ends with the student holding three specific problems to fix and no new text in the document. A bad one ends with a tidier document and a student who could not explain why it changed.

Be alert to the other end of this market. One provider found in the research for these pages sells completed Internal Assessments outright, at a published price. That is not tutoring. It is an academic-honesty breach that triggers IB malpractice procedures against the student, not the seller, and the consequence lands on the child. We will not produce assessed work, and we say so here rather than in small print.

The same applies to the Extended Essay and the TOK essay. A supervisor is allocated by the school and the formal process belongs to them; a tutor works alongside it, on research skills, argument structure, source evaluation and referencing. Where a student has a supervisor meeting coming, the most useful session is often rehearsing the questions they will be asked and preparing an honest account of their own progress.
bullets: Allowed: teaching content, unpacking criteria, questioning design, modelling on other examples
Allowed: feedback on the student's own draft, naming the criterion that is not yet met
Not allowed: writing, drafting, restructuring or finishing any submitted text
Not allowed: supplying a completed IA, EE or TOK essay at any price
The school's supervisor owns the formal process; a tutor works alongside it

sections.heading: Fifteen minutes that tell you whether a tutor knows the syllabus
paragraphs: Because the real risk in this neighbourhood is not distance but competence, here is a practical screening method. Ask six questions in the first fifteen minutes of any trial lesson, local or online. None requires you to understand the subject. All six have answers that a genuine IB specialist gives instantly and a generalist cannot fake.

First: what are the papers for this subject at this level, and what does each one weigh? A specialist answers in numbers. Second: what is the internally assessed component called in this subject, and what are its criteria? Note the wording changes by subject, and a tutor who says "the coursework" has told you something. Third: name two command terms that students confuse, and what each demands. Fourth: where in this syllabus do students at my child's current grade most often lose marks? A useful answer is topic-specific, not "exam technique".

Fifth: what will you not do with my child's internal assessment? The answer you want is unprompted and firm. Sixth: what should my child be able to do by the end of six sessions that they cannot do today? This one tests whether the tutor plans or improvises, and a specialist will narrow it rather than widen it: not "improve in Physics" but "handle uncertainty propagation and gradient-meaning questions without prompting".

Run the same six questions past two tutors and the difference is usually obvious within ten minutes. It is a better filter than any credential list, because credentials describe where somebody has been and these questions describe what they can do on Tuesday. Our trial lesson exists for exactly this: you should be using it to interrogate the match, not to be sold to.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory UAE subjects, and what they do to an IB week
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which the UAE government describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale running from Outstanding to Very Weak, and publishes the reports. If you are choosing between schools near Muhaisnah, the inspection report is the single most informative free document available to you, and it names subject-level performance rather than giving one verdict.

KHDA also sets a requirement that reshapes the week of every IB student in Dubai, including yours. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with the requirement to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

The instructional time for those subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic must hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited, which is a real constraint on how any Arabic or Islamic Education support can be described.

The practical consequence for a Muhaisnah Diploma student is that the timetable is already fuller than the six IB subjects suggest, and the hour you add has to come from somewhere. This is why we push families towards one subject at a time and towards the specific failure mode rather than general revision. A student carrying six IB courses, TOK, an Extended Essay, CAS and three mandatory UAE subjects does not have room for two hours of unfocused tutoring a week, and adding it tends to cost more in sleep than it returns in marks.

sections.heading: Starting, and the honest version of what happens next
paragraphs: The sequence is short. You tell us the subject, the level, the school and what specifically is going wrong, with the last report or marked paper if you have one. We identify a specialist for that course and level, not a generalist, and offer a trial lesson at a time that works around the school run. The trial is free and nothing is charged until after it. If the match is wrong, you say so and we look again; a mismatch found in week one costs nothing and a mismatch tolerated for a term costs the year.

What we will not do is tell you a specialist is available when they are not. If your child needs Diploma Visual Arts or Arabic A literature at Higher Level, the match may take a week or two and may be a tutor outside the UAE teaching on Gulf Standard Time over the same platform. We will say that upfront rather than booking you with whoever is free, because a Physics teacher taking a Psychology booking is how families lose a term and conclude that tutoring does not work.

There are also cases where the honest answer is that tutoring is not the right purchase. A student six weeks from a session with four subjects below target usually needs triage and a conversation with their school, not four tutors. A student whose marked papers show the content is known but the timing collapses needs an exam-run block, not a year-long weekly slot. A student who is not sleeping needs neither. We would rather say that at the consultation than sell a package that cannot work.

Finally, the practical note for Muhaisnah specifically. Build the slot around the commute rather than the clock. If the school run gets your child home at 4.45pm, a 4.30pm booking will fail every week and you will blame the tutor. The slots that hold in this neighbourhood are 6pm and 7.30pm on weekdays, and mid-morning on Saturday, and a session that holds is worth more than a session at the theoretically ideal hour.

process.title: Tell us the exact course
process.description: Subject, level, year group, school and the specific problem, with the last report or a marked paper if you have one. "Maths HL, DP1, dropped from a 5 to a 3 after the calculus unit" gets a better match in a day than "needs help with maths" gets in a week.

process.title: We find the specialist, not a generalist
process.description: We look for a tutor who teaches that course at that level habitually. Where the UAE pool does not cover it, we say so and match a specialist elsewhere in the network teaching over the same platform on Gulf Standard Time, rather than filling the slot with whoever is available.

process.title: Free trial lesson around the school run
process.description: A full one-to-one lesson at a time that survives the Muhaisnah commute, with no payment taken and no obligation afterwards. Use it to ask the six screening questions on this page; the trial exists to test the match, not to close a sale.

process.title: Agree a cadence and a target
process.description: One subject, a fixed weekly slot, and a specific thing the student should be able to do in six sessions. Written work set between sessions and marked before the next one, against the same criteria the school applies.

process.title: Review at session six, and change if needed
process.description: A short review against the thing you agreed, using the student's own marked work rather than impressions. If the match is wrong, we change the tutor. If tutoring is not the lever, we say that too, and we would rather lose the booking than keep a slot that is not moving anything.

whyPoints.title: Subject match beats proximity
whyPoints.description: The constraint in eastern Dubai is specialist supply, not travel time. Matching on the exact course and level, rather than on who can drive to Muhaisnah by 5pm, is the single change that most improves the quality of the teaching hour you buy.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits stated, not hidden
whyPoints.description: The coverage table on this page names the subjects where UAE-based specialists are thin and where the match will come from outside the country. Several providers in this market conceal non-UAE delivery behind a local-looking contact number; we would rather publish the limit.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published with sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, with the month it was collected. Three of six ranking competitors publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty treated as a line, not a feature
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work. We will not produce an IA, Extended Essay or TOK essay at any price, and we state the boundary on the page because the alternative puts the student, not the provider, in front of an IB malpractice panel.

whyPoints.title: Lessons that survive a Dubai week
whyPoints.description: Slots move, buses run late, Ramadan shifts the evening, families travel for Eid. An online slot can be rescheduled with a message, which is why continuity holds across a term. Continuity, not intensity, is what most families are actually buying.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claimed as an endorsement
whyPoints.description: We explain what KHDA, ADEK, SPEA and the Ministry of Education do, and link parents to them. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from any of them, and any tutoring site telling you it is KHDA-approved is making a claim you should ask it to evidence.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB home tutor in Muhaisnah who knows the Diploma syllabus?
faqs.answer: There are IB tutors who will travel to Muhaisnah, but the pool of genuine subject specialists living on this side of Dubai is small, and it thins sharply above Standard Level. The schools nearest Muhaisnah lean CBSE and British, so the local private-tutoring market reflects that. IB Gram does not send tutors to Dubai addresses at all; we match your child to a specialist for their exact course and level and teach one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The honest version is that the person who knows your child's syllabus best is probably not within driving distance, and that this matters less than it sounds.

faqs.question: Why does IB Gram not offer in-home visits anywhere in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Because the thing that limits a UAE family's result is which specialist they can reach, not how far that specialist travels. Restricting the shortlist to tutors who can drive to Muhaisnah by five in the evening removes most of the people who teach a given IB course at Higher Level for a living. Home visiting is a service we run only in India, where the supply geography is different. In the UAE every lesson is live, one-to-one and over video, scheduled around the school run, and the free trial lesson lets you test whether the format works for your child before anything is paid.

faqs.question: What do in-home IB tutors charge around eastern Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market bands put in-home one-to-one visits in Dubai at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table quoting 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages of four two-hour visits have been published at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Qualified tutors working online sit lower, roughly AED 150 to 300, with one Dubai agency publishing IB from AED 200. Those are other providers' figures, collected in October 2026, not ours. IB Gram's own position is set after the free trial, once the subject, level and cadence are known.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor need a UAE permit to teach privately?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, free of charge, valid for two years. Eligible holders include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's smart app, website or e-services, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without the permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine amount is published, so treat any specific dirham figure you see online as unverified.

faqs.question: Which IB schools are closest to Muhaisnah?
faqs.answer: The nearest Diploma provision sits in Dubai Festival City, with Mirdif and Nad Al Sheba next closest. Deira International School and Universal American School are both in Festival City, and Uptown International School in Mirdif runs the IB continuum. None of these is inside Muhaisnah itself, which is one reason the neighbourhood's own tutoring market is dominated by CBSE and British curriculum teachers. We name these schools as neighbourhood context only; no affiliation or endorsement is implied, and the KHDA inspection report for any school is the document worth reading before you choose.

faqs.question: How quickly can you find a tutor for a Muhaisnah student?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the subject. Mathematics, Chemistry and Biology at either level usually reach a trial lesson within two to five days, because the specialist pool is deep. Physics HL, Economics HL and English A at Higher Level typically take four to eight days. Psychology, Computer Science, Visual Arts and the less commonly taught languages can take one to two weeks, because we are looking for a particular person rather than any qualified teacher, and that person is often outside the UAE. We would rather tell you the wait than fill the slot badly.

faqs.question: How far can a tutor go in helping with my child's Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the content, explain what each criterion is asking for, interrogate the research question and design, and give feedback on the student's own draft, naming exactly which descriptor is not yet met. A tutor cannot write, draft, restructure or edit any part of the submitted work. The test is simple: after a session, the student should be holding specific problems to fix and the document should contain no new sentences the tutor supplied. Providers selling completed Internal Assessments exist in this market; buying one puts the student in front of an IB malpractice panel, not the seller.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP at a Mirdif school and the reports make no sense to me. Can tutoring help with that?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the commonest requests from this part of Dubai. MYP subjects are assessed against four criteria, each marked out of 8, converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries, with no percentage anywhere. Families arriving from CBSE or a British system often read a criterion mark as a score out of eight and conclude their child is failing. The useful tutoring work is teaching the student to read a descriptor and write to it deliberately, which lifts marks without adding content. Ask the school for the subject's criteria and the task-specific clarifications first.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring really as effective for a child in a busy Muhaisnah apartment?
faqs.answer: It depends on one controllable thing: whether the student has a door that closes and a device the tutor can see work on. With those, an online session delivers the full booked time and the written work can be marked before the next slot. Without them, a lesson competing with three siblings and a television is worse than any alternative. If your home cannot provide a quiet corner for an hour, say so at the consultation and we will talk about timing instead, because a 7.30pm slot after dinner often solves what no platform can.

faqs.question: How many sessions before I can tell whether it is working?
faqs.answer: Six, assessed against something you agreed in advance rather than a feeling. At the consultation we name one concrete capability the student should have by session six, such as handling uncertainty propagation without prompting, or structuring an evaluation paragraph that weighs rather than lists. At session six you look at the student's own marked work against that target. If it has not moved, the match or the diagnosis is wrong and we change it. Judging tutoring by the next school report is too slow, because the report arrives after the term you were trying to fix.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor cover two IB subjects for my child?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and usually it is a bad idea. Mathematics and Physics is the one pairing where a single specialist genuinely works, because the overlap in technique is real. Chemistry and Biology sounds similar but is not; the assessment habits differ and the organic chemistry mechanisms that eat a Chemistry student's hours have no Biology equivalent. A tutor who offers to cover four subjects is telling you they are a generalist. For a Diploma student, one subject properly taught by somebody who knows that syllabus beats two subjects covered by somebody who knows neither.

faqs.question: Do the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons affect my child's IB timetable?
faqs.answer: Yes, substantially. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. The practical effect is that a Diploma student's week is fuller than six subjects plus TOK suggests, which is why we recommend starting with one tutored subject rather than three and targeting a specific failure rather than general revision.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram hold a KHDA permit, and does it matter for an online lesson?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of any tutoring provider that says it is. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises and staff in Dubai, involving initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We explain what those bodies do and link to them; none of them endorses us. Ask any provider claiming approval to show the permit number.

faqs.question: What should I send you to get a useful match first time?
faqs.answer: Four things. The exact course title and level as the school writes it, because "Maths HL" splits into Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation and the tutors are different. The year group and the school. The most recent marked paper or report, which tells a specialist more in two minutes than a paragraph of description. And the two or three time slots that genuinely survive your school run, not the ones you wish worked. With those four, we can usually name a specialist and a trial time in the same reply.

faqs.question: What happens if there is no specialist available for my child's subject at all?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we tell you when we expect that to change. For a handful of Diploma courses, particularly Visual Arts, Film, Theatre and some first-language literature options, the specialist pool is genuinely small and a match can take a fortnight. We will not put a Physics teacher into a Psychology slot to avoid an awkward email. If we cannot cover the course properly, the honest recommendation is usually the school's own subject teacher, the IB coordinator, or a short conversation about which of your child's six subjects is the one actually worth buying help for.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-muhaisnah.closingHeading: A specialist for the syllabus, from a Muhaisnah address
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-muhaisnah.closingBody: If you have reached the bottom of this page you are probably still weighing distance against expertise. The answer we would give any family in Muhaisnah is to stop weighing it. Pick the person who teaches your child's exact course and level, book the slot that survives the school run, and let the lesson happen over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Tell us the subject, the level, the school and what is actually going wrong, send the last marked paper if you have one, and we will come back with a named specialist and a free trial lesson. Nothing is charged before that lesson, and if the match is wrong you say so and we look again.

intro.heading: The Diploma is a calendar problem before it is a teaching problem
paragraphs: Most parents who go looking for Diploma support are reacting to something that has already happened: a DP1 report, a failed mock, a coordinator's email about an internal assessment draft. By then the question is not what help is available but how many weeks are left and what can be done in them. The Diploma runs to a fixed two-year shape, and almost everything that determines the final points total is decided earlier than families expect.

Here is the shape. DP1 runs from August to June and ends with a set of internal examinations that most Dubai schools treat as predicted-grade evidence. Somewhere in the spring of DP1, subject teachers set the first internal assessment deadlines, and the Extended Essay supervisor conversations begin. DP2 starts in August with coursework already overdue in at least one subject for most students, runs into a mock window after the winter break, and then into the May session. The last term is almost entirely examination preparation, because by then every piece of coursework has been submitted.

Counted backwards from the May session, the useful windows are these. The last eight weeks are for timed papers and error correction, not for learning content. The autumn of DP2 is the last chance to repair a subject that is genuinely not understood. The spring of DP1 is when internal assessment topics are chosen, and a bad topic chosen then cannot be rescued in DP2 however good the later help is. And the first term of DP1 is where the subject and level choices either hold or begin to fail.

Nad Al Hamar sits on the eastern side of Dubai, between the Ras Al Khor sanctuary, the Dubai-Al Ain Road and the Al Rashidiya and Mirdif residential belt. Children here travel to schools in Dubai Festival City, Mirdif, Al Warqa, Al Qusais and Academic City, which means a school run of twenty to forty minutes and a door time that is rarely before 4pm. A tutoring plan built on a deadline has to survive that, week after week, which is the practical reason the online slot wins over the in-home one.

To be clear about what is on offer: lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, at a fixed weekly hour. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, because home tutoring is an India-only service for us. What you get instead is a tutor chosen because they have taken students through the specific component you are worried about, which on a Diploma deadline matters more than geography. The rest of this page is the calendar in detail, the market rates with their sources, the word limits on each component, and the line we will not cross on coursework.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-nad-al-hamar.programmesIntro: Nad Al Hamar families reach Diploma support from three directions, and the calendar looks different from each.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service. Each subject carries an internally assessed component that is marked by the school and moderated by the IB, and in most subjects that component sits around a fifth of the grade. The points total is built across two years rather than earned in one examination fortnight.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai private schools are inspected annually by KHDA on a six-band scale, and the Diploma accounts for a modest share of overall private-school enrolment in the emirate compared with the UK and Indian curricula. For a Nad Al Hamar family, that means Diploma schools are a short list reached by a twenty to forty minute drive, and the internal deadline calendar differs between them by a fortnight or more.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment across eight subject groups, with a Personal Project in MYP 5. The relevant point for a Diploma calendar is that MYP 5 ends with a Personal Project deadline and, in some schools, eAssessment, and a student who has just completed both arrives in DP1 already tired of long-form independent work.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving the eastern suburbs run the full continuum, so a Nad Al Hamar student can go from MYP into DP in the same building. That continuity helps, but it also means the first Diploma internal deadline arrives from teachers who already know the student, and the expectations are set accordingly.

programmes.name: IGCSE or MYP into DP1
programmes.description: The least-supported point in the whole sequence. A student moving from IGCSE or MYP 5 into DP1 meets a step change in independent work and in the level of justification expected, particularly in mathematics and the sciences. Six to eight weeks of bridging work over the summer is worth more than a term of remediation in the autumn.
programmes.countryNote: Nad Al Hamar families often have a long summer away, which makes the bridging block awkward in person and straightforward on video. A student in another time zone for July can still keep two sessions a week, and that is the single most common use of online delivery we see from this part of Dubai.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-nad-al-hamar.subjectsIntro: Diploma subjects are tutored unevenly, and the pattern is predictable. These are the subjects Nad Al Hamar families ask for most, with the component that usually prompts the call.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic route, with a non-calculator paper at both levels and an extra investigation paper at Higher Level. The call usually comes after the first DP1 assessment, when the pace of the algebra has outrun a student who was comfortable at IGCSE.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with technology permitted throughout. The call usually comes later, in DP2, when the Higher Level statistical content turns out to be harder than the course's reputation suggested.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields, waves and at Higher Level a heavier mathematical load. Uncertainty treatment and graph linearisation are the components that cost marks in the internal assessment, and both are fixable in a small number of sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, equilibrium and organic chemistry, with organic reliably the dividing line between a 5 and a 7 at Higher Level. Data processing in the internal assessment is where otherwise strong students lose a band.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content plus command-term precision. Students who revise by rereading rather than by answering past questions hold a lot of knowledge and cannot deploy it, which shows as a gap between classwork and examination marks.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation structure decide the essay papers, while Higher Level adds quantitative questions. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published articles, and article selection is the step most often rushed.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, plus the individual oral and at Higher Level the essay. The oral is the component students most often leave unprepared, and it is the easiest to rehearse on video.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-based analysis and a research project at Higher Level. Students lose marks for describing a business rather than applying a framework to it, which is a writing-structure problem rather than a content one.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The essay is capped at 4,000 words with a supervised research process; TOK carries an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay. Both are coached rather than taught, and the boundary on what a tutor may do is tighter here than anywhere else in the Diploma.

sections.heading: What a home tutor means in Dubai, and what we actually do
paragraphs: Home tuition in Dubai is a real market with real prices, and it is worth understanding before deciding against it. An in-home one-to-one visit is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is absorbed, with Bestimate's rate table showing AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages seen in the market run at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. A qualified subject tutor teaching online sits lower, at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200.

The difference between those two bands is not teaching quality. It is travel time, the cost of a tutor's unpaid hours in traffic, and the scarcity premium that comes from hiring within a twenty-minute radius. For Nad Al Hamar that radius is the problem rather than the price: this is a residential district on the eastern edge of the city, and the number of resident Diploma specialists in any given subject at any given level is small, and in a minority subject it may be zero on any given evening. A family insisting on a local visit is choosing from a short list that has nothing to do with the subject.

IB Gram's position is plain. We do not offer home visits in Dubai, or in Abu Dhabi, Sharjah or anywhere else in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we provide in India only. Every lesson for a Nad Al Hamar family is one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, at a slot fixed with the school run in mind. If what you need is genuinely an adult in the room, the right answer is an independently hired local tutor holding a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and there is no reason not to say so.

What the online model buys, specifically, is the ability to pick a tutor because they have taken four students through a Chemistry internal assessment rather than because they live in Mirdif. On a two-year qualification with twenty per cent of each subject grade sitting in coursework, that is the variable with leverage.

sections.heading: The Diploma two years, counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Work from the session, not from today. The May session is the fixed point UAE schools sit, and everything else is a consequence of it. The final eight to ten weeks before it are examination weeks in practice: timed papers, mark-scheme work, error correction. Content learned in that window rarely survives into a paper. Anything that has to be understood from scratch needs to be done in the autumn term of DP2 at the latest.

Before the autumn of DP2 come the internal assessment deadlines, and these are the part families consistently underestimate. Schools set internal dates well ahead of the IB upload windows, because teachers need time to mark and moderate. In practice this means most Diploma coursework in most subjects is submitted during DP2's first two terms, and the topics were chosen in DP1. A student who arrives in DP2 with no internal assessment drafts has a problem that no amount of weekly tutoring in the spring will solve.

Before that again is the spring of DP1, which is the single highest-leverage window in the whole two years and the one nobody books. Internal assessment topics are chosen here. An Extended Essay research question is settled here. A student who commits to a thin topic in April of DP1 has set a mark ceiling that remains in place through everything that follows, and the help needed to avoid that is an hour of screening, not a term of teaching.

The table below is the shape rather than a set of dates, deliberately. Specific IB session and results dates are not published on this page, because IB dates are revised and we have not verified them against the IB directly. Your child's coordinator has the current internal calendar and the IB publishes the official dates on ibo.org. For the IGCSE year below, Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series and Pearson Edexcel runs May and June and November.

sections.heading: The internal assessment pile-up, and the word limits nobody prints
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an internally assessed component, and they are not spread evenly through the year. Because schools set internal deadlines to allow marking and moderation time, three or four of them tend to land within the same six-week stretch of DP2, usually alongside the mock window. A student who has managed each one individually finds the cluster unmanageable, and this is the most common reason a capable Diploma candidate loses points across several subjects at once.

The limits themselves are worth having in one place, because students routinely write to the wrong length. The Extended Essay is capped at 4,000 words. The mathematics exploration runs to roughly twelve to twenty pages. Science internal assessments are capped at a word count in the low thousands. The Theory of Knowledge essay has its own prescribed-title limit and the exhibition a separate commentary limit. Writing substantially over a limit does not earn more credit; markers stop reading at the limit, and the work that mattered may sit beyond it.

What tutoring can genuinely do about the pile-up is sequencing. Looking at a student's actual internal deadlines in September of DP2 and deciding the order in which to attack them, with the one carrying the most marks and the least progress first, is an hour of planning that saves weeks. The second thing is topic screening, done early: a topic that cannot sustain the required depth should be rejected in DP1, not discovered in November of DP2.

The boundary matters most here, so it is stated plainly. A tutor may explain the assessment criteria, show a worked example on a completely different topic, read your child's own draft and respond with questions, and point out where the work falls short of the level claimed. A tutor may not choose the topic, supply the content, write or rewrite any passage, or edit a draft into shape. IB academic-honesty rules make the candidate responsible, and a malpractice finding falls on the student.

sections.heading: The eight-week block, and what it can honestly achieve
paragraphs: The most common request a platform in this market receives is for intensive help in the final weeks, and the most common failure is pretending that window does more than it does. Eight weeks of good work before a session can move examination technique substantially: pacing, command-term handling, showing method, choosing which questions to attempt first, and eliminating the accuracy errors that cost single marks across a whole paper. Those gains are real and sometimes large.

What eight weeks cannot do is replace two years of content. A Higher Level student who has not understood a core topic will not acquire it alongside revision in every other subject. Promising otherwise is how families end up spending heavily in the final term for a small return, and it is the specific thing a parent should be sceptical of when a provider quotes a block of twenty sessions in April.

Used properly, the block looks like this. It opens with a full past paper under timed conditions, marked honestly, with the errors sorted into four buckets: method not known, method known but misapplied, accuracy, and question misread. Those four need different responses, and most students are losing most of their marks in the last three. Sessions then work paper by paper rather than topic by topic, because the paper is the thing being sat.

For a Nad Al Hamar family the practical point is scheduling. In the final weeks most students want more frequent, shorter sessions, and an evening slot plus a weekend morning works better than two long weeknight sessions. Online delivery makes that pattern possible without anyone making four journeys a week across the eastern corridor.

sections.heading: The Nad Al Hamar school run and the slot that survives it
paragraphs: A Diploma plan tied to a deadline only works if the weekly session actually happens, and in this part of Dubai the obstacle is the journey rather than the willingness. Nad Al Hamar children travel out to Dubai Festival City, Mirdif, Al Warqa, Al Qusais or Academic City. A fifteen-minute run to Festival City becomes twenty-five at pickup. A Mirdif run is twenty off-peak and thirty-five at 3pm. Academic City is longer still. Door times land between 3.50pm and 4.30pm on an ordinary day and after 5pm on an activity day.

Diploma students then have a heavy evening. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus whatever coursework is live. A session placed at 4.30pm catches a student who has just walked in. One placed at 8.30pm catches one who has finished thinking. The slot that works across a whole term is 6pm to 7.30pm, and in the eastern suburbs that is exactly the window an in-home tutor cannot promise without a travel buffer, because they are crossing the same roads your child just came home on.

Two practical notes. First, Diploma sessions benefit from being ninety minutes rather than sixty once coursework is live, because reading a draft and discussing it does not fit into an hour. Second, in the final revision block the pattern should change: shorter, more frequent, and with a weekend morning in it, since timed paper work plus review needs a clear two hours that a weeknight does not have.

Ramadan reshapes all of this for a month. School days shorten, door times come forward, and households split between an early-afternoon slot and a post-Iftar one. Both work on video. What does not work is pretending the month will run normally, so a DP2 revision plan should front-load the weeks before it rather than assume them.

sections.heading: What a two-year plan costs, and where the money is wasted
paragraphs: Set the sums out across two years rather than per hour, because that is how a Diploma plan is actually bought. One weekly session in one subject at the qualified-online band of AED 150 to 300 an hour runs to something in the region of AED 600 to 1,200 a month on Bestimate's monthly estimates, with their specialist examination-year band at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. Over two academic years in a single subject that is a substantial commitment, and it is worth deciding deliberately rather than drifting into it.

The commonest waste is buying hours in the wrong term. Twenty sessions in April of DP2 cost the same as twenty spread across DP1 and achieve less, because the April sessions arrive after the coursework is submitted and after the content window has closed. The second commonest waste is buying three subjects at once when one subject is dragging the points total and the other two are fine; a parent who cannot say which subject is the problem should pay for a diagnostic rather than a programme.

The third is paying a specialist premium for work a generalist can do. Timed-paper drilling and accuracy routines do not require an examination-band tutor at AED 400 an hour. Topic screening for a Higher Level internal assessment does. Matching the tier of tutor to the task, rather than buying the top tier for everything, is the single biggest saving available, and no agency will volunteer it.

For household context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's AED 1.5 billion second economic incentives package. School fees are flat and tutoring is the variable line. Every AED figure on this page is a market figure published by the provider named, read in October 2026; IB Gram quotes its own rate after the trial, which is forty-five minutes, free, and takes no card details.

sections.heading: Academic honesty on coursework, stated once and clearly
paragraphs: At least one site ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Since the consequence of buying one lands on the student rather than the seller, the line is worth drawing precisely. Under IB rules all coursework must be the candidate's own work, the school attests to that, and a malpractice finding can cost a candidate the diploma. There is no grade worth that risk, and there is no version of this service that includes it.

A tutor may teach the subject content a student needs in order to attempt a piece of work. A tutor may explain each assessment criterion, how the marks are distributed and what the descriptors actually reward. A tutor may demonstrate a complete worked example built on an entirely different topic. A tutor may read the student's own draft and respond with questions about assumptions, evidence, structure and whether the analysis reaches the level claimed. A tutor may say plainly that a section is below standard and explain why.

A tutor may not select the topic, supply the content or the data, write or rewrite any passage, edit the draft into shape, or produce material the student then submits. The same applies to the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the MYP Personal Project. We also do not host or supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; those belong to the IB and the examination boards, and your child's school has proper access to them.

The useful consequence of working this way is that the student can defend their own work. A candidate who can explain every line of their internal assessment in conversation with their coordinator has nothing to worry about. One who cannot is exposed regardless of the mark the work would otherwise have attracted.

sections.heading: Availability, fallback and the questions worth asking us
paragraphs: Coverage is the thing platforms in this market conceal, so here is the honest shape of it. Common Diploma subjects at Standard Level in mid-evening slots are generally available at short notice. Higher Level specialists in the sciences, and tutors with real experience of a specific internal assessment component, are a narrower pool, and in the eight to twelve weeks before the May session that pool is at its tightest. If nobody suitable is free at your preferred hour, we will say so rather than filling the slot.

The fallback options are limited and worth stating: the nearest available slot with the right specialist, a different tutor with the right subject at a different level of seniority, or a date when the specialist opens up. What we will not do is put a tutor with no experience of the component in front of a student three weeks from a coursework deadline, because the parent cannot see the difference until it is too late to correct.

Questions worth putting to us, or to any provider. Which specific subject and level have you taught, and for how many cohorts. Have you taken a student through this exact internal assessment component. What will you not do with my child's coursework. What happens if the match is wrong after two sessions. Do you hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and may I see it. What is the rate, in AED, per hour, including or excluding anything else.

And one question to ask us that we will answer in the negative: will a tutor come to our home in Nad Al Hamar. No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one teaching over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are an India-only service. If an adult in the room is the requirement, hire locally, check the permit, and use the rate bands on this page to judge whether you are being quoted fairly.

process.description: The mock window, the internal assessment date your school has set, or the session. A plan built backwards from a real date looks different from one built forwards from today, and the date is the piece of information most parents leave out of the first message.

process.description: DP1 autumn, DP1 spring, the summer between, DP2 autumn or the final block. Each one supports different work, and we will tell you if what you are asking for belongs to a window that has already closed.

faqs.question: Do IB tutors come to homes in Nad Al Hamar?
faqs.answer: Not ours. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we run in India only, not in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE. The in-home market here is real, with visits quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is absorbed, so if an adult in the room is your requirement you can hire independently and should ask to see the tutor's MoHRE private tuition work permit. What we offer instead is a tutor matched by subject, level and coursework component rather than by postcode.

faqs.question: How far ahead of the May session should we start Diploma tutoring?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families do. The final eight to ten weeks move technique, pacing and accuracy, which is worth having but will not replace content. The autumn term of DP2 is the last window in which a misunderstood topic can genuinely be rebuilt. The spring of DP1 is the highest-leverage point of all, because that is when internal assessment topics are chosen and a thin topic sets a ceiling nothing later can lift. If you are reading this in DP1, the useful move is a few hours of topic screening.

faqs.question: Which Diploma deadlines actually matter in DP2?
faqs.answer: Your school's internal dates, not the IB's upload windows. Schools set earlier deadlines so teachers can mark and moderate, and three or four subjects often land within the same six-week stretch, usually overlapping the mock window. That cluster, rather than any single component, is what sinks capable candidates. An hour spent in September of DP2 sequencing the internal deadlines by marks at stake and progress made is worth several weeks of unplanned work later. Your coordinator holds the current internal calendar.

faqs.question: Where exactly does Extended Essay coaching stop being allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary we will state to your child in the first session. A tutor can help frame a research question, discuss whether sources are adequate, explain how the criteria distribute marks, and read the student's own draft and respond with questions about argument and evidence. A tutor cannot choose the topic, supply the content, write or rewrite a passage, or edit the essay into shape. The essay is capped at 4,000 words and must be the candidate's own work; a malpractice finding falls on the student, not the tutor.

faqs.question: What does a two-year Diploma tutoring plan cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Using market figures rather than ours: a weekly one-hour arrangement at the mid band is estimated by Bestimate at roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month, with their specialist examination-year band at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. A qualified subject tutor online is quoted at AED 150 to 300 an hour, and Unitors publishes IB from AED 200. Across two years in one subject that is a serious commitment, which is why it is worth buying the terms with leverage rather than a continuous subscription. We quote our own rate after a free trial.

faqs.question: Is the final term too late to make any difference?
faqs.answer: No, but be clear about what changes. In the last eight weeks you can fix pacing, command-term handling, showing of method, question selection and the accuracy errors that cost single marks across a whole paper. Those gains are real. What will not happen is the acquisition of a core topic the student never understood, alongside revision in five other subjects. A provider who sells twenty sessions in April on the promise of content recovery is selling something they cannot deliver.

faqs.question: How do we fit Diploma sessions around a Nad Al Hamar school run?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from the door. Festival City runs put a student home around 3.50pm to 4.10pm, Mirdif around 4.00pm to 4.25pm, Academic City after 4.15pm, and activity days after 5pm. Diploma students then have heavy evening work, so the slot that survives a whole term is usually 6pm to 7.30pm, often ninety minutes once coursework is live. Online delivery holds that start time exactly, because nobody is driving back across Ras Al Khor Road at 5.45pm to reach you.

faqs.question: How does the Ramadan timetable change our weekly Diploma slot?
faqs.answer: The month reshapes the day rather than cancelling it. School hours shorten, so door times come forward, and households generally split between an early-afternoon slot and a post-Iftar one. Both work on video, which they would not with a tutor travelling across the eastern suburbs at Iftar. Tell us which pattern you keep and the slot is rebuilt for the month. The planning point for a DP2 student is to front-load revision into the weeks before Ramadan rather than assume those weeks will run at full intensity.

faqs.question: Which schools near Nad Al Hamar run the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: The nearest clusters are Dubai Festival City and the creek side, including Deira International School and Universal American School Dubai, and the Mirdif and Al Mizhar belt, including Uptown International School. Other schools serving the eastern suburbs take students to IGCSE before an A Level or Diploma split. Dubai had 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate a modest share of enrolment compared with the UK and Indian curricula. Schools are named as local context only, with no affiliation implied.

faqs.question: My child has three internal assessments due in the same month. What do we do first?
faqs.answer: Sequence them by marks at stake against progress made, not by deadline order. The piece carrying the largest share of a subject grade with the least done on it goes first, even if its date is later, because it has the most recoverable value. Pieces that are nearly finished need an hour of criteria-referenced reading rather than a block of sessions. Then tell each subject teacher the order you have chosen; schools will sometimes move an internal date by a week when a student asks in advance rather than apologises afterwards.

faqs.question: Do you publish the IB exam and results dates for this year?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately. UAE schools sit the May Diploma session, and that is as specific as this page gets, because IB session and results dates are revised and we have not verified them against the IB directly. Your child's IB coordinator holds the confirmed internal and external dates, and ibo.org publishes the official ones. For the IGCSE year below, the position is firmer: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November.

faqs.question: Could a single tutor take on both of our Higher Level subjects at once?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, but it is less often a good idea than it sounds. A tutor genuinely strong in Physics and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level exists and is valuable, because the overlap is real. A tutor claiming Chemistry, Economics and English at Higher Level is claiming three specialisms. For a student whose problem is a single weak subject, one specialist beats one generalist. For a student whose problem is organisation across six subjects, a single tutor who sees the whole week can help more.

faqs.question: What should we send you to get a sensible answer quickly?
faqs.answer: Four things. The subjects and levels, written out precisely, including whether mathematics is Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation. The school and the year group. The most recent report or marked assessment, which tells a tutor more in two minutes than a description does in ten. And the date you are working to, whether that is a mock, a coursework deadline or the session. With those four, a useful tutor suggestion takes a day rather than a week of exchanged messages.

faqs.question: How quickly can a Diploma tutor start for a family in Nad Al Hamar?
faqs.answer: For a common Standard Level subject in a mid-evening slot during term time, usually within a few days. For a Higher Level science specialist, or for a tutor with experience of one specific internal assessment component, allow up to a fortnight, and longer in the eight to twelve weeks before the May session when that pool is tightest. If nobody suitable is free at your hour we will tell you, and offer the nearest slot, a different tutor, or a date, rather than filling the gap with whoever is available.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma Programme subjects at Higher and Standard Level and work from mark schemes rather than from textbooks. Each can take a marked paper from your child's school and show you, question by question, which marks were available and why they were not awarded.

intro.heading: The Diploma is lost in components, not in subjects
paragraphs: A Diploma report that says 4 in Chemistry tells a parent almost nothing. The grade is an aggregate of a multiple-choice paper, a data-based paper, an extended-response paper and an internal investigation, each weighted differently, each failing for different reasons. A student can know the chemistry and still arrive at a 4 because every six-mark question was answered as a description, or because the investigation lost nine of its twenty-four criterion marks on evaluation. Until somebody opens the components, nobody is fixing anything.

That is the work this page describes. Nad Al Sheba families sit within a short drive of several established Diploma schools, and the enquiries we receive from this community are rarely about missing content. They are about a student who understands the material in conversation and underperforms on paper. In almost every case the diagnosis turns out to be one of four things: command-term misreading, calculation presentation, internal-assessment criteria nobody translated, or past-paper practice done without a mark scheme.

Take command terms first, because they are the cheapest fix in the programme. The IB publishes a defined vocabulary and the verb in the question tells the examiner what to award. State wants a bare answer. Outline wants a brief account. Explain requires the reason as well as the effect. Discuss requires a balanced review of several arguments. Evaluate requires judgement against stated criteria. A capable student who answers every verb as though it said describe will produce fluent, informed work and score consistently in the middle bands.

Then calculation presentation. In Mathematics the method marks exist independently of the answer, so a student who writes a chain of numbers and arrives correctly can score less than one who sets out reasoning and makes an arithmetic slip. In the sciences the same applies with units, significant figures and uncertainties attached. Nad Al Sheba students in strong cohorts frequently lose these marks for years without anyone naming the habit, because their final answers are right often enough to mask it.

Third, the internal assessment. Every Diploma subject carries one, usually worth twenty per cent of the grade, and every one is marked against lettered criteria with published mark allocations. The sciences investigation is assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each. The mathematics exploration is assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Students who have never read those descriptors routinely submit good work that was never aimed at them.

Fourth, past papers. Working through old papers without the mark scheme is revision theatre. Working through them with the scheme, marking honestly, and recording which criterion or which command term failed is the single most productive hour available in DP2. On several subjects the syllabus has changed recently, so older papers need to be used selectively rather than chronologically, and knowing which parts are still live is part of what a specialist is for.

On format: lessons for Nad Al Sheba families are delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. The section further down prices what the Dubai in-home market charges and what that premium buys, so the comparison is made with numbers rather than with adjectives.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.programmesIntro: Nad Al Sheba sits beside both IB continuum schools and British-curriculum schools, so students arrive at the Diploma from two quite different places. The programme a child comes from decides what the first six weeks of tutoring should actually do.

programmes.name: The IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service. Twenty-four points come from the subjects and up to three more from the core, giving a ceiling of forty-five. Most of the diagnostic work on this page concerns the subject components, because that is where thirty-nine of the forty-five points are decided.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in Dubai also carry the Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies requirements KHDA places on all private schools in the emirate regardless of licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. A Nad Al Sheba DP2 week is therefore tighter than the six-subject list implies, which is why tutoring slots here need to be placed rather than merely booked.

programmes.name: Arriving from the Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Students from the MYP bring strong research habits, comfort with documented process and experience of criterion marking, which makes internal assessments easier for them than for their peers. What they commonly lack is procedural fluency: the drilled, repetitive accuracy the Diploma papers demand under time pressure. The first block of tutoring should be arithmetic and algebraic routine, not study skills.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools near Nad Al Sheba run the full IB continuum, so a sizeable share of local DP1 students have never sat a timed external examination of any kind. Building examination stamina is a separate job from teaching content, and it should be scheduled as one.

programmes.name: Arriving from IGCSE or Year 11 British
programmes.description: The mirror image. These students are fluent in timed papers and accurate under pressure, and they struggle with the extended independent work: the exploration, the investigation, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge. They have rarely been asked to design their own research question or evaluate their own method. The gap is real, nameable and closes in a term if it is addressed in DP1 rather than discovered in DP2.
programmes.countryNote: The transition also changes the mathematics vocabulary. A student fluent in IGCSE Extended methods meets the graphic display calculator as an assessed tool rather than a convenience, and Paper 1 at Diploma level is sat without one, which catches out students who learned to lean on it.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: Three of the forty-five points, and disproportionately stressful for the time they occupy. The Extended Essay runs to a 4,000-word ceiling and is assessed largely on the quality of the research question and the engagement with the process. The TOK essay has a 1,600-word ceiling and the exhibition a 950-word one. Students lose marks on scope rather than on intelligence: questions too broad to answer in the words available.
programmes.countryNote: Supervision sits with a member of staff at your child's school, and an outside tutor works alongside that rather than replacing it. A tutor may question, challenge and give feedback on the student's own writing. A tutor may not write or complete any part of the essay, and no provider should offer to.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.subjectsIntro: Below are the Diploma subjects we are asked for most often from this part of Dubai, each with the component that carries the marks and the specific place students lose them. Bring a marked paper and the conversation starts here rather than at the end of a diagnostic month.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which exposes algebraic fluency precisely. At Higher Level Paper 3 presents two extended problem-solving investigations where the first few marks are accessible and the later parts require sustained reasoning. The exploration carries 20%, and its marks are lost on reflection and mathematical communication rather than on the mathematics itself.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: More modelling, more statistics, heavier calculator use. The losses cluster around interpreting output in context: a student produces a regression line and then says nothing about what it means for the situation described. Higher Level Paper 3 rewards students who write about their model, not just about their numbers.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 1 splits into multiple choice and a data-based section; Paper 2 carries the extended responses and the larger weighting. Organic mechanisms, energetics arithmetic and significant-figure discipline cost the most marks. The data booklet is provided and under-used: students who have not practised with it lose time they cannot recover.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The data-based section of Paper 1 is the most improvable part of the subject and the least revised. Uncertainties, gradients and unit prefixes account for a large share of avoidable losses, and a physics grade is frequently limited by the mathematics course the student chose rather than by their physics.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the visible problem and precision is the real one. Six-mark questions require named structures, named processes and stated directions of movement; general accounts earn a fraction of what is available. The investigation rewards a tightly controlled design over an ambitious one.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is an unseen guided analysis and Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied texts. The individual oral is assessed on the link between a global issue and specific extracts. Students lose marks by writing about the text rather than about the writer's choices and their effect.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are marks, correctly labelled on both axes with the shift explained in words. At Higher Level Paper 3 is quantitative and is where the grade is most often decided. The internal assessment commentaries fail on the link between the article and the syllabus concept rather than on the economics.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application is everything: the question does not ask what a tool is, it asks what the tool shows about the stimulus organisation. Evaluation marks require a judgement with a stated basis, and that final paragraph is the one most candidates omit under time pressure.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source work on Paper 1 is a technique with defined moves: origin, purpose, content, value and limitation. Higher Level Paper 3 demands regional depth that cannot be improvised. The internal assessment is a structured historical investigation with its own sections, each separately assessed.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies must be used as evidence rather than recounted. The highest-scoring answers name a study briefly and spend the remaining words on what it demonstrates and where it is limited, which is the opposite of how most students revise.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title and a 950-word exhibition built on three objects. Marks are lost to scope: titles answered in general terms rather than through specific, contrasting examples from two areas of knowledge.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words, and the research question decides the grade before any writing happens. Questions that are too broad cannot be answered inside the limit, and no amount of good prose rescues them. The reflection sessions with the supervisor carry marks of their own.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Nad Al Sheba is actually hired to fix
paragraphs: The search phrase is about a format and the problem never is. Families in Nad Al Sheba contact us with one of four situations: a DP1 student whose first reports came back two grades below their MYP or IGCSE level, a DP2 student whose mocks did not match their classwork, an internal assessment deadline approaching with no draft worth submitting, or a Higher Level subject chosen in DP1 that now looks like a mistake. None of those is solved by proximity.

Each of them is solved by reading a marked script. A DP1 collapse after a strong Year 11 is almost always the transition rather than the content: a student who sat IGCSE papers accurately now faces extended independent work, or a student from the MYP now faces timed accuracy. Mocks below classwork point at command terms or at examination stamina. A stalled internal assessment points at a research question that was never narrow enough to answer.

This is the honest answer to the home-tutor question. What a family in Nad Al Sheba needs is not somebody within driving distance; it is somebody who knows which component is failing and what the mark scheme awards there. The Dubai market will sell you either. The rest of this page is written so you can tell the difference before you pay for a term, and so you can audit what any tutor is doing for you after you have. Ask any tutor to name the failing component in writing after the second session; one who still talks only about the subject, rather than about Paper 1, Paper 3 or the internal assessment, has not started the diagnosis yet.
bullets: A grade is an aggregate; the diagnosis lives in the components
A DP1 drop after strong IGCSE results is usually the transition
Mocks below classwork point at command terms, not at content

sections.heading: Diploma components, subject group by subject group
paragraphs: The weightings below are published by the IB and they should govern how tutoring hours are allocated. The most common misallocation we see is a student spending every session on content recall for a paper worth a third of the grade, while the internal assessment worth a fifth receives nothing until a fortnight before submission. The second most common is Higher Level students ignoring Paper 3 entirely until the mocks reveal it.

Read the table as a budget rather than as information. If your child's weakest component carries the largest weighting, the plan is obvious. If their weakest component carries ten per cent, the honest advice may be to leave it and work elsewhere. Either way the decision requires the numbers, and a surprising number of Diploma families have never seen them laid out for the subjects their child actually takes. Sort the components into two buckets before you plan anything: the share of the grade marked inside the school, and the share marked externally in the June or November session. The internally marked share is the part still open to influence in DP2, because drafts and deadlines are negotiable in a way that an examination timetable is not. The externally marked share rewards technique work started early and almost nothing started late.

One caution on precision. The IB revises subject guides on a rolling cycle, and weightings and component names change with them. Everything here matches the structure Nad Al Sheba schools are currently teaching, but the authoritative source is your child's subject guide, held by the school. Ask the coordinator for the current version before building a revision plan on any figure, including these ones.

sections.heading: Command terms: the vocabulary that decides the mark
paragraphs: The IB publishes command terms and groups them by the level of thinking they require. The verb is not decoration. It is the instruction to the examiner about what to credit, and a mark scheme written for discuss will not award marks to an answer that describes, however accurate the description. This is the single most reliable cause of a capable student scoring in the middle bands across several subjects at once.

The pattern is easy to spot once you look for it. Ask your child to read a six-mark question aloud and say what the verb is asking for before answering. Students who have never been taught the distinction will answer explain and evaluate identically. Students who have will produce visibly different shapes of answer: a causal chain for one, a weighed judgement with a stated basis for the other.

Fixing it is a technique job measured in weeks, not a content job measured in terms, which makes it the best-value work in the whole Diploma. It also transfers across every subject group simultaneously, so a student who learns to read command terms in Biology stops losing the same marks in History. The table sets out the terms that cost Nad Al Sheba students the most, with what an examiner is looking for in each case. Keep a one-page list of the command terms that appear most often in your child's written feedback and check it against the current subject guide. Where the teacher's shorthand and the guide differ, the guide wins: it is the document the examiner was trained against.

table.caption: IB COMMAND TERMS AND WHAT THE MARK SCHEME EXPECTS
rows: The bare fact, nothing more; no marks for elaboration
A paragraph where a line was wanted, losing time elsewhere
A brief account of the main points, no detail
A full explanation, spending five minutes for one mark
What happens, in sequence, without reasons
Reasons given and the sequence left incomplete
What happens and why, with the causal link stated
A description with the because clause missing
A reasoned proposal for an unfamiliar context
A recalled textbook answer that ignores the stimulus
A balanced review of more than one argument
A one-sided case asserted with confidence
A judgement reached against stated criteria
Two sides listed and no conclusion offered

sections.heading: Where Nad Al Sheba students lose marks in the Diploma sciences
paragraphs: The data-based section of Paper 1 is the most improvable part of a Diploma science and almost nobody revises it. It tests graph reading, gradient calculation, uncertainty handling and the ability to say what a data set does and does not support. None of that requires remembering the syllabus, which means marks are available to a student who is behind on content, and lost by a student who is ahead on it but has never practised the skill.

Significant figures and units are the next layer. Science mark schemes award the final mark for a correctly expressed answer, and a correct number with the wrong number of significant figures or a dropped prefix does not get it. Students in strong Nad Al Sheba cohorts lose these marks for two years, because their answers are right often enough that no teacher flags the habit, and the cost appears only in aggregate at the end.

The scientific investigation is the third. It is worth twenty per cent and assessed on four criteria — research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation — with six marks each. Students pour effort into the practical work and the write-up of results, then lose heavily on evaluation, which asks for the limitations of the method and improvements that are specific rather than generic. More apparatus would help is not a mark. Naming the uncontrolled variable and how it would be controlled is.

The data booklet is the quiet fourth. It is provided in the examination and students who have not worked with it routinely spend minutes locating constants and relationships they should be able to find instantly. Practising with the booklet in hand, on timed questions, converts directly into marks and costs nothing but the habit.

sections.heading: Where Nad Al Sheba students lose marks in Diploma mathematics
paragraphs: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels, and that single fact explains most of the Diploma mathematics problems we are asked to solve in this part of Dubai. Students arriving from IGCSE or from the MYP have usually learned to reach for a calculator at the first sign of arithmetic. Removing it exposes fraction work, surd manipulation, factorising and index laws, and a student can know every topic on the syllabus and still fail to finish the paper.

Method marks are the second theme. A mark scheme awards credit for setting up the correct expression, for the correct substitution, for the correct manipulation, independently of whether the final number is right. A student who writes only a line of working and a final answer surrenders all of those when the arithmetic slips. Teaching a student to write reasoning they consider unnecessary is unglamorous work and it is worth several grade boundaries.

At Higher Level, Paper 3 is the component that decides grades. It presents two long investigations where the opening parts are approachable and the later parts require sustained argument across a problem the student has not seen before. It is also the component most often left unpractised until the mocks, which is when families typically contact us. Six weeks of Paper 3 work in DP2 is a defensible purchase; two weeks is triage.

The exploration completes the picture. Twenty per cent of the grade, assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The mathematics is rarely the problem. Reflection is, because students describe what they did rather than what they learned about the mathematics, and mathematical communication is, because notation is inconsistent and variables are never defined.
