sections.heading: Languages, humanities and the core: the other half of the Diploma
paragraphs: In Language A the recurring fault is writing about the text rather than about the writer. Paper 1 presents an unseen passage with a guiding question, and the marks sit in the analysis of specific choices and their effect on a specific reader. A student who paraphrases the passage accurately and comments generally on its mood will score consistently in the middle. The individual oral fails for a related reason: a global issue asserted rather than demonstrated through the chosen extracts.

In Economics and Business Management the losses are mechanical and therefore cheap to fix. Diagrams must be fully labelled on both axes with the shift explained in words beside them; an unlabelled diagram earns nothing however correct its shape. Evaluation requires a judgement with a stated basis, which is the paragraph students omit when time runs short, and it is usually the paragraph carrying the top band. At Higher Level, the quantitative paper in Economics is where a grade is most often decided.

In History, Paper 1 source work is a defined technique: origin, purpose, content, then value and limitation derived from the first three. Students who describe what a source says, without saying what kind of source it is or why it was produced, lose most of the available marks on a component they could have been drilled for. Higher Level Paper 3 requires regional depth that cannot be improvised in the final weeks.

The core is where the three remaining points sit. The TOK essay runs to 1,600 words on a prescribed title and the exhibition to 950 words on three objects, and the Extended Essay to 4,000. All three are decided by scope: a question narrow enough to answer in the words available. A tutor can challenge a question, test whether it is answerable and give feedback on the student's own writing. A tutor may not write or complete any part of the essay, and the student should hear that said plainly at the start.

sections.heading: The internal assessment: criteria, letters and the line
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an internal assessment, and every one is marked against lettered criteria with published mark allocations. This is public information that a large share of students have never been shown. They produce work aimed at what they imagine a good piece looks like, when the marks are awarded against a specific list, and the gap between those two things is where twenty per cent of the grade quietly disappears.

The arithmetic is worth stating. A sciences investigation is twenty-four criterion marks across four criteria. Losing three marks on evaluation and two on data analysis is five of twenty-four, which is a fifth of that component and four per cent of the final subject grade. Across three sciences, that is the difference between a Diploma total that reaches a university offer and one that does not, and it was all available to a student who read the descriptors in advance.

The honesty boundary is simple and we say it out loud in the first supervision session. A tutor may question a research design, point out that a conclusion is not supported by the data presented, explain what an evaluation criterion is asking for, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write the internal assessment, may not draft the exploration, and may not edit either to completion. That is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, not on the tutor.

A provider offering completed coursework should be refused on that basis alone, and they exist in this market. Our position is a differentiator rather than a limitation: a student who has been talked through a criterion understands it for the next assessment too, and there are five more of those coming.

sections.heading: In-home or online for a Nad Al Sheba Diploma student
paragraphs: Parents using this search phrase deserve the market position stated rather than deflected. Dubai prices an in-home one-to-one visit at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, against AED 150 to 300 for an equivalent qualified tutor working online, with IB and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. Advertised monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions have run at AED 1,599 to 1,799. The premium is travel time converted into fee.

For a Diploma student the premium also buys a narrower choice, and the narrowing matters more here than at any other level. The specific need is rarely a tutor, it is a tutor who knows Higher Level Paper 3 in Analysis and Approaches, or the current sciences investigation criteria, or Higher Level Economics Paper 3. The set of people with that expertise who will also drive to Nad Al Sheba on a Tuesday evening is small, and may be empty. Choosing from it means choosing on geography.

IB Gram does not sell home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we operate only in India. Diploma sessions for Nad Al Sheba families run one-to-one over live video to Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own marked script shared on screen. For component repair that format is better than a kitchen table, because the paper, the mark scheme and the student's redraft can all be visible simultaneously, which is exactly how this work is done.

sections.heading: Past papers used properly on a syllabus that has changed
paragraphs: Most Diploma students work through past papers and most do it in a way that produces very little. The pattern is familiar: attempt a paper untimed, check the answers, note the score, move on. That measures the student and teaches nothing. The productive version is timed, then self-marked against the scheme before anyone else sees it, then logged by failure mode: command term misread, method not shown, criterion misunderstood, content gap, ran out of time.

After six papers logged that way, a pattern appears that no amount of lesson observation would produce. One student loses eleven marks to unshown method and two to content. Another loses everything on the final extended-response question because they reach it with four minutes left. Those two students need completely different plans, and the log is what tells you which you have. It is also the cheapest diagnostic instrument in the Diploma, because it costs the student's own time rather than a tutor's hour.

The syllabus caveat is important in the sciences and in mathematics particularly, where recent guide revisions mean older papers contain content that is no longer examinable and omit components that now exist. Working chronologically backwards through a decade of papers therefore wastes effort and, worse, builds confidence on questions that will not appear. Knowing which older papers remain useful and which sections of them to skip is a genuine part of what subject expertise buys.

One practical limit: we do not supply papers, mark schemes or subject guides. Those are published by the International Baccalaureate and are available to your child through their school and the coordinator. We work from the material the student legitimately holds, and we reference the official sources rather than reproducing them.

faqs.question: My child understands the subject but the Diploma grades do not show it. Where is that going wrong?
faqs.answer: Four causes account for most cases. Command terms misread, so every verb is answered as though it said describe. Method not shown, so mark schemes cannot award the credit that exists independently of the final answer. Internal assessment criteria never translated, so twenty per cent of the grade was aimed at nothing in particular. Or examination timing, where the final extended-response question is reached with minutes left. All four are visible on a single marked script, which is why we ask for one before quoting any plan.

faqs.question: Which Diploma component is the most improvable for the hours spent?
faqs.answer: In the sciences, the data-based section of Paper 1. It tests graph reading, gradients, uncertainties and what a data set supports, none of which requires syllabus recall, so marks are available even to a student who is behind on content. In mathematics, method presentation on Paper 1. In the humanities, source technique on History Paper 1 and diagram labelling in Economics. All of those are habits rather than knowledge, and habits move in weeks where content takes terms.

faqs.question: What exactly are the criteria on a Diploma sciences investigation?
faqs.answer: Four, each worth six marks, giving twenty-four in total: research design, data analysis, conclusion, and evaluation. Research design wants a focused question with named and controlled variables and a method somebody else could repeat. Data analysis wants processing with uncertainties carried through. Conclusion wants a judgement the data actually supports, related to accepted science. Evaluation wants specific limitations of the method with specific realistic improvements, which is where most students lose the most, because generic suggestions earn nothing.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks when their final answers are correct?
faqs.answer: Because a large share of Diploma marks are method marks, awarded for setting up the correct expression, substituting correctly and manipulating correctly, regardless of the number at the end. A student who writes two lines and a correct answer collects fewer of those than one who sets out reasoning and slips on arithmetic. In the sciences the same pattern appears with units, significant figures and prefixes: the final mark is for a correctly expressed answer, and a right number wrongly expressed does not earn it.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Paper 3 worth paying for separately?
faqs.answer: In mathematics, usually yes. It carries twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade, presents two extended investigations on unfamiliar problems, and is the component most often left unpractised until the mocks reveal it. Six weeks of structured Paper 3 work in DP2 is a defensible purchase with a clear target. Two weeks before the papers is damage limitation. In Economics and History the equivalent third papers carry even heavier weightings, so the same logic applies with more urgency.

faqs.question: How should a DP2 student actually use past papers?
faqs.answer: Timed first, self-marked against the scheme second, and tutor-marked third, with a written log of the failure mode for each lost mark: command term, method not shown, criterion misunderstood, content gap, or time. After six papers logged that way a pattern appears that no amount of lesson observation would produce, and the pattern decides where the remaining weeks go. Checking answers and recording a score measures the student and teaches nothing, which is how most students spend the time.

faqs.question: Do older past papers still work after a syllabus revision?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the filtering matters. Recent guide revisions in the sciences and mathematics mean older papers contain content no longer examinable and omit components that now exist, so working chronologically backwards through a decade wastes effort and builds confidence on questions that will not appear. Knowing which older papers remain useful, and which sections to skip inside them, is a real part of what subject expertise buys. Your child's coordinator holds the current subject guide, which is the authority on what is live.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do with an Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Question the research question hard, which is where the grade is actually decided, and test whether it can be answered inside 4,000 words. Explain what the assessment criteria reward. Point out where an argument is asserted rather than evidenced, and give feedback on writing the student has produced. What a tutor may not do is write or complete any part of it, or edit it to completion. Supervision sits with a member of staff at the school, and an outside tutor works alongside that rather than in place of it.

faqs.question: My child is in DP1 and the first reports dropped two grades from Year 11. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is common and it is usually structural rather than academic. A student fluent in IGCSE papers now faces extended independent work they have never been asked for: a research question of their own, a method of their own, an evaluation of their own. A student from the MYP faces the opposite problem, meeting timed accuracy for the first time. Identify which transition your child is in, because the two need opposite first blocks, and treating one as the other wastes a term.

faqs.question: Does the maths course my child chose limit their science grade?
faqs.answer: It can, particularly in Physics. The data-based and calculation-heavy parts of a Diploma science assume comfort with rearrangement, standard form, logarithms and gradient work, and a student on the lighter mathematics route can hit a ceiling in Physics that looks like a physics problem and is not. The practical consequence is that a physics tutoring plan sometimes starts with mathematics. We will say so if that is what the marked script shows, even though it is not what the enquiry asked for.

faqs.question: How many marks is it actually worth translating the criteria?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect. A sciences investigation is twenty-four criterion marks. Dropping three on evaluation and two on data analysis is five of twenty-four, which is a fifth of a component worth twenty per cent, so roughly four per cent of the final subject grade. Repeat that across three sciences and it is the difference between a Diploma total that clears a university offer and one that does not. Reading the descriptors in advance costs one session.

faqs.question: Can the individual oral be prepared for, or is it improvised?
faqs.answer: It is highly preparable, and students who treat it as a conversation underperform. The assessment rewards a clear global issue genuinely demonstrated through the chosen extracts, with specific textual detail used as evidence rather than mentioned. The failure mode is asserting the issue and then summarising the texts. Structured preparation means choosing extracts that actually carry the issue, building the argument around specific lines, and rehearsing to time so the closing analysis is not lost.

faqs.question: What does the data booklet change about science revision?
faqs.answer: It changes what is worth memorising and what is worth practising. Constants and relationships that are provided in the examination do not need committing to memory, but finding them quickly under time pressure does need rehearsing. Students who have never worked with the booklet lose minutes locating what they should find instantly, and those minutes come out of the extended-response questions at the end of the paper. Practising timed questions with the booklet open converts directly into marks and costs nothing.

faqs.question: Is an in-home Diploma tutor in Nad Al Sheba better than an online one?
faqs.answer: The Dubai market charges roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour for in-home visits against AED 150 to 300 for an equivalent qualified tutor online, and that gap is travel priced into the hour. For Diploma work the bigger cost is the narrowing: the people who know Higher Level Paper 3 or the current investigation criteria and will also drive to Nad Al Sheba in the evening are few. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; sessions run over live video to Gulf Standard Time with the marked script on screen.

faqs.question: Will a tutor supply IB past papers and mark schemes for us?
faqs.answer: No. Subject guides, past papers and mark schemes are published by the International Baccalaureate and are available to your child through their school and the Diploma coordinator. Reproducing or distributing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, an academic-integrity one. We work from the papers and schemes the student legitimately holds, cite the official source when we reference anything, and point you to the coordinator for material you do not have.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.closingHeading: Send one marked script and the diagnosis is most of the work
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.closingBody: If a Diploma student in Nad Al Sheba is underperforming, the thing standing between you and a plan is not a tutor. It is knowing which component is losing the marks and why. Send one recently marked paper or internal assessment draft with the subject and level, and the trial session will tell you whether the fault is command terms, method presentation, a criterion nobody translated, examination timing or genuine content. Those five need different plans and very different numbers of hours, and you should know which one you are buying before you buy it.

intro.heading: The worry behind the search is syllabus currency, and it is justified
paragraphs: Parents in Oud Metha ask for an IB home tutor and are usually asking something more precise than they say out loud: is there anybody within reach who genuinely knows the syllabus my child is sitting, as it exists now? That is a sharper question than it sounds, and it deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. The International Baccalaureate revises its subject guides on a cycle, and several have been rewritten in the last few years. A tutor whose most recent classroom experience predates the revision is not incompetent. They are working from a map that has changed.

The consequences are specific rather than vague. In the sciences the guides published in 2023, first assessed in 2025, restructured content and changed the assessment architecture: the old optional topics went, the paper structure changed at Higher Level, and the internal assessment became a single scientific investigation. In Economics the 2020 guide introduced a conceptual framework and a different internal assessment format entirely. In Theory of Knowledge the exhibition replaced the presentation. In Language A the individual oral replaced the older oral commentary and a learner portfolio appeared. A tutor who prepares a student for an option topic that no longer exists has wasted the hours and, worse, has built confidence in the wrong place.

This is also why the most common form of evidence a family has - a recommendation from another parent in Oud Metha - is the weakest kind here. The neighbour's child may have sat a different guide, a different subject, a different level, or all three. A tutor who was genuinely excellent for a Higher Level Chemistry student three years ago may be teaching a structure that no longer matches the paper. The recommendation was honest and it has quietly expired, and nobody involved knows that.

What a parent without subject knowledge can do about it is more than they think. Four questions, answerable in a few minutes, separate a tutor who is current from one who is not, and they do not require you to understand the chemistry. Those questions are in a table further down, along with what changed in which subject. We would rather hand them over than ask anybody to trust a claim, including ours.

On delivery, since the URL says home tutor and that is the phrase parents type: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India, and every lesson for an Oud Metha family is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. The syllabus-currency problem is, in fact, the clearest argument for that model. Insisting on somebody who can drive to Oud Metha narrows the field to whoever is nearby and available, and currency on a revised guide is not distributed by postcode.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The current guide organises content as Structure and Reactivity rather than the older numbered topics, the optional topics are gone, and the internal assessment is a single scientific investigation. subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Content is grouped into five themes and the paper structure changed, with Paper 1 carrying a multiple-choice section and a data-based section. Anyone preparing a student for a separate options paper is preparing for something that is not sat. The investigation is one piece of work on four criteria, worth 20 per cent.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Restructured around unifying themes and levels of biological organisation rather than the older topic list, with options removed and a single scientific investigation. The content overlap with the previous guide is large, which is exactly why a stale tutor sounds convincing - the facts are mostly right and the structure and assessment are not.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The current guide is built around a set of key concepts and the internal assessment is a portfolio of commentaries framed by those concepts. A tutor working from the previous format will coach commentary writing against the wrong framing, which caps the internal assessment regardless of how well written it is.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by an exhibition of three objects against a prompt plus an essay on a prescribed title. The exhibition replaced an earlier presentation format. subjects.name: Language A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: An individual oral examining how a global issue is presented across two works, a learner portfolio, an unseen analysis paper, a comparative essay paper and at Higher Level an additional essay. subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: One of the two routes that replaced the earlier Mathematics structure, with proof, calculus and algebraic technique emphasised and a mathematical exploration as the internal assessment. A tutor describing the old Studies, Standard and Higher structure is describing something that no longer exists.

subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route, with heavier technology use and the same exploration component. Students and parents often assume this is the easier option; it is a different emphasis rather than a lower demand, and university requirements treat the two routes differently.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Revised in recent years with changes to both content organisation and the internal assessment. Anyone coaching the previous internal assessment format is coaching a structure that is no longer submitted, which is a whole component's worth of misdirected work.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: A longer-stable guide, with a source-based paper, an essay paper, a Higher Level regional paper and an internally assessed historical investigation. Stability makes currency less of a risk here, which is worth knowing - the check matters more in some subjects than others and it is not uniform.

subjects.name: Language B
subjects.description: Writing, listening and reading papers plus an individually assessed oral on a stimulus. The oral format and the themes framework are the parts most likely to be out of date in older material, and the oral carries enough weight that getting its structure wrong is expensive.

subjects.name: The Arts
subjects.levels: Visual Arts, Music, Theatre, Film · HL and SL
subjects.description: Heavily internally assessed through portfolios, exhibitions and performance components, with documentation requirements that have been revised. sections.heading: Which IB guides have moved, and what a stale tutor teaches wrong
paragraphs: The reason this matters more than it sounds is that a stale tutor is convincing. The factual content of a revised guide usually overlaps heavily with the version before it, so the explanations are right, the worked examples are right, and the manner is confident. What has changed is the structure: which content is examinable, how the papers are built, and what the internally assessed component actually is. Those are the things that decide marks, and they are invisible to a parent sitting in the next room hearing competent chemistry.

The sciences are the clearest case. The current Biology, Chemistry and Physics guides, published in 2023 and first assessed in 2025, removed the optional topics, reorganised content - Chemistry into Structure and Reactivity, Physics into five themes, Biology around unifying themes and levels of organisation - and changed the assessment architecture, with a single scientific investigation worth 20 per cent across four criteria. A tutor preparing a student for an option topic is preparing for something not sat. A tutor describing a separate Higher Level options paper is describing a paper that is not set.

Outside the sciences the changes are different in kind but equally consequential. Theory of Knowledge is now assessed through an exhibition of three objects against a prompt, plus the essay; the exhibition replaced an earlier presentation format, so a tutor coaching a presentation is coaching a component that no longer exists. Economics is organised around key concepts with an internal assessment framed by them. Language A uses an individual oral examining a global issue across two works, which differs from the older oral commentary in both structure and preparation. Business Management has been revised in both content and internal assessment.

Two honest caveats. First, not every subject has changed: History, for instance, has been relatively stable, so the currency risk is not uniform and a family should not treat every tutor as suspect. Second, your child's school is the authority on which version applies, not us and not a web page - guides have transition periods and schools confirm what their cohort is sitting. Ask the IB coordinator for the subject guide version and first-assessment year for each subject, and use the table below as a checklist rather than as a verdict.

sections.heading: Four questions that expose a stale syllabus without any subject knowledge
paragraphs: A parent does not need to understand chemistry to find out whether a chemistry tutor is current. The questions below work because they ask about structure rather than content, and structure is exactly what a stale tutor gets wrong. They take about four minutes and they work on anybody, including us.

First: what is the internally assessed component in this subject, and how is it marked? In the current science guides the answer is one scientific investigation, assessed on four criteria, worth 20 per cent. If an answer involves two separate pieces of practical work, or a distinct group project submission, or describes criteria that do not match what the school has told you, the tutor is working from an earlier version. Second: how many papers does my child sit, and what is in each? A tutor who teaches the subject answers without hesitation, because the paper structure determines the teaching order.

Third: which content is optional, and what has my child chosen? In the current science guides this is a trick question with a correct answer of none, because the optional topics were removed. A tutor who starts discussing which option to revise has told you everything you need to know. The equivalent in Theory of Knowledge is asking what the non-essay component is: exhibition is current, presentation is not. Fourth: what is the top-level structure of the course - name the main divisions? Structure and Reactivity for Chemistry, five themes for Physics, the two routes for Mathematics.

Then do one more thing, which costs nothing. Email the school's IB coordinator and ask for the subject guide version and first-assessment year for each of your child's subjects. With those in hand the four questions become checkable rather than suggestive, and the conversation with any prospective tutor takes two minutes instead of four. Families in Oud Metha who do this consistently report that it changes who they hire, and occasionally that it changes whether they hire anybody at all.

sections.heading: Why another Oud Metha parent's recommendation is the weakest evidence here
paragraphs: In a district where families know each other and children attend the same handful of schools, a recommendation carries real weight, and it should - for most services it is the best signal available. For Diploma subject tutoring it is the signal most likely to be quietly out of date, and it is worth understanding why before acting on one.

A recommendation encodes an experience from one to three years ago, in one subject, at one level, under whatever guide was then in force. Every one of those four variables can differ from your case. The other child may have sat Standard Level where yours sits Higher. They may have been on the previous guide where yours is on the current one. They may have needed content teaching where yours needs internal assessment design. And the tutor who was excellent at the first thing may never have taught the second.

What makes this particularly hard to detect is that the recommendation was honest. The other family's experience was good, the grade came out well, and they are passing on something real. Nobody in the chain knows that the course has been rewritten underneath the advice. This is the single most common way we see Oud Metha families spend money on tutoring that is competent and misaimed, and it is not anybody's fault.

The fix is not to distrust your neighbours. It is to add one step: take the recommendation, then run the four currency questions and check the answers against what the coordinator has told you about your child's guide. A genuinely current tutor passes that in two minutes and nobody is offended. A tutor who does not pass it has just saved you a term. Ask us the same questions - we would rather be checked than believed.

sections.heading: The school is the authority, and it will tell you in one email
paragraphs: Everything on this page rests on a fact a web page cannot supply: which version of each subject guide your child is actually being taught. Guides have transition arrangements, schools confirm what their cohort is sitting, and a tutoring site that tells you with certainty what your child is studying is guessing. The IB coordinator at your child's school knows, and the question is ordinary rather than awkward.

Ask for five things in one message. The subject guide version and first-assessment year for each of your child's six subjects. The internally assessed component for each and its weighting. The school's internal deadlines for those components, which are the dates that actually govern a student's year. The Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay internal deadlines. And whether any subject is in a transition cohort, because that is where confusion concentrates.

Those five answers do more for a family than most first tutoring sessions. They tell you what is being examined, what is already closed, what is still open, and - once you have the guide versions - whether any prospective tutor is working from the right material. They also tell you where there is no problem: if a subject's guide has been stable for years, the currency question is largely moot and you can judge a tutor on ordinary grounds.

One further reason to go to the school first: it is free, and some of what families buy tutoring for is already provided. Oud Metha households sit inside the school belt, which means after-school support, departmental revision sessions and teacher availability are physically easy to access. Before paying anybody, it is worth establishing what the school already runs. We would rather a family used a free departmental session than bought an hour from us to cover the same ground, and we will say so when the free option looks adequate.

sections.heading: What a current specialist does differently inside the hour
paragraphs: It is fair to ask what currency actually looks like in practice, because the claim is easy to make and harder to evidence. Three things change in a session when a tutor is working from the right guide, and all three are observable from the next room if you know what to listen for.

The first is that the internally assessed component is framed by its real criteria from the first minute. In the current science guides that means research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, with the ceiling set by whether the chosen variable can be measured precisely enough against the instrument's resolution. A current tutor asks about instrument resolution early. A stale tutor talks about having a clear hypothesis and working hard, which is advice that fits any version and improves none.

The second is that past-paper work matches the paper being sat. A tutor who knows that Paper 1 carries a data-based section will drill uncertainty handling and graph reading, because that is where the marks are. A tutor on the previous architecture will spend proportionally more time on content recall and less on data skills, and the student will meet the data section underprepared while feeling well taught.

The third is that the teaching sequence matches the school's. The current guides reorganised content, which means the order a school teaches in has changed too. A current tutor can follow the school's sequence because they recognise it; a stale one imposes their own, and the student ends up being taught next term's material this term while this term's assessment goes unprepared. That mismatch is one of the most frequent complaints we hear from families who have had tutoring that did not work, and it is almost always this rather than teaching quality.

sections.heading: What currency is worth paying for, and what it is not
paragraphs: Currency is a real reason to pay a specialist rate rather than a budget one, and it is worth being precise about where that premium earns its keep rather than applying it everywhere.

The market figures first, each attributed and read in October 2026. At the budget end Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, which buys homework supervision. Unitors publishes IB from AED 200 an hour and IGCSE from AED 150. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table places IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. TutorChase publishes AED 270. BartyED sits at AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors. Monthly, Bestimate estimates a weekly hour at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work, with packages advertised around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Where currency justifies the specialist band: anything touching the internally assessed component, because that is where a wrong rubric costs 20 per cent of a grade rather than a few marks; and past-paper diagnosis, because reading a script usefully requires knowing which paper it came from and what that paper rewards. Where it does not: content explanation of material that did not change. A competent tutor at the mid band explaining bonding or kinematics is giving you the same thing as a specialist at twice the price, because the physics did not move.

Where no premium is justified at all is the final fortnight's technique practice, which is the student's own work, and homework supervision, which is what the budget band actually sells and is sometimes exactly the right purchase. None of these are IB Gram prices - we publish no rate card on a landing page, hold no office or centre in the UAE, and claim no approval, accreditation or licence from the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International or Pearson.

sections.heading: Oud Metha has the shortest drive in Old Dubai, and online still wins
paragraphs: This is the one district where the in-home argument is at its strongest, so it deserves a fair hearing. Oud Metha sits inside the school belt with large schools within walking distance, so commutes are short, children get home early, and a tutor travelling here faces an easier journey than one heading for Al Nahda. If distance were the only consideration, this is where in-home would make most sense.

Our position remains what it is, stated before payment rather than after: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every lesson for an Oud Metha family is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We hold no office, centre or branch in the UAE either, so there is nowhere to visit. We put this on the page because two providers ranking for these searches route UAE parents to overseas phone numbers without disclosing where their tutors actually sit.

And the reason the short drive does not change the answer is the whole subject of this page. The binding constraint is not travel time; it is whether anybody available is current on your child's subject guide. Shortening the radius from twenty minutes to ten makes the pool smaller, not larger, and currency on a guide revised two years ago is not distributed geographically. For Higher Level Chemistry on the current guide, or Theory of Knowledge with the exhibition component, the question is not who can get here but who has taught this version, and those are different lists.

What the short Oud Metha commute does genuinely buy is the best scheduling position in Old Dubai. A 4pm or 4.30pm start is realistic here in a way it is not in Karama or Al Nahda, which means a session can happen before fatigue sets in and before a shared study surface is contested. That is a real advantage and it applies equally to an online session. Use it: claim the early slot at the start of term, choose it against the worst realistic day rather than the best, and agree in advance that it shifts during Ramadan when school days shorten.

sections.heading: Permits, claims and the dates we will not print
paragraphs: A page about verifying tutors should be verifiable itself, so here is everything checkable about our position. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and states a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published officially, nobody should quote you an amount.

Add that to your currency questions, because it is the easiest one to verify and the permit is free, which removes any cost excuse for not holding one. One related rule: in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct likewise bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. In a district like Oud Metha where the schools are a short walk away, that is the arrangement most likely to be offered informally and it is the one to decline.

On accreditation: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, certification, licence or partnership from the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge International or Pearson. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai - initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry - and we do not hold one. Anyone implying such approval should be asked for the permit or centre number.

Three further absences, each deliberate. There is no IB examination or results date on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date in a Diploma plan is a date a family acts on - take every date from your coordinator or ibo.org. There is no satisfaction percentage, star rating or tutor headcount, because none could carry a sample size, a date and a method. And we do not publish or redistribute IB subject guides, assessment criteria documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads; we reference them and cite the source, because they are the IB's copyright. We also do not write, co-write or edit to completion any part of an internally assessed component - we teach, question and give feedback on the student's own work, and one provider ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments outright.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and the week behind the question
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. In 2024-25 the sector was 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of students, Indian at 26 per cent and US at 14 per cent. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools - four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate - creating 16,846 new places, after six opened in 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent.

That last figure is relevant to the currency problem in a slow way. More IB provision in Dubai means, over several years, more teachers with recent experience of current guides, which gradually improves the local pool. It does not help a family deciding this term, and it does not help in Oud Metha specifically, where the nearest Diploma provision is across the creek.

The timetable facts matter to the week any tutoring has to fit into. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, under KHDA requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and requires teachers of those subjects to hold the appropriate KHDA approval. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited.

Put those hours beside six Diploma subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, and the week is full. A student in Oud Metha who says there is no time is usually describing arithmetic. In that situation the useful first move may be the school's own free departmental support, or a conversation with the coordinator about an internal deadline, rather than a purchase. We would rather name that than sell against it, and a two or three session diagnosis will tell you which it is.

faqs.question: How do I know whether a tutor knows the current IB syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask four questions about structure rather than content, because structure is what a stale tutor gets wrong. What is the internally assessed component and how is it marked? How many papers does my child sit and what is in each? Which content is optional - in the current science guides the correct answer is none, because options were removed. And name the top-level structure of the course. A current tutor answers all four without hesitation, because those facts determine how they teach.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects have had their guides rewritten recently?
faqs.answer: The sciences most visibly: the current Biology, Chemistry and Physics guides were published in 2023 and first assessed in 2025, removing optional topics, reorganising content and consolidating the internal assessment into a single scientific investigation worth 20 per cent. Economics was rebuilt around key concepts with a new internal assessment framing. Theory of Knowledge replaced its presentation with an exhibition. Language A moved to an individual oral on a global issue. History has been comparatively stable. Confirm which version applies with your school's IB coordinator.

faqs.question: What exactly does a tutor get wrong if they are using an old guide?
faqs.answer: Usually not the facts, which is why it is hard to spot. The explanations and worked examples are often right. What is wrong is the structure: which content is examinable, how the papers are built and what the internally assessed component is. A tutor preparing a student for a removed option topic has wasted the hours. One coaching the wrong internal assessment rubric has misprepared 20 per cent of a science grade. One imposing an old teaching sequence leaves this term's assessment unprepared.

faqs.question: Should I trust another parent's tutor recommendation in Oud Metha?
faqs.answer: Take it, then verify it. A recommendation encodes an experience from one to three years ago, in one subject, at one level, under whatever guide was then in force, for whatever need that family had. All four can differ from your case, and the course may have been rewritten underneath the advice without anyone noticing. The recommendation is honest and may have quietly expired. Add one step: run the four currency questions and check the answers against what your coordinator confirms.

faqs.question: What should I ask my child's IB coordinator?
faqs.answer: Five things in one email. The subject guide version and first-assessment year for each of the six subjects. The internally assessed component for each, and its weighting. The school's internal deadlines for those components, since those are the dates that actually govern the year. The Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay internal deadlines. And whether any subject is in a transition cohort, because that is where confusion concentrates. Those answers do more than most first tutoring sessions.

faqs.question: Does syllabus currency really change what happens in a session?
faqs.answer: In three observable ways. A current tutor frames the internally assessed component by its real criteria from the first minute - for the current sciences, research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation - and asks early about instrument resolution against the expected change. Their past-paper work matches the paper actually sat, so they drill the data-based section rather than only content recall. And their teaching sequence follows the school's, because the content order changed in the revision and they recognise it.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying a specialist rate just for syllabus currency?
faqs.answer: For some work, decisively. Anything touching the internally assessed component justifies the specialist band, because a wrong rubric costs 20 per cent of a grade rather than a few marks. So does past-paper diagnosis, since reading a script usefully requires knowing which paper it came from. For explaining content that did not change - bonding, kinematics - a competent mid-band tutor gives you the same thing, because the physics did not move. For final-fortnight technique practice, no premium is justified at all.

faqs.question: Oud Metha has schools within walking distance. Why not use a local tutor?
faqs.answer: The short drive is a genuine advantage of this district and it does not address the binding constraint. Whether somebody is current on your child's subject guide is not distributed geographically, and narrowing the radius from twenty minutes to ten makes the available pool smaller rather than larger. What the short commute does buy is the best scheduling position in Old Dubai - a 4pm or 4.30pm start is realistic here - and that advantage applies just as fully to an online session.

faqs.question: Do you provide a tutor who comes to our home in Oud Metha?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every lesson for an Oud Metha family is one-to-one over live video in a Gulf Standard Time slot, and we state that before you pay. We also hold no office, centre or branch in the UAE, so there is nowhere to visit. Two providers ranking for these searches route UAE parents to overseas phone numbers without disclosing where their tutors sit.

faqs.question: Could the school's own support be enough instead of tutoring?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and in a district inside the school belt it is worth checking first. Departmental revision sessions, after-school support and teacher availability are physically easy to reach from Oud Metha, and they cost nothing. Establish what the school already runs before paying anybody. We would rather a family used a free departmental session than bought an hour from us covering the same ground, and we will say so where the free option looks adequate for what is actually wrong.

faqs.question: What is the Theory of Knowledge exhibition, and why does it matter here?
faqs.answer: It is one of the two assessed Theory of Knowledge components: three objects presented against a prompt, alongside the essay on a prescribed title. It replaced an earlier presentation format, which makes it one of the easiest stale-syllabus errors for a parent to detect without any subject knowledge - ask a tutor what the non-essay Theory of Knowledge component is. Exhibition is current; presentation is not. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together contribute up to 3 points through a published matrix.

faqs.question: My child had a tutor last year and it did not help. Why might that be?
faqs.answer: The most common explanation we see is not teaching quality but alignment. A tutor working from a superseded guide imposes their own teaching sequence, which no longer matches the school's reorganised content order, so the student is taught next term's material while this term's assessment goes unprepared. The second most common is that the hours went to a component already closed, or to the wrong component entirely. A two or three session diagnostic, read against the current criteria, usually identifies which happened.

faqs.question: Does the same currency problem apply to IGCSE tutors?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is easier to check. Cambridge and Pearson revise syllabuses too - Cambridge Mathematics 0580 now sets a non-calculator paper worth half the grade, which a tutor working from older practice will not have prepared a student for. The advantage is that syllabus codes and first-examination years are published and searchable, and the code is printed on the exam entry. So the verification is the same conversation with a firmer evidence base behind it.

faqs.question: Are there IB subjects where currency is not a concern?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth saying so rather than treating every tutor as suspect. History, for example, has had a comparatively stable structure, so a tutor with experience from several years ago is likely to be working from substantially the same assessment architecture. The risk is not uniform across subjects. That is precisely why the first step is asking the coordinator for the guide version and first-assessment year per subject - it tells you where to be careful and where to relax.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the scientific investigation under the current guide?
faqs.answer: Within a clear boundary, yes. A tutor can interrogate the research question, ask whether the dependent variable can be measured precisely enough against the instrument's resolution, teach uncertainty propagation and graph technique, explain what each of the four criteria rewards, and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor cannot design the experiment, collect or process the data, or write any part of the report. We put that boundary in writing before any investigation work begins, because the consequence of crossing it falls on the student.

faqs.question: How can I verify a tutor is legally allowed to teach privately in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Ask directly - add it to the currency questions, since it is the easiest one to check. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. The permit costs nothing, so there is no excuse for not holding one.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-oud-metha.closingBody: The worry behind the search is legitimate: several IB subject guides have been rewritten, and a tutor working from the previous version teaches a structure that has moved. Two steps settle it. Email your child's IB coordinator for the guide version, first-assessment year and internally assessed component for each subject. Then put the four currency questions on this page to any prospective tutor, us included - a current one passes in two minutes. After that, take the free trial lesson: one hour, no cost, with the tutor you would continue with, spent on a marked script or a live draft read against the current criteria. All lessons for Oud Metha families are one-to-one over live video, and we do not send tutors to UAE addresses.

intro.heading: The question behind the search, answered plainly
paragraphs: Palm Jumeirah is a residential island with no IB secondary campus of its own. Every Diploma student living on the trunk, the fronds or the Crescent commutes off the island each morning, most often to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, Umm Suqeim or Jumeirah. That single geographic fact shapes the tutoring problem. A family looking for help in Physics HL or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL is not choosing from everyone who teaches that subject in Dubai. They are choosing from the much smaller group willing to cross the trunk, find parking on a frond, and be back out again before the evening traffic on Al Sufouh Road builds up.

The honest answer to "is there an IB home tutor in Palm Jumeirah who knows this syllabus" is that there are certainly tutors who will travel to the island, and that the subset of them who have taught your child's exact course at your child's exact level is small. The deeper you go into the Diploma, the smaller it gets. Plenty of tutors in Dubai teach secondary mathematics. Far fewer have marked a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL Paper 3 or supervised a Chemistry HL internal assessment through to submission. Proximity filters on the wrong variable.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home tutoring in a family's own house is a service we run in India only. For Palm Jumeirah the delivery is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen for working through papers and a recording of the whiteboard where the tutor allows it. We state that first rather than at the bottom of a form, because it is the whole reason we can offer a Diploma specialist rather than a nearby generalist.

What that trade looks like in practice: a Crescent family whose daughter needs Economics HL support is matched on the strength of the tutor's Paper 3 and internal assessment experience, not on whether the tutor lives a twenty-minute drive away. The session starts at the time you choose and ends when it ends, with no travel charge attached to either side of it. Nobody is sitting in a car on the Palm trunk at 6pm, and the hour you pay for is an hour of teaching.

The rest of this page is written for the test you are actually trying to run. It sets out how to check a tutor's syllabus knowledge in a single conversation, what the Dubai market charges by provider model with sources and dates, who is legally permitted to tutor in the UAE and how you can verify it, what a non-specialist typically gets wrong in each Diploma subject group, and where the academic-honesty line sits on an internal assessment or extended essay. Where we cannot cover a subject with a UAE-based tutor, the page says so and says what happens instead.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.programmesIntro: Palm Jumeirah students sit in schools licensed by KHDA to run their own curricula, so the programme a child is in matters more than the emirate. These are the IB stages we teach to island families, with what each one demands of a student commuting off the Palm every day.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the extended essay and creativity, activity, service. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked against published criteria and moderated externally. Final grades run 1 to 7 per subject with up to three points available from the Theory of Knowledge and extended essay combination. The load is cumulative rather than modular, which is why a gap opened in the first term of Year 12 is still costing marks in the second term of Year 13.
programmes.countryNote: For a Palm Jumeirah student the binding constraint is the calendar, not the content. Internal assessment deadlines in several Dubai schools cluster in the same six-week window, and that window overlaps the extended essay's final submission. Students who commute off the island arrive home late, so the realistic tutoring slot sits between 5pm and 8pm on weekdays. We plan around that rather than pretending a 4pm start works.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked 0 to 8 and reported on a 1 to 7 scale. The criteria reward process: investigating, communicating, thinking critically, applying skills in unfamiliar situations. Students who have been rewarded for presentation and effort through the Middle Years can be surprised by the Diploma's narrower, more technical marking, which is the single most common reason a strong Year 11 report is followed by a shaky Year 12 one.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Palm Jumeirah families run the Middle Years Programme to Year 11 and then split into the Diploma or a Cambridge route. The bridging year is where island families usually first look for a tutor, often because the maths and sciences suddenly require fluency that criterion-based feedback did not test directly. Diagnostic work before Year 12 begins is cheaper in both money and stress than remedial work in the exam year.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: An inquiry-led primary framework organised around transdisciplinary themes rather than separate subject syllabuses, with no external examinations. Reporting is against learning outcomes and the approaches to learning skills. The useful tutoring work at this stage is narrow and mechanical: number bonds, written methods, reading fluency and the stamina to write at length, all of which are assumed rather than taught once a student reaches the Middle Years Programme.
programmes.countryNote: Primary families on the Palm often use a short block of weekly sessions to close one specific gap before a transfer, because the island's households move schools more often than the Dubai average when leases and job postings change. Online delivery suits this age group in 30 to 40 minute sessions rather than full hours, and we say so rather than selling the longer slot.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Palm Jumeirah families ask for most, with what each one actually assesses and where marks go missing. A tutor who cannot describe the paper structure of the subject they claim to teach is the first filter you should apply.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries this course. Higher Level adds a third paper that mixes extended problem solving across topics, so students who have drilled topic-by-topic are exposed when a question needs proof technique and calculus in the same answer. Marks go missing on notation, unjustified steps and calculator work shown without method.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use dominate. The common failure is treating it as the easier maths: Higher Level Applications includes substantial statistical inference and graph theory that punishes a student who chose the course to avoid proof. Interpretation marks need sentences about context, not just correct numbers.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium are where Higher Level separates from Standard. The internal assessment is a single scientific investigation, and most of its lost marks sit in the analysis and evaluation criteria rather than in the practical work itself. Data processing with uncertainties is the most teachable high-value skill.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Students lose marks less on the physics than on the explanation: unit errors, unstated assumptions and answers that describe rather than derive. Higher Level content in fields and induction rewards consistent sign conventions. Paper work improves fastest when a student practises writing the argument, not just reaching the number.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The volume of terminology makes this course feel like memorisation, but command terms decide the mark. A question asking a student to evaluate wants a judgement; one asking to outline does not want an essay. Higher Level demands more linking across topics, especially between physiology and biochemistry.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and definitional precision carry early marks; the extended responses need evaluation with real reference points. Higher Level adds quantitative work and a further paper. The internal assessment commentaries fail most often on weak linking between the chosen article and the specific syllabus concept being applied.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper one guided analysis are the two components students most often approach without a method. Marks come from close reading of how a text works, not from what it is about. Higher Level adds an essay on works studied, which needs an argument sustained across a long piece of writing.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools are easy to name and hard to apply. The marks sit in choosing the right framework for the stimulus and then using the case material, rather than reciting the framework. Higher Level extensions and the case study release reward students who practise under timed conditions with the published assessment criteria beside them.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, worth points alongside the extended essay. Students treat it as a general discussion subject and then write an essay with no knowledge question driving it. Support here is structural: choosing a title you can argue, finding real examples, and keeping the claims testable.

subjects.name: Extended essay supervision support
subjects.description: A four-thousand word independent piece in a chosen subject, supervised at school and marked against published criteria. The common collapse is a research question too broad to answer in the word limit. Tutoring here is process coaching and feedback on the student's own drafts, never production of the text.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.regionsTitle: Where the island's students go to school, and what that does to the evening
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.regionsIntro: Palm Jumeirah sends its students off the island every morning. These are the neighbourhoods the school run actually reaches, and what each one implies for when a session can realistically start.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: The first mainland district past the trunk and the closest cluster of large campuses. A frond-to-Al Sufouh run is short in distance and unpredictable in time, so afternoon finishes land home anywhere between 3.30pm and 4.45pm depending on the bus route.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor search on Palm Jumeirah is really asking
paragraphs: A parent typing "IB home tutor in Palm Jumeirah" into Google is usually three weeks into a problem. A report has come home, or a mock has been marked, or a teacher has used the phrase "not on track". The search is for proximity because proximity feels like the solvable part. What the parent actually needs is somebody who has taught the exact course, at the exact level, and can tell within one session whether the issue is content, technique or confidence.

Those two things pull in opposite directions on an island. Palm Jumeirah has roughly eighty thousand residents on a single connected landmass with one road on and off the trunk. A tutor who comes to the house is accepting a round trip that can swallow an hour of their evening, which means they will do it for a limited number of families, at a limited number of times, and will price the travel in. Every constraint they accept narrows the pool further. The subject-specialist filter is the first one to be dropped, because it is the one the parent cannot easily check.

So the page you are reading answers the question in its honest form. There are tutors who will travel to the Palm. The specialist you want for Physics HL in an exam year may well not be among them. IB Gram's answer is to drop the geography constraint entirely: the tutor is matched on subject, level and assessment experience, and teaches your child one-to-one over live video at a time that fits the commute off the island. That is a real trade, not a workaround, and the next section is about how to test whether it is paying off.

sections.heading: How to tell in twenty minutes whether a tutor knows the syllabus
paragraphs: You do not need to know the subject to test whether somebody teaches it. You need four questions whose answers are specific, checkable and impossible to bluff. Ask them in the trial lesson, in front of your child, and listen for whether the answer names things or describes feelings about things.

First: what are the assessment components in this course at this level, and what is each one worth? A specialist answers in a sentence with numbers in it. Second: what is the internal assessment in this subject and which criterion carries the most marks? A specialist names the criteria by letter and says where students lose them. Third: what are the command terms in the last paper you worked through, and what does each one require? A generalist talks about exam technique in general; a specialist tells you that "evaluate" needs a judgement and "outline" does not need a paragraph. Fourth: show the tutor one marked piece of your child's work and ask what the next ten marks are. A specialist points at a page.

The reason this matters more on Palm Jumeirah than in a city centre is supply. When a family is choosing among whoever is willing to drive onto a frond at 5.30pm, the temptation is to accept a confident generalist because the alternative is nobody. Asking these four questions costs nothing and removes the guesswork. It is also exactly what the free trial lesson exists for, and why we would rather you spent it interrogating the tutor than watching a sales presentation.
bullets: Ask for component weightings; expect numbers, not adjectives

sections.heading: Subject coverage from the island, and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: Every tutoring service has coverage limits. Almost none publish them. The table below sets out what a Palm Jumeirah family can realistically expect by subject and level, how quickly a match usually happens, and what we do when no UAE-based specialist has a free slot at the time you need. We would rather lose a booking to this table than take one and then substitute a generalist.

Two patterns repeat. Higher Level sciences and Higher Level mathematics in the exam term are the hardest slots to fill, because the same small group of specialists is in demand across Dubai at the same six-week point in the year. Group 2 languages at Higher Level and the less commonly taken group 3 subjects are harder again, because the pool is small in absolute terms rather than merely busy.

Where no UAE-based tutor covers a subject, we say so and offer a specialist based elsewhere who teaches the same syllabus on Gulf Standard Time. That is a disclosure, not a bait and switch: the tutor is named, the location is stated, and the time zone the lessons are held in is yours. If neither option works, we tell you to look elsewhere. A family that books in the dark and discovers the gap in week three has lost three weeks it did not have. The one thing that reliably widens your options is offering two possible evening slots rather than one, because the overlap between your week and a specialist's is what the match actually turns on, far more than the subject itself.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, and who published each figure
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for this kind of search publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars. That is unhelpful to a family budgeting in dirhams. The figures below were read from the providers' own public pages in October 2026 and are attributed to whoever published them. They describe the market, not an IB Gram price list: our own model starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and we quote per student after the diagnostic rather than from a rate card.

The range is wide for a reason. At the bottend sit platforms using university students for school-level work, which can be the right answer for a Year 8 numeracy gap and the wrong one for Physics HL eight weeks from a mock. At the top sit named premium tutors charging several times that. In between is the band most Diploma families actually transact in, and the single largest variable inside it is whether anybody is being paid to travel.

Two practical notes on reading the table. First, an in-home rate is not comparable to an online rate at the same number, because the in-home figure includes a journey and often a minimum of two hours. Second, a monthly package price only makes sense next to the number of sessions it contains: a provider advertising a monthly figure for eight online sessions and a competitor advertising a higher monthly figure for four in-home sessions are selling very different amounts of teaching.

sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE, and how would you know?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the ministry's own service page for it is "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days. Individuals who offer private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts is published, so no figure should be quoted to you by anybody.

The eligible categories are broader than most parents expect. They include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. That last category is why a confident sixteen-year-old offering IGCSE maths help on a community noticeboard may be entirely within the rules, and also why the permit alone tells you nothing about teaching quality.

A separate thing entirely is an operation with premises and staff. A tuition centre in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which runs through initial approval, a maximum six-month window to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold that permit, does not operate premises in the UAE, and is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge. Any service telling you otherwise is making a claim you should ask it to evidence with a permit number.

sections.heading: What a non-specialist gets wrong, subject group by subject group
paragraphs: The case for specialism is usually made with adjectives. Here it is made with failure modes. In group 4 sciences, a competent generalist teaches the content correctly and then lets a student write up an investigation that scores poorly, because the marks in that component sit in analysis and evaluation rather than in the practical itself. Uncertainties, anomalies and the limitations paragraph are learned behaviours, and a tutor who has not marked against those criteria does not know to drill them.

In group 5 mathematics, the gap shows up in the exploration and in the Higher Level third paper. A generalist can teach differentiation. Fewer can look at a student's chosen exploration topic in week two and say, accurately, that it will not generate enough mathematics to reach the top band of one criterion and that changing it now costs an afternoon rather than a grade. In group 3, economics and business responses lose marks on evaluation and on the use of the stimulus material, not on the diagrams, which is the opposite of where most tutoring time goes.

In group 1 and group 2, the individual oral and the guided analysis are the components students most often meet unprepared, because they are the least like anything in the Middle Years Programme. A specialist knows the structure of the assessment and can rehearse it. A generalist improves the student's general English, which is worth having and will not move that mark. None of this is an argument that generalists are bad teachers. It is an argument that the filter you apply first should be the subject and the level, and geography should come a distant second.

sections.heading: The academic-honesty line, stated so your child is not the test case
paragraphs: This matters more on a Diploma page than anywhere else, because the internet is full of services offering to supply assessed work. There are operators in this market selling finished internal assessments for four-figure sums. A student who submits one is exposed to a malpractice finding, and a malpractice finding in the Diploma is not a telling-off.

The boundary is not vague. A tutor may teach the content, explain the published criteria, discuss method, question a research question, point at a paragraph and say it does not do what the criterion asks, mark a draft against the descriptors and set up practice under timed conditions. The student generates every word, every data set and every line of code that is submitted. If a tutor offers to supply text, restructure a draft into final form, or hand over a worked example that is indistinguishable from the submission, that is the moment to end the engagement, not negotiate it.

We also do not supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those are the boards' copyright material. We reference them, cite the official source, and link to it, and we work from the papers the school has legitimately given the student. On Palm Jumeirah specifically, where several families use the same small set of schools, there is a second reason for care: a tutor working with two students in the same class at the same school has an obligation not to move work between them, and we ask about that at the matching stage.

sections.heading: Starting from Palm Jumeirah, with the limits stated up front
paragraphs: The first step is a short conversation about the subject, the level, the school and what the last marked assessment said. That is enough to know whether the problem is a content gap, an exam-technique gap or a workload-management gap, and those three need different tutors. We ask for the school's name because the scheme of work and the internal deadlines differ, and a session that ignores them is a session spent on the wrong topic.

The second step is a free trial lesson with the proposed specialist. Use it to run the four questions above. If the match is wrong, say so and we change the tutor rather than asking you to persist; a mismatched match is a sunk cost, not a commitment. If the match is right, you choose a fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, which for most island families means something between 5pm and 8pm on a weekday, or a Saturday morning when the week has been heavy.

The honest caveats. In the weeks before the May session, Higher Level science and mathematics slots are the scarcest thing we have, and a family that waits until April is choosing from what is left rather than from everyone. During Ramadan, we move sessions later and shorten them where families prefer, and many island households switch to post-Iftar timing for the month. And if no UAE-based specialist covers the subject at the time you need, you will be told before you pay, with a named alternative and their location, or told to look elsewhere.
