faqs.question: Is there an IB home tutor in Palm Jumeirah who really knows the Diploma syllabus?
faqs.answer: There are tutors who will travel onto the island, and the subset who have taught your child's exact course at your child's exact level is small. The deeper into the Diploma you go, the smaller it becomes. Plenty of people in Dubai teach secondary maths; far fewer have supervised a Higher Level exploration or marked a Paper 3. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE homes at all. We match on subject, level and assessment experience and teach one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which is how a Palm Jumeirah family reaches a specialist rather than a neighbour.

faqs.question: How can I test whether a tutor actually knows my child's IB subject?
faqs.answer: Ask four questions in the trial lesson. What are the assessment components at this level and what is each worth? What is the internal assessment in this subject and which criterion carries the most marks? What do three command terms from the last paper actually require? And, holding one marked piece of your child's work, where are the next ten marks? A specialist answers with numbers, criterion letters and a finger on the page. A generalist talks about confidence and exam technique in general terms. The difference is audible within twenty minutes and costs you nothing to find out.

faqs.question: Why is a Higher Level specialist harder to find than a general maths tutor?
faqs.answer: Because the pool shrinks at every filter. Secondary maths teachers in Dubai are numerous. Those who have taught Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level are fewer. Those who have taken a cohort through the exploration and the third paper are fewer still, and in the term before the May session they are all busy at the same hours. Add a requirement to drive onto a Palm Jumeirah frond at 5.30pm and the list can reach zero. Removing the travel requirement is what puts the specialist back on the list.

faqs.question: Is a permit required before anybody can charge us for private lessons?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, free of charge for two years. Individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts is published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted as unverified. Eligible applicants include school and government employees, private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask to see the permit before the first paid session.

faqs.question: What if nobody in the UAE teaches the exact course my child sits?
faqs.answer: You are told before you pay. The coverage table on this page names where availability is tight: Higher Level sciences and Higher Level mathematics in the exam term, and the less commonly taken group 2 and group 3 courses year-round. Where no UAE-based specialist has a free slot at your times, we name a specialist based elsewhere who teaches the same syllabus and holds sessions in Gulf Standard Time, and we state where they are. If neither works, we say we cannot cover it. A family that finds this out in week three has lost three weeks.

faqs.question: Can a teacher from my child's own school tutor them in the evening?
faqs.answer: Be careful here. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat that as press-reported and check the current policy document before relying on it. The practical point for a Dubai family is that "your child's own teacher, privately" is not a service we market or arrange, and a tutor who offers it is worth questioning rather than hiring.

faqs.question: How quickly can a Palm Jumeirah student start sessions?
faqs.answer: Two to four days for most Middle Years subjects and Standard Level Diploma courses, three to seven days for Higher Level sciences and Higher Level mathematics, and a week or more for less commonly taken courses. The free trial lesson sits inside that window rather than after it. The constraint is rarely the matching and almost always the overlap between your available evening slots and a specialist's, which is why families who can offer two possible times start sooner than families fixed on one.

faqs.question: What does the Dubai market charge for an IB specialist per hour?
faqs.answer: Published rates read in October 2026 run from AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik for budget online platforms, from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB at Unitors, AED 270 at TutorChase, AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists in the Bestimate Dubai guide, and AED 650 at BartyED at the premium end. In-home visits sit around AED 180 to 350 in that guide and up to AED 500 in listings, because the hour includes a journey. None of these are IB Gram prices; ours follow a free trial and a diagnostic.

faqs.question: Will a tutor drive onto the fronds for an early evening session?
faqs.answer: Some independent tutors in Dubai will, and they price the round trip into the hour or set a two-hour minimum. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service for us, and we would rather state it than let you assume otherwise. For Palm Jumeirah, lessons run one-to-one over live video with a shared screen, scheduled at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot. Nobody is in a car on the trunk at 6pm, and the hour you pay for is an hour of teaching rather than forty minutes of it.

faqs.question: Which instruction words in an IB question decide the mark?
faqs.answer: Command terms are the instruction verbs in an exam question: outline, describe, explain, analyse, evaluate, justify. Each one defines how much is wanted and what kind of answer earns the marks. A student who writes a careful paragraph for a question asking them to state has spent time for nothing; one who gives a single sentence where a judgement was wanted has left marks behind. Most students lose more to this than to missing content, and it is among the fastest things to fix, which is why a specialist tests for it in the first session.

faqs.question: Is a general tutor ever the better choice for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, yes. If the gap is foundational arithmetic, written fluency or study organisation, a strong generalist can close it and will usually cost less. If the gap is in an assessed component, a Higher Level topic or exam technique for a specific paper, a generalist improves the subject in general and leaves the mark where it was. The question to ask is whether the problem is below the course or inside it. A diagnostic block of two or three sessions answers that before you commit to a term of anything.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a struggling Diploma student need?
faqs.answer: Most families start with one session a week on one subject, which is enough when the gap is diagnosed and the student does the work between sessions. Two subjects at once usually means two separate slots rather than a longer single one, because attention does not stretch. Short blocks of two or three sessions a week make sense around one assessed component or a mock, then drop back. More hours do not substitute for independent practice, and a tutor who recommends four sessions a week in the first conversation has not diagnosed anything yet.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with an internal assessment, and what is off limits?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the content, explain the published criteria letter by letter, question the research question, discuss method, mark a draft against the descriptors and say plainly that a paragraph does not meet the criterion it is aimed at. Off limits is supplying text, restructuring a draft into its final form, providing data, or handing over a worked example close enough to be submitted. The student generates everything that is handed in. Services selling finished coursework exist in this market and a student who uses one risks a malpractice finding, which is a far worse outcome than a low mark.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need to teach at a Dubai school to be useful?
faqs.answer: No, and it is a weaker signal than it sounds. What matters is whether the tutor knows the course your child sits and the way it is assessed: the components, the weightings, the criteria and the papers. A teacher at a Dubai school may know your child's school's internal deadlines, which helps, but a specialist who asks for the scheme of work and the assessment calendar gets the same information in one conversation. Ask about subject and level experience first, and about local school knowledge second.

faqs.question: How do I check a claim that a tutor is an examiner?
faqs.answer: Ask which board, which subject, which component and which years, then ask for something that evidences it. Examiner status is not a general badge; it is specific and time-limited. It also does not give anybody access to unreleased papers, mark schemes or grade boundaries, and a tutor who implies otherwise is telling you something that should worry you rather than reassure you. IB Gram does not describe tutors as IB or Cambridge examiners unless the current status can be evidenced, and the useful question is always what the tutor has taught and marked.

intro.heading: Think in months, not hours, when budgeting IB support in Pearl Jumeira
paragraphs: Almost every page competing for this search quotes an hourly rate, and an hourly rate is the least useful number a parent can hold. Diploma tutoring is not bought by the hour. It is bought for a term, or for the two years of the programme, and the figure that matters is what leaves the account each month. The published monthly packages in Dubai make the comparison unusually clear: roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four in-home sessions of two hours each. Same monthly spend, two very different weeks.

Translated into a Diploma year, those figures become decisions. A family paying the lower monthly figure across the two years of the programme is spending in the region of AED 16,000 to AED 19,000 if they run through the holidays, or closer to AED 14,000 on a school-term basis. The in-home figure roughly doubles that, for half as many contact points. Neither is a small sum, and both are worth planning deliberately rather than accumulating session by session. Families who never set the figure in advance tend to arrive at a larger one by accident, because each individual booking looks reasonable on its own.

What complicates the arithmetic in Pearl Jumeira specifically is the island. The community sits on reclaimed land off the Jumeirah 1 shoreline with a single causeway serving it, which means every in-home booking carries a travel cost that is not an average Dubai travel cost. A tutor coming from Al Barsha, Business Bay or Mirdif joins the Jumeirah Beach Road traffic and then joins one queue onto the island. In the late afternoon that is a predictable thirty to fifty minutes each way, and it is priced into the hourly figure whether or not anybody itemises it.

There is a second cost that nobody quotes, which is the value of a session that does not happen. Across a two-year Diploma, in-home bookings lost or shortened to traffic are a recurring line. Most families absorb a handful without noticing. In the term when the internal assessments are due and the mocks are sat, a missed session is not neutral, because the sequence of work matters more then than at any other point in the programme.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The honest case for that is the one this page makes with numbers rather than adjectives: the same monthly budget buys roughly twice the contact, the hour billed is the hour taught, and the tutor can be chosen for having taught the subject at Higher Level rather than for living within reach of the causeway.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-pearl-jumeira.subjectsIntro: A Diploma student takes six subjects and a tutoring budget cannot cover six. These are the subjects Pearl Jumeira families most often fund, with a realistic sense of how many monthly hours each tends to absorb.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most funded subject in this community and the one that most often needs the whole of a weekly hour. Higher Level adds a third paper and the proof-style reasoning that students find hardest to self-teach, which is why it rarely compresses into a shared slot.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Lighter on abstraction and heavier on modelling, statistics and technology use. Students often need less of a tutor's time here but need it at specific points, particularly around the statistical content and the exploration.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Absorbs budget unevenly: manageable in the first year, then demanding in the term when the fields content and the investigation arrive together. Families who plan for a second hour in that term spend the same as those who panic, with a better result.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The subject with the strongest case for two shorter sessions rather than one long one, because the quantitative half and the organic half need different kinds of practice. In-home pricing pushes families the other way, towards one long visit.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and recall-dependent, which means it rewards frequent short contact over occasional long sessions. The least well served subject by a monthly package built around four two-hour visits.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation are where the marks sit, and both are teachable quickly. Often needs a short block rather than a standing weekly hour, which makes it a good candidate for a term of support rather than two years.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the written assessments reward structure and close reading. A student who writes well generally needs occasional feedback rather than weekly teaching, and over-funding this subject is a common pattern here.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-based and command-term sensitive. Students lose marks by writing knowledge where the question asks for evaluation, which is a bounded problem that responds to a handful of sessions rather than a standing booking.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Argument construction and source evaluation carry the grade. Needs feedback on written work more than it needs explanation, so the useful arrangement is fewer, longer gaps between sessions with real writing in between.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and internal assessments
subjects.description: The components that eat a budget quietly, because each needs blocks rather than hours. A tutor teaches the criteria and gives feedback on the student's own drafts; no part of any of them may be written for the student.

sections.heading: The monthly numbers, and what each package actually delivers
paragraphs: Set the hourly rates aside for a moment and look at what the market charges per month, because that is the unit a Diploma family commits to. Published monthly packages in Dubai cluster into a small number of shapes, and the table sets them out with the figures as published and read in October 2026. None of these is an IB Gram price list.

The headline comparison is the one worth sitting with. Around AED 799 a month buys eight online sessions. AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month buys four in-home sessions of two hours each. The total contact time is similar; the number of occasions is not. For a Diploma student, occasions matter more than minutes, because the work that produces progress happens between sessions and each session is the point at which it gets marked and corrected. Four occasions a month gives a student one chance a week at best to have work looked at. Eight gives two.

The second thing the table shows is how quickly the figures scale. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. A family funding two subjects at the specialist end for the second Diploma year is looking at a materially different number from a family funding one subject from the start of Year 12, and the second arrangement usually produces the better result.

What none of these figures contains is the cost of the sessions that do not happen. That is the line a monthly package conceals and an island community feels most acutely, and it is dealt with in its own section below.

sections.heading: What the Pearl Jumeira travel premium actually buys
paragraphs: In-home tutoring in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common range at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to AED 500. Those figures are real and they are not inflated by anybody acting in bad faith. A tutor who spends ninety minutes driving in order to teach for sixty has to price the ninety minutes somewhere.

On this island the geography sharpens it. Pearl Jumeira is reached by one causeway from the Jumeirah 1 shoreline. A tutor arriving from Al Barsha, Business Bay or further east joins Jumeirah Beach Road or Al Wasl Road at the end of the school day and then joins a single queue onto the island. Thirty to fifty minutes each way is a reasonable late-afternoon expectation, and the return trip is often worse. That is the premium, itemised.

The question is what a family receives in exchange for it, and the honest answer is: a person in the room, and a smaller choice of person. Requiring somebody to physically reach this island at a fixed hour on a fixed weekday narrows the available set to those who live close enough, are free then, and are willing to make the trip. Narrow it further by requiring that they have taught Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or marked the chemistry investigation criteria, and the set can empty entirely. What frequently happens next is that a capable general tutor is engaged at a specialist price.

That trade is worth making for some families and not for others, and nobody should pretend otherwise. What should not happen is making it without seeing it. The premium is not a quality signal; it is a distance signal, and the two are routinely confused in this market because nothing on a competitor's page separates them.

paragraphs: This is the comparison the whole page turns on, so it is worth making concrete rather than rhetorical. The table sets the two formats against the things that differ for a family living on reclaimed land with one road in.

Two rows deserve particular attention. The first is sessions lost or cut short. Across a two-year Diploma this is not a rounding error for an in-home arrangement on this island, and the losses cluster in exactly the wrong term: the one when internal assessments are due, mocks are sat and the heaviest content is taught. A missed session in the first Diploma term is inconvenient. A missed session in the week a draft is due is expensive in a way no refund covers.

The second is the ability to add a second subject for a single term. The heavy-term arrangement described earlier depends on being able to add an hour for twelve weeks and then stop. With a visiting tutor that means finding a second person willing to make the same journey, at the same hour, for one term only, which in practice is why families either over-commit for two years or do without.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. sections.heading: The four lines of an IB tutoring bill that do nothing
paragraphs: Overspending on Diploma support in this community is rarely a matter of paying too much per hour. It is a matter of buying the wrong things, and the same four appear repeatedly.

The first is the two-hour block. It exists because a tutor who has driven across the city and onto the island needs the trip to be worth making. It does not exist because a sixteen-year-old does productive quantitative work for 120 consecutive minutes. Attention on technical material degrades well before that, and the second half of a long session routinely becomes supervised homework at a teaching rate. Two shorter occasions, with work attempted in between, teach more and cost the same.

The second is funding subjects the student is already fine in. Six Diploma subjects create six anxieties, and it is tempting to cover the lot. A student scoring well in English A and funded weekly in it is paying for reassurance. The test is simple and it is the marked work: if the lost marks in a subject are not concentrated anywhere, there is nothing for a tutor to target, and the money belongs in the subject where they are.

The third is starting in Year 13. The first Diploma year is the cheap year, when content is lighter, the mathematics is manageable and the internal assessments can be done properly. A family that funds one weekly hour from September of Year 12 spends less across the programme than one that funds two hours a week from January of Year 13, and ends up in a better position. The compressed version pays for urgency.

The fourth is buying hours where a diagnosis would do. A single paid session spent reading a marked mock script and producing a topic list with mark values attached frequently shows that the problem is narrower than it looked. That hour is the most useful one in the entire budget, and it is the one families almost never buy first.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost set against the rest of a Dubai school bill
paragraphs: Tutoring is one line in a larger education budget, and in Dubai that budget has recently been stable in a way worth planning against. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total.

The market around that decision continues to grow. Dubai had 387,441 students in 227 private schools in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, US at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, following six openings in 2025-26 and a 6 per cent rise in enrolment.

For a Pearl Jumeira family two things follow. First, a stable fee position means a tutoring budget can be set for two years rather than revised annually, which favours the steady weekly arrangement over reactive block-buying. Second, the Diploma remains a minority curriculum at 7 per cent of enrolment, which means the supply of tutors who have actually taught Higher Level subjects is proportionally thinner than the supply of tutors generally, while the rates quoted for both look similar. Price, in this market, does not reliably signal subject depth.

That is the practical reason to interrogate experience rather than rate. Ask which Higher Level subjects a tutor has taught, which internal assessment criteria they have marked against, and how many Diploma cohorts they have taken through. None of those questions costs anything, and the answers separate the two groups that the price does not.

sections.heading: Verifying who you are paying, before the first monthly invoice
paragraphs: A monthly commitment deserves one round of checks, and in the UAE those checks are short and free. Private tutoring is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and it is granted free of charge for two years.

Eligibility is wider than families expect, which is why a missing permit is a choice rather than an obstacle. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fees stated and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule has been published, any specific figure quoted to you should be treated with caution.

Two related facts are worth knowing. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai is legally distinct from an individual tutor and requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, a restriction echoed by the MoHRE permit's code of conduct.

The parent's version is two questions, asked before any monthly arrangement begins: does this person hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and is my child enrolled at the school where they teach? Neither is an awkward question and neither costs anything.

sections.heading: What the money may not buy: internal assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
paragraphs: The components that most tempt a budget are the ones where spending is most tightly constrained, and this needs stating plainly on a page about cost. Every Diploma subject carries an internal assessment with a fixed share of the grade. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge sit alongside them. All of it must be the student's own work.

What a tutor may legitimately be paid for is substantial and worth buying. Explaining what each assessment criterion rewards and what the mark allocations are. Teaching the subject content the student has chosen to work with. Showing how a calculation or an argument is structured. Asking the questions that narrow an unmanageable research question into one that can actually be answered. Reading a draft the student has written and saying what is missing from it. For most students this is the highest-value tutoring in the programme, because the criteria are published and the failures are predictable.

What may not be paid for, here or anywhere, is production. No part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay will be written, drafted, redrafted or supplied, and no research question will be handed over for adoption. At least one operator ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Submitting purchased work is a malpractice risk that falls on the student rather than on the seller, and the consequence sits on a transcript rather than on an invoice.

A related point about materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to the IB and to the examination boards. A tutor references and links them; a tutor who arrives offering a folder of copied material has disclosed their standards before teaching anything. Neither of these limits is a marketing position. They are the reason the honest version of assessment support takes longer and is the only version on offer.

faqs.answer: Published Dubai packages give the clearest answer. In-home arrangements are commonly quoted at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. Online packages appear at around AED 799 a month for eight sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are market figures from the named providers, read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Why are tutoring quotes higher for Pearl Jumeira than for Jumeirah 2?
faqs.answer: Because of the causeway, not the teaching. The island is reached by one access road from the Jumeirah 1 shoreline, so a tutor coming from Al Barsha or Business Bay joins the coastal traffic and then joins a single queue onto the island. Thirty to fifty minutes each way is a reasonable late-afternoon expectation, and that unpaid time is priced into the hourly figure. Identical tutoring quoted a few streets inland is often cheaper for reasons that have nothing to do with subject knowledge.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to a Pearl Jumeira villa?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, because in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen-shared papers, annotated working that is kept after the session, and recordings available. This page states that near the top rather than at the end of a call, because a monthly commitment should not start with a surprise about how lessons are delivered.

faqs.question: Is a two-hour session once a week better value than two single hours?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the pricing reflects travel economics rather than teaching. A tutor who has driven across the city and onto the island needs the trip to be worth making, which is why monthly in-home packages are built around four long visits. Attention on technical Diploma material degrades well before 120 minutes, so the second half of a long session often becomes supervised homework at a teaching rate. Two shorter occasions, with work attempted in between, give the tutor something to mark.

faqs.question: How much should a family budget for the whole two-year Diploma?
faqs.answer: At the lower published monthly figure, one subject weekly across both years comes to roughly AED 14,000 on a term-time basis and closer to AED 16,000 to AED 19,000 if sessions run through the holidays. In-home arrangements at the published monthly rates roughly double that for half as many contact points. A specialist second subject added for one heavy term adds a few thousand. None of that is small, which is why the figure is better set in advance than accumulated session by session.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subject should a limited budget be spent on?
faqs.answer: The one where the marked work shows concentrated losses, which is usually not the one that feels hardest. Six subjects create six anxieties and a budget cannot cover six. The test is whether lost marks cluster anywhere: if they are spread thinly across a subject with no pattern, a tutor has nothing to target and the money belongs elsewhere. A single diagnostic hour on a marked mock script answers this better than any amount of discussion about which subject is hardest.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start Diploma tutoring in Year 12 or wait until Year 13?
faqs.answer: Starting in Year 12 is cheaper in total and more effective. The first Diploma year is the light year: content is more manageable, the mathematics has not yet compounded, and the internal assessments can be done properly rather than rescued. One weekly hour from September of Year 12 costs less across the programme than two weekly hours from January of Year 13, which is what families typically end up buying. The compressed version is paying for urgency rather than for teaching.

faqs.question: What is the single most useful hour to buy first?
faqs.answer: A diagnostic session on a marked mock or recent assessment, producing a topic list with approximate mark values attached. It is the hour families almost never buy first and the one that most often changes the plan, frequently by narrowing it. It converts a vague sense that a subject is going badly into a short list of specific, costed gaps, and that list is what makes the rest of the monthly budget a decision rather than a guess.

faqs.question: How many sessions get lost to traffic over a two-year in-home arrangement?
faqs.answer: Enough to matter, and nobody quotes it. For an island community served by one causeway, late-afternoon arrivals are unreliable in a predictable way, and across two Diploma years the cumulative loss of cancelled or shortened sessions is a real line in the cost. What makes it expensive is timing: losses cluster in the term when internal assessment drafts are due and mocks are sat, which is the point in the programme where the sequence of work matters most and a gap is hardest to recover.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Extended Essay or internal assessments?
faqs.answer: With the criteria, the content and feedback on drafts, yes, and that is where most of the value sits. A tutor explains what each criterion rewards and its mark allocation, teaches the subject material involved, and asks the questions that narrow an unmanageable research question into an answerable one. A tutor does not write, draft, redraft or supply any part of it, and will not hand over a research question. Submitting purchased work is a malpractice risk carried entirely by the student.

faqs.question: How do I tell a Higher Level specialist from a general tutor at the same rate?
faqs.answer: By asking, because the price will not tell you. The IB accounted for 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment in 2024-25, so the pool of tutors who have actually taught Higher Level subjects is proportionally thin while rates for general and specialist tutors look similar. Ask which Higher Level subjects they have taught, which internal assessment criteria they have marked against, and how many Diploma cohorts they have seen through. The answers separate the two groups quickly and cost nothing.

faqs.question: How do I check a tutor is permitted to teach privately in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Ask two questions before the first invoice. First, do they hold the MoHRE private tutor work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023? It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligibility covers school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, so lacking one is a choice. Second, is your child enrolled at the school where they teach, since the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school?

faqs.question: Are Dubai school fees rising, and should that change a tutoring budget?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. For a tutoring budget that stability is useful: it means a two-year figure can be set in advance rather than revised annually, which favours a steady weekly arrangement from the start of Year 12 over reactive block-buying in the second year.

faqs.question: Should an IB tutor be handing over copied IB subject guides and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: They should reference and link them rather than supply them. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to the IB and to the examination boards, and the proper route is the official site or the school's own licensed access. A tutor arriving with a folder of copied material has told you something about their standards before teaching anything. Working through a paper the student has legitimately obtained, marked against the published criteria, needs nothing copied.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-pearl-jumeira.closingHeading: Set the monthly number, buy the diagnostic hour, then commit
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-pearl-jumeira.closingBody: Three steps in that order will save a Pearl Jumeira family more than any amount of rate comparison. Decide what the household will commit per month across the Diploma, using the published package shapes as a reference point. Spend one hour on a diagnosis from marked work, which regularly narrows the plan rather than widening it. Then commit to one subject weekly from the start of Year 12, adding a second only for the term when assessments and mocks collide. Take the free trial lesson first, which is taught rather than pitched. Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-remraam.tutorsIntro: The profiles below name subject groups and levels rather than districts. A request for Economics HL commentary work reaches someone who has marked Economics commentaries, and the lesson reaches Al Ramth or Al Thamam over video either way.

intro.heading: Six subject groups, and the marks sit in different places in each
paragraphs: A Diploma result is six subject grades plus the core, and each of those six is assembled differently. The sciences put a fifth of the grade in an investigation and most of the rest in a response paper. Mathematics puts a fifth in an exploration and splits the rest across papers that test different skills. Languages put real weight on an oral. Individuals and societies subjects reward application to a named case rather than general knowledge. A plan that treats all six the same wastes most of its hours.

Remraam adds a particular constraint. It is a low-rise apartment community in Dubailand, built across the Al Thamam and Al Ramth clusters with its own park and retail, reached from Al Qudra Road and Emirates Road. South View School sits close by, which makes it one of the few communities in this belt where a secondary school is genuinely near. What Remraam does not have is a Diploma school on its doorstep, so sixth-form students travel further than their younger siblings.

That travel is why a subject-led approach matters more here than a proximity-led one. A tutor who can reach an Al Ramth apartment within twenty minutes is drawn from the pool living around Dubai Sports City, Motor City and Dubai Investment Park, and that pool is made of generalists covering several subjects at two levels. For Standard Level support that is often adequate. For Chemistry at Higher Level, or an Economics commentary three weeks from a deadline, it usually is not.

The subject detail is also what a parent can check. Asking a tutor which option their school teaches, which papers they have marked, or what a particular criterion rewards produces answers you can verify against the school. Asking whether they are experienced produces a sentence. Half of this page exists so that a Remraam family has the first kind of question available to them before any money moves.

One more thing is worth saying before the subject detail starts. A Diploma is a long game with a small number of decision points, and almost all of them arrive before a family feels any urgency. Subject and level combinations are fixed in Year 11. Internal assessment topics are approved early in Year 12. The Extended Essay question is settled before the writing. A family that understands the subject structure early makes those decisions well and often needs fewer tutoring hours afterwards, which is the opposite of how this market usually works.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time so a session can begin at a quarter past four for a student home early or after eight where both parents commute. Home visits are something IB Gram runs in India only, and no sentence here should be read as an offer to arrive at a Remraam address. The comparison table in the next section sets out what that trade actually buys.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-remraam.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes appear in requests from this part of Dubailand, and the subject work differs completely across them.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects spread across the groups, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. External papers carry most of each subject grade and every subject has an internally assessed component. Higher Level usually means extra content and, in several subjects, an additional paper.
programmes.countryNote: Remraam Diploma students travel outward, most often towards Dubai Hills, Al Barsha South or The Sustainable City. The practical result is a compressed evening, which argues for sessions built on timed questions rather than on content delivery that repeats the school day.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four published criteria each, marked out of eight and converted to a 1 to 7 grade. There is no compulsory external examination, so the criterion descriptors carry the entire assessment language of the programme.
programmes.countryNote: In Remraam the MYP is less common than IGCSE, so families asking about it have usually moved a child into a continuum school recently. The first reporting cycle is where most of the questions come from, and they are about vocabulary rather than about content.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: A Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay, plus a 4,000-word Extended Essay in a chosen subject. Both add points on top of the six subject grades, and both are routinely left until the point at which they are expensive to rescue.
programmes.countryNote: The Extended Essay subject choice deserves a session of its own long before any writing. Students in this belt often choose a subject they enjoy rather than one with accessible sources and a question answerable in 4,000 words, and that decision sets the ceiling.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-remraam.subjectsIntro: Below is subject detail rather than a list: what each component examines and the loss that recurs most often in marked work.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry through to organic mechanisms. Equations left unbalanced and state symbols omitted cost marks mechanically; arrows drawn from a positive centre make a mechanism wrong even when the product is right.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Extended responses need the assumption named, not implied. Gradients must be converted into the physical quantity the question asked for, and the Higher Level extension in fields and induction separates students with identical notes.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Data questions reward reading axes, units and scale before any biology is applied. Long answers reward sequence and named products, and the command term decides whether description or explanation earns credit.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is taken without a calculator, so fluency rather than understanding is tested there. The exploration credits presentation, engagement and reflection separately from the mathematics, which is where most marks are left.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics, with technology assumed. The reliable loss is finishing a correct calculation without the sentence that interprets the result in the context the question described.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries form the internal component, and article choice is part of the assessment. Diagrams earn marks when applied to the named market and almost none when described in the abstract.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Stimulus-based papers where frameworks score only against the named organisation. The Higher Level research project needs a question that primary research can actually answer within the constraints available.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis, a comparative essay, the Individual Oral on a chosen global issue with two extracts, and at Higher Level the HL Essay. Comparative answers that treat texts in sequence lose the comparison credit.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Reading, writing in specified text types, and the oral components. Distinct from the Arabic that KHDA requires all Dubai private schools to teach, which sits beside the Diploma rather than inside it.

sections.heading: What a home tutor search means from a Remraam apartment
paragraphs: Taken literally, the search is for someone to arrive at a flat in Al Thamam or Al Ramth at a usable hour. That service exists in Dubai and it is quoted accordingly: in-home one-to-one visits are advertised at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel folded into the price, Bestimate's range being AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors publishing AED 200 to 500. Nobody itemises the drive; it simply sits inside the rate.

What a Remraam family is really choosing between is a tutor selected by distance and a tutor selected by subject. Distance narrows the field to people living along this corridor, around Dubai Investment Park, Dubai Sports City and Motor City, and that field is mostly made of people who teach several subjects at IGCSE level with Diploma work as an extension. Subject selection removes the geographic filter entirely.

There is a scheduling dimension too, and for apartment families with two children at different schools it often decides the matter. A visiting tutor needs a fixed arrival window and cannot absorb a twenty-minute delay when a bus is late, because the next household is somewhere else. A video session begins when the student sits down, and a slot can shift by half an hour without renegotiating anything, including after Iftar during Ramadan.

IB Gram runs home visits in India only, so the honest answer to the literal search is no, with a comparison attached rather than a deflection. The table below sets the two formats side by side on the terms that matter from this community.

sections.heading: Group 4: how a Diploma science grade is assembled
paragraphs: The sciences share a structure, which makes them easy to plan once it is understood. Each subject has external papers plus an internally assessed investigation worth roughly a fifth of the grade, and the investigation is marked against criteria rather than against whether the experiment worked. A modest investigation, carefully designed and honestly evaluated, scores better than an ambitious one written up loosely.

On the papers, the highest-value technique is answer construction in the extended-response questions. Physics loses marks to unstated assumptions. Chemistry loses them to loose notation and unbalanced equations. Biology loses them to description where the command term asked for explanation or evaluation. All three lose marks to answers that do not match the mark allocation, because a six-mark question wants six creditable statements rather than one long paragraph.

The investigation is also where online tuition has a clear limit worth stating. The experiment belongs to the school, its equipment and its safety rules. What a session does is interrogate the research question before the laboratory, then examine the data, the graph choice, the uncertainty propagation and the evaluation afterwards. Those stages hold most of the criterion marks, and students rush them.

Option topics vary between schools, so a Remraam student at GEMS International School Al Khail and one at Fairgreen may sit the same core and different option questions. Naming the school with the enquiry prevents a term of preparation aimed at the wrong material.

A note on the laboratory scheme itself. Schools differ in how much practical work they run and when, and that determines when an investigation can realistically be designed and carried out. Asking the department early for the practical calendar, rather than waiting for a deadline to be announced, is the cheapest piece of planning available in any science subject.

sections.heading: Group 5: the two mathematics routes and what each punishes
paragraphs: Mathematics at Diploma level is two courses, not one subject at two difficulties. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-centred with calculus at its core, and its first paper is taken without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation is built on modelling and statistics with technology assumed throughout. Both exist at Higher and Standard Level, and both carry an exploration worth roughly a fifth of the grade.

Each punishes a different thing. In Analysis the punishment is arithmetic fragility: a slip in the second line of a manipulation reaches the final answer, and follow-through credit only partly rescues it. Classwork is almost always done with a calculator to hand, so this fluency degrades invisibly and is discovered in a mock. The repair is short timed non-calculator sets, marked at once, with every error labelled as either a slip or a method failure.

In Applications the punishment is silence. A student produces correct mathematics, reaches a modelled value, and never writes the sentence interpreting it in the context the question set out. That sentence is where the mark scheme puts the credit. The repair is a rule: no answer is finished until it has been read back in the language of the question.

The exploration behaves the same way in both routes. Students spend their effort on the mathematics, which is one criterion, and lose marks on presentation, personal engagement and reflection, which are credited separately. A reflection identifying a limitation in a model and considering what relaxing an assumption would change scores; one saying the topic was interesting does not.

sections.heading: Groups 1, 2 and 3: languages and the human sciences
paragraphs: Language and literature subjects are often treated as unteachable by tutors, which is wrong. Their components are as structured as a science paper. Guided textual analysis rewards a line of argument about how a text works rather than what it says. The comparative essay rewards texts held in conversation rather than described in sequence. The Individual Oral rewards a global issue the student can defend with two extracts they know intimately, and it is the most preparable component in the Diploma.

Language acquisition subjects, including Arabic B, sit on specified text types and oral components. The reliable loss is register: a task asking for a blog post that receives an essay loses marks that strong language cannot recover. Learning the conventions of each text type is a short, mechanical piece of work with a high return.

Individuals and societies subjects reward application. In Economics, a diagram earns marks when it is applied to the named market and almost none when it is described; the three commentaries are assessed partly on the article chosen, which makes article selection part of the work rather than a preliminary to it. In Business Management, a framework earns marks against the named organisation and nothing in the abstract.

Across all three groups the single most common avoidable loss is answering a different question from the one asked, usually because the command term was skipped in a long stem. That is diagnosable from any marked script and it responds to a fortnight of deliberate practice.

sections.heading: Internal assessment across the six groups, compared
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject has an internal component and they are easy to confuse, because they have different names, different lengths and different criteria. What they share is the thing that matters most: they must be the student's own work, authenticated by the teacher, and they carry a meaningful share of the grade with a deadline a family can still influence.

That last point makes internal assessment the highest-return work available in Year 12. Papers are months away and can only be prepared for. The investigation, exploration or commentary is in front of the student now, and a session spent interrogating a research question is worth several spent polishing a draft later. Families who understand this move their tutoring spend earlier in the year and buy less of it overall.

The failure modes differ by group and are worth knowing in advance. Science investigations fail on scope, with a question the school's equipment cannot answer. Mathematics explorations fail on the non-mathematical criteria. Economics commentaries fail on article choice. Extended Essays fail on a research question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words. In every case the failure happens before any writing, which is exactly when help is cheapest.

The boundary applies identically across all of them. A tutor explains criteria, interrogates a question, critiques a method and marks the student's own draft. A tutor does not draft, rewrite, edit to completion, supply text or provide data the student did not collect.

sections.heading: The highest-frequency loss in each group
paragraphs: If a Remraam family wanted one page of this to keep, it would be this one. Across marked Diploma work the losses are strikingly repetitive, and each group has a signature failure that accounts for a disproportionate share of missing marks.

In the sciences it is the unstated step: a calculation without its assumption, a conclusion without the reasoning line, an evaluation that lists rather than judges. In mathematics it is the unwritten interpretation or, in Analysis, the arithmetic slip under non-calculator conditions. In language and literature it is sequential treatment where comparison was asked for. In language acquisition it is register. In individuals and societies it is description where application was required.

These signatures are useful because they make the first session efficient. A tutor who knows the signature for the subject can look at one marked script and confirm or rule it out within minutes, rather than running a generic diagnostic hour. Where the signature is present, the plan is obvious. Where it is absent, something more specific is going on and that is worth knowing too.

The second use is for the student. A teenager who can say out loud that they lose marks by calculating without stating assumptions has something actionable. A teenager who believes they are bad at chemistry does not. Converting the second sentence into the first is a large part of what a good first session does.

One caveat. A signature loss is a starting hypothesis, not a diagnosis. Where a script does not show it, the honest response is to look harder rather than to force the evidence, and occasionally the answer is that the student is doing nothing wrong technically and simply has not covered two topics. That is a different plan with a longer timescale, and it should be said plainly rather than dressed up as technique work.

sections.heading: Remraam, South View School and the sixth-form question
paragraphs: Remraam is unusual in this belt for having a secondary school close at hand. South View School sits near the community and takes students through Year 11, which makes the IGCSE years straightforward for families here in a way they are not for Mudon or Town Square. The Diploma question is different, because it generally means moving.

That move is the conversation that shapes tutoring demand from this community. A student finishing Year 11 locally and entering a Diploma at GEMS International School Al Khail, Fairgreen International or elsewhere is changing assessment systems as well as schools. IGCSE is examined, linear and content-dense; the Diploma adds internal assessment, the core components and the expectation of sustained independent work.

The subject-specific part of that step is larger than families expect in mathematics, chemistry and physics, where notation, mathematical demand and the requirement to justify all rise at once. Six to eight sessions across the summer between the two years, aimed at those specific gaps, converts a difficult first term into an ordinary one. That block has to be booked before results arrive if it is going to happen.

The administrative part is worth asking about early too: which Diploma subjects the receiving school actually offers, which option topics it teaches in the sciences, and what its entry thresholds are from an IGCSE profile. Those three answers shape both the subject choice and the first year of tutoring.

There is a practical timing point as well. Sixth-form applications in this market open well before Year 11 results, and several schools interview. A student who has thought about subject combinations, and can say why they want Higher Level in a particular subject, interviews better than one who has not, and that conversation costs nothing to have early.

sections.heading: Honesty, permits and the four questions worth asking
paragraphs: Two rules bound what any Diploma tutor should do. Assessed work must be the student's own, which means a tutor teaches, explains criteria, questions a method and marks a student's own draft, and never writes, completes, edits to completion or supplies text or data. One provider competing for these searches sells completed internal assessments; that is the offer to refuse, and it is worth saying so to the student as well as declining it yourself.

The second rule concerns board material. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to their publishers. Sessions reference and link to the official pages rather than circulating copies, and nobody holds unreleased material whatever is claimed about examiner connections.

On the legal side, an individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE's own service listing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

The four questions that separate a useful tutor from a plausible one are short. Which level and option have you taught, and for how many cohorts. Which papers or criteria have you marked. What will you refuse to do with an internal assessment draft. Do you hold the private tuition permit. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, no ADEK registration and no board affiliation, and will not describe its tutors using a regulator's name.

process.title: Name the subject, level, option and school
process.description: Four facts in one message. The subject and level decide the tutor; the option and school decide the material and the internal deadlines. Two Diploma students in Dubai studying nominally the same subject can be examined on different option content.

process.title: Attach one marked script or draft
process.description: A marked response paper, a returned investigation draft or a commentary with comments on it lets the first session confirm or rule out the group's signature loss within minutes instead of spending an hour on a generic diagnostic.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the subject tutor
process.description: Over live video, at no cost, before any payment, with the student doing most of the talking. The test afterwards is whether they can state their own error pattern in one sentence. If the lesson did not produce that, ask for a different tutor.

process.title: Fix a slot the Remraam evening can hold
process.description: Sessions sit on Gulf Standard Time around the run back along Al Qudra Road or Al Khail Road. A quarter past four suits students home early; after eight suits commuting households. The slot can move within the evening, or after Iftar during Ramadan, at no cost.

process.title: Review by component, not by feeling
process.description: Every four to six weeks the plan is checked against the internal deadline and against which component still holds recoverable marks. Session notes record the named error pattern and whether it has closed, so the review is short and factual.

whyPoints.title: The match is made on subject, not on range
whyPoints.description: Selecting by distance from Remraam means selecting from generalists based around Dubai Investment Park, Dubai Sports City and Motor City. Selecting by subject means selecting from people who have taught that level. At Higher Level that is the difference the grade responds to.

whyPoints.title: Each group is planned by where its marks sit
whyPoints.description: Sciences, mathematics, languages and the human sciences place their marks differently, and a plan shaped for one wastes hours in another. Knowing the signature loss for a group makes the first session fast and the first month targeted.

whyPoints.title: Internal assessment is treated as the live component
whyPoints.description: Papers can only be prepared for; the investigation, exploration or commentary is in front of the student now and has a deadline a family can still influence. Buying help earlier in Year 12 usually means buying less of it in total.

whyPoints.title: What a parent can check is published
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here is attributed to the provider or cost table that published it, and the questions worth asking a tutor are listed so they can be asked before money moves. Claims about experience are not checkable; claims about papers marked are.

whyPoints.title: The laboratory limit is stated outright
whyPoints.description: Online lessons cannot run an experiment. They prepare the design and interrogate the analysis and evaluation, which hold most of the investigation's criterion marks. Implying more would be easy to write and dishonest to sell.

whyPoints.title: Availability is disclosed, not discovered
whyPoints.description: Some combinations, including Further Mathematics at Higher Level and less-taught languages, are thin in every market. Where that applies you are told with a timescale or an alternative rather than matched with a generalist and left to find out.

faqs.question: Will an IB tutor come to our apartment in Remraam?
faqs.answer: Not one arranged through IB Gram. Lessons are taught one-to-one over live video, and home visits are something IB Gram runs in India only. Visiting tutors do exist in Dubai and are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel folded into the price, according to Bestimate's Dubai cost table and the rates independent home tutors publish. From Remraam the practical argument for the online route is selection: you choose a tutor who has taught Chemistry at Higher Level rather than whoever can reach Al Ramth by five.

faqs.question: Which Diploma component should we spend the first month on?
faqs.answer: Whichever internal component is currently open, in most cases. Papers are months away and can only be prepared for, while an investigation, exploration or set of commentaries sits in front of the student now with a deadline that is still movable. It also carries a meaningful share of the subject grade. A session interrogating a research question or an article choice before any writing is worth several spent improving a draft later, and it usually reduces how much tutoring is needed overall.

faqs.question: What is the signature mistake in Diploma sciences?
faqs.answer: The unstated step. A calculation is correct and the assumption behind it is never named. A conclusion is reached and the reasoning line is missing. An evaluation question receives a list of advantages with no judgement. The marks for those steps are separately available and the student usually knew the physics or chemistry involved. The repair is to plan two lines before writing any extended response, naming the science to be used and the assumption to be stated, then to self-mark against the published scheme until the habit holds.

faqs.question: My son is at a 4 in Chemistry HL. Where does the first session go?
faqs.answer: Into a marked script rather than a syllabus. A 4 at Higher Level is normally a pattern: equations left unbalanced, state symbols omitted where the scheme wanted them, mechanisms drawn with arrows from the wrong species, equilibrium answered qualitatively where a quantitative line was required. The session names the pattern and the next three attack it with timed questions from his own option, marked against the scheme, with annotated scripts going back to him. Marks on individual questions move before a predicted grade does.

faqs.question: Does the exploration in maths really need separate work?
faqs.answer: Yes, because three of its criteria are not about mathematics. Presentation, personal engagement and reflection are credited separately, and students pour effort into the mathematics while leaving those thin. A reflection that identifies a limitation in a model, and considers what would change if an assumption were relaxed, scores properly; one that says the topic was interesting does not. The mathematics does not need to be exotic to score well. It needs to be correct, clearly communicated and genuinely owned by the student.

faqs.question: How preparable is the Individual Oral?
faqs.answer: More than any other component in the Diploma, which is why it is worth prioritising. The student chooses a global issue and defends it using two extracts, so the entire shape of the assessment is known in advance. The work is choosing an issue that both extracts genuinely support, knowing those extracts in detail, and rehearsing aloud until the structure holds under questioning. Students who leave this to the fortnight before lose marks they could have banked months earlier with three or four sessions.

faqs.question: Why do Economics commentaries lose marks when the economics is right?
faqs.answer: Usually because of the article, or because diagrams are described rather than applied. The article is part of the assessment: too old, too long, or lacking the economics the student wants to apply, and the commentary is capped before it is written. On diagrams, a labelled curve shifted with an explanation tied to the named market earns marks; the same diagram described in general terms earns little. Choosing and rejecting candidate articles together is one of the most efficient sessions available in that subject.

faqs.question: Can online lessons support a science investigation without a laboratory?
faqs.answer: They support everything except the measuring, and the measuring carries the fewest marks. Before the practical, a session can interrogate the research question, test whether the method will produce a measurable relationship, name the variables needing control and anticipate the dominant uncertainty. Afterwards it can examine the raw data, check whether the chosen graph hides the relationship, work propagation on the student's own numbers and read the draft against each criterion. The experiment belongs to the school and its equipment, which this page states rather than glosses.

faqs.question: Is a tutor allowed to look at an internal assessment draft at all?
faqs.answer: Yes, as teaching and feedback on the student's own writing. A tutor can explain what each criterion rewards, ask the questions the descriptors imply, say that a method will not produce usable data, point out that a paragraph asserts rather than evidences, and mark the draft against the published descriptors. A tutor must not draft, rewrite, edit to completion, supply text or provide data the student did not collect. The work is authenticated by the teacher, and an authenticity finding can cost the Diploma rather than marks.

faqs.question: How does the step up from South View School to a Diploma feel?
faqs.answer: Larger in independence than in content. IGCSE is examined, linear and content-dense; the Diploma adds internal assessment in every subject, the core components, and the expectation that a student manages long-horizon work without being set exercises weekly. In mathematics, chemistry and physics the subject-level jump is also real, with notation, mathematical demand and the requirement to justify all rising at once. Six to eight sessions across the summer aimed at those specific gaps turns a difficult first term into an ordinary one.

faqs.question: Which questions actually tell us whether a tutor is any good?
faqs.answer: Specific ones. Which level and option have you taught, and for how many cohorts. Which papers or criteria have you marked. What will you refuse to do with an internal assessment draft. Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free of charge, valid two years and issued in a stated two working days. Those four answers are checkable against the school and the regulator. A question about whether a tutor is experienced produces a sentence that cannot be verified by anyone.

faqs.question: What does a Higher Level Diploma tutor cost along this corridor?
faqs.answer: Specialists publish roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai cost table giving AED 200 to 450 or more, while premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the quote. These are published market figures with their sources named, not IB Gram prices, and a free trial comes before any payment.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take two subjects for the same Remraam student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking where the subjects share content. Physics and Analysis and Approaches overlap in calculus, vectors and graph interpretation, so one can reinforce the other. Chemistry and Biology share the science-group investigation criteria exactly, so coursework coaching transfers without relearning the assessment language. At Higher Level in two heavy subjects simultaneously the honest answer is often two tutors. Either way the scheduling is identical, since no travel has to be arranged between slots.

faqs.question: What if the subject or option we need is not covered?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a timescale or an alternative, rather than matched to a generalist. Common combinations such as Biology SL, Applications SL, English A and Business Management are usually covered within a few days of you naming subject, level, option and school. Narrower ones, including Further Mathematics at Higher Level, less-taught languages and certain option topics, can take a week or more, and occasionally the honest answer is that we cannot cover it well. Saying so loses a booking and prevents a wasted term.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-remraam.closingBody: From Remraam the useful first message contains four facts and one attachment: the subject, the level, the option the school teaches, the school itself, and one marked script or draft. That is enough for a tutor to confirm the group's signature loss in minutes and propose something specific. A free trial lesson over live video is arranged before any payment is taken, and if the match is wrong you say so and another tutor is proposed. Lessons are delivered online on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only.

intro.heading: What an IB home tutor actually costs a Serena household
paragraphs: Serena is a townhouse community off Al Qudra Road, built around clusters including Bella Casa and Casa Viva, sitting between Mudon, Villanova and Remraam at the outer edge of the Dubailand belt. Its position is the single biggest influence on what tutoring costs here, and almost nobody says so out loud. A tutor who drives to Serena spends forty to sixty minutes each way on an ordinary weekday afternoon, and that time is paid for in the hourly rate.

The numbers are published, just not in one place. Market in-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel — Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table shows AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500. The same qualified tutor teaching online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. The gap is the drive, and in Serena it sits at the top of the AED 50 to 150 range.

That makes the honest question not 'what does a home tutor cost' but 'what is the premium buying'. It buys presence. For a child under about ten who needs an adult in the room, or a student whose particular needs make screen work genuinely harder, presence is worth paying for and the in-home market in this belt exists to serve it. For a sixteen-year-old working on a Chemistry Internal Assessment, it buys a car in the driveway and nothing academic.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. They are a service we run only in India, and Serena students are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We state that in the first screen rather than after a deposit, because a family who specifically wants a visitor should spend their time on the independent in-home market instead of on us.

What follows is the whole cost picture for an IB family in this community: the per-hour bands with sources, a year of support priced three ways, which subjects cost most to support, the extras that never appear in an hourly quote, what cannot be bought at any price, and how tutoring sits beside the other education costs in a Dubai household. Every figure names its publisher so you can check it.

One useful piece of context before the numbers. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are a known quantity this year. Tutoring is the line a family actually controls. The sector context is that Dubai has 227 private schools teaching 17 curricula to 387,441 students, so price variation between providers reflects positioning rather than any single market rate.
