dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-serena.programmesIntro: What IB support costs over a year depends mostly on the stage, because each stage has a different number of things that can go wrong at once.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The cheapest stage to support and the one where the in-home premium is most often justified, because a seven-year-old may genuinely need an adult in the room. Sessions are short, 40 to 45 minutes, and the useful work is number fluency, reading stamina and writing that holds a reason. Budget-band supervision at AED 33 to 65 an hour is frequently the right purchase here.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the primary years also carry the KHDA-mandated Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies requirement, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs. Families who did not budget for Arabic support discover the need around Year 2, and it is a separate stream rather than something a general tutor absorbs.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Marked against four criteria per subject, each out of 8. Costs here are usually modest because the efficient intervention is a four to six session block on one criterion rather than a year of content teaching. Families who buy weekly sessions for a criterion problem spend roughly five times what the diagnosis required.
programmes.countryNote: MYP provision around Dubailand is thinner than Diploma or British-curriculum provision, so Serena students on this track often travel further to school. The longer commute shortens the evening, which is why the in-home option is doubly expensive here: a later start and a higher travel component in the rate.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The most expensive stage, with six subjects, three Internal Assessments or more landing in overlapping windows, and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge alongside. Specialist rates apply at Higher Level: AED 200 to 450 or more per hour, per TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate at AED 200 to 450+. The controllable variable is how many subjects you support, and the answer is usually one or two.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. We publish no IB exam or results dates, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and a date a family budgets around must be checkable. Ask your child's IB coordinator for the window and for the school's internal coursework deadlines, which fall earlier and drive the spending calendar.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: DP courses paired with a career-related study and a reflective project. Support costs tend to concentrate on the DP courses carried into the programme plus the written reflection, which is assessed against descriptors students have rarely been shown. A narrower spend than a full Diploma, because there are fewer subjects competing.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision in Dubai is limited, so a Serena family considering it is usually also weighing a change of school and therefore a change of commute. For Ministry of Education equivalency the British-track rules are published in specific terms while no IB points threshold has been read on moe.gov.ae, so verify any equivalency question with the Ministry rather than inferring it.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-serena.subjectsIntro: Support costs vary by subject more than families expect, mostly because specialist scarcity differs. These are the IB subjects Serena households ask about, with the cost logic attached.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most expensive IB subject to support at Higher Level, because Paper 3 technique and proof work need a genuine specialist and the specialist band applies. At Standard Level a qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 is adequate for most cases.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Cheaper to support than Analysis and Approaches at the same level, because the commonest losses are statistical process habits — unstated hypotheses, conclusions not written in context — which close in three or four sessions rather than needing sustained content teaching.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Specialist band at Higher Level. The cost depends sharply on the diagnosis: an organic mechanisms habit is four to eight sessions, while an unsecured bonding foundation from DP1 is a twenty to thirty session content programme. Those two present identically to a parent.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Specialist band at Higher Level, where fields and the data-analysis component carry the losses. Good value in short blocks: three sessions on uncertainties and graph work address a component almost nobody practises deliberately.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-dense, so parents assume high hours. Usually the opposite: the dominant loss is command-term failure — describing where explanation was asked for — which is one or two sessions of strict marking rather than a term of revision.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the fastest gain available and takes very few sessions. The three IA commentaries are where costs rise if left late, because each has a strict word limit and a different unit, and emergency help cannot change a commentary already built on the wrong article.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application to the stimulus case is the whole examinable skill, and it is cheap to teach. The pre-released Paper 1 case study rewards structured reading months ahead, which is unpaid work the student does rather than tutored hours.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral is where support pays, because a global issue too broad to sustain ten minutes cannot be rescued later. Two or three sessions at the choosing stage are worth more than six in the week before.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Scarce at Diploma level, especially first-language Arabic, so availability rather than price is the constraint. Worth asking three to four weeks ahead rather than at a deadline, from any provider.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Underspent on, and cheap to support well: most low marks come from exhibition objects that illustrate rather than evidence a knowledge claim. Two sessions at the object-choosing stage are the whole of the value.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Process coaching only, and the money works at the start: narrowing a question that is actually answerable. Spent late, it buys presentation improvements on a question that was never viable. We do not draft, rewrite or edit an Extended Essay to completion.

subjects.name: Internal Assessment supervision
subjects.description: Three to six sessions per subject, timed before the research question or topic is locked. The highest return per dirham in the Diploma, because each IA carries 20 to 25 per cent of a subject grade and the ceiling is set at the design stage.

sections.heading: The travel premium, measured
paragraphs: Serena is far enough out that the cost of a tutor's journey is not a rounding error. On a weekday afternoon a tutor coming from Jumeirah, Al Barsha or Business Bay spends forty to sixty minutes each way, and no professional absorbs ninety minutes of unpaid time. It appears in the rate, and the published market figures show exactly how much.

Market in-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel: Bestimate's 2026 rate table gives AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500. The same qualified tutor online is AED 150 to 300, and an IB specialist online is AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. The spread between the two formats for the same person is the AED 50 to 150 travel premium, and Serena sits at its upper end.

Over a block of sessions the arithmetic becomes concrete. Twenty sessions at a AED 100 premium is AED 2,000 spent on driving. A full school year of weekly sessions at the same premium is around AED 3,000. For most families that is a meaningful sum spent on logistics rather than teaching, and it is invisible because it never appears as a separate line on an invoice.

The honest counterpoint: the premium is worth paying in specific cases. A young child who needs an adult present to stay on task, a student whose particular needs make video work genuinely harder, or a household with no quiet surface where a screen session can work. In those cases the independent in-home market in this belt is the right place to look, and the premium is its honest price rather than a mark-up.

sections.heading: A year of IB support, priced three ways
paragraphs: Families budget by the year, so here is the year. Three realistic arrangements for a Serena Diploma household, costed at published market bands, with the thing each one actually delivers. The point of setting them side by side is that the cheapest is not the weakest and the most expensive is not the most effective.

The targeted arrangement buys two Internal Assessment blocks and one short technique block across the year: roughly fifteen sessions, AED 3,000 to 6,750 at the specialist band. It protects the components where the ceiling is set early and fixes the habits that leak marks across every paper. For a student who is broadly coping and losing marks to specifics, it outperforms everything else in the table.

The weekly arrangement in one subject is thirty sessions and AED 6,000 to 13,500 at the specialist band. It is the right purchase for a genuine content deficit, where a student has missed a foundation and needs sustained teaching. It is the wrong purchase for a technique problem, which is what most families who buy it actually have.

The two-subject weekly arrangement is sixty sessions and AED 12,000 to 27,000, and it is rarely justified. In nearly every case we see, splitting attention across two subjects for a year produces less movement than one subject plus targeted blocks elsewhere. If the budget is there, the better use is a specialist for the weakest subject and school support plus structured independent practice for the rest.

sections.heading: Which IB subjects cost most to support, and why
paragraphs: Subject choice affects the bill more than tutor choice does, because specialist scarcity differs sharply across the Diploma and scarcity sets the band. Knowing which subjects sit where lets a family plan rather than react.

The expensive end is Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, Higher Level Chemistry and Higher Level Physics, plus first-language Arabic and Theory of Knowledge supervision. These are in the specialist band at AED 200 to 450 or more per hour, and in two of them availability rather than price is the binding constraint. For those, the useful behaviour is to ask three to four weeks before you need to start.

The cheaper end is not the easier end. Biology, Economics, Business Management and English A are frequently supportable in a small number of sessions because their dominant losses are habits rather than content gaps: command terms in Biology, diagram accuracy in Economics, applying a tool to the stimulus in Business, choosing a sustainable global issue in English. A family can often buy three sessions in each of two subjects for less than a term of weekly work in one.

The one place where spending early beats spending more is Internal Assessment supervision in any subject. Each IA carries 20 to 25 per cent of its subject grade, and the ceiling is set when the topic or research question is chosen. Three to six sessions at that point protect the component. The same money spent after the data is collected improves the writing of something that was already capped.

sections.heading: Where Dubailand families waste IB tutoring money
paragraphs: Five patterns, each seen often enough in enquiries from this belt to be worth naming. Each is avoidable with one question asked before the first payment, and together they account for most of the overspending we see.

The first is paying the travel premium by default. If your child works perfectly well on a screen, the AED 50 to 150 an hour that a visiting tutor adds for the drive to Serena is cost without return, and over a year it is around AED 3,000. The second is buying a weekly year for a technique problem. Command terms, diagram accuracy and unshown method are habit fixes of one to four sessions; thirty sessions costs eight times as much and spends most of its time on topics the student already has.

The third is buying Internal Assessment help too late. The component is worth 20 to 25 per cent of a subject grade and its ceiling is set at the topic-choosing stage. Emergency sessions in the final fortnight can improve presentation and cannot change a capped research question. The fourth is supporting two subjects simultaneously from the start, which makes it impossible to tell which intervention worked and splits the student's attention when they have six subjects already.

The fifth is spending the entire budget before results. Entry fees, review-of-results requests and any retake route are real costs that arrive after the tutoring money has gone, and they are quoted by the exam centre rather than by any tutor. A plan that keeps a reserve is a plan that can respond to a result.

sections.heading: The extras that never appear in an hourly quote
paragraphs: An hourly rate is the start of the cost rather than the whole of it. Ask about every item below before a first paid session, from any provider including us, and get the answers in writing.

Session length and billing unit. An hour sometimes means fifty minutes. Ninety-minute sessions are sometimes billed as two hours. Ask whether the quote is per hour or per lesson, because they are different questions with different answers and the difference compounds across thirty sessions.

Cancellation terms. How much notice avoids a charge, and what happens when a school event moves at a day's notice, which in Dubai happens regularly. This matters more for in-home arrangements, where a wasted journey is a real cost to the tutor and is normally charged in full. Online, a clashed session can often be moved inside the same week, which over a two-year Diploma is several hours of teaching kept rather than lost.

Materials, platform fees and VAT. Ask whether any materials charge applies, and note that nobody should be selling you IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables: those are published by the IB and should be cited and linked, not resold as a resource pack. On VAT, the only honest position is to require clarity in writing about whether a quoted price includes it; we will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as a general fact, because that needs a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than an opinion.

sections.heading: What no price can buy
paragraphs: Three things are on sale in this market that should not be, and recognising them protects both the budget and the student's qualification.

A promise about the final grade is the first. No tutor, centre or platform controls an examination outcome, and a page offering one either has unpublished refund terms or is making a claim it cannot honour. Where a refund promise exists, its exact terms should be printed on the same screen as the promise. Treat any promise of a specific points total, a specific grade or a promised improvement as a reason to look elsewhere rather than a premium feature.

Completed coursework is the second, and it is the more serious. At least one operator ranking for searches like this one sells finished Internal Assessments. Buying one is not a shortcut; it is passing off another person's work as your child's own, which is academic misconduct under IB rules and risks the Diploma rather than a grade. Legitimate support means teaching the content, explaining the criteria, questioning the reasoning and giving feedback on what the student wrote. It never means supplying text or data.

Board and IB material as a product is the third. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are published by the IB and the examination boards, and should be cited and linked rather than reproduced or resold. A provider charging for them is selling access to something free and redistributing material they do not own. A fourth, smaller point: a star rating nobody can trace is not a reason to accept a higher quote, and competitor pages in this market show conflicting rating figures within a single page.

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor your child, and why checking is free
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work rather than unregulated work, and the verification costs nothing, which makes it worth doing regardless of price band.

The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The route is MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service, through the smart app, website or e-services system, with a two-working-day completion time and no listed fee.

Two consequences for a family comparing quotes. Because the permit is free, no tutor should be passing on a licensing cost in their rate. And because u.ae states plainly that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, a tutor who tells you the permit is optional has told you something useful about themselves. No fine schedule has been published — Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify amounts — so treat any figure quoted at you as unverified.

The institutional layer is separate. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific licence with initial approval, completion steps and annual renewal. IB Gram holds none and claims none, has no UAE office or centre, and does not describe any school as a client or partner. KHDA is responsible for overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai; that is a fact about KHDA rather than an endorsement of anybody.

paragraphs: Tutoring competes with other education costs rather than existing beside them, so the last table sets it against the rest of the budget. The surrounding figures are included so the tutoring line can be judged against something concrete.

The anchor is the fee position. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That makes school fees a known quantity this year and tutoring the variable a family chooses.

The sector context is worth having too. Dubai has 227 private schools teaching 17 curricula to 387,441 students as of 2024-25, with UK curricula at 37 per cent of enrolment and International Baccalaureate programmes at 7 per cent. Seven new private schools were approved for the 2026-27 intake — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. More IB provision over time means a slightly deeper local tutor pool, though not quickly.

The items that catch families out are at the bottom of the table: examination entry fees, review-of-results requests and any retake route, all quoted by the exam centre rather than by a tutor. Build them in from the start. A family that has spent its entire tutoring budget by May has no capacity to respond to a result, and responding to a result is sometimes the highest-value spending of the whole two years.

process.description: We say how many sessions the job looks like, then quote. That order matters because IB cases range from two sessions to thirty, and a headline rate quoted in advance of any evidence tells a family nothing about what they will actually spend across a year.

process.description: A real lesson with the person who would continue, no card required. It tests the diagnosis and the fit together, and it ends with a session count. Sometimes the count is smaller than the family expected; occasionally the honest answer is that no tutoring is needed yet.

process.title: A written plan with a finish date
process.description: The plan names the component to attack first, the session count, and the date it ends, set against your school's internal deadlines rather than a generic schedule. A plan without a finish date is a subscription, and subscriptions are how tutoring budgets quietly double.

process.title: Reviewed each term, stopped when done
process.description: Each session produces notes naming coverage and set work. Each term the arrangement is reviewed against marked evidence, and when the gap closes we say so rather than letting the slot run. Keeping a reserve for entry fees and post-results decisions is part of that conversation.

whyPoints.title: No drive, so no premium
whyPoints.description: Serena sits at the top of the AED 50 to 150 hourly travel premium in this market because of how far out it is. Online delivery removes it rather than discounting it, which over a year of weekly sessions is roughly AED 3,000 not spent on somebody's journey.

faqs.question: What does an IB home tutor cost for a family in Serena?
faqs.answer: In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are advertised at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table showing AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. Serena sits at the upper end because it is among the furthest-out communities in the Dubailand belt, so a tutor's round trip is eighty to a hundred and twenty minutes. Online, the same qualified tutor is AED 150 to 300 and an IB specialist AED 200 to 450 or more. Those are published market figures, not our prices.

faqs.question: Why is my Serena quote higher than my friend's in Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: Distance, almost always. Serena sits twenty to thirty minutes further out than the Ranches for most of Dubai's tutoring workforce, and that time is priced into an in-home hour. The difference commonly shows as AED 30 to 50 an hour on an otherwise identical arrangement, which across thirty sessions is AED 900 to 1,500. If both quotes are for online sessions and still differ, you are probably comparing a generalist with a subject specialist rather than two prices for the same service.

faqs.question: Is the travel premium ever worth paying?
faqs.answer: Yes, in specific cases. A child under about ten who needs an adult physically present to stay on task, a student whose particular needs make screen work genuinely harder, or a household with no quiet surface where a video session can work. Those are real reasons, and the independent in-home market in this belt serves them at AED 180 to 500 an hour. What is not a reason is the assumption that presence equals better teaching: a specialist on a screen who has read the subject guide beats a generalist in the dining room who has not.

faqs.question: How much should a year of IB tutoring cost in total?
faqs.answer: It depends on the arrangement rather than the rate. A targeted year — two Internal Assessment blocks plus one technique block, about fifteen sessions — is AED 3,000 to 6,750 at the specialist band. Weekly sessions in one subject, about thirty, is AED 6,000 to 13,500. Two subjects weekly doubles that again and is rarely justified. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one hour a week are AED 240 to 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 mid, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are the most expensive to get help with?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, Higher Level Chemistry and Higher Level Physics, plus first-language Arabic and Theory of Knowledge supervision. All sit in the specialist band at AED 200 to 450 or more an hour, and in Arabic and TOK the real constraint is availability rather than price. Biology, Economics, Business Management and English A are usually cheaper to support well, because their dominant losses are habits — command terms, diagram accuracy, applying a tool to the stimulus — that close in a handful of sessions.

faqs.question: When is the best time to spend money on Internal Assessment support?
faqs.answer: Before the topic or research question is locked in, which is usually several months earlier than families act. Each IA carries 20 to 25 per cent of its subject grade, and the ceiling is set at the design stage: a research question without a measurable, controllable relationship cannot score well however carefully the write-up is done. Three to six sessions at that point protect the component for AED 600 to 2,700. The same money spent after the data is collected improves presentation on something already capped.

faqs.question: What should I ask about before paying for the first session?
faqs.answer: Five things, in writing. Whether the quote is per hour or per lesson, and whether an hour means sixty minutes. How much cancellation notice avoids a charge, and what happens when a school event moves at a day's notice. Whether any materials fee applies — and note that nobody should be reselling you IB past papers or mark schemes. Whether the quoted price includes VAT. And how many sessions the provider thinks the job will take, which is the number that actually decides your spend.

faqs.question: Can a tutor guarantee my child's IB points will improve?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider offering it is telling you something about themselves. Nobody controls an examination outcome, and a refund promise means nothing unless its exact terms are published on the same screen as the promise. What a good arrangement can offer instead is a diagnosis you can check, a plan with a session count and a finish date, marked work you can read, and a termly review against evidence. Treat promises of a specific grade or points total as a reason to look elsewhere rather than a premium feature.

faqs.question: Will someone come to our villa in Serena for lessons?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We teach UAE students one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we run only in India, so no tutor will arrive at a Dubailand address. There is no IB Gram office or centre anywhere in the UAE either. Independent in-home tutors do work in this belt at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, and if presence in the room is what your child needs, that market is the right one to approach rather than us.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre in Motor City cheaper than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes; monthly packages in this market are advertised from around AED 799 for eight sessions. Per outcome, it depends on what your child needs. A group class delivers a fixed syllabus at a fixed pace, which suits a student who is broadly on track and wants more practice. It cannot address an individual diagnosed gap. Add the drive from Serena — thirty to forty minutes each way plus waiting, so around two hours of household time per session — and a short one-to-one block is often cheaper to the finish line.

faqs.question: Do I have to check whether a tutor holds a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: If you are hiring directly, yes, and it costs nothing. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, with applications through MoHRE's Private Tutor Licensing service. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Because the permit is free, no tutor should pass on a licensing cost. No fine schedule is published, so distrust any penalty figure quoted at you.

faqs.question: What happens to the money if the tutor turns out to be the wrong fit?
faqs.answer: With us the first lesson is free and is taught by the tutor who would continue, so the fit is tested before anything is paid. If the pace or style does not suit your child, say so and we match again rather than running a paid block that nobody is enjoying. When hiring an independent tutor directly, ask before the first session what happens if the arrangement ends after one lesson, and whether any block payment is refundable — that answer is worth more than a small difference in the hourly rate.

faqs.question: Should I budget for exam entry fees and retakes separately?
faqs.answer: Yes, and families who do not are the ones who feel overcharged in May. Examination entry fees, review-of-results requests and any retake route are quoted by the examination centre rather than by any tutor, and they arrive after the tutoring budget has typically been spent. Keeping a reserve also means you can act on a result: responding to one disappointing subject with a short, well-aimed block is sometimes the highest-value spending in the whole two years, and it is only possible if the money has not all gone.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education add to the tutoring budget in Dubai?
faqs.answer: They often should and usually do not. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and separate classes organised for Arabs and non-Arabs, since combined classes are prohibited. For a non-Arab Diploma student those periods are genuine additional work in a language not used at home. We run Arabic as its own stream for that reason, and it is worth pricing in rather than discovering in a report.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-serena.closingHeading: Price the arrangement, not the hour
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-serena.closingBody: Before hiring an IB home tutor in Serena, decide which arrangement you are buying: a targeted set of blocks, weekly support in one subject, or supervision for a younger child. Each has a different annual figure and a different purpose, and the hourly rate is the least informative number in the decision. Tell us the subject, the level, the problem in one sentence and what you can spend, and you will get a session count, a plan with a finish date, and a rate quoted after the free trial lesson. Teaching is live, one-to-one and online; nobody drives to Dubailand.

Each teaches a named subject at a named level, works from the student's own marked papers, and reports what is costing marks rather than how the session felt.

intro.heading: The honest answer to "is there anyone near me who knows this syllabus?"
paragraphs: Mostly, no. That is the answer, and the rest of this page explains why it is the right answer rather than a discouraging one. Sobha Hartland has two well-regarded schools inside it and more within a short drive, so it is not a community short of education. It is short of something narrower: people who can teach a specific IB Diploma subject at a specific level to examination standard and who are available at six in the evening on a Tuesday.

Start with the arithmetic. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula. KHDA's published enrolment shares for that year put the UK curriculum largest, Indian second and American third, with the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent of students. Seven per cent of a very large market is still a lot of children, but it is a minority, and the teachers who serve it are employed by the schools that run the programme. They are not distributed evenly across Dubai's communities. They live near their schools, and they are already teaching all day.

Now narrow it further, because the Diploma is not one subject. A student takes six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. A parent in Sobha Hartland does not need an IB tutor. They need, say, a Chemistry Higher Level tutor, or someone who can supervise an Economics internal assessment, or a Maths Analysis and Approaches tutor who can handle Paper 3. Each of those is a different person, and the number of each living within a twenty-minute drive of Hartland is very small. Not zero, but small enough that availability, not quality, becomes the thing that decides who teaches your child.

This is where the home-visit model breaks down, and it breaks down quietly. A family searching locally gets matched not to the person who knows the syllabus best but to the person who knows it well enough and will make the drive. Those are different standards and nobody says so out loud. The market rate reflects the compromise too: in-home one-to-one in Dubai runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour because the figure includes travel, which means a Hartland family can pay specialist money for a generalist who happens to be nearby.

IB Gram does not solve this by sending someone better to your door. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. What we do instead is remove geography from the decision. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the tutor is chosen because they teach your child's subject at your child's level. A Hartland student taking Chemistry Higher Level gets a Chemistry Higher Level teacher rather than whoever was both competent and close. The rest of this page gives you the costs, the comparison, the subject-by-subject coverage picture and the six things to test in a first lesson.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.programmesIntro: Sobha Hartland families sit across the IB continuum and the British curriculum, sometimes within the same household. These three programme contexts change what a first lesson needs to contain, and each one has a different supply problem behind it.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries its own internal assessment, and those deadlines land in clusters rather than spread evenly. This is the programme where subject-specific tutoring matters most, because a Higher Level Physics paper and a Standard Level Economics paper have nothing in common except the student sitting them.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision near Sobha Hartland is good by Dubai standards and the subject combinations available still vary school by school. What does not vary is the supply picture for tutors: the teachers delivering those courses work full days at the schools that employ them, so the pool available for evening one-to-one work in this community is thin and subject-specific.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject rather than through examinations, with the Personal Project in the final year. MYP tutoring is a different job from Diploma tutoring: the work is about meeting criteria descriptors, structuring investigations and writing reflectively. A tutor who knows Diploma Chemistry may not know how MYP Sciences criterion descriptors are applied, and the reverse is also true.
programmes.countryNote: Several central-corridor schools run MYP and then offer both the Diploma and A Levels at sixteen, so Hartland parents face a real choice. The MYP-to-Diploma transition is where most of our early enquiries from this community start, and the gap is usually examination technique rather than subject knowledge.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with transdisciplinary units rather than separate subjects and an exhibition in the final year. Tutoring at this stage is mostly about securing literacy and number fluency so that the inquiry work has something to stand on. It is also the stage where parents most often over-buy, because a seven-year-old rarely needs weekly one-to-one support across a year.
programmes.countryNote: Hartland and the surrounding communities have substantial primary provision, and the honest advice for most PYP families is that a short block addressing a specific gap, such as number bonds or reading fluency, does more than an open-ended arrangement. We will say that rather than sell the arrangement.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.subjectsIntro: The Diploma's structure is why this page talks about supply rather than about quality. Each subject below is a separate specialism with its own mark scheme and its own internal assessment. These are the ones we cover for Sobha Hartland families, with a note on where marks are genuinely lost in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which exposes algebraic fluency immediately, and Higher Level adds a third paper with its own style of extended problem. Marks go missing in proof, in calculus where multiple rules combine, and in trigonometric manipulation under time pressure.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with calculator competence examinable rather than assumed. Students who moved here to reduce workload often find the content different rather than lighter, and lose marks interpreting output they can generate but cannot explain.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Two written papers and an independent scientific investigation worth a fifth of the grade. Equilibrium reasoning, organic mechanism detail and significant figures in the data-based section are the reliable mark-losers at both levels.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Rewards algebraic confidence and precise definitions in roughly equal measure. Uncertainty treatment in practical work is the area students are least taught and most penalised for, and it transfers directly into the data questions.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Terminology precision carries more weight than calculation. Students who write fluently but imprecisely plateau around a 5, and the fix is command-term discipline rather than more content revision.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published news articles, which collides with other subjects' deadlines in DP1. Diagram accuracy and evaluation depth are where Higher Level students separate from Standard Level ones.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Carries the Individual Oral and, at Higher Level, the essay. Students lose marks by describing texts rather than analysing how meaning is constructed, which is a habit that responds quickly to targeted work.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools are straightforward and the analysis marks are not. A student who applies a framework without evaluating it will sit in the middle bands indefinitely, and that is the single most common pattern we see in this subject.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the essay are assessed against published instruments that most students never read. Our support is structural: reading the prescribed title properly, building an argument, and locating where marks are actually awarded.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of independent research with a supervisor at school. Tutoring here is process coaching: narrowing a question, planning the research, and giving feedback on the student's own drafts rather than contributing text.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.regionsIntro: Hartland sits in a dense band of central communities, and the supply argument in this page holds across all of them. Each note below says something about the local IB picture rather than about the architecture.

regions.name: Sobha Hartland
regions.note: Towers and villas around two well-known schools, with a high concentration of Diploma families relative to its size. Local demand for IB tutoring here outstrips the local supply of IB teachers by a wide margin.

regions.name: Meydan
regions.note: Immediately west, sharing several schools with Hartland. The tutoring picture is the same, and families often discover they are competing for the same handful of evening slots with the same tutors.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: Established IB provision a short drive south. One of the few nearby communities where IB teachers actually live in any number, because the schools that employ them are here.

regions.name: Business Bay
regions.note: Mostly towers with a transient population and frequent mid-year arrivals. Students joining a Diploma cohort in DP1 or DP2 are common here, and they need subject-specific catch-up rather than general support.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Short drives to several schools and the easiest access to tuition centres. Group provision is reachable, which is useful for a shared topic gap and unhelpful for a Diploma internal assessment.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Close to an IB continuum school and to the creek crossings. Sessions can start soon after the school day ends here, which is the one genuine local advantage in this part of the corridor.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Rashid City
regions.note: Large plots and longer internal drives than the map suggests, which pushes in-home quotes towards the top of the market band for no academic gain.

regions.name: Al Quoz
regions.note: Mixed use, with schools and the corridor's tuition centres. Worth knowing as the cheapest group-class option nearby, and as a reminder that cheap and suitable are different tests.

schoolClusters.city: Sobha Hartland, Meydan and Nad Al Sheba
schoolClusters.note: The schools closest to Hartland include IB Diploma provision and British-curriculum routes within minutes of each other. That mix is exactly why a tutor cannot be matched from an address: two students on the same floor of the same tower may be sitting entirely different qualifications.

schoolClusters.city: Al Jaddaf, Downtown, Al Quoz and Al Barsha
schoolClusters.note: The schools Hartland families drive to for a particular programme or subject combination. Several run an IB continuum and others run IGCSE before splitting into the Diploma or A Levels, which sets the subject-choice conversation a year earlier than most parents expect.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.modesIntro: Three formats, all delivered one-to-one online. The choice depends on whether the problem is a subject, a piece of coursework or a looming session, and the free trial lesson is where that gets established rather than assumed from an enquiry form.

modes.title: Weekly subject tuition
modes.description: One session a week in one named subject at one named level, with the same tutor throughout. This is the format that moves a grade over two terms, because it leaves the student time to practise and gives the tutor a chance to see whether the practice happened. The tutor works slightly ahead of the school's scheme of work rather than behind it, so lessons prepare rather than repair.

modes.description: A short block around an internal assessment, the Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge. The tutor explains the assessment criteria, questions the research question until it is workable, and gives written feedback on drafts the student has written. The student chooses the question, does the work and writes the text. We state that boundary to the student directly in the first session.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor costs in this part of Dubai, and what the travel buys
paragraphs: Since the search is for a home tutor, the home-tutor market deserves a straight answer rather than a redirection. In Dubai, in-home one-to-one tuition runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with the figure including travel. Monthly in-home packages are advertised around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Online equivalents sit lower: qualified subject tutors around AED 150 to 300 an hour, with specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, and advertised packages around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. All of those are other providers' published figures, read in October 2026, and they are market context rather than IB Gram's price list.

The useful question is not which number is bigger but what the difference pays for. It pays for a car journey, a person in the room, and the convenience of not having to set up a video call. Those are real things and for a younger child, particularly at PYP age, the person in the room can matter. What the premium does not pay for is subject knowledge. There is no mechanism by which driving to Sobha Hartland makes someone better at Physics Higher Level.

Worse, the premium often buys less subject knowledge rather than more, because it narrows the field to those within driving distance. At AED 350 an hour a Hartland family could be paying specialist rates for a tutor whose actual specialism is a different subject, and the only reason they are in the room is proximity. That is the compromise the home-visit model makes quietly, and the table below puts the two options side by side so you can see which column the money is actually buying.

sections.heading: Online against a home visit, compared on the things that decide a grade
paragraphs: A fair comparison needs to be about more than price, so here are the five variables that actually determine whether tutoring works: who is teaching, how much of the paid hour is teaching, when the session can start, what happens between sessions, and what happens when the schedule changes. Taken one at a time, four of the five favour online delivery from a Sobha Hartland address and one is genuinely mixed.

On who is teaching, online wins outright, and this page has already made the argument: the pool is the whole market rather than the drivable subset. On paid-hour efficiency, online wins because no part of the arrangement absorbs a commute, and a tutor who has driven through the corridor at 4pm arrives with less patience than they left with. On start time, online wins because the session can begin as soon as the student is home rather than when the tutor arrives.

On work between sessions, it is a draw in principle and online tends to win in practice, because written feedback and marked practice are easier to deliver and to keep than verbal comments in a living room. On scheduling, online wins comfortably: Ramadan timings, travel, examination weeks and school trips can all be absorbed without renegotiating a journey. The genuinely mixed variable is presence. Some students, especially younger ones, work better with a person beside them, and no amount of argument changes that. For a Diploma student working on paper technique it rarely decides anything. To be unambiguous: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so the choice is between our online delivery and an in-home arrangement you would make locally.

sections.heading: Subject by subject: where the supply is thin and what we do about it
paragraphs: Nobody else in this market publishes a coverage picture, which is strange, because it is the thing a parent is actually asking about when they ask whether anyone nearby knows the syllabus. So here it is, honestly. Some Diploma subjects are well covered in Dubai and some are not, and the pattern follows how many schools teach them rather than how difficult they are.

Mathematics and the sciences are comparatively well covered, because every school teaches them and the teaching population is large. English and Economics are reasonably covered. The thin areas are the ones a parent only discovers when they need them: Higher Level Paper 3 work in mathematics, individual sciences at Higher Level in combination with internal assessment supervision, second languages beyond the commonly taught ones, and the smaller group three and group six subjects. Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay supervision are thin everywhere, because almost nobody teaches them as a subject.

What we do when a subject is thin is tell you, before you book, and offer the real alternative rather than a nearby substitute. Usually that means a different time slot, occasionally a short wait, and sometimes a tutor based outside the UAE who teaches the same syllabus and works to Gulf Standard Time. What we do not do is put a Biology graduate in front of a Chemistry Higher Level student because the diary was tidier that way. The table sets out the picture as it stands, and it is a picture that changes, so treat it as a conversation starter rather than a guarantee.

sections.heading: What "knows the syllabus" actually means, and six ways to test it in one lesson
paragraphs: The phrase every tutoring site uses is syllabus knowledge, and it is almost never defined. For a Diploma subject it has a specific meaning, and a parent can test for all of it in a single trial lesson without understanding the subject themselves. The tests below are the ones we would apply to our own tutors, and we would rather you ran them than took a claim on trust.

A tutor who knows the syllabus knows the assessment structure in numbers: which papers exist, how long they are, what percentage each carries, and what the internal assessment is worth. They know the command terms and treat them as instructions rather than as synonyms. They know which topics recur and which are examined lightly. They know what the internal assessment criteria are called and roughly what each is worth. They know what a mark scheme rewards, which is why they talk about method rather than about answers.

And they know where this particular student is losing marks, which they can only know by looking at the student's own work. That last point is the real test. A tutor who spends the trial lesson explaining the subject in general terms is performing competence. A tutor who asks for a marked paper, reads it, and names the pattern is demonstrating it. Ask afterwards what is costing your child marks and judge the answer on its specificity, not its warmth. A warm tutor who cannot name the pattern will be pleasant company for a year and leave the grade where it was.
bullets: Can they state the paper structure and weightings from memory?
Do they treat command terms as instructions with different mark expectations?
Do they name the internal assessment criteria and what each rewards?
Did they ask for the student's own marked work before teaching anything?
Can they describe what the mark scheme gives credit for, not just the right answer?
Can they say what they will not do with assessed coursework?

sections.heading: The Diploma year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE IB schools sit the May examination session, and planning backwards from it is more useful than planning forwards from today, because the deadlines that actually constrain a student are set by the school rather than by the IB. Families routinely assume the opposite and are then surprised when an internal assessment deadline arrives months before anything the IB publishes.

Two cautions before using the table. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages. The IB holds those, and your child's Diploma coordinator holds the school's internal versions, which govern the internal assessments, the Extended Essay drafts and the Theory of Knowledge submissions. Confirm every date with the coordinator rather than with a tutoring website, this one included. And treat an internal deadline as firm from the moment it is announced, because schools do pull them forward.

Read practically, the calendar identifies two sensible entry points for tutoring and one bad one. The first good point is early in DP1, when subject foundations are cheap to repair and internal assessment questions have not yet been chosen badly. The second is immediately after the DP2 mock, when there is marked evidence to work from and eight to twelve weeks of usable time. The bad point is the fortnight before an internal assessment deadline, when the only honest help available is process advice and the student has already lost the time that mattered. A tutor who takes that booking without saying so is taking your money for a problem that can no longer be solved.

sections.heading: KHDA, the Hartland schools and the mandatory UAE subjects nobody mentions
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Inspection runs annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, published school by school. For a Hartland parent the secondary commentary inside a report is worth more than the headline band, because a strong department can sit inside an averagely rated school and the reverse is also true.

The sector is growing, which eventually eases the supply problem this page describes. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. More IB schools means more IB teachers in the city, which is the only thing that genuinely widens the pool for evening tutoring. KHDA also confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

Something families new to Dubai often miss: the mandatory UAE subjects run alongside the Diploma rather than instead of it. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. It requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. For a Diploma student that is real timetable pressure in an already full year.

On credentials, plainly: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or IB accredited, and does not claim to be. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. KHDA separately requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic in schools hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential question for a school rather than for a tutoring service. Any service advertising KHDA-approved tutors is describing something else or saying something untrue.

sections.heading: The internal assessment, the Extended Essay, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries an internal assessment, and together with the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay that is a large share of the final result sitting in work the student must produce themselves. It is also where tutoring most often goes wrong. At least one operator ranking for UAE IB queries sells completed Internal Assessments outright, at a published price. That is not a service tier. It is academic misconduct under IB rules, and the student bears the consequence, which can be the loss of the Diploma.

What a tutor may do is substantial and worth paying for. They may explain the assessment criteria in the language the examiner uses. They may question a research question until it is narrow enough to answer with the resources available. They may point out that a planned method will produce too little data, or that a chosen text will not sustain four thousand words. They may teach the underlying subject content. They may read a draft the student has written and say where the reasoning is thin, where the evaluation is missing, and where a conclusion outruns the evidence.

What a tutor may not do is choose the question, supply the method or the data, write any part of the text, or edit a draft into its final form. Nor may they hand over a worked example so close to the student's own task that copying becomes the obvious next step. We state these boundaries to the student in the first session, because a sixteen-year-old under deadline pressure deserves to know where the line is before they are standing on it. We also do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we reference them and link to the official source.

sections.heading: Getting started from Sobha Hartland, and what we say when nobody is free
paragraphs: Begin with the subject and the level rather than with the word IB. Tell us which subject, whether it is Higher or Standard, the mock grade, and what the teacher's last report said. Add what time the school day ends, because in this corridor that varies by school and it sets the window a session can occupy. Those four pieces of information change who we propose; the word IB on its own does not.

We then propose a tutor and run a free trial lesson, which is a diagnosis rather than a sales call. Run the six tests from earlier in this page on whoever takes it. The tutor should finish able to tell you specifically what is costing marks, and you should finish knowing whether your child will work with this person weekly without resistance. If not, say so and we propose someone else. A match a teenager merely tolerates does not survive to the second term.

And the honest part. Diploma teaching capacity is limited and some subjects, as the coverage table shows, are limited in ways that will affect your booking. When the right tutor is not free at your preferred time, we say so and offer a different slot, a short wait, or a tutor outside the UAE teaching the same syllabus to Gulf Standard Time. We will not substitute a related subject or a related level and let you discover it in week three. If none of the alternatives suits, you have lost nothing but an email, because the trial lesson is free and comes first.

process.title: Name the subject and the level, not the programme
process.description: Chemistry Higher Level and Chemistry Standard Level are different jobs, and Theory of Knowledge is a third. Send the subject, the level, the mock grade and the teacher's last comment. That is what determines who we propose; the word IB on its own narrows nothing.

process.title: We match on the subject, not the drive
process.description: Because lessons are online, the shortlist is drawn from every available specialist in that subject rather than from those willing to drive to Hartland at 4pm. We tell you who the tutor is and why they fit this gap before any lesson is booked.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then the six tests
process.description: The first session costs nothing and its job is to find the problem. Ask afterwards what specifically is costing marks, whether they asked for the student's own work, and what they will refuse to do with coursework. If the answers are vague, do not book the block.

process.title: Set a slot that survives the school run
process.description: School days in this corridor end between roughly 2:45pm and 3:30pm, and the drive from Al Barsha or Al Quoz eats the afternoon. We fix a time that works in term and revisit it for Ramadan, mock weeks and travel rather than assuming it holds for a year.

process.title: Practice set, practice marked
process.description: Each session ends with named past-paper work and the next begins with it marked against the published criteria. Unmarked practice is the commonest reason a weekly arrangement changes nothing, and checking that it happens needs no subject knowledge from you.

process.title: Review against the calendar and stop when done
process.description: Every few weeks the plan is checked against the Diploma year: internal assessment deadlines, mocks, the final block. Intensity rises for a defined period before the session and falls afterwards, and when a gap is closed we say so rather than renewing by default.

whyPoints.title: The supply problem stated, not hidden
whyPoints.description: We tell you that IB teaching in Dubai is concentrated near IB schools and that it is subject-specific. Every other page in this market implies a local specialist is waiting. Knowing the real constraint is what lets you make a sensible decision.

whyPoints.title: Coverage published subject by subject
whyPoints.description: Our coverage table says which Diploma areas are well served, which are thin, and what the fallback is when nobody local is free. No competitor in this market discloses a coverage limit, and several conceal non-UAE delivery behind a local-looking number.

whyPoints.title: AED figures with named sources
whyPoints.description: The home-visit and online bands on this page carry the provider that published each one and the month we read it. They are market context, not our price list, which follows a free trial lesson and an honest count of the sessions needed.

whyPoints.title: Six tests you can run yourself
whyPoints.description: Rather than asking you to trust a claim about syllabus knowledge, we give you the questions that test it in one lesson. Apply them to us as well as to anyone else you are considering.

whyPoints.title: The coursework line stated to the student
whyPoints.description: Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work. We say what we will and will not do in the first session, to the student, not in small print at the bottom of a page.

whyPoints.title: No borrowed credentials
whyPoints.description: We explain what KHDA does and link to its own material. We do not describe IB Gram or any tutor as KHDA approved, ADEK approved or IB accredited, because none of that is true of us and the phrase is the most common untruth in this market.

faqs.question: Are there any IB tutors who actually live in Sobha Hartland?
faqs.answer: A few, and not in the subjects most families need. IB teachers in Dubai live near the schools that employ them, and the Diploma is not one subject but six plus three core components, so the realistic question is whether a Chemistry Higher Level or Theory of Knowledge specialist lives within a short drive. Usually not. Rather than matching your child to whoever is both competent and close, we match on the subject and level and deliver the lesson one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: Do your tutors travel to homes in Sobha Hartland?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video throughout the UAE, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. We are explicit about it because the phrase home tutor is what parents search and it would be easy to leave the impression ambiguous. If a person in the room is non-negotiable for your child, a local in-home arrangement is the right choice and this page gives you the market rates to judge it by. For a Diploma student working on paper technique, online delivery usually produces the better-matched tutor.

faqs.question: What does a home tutor cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: In-home one-to-one in Dubai runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, and the figure includes travel. Advertised monthly in-home packages sit around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Online equivalents are lower: about AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor, AED 200 to 450 and above for a specialist, and around AED 799 a month for an eight-session package. Those are other providers' published figures read in October 2026, each attributed in the table on this page, and they are market context rather than our prices.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a tutor really knows my child's Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: Test six things in the trial lesson. Can they state the paper structure and weightings from memory? Do they treat command terms as instructions with different mark expectations? Can they name the internal assessment criteria and what each rewards? Did they ask for your child's own marked work before teaching anything? Can they describe what the mark scheme credits rather than just the right answer? And can they say what they will refuse to do with assessed coursework? A tutor who passes all six is demonstrating knowledge rather than claiming it.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects are hardest to find a tutor for in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay supervision are thin everywhere, because almost nobody teaches them as a standalone subject. Higher Level mathematics including Paper 3 is thinner than Standard Level. Individual sciences at Higher Level combined with internal assessment supervision are harder than the same subject without it. Second languages beyond the commonly taught ones are genuinely scarce. Mathematics at Standard Level, the main sciences, English A and Economics are comparatively well covered. We publish this picture before you book rather than discovering it together afterwards.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is available in my child's subject?
faqs.answer: We tell you, which is not the market norm. The options are a different time slot, a short wait while we look, or a tutor based outside the UAE who teaches the same syllabus and works to Gulf Standard Time. What we will not do is substitute a related subject or a different level and let you discover it in week three. If none of the alternatives suits, nothing has been lost, because the trial lesson is free and comes before any commitment. Several competitors in this market conceal non-UAE delivery entirely, which is the practice we are reacting to.

faqs.question: Is online tuition genuinely as effective for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: For paper technique, internal assessment feedback and subject teaching, yes, and often better, because the tutor is chosen for the subject rather than for the journey. Written feedback and marked practice are easier to deliver and to keep than verbal comments in a living room. The honest exception is presence: some students, particularly younger ones, work better with someone beside them, and that is a real preference rather than a misconception. For a sixteen-year-old working on a Higher Level paper it rarely decides the outcome, and the wider tutor pool usually does.

faqs.question: How many subjects can we get tutoring in at once?
faqs.answer: As many as genuinely need it, but rarely as many as a worried parent first asks for. A Diploma student already has six subjects, three core components and school homework, so adding three weekly tutoring sessions can make the week worse rather than better. In most cases one or two subjects carry the problem and the rest are collateral: a maths weakness showing up in Physics, or a writing weakness showing up in two essay subjects. We would rather fix the underlying one and review in a month.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's internal assessment without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within boundaries we state to the student in the first session. A tutor may explain the criteria, question a research question until it is answerable, warn that a method will generate too little data, teach the underlying content, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not choose the question, supply the method or data, write any of the text, or edit a draft into its final form. Submitting work that is not the student's own is misconduct under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student.

faqs.question: When do IB students in Dubai sit their exams?
faqs.answer: UAE IB schools overwhelmingly sit the May session, which suits an academic year starting in late August or early September. A November session exists for parts of the world where the year runs the other way round. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages, because the IB holds those and we will not have a parent act on a date taken from a tutoring site. Your child's Diploma coordinator has the school's version of the calendar, including the internal assessment deadlines that constrain the year most.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and can I check?
faqs.answer: Yes, and asking is reasonable. MoHRE issues a private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you see quoted as unverified.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school teacher tutor them privately instead?
faqs.answer: It is usually the wrong arrangement and in Abu Dhabi it is prohibited. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat the detail as press-reported and verify against current policy before relying on it. Beyond the rules, a second opinion from outside the school is often more useful than more of the same explanation.

faqs.question: Do the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons affect a Diploma timetable?
faqs.answer: They do, and families new to Dubai are often surprised. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Separate classes are required for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of these subjects, and instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. For a Diploma student the practical effect is fewer free periods than the programme assumes, which is worth factoring into any tutoring schedule.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan or while we are travelling?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the clearer practical advantages of online delivery. During Ramadan sessions commonly shift to a post-Iftar slot, which is simple when there is no journey to renegotiate. When a family travels, the lesson follows the student rather than the address, so two weeks away does not cost two weeks of a subject. Agree in advance which time zone the session is pinned to, so a student abroad is not sitting a Higher Level lesson at six in the morning, and tell us early enough that the slot can be held.

faqs.question: My child is in DP1 and coping. Is tutoring premature?
faqs.answer: Often it is, and we will say so. The exception worth considering is the subject where a Higher Level choice was made on enthusiasm rather than on prior attainment, because that gap widens through DP1 and is cheapest to close early. The other exception is the internal assessment question, where one session spent narrowing a research question prevents a term of work on something unanswerable. Beyond those, a coping DP1 student usually needs time rather than tuition, and buying weekly sessions in September that nobody has diagnosed is how families overspend.

faqs.question: What should I send you to get a useful recommendation?
faqs.answer: Four things, and a photograph of a marked paper beats all of them. The subject and whether it is Higher or Standard Level. The most recent grade, with whether it came from a mock or classwork. The teacher's last written comment, quoted rather than summarised. And the time the school day ends, because that sets which slots are realistic from Sobha Hartland. With those, we can usually propose a tutor the same day and tell you honestly whether the subject is one of the thinly covered ones.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.closingHeading: Ask for the subject specialist, not the nearest tutor
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.closingBody: The search that brought you here asks about distance. The thing that changes your child's grade is whether the person teaching them knows the Diploma subject at the level they are sitting it. In Sobha Hartland those two requirements rarely point at the same person, and we would rather tell you that than imply otherwise. Send the subject, the level, the latest grade and the teacher's last comment, and we will propose a tutor and run the first session free. Then run the six tests on them, and on us.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-tecom.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects to students living in the TECOM and Barsha Heights towers. Rates are quoted per subject and level before anything is booked, and the first lesson is free, so the cost conversation happens before the teaching rather than after it.

intro.heading: Pricing two years, not one hour
paragraphs: Almost every tutoring conversation in Dubai starts with an hourly rate, and almost every tutoring budget is blown by something else. A TECOM family hiring at AED 220 an hour thinks they are buying a AED 880 month. What they actually commit to, once a second subject appears in DP1, the Internal Assessments arrive in DP2, and the pre-mock panic adds a weekly extra session, is a figure several times that across two years. Nobody is being dishonest. The hourly frame simply hides the shape of the spend.

So this page does the arithmetic the other way round. It starts from the two-year Diploma total, works back to the monthly figure, and then shows where the money actually goes. It itemises the travel premium, because in a tower district an in-home visit is priced with the commute inside the hour and that commute is a Sheikh Zayed Road commute. And it names the six specific ways families in Barsha Heights overspend, all of which are avoidable and none of which involve choosing a cheaper tutor.

The figures here are market figures. EdFlik advertises online tuition from AED 45 to 65 an hour. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table shows in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, and monthly estimates for a weekly hour at AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. BartyED advertises AED 650. Every one of those belongs to the provider that published it in 2026, with the source stated, and none of them is an IB Gram price.

Context helps. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family in TECOM that means the largest education line in the household budget is flat this year and the tutoring line is the one still moving. Getting that line right is worth more attention than it usually receives.

One thing to settle before any of the numbers matter. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to any school or examination board, and tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. The in-home market in Dubai is real, other providers price it, and this page quotes those prices honestly so you can see what the travel actually costs.
