dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-lakes.programmesIntro: The IB runs as a continuum, and the scheduling problem changes at each stage. A PYP child has an evening; a DP2 student has a calendar. Here is what each stage demands of a Lakes weeknight.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher Level and three Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Externally examined in the May session for UAE schools, with internal assessments marked by teachers and moderated by the IB. The time problem is that the core work has no timetabled slot and competes directly with the evening a tutor wants.
programmes.countryNote: In The Lakes, DP students are typically at schools in Al Barsha, Al Sufouh or Emirates Hills and home by 16:30 on a good day. One or two weekly hours fit; three does not, unless one of them lands at the weekend. DP2 autumn is the pressure point, when internal assessment deadlines and the Extended Essay converge on the same fortnight.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four published criteria each, every criterion marked from 0 to 8 and combined into a grade from 1 to 7. MYP 5 carries the Personal Project. There is no external examination unless the school enters students for optional eAssessment, so the calendar pressure is internal deadlines rather than a published exam window.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students in The Lakes have more evening left than their Diploma siblings and more sport in it. A 17:00 or 17:30 slot usually holds better than a 16:30 one, because the activity block is what moves, not the bus. Families with an MYP and a DP child in the same villa should stagger rather than stack.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary learning across transdisciplinary themes, finishing with the Year 6 Exhibition. No external assessment and no grades in the MYP sense, so the useful questions are specific: reading fluency, number fact recall, and whether written work has a structure the next programme will assume.
programmes.countryNote: Primary finish times in Emirates Living are earlier, which makes a 15:30 or 16:00 slot possible for a younger child before the secondary bus arrives. Lakes households with children at both ends often run the primary lesson first and the Diploma lesson after dinner, which is the only arrangement that fits both into one evening.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: The Diploma core carries up to three bonus points from the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Extended Essay together, and CAS is a completion requirement rather than a graded one. None of it is taught in a daily timetabled lesson, so the work lands in the evening - the same evening a subject tutor wants - and that collision is the most common scheduling failure in DP2.
programmes.countryNote: Lakes families routinely discover the Extended Essay problem in October of DP2, when the school's internal deadline and two internal assessments arrive together. Booking core coaching as a short block at three decision points, rather than as a weekly slot, is what keeps the subject hours intact through that fortnight.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-lakes.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Lakes families ask for most, with the component that usually eats the evening named for each. The scheduling consequence is in the description, because that is what this page is about.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route Higher Level sciences and engineering courses expect. Paper 3 at Higher Level is an extended investigation under time pressure, and it is the component that needs a long, undisturbed slot rather than a tired half hour. Best scheduled as a weekend morning in DP2 if the weekday evening is already full.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology-heavy and modelling-led, with a graphical display calculator assumed throughout. Sessions need the actual calculator in the student's hand, not a laptop emulator, which is worth checking before the first lesson. The exploration is the piece that overruns and should be coached in blocks.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Problem-solving under time pressure, and the subject where Lakes students most often arrive with the content learned and the technique missing. Needs a full hour with past-paper questions timed, which rules out the 16:00 slot for a student who has just stepped off a bus from Al Barsha South.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and the energetics topics carry most of the lost marks at Higher Level. The internal assessment is a single investigation with a strict honesty boundary: a tutor questions the design and reads the student's draft, and writes none of it. Fits a weekday evening better than maths does.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume-heavy, with command terms doing more work than students expect. Short, frequent sessions beat long ones, so two 45-minute slots a week often fit a Lakes timetable where one 90-minute block does not. Data-based questions are the fastest marks to recover.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the evaluation paragraph decide most grades. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries built on news articles, which students leave late and then write in the same week as something else. Deadline-led, so plan the term rather than the week.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study based, with tool application marked more strictly than tool recall. Higher Level students sit a pre-released case study that rewards structured preparation across months, making this a subject where a steady weekly hour genuinely outperforms a pre-exam sprint.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis against time, and the Individual Oral is a rehearsed assessment that benefits from recorded practice. Both need a quiet room and a working microphone, which in a villa with younger siblings means the slot matters more than the subject.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Four skills assessed, with the productive ones carrying the marks that move. Speaking practice is the component families most often skip because it feels awkward at home; over video with a tutor it is simply the lesson, and it is where the quickest improvement sits.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies have to be recalled precisely and used as evidence rather than retold. The internal assessment is a replication of a simple experiment with a strict format, and the write-up is where students lose marks. A short coaching block beats a weekly slot for that component.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-lakes.regionsTitle: The Lakes clusters and the communities around them
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-lakes.regionsIntro: Each cluster inside The Lakes sits on a different bus loop, and the loop decides what time a lesson can start. These are the practical differences a timetable has to account for.

regions.name: Deema
regions.note: Towards the Emirates Golf Club side, usually earlier on the loop out and earlier back. A 16:15 start is realistic here on a normal school day, which makes it the one cluster where an early slot holds.

regions.name: Forat
regions.note: Mid-loop and close to the community centre, so the bus arrives after Deema and before Hattan. Households here commonly settle on 16:45, which also absorbs a fifteen-minute delay without collapsing the lesson.

regions.name: Ghadeer
regions.note: Backs onto the lake frontage with a longer internal drive. Parents who collect by car rather than use the bus often get back earlier than the bus families, so the workable slot depends on which the household uses.

regions.name: Hattan
regions.note: Largest villas and the furthest internal stop on several routes. Expect the child through the door nearer 16:40 than 16:00, which is why a 17:00 slot is the standard recommendation for Hattan households.

regions.name: Maeen
regions.note: Compact and close to the exit onto Sheikh Zayed Road, so car collection is quick and bus drop-off is late. Siblings at different schools frequently arrive forty minutes apart here, which forces staggered sessions.

regions.name: Zulal
regions.note: Quietest cluster and the one where families most often report the child doing activities straight after school rather than coming home. Later slots dominate, and a 18:00 lesson is normal rather than unusual.

regions.name: The Meadows
regions.note: Next door and sharing several bus routes, with Emirates International School Meadows inside the community. Lakes families with a child at that school get the earliest start times available in Emirates Living.

regions.name: Emirates Hills
regions.note: Feeds Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills and Dubai British School Emirates Hills. Short commute, so the constraint for these students is the activity block rather than the bus.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Apartment stock on the Marina side, closer to the Al Sufouh corridor. Shorter journeys but a noisier home environment, which makes the quiet-room question a real part of planning an online lesson.

schoolClusters.city: The Al Barsha and Al Barsha South corridor
schoolClusters.note: Where the largest share of Lakes secondary students study. Secondary days in Dubai commonly end between 14:45 and 15:30, and the return bus into Emirates Living at that hour is what sets the earliest realistic lesson time. Confirm your own school's bell times before fixing a slot.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Living and Emirates Hills
schoolClusters.note: The schools reachable without crossing Sheikh Zayed Road, and the only ones that give a Lakes household a genuinely early evening. A child walking or driving back from inside Emirates Living can hold a 16:15 slot that a bussed child cannot.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh and the Marina corridor
schoolClusters.note: Reached down Al Sufouh Road, with the return leg crossing the busiest stretch of the afternoon. Students here are frequently the last home in a Lakes household, which is why a sibling pair at different schools almost always needs two different slots.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-lakes.modesIntro: Three formats, each chosen for how it fits an evening rather than for what it sounds like. All IB Gram teaching in the UAE is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video.

modes.title: The fixed weekday evening slot
modes.description: One hour a week, same day, same tutor, set after your school's actual finish time plus a buffer. The buffer is the point: a slot set at the earliest theoretically possible minute gets moved three times and then quietly stops. Lakes households usually land on 16:45 or 17:00 for a bussed secondary student.

modes.title: Weekend morning for the long components
modes.description: Some work does not fit a tired weekday hour. Higher Level Paper 3 investigations, timed unseen analysis for English Paper 1, and full past papers under exam conditions need a clear ninety minutes with a fresh student. A Saturday or Sunday morning slot is where those belong, and running one weekend session plus one weekday hour beats two weekday hours in DP2.

modes.title: Core coaching in short blocks
modes.description: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are deadline-driven rather than weekly. Three or four coaching sessions placed at the planning stage, the first full draft and the reflection are worth more than a standing slot, and they cost less in total. The student writes; the tutor questions, reads and marks against the criteria.

sections.heading: What a home-tutor search from a Lakes villa actually returns
paragraphs: Type the phrase and you will get three kinds of result. Agencies that will quote a visit at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour and send whoever is free within a twenty-minute drive. Classified listings from individual tutors, where the rate is lower and the vetting is yours to do. And online platforms, which is what IB Gram is, teaching one-to-one over live video at the AED 150 to AED 300 band for an equivalently qualified tutor. All three are legitimate purchases. They are not the same purchase.

The question worth asking first is not which is cheaper but which can actually supply the subject. A Diploma student takes three Higher Level subjects, and a Higher Level Chemistry specialist, a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialist and a Higher Level History specialist do not live in the same neighbourhood. An in-home arrangement in The Lakes gives you whoever is geographically available for each one, which in practice means one good match and two compromises. A video lesson gives you the specialist for all three.

The second question is about the clock, and it is the one this page is built around. In-home tutoring in Emirates Living is priced with the drive inside it, and that drive happens during the worst part of the Dubai afternoon. The tutor who has to be in Hattan at 16:30 leaves Al Barsha at 16:00 and arrives flustered or late. The lesson that starts fifteen minutes late ends on time, so you have bought forty-five minutes at the sixty-minute rate, every week, for a year.

So the honest position. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service and nobody arrives at a Lakes address under any arrangement we sell. The phrase in the heading is the phrase parents type, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. The answer is that the thing you want - a specialist teaching your child one-to-one in your own house, at a time that works - is available, over video, and the comparison two sections down sets out exactly what you gain and what you give up.

sections.heading: The Lakes weekday, bell to screen
paragraphs: Dubai secondary days commonly end between 14:45 and 15:30, and most Dubai private schools now run a Monday-to-Friday week after the 2022 change, with a shortened Friday. Between the final bell and a child sitting down at a desk in The Lakes there is a bus queue, a loop with several stops, and the Al Barsha or Al Sufouh afternoon. The table below sets out what that adds up to, by catchment, so a slot can be chosen from evidence rather than optimism.

Read it as a floor rather than a timetable. The earliest column is the earliest a lesson can start on a normal day with nothing going wrong. A slot set at that minute will be missed whenever the bus is late, a club overruns or a sibling needs collecting, and three missed starts is usually the end of a weekly arrangement. The working recommendation in Emirates Living is to add fifteen minutes to the floor and then protect that time absolutely.

Two patterns show up repeatedly in Lakes households. First, the child who attends school inside Emirates Living is home nearly an hour before the child bussed from Al Barsha South, so sibling pairs at different schools need staggered slots rather than a shared evening. Second, the activity block does more damage than traffic does: a swim squad or a football academy on two evenings removes those evenings entirely, and the family that books around them rather than hoping keeps the arrangement alive.

One practical note on the room. An online lesson needs a screen the student can write beside, a microphone that works, and a door. In a villa with younger siblings the dining table at 17:00 is not that place. Families who set up a fixed corner - desk, headset, calculator, the school's own textbook - lose less of each lesson to logistics than families who relocate every week. It is a small thing that compounds across forty sessions.

sections.heading: What the travel premium buys, and what it costs you
paragraphs: The in-home premium is real and it is quantifiable. Dubai in-home visits are published at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 rate work placing the common band at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent listings running to AED 500. An equivalently qualified tutor teaching online is quoted at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE support from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and TutorChase quoting AED 270 for specialist work. The gap is the car, not the credential.

What the premium genuinely buys is worth stating fairly. A person in the room can see a student's page without asking them to hold it up, can stop a phone being picked up, and does not depend on the household's internet. For a younger child who will not sit still, or a student who needs supervision as much as teaching, that is a real purchase and some Lakes families should make it. Nobody should pretend otherwise.

What it costs is the tutor pool and the clock. Inside a twenty-minute radius of Emirates Living there are a limited number of tutors who can teach Higher Level Physics to a DP2 student, and in a given term some of them are full. The in-home model asks you to take the best available within that radius; the video model asks you to take the best available for the subject. Over three Higher Level subjects, that difference is larger than the hourly rate difference, and it compounds across two years.

The table puts the two side by side on the dimensions that actually differ for a Lakes household. It is a comparison of delivery models rather than of named companies, and the rates in it are other providers' published figures read in October 2026. IB Gram sells only the online column; the in-home column is there because it is the honest alternative and because a parent typing this search deserves to see both sets of numbers before choosing.

sections.heading: DP1 and DP2 need different weeks, not different tutors
paragraphs: The most common scheduling mistake in The Lakes is booking the same weekly hour for two years. DP1 and DP2 are not the same job. DP1 is content acquisition with internal assessments appearing towards the end; DP2 is deadlines first, then revision, then examinations, with the core work colliding with everything in the autumn. The sensible hour count changes across the two years, and so does what that hour should contain.

In DP1, one weekly hour per difficult subject is usually right, and the content is the content: building the topics as the school teaches them, with past-paper questions used to check rather than to cram. The useful addition is a short block in the spring on whichever internal assessment the school starts first, normally a science investigation or the Mathematics exploration. That block is three or four sessions, not a new standing slot, and it prevents the autumn pile-up in DP2.

DP2 autumn is the fortnight that breaks timetables. Internal assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay draft and the Theory of Knowledge essay all land within a few weeks of each other at most Dubai schools, and the subject tutoring hour gets cannibalised to deal with them. The fix is to plan for it: move core coaching into blocks placed at the known deadlines, keep the subject hour, and accept that for three weeks the subject hour will be used for the subject's internal assessment rather than for new content.

From January in DP2, the shape changes again. Timed practice under conditions becomes the most valuable hour of the week, and it needs ninety minutes with a fresh student rather than sixty with a tired one. That is the point where a weekend morning slot earns its place and a second weekday evening does not. The table sets out the whole two years, term by term, with an hour count that a Lakes evening can actually absorb.

sections.heading: Two children, one router, one evening
paragraphs: Lakes villas commonly hold two or three school-age children, and the evening they share is finite. The arithmetic is unforgiving: two one-hour lessons between 16:45 and 19:00, with dinner in the middle, works only if the two slots are genuinely staggered and both students have somewhere to sit. Stacking them back to back in the same room produces one good lesson and one in which somebody is listening to the other lesson.

Start from the arrival times rather than from preference. A child at Emirates International School Meadows is home around 15:30; a sibling bussed from Al Barsha South arrives closer to 16:30. That hour of difference is the staggering, free of charge: the younger child takes 16:00, the older takes 17:15, and the evening holds. Households that ignore the arrival gap end up with both lessons after 18:00, and the second one is taught to a tired student.

The technical side is smaller than families expect but not nothing. Two simultaneous video lessons on a domestic connection are generally fine; two in the same room are not, because the microphones fight. Headsets solve it for under a few hundred dirhams. What matters more is that each student has a surface to write on beside the screen and a door that closes, because the lesson a tutor can see into is the lesson they can actually mark.

One scheduling rule saves more Lakes arrangements than any other: do not give two children the same tutor to save money unless the subjects and the weak points genuinely overlap. A tutor alternating between an MYP 3 science criterion and a DP2 Chemistry internal assessment is running two unrelated jobs in fortnightly instalments and will end up supervising homework for both. Two tutors, two slots, two diagnoses is the arrangement that survives a full year.
bullets: Use the natural arrival gap between schools as the stagger
Headsets, not separate rooms, solve two lessons at once

sections.heading: The Monday-to-Friday week, the short Friday, and where the weekend went
paragraphs: Dubai's school week changed and the tutoring week has not caught up. Most private schools in the emirate now run Monday to Friday with a shortened Friday, though a small number kept a Sunday-to-Thursday pattern, so the first thing to check is your own school's calendar rather than a general rule. What follows from the common pattern is that Friday afternoon became the most under-used teaching slot in the city and Saturday morning became the most contested one.

A shortened Friday puts a secondary student home by about 12:15 to 13:15. That is a fresh student with an entire afternoon in front of them, and it is the single best slot in a Lakes week for anything that needs ninety undisturbed minutes: a full past paper under conditions, a Higher Level Paper 3 investigation, an unseen analysis for English Paper 1. Families who use it get their timed practice done without touching a weekday evening.

Saturday morning is the slot everyone wants, which means it goes first and it competes with sport. Sunday is quieter and, for a Monday-to-Friday school, has the advantage of landing the day before the school week restarts, so work done on Sunday is still in the student's head on Monday. For a household running one weekday hour plus one longer session, Friday afternoon or Sunday morning is usually the better second slot, and both are easier to book than Saturday.

The holiday question follows the same logic. The long Dubai summer and the winter break are when most Lakes families travel, and because lessons are over live video the timetable can follow a trip rather than pausing for it - subject to a time-zone conversation if the family is far west. A pause is also perfectly reasonable and costs nothing structurally. The only break worth protecting is the one before DP1 starts, where six weeks of bridging work changes the following year.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the examination term in the same calendar
paragraphs: Ramadan reshapes a Lakes evening completely, and a tutoring arrangement that ignores it loses a month. School days shorten, the household eats after sunset, and the hours between the end of school and iftar are low-energy for a fasting student. The practical answer is to move the slot rather than to pause: either a late-morning or early-afternoon session when the school day has ended early, or a post-iftar slot once the family has eaten.

Post-iftar works better than most families expect for Diploma students, because it is quiet, the student has eaten, and there is no bus to catch afterwards. It does not work for younger children, who are usually finished for the day by then. A household with both should expect to run the MYP child in the early afternoon and the DP student after iftar during that month, which is a different shape from the rest of the year and needs setting up before Ramadan starts, not during it.

The timing matters more in some years than others because Ramadan moves earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, which changes how close it sits to the spring examination term. In a year where it falls near the mock examinations or the final weeks before the May session, the sensible plan is to front-load revision into the weeks before it and to use Ramadan for lighter, shorter, more frequent sessions rather than for ninety-minute timed papers.

Two adjacent calendar facts are worth having in front of you. Cambridge runs its International GCSE and International A Level examinations in June and November series, with centres allocated to one of six administrative zones and a warning that the correct zone timetable must be used. Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November series and publishes provisional timetables in advance. For the IB, no session or results date is published on this page: confirm your child's dates with the school's IB coordinator or on the IB's own site.
bullets: Set the Ramadan slot before Ramadan starts, not in the first week of it

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
paragraphs: This is the part of a Diploma arrangement where a tutor can do real harm, so the boundary is worth stating in full rather than gesturing at. The Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay are assessed work that must be the student's own, submitted with a declaration to that effect. The student has a supervisor at school. A tutor is an additional reader, and an additional reader has a narrow and genuinely useful role.

What that role contains: questioning whether a research question is answerable in 4,000 words; checking that the methodology will produce evidence rather than opinion; reading a draft the student has written and saying which assessment criterion is not yet met; rehearsing the reflection sessions so the student can discuss their own process; and teaching the difference between describing a source and evaluating one. That work is coaching, it is permitted, and it is where most of the recoverable marks sit.

What it does not contain: a tutor never writes the Extended Essay, never drafts a Theory of Knowledge essay, and never rewrites a student's paragraph into their own prose. Line-editing a draft until the words are the tutor's is authorship by instalment, and the IB treats authorship as the student's responsibility. A submission that is not the student's own work is a malpractice matter with consequences for the student, not a service complaint against a provider. Providers in this market do sell finished coursework; that is the risk being sold.

The practical test for a Lakes parent is simple. Ask the tutor what they will send back after reading a draft. The right answer is questions, criterion references and a list of what the student needs to decide. The wrong answer is a marked-up document with replacement sentences in it. Both look like help; only one of them leaves the student able to defend the work in a reflection session with their own supervisor.

sections.heading: Starting from The Lakes, and what we cannot promise
paragraphs: The start is short. Tell us the school, the year, the subjects and - most usefully for this page - what time the student is genuinely through the door. We come back with a tutor who teaches that subject at that level and a slot that sits after the bus with a buffer. The trial lesson is free, covers one subject, and takes no card details, and you decide afterwards whether the match is right.

The limit is availability, and it is worth hearing before you book rather than after. For mainstream Diploma subjects a match usually takes a few days. For a narrow combination - Higher Level Philosophy, a less common Language B, Music, or an unusual Higher and Standard pairing that needs one tutor - it can take longer, and the tutor may be based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time. We say which, and from where, before anything is agreed. No provider researched in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

What we will not do is promise an outcome. No grade, no point total, no improvement figure, and nobody can honestly offer one. What is measurable is narrower and more useful: the criterion or component targeted, the work marked between sessions, and whether the mark on that component moved by the review point at six sessions. If it has not, the options include changing the focus, changing the tutor, or stopping, and we will say which we think it is.

One last practical matter. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a permit: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years to a wide list of eligible categories. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, Ministry, IB or Cambridge accreditation and claims none; the regulators are named on this page to explain what each governs, not as a badge.

process.title: Tell us the clock, not just the subject
process.description: The most useful first message names the school, the year, the subject and the time the student is actually through the door in The Lakes. A tutor matched to a 16:30 slot that was never realistic is a tutor you will replace in six weeks, so the arrival time does more work than the subject label does.

process.description: A tutor who teaches that subject at that level and who is free in the window your evening has, on Gulf Standard Time. If the subject is narrow we say how long the match will take and whether the tutor is UAE-based or teaching in from elsewhere, before you agree to anything.

process.title: Free trial lesson, one subject, no card
process.description: Sixty minutes with the student's own work on screen. You are checking two things: whether the tutor finds the same weakness the school's reports do, and whether the time of day worked for your child. Both answers are clearer after one lesson than after any amount of discussion.

process.title: Fix the slot and build in the buffer
process.description: The agreed slot sits fifteen minutes after the realistic door time, and it is protected. School trips, tournaments and travel move a session rather than cancelling it. During Ramadan the slot shifts, including to post-iftar for Diploma students, and that shift is agreed in advance.

process.title: Review at six sessions, with stopping allowed
process.description: Before the second lesson we write down the component being targeted and how you will know it moved. At six sessions we look at the mark on that component. The honest options are continue, change focus, change tutor, or stop, and we will tell you which one we think applies.

whyPoints.title: The timetable is designed around your bus, not ours
whyPoints.description: Slots are set from the school's actual finish time plus the return journey into The Lakes plus a buffer. That is why our sessions are still running in March. A lesson scheduled at the earliest theoretically possible minute is a lesson that gets moved three times and then abandoned.

whyPoints.title: The specialist, not the nearest available person
whyPoints.description: Because the lesson is over video, the tutor is chosen for teaching your child's subject at your child's level. A Diploma student with three Higher Level subjects needs three specialists, and three specialists do not live within twenty minutes of Emirates Living. That is the whole of the argument.

whyPoints.title: In-home rates published, not hidden
whyPoints.description: The Dubai in-home band of AED 180 to AED 500 an hour is printed on this page alongside the online band of AED 150 to AED 300, with each figure attributed to the provider or rate study that published it in 2026. Three of the six competitor pages researched in this market publish no price at all.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line on the core, written down
whyPoints.description: A tutor questions a research question, reads what the student wrote and names the criterion that is not yet met. No Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or internal assessment is produced for a student. The test is what comes back after a draft: questions, or replacement sentences.

whyPoints.title: Sessions move rather than disappear
whyPoints.description: Emirates Living runs on tournaments, school trips and travel. A missed session is rescheduled within the same week where the tutor's diary allows, and the Ramadan shift is agreed before Ramadan begins rather than improvised during it.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits stated before you book
whyPoints.description: Where no UAE-based specialist is free for a narrow Diploma subject we say so and name the alternative, including when the tutor is outside the UAE teaching into your evening. That disclosure is the opposite of the practice in this market, where non-local delivery is routinely concealed.

faqs.question: Will an IB home tutor actually come to our villa in The Lakes?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; villa visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons for Lakes families are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen and the student's work marked during the lesson. Agencies in Dubai do sell in-home visits, at a published AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 for an equivalently qualified tutor online. The difference is travel, and the comparison table on this page sets out what that premium buys and what it costs you.

faqs.question: What time can a DP2 student living in The Lakes realistically start a weekday lesson?
faqs.answer: If they attend school inside Emirates Living, about 16:00. If they are bussed from Al Barsha or Al Barsha South, 16:45 is the first slot that holds. From Al Sufouh, the Marina corridor or the Motor City belt, 17:00. Those are floors on a normal day, so add fifteen minutes and protect that time. Dubai secondary days commonly end between 14:45 and 15:30, and the return loop into The Lakes is the variable. Hattan and Zulal households, being furthest along several internal routes, should assume the later end of each band.

faqs.question: Our child is bussed back from Al Barsha South. How much does that push the session back?
faqs.answer: Typically twenty to thirty-five minutes beyond the final bell, with the inbound loop through Emirates Living adding more for the clusters furthest in. A child who leaves school at 15:15 is commonly through the door in The Lakes between 15:50 and 16:20, which makes 16:45 the earliest slot worth committing to. The reason to use the later time rather than the earlier one is simple: three missed starts usually end a weekly arrangement, and a bus is late more than three times a term. Choose the slot that survives a bad week.

faqs.question: Is a Friday afternoon session a good idea now that Dubai schools finish early?
faqs.answer: It is the most under-used slot in the week and often the best one. Most Dubai private schools now run Monday to Friday with a shortened Friday, putting a secondary student home around 12:15 to 13:15 with a whole afternoon ahead and no bus to catch. That makes it the right slot for anything needing ninety undisturbed minutes: a full past paper under conditions, a Higher Level Paper 3 investigation, or timed unseen analysis. Check your own school's calendar first, because a small number of Dubai schools kept a Sunday-to-Thursday week.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a DP1 student need, and does DP2 need more?
faqs.answer: DP1 generally works at one hour a week per genuinely difficult subject, plus a short three or four session block in the spring when the first internal assessment appears. DP2 is not more hours but differently shaped ones: during the autumn, when internal assessments, the Extended Essay draft and the Theory of Knowledge essay collide, core coaching goes into blocks at the deadlines and the subject hour is used for that subject's own coursework. From January, one weekday hour plus ninety timed weekend minutes beats two weekday evenings.

faqs.question: Can both my children have online lessons on the same evening in a Lakes villa?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the natural arrival gap usually does the staggering for you. A child at a school inside Emirates Living is home around 15:30 while a sibling bussed from Al Barsha arrives nearer 16:30, so 16:00 and 17:15 fits both without either lesson running late. Two simultaneous video lessons on a domestic connection are generally fine, but not in the same room, because the microphones interfere; a pair of headsets solves it. Each student needs a writing surface beside the screen and a door that closes.

faqs.question: What internet connection and setup does an online IB lesson actually need?
faqs.answer: Less than families expect. A standard Dubai home connection carries a one-to-one video lesson comfortably, including a second one at the same time. What matters more is the physical setup: a headset so the microphone picks up the student rather than the room, a surface to write on beside the screen, the student's own textbook and calculator within reach, and a door. A graphical display calculator must be the real device rather than a laptop emulator for Applications and Interpretation work, which is worth checking before the first lesson.

faqs.question: Does the tutor follow my child's own school deadlines or a generic plan?
faqs.answer: The school's. Internal assessment deadlines, mock windows and Extended Essay checkpoints are set by each school and they differ, so a generic plan is wrong for almost everyone. Send the school's published deadline list at the start and the tutoring plan is built backwards from it: coursework coaching placed at the planning stage, the first draft and the reflection, with the weekly subject hour protected around them. For examination dates, confirm with your school's IB coordinator, since no IB session date is published on this page.

faqs.question: During Ramadan, what time of day works best for a Lakes household?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for Diploma students it often works better than the rest of the year. The household has eaten, the house is quiet and there is no bus the next morning at the usual hour. Set it up before Ramadan begins rather than in the first week. Younger children are usually finished for the day by then, so a household with both an MYP and a DP child should expect to run the younger one in the early afternoon, when school days are shortened, and the older one after iftar.

faqs.question: What does an in-home IB tutor charge in Dubai, and how much of that is the travel?
faqs.answer: Published in-home rates run AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai work placing the common band at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent listings reaching AED 500. Equivalently qualified tutors working online are quoted at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and TutorChase quoting AED 270. On those figures roughly AED 60 to AED 150 an hour is the drive. Monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits are also advertised in this market.

faqs.question: We travel between Dubai and abroad in the holidays. Can the timetable follow us?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and this is one practical advantage of video delivery that an in-home arrangement cannot match. The constraint is time zones rather than geography: a trip eastwards or within a few hours of Gulf Standard Time changes little, while a long westward trip may need the slot moved to a morning. Tell us the dates in advance and the sessions are rescheduled rather than lost. A pause is equally reasonable, except in the summer before DP1, where bridging work genuinely changes the following year.

faqs.question: Which schools do children living in Hattan and Zulal usually attend?
faqs.answer: Mostly schools outside Emirates Living. The common destinations are the Al Barsha and Al Barsha South corridor, including Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Kings' School Al Barsha, Safa Community School and GEMS Wellington International School, with Dubai College and American School of Dubai on the Al Sufouh side. Inside Emirates Living the options are Emirates International School Meadows, Dubai British School Emirates Hills, Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills and Regent International School. Named schools here describe the catchment a family is timetabling around; no affiliation is implied.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay without crossing the IB honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the permitted work is substantial. A tutor can question whether a research question is answerable in 4,000 words, check that the methodology produces evidence, read a draft the student has written and name the assessment criterion not yet met, and rehearse the reflection sessions. What a tutor must never do is write the essay, draft sections of it, or rewrite paragraphs into their own prose. The test for a parent is what comes back after a draft: questions and criterion references, or replacement sentences. Only the first leaves the student able to defend the work.

faqs.question: What happens if the weekly slot keeps getting moved by school activities?
faqs.answer: Then the slot is wrong and it should be changed rather than endured. A session moved three times stops being weekly, and a non-weekly arrangement does not produce the feedback cycle that makes tutoring work. The fix is to book around the fixed activity block rather than hoping it shifts: if there is squad training on Monday and Wednesday, those evenings are gone, and Friday afternoon or Sunday morning is the better slot. Missed sessions are rescheduled within the same week where the tutor's diary allows, not forfeited.

faqs.question: Is a weekend morning session better than a weekday evening for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: For timed work, clearly yes. A full past paper under conditions needs ninety minutes and a fresh student, and neither exists at 18:30 after a day at school and a bus home. From January of DP2 the highest-value hour of the week is usually a weekend or Friday-afternoon session spent on a timed paper, marked live, with the gaps it exposes worked on during the weekday hour. Saturday mornings compete with sport in Emirates Living, so Sunday or Friday afternoon is often both better and easier to book.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-lakes.closingHeading: Send us the door time and we will build the week around it
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-lakes.closingBody: Tell us the school, the year, the subjects and the time your child is genuinely through the door in The Lakes, and we will come back with a tutor who teaches that subject at that level and a slot that sits after the bus with a buffer in it. The trial lesson is free, covers one subject, and takes no card details. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; nobody arrives at a Lakes address, because home visits are a service we offer only in India. If the honest answer is that the evening has no room in it, we will say that and suggest Friday afternoon instead.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-meadows.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma and Middle Years Programme subjects to students living in The Meadows and across Emirates Living. Matching is by subject and level rather than by postcode, and every lesson is one-to-one over live video.

intro.heading: Accounting for the hour before arguing about the format
paragraphs: A Meadows parent asking for a home tutor is solving a real problem. The villa is quiet, the child is already there, nobody has to drive anywhere at half past four, and the whole thing fits inside the one window the family has. That is a sensible thing to want, and the usual response from tutoring companies - a paragraph about how online is just as good - does not engage with it. So before any argument about format, here is the hour itself, broken into what a household is actually paying for.

A visiting tutor's hour is not sixty minutes of teaching. It is sixty minutes of teaching plus a round trip, and in this part of Dubai that round trip is typically twenty to forty minutes depending on which direction they come from and what Al Khail Road is doing. Somebody is paying for that time, and it is either the tutor, by earning less per hour of work, or the family, through a higher rate. The published figures show which: in-home one-to-one in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500. Named IB specialists teaching online are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270.

Those two bands overlap almost exactly, and that is the whole argument in one line. At AED 300 an hour a Meadows family is choosing between a journey and a specialism. The teaching hour is the same length either way. The question is whether the money buys somebody who happened to be within driving distance, or somebody who has taught Chemistry at Higher Level to examination for nine years and lives wherever they live.

So the honest statement, stated early because burying it would be dishonest. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are a service offered only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and a written summary afterwards. That is not a lesser version of what you searched for; it is a different allocation of the same money, and the rest of this page sets out where that allocation wins and where it genuinely costs you something.

What follows is written from the Meadows evening outwards: the villa and the gate, what happens when a lesson has to move, how big the local tutor pool really is in each subject, the sibling problem that two children in one villa create, when in the Dubai academic year the load should rise, and how a parent sees progress without sitting in the room. None of it is a sales argument dressed as information. Where the online format is the weaker option, the page says so.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-meadows.programmesIntro: A Meadows household usually has more than one programme running at once, because the community feeds both an IB campus and several British-curriculum schools. These are the stages this page covers.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, with no external examination in most years. Support here is usually a short block on one weak criterion rather than a standing weekly commitment, and it schedules more easily into a Meadows evening than Diploma work does.
programmes.countryNote: Emirates International School Meadows sits inside the community, so a large share of this neighbourhood's middle-years students share one internal calendar for projects and reports. That makes sibling scheduling easier here than in areas where every child is on a different school's deadlines.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and internal assessments in most subjects. The components that need support most are the ones with no timetabled teacher attached, and they do not fit a short weekday slot comfortably.
programmes.countryNote: A Diploma student in The Meadows is usually home between 15:30 and 16:00 if they attend the campus inside the community, and later if they travel to Al Barsha or Al Sufouh. Sixth-formers generally prefer a 19:00 slot, because their study time is already self-directed.

programmes.name: IGCSE alongside the IB
programmes.description: Many Meadows households run an IB child and an IGCSE child in the same week, because the villas sit between an IB campus and several British schools. Cambridge and Pearson syllabus codes decide who the right tutor is, and the two boards set different papers for the same subject.
programmes.countryNote: The practical effect in this community is two different sets of internal deadlines, two reporting formats and two sets of holidays that do not always align. Families who map both calendars onto one page in September find the rest of the year considerably easier to schedule.

programmes.name: The Diploma core
programmes.description: The Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the internal assessments together account for a substantial part of the final result and almost none of the timetable. Supervision, questioning and feedback on the student's own drafts is legitimate work here; producing any part of it is not.
programmes.countryNote: The dates that actually govern core work are the school's internal deadlines, which sit well before anything external because the school must supervise and authenticate submissions. Ask the coordinator for those dates in September of DP1 rather than waiting for them to arrive.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-meadows.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects Meadows families most often request, with what each one assesses. The list is here because it is also the answer to how large the local tutor pool is in each case.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic, proof-oriented, with a non-calculator paper at both levels. Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers, Maclaurin series and differential equations. The most requested subject in this community and the one with the deepest local pool.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with a calculator expected throughout, plus matrices, graph theory and Voronoi diagrams at Higher Level. A genuinely different specialism from Analysis and Approaches, and a much thinner pool at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, equilibrium and energetics carry most of the lost marks, with the scientific investigation assessed against its own criteria. Higher Level specialists are among the scarcest in Dubai, which is the clearest case for a wider pool.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Equation selection, unit discipline and multi-step calculation, with an investigation that most students underestimate. Higher Level physics requests in Emirates Living regularly cannot be filled from within a short driving radius.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term precision and data-based questions decide the grade more than content recall does. A deeper local pool than physics or chemistry, which makes it one of the subjects where proximity genuinely costs least.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, evaluation structure and the internal assessment commentaries. Higher Level adds quantitative work that catches students who chose it expecting an essay subject.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral, the comparative essay and the paper on unseen texts. Marks turn on handling a text under time pressure rather than on having read widely, which is a trainable skill.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study application and the research project. Students lose marks defining terms instead of applying them to the organisation in front of them, which is a structural habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: Arabic and other languages
subjects.levels: Ab initio, B SL and HL
subjects.description: Phase and route matter more than year group. Dubai private schools also teach Arabic as a mandatory subject separately from any IB language course, and the two have different expectations.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title, with almost no timetabled teaching in many schools. Support is questioning and feedback on the student's own thinking, and it is one of the most commonly requested core components in this community.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of independent research with a supervisor at school whose time is limited. A tutor may discuss the research question, explain the assessment criteria and comment on drafts the student has written; nothing more than that.

subjects.name: Internal assessments across subjects
subjects.description: Each subject has its own criteria, word limits and internal deadline. These are the components where a Meadows family most often discovers in February that something substantial was due, which is a scheduling problem before it is an academic one.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-meadows.regionsIntro: The Meadows is nine villa communities inside Emirates Living, and the practicalities change between them and their neighbours. These are the areas this page serves.

regions.name: The Meadows 1 to 3
regions.note: Nearest the Emirates International School Meadows campus, so school runs are short and a 16:15 slot is realistic. Villas here usually have a room that can be a study, which makes a longer session workable.

regions.name: The Meadows 4 to 6
regions.note: The middle of the community, mostly on bus routes to the Al Barsha and Al Sufouh ring. Arrival home clusters around 16:00 to 16:30, which makes 17:00 the dependable weekday slot.

regions.name: The Meadows 7 to 9
regions.note: Furthest from the main gates and usually last on the bus loop. Families here more often take a 17:30 weekday slot or a Saturday morning block for Extended Essay and internal assessment work.

regions.name: The Springs
regions.note: Townhouses rather than villas, immediately adjacent and sharing the same bus contractors. Study space is tighter, so the scheduling conversation there is about where in the house rather than when.

regions.name: The Lakes
regions.note: Larger plots, long-settled families and a tilt towards the Emirates Hills school ring. Requests here skew towards Higher Level subject specialists rather than general Diploma support.

regions.name: The Views and The Greens
regions.note: Apartments on the Sheikh Zayed Road edge with Regent International School in the ring. A fixed quiet hour matters more than lesson length for a student working at a bedroom desk.

regions.name: Emirates Hills
regions.note: The shortest school run in the cluster, with two well-known campuses on its boundary. Also where the local tutor pool is thickest, which is why proximity feels like less of a constraint there.

regions.name: Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Dubai Marina
regions.note: Where many Meadows children actually go to school, and the direction most visiting tutors would drive from. A fifteen-minute map distance becomes a thirty-minute round trip at five o'clock.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Living and Emirates Hills
schoolClusters.note: The campuses closest to a Meadows front door, including the IB school inside the community itself. A single street here can hold a Diploma student, an MYP student and a Year 11 sitting IGCSE.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and the southern ring
schoolClusters.note: The second and third rings, reached by bus in twenty to thirty-five minutes. This is also the direction a visiting tutor would most likely travel from, which is what the travel premium is paying for.

sections.heading: The hour accounted for: what a visiting tutor's fee actually covers
paragraphs: Begin with the arithmetic rather than the argument. A visiting tutor leaves somewhere, drives to Emirates Living, teaches, and drives away. From Al Barsha or Al Sufouh, the directions most tutors come from, that is a twenty to forty minute round trip in the late afternoon, longer on a bad day at the Al Khail interchange. The teaching is sixty minutes. The tutor's working block is ninety to a hundred, and somebody pays for the difference.

The published rates show who. In-home one-to-one tutoring in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages in this market run AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Online named specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Budget online is advertised from AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik and AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya. Premium named tutoring reaches AED 650 with BartyED.

Set the in-home band against the online specialist band and the overlap is almost complete. That is the finding worth sitting with. It means the travel premium in Dubai does not buy better teaching; it buys the same length of teaching from a smaller pool of people, selected partly on where they live. For a subject with a deep local pool that costs a family very little. For Higher Level Chemistry or Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, it can cost them the specialist entirely.

All of those figures are other providers' published rates, read in October 2026, reproduced here so a Meadows family can judge any quote they receive from anybody. None of them is IB Gram's price list. Our own conversation starts with a free trial lesson and an honest estimate of how many hours the diagnosis justifies.

sections.heading: The villa, the gate and the driver: logistics nobody publishes
paragraphs: Several practical details decide whether a home-tutoring arrangement survives its first term in Emirates Living, and no tutoring company writes them down. The first is access. Villa communities have gates and visitor procedures, and a tutor arriving at 17:00 four times a month becomes a recurring administrative item for the household rather than a single booking. It is minor, until it is the third Tuesday somebody has had to be at home to let someone in.

The second is the room. A Meadows villa usually has somewhere a lesson can happen without the rest of the family vacating the ground floor, which is a genuine advantage over a townhouse in The Springs. But that room has to be given over for ninety minutes plus greeting and leaving time, and in a household with two children it is the same room both of them need.

The third is the person. A visiting tutor is somebody in the house, and that comes with ordinary considerations about who is home, which adult is present and what the expectations are. Families handle this sensibly and it is rarely a problem, but it is part of the real cost of the arrangement and it is never mentioned in a price list.

The fourth is the thing most families do not anticipate: what happens to the arrangement when the tutor is the constraint. A visiting tutor has a route, and a route has a shape. If the 17:00 slot in The Meadows sits between a 16:00 in Al Barsha and an 18:30 in The Springs, the family cannot move to 17:30 without disrupting two other households. Online scheduling has no route, so a slot can shift by half an hour when a mock timetable changes without anybody renegotiating a week.
bullets: Gate access becomes a recurring household task, not a one-off

sections.heading: What happens when a lesson has to move
paragraphs: Over a school year in Dubai, lessons move. A mock timetable lands, a child is unwell, a flight home from a half term is delayed, a school trip appears, a sibling has a fixture. The question that decides whether a tutoring arrangement lasts is not what happens on a good week; it is what happens on the fourth cancelled one.

For a visiting arrangement, a late cancellation has already cost somebody a journey, and the policies reflect that: notice periods are longer, and a missed lesson is more often simply lost. The tutor has usually blocked the surrounding travel time as well, so a rescheduled slot has to fit a route rather than a diary. None of that is unreasonable - the tutor's cost is real - but it is a constraint the family carries.

For an online arrangement the calculation is different in both directions. A lesson cancelled at short notice costs nobody a drive, so it is easier to move within the same week. A lesson can also happen when it otherwise could not: a student home with a cold who is well enough to work, a family already away for a long weekend, a half term spent in the UK. Those are not hypothetical savings; across a two-year Diploma they are the difference between twenty-eight lessons and thirty-four.

The honest counterpoint belongs here too. Online lessons are easier to cancel, which means a household with weak follow-through can let an arrangement decay more quietly than they could if somebody were due at the door. That is a real risk and the answer to it is structural: a fixed slot, treated as fixed, with a written summary each week that a parent actually reads. Families who protect the slot get the benefit; families who treat it as optional get the drift.

sections.heading: How big the local pool really is, subject by subject
paragraphs: This is where the proximity question becomes concrete rather than philosophical. For a Diploma subject with a deep pool - Biology at Standard Level, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level, English A - a family in The Meadows can reasonably expect to find somebody competent willing to drive, and the cost of insisting on proximity is close to zero. For a narrow combination, insisting on proximity means choosing between the wrong specialist nearby and no specialist at all.

The thin ones are predictable: Chemistry at Higher Level, Physics at Higher Level, Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, Economics at Higher Level in a mock season, Theory of Knowledge, and any language beyond the common ones. These are the subjects where the entire argument for a wider pool lives, and a family that has met this wall knows exactly what it feels like: three polite refusals and a suggestion to try again in September.

No competitor page examined in this market discloses a coverage limit of any kind. Several route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers while implying local delivery, which is the same information withheld rather than given. The useful version is to say it plainly: here is which subjects fill easily, here is which do not, and here is what happens when yours does not.

What happens, specifically, is that we say so and offer a specialist elsewhere teaching in your Gulf Standard Time slot at the same rate, or a different hour with the right person, or an honest wait with an estimate. What we will not do is put an available but unsuitable tutor into a booked slot, because that is how a family concludes that tutoring does not work when what actually happened was a bad match sold as a good one.

sections.heading: Two children, one villa, one evening
paragraphs: The Meadows generates a particular scheduling problem more often than most Dubai communities, because the villas sit between an IB campus inside the neighbourhood and several British-curriculum schools a bus ride away. The result is households with a Diploma student and a Year 10 or Year 11 sitting IGCSE, on two different reporting calendars, with two sets of internal deadlines and two sets of holidays that do not always align.

With a visiting tutor, two children means either two visits or one tutor stretching across two curricula. The first costs two journeys and two evenings. The second sounds efficient and usually is not: the person who is genuinely good at Diploma Chemistry internal assessments is not necessarily the right person for Cambridge 0620 Extended paper technique, and a tutor who accepts both is often accepting the second to keep the first.

The arrangement that works in practice is two consecutive slots on one evening with two different specialists. One quiet room is used twice rather than two rooms at once, one evening is spent rather than two, and each child gets somebody matched to their actual qualification. This is straightforward to organise when nobody has to drive between the two lessons, and awkward when they do.

The second sibling pattern worth planning for is the transition year. When the older child is in DP2 and the younger is in MYP 5, the household has a high-stakes examination year and a transition year happening simultaneously, and the natural instinct is to put everything into the older one. The cheaper decision is usually six to ten lessons for the younger child in the summer, which prevents the first term of DP1 or Year 10 becoming next year's crisis.

sections.heading: The Dubai academic year, and when the tutoring load should rise
paragraphs: Families tend to buy tutoring when a report arrives, which means demand across Dubai spikes in November and February and the right tutors are hardest to get at exactly those moments. The calendar argues for a different pattern, and knowing it is worth real money in a community where the same specialists serve several hundred households.

The shape of the year in a Dubai private school is a long first term to mid-December, a second term with a half term and a spring break, and a third term ending in late June or early July. Ramadan moves within that and shortens the school day while it lasts. The long summer is the single largest uninterrupted block available to any student in a two-year course.

Where the load should rise is at the transitions and immediately after diagnostic information arrives. The fortnight after mock results is the highest-yield period in the whole year, because the school has already done and paid for the diagnosis and the student is briefly motivated to act on it. Study leave is the second, because a Year 11 or DP2 student has whole days and no supervision. The summer before a new course is the third, and the cheapest of the three.

Where it should not rise is in the final three weeks before papers, which is when most families try. By then the useful work is narrow and self-directed, the tutor pool is fully booked, and adding hours tends to raise anxiety rather than marks. A Meadows household that books the fortnight after mocks instead of the fortnight before papers typically spends less and gets more, and gets the tutor it actually wanted.

sections.heading: Seeing progress without being in the room
paragraphs: One honest advantage of a tutor in the house is that a parent overhears the lesson. You can tell from the kitchen whether the hour was serious. Remove that and something real is lost, so it has to be replaced with something deliberate rather than waved away.

What replaces it is written. Each lesson ends with a short summary: what was covered, what the student could and could not do, and what they should practise before next week. That document is more useful than overhearing, because it is specific and because it accumulates - after eight weeks a parent can read back and see whether the same weakness keeps reappearing. Overhearing tells you the tone of one hour; a run of summaries tells you the shape of a term.

The second replacement is the student's own marked work. The point of a lesson is a change in what the child produces on paper, so the evidence is a piece of their writing or working from before and a piece from after. Ask for that comparison at four lessons. If the tutor cannot produce it, the lessons have been conversations.

The third is the school. A parents' evening comment, a criterion mark, or a question-level analysis of a mock is independent evidence that nobody in the tutoring arrangement controls. Families who check tutoring against school data rather than against their own impression of the tutor make better decisions, and they stop paying for arrangements that feel good and change nothing. That applies equally to a visiting tutor, incidentally; a warm hour in the dining room is not evidence either.

sections.heading: Why a screen is easier to keep honest than a dining table
paragraphs: There is one place where the online format is clearly stronger on academic integrity, and it deserves saying because this market has a real problem. The IB's rules require that assessed work - the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay, internal assessments - is the student's own. A tutor may discuss a research question, explain the criteria, question the reasoning and comment on a draft the student has written. A tutor must never write the essay, dictate paragraphs, or edit a piece to completion.

Providers in this market cross that line commercially. One sells completed Internal Assessments at four-figure prices. That is not a shortcut with a small risk attached; it is a malpractice trigger that falls on the student, whose entire Diploma is exposed, and not on the company that took the fee.

Where the format matters is in what is visible. A tutor and a student at a dining table with one laptop can produce a document whose authorship nobody can later reconstruct, and the parent two rooms away cannot tell the difference between coaching and composing. A screen-shared session where the student types in their own document, and where each lesson ends with a summary of what was discussed rather than what was produced, leaves a clearer trail. That is not a guarantee of anything - a determined family can misuse either format - but it makes the honest version easier to run and the dishonest version harder to hide.

Ask any prospective tutor, in either format, exactly where they draw this line on an Extended Essay. The answer takes thirty seconds and it is the most informative question available to a parent. Somebody who says they help polish it until it is ready has told you what they do.

sections.heading: Starting from The Meadows, and the sentence we will not write
paragraphs: The practical sequence is short. Tell us which school and which year each child is in, what time the bus reaches your part of The Meadows, and which evenings are already committed. Name the subject and level, and the specific component that is failing if you know it. Ask the school for the internal deadlines on any core or internal assessment work. Then take the free trial lesson, which is sixty minutes of real teaching ending in a written note of what the tutor found.

Three things get said before anybody pays. First, delivery: lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram tutors do not travel to addresses in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, because home tutoring is a service offered only in India. We will not write the sentence promising somebody at your door, in any wording, because it would be untrue.

Second, coverage. Some combinations of subject, level and hour cannot be filled from the UAE-based pool, and the thin ones are predictable: Higher Level Chemistry and Physics, Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, Theory of Knowledge supervision, and less commonly taught languages. When yours is one of them we say so and offer a specialist elsewhere in your time slot at the same rate, a different hour, or an honest wait with an estimate.

Third, claims. IB Gram holds no accreditation from the IB or from KHDA and does not present itself as holding one; a provider in this market claiming board approval for its tutors is making a claim worth questioning closely. No tutor can guarantee a grade. And on assessed work the line does not move: a tutor must never write the Extended Essay or the internal assessment, whatever the deadline looks like.
