faqs.question: Will an IB home tutor actually come to our villa in The Meadows?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We do not send tutors to addresses in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The reason is set out on this page rather than hidden: published in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour overlap almost exactly with online specialist rates of AED 200 to 450 and above, so the travel premium in this market buys a journey rather than better teaching. If proximity is non-negotiable for you, that is a legitimate position and we are not the right provider.

faqs.question: What exactly am I paying extra for when a tutor drives to Emirates Living?
faqs.answer: The round trip. From Al Barsha or Al Sufouh, where most tutors would travel from, that is twenty to forty minutes in the late afternoon and longer at the Al Khail interchange. The teaching is still sixty minutes, so the tutor's working block is ninety to a hundred and somebody pays for the difference. Published Dubai in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 including travel sit alongside online specialist rates of AED 200 to 450 and above, which tells you the premium is the journey rather than the quality of the hour.

faqs.question: Does it matter that I cannot overhear the lesson from the kitchen?
faqs.answer: It matters and it has to be replaced deliberately. What replaces it is written: a short summary after each lesson saying what was covered, what the student could and could not do, and what to practise. That accumulates, so after eight weeks you can see whether the same weakness keeps reappearing, which overhearing one hour cannot tell you. The second replacement is before-and-after samples of your child's own marked work at four lessons. Ask for both. A warm-sounding hour in the dining room is not evidence either.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are genuinely hard to find a tutor for near The Meadows?
faqs.answer: Predictably: Chemistry and Physics at Higher Level, Mathematics Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay supervision, and less commonly taught languages. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level, Biology and English A have a reasonable local pool, so insisting on proximity costs those families very little. For the thin subjects it costs them the specialist, which is the whole case for drawing from a wider pool in your own time slot.

faqs.question: What happens to a visiting arrangement when the mock timetable changes our usable hour?
faqs.answer: It usually needs the tutor's whole route rearranged, because a visiting slot sits between two other households and a thirty-minute shift disrupts both. That is a week of negotiation rather than an email. An online slot can move by half an hour directly, which over a two-year Diploma is worth several lessons. The honest counterpoint is that an online arrangement is also easier to let slide, so the answer is a fixed slot treated as fixed and a weekly summary a parent actually reads.

faqs.question: Can both my children have lessons on the same evening in one villa?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the arrangement most Meadows households settle on. Two consecutive slots with two different specialists means one quiet room used twice rather than two rooms at once, one evening spent rather than two, and each child matched to their actual qualification. That matters here because the community feeds both an IB campus and several British-curriculum schools, so a household often has a Diploma student and a Year 11 sitting Cambridge or Pearson papers in the same week.

faqs.question: Should one tutor take both children if they study different curricula?
faqs.answer: Usually not, however convenient it sounds. Somebody genuinely strong on Diploma Chemistry internal assessments is not necessarily the right person for Cambridge 0620 Extended paper technique, and a tutor who accepts both is often accepting the second to keep the first. Two specialists in consecutive slots costs the same evening and produces better teaching for the second child. Where one tutor does make sense is a pairing within one curriculum, such as Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and Higher Level Physics, where the technique genuinely overlaps.

faqs.question: When in the Dubai school year should we increase tutoring hours?
faqs.answer: The fortnight after mock results is the highest-yield period of the whole year, because the school has already produced the diagnosis and the student is briefly motivated to act on it. Study leave is next, because a DP2 or Year 11 student has whole days and no supervision. The summer before a new course is third and cheapest. The worst time is the last three weeks before papers, when the useful work is narrow, every good tutor is booked and extra hours tend to raise anxiety rather than marks.

faqs.question: Which deadlines actually govern a Diploma student's plan?
faqs.answer: The school's internal ones, not anything published centrally. Schools set their own dates for internal assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge well before external deadlines, because they need time to supervise, authenticate and mark. Ask the coordinator for those dates in September of DP1 and build backwards from them. This page deliberately publishes no IB examination or results dates: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so nothing here could be verified, and an unverified date across a large set of pages would eventually mislead somebody badly.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay when the deadline is close?
faqs.answer: Within a fixed boundary. A tutor may discuss the research question, explain the assessment criteria, question the reasoning and comment on a draft the student has written. A tutor must never write the essay, dictate paragraphs or edit it to completion. At least one provider in this market sells completed coursework at four-figure prices; buying that exposes your child's entire Diploma to a malpractice finding while the seller carries no risk at all. Ask any tutor where the line sits and listen to the exact wording of the answer.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring easier or harder to keep academically honest?
faqs.answer: Easier, in one specific respect. A tutor and a student at a dining table with one laptop can produce a document whose authorship nobody can later reconstruct, and a parent two rooms away cannot distinguish coaching from composing. A screen-shared session where the student types in their own document, with a lesson summary describing what was discussed rather than what was produced, leaves a clearer trail. Neither format prevents misuse by a determined family, but one makes the honest version easier to run.

faqs.question: Do lessons continue when we travel from The Meadows over half term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the clearer practical gains. A family in the UK, India or Europe for three weeks keeps its weekly slot if it wants one, with the time adjusted for the destination. A visiting arrangement pauses for the whole break. Across a two-year Diploma that difference typically adds up to several lessons. Ramadan works the same way: the slot moves to a post-iftar hour rather than stopping, which keeps continuity through a month that many families lose entirely.

faqs.question: How do we make sure an online slot does not quietly fade out by February?
faqs.answer: Three things, and they are structural rather than motivational. Fix the day and time and treat it as non-negotiable against fixtures and activities, which is easier to defend if the household only has to protect one evening. Read the written summary each week, because a parent who reads them is a parent the arrangement stays accountable to. And review properly at four lessons against a new piece of the student's marked work. Arrangements that decay are almost always arrangements nobody reviewed.

faqs.question: Is the person tutoring my child permitted to do it in the UAE?
faqs.answer: They should hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, with MoHRE listing a two-working-day completion time. The u.ae guidance states that tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published nobody should quote you an amount. A tuition permit is also not the same thing as a KHDA permit for premises.

faqs.question: Could we hire a teacher from my child's own school privately instead?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement most likely to create a problem for everybody. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. That reporting should be verified against the current policy document, but the practical point holds in Dubai too. A teacher who marks your child's work and is paid by you privately is in a position neither of you should want them in.

faqs.question: What if nobody suits our subject, level and hour at all?
faqs.answer: We say so, which is not standard practice here. A narrow combination - Higher Level Chemistry at a fixed half-hour on a Tuesday, or Theory of Knowledge supervision in February - cannot always be filled. The options are a specialist elsewhere teaching in your Gulf Standard Time slot at the same rate, a different hour with the right person, or an honest wait with a realistic estimate. Putting an available but unsuitable tutor into a booked slot is how a family concludes tutoring does not work, when what happened was a bad match sold as a good one.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-meadows.closingBody: Work out what you want the money to do. If the subject has a deep local pool and proximity is what matters most to your household, that is a reasonable choice and this is not the service for it. If what matters is that the person teaching Higher Level Chemistry has taught Higher Level Chemistry to examination, the pool has to be wider than a twenty-minute drive from The Meadows. Tell us the school, the bus time, the subject and level and the component that is failing, and take the free trial lesson: sixty minutes of real teaching and a written note of what was found.

intro.heading: The school run, not the syllabus, decides when tutoring happens here
paragraphs: The Springs is fifteen gated townhouse clusters off Sheikh Zayed Road, wedged between The Meadows, The Lakes and The Greens, with Springs Souk and Springs Village as the places everybody actually meets. Almost nobody here walks to school. Children board a bus between 06:30 and 07:15, ride it to Emirates Hills, Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Umm Suqeim, and come back somewhere between 15:15 and 16:30 depending on the route and the afternoon activity. That single fact shapes every tutoring decision a Springs household makes, and it is the reason a search for an IB home tutor in The Springs is really a search for a workable hour.

Work the clock forwards from the bus and you can see the problem. A Year 12 student back at 16:15 needs twenty minutes to eat and change. Diploma homework, Internal Assessment drafting and CAS logging want two hours of their own. Arabic and Islamic Education homework sits on top of the licensed curriculum, because KHDA requires those subjects in every Dubai private school whatever the school teaches otherwise. By 19:30 the useful part of a teenager's day is finished. The window for real teaching is roughly 16:45 to 19:00, four or five evenings a week, and it is contested.

Now put a visiting tutor into that window. The tutor has to leave their own area by about 16:00 to clear Al Khail Road or Hessa Street, find the right cluster and gate, park, and settle. Thirty to fifty minutes of travel each way is normal across New Dubai in term time, and it is the family who pays for it, either in the hourly rate or in a session that starts late and ends in a rush. Worse, the tutor pool shrinks to whoever is willing to make that drive, which is how a child studying Higher Level Chemistry ends up with a general science graduate.

IB Gram works the other way round. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, so the only constraint on who teaches your child is whether they know the syllabus. A Springs student taking Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL gets a tutor who teaches that course and nothing like it, starting at 17:00 on the dot because nobody had to drive anywhere. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service that exists only in our India operation, and pretending otherwise on a Dubai page would waste your time and ours.

What follows is the honest version of this search. What the Dubai home-tutoring market charges, taken from published sources and attributed. Which schools a Springs address actually feeds and what time each of those days ends. How to count backwards from the series your child is entered for. Where the line sits on Internal Assessments. And what we will tell you if no specialist is free for a niche Higher Level subject in the week you ask.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-springs.programmesIntro: Springs children sit in three different IB stages at once in some households, and the stages do not behave alike. A PYP Year 4 pupil needs twenty-five focused minutes; a DP2 student needs ninety and a deadline. Here is what each stage demands of the evening, and what that means for scheduling in Emirates Living.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations, so support here is about literacy and number fluency rather than grades. Transdisciplinary units mean a child may be reading about migration in the morning and measuring volume after break. The exhibition in the final PYP year is the first piece of genuinely independent research a child produces, and it rewards a student who can plan, not one who can memorise. Sessions are short and frequent.
programmes.countryNote: Primary pupils from The Springs ride the earliest buses and are home by around 15:00, which makes them the easiest group to schedule. A 15:30 start works while concentration is still available. Parents here often pair a thirty-minute literacy session with Arabic homework support, because Arabic as an additional language starts in Dubai primary classrooms regardless of the licensed curriculum.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, criterion-referenced marking from A to D in each, and a Personal Project in MYP 5. The marking is what unsettles families moving from a British school: there are no percentages, and a strong piece of work can still score four out of eight because the criterion asked for evaluation rather than description. Tutoring at this stage is largely about teaching a student to read the criterion before writing the answer.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 4 and 5 students in The Springs are the group with the least free evening. They carry the heaviest homework load of any pre-Diploma stage, often with football or swimming at Springs Village afterwards. A 17:30 or 18:00 start twice a week is the realistic pattern, and the Personal Project supervision period in MYP 5 usually needs a third slot for six to eight weeks.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The Diploma is a two-year clock, and the Internal Assessment deadlines set inside your child's own school are the ones that bite first, usually months before any external paper. Higher Level papers carry the specialist content and the Paper 3 style questions where most of the marks separate a five from a seven.
programmes.countryNote: DP students from The Springs often get home last, because Diploma timetables run later and CAS activities sit after school. Sessions at 18:00 or 19:00 are common, and in the final two terms families frequently move to a weekend morning as well, since a ninety-minute block on a Saturday does more for Paper 3 technique than a tired hour on a Tuesday.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The least common IB route in Dubai, built around a career-related study, two or more DP courses, and a personal and professional skills core with a reflective project. Students on the CP still sit real DP examinations in their chosen subjects, so the subject tutoring they need is identical to a Diploma student's, even though the surrounding programme looks different.
programmes.countryNote: Only a handful of Dubai schools offer the CP, so a Springs family on this route is usually travelling further than the Emirates Living cluster for school. Support is nearly always subject-specific: the DP courses inside the CP are tutored exactly as they would be for a full Diploma student, and the reflective project is coached as a process, never drafted for the student.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-springs.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects Springs households ask about most often, and what actually goes wrong in each. A tutor who knows the course knows where the marks leak; a tutor who knows the topic only knows the content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and the algebra that carries it. Most lost marks at HL sit in Paper 1, where no calculator is allowed and a student who has learned to type into a graphing screen has nowhere to go. The HL Paper 3 extended problems reward students who can carry an unfamiliar definition through several steps rather than recognise a familiar question type.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-heavy work. The common failure is treating it as the easy maths: AI HL contains serious statistical inference and matrix work, and the graphical calculator skills are examined rather than optional. Students lose marks by not stating a model's assumptions or by reporting a regression without interpreting it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics generate most of the distress calls. The HL additional content on entropy, equilibrium constants and acid-base calculations is where a five becomes a seven. Written answers lose marks for describing a mechanism without naming the species, and the internal assessment often fails on uncertainty handling rather than chemistry.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields, circuits and the quantum sections. Students arrive able to use equations and unable to explain them, which Paper 2 punishes immediately. Graph-based questions carry a large share of marks and are frequently answered without reading the axes. HL rotational dynamics and thermodynamics need deliberate practice rather than revision.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the enemy here, not difficulty. The course rewards precise terminology, and answers that say cells rather than naming the organelle lose easy marks. Data-based questions in Paper 2 need practised reading of unfamiliar experiments, and HL students routinely underestimate the plant-science and genetics extensions.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The Internal Assessment commentaries are the most common reason for a disappointing grade, because they fail on diagram accuracy and on using a real news article properly rather than on economic understanding. HL quantitative questions demand working, and Paper 1 essays need evaluation that goes beyond listing two opposing views.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Deceptively friendly. Students who treat it as common sense write unstructured answers and lose the application marks that require named tools used correctly. The HL extension topics and the business research project need planning time, and command terms such as examine and discuss have precise mark implications students rarely learn in class.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen textual analysis is the hardest part for second-language students, and the Individual Oral requires a global issue genuinely traceable through two texts. Grades rise fastest when a student stops summarising and starts writing about how a writer's choices create effect, which is a teachable habit rather than a talent.

subjects.name: Mathematics support across MYP 4 and 5
subjects.description: The bridge year. MYP marking assesses knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating and applying mathematics in real-life contexts as four separate criteria, and a student strong at calculation can still score poorly on investigation. This is the stage where Diploma maths route choices are effectively decided.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the essay are both tightly specified and both routinely left late. The essay must answer one of the prescribed titles using knowledge arguments rather than opinions, and the exhibition needs three real objects with genuine links to a chosen prompt. Coaching here is about structure and argument, and the student writes every word.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-springs.regionsIntro: The Springs sits inside the Emirates Living cluster, and the surrounding communities share its school buses, its traffic and its evening timetable. If you live in one of these, this page applies to you almost unchanged.

regions.name: The Meadows
regions.note: The villa community immediately north of The Springs, sharing Emirates International School Meadows as its nearest campus. Larger plots, slightly earlier bus returns, and the same Al Khail Road constraint on any tutor driving in from Deira or Bur Dubai.

regions.name: The Lakes
regions.note: Quieter and closer to Emirates Hills, with many families at Dubai British School and Dubai International Academy. Household timetables here often include an after-school sport at the community club, which pushes tutoring to 18:00 or later.

regions.name: The Views
regions.note: Apartment blocks beside The Greens, popular with families whose children are still in primary. Shorter bus routes mean a 15:30 start is genuinely available here, which is rarer than it sounds across New Dubai.

regions.name: The Greens
regions.note: Mid-rise apartments with Regent International School on the doorstep, so a proportion of children here walk or take a five-minute ride. Those households have the most flexible evenings in the whole cluster.

regions.name: Emirates Hills
regions.note: Large villas and the school cluster that several Springs children travel to each morning. Journeys in both directions are short in distance and unpredictable in time, because the Umm Al Sheif and Al Thanya junctions bind at pick-up.

regions.name: Jumeirah Park and Jumeirah Islands
regions.note: West of the Springs across Sheikh Zayed Road, with a similar townhouse-and-bus pattern. Families here often share tutoring recommendations with Springs neighbours, and the same evening window applies.

regions.name: Al Barsha South and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: The newer expansion to the south, with a growing set of British and IB campuses of its own. Buses from here run against Springs traffic rather than with it, so return times are frequently fifteen minutes later.

schoolClusters.city: Campuses on the Springs bus routes
schoolClusters.note: These are the schools Springs and Emirates Living children most commonly attend. Each runs its own bell times and bus contracts, so treat the timings in the table further down as the typical Dubai pattern and check your own school's calendar. Programmes offered change when a school adds a stage, and KHDA's school listing is the authority on what each campus is currently licensed to teach.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim campuses
schoolClusters.note: The second ring, a longer bus ride from The Springs and the reason some children are not home until 16:30. Several of these are British-curriculum schools running IGCSE at sixteen before splitting into A Level or the IB Diploma, which is why Springs households so often need both boards in the same week.

It works because it is repeatable: the same two evenings every week become the hours the family stops negotiating about, which matters more than any individual lesson.

sections.heading: What a Springs parent is actually asking when they search for a home tutor
paragraphs: The phrase means something precise in Dubai, and it is worth saying out loud. A home tutor is someone who comes to the townhouse, teaches at the dining table for an hour, and leaves. Families want it because it removes a journey, keeps a young child in a familiar room, and lets a parent overhear the lesson. Those are good reasons and they are not imaginary benefits.

The trade-offs are also real and rarely discussed by the agencies selling the service. You are not choosing from the pool of people who teach your child's syllabus; you are choosing from the much smaller pool willing to drive to Emirates Living at five in the afternoon. The rate carries the travel whether or not it is itemised. A cancelled session is harder to recover, because a tutor who has already driven across town will not come back later that evening. And the arrangement quietly caps how specialist your tutor can be, which matters enormously at Higher Level.

IB Gram's answer is to keep the one-to-one part and drop the driving. Your child works with a named subject specialist over live video, screen shared, same tutor each week, at a time chosen around the Springs bus rather than around a commute. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses and we say so before you ask, because the alternative is a conversation that ends in disappointment two emails later. The comparison in the next section is the honest arithmetic, with the market rates attributed to the people who published them.

sections.heading: The Springs school run, hour by hour, and where a lesson fits
paragraphs: Dubai secondary days generally end between 14:30 and 15:30, and primary days a little earlier, but the bell time is not what matters to a Springs family. What matters is the bus. A route that serves Al Sufouh or Umm Suqeim collects from several communities, crosses Sheikh Zayed Road at the worst hour of the afternoon, and deposits children in the Springs clusters anywhere up to an hour after dismissal.

The table below is the typical pattern for the campuses on these routes. It is deliberately a range rather than a claim about any individual school, because bell times and bus contracts change every academic year and only your school's own calendar is authoritative. Use it to work out which column your household sits in, then pick the session start that leaves twenty minutes for food and a change of clothes.

Two patterns show up again and again once families map this properly. First, the earliest realistic start for a secondary student on a second-ring bus is 16:45, and anything advertised at 16:00 will be attended by a child still on Al Khail Road. Second, families who choose a fixed slot and defend it get far more teaching done over a term than families who schedule week by week, because the negotiation itself eats the window. Springs school bus timings are the one variable a tutoring plan cannot argue with, so build the plan around them and treat everything else as adjustable.

There is a quieter benefit to online one-to-one IB tutoring that only shows up after a few weeks. Because no journey has to be absorbed at either end, a session that would have been cancelled can usually be moved by an hour instead. A dentist appointment, a late bus or a school assembly that overruns stops being a lost lesson and becomes a shifted one. Over a Diploma year that difference accumulates into whole weeks of teaching that an in-home arrangement in Emirates Living would simply have forfeited, and it is one of the reasons the fixed-slot habit survives contact with a real family calendar.

sections.heading: Online or a tutor in the car: the Emirates Living arithmetic
paragraphs: Put the two options side by side with real numbers and the decision stops being about preference. The AED figures below are market rates published by named providers and by Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table for 2026; they are not IB Gram's price list, and none of them is ours to quote as our own. What they show is that the in-home premium is not a small convenience charge. It is the cost of a car, a driver's hour and a narrowed shortlist.

Read the travel column as the part no price list shows. A tutor crossing New Dubai in term time spends between thirty and fifty minutes each way. Over a two-session week that is up to three and a half hours of unpaid driving, and unpaid time always finds its way into either the rate or the reliability. This is also why in-home arrangements in Emirates Living tend to be built around whoever lives nearby rather than whoever knows Higher Level Chemistry.

The last column is the one that decides most Diploma cases. Online delivery means the shortlist for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL is everyone who teaches that course on a compatible timezone, which is a genuinely different pool from everyone who teaches it and is willing to drive to Springs 9. For a subject your child will be examined in for two years, that difference is worth more than the saved minutes.

One warning about how to use Dubai market tutoring rates in AED per hour. A quoted rate is only comparable if you know what sits inside it: session length, whether notes or marked work are included, whether a cancelled lesson is credited, and whether the figure covers travel. The cheapest hourly number on this table can be the most expensive arrangement in practice if half of each session is spent re-explaining last week. Ask providers to price a term rather than an hour, and compare what arrives in writing afterwards. Families comparing IB tutoring in Emirates Living almost always find the gap between providers is in inclusions, not in headline rates.

sections.heading: Why two boards land in one Springs house in the same week
paragraphs: Emirates Living is unusual in how mixed its school choices are. One family will have a child at an IB continuum school in Emirates Hills and another at a British-curriculum school in Al Sufouh sitting Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE at sixteen. UK-curriculum schools account for the largest share of Dubai private-school enrolment, around thirty-seven per cent, with Indian curriculum at about twenty-six per cent, American at fourteen per cent and IB programmes at roughly seven per cent, on KHDA's 2024-25 figures. In practice that means IB and IGCSE share a lot of kitchen tables here.

The consequence is a scheduling problem dressed up as a subject problem. The MYP child is being marked against criteria A to D with no percentages; the IGCSE child is being marked against grades nine to one with tiered papers. They are not interchangeable, and a tutor comfortable with one is not automatically useful for the other. Families who try to solve this with a single generalist usually end up with two mediocre arrangements rather than one good one.

The workable pattern is to split by board and share the week. Give the IGCSE child the earlier slot, because their homework load is lighter in Year 10 than a DP student's, and give the Diploma student the later block when the house has gone quiet. Two different specialists, two fixed evenings each, and a shared family calendar. It costs the same as one tutor trying to cover both and produces work that each board's examiners would actually recognise.
bullets: MYP uses criteria A-D; IGCSE uses grades 9-1 with tiered entry

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in the same evening
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside whatever international curriculum it is licensed for. This is a federal requirement reflected in KHDA's own mandatory-subjects guidance, which schools were required to implement from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. It is not optional and it does not disappear because a child is in the IB Diploma. For a Springs family it means the evening has a second homework stream nobody mentions in the IB brochure.

The detail matters. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Islamic Education for Arab students and Arabic as a first language are taught in Standard Arabic; Social Studies is taught in Arabic for Arab students and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises that no mandatory-subject lesson should run shorter than twenty-five minutes.

For tutoring, two things follow. First, a non-Arabic-speaking family in The Springs usually needs Arabic as an additional language support rather than first-language support, and the two are different courses with different expectations. Second, the content is tightly controlled: for mandatory subjects, using different or additional material without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited, so good support means teaching the child to handle the school's own material rather than substituting something livelier. Schools, for their part, must ensure their Arabic and Islamic Education teachers hold the approval KHDA requires.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the series your child is entered for
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a Springs family can do in October is open a calendar and count backwards from the examination series, because every deadline that matters sits months before the papers. Nobody in this market publishes that calendar, which is odd, since it is the part parents consistently get wrong. Entry deadlines are set by the board and administered by the school, and a missed entry is not something a tutor can repair.

For Cambridge International, examinations run in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October; the February and March series is offered to India only and a Springs candidate cannot enter it, whatever a timetable found online appears to show. The cleanest worked example for this region is therefore Pearson's, because its International GCSE November window is published with dates a parent can check: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, results reached students the following January in the way November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026, and the June route is the same shape one term earlier, with June 2026 results going to centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026. Cambridge June entries close in the spring, months ahead of the first paper, and the exact day belongs on the statement of entry your school issues rather than on a page like this one. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always work from the live PDF on its site rather than a date copied onto a tutoring page. For the IB, this page deliberately prints no session or results dates: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so every IB date here would be second-hand. Ask your school's IB coordinator, or read it on ibo.org directly.

sections.heading: Where the line sits on Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and TOK
paragraphs: This matters more in the IB than in any other curriculum a Springs family might be in, because the consequences land on the student. The work has to be the student's own, and the IB's academic-honesty rules treat breaches as malpractice with outcomes up to the loss of the Diploma. There is an active market in Dubai selling finished Internal Assessments, including one site publishing a price for them. A family should treat any such offer as a risk to their child's qualification.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial, and worth spelling out so you know what you are buying. Teaching the underlying content. Explaining what each assessment criterion asks for and what the examiner reads it against. Discussing whether a research question is answerable within the word limit. Reading a draft the student has written and giving feedback at the level of structure, reasoning and clarity. Teaching referencing. Running a mock oral. Helping a student build a timeline they can hold themselves to.

What a tutor may not do is just as clear. No supplying text, no drafting sections, no editing a piece to completion, no providing data the student did not gather, no sourcing a ready-made topic with a ready-made conclusion. If a session ever drifts towards that, the right response is to stop and reset, and a tutor who offers it should be declined. The practical version is a simple test: at the end of a session, could your child explain every line of their own document to a teacher who asked? If yes, the help was legitimate.
bullets: Legitimate: content teaching, criterion explanation, feedback on the student's own draft
Legitimate: referencing, timeline planning, mock orals and viva practice
Not legitimate: supplied text, drafted sections, editing to completion, supplied data
The test: your child can explain every line of their own work unaided

sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child allowed to tutor in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated, and the regulation is more specific than most parents realise. Under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, individuals giving private lessons need a private tuition work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone offering private tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting an amount is guessing.

The eligible categories are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. MoHRE's own service is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fee shown and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. That is the route to point a prospective tutor at, and it is short enough that an unwillingness to complete it tells you something.

Two further points a Springs parent should know. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is why the phrase describing tutors as regulator-endorsed should always be questioned. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules have been reported as barring school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE permit's code of conduct pointing the same way. Treat the idea of hiring your child's own class teacher privately as a problem rather than a shortcut.

sections.heading: What UAE equivalency asks of an IB or IGCSE student later
paragraphs: Families in The Springs move, and a qualification that works for a UK university is not automatically the one the UAE Ministry of Education will attest for a local university place or a government role. Equivalency is a separate administrative process run by the Ministry, and it is worth understanding in Year 10 rather than discovering in Year 13. IB Gram does not perform equivalency or attestation and nobody should present it as something a tutoring platform arranges.

The British-curriculum requirements are published and specific. A student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects. One competing tutoring site currently tells UAE parents that six IGCSE subjects are required; the published rule is five, and subject choice decisions have been made on that wrong number.

For the American track, English proficiency is shown by an IELTS academic score of 5, a TOEFL iBT score of 61, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics by at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB, this page publishes no points threshold, because the figure has not been read on the Ministry's own site and an unsourced number repeated across many pages is simply a mistake at scale. Check moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation channel, and plan subject choices with the published British and American rules in hand.

sections.heading: Starting from The Springs, and the limits we will tell you about
paragraphs: The useful first conversation is short and factual. Which school, which stage, which subjects and levels, what the last report said, and crucially which two evenings are genuinely free once the bus and the activities are accounted for. Families who bring that last answer get matched faster, because availability is the constraint that actually binds. Everything else about this process is easier than parents expect.

The first lesson is free, one per family, with no card details taken beforehand. It is a real lesson with the tutor we are proposing, not a sales call, and the point of it is diagnostic: your child should finish it knowing something they did not know at the start, and you should finish it knowing whether this is the right person. If it is not, say so and we will propose someone else rather than defend the match.

Here is the limit, stated before you spend time on it. Demand for some Higher Level combinations outruns supply in any given week, and the honest answer is sometimes that no specialist for a niche subject is free in your preferred evening slot. When that happens we say so and offer the real options: a different time, a short wait, or a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same syllabus on a compatible timezone. We will not put a general science graduate in front of a Higher Level Chemistry student and describe it as a match.

It is a working session: the tutor finds out where the understanding actually stops, your child learns something, and you get a short written note of what was covered and what should come next.

process.description: Agree the days and times and hold them. A fixed Monday and Wednesday at 17:30 produces far more over a term than an hour negotiated each week, because the negotiation is what the evening cannot afford. Reschedule with notice when travel or exams interrupt.

process.description: Progress is checked against your child's school reports and internal assessment deadlines rather than against our own invented scale. Every few weeks the plan is adjusted: a topic closed, a paper technique added, a session moved to a weekend block for the final Diploma terms.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built around the Springs bus
whyPoints.description: Sessions start at 15:45, 16:30, 17:00, 18:00 or 19:00 GST because those are the times that exist in Emirates Living once the bus, the food and the change of clothes are accounted for. No lesson is booked at a time your child will spend on Al Khail Road.

whyPoints.description: A tutor is matched to Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL or Chemistry SL, not to maths or science in general. Online delivery is what makes that possible, since the shortlist is not limited to people willing to drive across New Dubai at five in the afternoon.

whyPoints.title: Prices on the page, attributed to their sources
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are published market rates with the provider named and the month they were read. They are context for your decision, not our price list. Three of the six ranking competitors for this search publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criterion explanation and feedback on the student's own draft. Never supplied text, drafted sections or editing to completion. The Dubai market contains sites selling finished Internal Assessments, and that is a risk to a student's Diploma rather than a service.

whyPoints.title: Regulation explained, not implied
whyPoints.description: This page sets out the MoHRE private tuition work permit, who needs it, and how to check it. IB Gram claims no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, because it holds none.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you commit
whyPoints.description: If no specialist for a niche Higher Level subject is free in your slot, you hear that in the first conversation along with the real alternatives. Disclosing a coverage limit costs us a booking occasionally and saves everyone a month of unsatisfactory lessons.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our townhouse in The Springs for IB lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE tutoring as one-to-one lessons over live video, and does not offer home visits in the UAE. In-home tutoring exists only in our India operation. The format stays the same as a home lesson in the ways that matter: one named tutor, your child alone with them, the same time each week, work shared on screen. What changes is that the tutor is chosen because they teach your child's syllabus rather than because they are willing to drive to Emirates Living at five in the afternoon.

faqs.question: What time can an IB session realistically start after the Springs school bus arrives?
faqs.answer: It depends which campus ring your child travels to. Children at Emirates Living or Greens campuses are often back by 15:45, so a 15:45 or 16:30 start works. Buses from Al Barsha and Dubai Hills usually land between 15:30 and 16:15, making 16:45 the earliest sensible slot. Al Sufouh and Umm Suqeim routes can run to 16:30, which pushes the start to 17:00. Diploma students with after-school CAS or sport are generally best served at 18:00 or 19:00, or with a weekend morning block.

faqs.question: Which IB schools do children living in The Springs usually attend?
faqs.answer: The closest options sit in the Emirates Living and Emirates Hills cluster, including Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills, Emirates International School Meadows and Dubai British School Emirates Hills, with Regent International School in The Greens. A second ring in Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim takes a longer bus ride. Programmes change when a school adds a stage, so confirm what any campus is currently licensed to teach on the KHDA school listing rather than on a tutoring page. We name schools as context and have no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: How much do Dubai families pay per hour for IB tutoring at the moment?
faqs.answer: Published market rates read in October 2026 run roughly as follows. Budget online tutoring starts around AED 33 to 65 at Tutopiya and EdFlik. Qualified online subject tutors sit around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 once travel is priced in, per Bestimate and independent home tutors. Specialist exam-year support runs AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase quoting AED 270. These are other providers' figures, not ours.

faqs.question: Does an in-home IB tutor in Dubai really cost more than an online one?
faqs.answer: On published rates, yes, and the gap is not small. Bestimate's Dubai table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. The premium buys a journey, not better teaching. It also narrows your shortlist to tutors willing to drive to your community in afternoon traffic, which is the point at which Higher Level specialist cover usually disappears from the options.

faqs.question: Our Springs household has one child in MYP and one in the Diploma. How should we arrange the week?
faqs.answer: Split by stage and stagger the slots. The MYP student usually has the lighter evening load, so give them the earlier session once the bus is back, often 16:30 or 17:00. The Diploma student takes the later block, when the house is quiet and a full ninety minutes is possible. Use two specialists rather than one generalist: criterion-based MYP marking and Diploma paper technique are genuinely different skills, and one tutor stretched across both tends to serve neither child well.

faqs.question: Why does this page refuse to print IB examination dates?
faqs.answer: Because we have not been able to verify them from the source. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so any IB session or results date we published would be copied from a secondary source and could be wrong by days. Dates that are wrong on a tutoring page cause real damage, because families build revision plans on them. Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page come directly from those boards' published key-date documents and are safe to use. For IB dates, ask your school's IB coordinator or read ibo.org.

faqs.question: Does my child still have to do Arabic and Islamic Education if they are in the IB?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in every Dubai private school whatever international curriculum it is licensed for, under federal rules reflected in KHDA's mandatory-subjects guidance that schools implemented from the 2025-26 academic year. Non-Arab students take Arabic as an additional language rather than first language, and the two are different courses. KHDA also requires Arab and non-Arab groups to be taught separately in these subjects, because the content and language of instruction differ.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child with their Internal Assessment without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can teach the underlying content, explain what each assessment criterion is marked against, discuss whether a research question is answerable in the word count, read a draft your child has written and give feedback on structure and reasoning, teach referencing and help build a timeline. A tutor must not supply text, draft sections, edit a piece to completion or provide data the student did not gather. The test is simple: your child should be able to explain every line of their own document unaided.

faqs.question: Does the person tutoring my child privately in Dubai need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, anyone giving private lessons in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time via its app, website or e-services. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts has been published, so treat any page quoting a figure with scepticism. Ask any prospective tutor to show theirs.

faqs.question: Can we hire a teacher from my child's own school to tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: It is a bad idea and in Abu Dhabi it has been reported as prohibited. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct pointing in the same direction. Beyond the rules, it creates an obvious conflict between the person teaching your child and the person assessing them. A specialist with no connection to the school gives feedback without that complication.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do Springs families usually start with for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Two sixty-minute sessions a week in one subject is the common starting point, placed on fixed evenings rather than arranged week by week. Families adding a second subject normally give it two separate slots instead of splitting an hour. In the final two Diploma terms many households move one subject to a ninety-minute weekend morning block, because past-paper technique and assessment feedback need an uninterrupted stretch that a school night in term time cannot provide.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for a niche Higher Level subject in our slot?
faqs.answer: You are told in the first conversation rather than after you have paid. Demand for some Higher Level combinations outruns supply in a given week. The options we put on the table are a different time slot, a short wait for the right specialist, or a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same syllabus on a compatible timezone. What we will not do is put a general graduate in front of a Higher Level student and present it as a match, which is how most unsatisfactory arrangements begin.

faqs.question: How do lessons work during Ramadan and the Dubai summer break?
faqs.answer: Both are scheduling questions rather than teaching ones. During Ramadan, school days shorten and families commonly move sessions to a post-Iftar slot or to late morning at weekends, and the fixed-slot approach needs resetting for the month rather than abandoning. Over the summer, families who are travelling usually keep one session a week on the timezone they are actually in, which preserves the habit and the tutor relationship. Households staying in Dubai often use July and August for bridging work before a new stage.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE grades will the UAE Ministry of Education count for equivalency later?
faqs.answer: For the British track the published rule is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus either one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking tutoring site tells UAE parents that six subjects are required, which is wrong. Verify on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation channel; IB Gram does not perform equivalency and should not be asked to.

faqs.question: Is online one-to-one teaching genuinely as good as having someone at the dining table?
faqs.answer: For secondary IB work, the evidence in our own matching is that the format matters less than the specialist. A shared screen is better than a shared notebook for annotating a past paper, working through a mark scheme or building a graph together, and the recording of what was covered is written rather than remembered. What online delivery definitely changes is the choice of tutor: a Springs family gets a Higher Level specialist instead of whoever lives within a twenty-minute drive, and at Higher Level that is the difference that shows up in the grade.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-springs.closingHeading: Start with the two evenings that are actually free
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-springs.closingBody: If you have read this far, you already know the hard part is not finding a tutor but finding an hour. Work out which two evenings survive the bus, the homework and the activities, then tell us the school, the stage and the subjects. We will propose a specialist who teaches that named course, run one free lesson for you to judge, and give you a written note of what your child needs next. If nobody suitable is free in your slot, we will say so and give you the alternatives rather than fill the gap with a generalist. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, from the first session onwards.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-sustainable-c.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects for students in The Sustainable City and the wider Dubailand belt. Each one teaches a named subject at a named level rather than general study skills, and each session is booked against your child's own school assessment calendar.

intro.heading: Start from the date on the calendar, not the subject on the report card
paragraphs: Almost every enquiry that reaches us from The Sustainable City arrives with a deadline attached. A Diploma Programme student has an internal assessment draft due at the end of the month. A Middle Years student has criterion-marked tasks landing in the same fortnight as a summative test. A DP2 student has worked out that the May session is closer than the number of free weekends between now and then. The subject matters, but the date is what decides whether tuition is useful or decorative.

That is why this page is organised around time rather than around a subject list. The IB year in a Dubai school runs from late August to late June, with assessment pressure concentrated in three places: the November window when DP1 coursework topics have to be settled, the February and March stretch when internal assessment drafts and mocks collide, and the final run into the May examinations. A tutor engaged in week one of a term does different work from a tutor engaged in week eight, and pretending otherwise wastes a family's money.

The Sustainable City is an unusual Dubai neighbourhood to tutor into, in one specific and useful way. Fairgreen International School sits inside the community, which means a large share of the children here walk or take a buggy to an IB continuum school a few hundred metres from their front door. The school run that eats ninety minutes a day in other parts of Dubai barely exists here. What that buys is a genuinely usable 4pm to 6pm window — the one slot a working parent in Dubai Investments Park or Business Bay can still get a tutor into without pushing a session past eight in the evening.

The flip side is that a community of roughly five hundred villas does not contain a resident Chemistry Higher Level specialist, a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches examiner-standard tutor and a Theory of Knowledge supervisor waiting for your call. The pool of people who can drive to Al Qudra Road for a 4pm Tuesday is small, and it is small in exactly the subjects where Higher Level depth matters most. Online one-to-one removes that constraint entirely: the tutor is chosen for the syllabus they teach, not for the distance between their flat and your gate.

So, plainly stated before anything else on this page: IB Gram delivers tuition to The Sustainable City as live one-to-one video lessons. We do not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE — household visits are a service we run only in India. Everything below is written on that basis, including an honest comparison of what a visiting tutor in this part of Dubai costs and what the travel premium actually buys you.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-sustainable-c.programmesIntro: Children in The Sustainable City move through the IB continuum inside their own community, which means a family often needs two very different kinds of help in the same year — criterion coaching for a younger child and deadline-driven subject work for an older one. These are the three programmes we tutor, and what the calendar looks like in each.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The Primary Years Programme has no external examinations, so the calendar driver is the unit of inquiry and the exhibition in the final year. Reporting is descriptive rather than graded, which means parents often discover a gap only when a child reaches Middle Years and marks appear. The useful tutoring work here is foundational: number fluency, reading stamina, and the habit of explaining reasoning out loud rather than producing an answer.
programmes.countryNote: At Fairgreen International School, inside The Sustainable City itself, PYP children finish close to home, so a 3.30pm session is realistic in a way it rarely is elsewhere in Dubai. Families who later move a child to a British-curriculum school in Motor City or Arabian Ranches usually need a short bridging block, because Year 6 in an English National Curriculum school expects written arithmetic conventions the PYP does not drill.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Middle Years subjects are marked against four criteria, each on an eight-point scale, and converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. A student can know the content and still sit at a 4 because the criterion being assessed is communication or reflection rather than knowledge. Term calendars in MYP are dense with summative tasks, so the planning question is which task carries which criterion and when it lands.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 5 students in The Sustainable City face a decision in the second term that the calendar makes urgent: continue into the Diploma Programme at Fairgreen, or move to an IGCSE or A Level route at a school in Motor City, Dubai Sports City or Arabian Ranches. Subject choices are usually locked by February, so any maths or science strengthening meant to influence that choice has to happen in the first term, not the third.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma Programme is two years, six subjects at Higher or Standard Level, and a core of Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Subject grades run 1-7 with up to three further points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix. Nearly every Diploma crisis we see is a scheduling crisis first: coursework in four subjects maturing in the same six weeks as the mock examinations.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session, and Dubai schools set their internal deadlines months ahead of it. The practical consequence for a Sustainable City family is that the second term is the expensive term — if the Extended Essay, the Mathematics exploration and two science investigations are all unfinished in February, there is no amount of tutoring that recovers all four. Starting the planning in the first term costs less and works better.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: The core is where the three bonus points live and where most late-stage panic happens. Theory of Knowledge requires an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay; the Extended Essay is an independent 4,000-word piece with a supervisor and reflection sessions. Neither is content a tutor can teach in the ordinary sense. What a tutor can do is interrogate a research question, test whether a knowledge claim is actually arguable, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools typically set the Extended Essay question deadline in DP1 and the full draft in the first term of DP2, well before any IB upload date. For a student in The Sustainable City, the most valuable core sessions are the earliest ones — narrowing a question from something unanswerable to something that fits 4,000 words. The work IB Gram will not do is write, rewrite or complete any part of it; that is an academic honesty breach and a malpractice risk for the student.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-sustainable-c.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma and Middle Years subjects The Sustainable City families ask for most often, with the specific thing that tends to cost marks in each. The point of listing them this way is that a tutor booked for a named weakness works faster than a tutor booked for a subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Marks go missing in the proof and calculus-heavy sections rather than in arithmetic. At Higher Level, Paper 3 is an extended investigative problem that rewards students who have practised writing out a structured argument. The exploration carries 20% and is assessed on criteria including mathematical communication, where notation discipline matters more than ambition.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology is assumed throughout, and the common failure is treating the calculator as the answer rather than as a step to be justified. Statistical reasoning, modelling and interpretation of real data dominate. Students moving from a Middle Years extended maths course often underestimate how much written interpretation the papers demand.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The current syllabus is organised into five themes from space, time and motion through to nuclear and quantum physics. The scientific investigation is 20% of the grade at both levels. Students lose marks on uncertainty treatment and on explanations that describe an effect without naming the mechanism behind it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structured around Structure and Reactivity, with the same 20% scientific investigation. The reliable mark-losers are energetics calculations with sign errors, organic mechanism arrows drawn from the wrong species, and equilibrium questions answered qualitatively when the command term asked for a calculation.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem rather than difficulty, and the course is now built around unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, and continuity and change. Data-based questions reward students who read the axes before the question. Precise terminology is worth more here than in any other science.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Assessment is Paper 1 guided analysis of unseen texts, Paper 2 comparative essay, an individual oral, and at Higher Level a written essay. The individual oral is where confident speakers still lose marks, because the global issue has to be genuinely visible in both extracts rather than asserted over them.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries on published news articles form the internal assessment, each with a word limit and a required diagram. Students lose marks by summarising the article instead of applying theory to it. At Higher Level the extension topics and quantitative paper need separate practice from the essay papers.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study heavy, with command terms that decide the mark more than content does. Evaluate, examine and discuss each require a different shape of answer, and a well-informed response written to the wrong command term scores in the lowest band. The internal assessment requires real organisational material rather than invented figures.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The solution is a working product with documentation, and the documentation is where marks are won. Paper questions on data structures, networks and abstraction reward precise vocabulary. Students who code fluently often write the weakest design documents, which is the gap a tutor should target first.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. These grades sit on a Dubai school report alongside IB subjects and are a frequent, unglamorous source of lost ground for families who arrived mid-phase.

sections.heading: What a Sustainable City family is actually asking for when they search for an IB home tutor
paragraphs: The search phrase is about location and the problem is about time. When a parent on Al Qudra Road types "IB home tutor in The Sustainable City", what they mean is: find me someone competent who can be in front of my child this week, at an hour that exists, without me spending two evenings interviewing candidates. The word home is doing work in that sentence, but it is logistical work, not pedagogical work. The underlying requirement is proximity in time, not proximity in space.

That distinction is why online delivery is not a compromise here. A tutor who drives to The Sustainable City has to leave somewhere, sit on Al Qudra Road or the E311, teach, and drive back. On a weekday that round trip is rarely under ninety minutes, and it has to be paid for either in money or in a session time that suits the tutor rather than your child. An online slot has no travel at either end, which is precisely why it can start at 4pm on a Tuesday and still be a tutor who teaches Chemistry Higher Level for a living.

To be unambiguous about it: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. No tutor will arrive at a villa in The Sustainable City, and we do not quote for it. Lessons are one-to-one, live, over video, with a shared whiteboard, screen-shared past-paper questions and a recording of the session if the family wants one. Home visits exist in our India operation and nowhere else. The rest of this page assumes that and then makes the case for it against the real cost of the alternative, with figures attributed to the people who published them.

sections.heading: The IB year counted backwards, and where the pressure actually lands
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market publishes a calendar. That is the single most useful thing a tutoring page can contain, because every real decision a parent makes about tuition is a decision about timing. UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session; the November session exists primarily as a resit and alternative route. Everything a school does internally is positioned relative to May, which means the deadlines that matter to your child mostly come from the school, not from the IB.

Read the table below from the bottom up and the logic becomes obvious. Study leave is fixed, so the mock window is fixed, so the internal assessment deadlines sit before the mocks, so the Extended Essay full draft sits before those. Each layer compresses the one above it. A family that engages a tutor at the top of this list has a dozen weeks of room; a family that engages one at the bottom is buying triage. Both are legitimate purchases, but they are not the same purchase and should not cost the same amount of hope.

The practical rule we give Sustainable City families is this: anything involving written coursework needs to start at least ten weeks before the school's deadline, because the first three weeks go on narrowing and planning rather than writing. Anything involving examination technique can start later and still work, because past-paper practice compounds quickly. If the choice is between beginning Extended Essay support now and beginning Physics paper practice now, and only one is affordable, start the one with the fixed submission date attached to it.

sections.heading: What eight weeks of tuition can and cannot change
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the window most families in The Sustainable City actually commit to, usually because something on the calendar is eight weeks away. It is long enough to be worth planning properly and short enough that wasting the first fortnight is fatal. The honest answer about what it achieves depends almost entirely on what the problem is. A student who understands the physics but cannot structure a six-mark explanation can move a long way in eight weeks. A student who has not met half the Higher Level syllabus cannot cover it in eight weeks, and anyone who says otherwise is selling.

The shape below is what we actually run. The first two weeks are diagnostic and they look slower than parents expect — past-paper questions under timing, with the tutor watching where the student stalls rather than teaching over the top of it. The information from those two weeks is what makes the remaining six efficient. Skipping the diagnosis to feel productive is the most common and most expensive mistake in short-block tutoring.

What also matters is what happens between sessions. Sixty minutes a week is roughly 1% of a student's waking hours, so the session has to change what the other 99% looks like. Every block we run sets specific between-session work with a named output: three past-paper questions marked against the official command terms, a corrected set of worked solutions, a redrafted paragraph. A family that treats the weekly hour as the whole intervention gets a fraction of what a family that treats it as the planning meeting gets.

sections.heading: What IB tutoring costs in this part of Dubai, with the sources named
paragraphs: Three of the six pages ranking for this kind of search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars — a currency no Dubai family pays a tutor in. So here are the AED bands, attributed. Take the monthly figure first, because that is how a household budget works: a weekly one-hour session with a qualified subject tutor runs roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates, rising to AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more a month for specialist examination-year support. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Converted to hours, the market splits into five fairly clean tiers. Budget online tutoring, often delivered by university students, advertises from AED 33 to AED 65 an hour at the bottom end. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between AED 150 and AED 300, with one agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An in-home one-to-one visit, travel included, runs AED 180 to AED 500. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with one UK agency publishing AED 270. At the top, a named or examiner-level tutor has been advertised at AED 650 an hour.

What a parent should take from that spread is where the money goes rather than what the number is. The gap between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour is subject depth — whether the person in front of your child has taught Higher Level to examination for several cohorts. The gap between AED 200 online and AED 400 in-home is mostly travel, paid for in cash and in the loss of whichever tutor could not make the drive. IB Gram does not publish an hourly price list on these pages; the figures above are the market's, read in October 2026, and the sensible next step is a free trial lesson and a quote for your child's actual subject and level.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor on Al Qudra Road versus an online specialist, honestly compared
paragraphs: There are real arguments for a tutor in the room. A younger child concentrates better with an adult physically beside them. Handwriting, ruler work and practical apparatus are easier to correct in person. Some students simply behave differently when the laptop is the teacher. None of that is in dispute, and a page that pretended otherwise would not be worth reading.

The argument against, in this specific location, is arithmetic. The Sustainable City sits off Al Qudra Road, which means a tutor coming from Jumeirah, Al Barsha or anywhere on the Dubai Marina side is committing to a drive that is unpredictable between four and seven in the evening. That drive gets paid for one way or another — as a higher hourly rate, as a two-hour minimum booking, or as a cancelled session when the tutor's own evening overruns. And it shrinks the candidate pool to people willing to make the trip, which in Higher Level sciences and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is a very short list.

The comparison table below is the one we would want a parent to read before deciding. It compares delivery models rather than companies, and the travel column is written for this neighbourhood specifically rather than for Dubai in general. Our position is stated plainly and is not neutral: IB Gram delivers online one-to-one only, with no UAE home visits, because that is the model that lets a Sustainable City family book the tutor who teaches their child's exact syllabus instead of the tutor who lives nearest.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the internal assessment deadline is three weeks away
paragraphs: This is the point in the calendar where families get offered things they should refuse. There are operations in this market that sell completed Internal Assessments outright — one advertises them at AED 3,750. Buying one is not a shortcut with a risk attached; it is academic misconduct under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student, whose diploma is the thing at stake. No tutoring arrangement is worth that trade, and the fact that it is on sale nearby does not make it survivable.

The boundary is actually clear once stated. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain an assessment criterion, ask why a conclusion follows from the data, point out that a method is not reproducible, and give feedback on writing the student produced. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite a paragraph into publishable shape, choose and execute the research, or hand over a model answer to be adapted. The test we apply internally is simple: if a passage in the final submission exists because the tutor wrote it, the line has been crossed.

Practically, that means our core and coursework sessions generate feedback rather than content. The student brings a draft; the tutor returns questions and criterion-referenced comments; the student redrafts. We keep a written record of the feedback given, which matters because a school investigating a submission may reasonably ask what external support a student received. Families in The Sustainable City whose children are at an IB continuum school inside the community should assume that supervisors know their students' writing well — which is another reason the honest route is also the practical one.
