sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and why that changes the tutoring plan
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In 2024-25 that covered 227 private schools and 387,441 students across 17 curricula, with UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no private school fee increase for the following academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package.

The regulator matters to a tutoring plan for two concrete reasons. First, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students and combined classes prohibited. Those subjects appear on the report card next to IB grades and are a routine source of lost ground for families who arrived in Dubai mid-phase. Second, the emirate you live in determines which authority publishes your school's inspection rating, and those ratings are what parents here are actually comparing when they discuss secondary options.

A separate point worth stating because competitors blur it: a tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, and an individual offering private lessons needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. IB Gram is not KHDA-approved, ADEK-approved or IB-accredited, and no page of ours will say otherwise. We name the regulators because understanding them helps a parent; we claim nothing from them.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the Gulf week and when a session can realistically start here
paragraphs: A tutoring plan that ignores the UAE calendar fails for reasons that have nothing to do with teaching. The working week runs Monday to Friday with a half-day Friday, so Saturday and Sunday are the only full days free, and they are also when families travel, host and rest. During Ramadan, school days shorten and the useful study window moves late — a session after Iftar is often the most productive hour of the day, and insisting on a 5pm slot during that month means fighting a tired, fasting teenager.

The Sustainable City has one structural advantage worth using. Because Fairgreen International School is inside the community, children living here are typically home far earlier than peers whose school run crosses Dubai. That makes the 3.30pm to 5pm band genuinely available, which is the band where a student is still alert. Families in Mudon, Remraam or Arabian Ranches 3 whose children travel outward to Motor City or Al Barsha should plan on 5.30pm as the earliest honest start, and should protect it against sports training rather than assuming it will survive.

Our scheduling position is therefore deliberately flexible in two specific ways. Slots are held in Gulf Standard Time and can be moved to post-Iftar timing for the Ramadan weeks without losing the tutor. And a block can be paused during a school's own examination fortnight, when adding tutoring to a packed assessment week produces fatigue rather than marks. What we do not do is reschedule a student into a different tutor's diary to fill a gap; continuity with one tutor is worth more than a perfectly full calendar.

sections.heading: Where this fits if you are planning the next two years rather than the next two weeks
paragraphs: Most of this page is written for a family with a date in front of them. The longer view is worth a few hundred words too, because the decisions that save the most money in a Dubai IB household are taken early and quietly. Dubai's private school sector added six schools during 2025-26 and is adding seven more for 2026-27 — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — creating 16,846 new places, with enrolment up 6%. More IB provision in this part of Dubai means more families facing a genuine programme choice at age sixteen rather than defaulting to whatever their school offers.

That choice is where early tutoring pays. A student who strengthens mathematics in MYP 4 has the option of Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level two years later, which several engineering and economics degree routes effectively require. A student who leaves it until the second term of MYP 5, when subject selections are being locked, has the option taken away by the calendar rather than by ability. The same logic applies to a second language and to the sciences: capability built in Years 9 and 10 becomes choice in Year 11, and choice becomes university eligibility.

For families thinking about university in the UAE, the Ministry of Education equivalency rules are worth reading early rather than discovering late. The British-track requirements are published and specific. The IB position is not something we will put a number on without a Ministry source, and any page that quotes an IB points threshold without one should be treated carefully. The honest guidance is to check moe.gov.ae and ask your school's university counsellor well before the application year, and to treat equivalency as a process your family manages rather than a service a tutoring company performs.

process.title: Tell us the date, not just the subject
process.description: The first message should name what is coming and when: a mock week, an internal assessment deadline, a results decision. That single detail determines whether the sensible answer is a weekly slot, an eight-week block or a short run of coursework feedback sessions, and it saves a round of guessing.

process.title: A short call to establish the real gap
process.description: Fifteen minutes, usually with the parent and sometimes with the student. We ask which papers have been sat, what the last marked piece scored, which topics the student avoids, and what the school has said. Vague answers here produce vague first sessions, so specifics are welcome.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the tutor you would keep
process.description: Not a sales call and not a different tutor from the one who would teach. The trial runs as a real session on a real topic, and ends with the tutor naming what they would work on first and why. If the match is wrong, say so and we will propose someone else.

process.description: After the trial you receive a short plan: the sessions, the sequence, the between-session work, and the date everything is built backwards from. It is deliberately specific enough to argue with, because a plan a parent cannot challenge is a plan nobody is accountable for.

process.title: Weekly sessions with notes you actually read
process.description: Each session ends with a short written note: what was covered, what was fixed, what is still weak, and what the student owes before next week. Progress is visible in whether the same error stops recurring, not in a satisfaction score. If it is not moving, we change the approach or the tutor.

whyPoints.description: Sessions are sequenced from your child's own school deadlines rather than from a generic syllabus march. That is the difference between tutoring that arrives in time to change a submitted piece of work and tutoring that arrives after the mark has already been recorded.

whyPoints.description: Because delivery is online, the tutor is selected for the exact syllabus and level your child sits, not for the distance from their home to Al Qudra Road. For Higher Level sciences and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, that is the whole difference in quality.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our villa in The Sustainable City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and no tutor will arrive at an address in The Sustainable City. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard and screen-shared past papers, timed to Gulf Standard Time. Home tutoring is a service we run in India only. The practical gain is that your child is matched to a tutor who teaches their exact subject and level rather than to whoever is willing to drive down Al Qudra Road at 5pm, which in Higher Level sciences is a very short list.

faqs.question: How much should we expect to pay a month for IB tutoring in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Taken monthly rather than hourly, Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates put one weekly hour with a mid-tier tutor at roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month, and specialist examination-year support at AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more. Packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not our price list. We quote after a free trial, against your child's actual subject and level.

faqs.question: My child has eight weeks until mocks. Is that enough time to be worth starting?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a realistic target. Eight weeks reliably improves examination technique: command-term discipline, structuring long answers, showing working, handling uncertainty in the sciences. It can also close two or three specific content gaps properly. What it cannot do is cover half a Higher Level syllabus that has never been met. The first fortnight of any eight-week block we run is diagnostic rather than instructional, because knowing exactly where marks are being lost is what makes the remaining six weeks efficient instead of broad.

faqs.question: Which exam session do IB students in Dubai actually sit?
faqs.answer: UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session. The November session functions mainly as a resit and alternative route rather than the default for Dubai schools. Note that IB session and results dates are set by the IB and can be revised, so confirm specifics with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org rather than relying on a tutoring website. What your family should plan around are the school's own internal deadlines for coursework and mocks, which are set months ahead of the examination window and are the dates that actually constrain tutoring.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my daughter's Extended Essay, or is that not allowed?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help, within a boundary that matters. They can test whether a research question is answerable in 4,000 words, discuss sources, explain what the assessment criteria reward, and give criterion-referenced feedback on a draft your daughter wrote. They cannot write, rewrite or supply text, choose and execute the research, or hand over a model essay to adapt. Operations in this market sell completed coursework; that is academic misconduct under IB rules and the consequence lands on the student. We record the feedback given so a school can see what support was provided.

faqs.question: Does living inside The Sustainable City make it easier to schedule sessions?
faqs.answer: It genuinely does, and for a boring reason. Because Fairgreen International School is inside the community, children who attend it are home far earlier than peers whose school run crosses the city. That makes a 3.30pm or 4pm session realistic, which is the band where a teenager is still alert. Families whose children travel outward to Motor City, Al Barsha or Dubai Hills should plan on 5.30pm as the first honest start, and should protect that slot against sports training rather than assuming it will survive the term.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in the UAE need a permit, and how would we check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you see with suspicion. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app and e-services. Ask any tutor directly, and ask a UAE-based agency how it verifies them.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody is available for a niche Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than filling the slot with someone approximate. Coverage is strong across Mathematics, the three sciences, English A, Economics and Business Management at both levels. It thins in smaller Diploma subjects — some Group 2 languages, some Group 6 options — and in those cases we say what we can offer, what the match time looks like, and when we would expect availability. A tutor who is a year out of date on a syllabus is worse than a clear no, particularly in a subject with a coursework component.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education really compulsory if my child is on an IB programme?
faqs.answer: In Dubai private schools, yes. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, with combined classes prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. These grades sit on the school report alongside IB subjects, and they are a common source of quiet underperformance for families who arrived in Dubai partway through a phase and never caught up on the Arabic strand.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do families in this community usually start with?
faqs.answer: One session a week in a single subject is the most common starting point, moving to two in the weeks immediately before a deadline or a mock block. Families with two children often book consecutive slots on the same evening, which online delivery handles without a second travel charge. We would rather start at one session and increase it when the diagnosis justifies it than sell a package of four weekly hours a student cannot absorb alongside school work, sport and the mandatory UAE subjects.

faqs.question: Can we pause tutoring during the school's own exam fortnight?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we often suggest it. Adding tutoring to a week already full of school assessments usually produces fatigue rather than marks. A block can pause and resume with the same tutor and the same slot held. The same applies to travel weeks, which are common here between terms. What we avoid is moving a student into a different tutor's diary to keep a calendar full — continuity with one tutor who knows where the gaps are is worth more than an uninterrupted schedule.

faqs.question: My son is in MYP 5 and choosing between staying IB and moving to A Levels. Can a tutor help with that decision?
faqs.answer: A tutor can inform it but should not make it. What helps is an honest read of current capability in the subjects that would be taken at Higher Level, which usually means a timed diagnostic rather than a conversation. The timing matters more than most families realise: subject choices are typically locked in the second term of MYP 5, so strengthening meant to keep a Higher Level option open has to happen in the first term. The decision itself belongs with your son, your family and the school's counsellor.

faqs.question: How do we know the tutoring is working rather than just happening?
faqs.answer: By whether the same error stops recurring. Each session ends with a written note naming what was covered, what was fixed, what is still weak, and what the student owes before the next session. Over four weeks that record either shows specific question types moving from wrong to right, or it does not. We do not publish satisfaction percentages or improvement statistics, because any figure without a sample size, a date and a method behind it is marketing rather than evidence.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring a real substitute for someone sitting next to my child?
faqs.answer: For Diploma and Middle Years students, in our experience yes, with one honest exception. Older students work from screens all day, and a shared whiteboard with a screen-shared past paper is closer to how they already study than a kitchen-table session is. The exception is younger children, roughly Year 5 and below, who often do concentrate better with an adult physically present. For those families, online still works but needs a shorter session, a parent nearby at the start, and realistic expectations about attention.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have a Dubai office or any KHDA approval we can check?
faqs.answer: No, and we would rather say so than imply otherwise. IB Gram holds no UAE office, branch or centre, and is not KHDA-approved, ADEK-approved, IB-accredited or a Cambridge or Pearson partner. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with physical premises in Dubai; several tutoring websites use language that suggests they hold one when they do not. We name the regulators on this page because understanding what each one governs helps you read your child's school report, not to borrow their authority.

If we do not have the right specialist for a niche Higher Level subject, we will tell you that instead of sending an approximation.

intro.heading: A community where everything is a drive away, including the tutor
paragraphs: The Valley is one of the newer additions to Dubai's southern edge, laid out along the Dubai to Al Ain road with its own town centre, sports village and parks and a rapidly growing population of young families. What it does not have, at the time of writing, is a school inside the community. Every school run from here goes outward — towards Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City, towards Nad Al Sheba, or across to the Arabian Ranches and Mira side — and that single structural fact shapes everything about how tutoring works in this neighbourhood.

It shapes it in two ways. First, your child gets home later than a child living inside a community with its own school, which pushes the first realistic session time towards half past five and makes an early-evening slot the only one that exists on a school day. Second, a tutor who drives here is committing to the same road in the same direction at the same time, which means the travel is not incidental to the price — it is a line item in it, paid for either in dirhams or in a session time that suits the tutor's diary rather than your child's concentration.

This page therefore does the comparison properly rather than claiming a local advantage that does not exist. It sets The Valley against Town Square, Mudon, Arabian Ranches 3 and the Silicon Oasis side on travel, school access and the realistic supply of Higher Level subject specialists. The answer, for Diploma tuition, comes out the same from every one of those communities, and the reasons are worth seeing rather than being asserted.

The honest version of the home-tutoring question starts with what the market charges. Published Dubai rates put in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour once travel is included, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The gap between those two bands is mostly a car journey, and on the Al Ain road in the late afternoon it is a long one. What it buys you is a person in the room; what it costs you is money, timing and the size of the pool you can choose from.

So, plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and no tutor will arrive at an address in The Valley. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard, screen-shared past-paper questions and an optional recording. Home visits exist only in our India operation. Everything below is written on that basis, and the case for it is made with the market's own numbers rather than with adjectives. Where a figure appears, the company or rate guide that published it is named alongside it.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-valley.programmesIntro: Families in The Valley are usually at one of three points in the IB continuum, and because children here attend several different schools, two neighbours can be in the same year group on genuinely different programmes. These are the three we tutor.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examinations, so the driver is the unit of inquiry and, in the final year, the exhibition. Reporting is descriptive, which means a gap in number fluency or reading stamina can go unnoticed until criterion marks appear in the Middle Years. The useful work here is foundational and short: arithmetic fluency, reading volume, and explaining reasoning aloud.
programmes.countryNote: Primary children in The Valley face the longest school day in the household, because the commute is added at both ends of an already full day. For this age group that argues strongly for weekend morning sessions rather than weekday evenings, when a seven-year-old has nothing useful left to give a tutor.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, converting to a 1 to 7 grade through published boundaries. A student can know the content and sit on a 4 because the criterion being assessed is communication or reflection. Summative tasks arrive every term, so there is no single revision window and no examination to count down to.
programmes.countryNote: Because Valley families attend schools scattered across the Silicon Oasis, Academic City and Nad Al Sheba side, the Middle Years cohort here is spread across several schools with different assessment calendars. Carpool conversations about what is coming up are therefore less useful here than in a single-school community, and a family has to track its own school's dates.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years, six subjects with three usually at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessments carry substantial weight — 20% in the sciences and mathematics — and are submitted to school deadlines months before any examination, which is the timing most families discover too late.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in The Valley face the longest commute in the house and the heaviest workload, which is a bad combination for weekday tutoring. For this group the pattern that works is one protected weekday evening slot plus a weekend block for internal assessment work, rather than two tired weekday hours.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: Up to three points from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix, and the part of the Diploma most often left late. Neither is content a tutor teaches in the ordinary sense. What a tutor can do is interrogate a research question, test whether a knowledge claim is genuinely arguable, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote themselves.
programmes.countryNote: Extended Essay supervision happens at school, and Valley students with a long commute have less incidental contact time with a supervisor than students who live near their school. That makes the early sessions — narrowing a question to something answerable in 4,000 words — more valuable here, not less.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-valley.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma and Middle Years subjects Valley families ask about most, with the specific place marks tend to go. Because children here attend several schools, naming the subject and level matters more than naming the school.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof and calculus carry the losses rather than arithmetic. Higher Level adds a third paper that is an extended investigative problem, rewarding a sustained written argument. The exploration carries 20% and is assessed partly on mathematical communication, where notation discipline matters more than ambition.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology is assumed throughout, and the common failure is presenting a calculator output as an answer rather than as a step requiring interpretation. Statistical reasoning and real-data modelling dominate, and the written interpretation is where the marks sit.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes from space, time and motion through to nuclear and quantum physics, with the scientific investigation at 20% at both levels. Marks go missing on uncertainty treatment and on explanations that describe an effect without naming its mechanism.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organised around Structure and Reactivity, with the same 20% investigation. Energetics sign errors, mechanism arrows drawn from the wrong species, and equilibrium questions answered in words when a calculation was demanded are the reliable losses.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume rather than difficulty is the obstacle, and terminology precision separates a 5 from a 7 more than recall does. Data-based questions reward reading the axes and units before the question stem.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, an individual oral and, at Higher Level, a written essay. The oral is where confident speakers still lose marks, because the global issue must be visible in both extracts rather than asserted over them.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries on published news articles form the internal assessment, each with a word limit and a diagram that must be used rather than decorative. Students lose marks summarising the article instead of applying theory to it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Command terms decide the ceiling more than content does. An accurate answer written to the wrong command term sits in the lowest band. The internal assessment requires genuine organisational material rather than invented figures.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The internal solution is a working product plus documentation, and the documentation carries most of the marks. Fluent coders often produce the weakest design records, which is usually where tutoring should begin rather than with more code.

subjects.name: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. These grades sit beside IB subjects on the report and are a common weak line for mid-phase arrivals.

sections.heading: What home tutoring really costs in a community with no school in it
paragraphs: Start with the question as asked. A family in The Valley searching for a home tutor wants somebody competent in front of their child this week, at an hour that exists. The word home is doing logistical work in that sentence rather than educational work. What the family actually needs is a tutor who can be present in time, and in a community at the southern edge of the city where every school run is outbound, time is the scarce resource rather than space.

The travel arithmetic is unforgiving here. A tutor coming from Jumeirah, Al Barsha or the Marina side is committing to a run down the Al Ain road or across the Dubailand corridor in the late afternoon, in the same direction and at the same time as everyone else. That journey is rarely under forty minutes each way and frequently much more. Nobody teaches during it, and nobody works for free, so it gets paid for — as a higher hourly rate, as a two-hour minimum booking, or as a cancelled session when the tutor's own evening overruns.

To be unambiguous: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. No tutor will arrive at an address in The Valley and we do not quote for it. Lessons are one-to-one, live, over video, with a shared whiteboard, screen-shared past papers and a recording if the family wants one. Household visits exist in our India operation and nowhere else. The remainder of this page compares that model honestly against the visiting alternative, using published market figures rather than assertion.

sections.heading: The Valley against its neighbours, on the things that actually differ
paragraphs: Families here compare communities constantly, usually because they have recently moved or are about to. For tutoring specifically, the comparison resolves into three columns: how long the school day is once the commute is added, what a visiting tutor would price the journey at, and how many Higher Level subject specialists live within a plausible driving radius. The first two genuinely differ between communities. The third does not, and that is the finding most parents do not expect.

The school-day column is where The Valley is distinctive. A community with a school inside it — Town Square, or The Sustainable City over on Al Qudra Road — gives a child two hours of their afternoon back. The Valley, at the time of writing, has no school within its own boundary, so every student here adds a commute at both ends. That is not a criticism of the community; it is a planning fact, and it means a 4pm tutoring slot that works elsewhere does not work here.

The specialist-supply column is where the comparison stops being useful. The number of people in Dubai who teach Higher Level Chemistry, Physics or Analysis and Approaches to examination standard is modest, and they are not distributed by villa community. A family in The Valley, Town Square, Arabian Ranches 3 or Remraam faces the same thin local pool, which is why the answer for Diploma tuition comes out identical from each of them and why online delivery changes the answer rather than the location does.

sections.heading: The travel line item, priced openly
paragraphs: Most tutoring businesses fold travel into the hourly rate and never mention it, which makes an in-home quote look like a premium for quality when a good part of it is a premium for distance. For a community like The Valley, that is worth taking apart. The published Dubai in-home band is AED 180 to AED 500 an hour once travel is included, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors AED 200 to AED 500. The online band for a qualified subject tutor is AED 150 to AED 300.

The difference is not only money. A tutor making a long round trip will quite reasonably want a two-hour minimum to justify it, so a family needing one focused hour buys two. They will want the slot that fits their own route, which may be seven in the evening rather than half past five. And if the drive goes wrong, the session is cancelled rather than shortened. None of those are failings on the tutor's part; they are the consequences of distance, and a parent should see them priced rather than discover them in week three.

What the travel premium buys is genuine and should be stated: a person in the room, which matters for younger children, for handwriting and ruler work, and for students who treat a laptop differently from an adult at the table. For a Diploma student working on uncertainty treatment or an organic mechanism, it buys very little that a shared whiteboard does not already provide. sections.heading: Online, in-home, a centre or a group: the four real options
paragraphs: A family here genuinely has four choices and each costs something different. Online one-to-one costs the least in time and gives the widest choice of tutor, at the published AED 150 to AED 300 band for a qualified subject tutor. An in-home visit costs the most in money and time at AED 180 to AED 500, and buys physical presence. A tuition centre costs a second journey and gives teaching pitched at a group's average. An older sibling or a parent costs nothing and is not syllabus-current for an examined course.

The comparison that matters is not price per hour but what each option can actually diagnose. One-to-one, in either format, can establish that a student knows the scale-factor rule and never notices which quantity the question asks for. A group of eight cannot, because the teaching addresses the average and a quiet student's specific recognition failure never surfaces. That is why a cheaper format sometimes produces no measurable change at all, and why the per-hour comparison misleads families with a specific problem.

Our position is not neutral and we would rather say so than imply balance. IB Gram delivers online one-to-one only, with no UAE home visits, because in a community like The Valley that model gives a family the tutor who teaches their child's exact syllabus instead of the tutor willing to drive the Al Ain road at five in the afternoon. For a Higher Level science or Analysis and Approaches, that is most of the difference in outcome.

sections.heading: Which schools Valley families actually reach
paragraphs: Because there is no school inside the community, the student body of The Valley is spread across several schools in two broad directions, and that has a practical consequence families notice in their first year here. Carpool knowledge is less useful than in a single-school community: the parent next door may be tracking an entirely different assessment calendar, a different board and a different set of internal deadlines. A family in The Valley has to know its own school's dates rather than relying on the neighbourhood to know them.

The two directions are the Silicon Oasis and Academic City side, reached along the Al Ain road, and the Arabian Ranches and Mira side across the Dubailand corridor. Both carry a mix of British-curriculum schools and IB provision, which means that in this community the post-16 conversation is frequently a choice between two different qualifications at two different schools rather than between two schools offering the same thing. That makes the subject-choice decision harder here than in a continuum school community.

It also means that when a family moves within Dubai to The Valley, a school change is usually part of the move, and school changes produce specific, closable gaps rather than general weakness. Schools teach the same specifications in different topic orders, so a student arriving mid-year typically has two or three unmet topics and two or three covered twice. A short diagnostic session names which, and that work is far cheaper in the first term than in the examination year.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, stated before anyone asks
paragraphs: At some point in a Diploma a family will be offered something they should refuse. Operations in this market sell completed Internal Assessments outright, one advertising them at AED 3,750. Buying one is not a shortcut with a risk attached; it is academic misconduct under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student, whose diploma is what is at stake. The fact that it is available locally does not make it survivable, and no tutoring arrangement is worth that trade.

The boundary itself is clear once stated. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain an assessment criterion, ask why a conclusion follows from the data, point out that a method is not reproducible, and give feedback on writing the student produced. A tutor may not supply text, redraft a paragraph into final form, choose and execute the research, or hand over a model answer to adapt. Our internal test is simple: if a passage in the final submission exists because the tutor wrote it, the line has been crossed.

Practically, that means core and coursework sessions here generate feedback rather than content. The student brings a draft; the tutor returns questions and criterion-referenced comments; the student redrafts. We keep a written record of the feedback given, because a school investigating a submission may reasonably ask what external support a student received. For Valley students, who have less incidental contact time with a school supervisor because of the commute, that record matters more rather than less.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and the regulator map
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. The scale is worth knowing: 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the following academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package.

Two regulator facts matter to a tutoring plan in this community. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and combined classes prohibited; instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Those grades sit on the report beside IB subjects. And the emirate decides the regulator: ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

A separate point worth stating plainly because competitors blur it. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit, and an individual offering private lessons requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. IB Gram holds neither, claims no approval or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no UAE office. We name regulators because understanding them helps a parent read a school; we claim nothing from them.

sections.heading: Scheduling around the Al Ain road and the Gulf week
paragraphs: A tutoring plan in The Valley lives or dies on the commute. The practical rule is that 5.30pm is the first honest start on a school day for a secondary student and later still for a primary child, and that a slot agreed at 4pm because it sounds better will be abandoned within a fortnight. Families who succeed here pick the one evening that genuinely works, defend it against sport and travel, and put longer coursework work on the weekend where uninterrupted time actually exists.

The UAE calendar then shapes the rest. The working week runs Monday to Friday with a half-day Friday, which leaves Saturday and Sunday as the only full days and also as the days families travel, host and rest. During Ramadan school hours shorten and the useful study window moves after Iftar; for a Valley student with a long commute, a post-Iftar session is often the most productive hour available in that month and an afternoon slot is largely wasted.

Our side of this is deliberately flexible in three ways. Slots are held in Gulf Standard Time and can sit wherever in the evening the household needs. They move to post-Iftar timing through Ramadan without changing tutor. And a block can pause during a school's own examination fortnight, when adding tutoring to a week already full of assessments produces fatigue rather than marks. What we do not do is move a student between tutors to fill a gap in a diary.

process.title: Tell us the school and the realistic earliest time

process.title: A short call to establish the real gap
process.description: Fifteen minutes, usually with the parent and sometimes with the student. We ask what the last marked piece scored, which topics are avoided, whether internal assessments are underway and what the school has said. Specific answers produce a specific first session.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the tutor you would keep
process.description: Not a sales call and not a different tutor from the one who would teach. The trial runs as a real session on a real weakness and ends with the tutor naming what they would address first and why. If the match is wrong, say so and we will propose someone else.

process.title: A written plan keyed to your child's calendar
process.description: After the trial you receive a short plan: the sessions, the sequence, the between-session work and the date everything counts back from. It is deliberately specific enough to argue with, because a plan a parent cannot challenge is a plan nobody is accountable for.

process.title: Weekly sessions with notes you actually read
process.description: Each session ends with a short written note: what was covered, what was fixed, what is still weak, and what the student owes before next week. Progress shows up as the same error ceasing to recur. If it is not moving, we change the approach or the tutor.

faqs.question: Will a tutor drive out to The Valley for a session?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at an address in The Valley. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard, screen-shared past papers and an optional recording. Home tutoring is a service we run in India only. In a community at the southern edge of the city the practical gain is large: your child is matched to a tutor who teaches their exact subject and level rather than to whoever is willing to make a long run down the Al Ain road at five in the afternoon.

faqs.question: How much of an in-home rate is actually paying for the drive?
faqs.answer: A substantial part of it. Published Dubai figures put in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. For a community like The Valley, where tutors arriving from Jumeirah or the Marina side face a long peak-direction run, the gap is mostly distance rather than quality. It also appears as a two-hour minimum booking and as cancellations when the road fails. Those figures were read in October 2026 and belong to the companies that published them.

faqs.question: Why does the lack of a school inside The Valley affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: Because it adds a commute at both ends of an already full school day, which moves the first realistic session time to about 5.30pm for a secondary student and later for a primary child. A community with its own school gives a child roughly two hours of their afternoon back. That is why a 4pm slot that works elsewhere in Dubai does not survive here, and why weekend blocks for coursework and whole-paper practice are unusually valuable in this neighbourhood rather than being a fallback option.

faqs.question: Is tutor availability better in Town Square or Arabian Ranches than here?
faqs.answer: For general and primary-level support, marginally, because those communities have denser informal recommendation networks. For Higher Level Diploma subjects, no. The number of people in Dubai who teach Higher Level Chemistry, Physics or Analysis and Approaches to examination standard is modest and they are not distributed by villa community. A family in The Valley, Town Square, Arabian Ranches 3 or Remraam faces the same thin local pool, which is why online delivery changes the answer and the postcode does not.

faqs.question: What is the best weekly structure for a Diploma student living here?
faqs.answer: One protected weekday evening slot at 5.30pm or later, plus a weekend block when coursework is live. The weekday hour carries content and technique work; the weekend block carries internal assessments, Extended Essay drafting or whole papers, all of which need uninterrupted thinking time rather than a squeezed evening. Families who try two weekday hours in a commuting household usually find the second one is the first thing cancelled, and that the between-session work stops getting done within a fortnight.

faqs.question: Our child attends a school in Silicon Oasis. Does the school matter for matching?
faqs.answer: Less than the subject and level do, but it matters for timing. What we need is the board and syllabus where relevant, the level, and the school's own assessment calendar, because internal deadlines are set by the school rather than by the IB and they drive the sequence of sessions. In The Valley specifically, children attend schools in two different directions, so neighbours often track entirely different calendars. A family here has to know its own school's dates rather than relying on the neighbourhood to know them.

faqs.question: We moved to The Valley mid-year and our daughter has fallen behind. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is extremely common, and the gap is usually narrower than it looks. Schools teach the same courses in different topic orders, so a mid-year arrival typically has two or three genuinely unmet topics and two or three covered twice, rather than a general weakness. A short diagnostic session names which, and the gap often closes within a term. The important part is doing it in the first term rather than the examination year, when the same repair competes with five other subjects.

faqs.question: Can an online session really hold a younger child's attention after a long commute?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and we would rather be honest about the limits. For children roughly Year 5 and below, a weekday session after an outbound school run is often the wrong purchase whatever the format, because there is little attention left. The structures that work for this age group in The Valley are weekend mornings and shorter sessions of thirty to forty minutes rather than a full hour. For Middle Years and Diploma students, an early-evening online session works well, because they already study from screens.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and can we verify it?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure with suspicion. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app and e-services. Ask any tutor directly, and ask an agency how it verifies them.

faqs.question: What happens if you have nobody for a niche Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than filling the slot with someone approximate. Coverage is strong across Mathematics in both routes, the three sciences, English A, Economics, Business Management and Computer Science at both levels. It thins in some Group 2 languages, several Group 6 arts subjects and a few smaller Group 3 options, and in those cases we say what we can offer, how long a match would take and when availability is likely. For a subject with a coursework component, an out-of-date tutor is worse than a clear no.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education compulsory even on an IB programme?
faqs.answer: In Dubai private schools, yes. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, with combined classes prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Those grades appear on the report alongside IB subjects, and they are a routine source of quiet underperformance for families who arrived in Dubai partway through a phase.

faqs.question: Can we pause sessions during school exams or family travel?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we often suggest it. Adding tutoring to a week already full of school assessments usually produces fatigue rather than marks, and travel weeks are frequent in this community. A block can pause and resume with the same tutor and the same slot held. What we avoid is moving a student into a different tutor's diary to keep a calendar full, because continuity with one tutor who knows where the gaps are is worth considerably more than an uninterrupted schedule.

faqs.question: How do we judge whether it is working rather than just happening?
faqs.answer: By whether the same error stops recurring. Each session ends with a written note naming what was covered, what was fixed, what is still weak and what the student owes before the next session. Across four weeks that record either shows specific question types moving from wrong to right, or it does not. We publish no satisfaction percentages or improvement statistics, because any figure without a sample size, a date and a method behind it is marketing rather than evidence.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have a Dubai office or any KHDA permit we can check?
faqs.answer: No, and we would rather say so than imply otherwise. IB Gram holds no UAE office, branch or centre, and is not KHDA-approved, ADEK-approved, IB-accredited or a Cambridge or Pearson partner. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with physical premises in Dubai, and several tutoring websites use language that suggests they hold one when they do not. The regulators are named on this page because understanding what each governs helps you read a school report, not to borrow their authority.

faqs.question: How soon can a first session happen?
faqs.answer: For mainstream Diploma and Middle Years subjects, usually within a few days: a short call, then a free trial lesson with the tutor who would continue, then a written plan. Niche subjects take longer and we will tell you how long rather than book a placeholder. If a school deadline makes the timing urgent, say so in the first message, because it changes which tutors we approach and in what order they are asked, and in a coursework subject the difference of a week can matter.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-valley.closingHeading: Tell us when your child is genuinely home
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-valley.closingBody: In a community where every school run is outbound, that one answer decides the structure: a protected weekday evening, a weekend block, or both. Send it with the subject and level and we will arrange a free trial lesson with the tutor who would actually teach, then a short written plan built backwards from your child's own school deadlines. Lessons are one-to-one over live video to The Valley, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE. The AED figures on this page are the market's, with their publishers named, and if we do not have the right specialist for a niche subject we will tell you that instead of sending an approximation.

intro.heading: What a home tutor in The Views can and cannot be arranged
paragraphs: Start with the honest answer, because the rest of this page depends on it. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in The Views, or anywhere else in the UAE. Visiting a student at home is a service we run in India only. For a family living in Fairways, Golf Towers, Mosela, Panorama, Travo, Turia or The Links, every lesson we arrange is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, with the same tutor each week.

That is not a workaround dressed up as a benefit. It is the arrangement that works best in a tower community sitting on Sheikh Zayed Road at Interchange 5. A visiting tutor needs a parking bay, a call to the security desk, a lift and a shoe-removal pause before anything academic begins, and the family pays for all of it inside the hourly rate. On a 60-minute booking, that overhead is not trimmed from the tutor's fee. It is added to your evening.

The second reason is the one parents care about more once they hear it. Proximity is a terrible filter for IB teaching. There is no reason the person who can best explain the Chemistry Higher Level energetics topic, or the difference between a descriptive and an analytical Economics commentary, should happen to live a ten-minute drive from Emirates Golf Club. Narrow the search to that radius and you are choosing from whoever is nearby and available, which is how a Views family ends up with a Physics graduate teaching Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level because he was free on Tuesdays.

This page answers the home-tutor question properly before it argues for anything. You will find what the Dubai market actually charges for an in-home visit against an online hour, attributed to the sources that published those figures. You will find the time cost of a tower visit broken down step by step. You will find what KHDA requires of your child's school in Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the Diploma, what the Ministry of Education will later ask of an IB transcript, and what a tutor is permitted to do with an Internal Assessment under the IB's own honesty rules.

What you will not find is a price list of ours, a star rating we invented, or a claim that any regulator has approved us. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. We hold no KHDA, ADEK, Ministry of Education, IB or Cambridge status, and any page in this market that implies otherwise is worth reading twice.

If you want to skip to the practical part: the first lesson is free, one per family, and takes about thirty minutes. Nothing is charged and no card details are collected to arrange it. You watch the first ten minutes, decide whether the tutor is explaining your child's syllabus or a general version of the subject, and go from there.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-views.programmesIntro: The Views sends children to schools running three different IB programmes plus a British track that converts to the Diploma at sixteen. Each programme asks for something different from a tutor, so the match is made at programme level before anyone talks about subjects.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the three core components: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment marked by the school and moderated by the IB, so a Diploma student is being assessed continuously from the first term of DP1, not only in the final examinations. Points are awarded out of 45, with up to three from the core.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students living in The Views generally travel outbound to Emirates Hills or Al Sufouh for school, which means the teaching day finishes late and the usable tutoring window is narrow. The commonest request from this community is Higher Level sciences and Mathematics in the hour between arriving home and dinner, with Internal Assessment feedback moved to a longer weekend block.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, lettered A to D, with no external examination unless the school enters students for eAssessment. Marks are criterion-related rather than percentage-based, which is the single thing parents find hardest to read on a report. A student can produce strong work and still score poorly on criterion D because the task asked for reflection and they wrote description.
programmes.countryNote: Views families moving from a British primary into MYP often arrive mid-phase, and the gap shows up in the criterion language rather than the content. Tutoring at this stage is mostly teaching a child to read the task instruction and the criterion descriptor together, which is why MYP sessions here are often fortnightly rather than weekly.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry across six themes, ending in the Year 6 Exhibition. There are no examinations and no grades in the familiar sense, so support at this stage is about literacy, number fluency and the research habits the Exhibition will expose. A child who cannot yet plan a question will struggle with inquiry regardless of how able they are.
programmes.countryNote: Primary demand from The Views is concentrated on English and mathematics fluency in the two years before a secondary transfer, because places at the oversubscribed Emirates Living and Al Sufouh schools are decided partly on assessment at entry. Sessions are short, thirty to forty minutes, and usually run twice a week rather than once.

programmes.name: IGCSE into the Diploma
programmes.description: Most children in this part of Dubai sit IGCSEs at sixteen before choosing between A Level and the Diploma. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both run the qualification, with different syllabus codes, different paper structures and different tiering rules. The grades matter twice: for school progression, and later for the Ministry of Education equivalency count.
programmes.countryNote: The IGCSE-to-Diploma handover is where Views students lose the most ground, particularly in mathematics. An Extended IGCSE grade 7 in 0580 does not prepare a student for Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, and the shortfall surfaces in the first proof and calculus unit of DP1. Bridging work over the summer between Year 11 and DP1 is the single most requested block from this community.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-views.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects most often requested by families in The Views and the wider Emirates Living cluster. Each is matched at level and route, because a tutor who knows Standard Level content is not the same person as one who can teach a Higher Level extension paper.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof-heavy route, and the one UAE and overseas engineering admissions usually expect. Higher Level adds Paper 3, a one-hour paper of two extended problem-solving questions worth 20% of the grade, which rewards students who can sustain an argument rather than complete a drill. Marks go missing in induction proofs, complex numbers and the rigour of a written justification.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with a graphic display calculator assumed throughout. Students who chose it to avoid difficulty are surprised by the statistics at Higher Level, especially hypothesis testing and the regression interpretation questions, where the mark is for the conclusion in context rather than the computed value.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Conceptually unforgiving and heavy on the data-based question. Higher Level students lose marks on uncertainty propagation, on sketching a graph gradient that answers the question asked, and on the written explanation questions where a correct equation earns nothing without the reasoning around it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The split between recall and reasoning catches students out. Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry most of the lost marks at Higher Level, and the extended-response paper punishes a student who has memorised reactions without being able to justify why one pathway dominates.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the trap, not difficulty. Students who revise content thoroughly still underperform because the command terms distinguish, outline and evaluate demand different answer shapes, and because the statistics and experimental design strands get far less practice time than they carry in marks.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the three Internal Assessment commentaries decide most grades. Students write what happened in the news article rather than applying one theoretical concept to it, which is the difference between a mid and a high mark against the criteria.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools are easy to learn and hard to apply. The frequent failure is a student who can define a SWOT or an Ansoff matrix but cannot use it to reach a defensible recommendation about the specific organisation in the case study.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen non-literary analysis under timed conditions, and the Individual Oral asks a student to link a global issue across a literary and a non-literary text. Both reward structure and precise textual reference over general appreciation.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by an exhibition of three objects and a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title. Able students underperform because they argue a position instead of examining how knowledge is produced and justified in two areas of knowledge.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece in a chosen subject, supervised by a school teacher. A tutor's role is process coaching: narrowing the research question, testing the method, and giving feedback on the student's own drafts. The research and the writing stay the student's.

sections.heading: Visitor parking, the lift and the forty minutes nobody bills for
paragraphs: An in-home visit to a Views apartment is not one event. It is a sequence, and each step takes real minutes out of an evening that a parent, not the tutor, absorbs. Visitor bays in the Fairways and Links clusters fill from about 18:00 as residents come home. A tutor circling for a space, then registering at the desk, then waiting for a lift in a tower with two serving twenty-odd floors, has spent a quarter of an hour before saying hello.

Then there is the departure. A tutor with a second booking in Dubai Marina or JLT begins watching the clock at the fifty-minute mark, because Interchange 5 at 19:00 is the difference between arriving on time and arriving twenty minutes late to the next family. The practical result is that the last ten minutes of an in-home hour are frequently the weakest ten minutes, exactly where a student should be consolidating what they just learned.

None of this is a criticism of in-home tutors, several of whom are excellent teachers. It is an argument about where the hour goes. The table below counts the overhead for a typical weekday visit to a Views tower, and the figure at the bottom is the one worth holding on to: on a 60-minute booking, something close to two thirds of an hour of elapsed time is spent on logistics that produce no teaching at all. An online lesson removes that line entirely. The student is at a desk with the document open and the tutor is already there.

The Views has one more wrinkle that villa communities do not. In a townhouse in The Springs or The Meadows there is usually a room with a door. In a two-bedroom flat overlooking the golf course, the quiet space is wherever a sibling is not. A visiting tutor and a student at the dining table means the rest of the household works around them for an hour. A headset and a screen in a bedroom is a smaller intrusion, and it is one reason apartment families settle into online tuition faster than their villa neighbours.

sections.heading: The travel premium, priced from the towers out
paragraphs: The clearest way to read the Dubai tutoring market is to ask what the difference between two numbers buys. An online hour with a qualified subject tutor is quoted in this market between AED 150 and AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An in-home one-to-one hour, travel included, is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table putting the usual band at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to AED 500. The overlap at the bottom is real, but the ceiling is roughly AED 150 to AED 200 an hour higher.

That gap is the travel premium, and it is worth being specific about what it pays for. It does not buy a better teacher. It does not buy more minutes of instruction, as the previous table showed. It buys the tutor's car, the fuel, the Salik toll and the hour of their evening that sits between your lesson and their next one. A tutor who can only take three bookings in an evening because two of them are in Emirates Living and one in the Marina has to recover that lost capacity somewhere, and the only place available is the rate.

Below that band, the market goes cheaper in ways that matter. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to AED 52, both online and generally with university-student tutors. At the top, named specialists and former examiners are quoted at AED 270 by TutorChase and AED 650 by BartyED. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages advertised in Dubai include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Every figure in that table is somebody else's published rate, dated to the October 2026 research round, and none of them is ours. IB Gram does not publish a fixed price list on these pages, because the rate for a Higher Level Chemistry specialist with a free Tuesday at 17:30 is not the rate for Standard Level Biology on a Sunday morning. What you get instead is the free first lesson and a figure quoted before anything is booked, which is a more useful thing than a number on a landing page.

sections.heading: Why distance is the wrong filter for a Diploma subject
paragraphs: A Diploma timetable is not one subject six times. It is six different assessments with six different failure modes, and the person who can diagnose a Physics data-based question is rarely the person who can tell you why an Economics commentary is losing marks against criterion C. Filter by who lives near Emirates Golf Club and you are filtering on something that has no relationship to either skill.

The effect gets worse as the subject gets narrower. Standard Level Biology is taught in every second school in New Dubai. Higher Level Chemistry with strong organic mechanism teaching is a smaller pool. Theory of Knowledge, where the essay is on a prescribed title and the exhibition needs three objects defended against a knowledge question, is smaller still. A family in The Views searching within a comfortable drive is choosing from the intersection of three conditions: knows the subject, knows the level, happens to be local and free at 17:30. The third condition is doing most of the eliminating, and it is the one that carries no academic value.

Removing it changes what is available rather than merely making booking easier. The same Views student can work with someone who teaches Analysis and Approaches Higher Level as their main subject rather than as an extension of general maths, and the lesson can be at 17:15 on a Tuesday because nobody is driving anywhere. Screen sharing also suits the work better than a dining table does: a graph plotted in a graphic display calculator emulator, a marked-up past paper annotated live, a mechanism drawn step by step on a shared whiteboard and saved for revision afterwards.

The coverage table below is an honest map of where that matters most. It does not promise instant availability. For a handful of Diploma subjects the realistic answer is that a specialist may be two or three days away, and we say so before you book rather than placing a generalist and hoping.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home visit, for a Views address
paragraphs: Comparisons like this are usually written to make one option look foolish, which is why most of them are useless. The fair version admits what in-home tuition genuinely does better. A tutor in the room can see a page a child is hiding, can physically reposition a ruler on a diagram, and carries an authority with younger children that a screen does not. For a Year 4 student who will not sit still, that is a real advantage, and if a family in The Views wants it they should hire it locally and we will say so.

For IB Diploma work specifically, the balance tips the other way, and not because of cost. Diploma teaching is document work. It is a past paper with a mark scheme beside it, a draft Internal Assessment with comments in the margin, a graph that needs redrawing three times. All of that is easier on a shared screen than across a table, and all of it is still there in the chat log the following week. The student who missed the uncertainty step in session two can scroll back to it in session six.

There is also a quieter advantage. A tutor arriving at a flat at 18:00 is a social event: the household tidies, somebody offers tea, the parent hovers. An online session at 17:15 is simply an hour. Over a two-year Diploma that difference compounds, because the sessions that survive are the ones that cost the family the least friction to keep.

The last row of the table is the one most parents underestimate. Dubai families travel. A Views household that spends three weeks of the summer abroad and a week in Oman at half term loses four sessions from an in-home arrangement and loses none from an online one, provided the time zone is manageable. Continuity through the DP1 summer is worth more than almost anything else a tutoring budget buys.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in a Diploma week
paragraphs: Parents who arrive in Dubai from a British or European system are regularly surprised to find three subjects on the timetable that have nothing to do with the IB. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and its guidance states these requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. For a child in The Views, that is real timetable time competing with Higher Level content.

The rules are more specific than most families realise. KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, and Arabic is the language for Social Studies for Arab students, while non-Arabs are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two further details are worth knowing before you arrange any support. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that no mandatory-subject lesson should be shorter than 25 minutes. And for these subjects specifically, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which means a tutor's job here is to teach the school's own material better, not to bring a parallel syllabus to it.

The practical consequence for a Views family is scheduling. A student who needs Arabic support as well as Chemistry Higher Level is competing for the same two free evenings, and the honest answer is usually to alternate fortnightly rather than to add a third session nobody will keep. KHDA also states that schools are required to ensure all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach these subjects, which is a reasonable thing to ask your school about directly.

sections.heading: What UAE equivalency will later ask of an IB transcript
paragraphs: Most Views parents meet the word equivalency late, usually when a child applies to a UAE university or needs a secondary certificate attested. It is a Ministry of Education process, it is not something a tutoring platform performs or can accelerate, and it is worth understanding two years before it matters rather than two weeks.

The British track requirements are published and specific. A student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects. That last clause is where a competing page in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong, and a wrong subject count is the kind of error that changes a family's option choices in Year 9.

The American track is also documented. English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB specifically, we publish no points threshold, because the figure circulating in this market has not been read on a Ministry of Education page. If an IB points number matters to your plan, check it on moe.gov.ae or with your school's IB coordinator and take their answer over ours.

What this means for tutoring is narrow but useful. If a Views student is taking IGCSEs before the Diploma, the five-subject rule is a reason to protect the grades in the subjects that will carry the count, and a reason not to drop a subject casually in Year 10 because the timetable is heavy. Tutoring is never required for equivalency, and any page that implies a regulatory process depends on buying lessons is selling urgency rather than teaching.

sections.heading: Where the line sits on Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
paragraphs: This part of the market has a problem, and a Views parent should know about it before buying anything. At least one site ranking for IB searches in this region sells finished Internal Assessments at a published price. Buying one is academic malpractice under the IB's own rules, it is the student who faces the consequence rather than the seller, and the consequence can be the loss of the Diploma. No part of what IB Gram arranges touches that.

The workable version is narrower and more useful than it sounds. A tutor can teach the assessment criteria, because they are published and the student is entitled to understand them. A tutor can help a student narrow a research question from something unanswerable to something a 4,000-word essay can actually address. A tutor can read a draft the student has written and say which criterion is underserved and why. A tutor can model the method on a different dataset entirely, so the technique transfers without the content being handed over.

What a tutor must not do is also clear. The writing is not ours to do. We do not draft the exploration, we do not rewrite a paragraph into our own prose, and we do not supply a dataset or a conclusion. The distinction a school looks for is whether the work in front of it is recognisably the student's, in their voice, with their errors. A session that leaves a student able to improve their own draft passes that test; one that leaves them with a better document they did not write does not.

Your child's school owns the process, and that is the right place for the formal side to sit. The supervisor signs off the Extended Essay, the school sets the internal deadlines, and the school submits the work. A tutor who tries to replace the supervisor is making your child's life harder, not easier. Ask us for feedback on drafts and for help understanding a criterion descriptor; ask the school for deadlines, forms and sign-off.

sections.heading: Permission to teach privately in the UAE, and how to check it
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE sits inside a permit system, and anyone telling you otherwise is either uninformed or hoping you are. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The official service is listed by MoHRE as the issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days.

Two facts are worth carrying into any conversation with a prospective tutor. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, so a tutor who tells you the paperwork is expensive is describing something else. And the eligibility list is broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students may all apply. A university student tutoring legally in Dubai is a perfectly ordinary thing; it is simply not the same product as a Diploma specialist.

The published position on enforcement is that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so this page quotes no amount, and you should treat any figure you see circulating with suspicion. A separate route exists for anyone running a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai, which needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a different thing from an individual tutor's permit and the two are often blurred in marketing.

One more rule catches Abu Dhabi families and is worth knowing even in Dubai. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar. If you are tempted to arrange lessons with your child's own classroom teacher, check the school's policy first. The arrangement that feels most convenient is often the one that puts a teacher's position at risk.
