sections.heading: Starting from The Views, and the limits we will tell you about first
paragraphs: The first step is a short conversation rather than a form. We need the school, the year group, the programme, the subjects and levels, and the two evenings that are genuinely free rather than the two you wish were. The school matters more than parents expect: a DP2 student at Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills is working to different internal deadlines from one at Emirates International School Meadows, and a tutor who asks for those dates in the first lesson is doing the job properly.

Then the free first lesson. One per family, about thirty minutes, no charge and no card details. Its purpose is diagnostic, not promotional. A good first session ends with the tutor able to name the specific thing going wrong, which is almost never the thing the report card named. A student who has lost confidence in Physics usually has a gap in handling uncertainties and an unrelated weakness in reading what a question is asking, and those are two different repairs.

After that, the arrangement is deliberately plain. The same tutor each week, a written note after each session, and a session cadence you can change. If the match is wrong, say so after the second lesson and we will move your child rather than defend the pairing. Nothing about this works if a family is sitting through sessions out of politeness.

The limits are these, stated before you commit. We do not send anyone to a UAE address. We do not publish IB examination dates, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and the only trustworthy source for your child's session is the school's IB coordinator. We do not guarantee a grade, and any claim of that kind in this market deserves scepticism. And when no specialist is free for a narrow Higher Level subject in your slot, we tell you the realistic start date instead of filling the hour with someone who will not help.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our apartment in The Views for IB lessons?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Visiting a student at home is a service we run in India only, and no tutor we match travels to a UAE address. Every lesson for a family in The Views is one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the same tutor each week. Independent in-home tutors do work in Emirates Living and the market quotes them at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel. If you want someone physically in the room with a younger child, that is a reasonable thing to buy locally, and we will say so rather than talk you out of it.

faqs.question: What does the extra cost of an in-home tutor in Dubai actually pay for?
faqs.answer: Capacity, not quality. The market quotes online hours with a qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to AED 300 and in-home hours at AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table putting the common band at AED 180 to AED 350. The difference covers the car, the fuel, the tolls and the evening hour the tutor cannot sell because they are driving between Emirates Living and the Marina. It does not buy more teaching minutes. On a 60-minute tower visit, access and an early departure typically leave 35 to 45 minutes of actual instruction.

faqs.question: How early can a lesson start for a child living in The Views?
faqs.answer: It depends on the school rather than the community. A child at Regent International School in The Greens or Emirates International School Meadows can usually be at a desk by 16:45, because the bus loop is short. A student travelling to Dubai College or GEMS Wellington International School in Al Sufouh is realistically ready at 17:30 or later. Online delivery is what makes the earlier slot possible at all: there is no tutor crossing Interchange 5 at the same time, so the lesson begins at the agreed minute rather than whenever parking was found.

faqs.question: Which schools do children living in The Views usually attend?
faqs.answer: Regent International School sits inside the adjacent Greens community and is the only genuinely walkable option. Emirates International School Meadows is a short bus ride and runs the full IB continuum, so it takes a large share of Views Diploma students. Dubai British School Emirates Hills and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills are the other heavy IB destinations. Across Sheikh Zayed Road, Dubai College, GEMS Wellington International School, Kings' School Al Barsha, Nord Anglia International School Dubai and American School of Dubai all draw from this area. These are named as context; IB Gram has no relationship with any of them.

faqs.question: Is a two-bedroom flat a workable place for a Diploma tutoring session?
faqs.answer: Yes, and more easily than for an in-home visit. A visiting tutor needs the dining table, which means the household works around them for an hour. An online session needs a desk, a headset and a door, and it can run in a bedroom while a sibling does homework in the living room. Screen sharing does most of the work a shared sheet of paper would: past papers annotated live, a mechanism drawn step by step, a calculator emulator both can see. The notes survive in the chat log, so a point missed in week two can be revisited in week six.

faqs.question: Why not just drive to a tuition centre in Barsha Heights instead?
faqs.answer: For some families that works, particularly where two siblings need the same subject at the same level and a small group is good value. The arithmetic for one child and one subject is less kind. A fifteen-minute drive each way at 17:30 plus waiting time turns a 60-minute lesson into a two-hour commitment for a parent, and the group size means the teaching cannot follow your child's specific gap. Centres also teach to a shared scheme of work rather than to your school's internal deadlines, which matters a great deal in DP2.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do Diploma families in Emirates Living usually start with?
faqs.answer: Two in one subject is the normal starting point, or one each in two subjects where the problems are unrelated. Three or more sessions in a week tends to collapse within a month, because the Views weekday simply does not contain the time once mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education homework, activity commitments and the Extended Essay are counted. A better pattern for most families is two fixed weekday hours plus a longer weekend block during the terms when an Internal Assessment draft is due, then back down afterwards.

faqs.question: Does my child still take Arabic and Islamic Education while doing the IB in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum they are licensed to teach, and its guidance states the requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. The rules are detailed: separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Support for these subjects is possible, but it competes for the same evenings as Higher Level content, so most families alternate fortnightly.

faqs.question: Where exactly does a tutor have to stop on a Diploma Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary that is easy to state. A tutor can teach the published criteria, help sharpen a research question, demonstrate a method on different data, and give feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. A tutor must not write any part of the work, rewrite a paragraph into their own prose, or supply the dataset or the conclusion. The test a school applies is whether the work is recognisably your child's, in their voice. At least one site in this market sells completed Internal Assessments; buying one risks your child's Diploma, not the seller's business.

faqs.question: Which tutoring permit should I ask a Views tutor to show me?
faqs.answer: They do. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by MoHRE, whose service page lists it as private tutor licensing with a two-working-day completion time. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen and university students. Ask a prospective tutor directly which permit they hold. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: Why does this page refuse to print the IB exam dates?
faqs.answer: Because we could not verify them from the IB. The organisation's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed at source. Secondary sites publish windows confidently and sometimes disagree with each other. UAE schools sit the May session, and that much is safe to say. For the dates your child is actually working to, ask the school's IB coordinator, who holds the registration deadlines and internal checkpoints that matter far more than a published exam window anyway.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody is free for Chemistry Higher Level in our slot?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a realistic date. Narrow Higher Level subjects and the core components are genuinely tight some weeks, and the alternative to honesty is placing a general science tutor in a Higher Level organic chemistry slot, which wastes a term before anybody admits it. Usually the fix is an adjacent evening or a weekend block rather than a wait. Occasionally the answer is that the specialist can start in nine days, and you decide whether to hold the slot. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, which is worth noticing.

faqs.question: How do the IGCSE grades my child takes now affect UAE equivalency later?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Education's British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. That rule is a practical reason not to drop a subject casually in Year 10 when the timetable feels heavy. One competing page in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong. Verify anything IB-specific on moe.gov.ae rather than here.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same Views household share one booking?
faqs.answer: Only where they are genuinely doing the same thing: the same subject, the same level, the same board, and close enough in attainment that one explanation serves both. Siblings a year apart in MYP sometimes qualify. A DP1 and a DP2 student almost never do, because their assessment pressures are different and the younger one ends up watching. Where a shared session does not work, two shorter separate slots on the same evening are usually easier to keep than two hours on different nights, and that is how most Views households with two Diploma students settle.

faqs.question: If the pairing does not suit my child, how soon can we swap tutors?
faqs.answer: Say so after the second lesson and we change the tutor. Not every pairing works, and the most common reason has nothing to do with competence: a patient explainer suits a student who has lost confidence, and a brisk one suits a student who is bored. Sitting through a mismatch out of politeness is the most expensive thing a family can do, because a term disappears before anyone speaks. The written session notes make this easier to judge than a general impression, since you can see whether the same gap is still being described in week five.

faqs.question: Do lessons continue through Ramadan and the Dubai summer break?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the timing changed rather than the arrangement paused. During Ramadan most Views families move sessions later, after Iftar, and some drop from two to one a week because school hours shorten and the evening fills. Over the long summer, DP1 students going into DP2 are the ones who most benefit from continuing, usually with a weekly session that holds the mathematics and science content in place. Online delivery means a family in Europe or South Asia for six weeks keeps the same tutor, which an in-home arrangement cannot offer.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-views.closingHeading: Start with the two evenings that are genuinely free
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-the-views.closingBody: If you have read this far you already know the honest answer to the search that brought you here: nobody arrives at a Views tower, and for Diploma work that turns out to be an advantage rather than a compromise. The next step is small. Tell us the school, the year, the subjects and levels, and the two evenings that are actually available after the bus. We will propose a tutor who teaches that route and that assessment, arrange a free first lesson of about thirty minutes with no card details taken, and tell you plainly if the specialist you need is a few days out rather than filling the slot with whoever is free tonight.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors covering IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects for Tilal Al Ghaf and the surrounding Dubailand communities. Each teaches a named subject at a named level, and you meet the person who would take every session before committing to anything.

intro.heading: The subject is the variable that matters
paragraphs: Tilal Al Ghaf is unusual among Dubai villa communities in having a school inside its own boundary, which changes what parents here are actually asking for. In a community with no school, the first tutoring question is logistical: who can get here, and when. In Tilal Al Ghaf the school run is short, the evening starts earlier than in most of the Dubailand belt, and the question that remains is the harder one — who actually knows the course my child is taking, at the level they are taking it.

That is a subject question, and the IB makes it a sharp one. A Diploma student takes six subjects at two levels, each with its own paper structure, its own weightings, its own Internal Assessment and its own set of places where marks disappear. A tutor who offers 'IB tutoring' is offering a category, not a course. The useful question to put to anyone is narrower: which subject, at which level, and what is the Internal Assessment marked out of.

So this page is organised by what the subjects actually require. There is a table of how the assessment is structured across the main subject groups, including which Internal Assessments carry what share of the grade, because that single number should drive how a family allocates tutoring hours. There is a section on command terms, which is the one skill that recovers marks in every subject simultaneously. And there is a breakdown of the Internal Assessment criteria by subject group, which no competitor page in this market publishes at all.

The phrase 'home tutor' in the URL deserves a straight answer rather than a sidestep. In-home tuition is widely available in Dubai and market rates run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel. It works for some children. IB Gram does not offer it anywhere in the UAE — home visits are a service we run only in India — and this page makes the comparison honestly rather than pretending the option does not exist.

What online delivery buys a Tilal Al Ghaf family is the removal of the only filter on tutor selection that has nothing to do with teaching. Instead of choosing among people who will drive out past Hessa Street on a Tuesday evening, you choose among people who teach Chemistry Higher Level, or History Higher Level with your child's prescribed subject, or Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level. In a programme where each of those is a distinct specialism, that trade is usually worth making.

Everything below is either sourced or marked as market context. Where a figure comes from a regulator it is named. Where it comes from a competitor's published rate card, the competitor's band is given as the market rather than as our price. Where an exam date could not be verified from the awarding body itself, this page says so rather than printing it.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.programmesIntro: Tilal Al Ghaf pupils reach the IB from several directions, and the subject-level work differs with the route. These are the stages, with what each leaves unprepared.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with no external examination, ending with the Grade 5 Exhibition. The target worth working to is a baseline rather than a grade: reading fluency, number sense and written stamina, all of which the Middle Years Programme assumes from the first week of Year 7.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, PYP schools are inspected by KHDA on the same six-band scale as every other private school and must also deliver Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies. For a Tilal Al Ghaf family that means a Year 5 timetable already carries three subjects outside the PYP framework, and Arabic is where non-Arab pupils most often need help first.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each out of eight, totalling thirty-two before conversion to a grade from one to seven. Marks accumulate from assessed tasks across the year, so a weak criterion identified in autumn remains in the final grade unless something changes. MYP5 adds the Personal Project.
programmes.countryNote: The practical use of a Dubai MYP report is the criterion breakdown rather than the grade, and schools will supply it if asked. Families around Tilal Al Ghaf who treat the report as a summary rather than a scorecard usually discover the problem in MYP5, when the Personal Project is competing for the same evenings.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across three Higher and three Standard Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Each subject has its own paper structure and its own Internal Assessment weighting, and those weightings vary considerably, which is why tutoring hours should follow the assessment rather than the anxiety.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session. No IB exam or results dates appear on this page: ibo.org blocks automated verification, and an unverified date that a parent acts on is worse than no date. Confirm every one with your school's Diploma coordinator.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two Diploma courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. The Diploma courses inside it are assessed identically to the full Diploma, Internal Assessment included, so subject tutoring is the same work at the same standard.
programmes.countryNote: Offered at a small number of UAE schools. The question families usually need settled is what the Ministry of Education recognises for a UAE university application, and the IB figures should be read on the Ministry's own channel rather than taken from any tutoring page, this one included.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects Tilal Al Ghaf families ask for most, with what the assessment actually rewards and where the marks go. A tutor who cannot name the components for a subject is not a specialist in it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, calculus and proof, with complex numbers at Higher Level and a non-calculator Paper 1. The exploration carries a fifth of the grade at both levels and rewards genuine mathematical process rather than presentation. Students who rely on a graphing display lose Paper 1 marks across the board.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-led method. Higher Level Paper 3 is extended problem solving and harder than the course's reputation suggests. Marks go to interpretation: correct calculator output with no statement of what it means in context earns very little.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, waves, fields and electricity, with Higher Level extension woven through rather than appended. Explanation questions reward reasoning from a principle, not describing a graph. The scientific investigation is marked out of twenty-four across four criteria.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure, reactivity, energetics and organic mechanisms. Multi-step calculations compound an early rounding error, so working must be visible for the method marks to survive. Organic chemistry memorised rather than reasoned collapses on unfamiliar molecules.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term precision decides the grade. Data-based questions reward careful axis reading, and the investigation struggles most often on controlled-variable justification. Students who write everything they know score below students who answer the verb.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries on published articles, each tied to a different syllabus unit and word-limited, forming the Internal Assessment. Diagram accuracy carries the explanation built on it, and Higher Level adds quantitative content plus a policy paper rewarding judgement over description.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen textual analysis under timing in Paper 1, a comparative essay in Paper 2, and an internally assessed Individual Oral linking a global issue to two texts. The usual loss is summarising rather than analysing, and choosing a global issue too broad to anchor in specific passages.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Assessed across receptive, productive and interactive skills, with text-type conventions examined explicitly. A blog, a formal letter and a speech are marked partly on register and format, so confident speakers often underperform on accuracy nobody taught them.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source-based Paper 1 on a prescribed subject, thematic Paper 2, and a Higher Level regional option in Paper 3. The historical investigation requires formal source evaluation, where students summarise content instead of assessing value and limitations.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools and theories applied to real organisations, with a Higher Level research project on a real business issue using primary and secondary evidence. Describing a company rather than applying a framework is the standard failure, as is choosing a business nobody can gather evidence about.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Systems fundamentals, computational thinking and a programming solution documented through planning, design, development and evaluation records. The solution needs a real client and a documented process rather than ambition. Hand-tracing algorithms is the missing skill.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition and a prescribed-title essay, assessed on the quality of knowledge-question analysis rather than content recall. Students find it hard because there is nothing to revise; what helps is structured argument practice against the actual assessment instrument.

sections.heading: What 'IB home tutor in Tilal Al Ghaf' gets you in practice
paragraphs: In the Dubai market the phrase means one of two things. Either a freelance or agency tutor who drives to your villa and teaches at your table, charging a rate that includes the journey, or an online specialist who teaches the same hour over live video without it. IB Gram is the second. We do not send tutors to UAE homes; that is a service we run only in India, and no part of this page should be read as offering it here.

Tilal Al Ghaf changes the usual arithmetic slightly, and in an interesting direction. Because the community has its own school and sits beside DAMAC Hills and Dubai Sports City, which also have schools inside them, the local school run is short and an in-home tutor's journey is the only long drive in the arrangement. The premium you would pay is therefore entirely the tutor's travel rather than a shared constraint: your child is home early, and the tutor is still crossing Dubai.

The second cost is the one that actually decides Diploma outcomes. In-home tuition restricts the choice to tutors willing and able to reach this part of Dubailand in your slot. For general Middle Years support that pool is adequate. For Chemistry Higher Level, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, or History Higher Level with a specific Paper 3 regional option, it is thin — not because Tilal Al Ghaf is remote but because those specialisms are narrow across the whole emirate. Online removes geography from the shortlist and leaves only the question of whether the tutor knows the course.

Where in-home genuinely wins is the youngest pupils and the most distractible ones, where an adult physically present is the intervention rather than the delivery method. A Year 3 child who needs someone beside them to stay on task is not well served by a screen, and we say so rather than arguing otherwise. For Diploma and upper Middle Years work, where a session means worked problems, a marked answer and a conversation about an Internal Assessment, the screen is not the limitation.

sections.heading: The subjects are not interchangeable: assessment structure compared
paragraphs: This is the table that should drive how a family spends tutoring money, and no competitor page in this market publishes anything like it. Diploma subjects differ substantially in how their grades are built. In some, the Internal Assessment carries a fifth of the mark; in others it carries a quarter or more. Some subjects set two papers, others three. Some Higher Level courses add a whole component; others deepen the existing ones.

The practical consequence is that the same number of tutoring hours produces different returns in different subjects. In a subject where the Internal Assessment carries a quarter of the grade and the student has not started it, the most valuable sessions available are the ones spent on viability and process. In a subject where the written papers carry the overwhelming share and the Internal Assessment is already submitted, hours belong in paper technique. Families who allocate by anxiety rather than by weighting routinely put the hours in the wrong place.

Confirm the current weightings for your child's specific subjects with their teacher or Diploma coordinator before planning around any description, this one included, because the IB revises subject guides periodically and the live guide is the authority. The table below is a structural guide to the kinds of difference that exist, not a substitute for the current guide.

One general rule does hold across subjects. Higher Level consumes roughly half again the tutoring time of the Standard Level version of the same subject to reach the same relative position, because there is more content and, in several subjects, an additional component with its own technique. Three Higher Level subjects tutored weekly is more evening than a Diploma student has, and it produces a student too tired to do the set work.

sections.heading: Command terms: the one skill that pays in every subject
paragraphs: If a Diploma student can only change one thing, it should be this. IB examination questions are built on command terms, and each one asks for a specific kind of answer. 'State' wants a sentence. 'Describe' wants what happens. 'Explain' wants why. 'Compare' wants both similarities and differences, not one of each. 'Evaluate' wants a judgement with reasons on both sides. 'Deduce' wants a conclusion drawn from information given. A student who writes everything they know satisfies none of them.

The reason this is the highest-yield intervention in the Diploma is that the verbs recur across every subject. A student who learns to answer 'evaluate' properly recovers marks in Economics, History, Biology and Business Management at once. No content teaching does that. Four to six focused sessions, using questions from the student's own subjects, marked against the actual criteria and rewritten in the session, changes how the student writes for the remainder of the course.

The second thing worth teaching explicitly is the mark-to-length relationship. A four-mark question wants four marks' worth of content, which is usually four distinct points rather than a paragraph of elaboration on one. Students who write at length on a four-mark question lose time they then do not have for the twelve-mark question later in the paper, and unanswered questions score nothing however well the subject is understood.

Both of these are learnable in a way content is not, and both are invisible in a school report. A student can be described as needing to 'develop exam technique' for two years without anyone specifying what that means. Naming it — the verbs, the mark-to-length relationship, the habit of finishing the paper — turns a vague comment into four weeks of concrete work.

sections.heading: Internal Assessment criteria, by subject group
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject has an internally assessed component and they are collectively worth a substantial share of a student's points total. They are also the component students start latest and the one a tutor can most legitimately and usefully influence, because the decisions that determine the mark are made early and are mostly about scope rather than content.

The criteria differ by subject group but the failure modes rhyme. In the sciences, the investigation is marked out of twenty-four across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and the commonest failure is a question whose effect is smaller than the measurement uncertainty. In mathematics, the exploration is marked out of twenty across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, and the commonest failure is a safe topic using mathematics below the course level. In History, the investigation requires formal source evaluation that students substitute with summary.

Across all of them the same two things are true. First, the criteria that reward the student's own thinking — personal engagement, reflection, evaluation — carry a meaningful share of the marks and are the cheapest to secure, because they reward work the student can actually do once they know it is being assessed. Most students who lose them lose them by not knowing they exist. Second, scope decides everything: a question too large produces description, one too small cannot reach the upper bands.

Confirm the current criteria and mark allocations for your child's subjects with their teacher, since the IB revises its guides. The table sets out the shape of what is assessed rather than the live detail, and the point of publishing it is that no competitor page in this market names a single criterion in any subject.

sections.heading: Past papers: how to practise each kind of component
paragraphs: Most Diploma students revise by reading and then wonder why mock results do not move. The components are different in kind and each requires a different sort of practice, which is worth setting out because nobody usually does.

Multiple-choice sections reward timed volume. The distractors are predictable once a student has seen enough of them, and working forty questions against a clock teaches more than reading a textbook chapter. Data-analysis sections reward a specific skill set — uncertainty, graph interpretation, gradients with physical meaning — that can be taught as a topic in two or three sessions and then applies every time.

Extended-response papers need to be practised whole, at least sometimes. A student who only ever works individual questions never discovers that their accuracy falls in the final half hour, and in a two-hour paper that is where a grade goes. Full-length practice is tiring and unpopular and it is the single thing most students have never done before a mock. Higher Level third papers, where a subject sets one, cannot be built from short questions at all, because the difficulty is sustaining an argument across connected parts.

The marking matters more than the doing. A paper worked and then marked against the published scheme, with every lost mark categorised as content, method, command term or timing, tells a student where to go next. The same paper worked and self-assessed as 'mostly fine' tells them nothing. One properly marked paper a fortnight, with the categories recorded, outperforms weekly papers nobody analyses — and it fits into a household week that has other demands in it.

sections.heading: What it costs, set against the fees you already pay
paragraphs: Tutoring decisions in Dubai are made inside a household budget that already carries school fees, so the useful comparison is against that line rather than in isolation. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion out of AED 2.5 billion in total. So the fee line is flat and predictable; tutoring is the variable one.

The market bands, read in October 2026 from competitors' own published figures: EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour, Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52, Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270, BartyED at AED 650. Bestimate's Dubai table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 budget, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Against a Dubai private-school fee bill, one weekly session at the mid band is a modest addition. Two subjects at two sessions a week through an exam year is not, and that is a decision a family should make deliberately rather than arrive at by accumulation. The honest guidance is to allocate by assessment weighting rather than by worry: a subject where a quarter of the grade is still in play through an unstarted Internal Assessment deserves the hours more than a subject where only paper technique remains.

IB Gram publishes no hourly rate on this page. The reason is that the right figure depends on the subject, the level and how many weeks remain, and one number spanning every IB subject would mislead. What we publish is the market band so any quote can be checked, including ours, and a free first lesson so the first hour costs nothing and you judge the teaching rather than the brochure.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and the school report you should read
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, inspecting annually across six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. The market is large: 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, American at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. Seven new schools open for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three IB, adding 16,846 places.

Those numbers explain something families in Tilal Al Ghaf notice without being able to name. The IB cohort is a minority of a very large market, and in a predominantly British-curriculum part of Dubailand a Diploma student may be one of a small number at their school taking a particular Higher Level subject. That is precisely the situation in which selecting a tutor by distance fails and selecting by subject works.

The part of the regulatory picture that affects your week is the mandatory-subject requirement. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, prohibiting combined classes because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and calculates mandatory-subject time on a 40-minute lesson unit. So a Diploma student's day carries load beyond six subjects.

One caution. IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved, or licensed or accredited by the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no provider should claim otherwise without showing a permit number. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. We name KHDA here because it governs your child's school and publishes the inspection report you should read — and the useful part of that report is the subject-level commentary, not the headline band.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, permits and the limits we work to
paragraphs: This market includes operations that sell completed Internal Assessments at a published price. That is not tutoring, and submitting bought work is academic misconduct whose consequence falls on the student rather than the seller. Because Dubai parents are approached by such providers through the same channels as legitimate ones, the boundary belongs on the page before anyone asks.

A tutor may teach the content a piece of coursework rests on, explain what each criterion rewards and what its descriptors mean, test whether a research question is viable, read the student's own draft and give feedback on it, and teach referencing properly. That is the range a supervising teacher works within and it is where almost all of the available improvement sits. A tutor may not write any part of the work, supply a topic to be adopted wholesale, edit a draft into something the student did not produce, or provide data the student did not collect.

We also do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. Those belong to the IB; we reference them, cite the official source and teach the student to read the assessment criteria themselves. And we do not describe tutors as IB examiners where current status cannot be evidenced, because examiner experience gives no access to marking, grade boundaries or unseen paper content in any case.

On regulation: private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Those operating without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so distrust any page printing an amount, and ask any tutor to show you the permit rather than describe it.

process.title: Name the subject and the level
process.description: Not 'IB maths' or 'IB science' but the specific course at the specific level, because each has its own components and weightings. That single answer determines what the plan looks like, and a tutor who does not ask for it is about to teach a category rather than a course.

process.title: Say where the Internal Assessment stands
process.description: No topic yet, a topic but no work, work underway, or a draft written. Those four states need entirely different first sessions, and the earlier your child is in that list the more a tutor can affect a component that frequently carries a fifth or more of the subject grade.

process.title: A diagnostic marked by category
process.description: The first session works real questions and categorises every lost mark as content, method, command term or timing, rather than producing a score. Most students have never had their losses categorised, which is why they revise content they already know and never touch the thing costing them most.

process.title: A free first lesson with the named tutor
process.description: One full lesson, no charge, with the person who would continue. Ask them what the Internal Assessment in that subject is marked out of and against which criteria. A genuine specialist answers immediately; much of this market cannot. Then watch whether they found the real gap.

process.title: Use the short local school run
process.description: Tilal Al Ghaf's own school provision means many pupils here are home early, so a four-thirty or five o'clock start is realistic rather than optimistic. That matters because an earlier session catches a student with attention left, which is worth more than any adjustment to the lesson plan.

process.title: Review against evidence, not habit
process.description: Each report, mock and marked draft is a checkpoint where the plan is tested rather than renewed. Sometimes the right answer is to stop in one subject and move the hour to another, and sometimes to stop entirely. A weekly session with no current target has become a routine rather than a plan.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the course, not the category
whyPoints.description: Chemistry Higher Level and Economics Standard Level are different jobs with different components, and we match by course and level rather than by subject area. A tutor who offers every IB subject equally is offering general academic help at specialist prices.

whyPoints.title: Hours allocated by assessment weighting
whyPoints.description: Diploma subjects build their grades differently, and the same hours produce different returns depending on which component is still in play. We plan from the weightings rather than from which subject worries the family most, which frequently moves the hours somewhere unexpected.

whyPoints.title: Command terms taught explicitly
whyPoints.description: Four to six sessions on how to answer the verbs, using questions from your child's own subjects, lifts marks across the whole timetable because the terms recur everywhere. It is the single most efficient block available in the Diploma and almost nobody sells it, because it is not a subject.

whyPoints.title: Internal Assessment criteria named by letter and mark
whyPoints.description: No competitor page in this market names a single criterion in any subject. We publish them, coach against them, and keep the writing entirely with the student, because the criteria that reward the student's own thinking are both the cheapest marks and the ones outsourcing destroys.

whyPoints.description: KHDA confirmed no fee increase for 2026-27, so the school line is flat and tutoring is the variable. The dirham bands here are competitors' own published figures with the month they were read, so any quote including ours can be checked against something real.

whyPoints.description: No home visits anywhere in the UAE. No special-educational-needs assessment. No distribution of IB papers or mark schemes. No examiner claims we cannot evidence. No guaranteed grades. No approval or accreditation from the IB, KHDA, ADEK or the Ministry of Education.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our villa in Tilal Al Ghaf?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition as live one-to-one lessons over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we run only in India. No tutor is sent to any UAE address. The page uses the phrase 'home tutor' because that is what parents search for, and the question deserves a direct answer. What you get instead is a tutor chosen for the course they teach rather than their willingness to drive out past Hessa Street on a weekday evening.

faqs.question: Why does the subject matter more than the tutor's location here?
faqs.answer: Because Tilal Al Ghaf already has the logistical advantage. The community has a school inside it and sits beside DAMAC Hills and Dubai Sports City, which also do, so the school run is short and your child is home early. The remaining constraint is specialist knowledge, and a tutor who knows Chemistry Higher Level and where its multi-step calculation marks disappear is scarce across the whole emirate rather than only in this community. Distance filtering removes the one variable unrelated to teaching quality.

faqs.question: How should we decide which subject to tutor first?
faqs.answer: By assessment weighting rather than by which subject worries you most. If a subject's Internal Assessment carries a fifth or more of the grade and your child has not started it, those are the most valuable sessions available, because the mark is largely determined by early decisions about scope. If the Internal Assessment is already submitted and only written papers remain, the hours belong in paper technique. Families who allocate by anxiety routinely put the hours where they can change the least.

faqs.question: What are command terms and why do they matter so much?
faqs.answer: They are the verbs IB questions are built on, and each asks for a specific kind of answer. 'Describe' wants what happens; 'explain' wants why; 'compare' wants both similarities and differences; 'evaluate' wants a judgement with reasons on both sides. A student who writes everything they know satisfies none of them. Because the verbs recur across every subject, four to six sessions learning to answer them recovers marks in several subjects simultaneously, which no content teaching achieves.

faqs.question: How many Higher Level subjects can realistically be tutored at once?
faqs.answer: One at two sessions a week, or two at one session each, is the sustainable maximum in term time. Higher Level consumes roughly half again the hours of the Standard Level version of the same subject, because there is more content and in several subjects an additional component with its own technique. Three tutored Higher Level subjects produces a student too tired to complete the set work, and the set work is where most of the improvement actually happens rather than in the session.

faqs.question: What is the Internal Assessment worth in each IB subject?
faqs.answer: It varies, which is exactly why it should be checked rather than assumed. In mathematics the exploration carries a fifth of the grade. In the sciences the individual investigation is marked out of twenty-four and carries a fifth. In Economics the Internal Assessment is three separate commentaries. Confirm the current weighting for each of your child's subjects with their teacher, because the IB revises subject guides, and then let those numbers rather than general impressions decide where the tutoring hours go.

faqs.question: How should a Diploma student actually use past papers?
faqs.answer: Differently for each component. Multiple-choice sections reward timed volume, because the distractors become predictable. Data-analysis sections reward a specific skill set that can be taught as a topic in two or three sessions. Extended-response papers have to be practised whole at least sometimes, or the student never discovers that accuracy falls in the final half hour. And the marking matters more than the doing: one paper a fortnight marked against the scheme with losses categorised beats weekly papers nobody analyses.

faqs.question: Which Dubai schools do Tilal Al Ghaf IB students attend?
faqs.answer: Provision inside and beside the community is predominantly British curriculum, including Royal Grammar School Guildford Dubai within Tilal Al Ghaf itself and Jebel Ali School nearby, so local Diploma students often travel further for IB provision, towards Al Barsha South, Dubai Hills Estate and the Arabian Ranches. Named schools here are ecosystem context only and IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them. Read the current KHDA inspection report for any school you are considering, particularly the subject-level commentary.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: With the thinking and the feedback, yes. A tutor can explain what the assessment instrument rewards, discuss whether a research question is viable, teach the subject content an essay rests on, help a student structure an argument, and give feedback on their own drafts. A tutor cannot write any part of it, choose the question outright, or edit a draft into something the student did not produce. Theory of Knowledge in particular responds well to structured argument practice, because there is no content to revise.

faqs.question: What does IB tutoring cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour for budget and university-student tutors, AED 150 to AED 300 for qualified subject tutors online, and AED 200 to AED 450 or above for IB specialists, with in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 500 including travel. Monthly at one weekly session that is roughly AED 240 to AED 600, AED 600 to AED 1,200, or AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above. Those are published market numbers rather than our prices; the first lesson is free.

faqs.question: Why does my child study Arabic alongside the IB in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because the emirate requires it regardless of the licensed curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies and prohibits combined classes, because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Two things follow: the school day carries load beyond six Diploma subjects, and Arabic is among the most requested tutoring streams in the emirate.

faqs.question: Is the free first lesson genuinely free, and what should I judge?
faqs.answer: One full lesson, no payment, no card required. Judge three things rather than rapport. Did the tutor show real knowledge of that specific course and level, including what the Internal Assessment is marked out of and against which criteria? Did they locate the actual gap rather than accepting your child's account? Was the work set afterwards clear enough to attempt alone? If any answer is no, say so and we match again. That hour settles the most important variable before any money moves.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free in our evening slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you which part is the constraint, because the fixes differ. If the specialist exists but not in your slot, a different evening or a weekend morning usually resolves it, and Tilal Al Ghaf's short school run gives more flexibility than most of this belt. If the subject at that level is not covered in UAE hours at all, the fallback is a tutor in another time zone teaching at a Gulf Standard Time-compatible hour, and we say where they are based rather than concealing it.

faqs.question: Should we book a tutor before or after the first Diploma report?
faqs.answer: Before, if a subject is already uncomfortable, because the first Diploma year is when Internal Assessments are still fully in play and content can be secured as it is taught rather than retaught. Waiting for a report means waiting for confirmation of something the student already knows. If a report has arrived, use it properly: ask which component the marks came from, because a Diploma report that simply says a subject is weak tells a tutor almost nothing actionable.

faqs.question: Do tutors in Dubai need a MoHRE permit, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so distrust quoted amounts. Ask to see the permit rather than accepting a verbal assurance.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.closingHeading: Name the course, then check the weighting
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.closingBody: Two pieces of information decide most of a sensible plan. The specific course your child takes and the level they take it at, and what each of its components is worth. With those in hand you can see immediately where the available marks still are: an unstarted Internal Assessment worth a fifth of the grade is a different proposition from a written paper six weeks away. Then book a free first lesson and ask the tutor what that Internal Assessment is marked out of and against which criteria. A genuine specialist answers at once. intro.heading: Is there an IB tutor near Town Square who knows the course?
paragraphs: Town Square is a Nshama community off Al Qudra Road, built out recently and populated largely by younger families in apartments and townhouses rather than by the long-established villa households of inner Dubai. It is a good place to live and a difficult place to find a Diploma specialist, because those two facts are connected. Dubai's professional tutoring supply grew up around the oldest international schools — Jumeirah, Al Barsha, Mirdif, the Greens — and the Dubailand corridor filled with residents faster than it filled with tutors.

There is a second constraint most parents never hear about. The people genuinely qualified to teach a named Diploma course to final grade are mostly serving school teachers, and both the MoHRE private tuition permit's code of conduct and, in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar a teacher from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. So the obvious local answer — your child's own teacher, privately — is not available, and any provider offering it is telling you something about itself.

The third constraint is the apartment. Home tutoring assumes a spare room with a door, and in a Town Square two or three bedroom apartment the realistic venue is the dining table with the rest of the household around it. Parents rarely raise this in advance and frequently discover it in week two. It is one of the quieter reasons online delivery suits this community: a laptop and a pair of headphones in a bedroom is more private than a stranger at the kitchen table.

IB Gram's model follows from all three. Lessons for Town Square families are delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service we run only in India. That means the pool your child is matched from is defined by which course a tutor has actually taught rather than by who will drive down Al Qudra Road at six in the evening.

This page does not skip the home-tutoring question, though. You will find what the Dubai market genuinely charges for a visit versus an online session, attributed to the providers who published those figures. You will find how the private-tutor permit works and how to check one. You will find who regulates what across the UAE, because the five emirate regulators are named by almost nobody in this search result. And you will find what happens when no specialist is free, which is a thing providers prefer not to describe.

KHDA reported 387,441 pupils across Dubai's 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the International Baccalaureate at 7% of enrolment. Dubai is also adding seven new private schools for 2026-27 — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — creating 16,846 new places. The Diploma population is growing. The local specialist supply in a community like Town Square is not growing at the same rate, which is the gap this page is about.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-town-square.programmesIntro: IB Gram covers the full IB continuum for Town Square families, and what a Primary Years pupil needs shares almost nothing with what a Diploma candidate needs. Here is what each programme asks and the part that bites in a Dubai school year.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Organised around transdisciplinary units of inquiry and assessed continuously by the class teacher against learning outcomes rather than by examination. Children document thinking in portfolios and finish Year 6 with the PYP Exhibition, a self-directed inquiry presented to the school community. The real outputs are reading fluency, number sense and written explanation.
programmes.countryNote: Town Square has a young population, so PYP enquiries outnumber Diploma ones here. The commonest issue is a child arriving mid-primary from another system who computes quickly and is marked down because the task wanted a method explained. That is a mismatch of expectation rather than ability, and it is cheap to fix at this age.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Every subject marked against four criteria, each 0-8, differing by subject group. Sciences mark knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Year 11 adds the Personal Project with its own criteria. Reports show criterion profiles rather than a single grade.
programmes.countryNote: Town Square families often meet the MYP after a move from a British or Indian curriculum school, and the four-letter report is the first shock. A profile of 7, 4, 5, 3 is an instruction rather than a middling result, and reading it properly usually identifies one transferable skill dragging several subjects at once.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher Level and three Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment marked internally and moderated by the IB. The total runs to 45 including up to three bonus points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. UAE schools sit the May session.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students from Town Square are usually travelling a considerable distance to school, because the community's own provision is primary-weighted and IB Diploma schools sit further in. That commute is one of the reasons we work online: it has already taken an hour out of the day before any tutoring is considered.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two DP courses paired with a career-related study, a reflective project, service learning, personal and professional skills and a language requirement. A route for a student who wants Diploma-standard academic subjects with an applied direction rather than the full six-subject load.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools offer the CP, so Town Square families typically meet it as a mid-sixth-form option rather than a Year 11 choice. The DP courses inside a CP are marked to the same standard as any Diploma candidate's, so the tutoring requirement for those subjects is identical.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-town-square.subjectsIntro: The IB subjects Town Square families request most, with the part that actually costs marks. Availability varies by level and term, and the trial lesson is where the match is confirmed rather than promised.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra carries this course. Marks disappear in proof, in HL calculus applications and in unstructured Paper 2 questions with no scaffold indicating a technique. The Exploration is a fifth of the grade and fails more often on absent personal engagement than on weak mathematics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and confident calculator work. The common error is choosing it as the lighter option and then meeting regression and hypothesis testing without statistical vocabulary. HL adds matrices, graph theory and complex numbers.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Loose definitions cost marks on the short-answer paper, and unshown working costs them on the structured paper. Uncertainty propagation and graph linearisation are the recurring gaps, and the HL practical paper is met late in most schools.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are the two walls, with moles underneath both. Reciting reagents is not explaining why a nucleophile attacks where it does, and sign conventions quietly destroy otherwise sound thermodynamics answers.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content is the trap rather than difficulty. Command terms decide the mark, and a knowledgeable student answering discuss with a list of facts scores low. Statistical treatment in the investigation is routinely thin.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams must be drawn, labelled and then used in the prose rather than placed beside it. Commentaries are assessed on application to a named real article, so the article choice sets the ceiling before any analysis is written.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Frameworks score nothing alone; the marks sit in applying them to the case material and reaching a supported judgement. The HL research project needs a live organisation and a question narrow enough for the word limit.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen analysis under time pressure and most lost marks come from summarising rather than analysing how meaning is produced. The Individual Oral needs a real global issue and two works properly prepared.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Every claim must be anchored in a named study with its method and findings; vague recall of a famous experiment scores little. The HL extensions and the experimental investigation with its inferential statistic reward structured support.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The written papers test architecture, networks and abstract data structures as much as code, and comfortable programmers still lose marks tracing algorithms by hand. The solution project needs a real client and documented success criteria.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by the exhibition of three objects and the prescribed-title essay, feeding the three bonus points with the Extended Essay. The essay fails when it becomes general opinion rather than claim and counterclaim grounded in areas of knowledge.

subjects.name: Extended Essay supervision support
subjects.description: Four thousand words of independent research against five criteria. The research question decides most of the grade. A tutor coaches question, method and reflection; the writing remains entirely the student's own.

sections.heading: What a home tutor actually means in a Town Square apartment
paragraphs: This is the part of the home-tutoring question nobody writes about, and in a community built mainly of apartments and townhouses it deserves to be first. A home tutor needs a working space. In a three-bedroom villa that is a study with a door. In a Town Square two-bedroom apartment it is the dining table, with a younger sibling in the next room, a television somewhere and the ordinary noise of a household at six in the evening.

Families discover this in week two rather than week zero. The tutor is competent, the student is willing, and the session is being conducted in the busiest room in the home while everyone else tiptoes around it. Concentration suffers on both sides, and nobody says anything because the arrangement was expensive and the problem feels petty.

An online session inverts that geometry. The student takes a laptop and headphones into a bedroom, closes the door, and has a genuinely private hour. Nobody else in the household has to adjust their evening. For a Diploma student working through a Chemistry past paper or talking through an Extended Essay research question, privacy is not a luxury: it is the difference between admitting what they do not understand and pretending they do.

None of which means in-home tutoring is bad. For a younger child who cannot self-regulate, a person physically present who can take a phone off the table is worth real money, and any page claiming otherwise is selling rather than advising. But the trade-off in Town Square specifically is sharper than in a villa community, and it is worth knowing before you pay a travel premium for a tutor to sit at your dining table.

sections.heading: Counting the specialist supply honestly
paragraphs: Replace the feeling of scarcity with structure and the decision becomes easier. Dubai had 387,441 private-school pupils in 2024-25 across 227 schools, with the IB at roughly 7% of enrolment. That is a substantial Diploma population, spread across the whole emirate, and only its final two years sit the Diploma at all. Narrow to one subject at one level and the citywide cohort is small; narrow to Town Square and it is very small.

The tutor side narrows faster than the student side. Somebody qualified to teach, say, Physics Higher Level to final grade is typically a current Diploma teacher at a Dubai school, a former one, or a graduate who has trained specifically on the course. Current school teachers are the largest group and the most constrained, because the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with their own school and press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules describes the same prohibition in Abu Dhabi.

Then geography removes most of the remainder. A tutor based in Al Barsha or Jumeirah will work locally before driving to Al Qudra Road, and the ones who will make that drive price the journey into the rate. What is left, for a named Higher Level subject on a specific weekday evening, is frequently nobody.

The table below describes the shape of that scarcity rather than claiming a census. The figures are estimates of structure, and the point is the pattern: for broad early-years support, local supply is adequate; for a named Diploma subject at Higher Level, it collapses. That collapse is the entire argument for matching online.

sections.heading: Who regulates what, and who regulates tutors
paragraphs: This is published by almost nobody in this search result, and it is the context that makes every other claim checkable. Private schools in the UAE are regulated by the emirate, not federally, and there are five bodies rather than one.

In Dubai, which covers every school a Town Square family uses, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. In Sharjah, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education. In Ras Al Khaimah, the Department of Knowledge does. And the Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods — so curriculum approval, not only inspection, sits at emirate level there.

What matters for tutoring is that none of those bodies regulates private tutors. That sits with the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, through the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. An organisation running tutoring from premises in Dubai is a different legal animal and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry.

So the common market phrase describing a tutor as approved by KHDA points at nothing that exists. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation, licence or partnership, has no office or centre in the UAE, and claims none. The table sets out the map so you can test any claim anyone makes to you.

sections.heading: What the market charges, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Start with what the extra money buys rather than with the rate card, because that is the question a Town Square family is actually asking. The gap between an online qualified tutor and an in-home visit is roughly AED 30-200 an hour depending on where you look, and it is worth knowing precisely what sits inside that gap.

It buys physical presence. Somebody in the room who notices attention drifting, takes a phone off the table and holds the authority a screen cannot. For a nine-year-old that is genuinely valuable. It also buys, for a community as far out as Town Square, a driver's time: a tutor coming from Al Barsha or Jumeirah is spending seventy to ninety minutes on the road for a single session, and that time is being paid for whether the invoice itemises it or not. What it does not buy is more subject expertise. Expertise correlates with who has taught the course, not with who lives within reach.

sections.heading: Is a visiting tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Most parents in Dubai have never been told this is a regulated activity, and the people who benefit from that silence are the ones operating without a permit. Private tuition in the UAE sits under a work-permit regime introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. The permit is issued by MoHRE, is granted free of charge for two years, and the official route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Because it costs nothing and takes two working days, there is no legitimate reason for any tutor to lack one. Eligibility is broader than parents expect: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. So a university student tutoring your Year 9 child can hold a perfectly valid permit — the question is only whether they do.

MoHRE states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, so a figure circulating informally as a specific dirham amount should be disregarded; we are not going to repeat an unverified number.

The code of conduct attached to the permit bars a tutor from serving students affiliated with their own school, which is the point worth repeating because it closes off the option families most want. If a provider offers you your child's own classroom teacher privately, that is information about the provider rather than a convenience.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with Diploma coursework
paragraphs: This has to be stated plainly on a UAE IB page, because the search results for Dubai IB help contain operators who sell finished coursework. One advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Buying one is not a shortcut with a price attached; it is an academic-honesty breach, and the IB withdraws awards for malpractice.

The permitted ground is wide and genuinely useful. A tutor may teach the content the assessment rests on. They may explain what each criterion asks for and what marks it carries. They may help narrow a research question until it is answerable within the word limit. They may review a method and say that it will not generate usable data. They may read a draft the student has written and give feedback on it. All of that is ordinary teaching and all of it is permitted.

What a tutor may not do is produce the work. Not write a section. Not supply a paragraph to insert. Not rewrite the student's prose into their own. Not provide a template needing only numbers. Not edit a draft to a finish so that the submitted text is substantially theirs. The student signs a declaration that the work is their own and the supervisor signs alongside them, so this is a practical line rather than a procedural one.

We also do not supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. Those are the awarding bodies' copyright, and for unreleased material there is a malpractice exposure as well. We reference them, cite the official source and teach from them, which is lawful and more useful than a folder of files.

sections.heading: When no specialist is free for your subject
paragraphs: No provider covers every IB subject at every level in every term, and the ones implying otherwise are the ones to distrust. Theory of Knowledge at short notice, Higher Level Computer Science, smaller Group 2 languages, Music and Film are genuinely scarce, and a Town Square family asking in March deserves a straight answer rather than a holding pattern.

So here is ours. If a matching specialist is free, we propose them and you take a free trial lesson with that person, not with a salesperson and not with a different tutor. If the only available specialist works from another time zone, we say so and offer the slots that genuinely exist, which for most of our roster means early morning or evening in Gulf Standard Time. If nobody suitable is free at all, we say that too, and we would rather lose the enquiry than put a general tutor in front of a Higher Level candidate eight weeks before a session.

There is one substitution we will never make, and it is worth stating because the market does make it. We do not offer a UAE home visit as a fallback when the online match is hard, because there is no UAE visiting service to fall back on. IB Gram has no office, centre or branch in the UAE, and nobody on our roster will arrive at a Town Square address. Everything delivered here is one-to-one over live video.

If the match turns out wrong after it starts, say so early. A mismatch between a competent tutor and a particular student is common and is nobody's failure — pace, explanation style and personality matter more than credentials once basic competence is established. Tell us in the first fortnight and we rematch.

sections.heading: What is deliberately missing from this page
paragraphs: Several things that competitors in this search result do publish are absent here on purpose, and the omissions are worth naming.

There is no specific IB exam date. The IB's own site blocks automated retrieval, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org, and we will not put an unverified date in front of a parent who will plan around it. UAE schools sit the May session; get exact dates from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org. Cambridge and Pearson dates are published and we do use them: Cambridge runs June and November series with the February/March series offered to India only, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with November results reaching students in January.

There is no star rating, no satisfaction percentage and no average score achieved by students we have supported. Competitors publish figures like 4.9 from several hundred reviews, sometimes in two conflicting versions on the same page, and none states a sample size, a date or a method. A number without those three is decoration, and self-asserted review markup is also against Google's structured-data policy.

There is no regulator claim, no UAE address, no examiner description we cannot evidence, and no grade guarantee. We also use no non-UAE phone number as the conversion path on a UAE page, which two ranking competitors do. And we will not imply that tutoring is required for Ministry of Education equivalency, university admission or school progression, because that is a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process.
