faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor to come to our apartment in Town Square?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We deliver one-to-one IB tuition to Town Square online, over live video, and make no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-home visiting is a service we run in India only. Other Dubai providers do visit, at published market rates of roughly AED 180-500 an hour including travel, and from Al Qudra Road a real share of that is the drive. There is also a practical point: in most Town Square apartments the only available venue is the dining table, which is rarely a good hour for either party.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring better than a home tutor for a Town Square apartment?
faqs.answer: For a Diploma student, usually yes, and the reason is privacy rather than technology. An in-home session in a two or three bedroom apartment happens in the busiest room of the home, with a sibling next door and the household adjusting around it. A student with a laptop and headphones behind a closed bedroom door has a genuinely private hour, which matters because admitting what you do not understand is easier without an audience. For a young child who cannot self-regulate, physical presence still wins.

faqs.question: Are there IB Diploma specialists living near Town Square?
faqs.answer: Some, and for primary or general MYP support the local pool is adequate. For a named Diploma subject at Higher Level it is frequently empty. The IB is roughly 7% of Dubai's 387,441 private-school pupils across 227 schools, spread across the whole emirate, and only the final two years sit the Diploma. Most qualified people are serving school teachers, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars tutoring students enrolled at their own school. Town Square is also a newer community where residential build-out outran tutoring supply.

faqs.question: Who regulates my child's school, and does anyone regulate tutors?
faqs.answer: Dubai private schools, including every school a Town Square family uses, come under KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects annually from Outstanding to Very Weak. Elsewhere it is ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. None of them regulates private tutors — that is MoHRE permit territory — so a tutor described as holding regulator approval is describing nothing that exists.

faqs.question: How do I check a tutor is permitted to teach in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask for the permit and verify it with MoHRE. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website or e-services. Because it costs nothing and takes two days, there is no legitimate reason to lack one. Eligible applicants include school and sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE states tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties; no amounts are published.

faqs.question: Why can't we just hire my child's own teacher privately?
faqs.answer: Because the rules bar it. The MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that prohibits serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and press reporting on Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules describes the same prohibition for private and charter school staff there. It is the option families most want and the one least available. A provider marketing your child's own teacher privately is telling you something about how carefully it reads the rules, which is worth knowing before anything else.

faqs.question: What does the in-home travel premium actually buy in Town Square?
faqs.answer: Two things, and not the third you might expect. It buys physical presence — somebody who notices attention drifting and can take a phone off the table — which is genuinely valuable for a younger child. And it buys a driver's time, because a tutor coming from Al Barsha or Jumeirah spends seventy to ninety minutes on the road for one session, paid for whether the invoice itemises it or not. What it does not buy is more subject expertise, which correlates with who has taught the course rather than who lives nearby.

faqs.question: What should a Town Square family expect to pay for IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures read in October 2026: budget online AED 33-65 an hour (Tutopiya, EdFlik), qualified online subject tutors AED 150-300 with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, IB specialists AED 200-450 and above with TutorChase at AED 270, in-home visits AED 180-500 including travel, and BartyED at AED 650 premium. Advertised monthly packages include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four in-home two-hour visits. Those belong to the providers named, not to us; we quote after the free trial.

faqs.question: Which schools do Town Square children usually attend?
faqs.answer: On the shorter runs: South View School, Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City, The Aquila School, Jebel Ali School, Ranches Primary School and JESS Arabian Ranches. For secondary, many travel to GEMS Metropole in Motor City, GEMS FirstPoint in The Villa, GEMS United in Dubai Sports City, Victory Heights Primary, Dunecrest American School or Safa Community School. For a specific Diploma combination, families go further to schools in Al Barsha and Silicon Oasis. We name these as context and have no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: What happens if you have no tutor for my child's subject?
faqs.answer: We say so. Theory of Knowledge at short notice, Higher Level Computer Science, smaller Group 2 languages, Music and Film are genuinely scarce, and in some terms we cannot cover them at all. In that case we decline rather than putting a general tutor in front of a Higher Level candidate, and we have lost enquiries doing it. If the only matching specialist works from another time zone, we say that too and offer the slots that actually exist. There is no in-home fallback, because no UAE visiting service exists to fall back on.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write part of my child's Internal Assessment or Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: No, and the boundary is easier to apply than parents fear. Permitted: teaching the underlying content, explaining what each criterion asks and what it is worth, helping narrow a research question until it is answerable, reviewing whether a method will produce usable data, and giving feedback on a draft your child has written. Not permitted: writing any part, supplying text to insert, rewriting the prose, or editing to a finish. Operators in this market sell completed Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750, which risks the student's entire Diploma.

faqs.question: Do you supply past papers and mark schemes to Town Square students?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is copyright rather than reluctance. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to the awarding bodies, and reproducing them is infringement — for unreleased material there is a malpractice exposure as well. We reference them, cite the official source and teach from them. In practice that works better than a folder of files, because the value was never in possessing the paper; it was in having somebody mark the attempt properly.

faqs.question: When is the IB exam session for Town Square students?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the May session. We deliberately publish no specific IB date, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and we will not put an unverified exam date in front of a parent who will plan around it — get it from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org directly. For Cambridge the position is published: International GCSE and O Level run in June and November series, and the February/March series is offered to India only, so UAE candidates sit June and November. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November.

faqs.question: Can lessons continue while we travel out of the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the real advantages of the model for Town Square families, many of whom travel during school breaks. Because the tutor's location is already part of the arrangement rather than an obstacle to it, a student can keep a weekly session running from another country with only the time of day adjusted. We reset the slot for the period rather than cancelling it, which matters most during a term carrying an Internal Assessment or Extended Essay deadline.

faqs.question: What if the trial lesson is fine but it stops working after a month?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we rematch. A mismatch between a capable tutor and a particular student can take a few sessions to surface, and it is nobody's failure — pace, explanation style and personality all matter more than credentials once basic competence is established. The first fortnight is the right time to say so, and a stalled review at the three-week mark is exactly where we would change the plan or the tutor. What not to do is spend a term hoping, which costs the money and the term together.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-town-square.closingHeading: One hour with the right specialist, then decide
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-town-square.closingBody: If you came looking for an IB home tutor in Town Square, you now have the honest picture: the local pool of Diploma specialists is thin, the travel premium buys presence and a long drive rather than expertise, an apartment rarely offers the private room in-home tutoring assumes, and nobody regulates tutors except MoHRE through a permit that costs nothing. IB Gram's answer is one-to-one tuition over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE. Tell us the school, the subject and the level, and we will arrange a free trial lesson with the specialist who would teach your child.

intro.heading: The same tutor, two prices, four streets apart
paragraphs: Families in Umm Al Sheif discover something odd when they start asking around for Diploma help. A tutor quotes one rate for a villa off Al Wasl Road and a lower one for an apartment in Al Safa, and occasionally a higher one again for the Palm. The tutor is the same person with the same experience teaching the same syllabus. What has changed is the length of the drive, the parking, the time of day the visit has to happen, and in some cases a judgement about what the address can bear.

That is worth understanding rather than resenting, because it tells you what you are actually buying when you buy an in-home hour. In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is absorbed, with Bestimate's rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500. A qualified subject tutor teaching online is quoted at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. The gap is travel, scarcity and address, in that order.

The second thing a comparison across this belt reveals is that the neighbourhoods differ far less than the quotes do. Umm Al Sheif, Umm Suqeim, Al Safa and Al Manara draw on an overlapping set of schools, sit within ten minutes of each other, and have a resident tutor supply that is broadly similar and broadly generalist. Palm Jumeirah is the exception, because the causeway makes it a genuinely awkward destination at 5pm and the quotes reflect that honestly.

Where the belt is genuinely well served is in schools. The Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim corridor holds some of the longest-established British and IB schools in Dubai within a short drive, which is why so many families live here. What it does not hold, because nowhere does, is a reliable supply of resident specialists in a particular Diploma subject at a particular level. A Chemistry Higher Level specialist free at 6.30pm is not an address-dependent commodity.

IB Gram's position is plain. Teaching is one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, at a fixed weekly hour. We do not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run in India only. The in-home market here is real and is priced in this page with sources attached so you can judge the alternative with numbers rather than impressions. What the online model removes is precisely the premium that your postcode attracts. What follows is the four-way comparison, the villa premium broken into its parts, the school map of this belt, what two children can and cannot share, which subjects the coast is short of, and what two Diploma years cost from an address like yours.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-umm-al-sheif.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes run along this stretch of the coast, and families here ask about all three, often at once within one household.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the creativity, activity and service requirement. Most subjects carry an internally assessed component marked by the school and moderated by the IB, typically around a fifth of the grade. Points accumulate across two years rather than being decided in one examination fortnight.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision along the Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim corridor is good and the subject menus differ school by school, particularly at Higher Level where cohort size decides what runs. A family here comparing two schools should ask which Higher Level subjects actually ran last year rather than which appear in the prospectus.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced across eight subject groups, with each subject assessed on four criteria and a Personal Project in the final year. Grades arrive as criterion levels rather than percentages, which is the thing parents most often ask a tutor to translate, and the standard or extended mathematics split in MYP 4 matters more than it looks.
programmes.countryNote: Several coast schools run the full continuum, so a child can move from the primary years into the Diploma in one building. That continuity is a genuine advantage and it also means the first Diploma internal deadline comes from teachers who already know the student and set expectations accordingly.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led and transdisciplinary, with no external examinations and mathematics and literacy embedded in units of inquiry rather than timetabled as separate subjects in the British manner. Support here is about number fluency and written method, and short frequent sessions suit it better than long ones.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP schools deliver the mandatory UAE subjects from the primary years, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ between the groups.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-umm-al-sheif.subjectsIntro: The Diploma subjects coast families ask for, and the component that usually prompts the first message.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic route, with a non-calculator paper and an additional investigation paper at Higher Level. Requests cluster in the first term of DP1, when the pace of the algebra outruns a student who was comfortable at IGCSE or in MYP extended mathematics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with technology permitted throughout. Requests arrive later, usually in DP2, when the Higher Level statistical content turns out to be considerably harder than the course's reputation on the school run.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic chemistry divides Higher Level students, and calculation accuracy accounts for most of the rest. The internal assessment loses marks in data processing rather than in experimental design, which is a quick and specific fix.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty treatment and graph linearisation cost more marks than any gap in physics, and fields and electromagnetic induction are where Higher Level students stall. Both are mathematics problems wearing a physics label.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume plus command-term precision. Students who revise by rereading hold a great deal and cannot deploy it, and the remedy is answering past questions under timed conditions rather than covering the syllabus again.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation structure decide the essay papers, with quantitative questions added at Higher Level. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published articles, and article selection is the rushed step.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis, the comparative essay, the individual oral and at Higher Level the essay. The oral is the component most often left unrehearsed and the one that rehearses best on video, because the format is already a conversation.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-based analysis and a research project at Higher Level. Students describe a business rather than applying a framework to it, which is a writing-structure problem and among the faster things to improve.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The essay is capped at 4,000 words with a school-appointed supervisor; Theory of Knowledge carries an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay. Both are coached rather than taught, and the boundary on what a tutor may do is tighter here than anywhere else.

sections.heading: Umm Al Sheif against Umm Suqeim, Al Safa and Palm Jumeirah
paragraphs: Set the four side by side and the similarities outweigh the differences. All four draw on an overlapping set of schools along the Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim corridor and out toward Al Sufouh. All four are within about ten minutes of each other outside peak hours. All four have a resident tutor supply that is small relative to demand and weighted toward generalists rather than Diploma subject specialists. None of them contains a reliable supply of, say, a Chemistry Higher Level tutor free on a Tuesday at 6.30pm.

What differs is density and access. Al Safa, with its mix of apartments and villas, supports more local tutoring activity simply because more people live within a short distance, and in-home quotes there come in lower for the same person doing the same job. Umm Al Sheif and Al Manara are low-density villa districts where a visit means a dedicated drive. Umm Suqeim has the best school access of the four. Palm Jumeirah is a genuine outlier, because the causeway and the frond layout turn a short map distance into a long journey at exactly the hour a session needs to start.

Door times are similar across the belt and worse than the map suggests. School runs along this corridor are short in distance and slow in practice between 3pm and 4pm, with the Al Wasl Road and Jumeirah Beach Road crossings doing most of the damage. Students are home between about 3.40pm and 4.20pm on an ordinary day and after 5pm on an activity day, which puts the durable session window between 6pm and 7.30pm in all four areas.

So the comparison resolves to one conclusion for all four: the differences are logistical and the right decision is identical. Choose a tutor by subject, level and component experience, set the hour after the real door time, and decline to pay a premium that reflects a drive rather than a difference in teaching. In Al Safa that is a mild saving. In Umm Al Sheif and on the Palm it is a substantial one.

sections.heading: Why a villa address changes the quote and not the lesson
paragraphs: Break an in-home quote into its parts and three of the four have nothing to do with teaching. The first part is the hour taught, which is the same wherever it happens. The second is travel time, which for a low-density villa district means a dedicated round trip rather than a visit squeezed between two others nearby. A tutor who can teach three consecutive hours in one Al Safa tower cannot do the same across Umm Al Sheif, and the difference lands in the rate.

The third part is scarcity, which is the quiet one. A tutor hireable within a twenty-minute radius of any single Dubai neighbourhood is drawn from a small pool, and small pools price upward regardless of quality. The fourth is the address effect, which some independent tutors apply deliberately and others arrive at by instinct, and which is worth naming because it is the component a family can simply decline to pay rather than negotiate down.

What a parent gets for all of that is convenience, which is a real benefit and should be priced as one, and an adult physically in the room, which genuinely matters for a younger or less independent child. What they do not get is a better-matched tutor. Diploma subjects split into Higher and Standard Level, mathematics splits into two separate courses, and the sciences split again by internal assessment component. The person who has taken four students through a Physics internal assessment is not more likely to live near you because your road is nice.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, so there is no version of this service where a tutor arrives at an Umm Al Sheif address. Home tutoring is a service we run in India only. Every lesson here is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which means the fee reflects the hour taught and the specialism, and nothing else. If an adult in the room is genuinely your requirement, hire an independent local tutor and ask to see their MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free to obtain and valid for two years.

sections.heading: The school map of this belt, and who feeds what
paragraphs: The reason families pay to live along this corridor is the schools, and on that measure the area delivers. Within a short drive of Umm Al Sheif sit several of the longest-established British schools in Dubai and several running the IB Diploma or the full continuum, alongside schools in Al Sufouh and the Al Barsha edge reached by Sheikh Zayed Road. For a family choosing a home around a school, this belt has more genuine options inside fifteen minutes than most of the city.

What that does not translate into is uniform Diploma provision. Higher Level subject menus differ between schools and depend on cohort size, so a subject listed in a prospectus may not have run last year. The question to ask at an admissions meeting is which Higher Level subjects actually ran in the most recent cohort and how many students took them, because a Higher Level class of four is a different experience from one of eighteen, and a subject that did not run is not an option at all.

Internal assessment calendars also differ across the belt, by a fortnight or more between the Jumeirah corridor and the Al Sufouh cluster. For a household with two Diploma students at different schools, that means two separate deadline peaks rather than one, and a tutoring plan built around a single family schedule will collide with one of them. Get both internal calendars in September.

On inspection, Dubai private schools are inspected annually by KHDA on a six-band scale, and the published report carries far more useful detail than the headline band. For a Diploma family the sections worth reading are secondary phase attainment and progress in the relevant subjects, and the commentary on teaching in the secondary phase. We do not publish ratings we have not read on the regulator's own site, and a strong overall band built on a good primary phase says little about Year 12 chemistry.

sections.heading: Two children, one evening: what can and cannot be shared
paragraphs: Households along this belt often have two or three children in the system at once, frequently at different schools and in different programmes, and the question that follows is whether tutoring can be shared. The honest answer has two parts. An hour cannot be shared: one-to-one means one student in the session, because two students in an hour is a group class with two people in it and the attention halves. An evening can be shared, and that is where the real saving sits.

Consecutive slots, typically 6pm and 7.15pm, give each child a full one-to-one hour while costing the household one weeknight rather than two or three. Each child gets their own notes, because they are assessed separately and a shared note is useless to both. If the subjects differ the tutors differ, and that is fine; the point of the arrangement is the household's calendar rather than the tutor's.

A genuine group arrangement is a different product and worth considering on its own terms. Two students in the same subject at the same level with the same school scheme can work productively together, particularly for timed practice and mark-scheme discussion, and the cost per child falls substantially. It fails when the two are at different levels, at different schools, or when one needs a topic the other already holds, which in practice is most sibling pairs.

The cheapest arrangement of all for a household with several children is the one families overlook: one child's session plus structured self-study for the others, with the tutored subject chosen as the one that most threatens a points total. Buying help for three children because there are three children is the same error as buying three sciences because there are three sciences, and it produces the same result.

sections.heading: The subjects this coast is short of
paragraphs: Demand along this belt is not evenly spread, and the pattern is consistent enough to plan around. The heaviest Diploma demand is in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at both levels, Chemistry at Higher Level and Physics at Higher Level, in that order. Those are also the hardest matches to make at a prime evening slot, and they are the subjects where resident local supply is thinnest in every one of the four neighbourhoods compared above.

Biology and Economics are easier to match and are requested later in the cycle, usually after a DP2 mock rather than in DP1. English A: Language and Literature requests cluster around the individual oral, which is a specific component rather than a subject-wide problem and which rehearses unusually well on video. Business Management requests are usually about writing structure rather than content.

The genuinely scarce categories are two. The first is a tutor with experience of one specific internal assessment component, which is a narrower pool than a subject specialist and which matters because the component carries around a fifth of the grade. The second is anything in a minority Diploma subject: a language B at Higher Level in a less common language, or a subject that only a handful of Dubai schools run at all.

The practical consequence is about lead time rather than price. For a common Standard Level subject at a mid-evening slot in term time, a match usually takes days. For a Higher Level science specialist, allow up to a fortnight, and longer in the eight to twelve weeks before the May session when that pool is tightest. If nobody suitable is free at your preferred hour we will say so and offer the nearest real option rather than filling the slot.

sections.heading: What two Diploma years actually cost from this address
paragraphs: Set the numbers out across two years rather than per hour, because that is how the decision is really made. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour arrangement run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for a specialist in an examination year. Over two academic years in one subject, the middle band alone is a significant household commitment, and it deserves a deliberate decision rather than a drift.

Converted to hourly, the Dubai market sorts cleanly. Budget online platforms advertise from AED 33 to 65, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified subject tutor online is quoted at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 500 to 650 and more, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home visits sit at AED 180 to 500 once travel is absorbed.

The two errors that cost coast families most are buying the premium tier for everything and buying hours in the wrong term. Timed-paper marking and accuracy drilling do not need a tutor at AED 500 an hour; internal assessment topic screening at Higher Level does. Twenty sessions in April of DP2 cost the same as twenty spread through DP1 and achieve less, because the April sessions arrive after the coursework has been submitted and the content window has closed.

For household context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are flat, which makes tutoring the moving line in an education budget and the one worth planning deliberately. sections.heading: The travelling family, and the gap nobody plans for
paragraphs: Households on this stretch of coast travel more than most, and the pattern is predictable: a long summer away, a substantial winter break, and often a mid-term trip. For a Diploma student those absences land on specific parts of the calendar, and one of them is genuinely consequential. The summer between DP1 and DP2 is when internal assessment work should be drafted, because it is the only stretch with no competing deadlines, and it is also when most families are out of the country.

An in-home arrangement stops at the airport. A video arrangement does not, provided the time zone is agreed once rather than renegotiated weekly and the frequency is set lower than term time rather than aspirationally the same. Two sessions a week during July, aimed at drafting rather than teaching, converts the summer from a gap into the most productive stretch of the two years. It is the single most common reason coast families choose video delivery over a local tutor.

The winter break has a similar shape with less at stake. In DP2 it sits just before the mock window, which makes it the right time for one or two timed papers and a proper review rather than for new content. A student who sits a paper in the first week of January has a diagnosis before the mocks rather than after them, and that changes what the whole spring term is spent on.

Mid-term trips are mostly a scheduling nuisance rather than an academic problem, with one exception: a trip that lands immediately before an internal deadline. That is worth checking against the school's own calendar in September, because the deadline will not move and the trip usually can. Families discover this collision in the week it happens with remarkable regularity.

sections.heading: What a higher price cannot buy
paragraphs: Since this page is largely about price, it should be explicit about what no amount of money purchases in this market. It does not buy a grade. Nobody can promise a particular points total, a particular subject grade or university admission, and an offer to do so should end the conversation rather than start a negotiation. It does not buy a regulator's approval either: IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge International or Pearson, and claims none. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; we operate no premises in the UAE.

It does not buy a school relationship. We do not describe any named school or group as a partner or client, because we have no such arrangement with any of them; students we support attend schools across Dubai, which is a different and true statement. Any provider listing a long roster of schools as partners should be asked what the relationship actually is, and in this market the answer is frequently nothing.

It does not buy coursework. We do not produce, rewrite or edit assessed work in any subject at any price, and where an internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project is involved a tutor teaches the content, explains the criteria, demonstrates a worked example on a completely different topic, and reads the student's own draft and asks questions. At least one site ranking for these searches sells completed internal assessments; the consequence of buying one falls on the candidate, who can lose the diploma.

And it does not buy board material. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB and the examination boards, and your child's school has legitimate access. A tutor working from them in a session is ordinary practice; a site hosting a download library is distributing someone else's property. What a higher price can legitimately buy is a scarcer specialism, which is why internal assessment screening at Higher Level is worth paying up for and timed-paper marking is not.

process.description: Door times across Umm Al Sheif, Umm Suqeim, Al Safa and Al Manara land between about 3.40pm and 4.20pm, later from the Palm and later again on activity days. We aim for the slot that works in week nine, not week one.

faqs.question: Why is the in-home quote for Umm Al Sheif higher than for Al Safa?
faqs.answer: Three reasons, none of them teaching. Umm Al Sheif is a low-density villa district, so a visit is a dedicated round trip rather than one of three in the same tower, and the unpaid driving lands in the rate. Local supply within a twenty-minute radius is small, and small pools price upward. And some independent tutors apply an address effect, deliberately or by instinct. The Dubai in-home band is AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is absorbed, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor.

faqs.question: Do you send tutors to villas in Umm Al Sheif or on the Palm?
faqs.answer: No, not to any UAE address. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home tutoring is a service we run in India only. The Dubai in-home market exists and is priced on this page with sources, so you can judge it fairly: visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour and monthly packages at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. If an adult in the room is your requirement, hire independently and ask to see the MoHRE permit.

faqs.question: Is Palm Jumeirah genuinely harder to serve than the mainland streets?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the higher quotes from that address are honest rather than opportunistic. The single causeway and the frond layout turn a short map distance into a real journey at exactly the hour a session needs to start, so a tutor visiting the Palm at 5.30pm is committing a large block of unpaid time. It is the one place on this belt where the in-home premium reflects something physical. Online delivery removes the problem entirely, which is why uptake there is high.

faqs.question: Can our two Diploma children share a tutoring hour to save money?
faqs.answer: Not usefully. One-to-one means one student in the session, and two students in an hour is a small group class in which the attention halves. What works is sharing an evening: consecutive slots at 6pm and 7.15pm, full rate each, giving each child a complete hour while costing the household one weeknight instead of three. A genuine pair session is a different product and works only when both are in the same subject at the same level working on the same papers.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level subjects are hardest to book on this side of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, Chemistry and Physics, in that order, and the position tightens considerably in the eight to twelve weeks before the May session. For a common Standard Level subject at a mid-evening slot in term time a match usually takes days. For a Higher Level science specialist allow up to a fortnight. Narrower again is a tutor with experience of one specific internal assessment component, which matters because that component carries around a fifth of the grade.

faqs.question: What should we ask a school along this belt before we enrol?
faqs.answer: Which Higher Level subjects actually ran in the most recent cohort and with how many students, because a subject in a prospectus that did not run is not an option and a Higher Level class of four is a different experience from one of eighteen. Also ask for the DP1 and DP2 internal assessment deadline dates, which differ by a fortnight or more between the Jumeirah corridor and the Al Sufouh cluster, and how the mandatory UAE subjects are organised into separate classes by group.

faqs.question: When is the best time in two Diploma years to spend money on tutoring?
faqs.answer: The spring of DP1, on internal assessment topic screening, which costs a few hundred dirhams and sets the mark ceiling on a component worth around a fifth of a subject grade. After that, a weekly hour from DP1 in the single subject that most threatens the points total. The worst value is twenty sessions in April of DP2, which cost the same as twenty spread through DP1 and arrive after the coursework is submitted and the content window has shut.

faqs.question: Can sessions keep running while we are away for the summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the summer between DP1 and DP2 is the most productive stretch of the two years if you use it. It is the only period with no competing deadlines, which makes it the right time for internal assessment drafting. Agree the time-zone shift once before departure rather than renegotiating weekly, and set a lower frequency than term time rather than an aspirational one. Two sessions a week in July aimed at drafting converts a gap into an advantage.

faqs.question: Is the winter break worth using for anything in the second Diploma year?
faqs.answer: For one or two full timed papers with a proper review, not for new content. The break sits immediately before the mock window at most Dubai schools, so a student who sits a paper in the first week of January has a diagnosis before the mocks rather than after them, and that changes what the whole spring term is spent on. The other thing worth doing is checking whether any internal deadline lands immediately after the break, because that work has to happen during it.

faqs.question: Does a strong KHDA inspection band mean our child will not need help?
faqs.answer: No, and the band is also coarser than it looks. Dubai private schools are inspected annually on a six-band scale and the published report carries the useful detail: secondary phase attainment and progress in the specific subjects, and the commentary on teaching in the secondary phase. A strong overall band built on an excellent primary phase says little about Year 12 chemistry. We do not publish ratings we have not read on the regulator's own site.

faqs.question: Is a premium tutor at AED 600 an hour worth it for Higher Level work?
faqs.answer: For some tasks and not for others. Timed-paper marking, accuracy drilling and command-term work are delivered just as well by a qualified subject tutor in the AED 150 to 300 band. Internal assessment topic screening at Higher Level, and content rebuilding in a genuinely difficult area such as fields or organic chemistry, benefit from somebody who has taught that material to Diploma standard. Buying the top tier for everything is the standard overspend on this side of the city.

faqs.question: Do you work with the schools in Umm Suqeim and Al Safa?
faqs.answer: No, and we would not claim to. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership, contract or endorsement from any school or school group, and we name schools only to describe the local education context. Students we support attend schools across Dubai, which is a different statement from a partnership. Any provider listing a long roster of schools as partners is worth asking what the relationship actually consists of, because in this market the answer is frequently nothing at all.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help finish an internal assessment that is behind schedule?
faqs.answer: Within a boundary we state to the student in the first session. A tutor teaches the content, explains how the criteria distribute marks, demonstrates a complete worked example on an entirely different topic, reads your child's own draft and asks questions about method, evidence and whether the analysis reaches the level claimed. A tutor does not choose the topic, supply the content, write or rewrite a passage, or edit the draft into shape. A malpractice finding falls on the candidate rather than on anyone else.

faqs.question: What is the smallest sensible amount of Diploma support to buy?
faqs.answer: One diagnostic session plus a small screening block at the internal assessment stage, which for most families is three or four hours in total across DP1. If a subject is genuinely misunderstood rather than underperforming, add a bounded block in the autumn of DP2 with a stated number of sessions and an end date. That is considerably less than most agencies propose, and for a student who is broadly coping it is usually what actually changes the outcome.

intro.heading: Why this search is about the clock, not the curriculum
paragraphs: The phrase "IB home tutor in Umm Suqeim" is typed by a parent who has already decided their child needs help. What is still open is logistics. Umm Suqeim 1, 2 and 3 run inland from Jumeirah Beach Road towards Al Wasl Road, with Umm Suqeim Road cutting across towards Al Barsha and Sheikh Zayed Road. Children from these three sub-communities are spread across schools in four directions: Kings' School Dubai and Raffles World Academy inside Umm Suqeim itself, Emirates International School Jumeirah a few minutes east, Jumeirah College and Horizon English School in Al Safa, Dubai College out at Al Sufouh. Each of those schools ends its taught day at a different time, and most of them run clubs afterwards.

That spread is the reason an in-home arrangement is harder here than it looks on a map. A tutor who lives in Al Barsha and takes a 4pm booking in Umm Suqeim 3 is on Umm Suqeim Road at exactly the hour the school traffic is clearing, and the return leg is worse. The family pays for that journey whether it is itemised or buried in the hourly rate. Market figures for in-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai run from AED 180 to AED 500 an hour depending on the tier, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The gap between those two bands is, in practical terms, the car.

IB Gram works the other way round. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, so the pool a family chooses from is defined by subject and level rather than by driving distance. A student taking Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is matched with somebody who teaches that course and knows where its marks are lost. A Visual Arts student is matched with somebody who has supervised a comparative study. Nobody is picked because they live near Sunset Mall.

Stated plainly, because it matters more than any marketing line on this page: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and home visits in Dubai are not a service we sell. Visiting tuition is something we run only in India. What a family in Umm Suqeim books is a live video lesson at an agreed time, with screen sharing, an annotated past paper and a written note afterwards on what was covered and what the student should practise before the next session.

The rest of this page is written around the thing that decides whether tutoring actually happens: the week. It maps the schools this neighbourhood feeds and when a session can realistically begin for each, prices the online and in-home options side by side with the source for every figure, walks the Diploma year backwards from the May examination session, sets out what a tutor may and may not do with an internal assessment, and ends with what happens when no specialist is free for a niche Higher Level option. Dates for the IB itself should always be confirmed with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org, because the IB sets them and revises them.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-umm-suqeim.programmesIntro: Umm Suqeim families meet the IB at three different stages, and a tutor is useful for different reasons at each. Raffles World Academy runs the full continuum inside Umm Suqeim 3; Emirates International School Jumeirah runs it a few minutes east. The notes below describe what each programme assesses and what tutoring does for a student on this particular coast.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations. Learning is organised around transdisciplinary themes and a student-led exhibition in the final year. Reporting is against learner-profile attributes and conceptual understanding rather than subject percentages, which is why PYP parents often cannot tell whether their child is behind. Tutoring at this stage is diagnostic: number fluency, reading stamina, writing structure and the research habits the exhibition assumes a child already has.
programmes.countryNote: A PYP child in Umm Suqeim is often in a household where the primary school day ends earliest of anyone, because younger year groups finish before secondary. That makes the 16:00 GST slot genuinely available here, and it is the only slot that stays free once an older sibling's club schedule is set.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses eight subject groups against four criteria each, marked out of eight and reported on a 1-7 scale after a published grade-boundary conversion. The personal project sits in the final year. Students arriving from a British primary often find the criteria unfamiliar: a technically correct answer can still score poorly against a criterion that asks for analysis rather than recall. Tutoring here is mostly criterion literacy plus the subject content underneath it.
programmes.countryNote: Umm Suqeim has an unusual mix, with MYP students at Raffles World Academy living streets away from Year 10 IGCSE students at Kings' School Dubai. Families compare notes at the same beach and reach contradictory conclusions. A tutor who knows both systems can explain why a 5 in MYP Science is not the same statement as a grade 5 at IGCSE.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the three core components. Each subject is graded 1-7, with up to three bonus points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix. The Diploma is examined in a single session at the end of two years, with internal assessment contributing a published percentage in every subject. The workload is front-loaded onto coursework deadlines that the school sets, not the IB.
programmes.countryNote: DP students in Umm Suqeim 3 frequently stay on site after the taught day for laboratory work or creativity, activity, service commitments. That pushes a realistic weekday session to 17:00 GST or later, and it is the single most common reason a well-intentioned 4pm booking collapses in the second week of term.

programmes.name: The DP core: Extended Essay, TOK and CAS
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is an independent 4,000-word research piece with a named supervisor. Theory of Knowledge is assessed by an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. Creativity, activity, service is not graded but must be completed for the Diploma to be awarded. Together the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge contribute up to three points. Students underestimate the core because it has no weekly lesson attached to most of it.
programmes.countryNote: Core deadlines are set by the school's coordinator, so two Umm Suqeim students in the same cohort year can have internal deadlines weeks apart depending on which school they attend. A tutor working with a student here plans backwards from that school's calendar, not from a generic Diploma timeline.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-umm-suqeim.subjectsIntro: Requests from this part of the coast skew towards the sciences and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, with English A and Economics close behind. The descriptions below say what each course actually assesses and where students on this syllabus tend to lose marks, which is more useful than a list of subject names.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic and calculus-heavy, with proof expected at Higher Level. Marks go missing in the extended response questions where method marks depend on showing an intermediate step. Higher Level adds a Paper 3 investigation that rewards students who can read an unfamiliar problem slowly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-assisted work. The graphical display calculator is assumed, and students lose marks by writing calculator output without the mathematical justification. Higher Level pushes into matrices, graph theory and more demanding statistical inference than most students expect from the "easier" route.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and electricity dominate early teaching; the Higher Level extensions in fields and nuclear physics arrive late and fast. The commonest loss is in multi-step numerical questions where units and significant figures are marked separately from the physics. Data analysis in the internal assessment needs uncertainty treatment done properly.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics carry the Higher Level load. Students who can recite definitions still lose marks on questions asking them to explain a trend using structure and bonding together. Paper 2 extended responses reward a candidate who answers the command term asked rather than the topic recognised.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content is the difficulty, not conceptual depth. Marks are lost in the data-based questions that open Paper 2, where students describe a graph instead of using it as evidence. The internal assessment needs a measurable independent variable, which is where most weak explorations fail before any work is done.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Assessed by Paper 1 unseen analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, the individual oral and, at Higher Level, the HL essay. The individual oral is where preparation pays most, because it requires a global issue argued through two specific extracts the student chooses and must defend.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are marks. A correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram earns credit that prose alone cannot, and an unlabelled axis loses it. Higher Level adds quantitative questions and a longer Paper 3. The three internal assessment commentaries must each use a different article and a different section of the syllabus.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-heavy, with specific frameworks expected by name in the answer. The Paper 1 pre-released case study rewards early familiarity, and students who leave it until revision lose easy marks. Higher Level adds extension topics and a longer response paper that demands evaluation rather than description.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions matter in the examination, and the internal assessment is a developed solution with documented success criteria agreed with a real client. Higher Level adds abstract data structures and a case study released annually. Students who code well often lose marks on the written design and testing documentation.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Assessed across productive and receptive skills with prescribed themes. For non-Arab students in Dubai this frequently runs alongside the KHDA mandatory Arabic requirement, which is a separate thing with its own expectations. Tutoring usually separates the two so a student is not revising one syllabus for the other's assessment.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Three assessed parts: the comparative study, the process portfolio and the exhibition. The written components are where marks are won or lost, not the artwork. Students with strong practical skill routinely underperform because the comparative study is treated as a caption exercise rather than an analytical essay.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case-study specificity decides the grade. An answer naming a place, a date and a number outperforms a general answer on the same concept. The internal assessment is fieldwork-based, which for Dubai students usually means a coastal or urban study, and the methodology section is marked on justification rather than effort.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-umm-suqeim.regionsIntro: Umm Suqeim is three numbered sub-communities plus the neighbourhoods it blends into, and the practical differences between them are about commute and school allocation rather than character. Session timing is set by which school a street feeds and by which road a household is on at 3pm.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim 1
regions.note: Closest to Jumeirah and the beach road, within a few minutes of Emirates International School Jumeirah. Households here often have both an IB continuum student and a younger child at a Jumeirah primary, so two different end-of-day times shape the evening.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim 2
regions.note: The middle band, bordered by Al Wasl Road. Journeys towards Al Sufouh and Dubai College are the longest in the area at pickup time, which is why families here tend to ask for a 17:30 GST slot rather than anything earlier.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim 3
regions.note: Inland towards Umm Suqeim Road, with Kings' School Dubai and Raffles World Academy both close by. Walkable school runs exist here, which means after-school clubs are easier to say yes to and sessions land later in the evening.

regions.name: Al Manara
regions.note: Immediately inland across Al Wasl Road, feeding a similar school set with a slightly easier run towards Sheikh Zayed Road. Families straddle the Umm Suqeim and Al Barsha school options and often hold places at both.

regions.name: Al Safa
regions.note: Home to Jumeirah College and Horizon English School. The 3pm pickup congestion on Al Wasl Road at Al Safa is the specific bottleneck that makes a 16:00 start unrealistic for anyone collecting a child here.

regions.name: Jumeirah 3
regions.note: Directly east along the beach road, sharing much of the same school catchment. Households move between Jumeirah 3 and Umm Suqeim without changing schools, so sibling timetables often stay unchanged after a move.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: West towards Dubai Media City, with Dubai College and Al Sufouh's university cluster. The longest commute of the set from Umm Suqeim 2, and the reason some Diploma students in this area are not home before 17:00.

regions.name: Al Wasl
regions.note: The inland strip tracking Al Wasl Road towards Safa Park. Mixed primary and secondary provision, and a useful comparison point because the same tutoring week here starts around thirty minutes earlier.

regions.name: Pearl Jumeira and La Mer
regions.note: Newer coastal development east of Umm Suqeim 1 with a growing school-age population. Most secondary students here travel inland or east, so evening sessions are preferred over anything before 17:00.

schoolClusters.city: Umm Suqeim and Al Manara
schoolClusters.note: The schools closest to the three sub-communities, covering both the IB continuum and the British route to IGCSE. A household on the same street can have one child on each, which is the practical reason Umm Suqeim parents ask more questions about curriculum comparison than families in single-curriculum neighbourhoods.

schoolClusters.city: Al Safa, Al Wasl and Jumeirah
schoolClusters.note: The inland and eastern options reached across Al Wasl Road. British-curriculum provision dominates, with IGCSE at 16 and a split into A Level or the Diploma afterwards, and one full IB continuum school at Jumeirah 1.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh and Al Barsha
schoolClusters.note: The western cluster, further by car but within the usual Umm Suqeim consideration set. Several of these schools run both IGCSE and the Diploma, which is where the curriculum choice at 16 is actually made for a lot of students on this coast.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-umm-suqeim.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every request from this area. The choice is usually set by how far into the Diploma a student is and whether the problem is a content gap or a coursework deadline.

modes.title: One weekly session, same slot every week
modes.description: A fixed hour in the same evening slot, chosen so it survives the school's club schedule rather than competing with it. The tutor works to the student's own school deadlines and leaves a short written note of what was covered and what to practise. This is where almost every Umm Suqeim family starts, and most stay here for a full term before changing anything.
bullets: Booked in Gulf Standard Time, typically 16:30 to 19:30 on a school night
Same tutor each week so the diagnostic work is not repeated
Written note after each session naming the practice set
Paused rather than cancelled during examination weeks

modes.title: Two sessions a week through an assessment block
modes.description: Used when mocks are close or two Higher Level subjects are both in trouble. One session covers teaching, the second covers timed practice marked against the published criteria. Families on this coast usually place the second session on a Saturday or Sunday morning, because the Dubai weekend is the only time a ninety-minute block exists without competing with a club.
bullets: One teaching session plus one timed-practice session
Weekend slot available on Saturday or Sunday in Gulf Standard Time
Marked against the published assessment criteria, not an invented scale
Agreed as a fixed block of weeks rather than an open-ended commitment

modes.title: Internal assessment and Extended Essay supervision
modes.description: Short, spaced sessions tied to a school deadline instead of a weekly rhythm. The student brings their own work and the tutor reads, questions and gives feedback against the criteria. The writing, the data collection and the decisions stay with the student, which is both the academic-honesty requirement and the only way the feedback is worth anything.
bullets: Scheduled backwards from the school coordinator's deadline
Feedback against criterion letters and their published mark allocations
The student's own work throughout, with the tutor commenting rather than producing
Useful for a research question that has not survived its first supervisor meeting

sections.heading: What a search for an IB home tutor in Umm Suqeim is really asking
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Umm Suqeim, in the way parents here mean it, is one-to-one Diploma or Middle Years support that happens at home on a school night without a commute attached. IB Gram provides exactly that, delivered over live video rather than by car. The hour is booked in Gulf Standard Time, the student sits at the kitchen table, and the tutor is a subject specialist who may be based anywhere. What a family in Umm Suqeim does not get from us is a visiting tutor, because visiting tuition is an India-only service and nothing on this site should suggest otherwise.

It is worth being specific about what that trade actually is. The thing a parent gives up is physical presence: a person in the room who can see a child fidget and respond to it. The thing a parent gains is the pool. Within a twenty-minute drive of Umm Suqeim 3 there is a modest number of people who teach Higher Level Chemistry to the current syllabus and are free at 17:30 on a Tuesday. Remove the driving constraint and the pool widens to everyone who teaches that course and is awake in Gulf Standard Time. For a Standard Level subject with plenty of generalist coverage, that difference is small. For Higher Level sciences, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, or a language B option, it is the whole decision.

The second thing the search is asking, usually unspoken, is whether the money is going to teaching or to logistics. Published Dubai rates make that answerable rather than rhetorical. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500. Unitors publishes online IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and online IB from AED 200. TutorChase lists AED 270 for a specialist. Those are their figures, published on their own pages, and the pattern across them is consistent: the in-home premium is real and it is roughly the cost of a car and a driver's hour.

So the honest answer to the query is a redirection rather than a refusal. Yes to one-to-one. Yes to at home. Yes to a Diploma specialist who knows the command terms and the internal assessment criteria. No to a tutor in your driveway, and the sections below set out what that choice buys in timetable terms, in subject coverage and in money.

sections.heading: The Umm Suqeim school day, dismissal by dismissal
paragraphs: The single most useful piece of planning for a family here is working out the earliest hour at which a session can start and still be any good. That is not the hour school ends. It is the hour after the club, the bus loop, the shower and the snack, and it differs by school rather than by neighbourhood. Umm Suqeim 3 households with a walkable school run can take a club and still be settled by 16:30. An Umm Suqeim 2 household collecting from Al Sufouh at the pickup peak is not realistically starting before 17:30, and a session booked at 16:00 for that family will be cancelled or half-attended within a fortnight.

The table below sets out the schools this area actually feeds, the curriculum each runs, and the earliest slot that has tended to hold for families attached to them. Taught-day end times are given as windows rather than clock times on purpose: schools adjust them by year group and by term, and your child's own timetable is the authority. What does not change much is the ordering. Primary finishes first, the British secondaries next, and the Diploma cohorts last because of laboratory and creativity, activity, service commitments that sit after the timetable.

There is a second variable the table cannot hold, which is the sibling. A household with a Year 4 child and a DP1 child has two end-of-day times, and the tutoring slot has to survive both. In practice that means the younger child's session goes early, around 16:00, and the Diploma session goes after 17:30 with the pickup run in between. Families who try to put both at 17:00 end up moving one of them inside a month. Booking the two at opposite ends of the evening from the start is less elegant and considerably more durable.

Ramadan moves all of this. School hours shorten, the working day compresses, and evening energy shifts to after iftar. Sessions that normally sit at 17:30 move to 21:00 or later for many households, and the practical approach is to agree the Ramadan slot in advance rather than rescheduling week by week. The Dubai winter and spring breaks are the opposite problem: the slot is free all day, which makes them the best weeks in the year to clear an accumulated content gap rather than keep ticking over.

sections.heading: What the travel premium actually buys, priced with sources
paragraphs: Start from the monthly number rather than the hourly one, because that is the figure a household budget actually contains. A single weekly hour with a qualified online subject tutor at the published Dubai band of AED 150 to AED 300 comes to roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions sit at AED 240 to AED 600 for budget provision, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and upwards for specialist examination-year support. The same weekly hour in-home, at the AED 180 to AED 500 band, lands between roughly AED 720 and AED 2,000 a month. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those figures are the market's, not ours, and each is attributed in the table below with the provider who published it. The reason to read them next to each other is that the difference is not a quality difference. Nothing in an in-home rate pays for better subject knowledge; it pays for a journey. On this coast the journey is substantial. A tutor coming from Al Barsha or Al Quoz to Umm Suqeim 3 at school-run hours is looking at twenty to forty-five minutes each way, and the beach road at the weekend is worse than the weekday run. Whether that cost appears as a travel charge or is simply folded into the rate, the family is paying for it.

What a parent can verify for themselves, without taking anybody's word for it, is narrower but more useful than a rate table. Ask for the hourly figure, whether it includes travel, whether it includes VAT, what the minimum session length is, what the cancellation window is, and what happens if the tutor is unwell. Ask whether the person teaching holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free of charge and valid for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. Those six answers separate providers faster than any price comparison, and three of them are the ones that generate the unexpected invoice later.

The honest position on our own pricing is that this page does not publish it. Rates depend on subject, level and how close the examination session is, and a number invented for a landing page would be worse than no number. The free trial lesson exists so a family can see the teaching before any money is discussed, and the consultation sets the rate against the actual subject and level. What is published here is the market, with sources, so a family can tell whether any quote they receive is normal.

sections.heading: Building a Diploma week that survives the whole term
paragraphs: Most tutoring arrangements fail in week three, and they fail for scheduling reasons rather than teaching ones. The pattern is consistent enough to plan around. A family books an ambitious slot in week one when motivation is high, discovers in week two that it clashes with something recurring, moves it in week three, and by week five the sessions are irregular enough that each one starts with recap instead of progress. The fix is unglamorous: pick the slot that is boring and certain rather than the one that is ideal.

A workable Umm Suqeim Diploma week looks like one fixed weekday evening session, one self-directed practice block the student does alone with a named task from the tutor, and nothing on the day before a school deadline. The practice block matters more than parents expect. An hour of teaching produces no grade change on its own; it produces a set of things to practise, and the practice is where the learning lands. A tutor who finishes a session without naming the next practice task has given the student a pleasant hour and no mechanism.

Two Higher Level subjects in trouble at once needs a different shape, and the honest version is that it needs two slots, not one slot doing double duty. Splitting a single hour across Physics and Mathematics produces thirty minutes of each, which is enough to identify a problem and not enough to fix it. Families on this coast who need two subjects usually put one on a weekday evening and one on a Saturday or Sunday morning, because the Dubai weekend is the only place a ninety-minute block exists without competing with a club or a commute.

Finally, plan the stop as deliberately as the start. Sessions should pause during the examination weeks themselves, when the student needs sleep and timed practice rather than new teaching, and they should pause during the long breaks unless a specific gap is being closed. A family that books for a defined block of weeks with a stated purpose gets a better outcome than one paying indefinitely for a maintenance hour nobody has reviewed since October.
bullets: One fixed weekday slot, chosen for certainty rather than ambition
A named practice task after every session, not a general instruction to revise
A second subject gets a second slot, usually at the weekend
No session the evening before a school coursework deadline
A review point every six to eight weeks to decide whether to continue

sections.heading: The Saturday and Sunday weekend, and where a second session goes
paragraphs: The UAE moved to a Monday-to-Friday working week in 2022, and Dubai private schools run the same pattern. That makes Saturday and Sunday the weekend, and it changes tutoring logistics in a way that families newly arrived from the United Kingdom or India consistently get wrong in their first term. A Friday evening session, which would be unthinkable in a British week, is a normal end-of-school-week slot here. A Sunday morning session, which sounds like a weekend intrusion, is actually the night before school.

The practical consequence is that Saturday is the best day in the week for a long session and Sunday morning is the best day for timed practice. Saturday carries no school the following morning, which means a ninety-minute block is tolerable in a way it is not on a Tuesday. Sunday morning sits immediately before the school week, which makes it the right place for a full past paper under timed conditions: the student is fresh, and the feedback arrives while the week ahead is still editable.

Families along this coast also have to reckon with the weekend's own traffic. Jumeirah Beach Road and the Kite Beach stretch are busy on Saturday afternoons in a way they are not on weekday mornings, which is another small argument for online delivery at the weekend specifically. A visiting tutor's Saturday afternoon journey into Umm Suqeim 1 is not quicker than the weekday version, and in the cooler months it is often slower.

One further scheduling note that applies to the whole year rather than the week. Dubai's academic calendar includes a winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break, and the Diploma cohort returns from each one with mocks or coursework deadlines close behind. Those breaks are the highest-value tutoring weeks in the calendar precisely because the daytime is free, and a family that treats them as a pause rather than an opportunity usually spends February trying to recover the ground.

sections.heading: The Diploma two years, counted backwards from the examination room
paragraphs: Nobody in this search results page publishes a calendar, which is odd, because the calendar is the thing that determines whether tutoring arrives in time to matter. The table below counts the Diploma backwards from the examination session rather than forwards from the first lesson. Read that way, a year that feels open in September turns out to have very few free weeks in it, and the coursework deadlines are the constraint rather than the examinations.

Two cautions before the table. First, the IB sets its own session and results dates and revises them, and ibo.org blocks automated checking, so this page publishes no IB date. Confirm every one of them with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly. Second, the internal deadlines in the table are set by the school, not the IB, which is why two Umm Suqeim students in the same cohort at different schools can have internal assessment drafts due weeks apart. Plan against your own school's published calendar.

What the backwards view reveals is where tutoring actually helps. In DP1 the leverage is in subject and level choice and in the internal assessment's early stages, because a weak research question costs more marks than any amount of later polishing can recover. In the first half of DP2 the leverage is in coursework supervision and in closing content gaps while there is still teaching time left. In the final stretch the leverage is almost entirely in timed practice and command-term discipline, and new teaching at that point tends to add confusion rather than marks. A family that starts six weeks out should expect the honest version of that: targeted paper technique, not a syllabus rescue.

For students sitting IGCSE components alongside or before the Diploma, the Cambridge and Pearson calendars are separately published and genuinely checkable. Cambridge runs its international examinations in a June series and a November series, and every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, with Cambridge stating that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable ending on 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results having reached students on 22 January 2026. Always open the live official timetable rather than trusting a restated date.
