sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch in an internal assessment
paragraphs: This boundary is worth setting out in plain words, because it is the one place in Diploma tutoring where getting it wrong harms the student rather than merely wasting money. Internal assessment, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Middle Years personal project are all work that must be the student's own. The IB treats a breach as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the candidate, not on whoever helped. There is at least one operator in this market selling finished internal assessments. That is not a cheaper version of tutoring; it is a different and much more expensive risk.

What a tutor can legitimately do is substantial. A tutor can teach the subject content the task depends on. A tutor can explain what each criterion letter rewards and what its mark allocation is. A tutor can ask the questions a supervisor would ask about a research question, a method or a source. A tutor can read a draft the student has written and say where the argument does not land, where the analysis stops at description, and which criterion is under-served. A tutor can teach referencing properly, and can show a student how to audit their own work against the criteria so they can do it alone next time.

What a tutor must not do is produce the work. Not a paragraph written for the student to insert, not an edit that rewrites rather than comments, not a dataset the student did not collect, not a bibliography the student has not read. The line is whether a reader of the finished piece would be seeing the student's thinking. If a tutor's contribution would need to be declared and cannot be, it has crossed over. Our position is that feedback is given on the student's own work, and the student makes every change themselves.

There is a useful practical test for parents. Ask the tutor what they would do if your child arrived the night before a deadline with nothing written. The right answer is some version of: salvage a structure, teach the criteria, and accept that the mark will be what it will be. A tutor who offers to take the file and sort it out overnight has told you what they are, and the person who carries the consequence of that answer is your child.
bullets: Teaching the content, the criteria and the referencing: legitimate and useful
Questioning a research question or a method the way a supervisor would: legitimate
Commenting on a draft the student wrote: legitimate, and where most of the value sits
Writing, rewriting or supplying any part of the submitted work: never
Supplying data the student did not collect: never

sections.heading: Starting from Umm Suqeim, with the limits stated first
paragraphs: The beginning is a conversation about the subject, the level and the deadline, followed by a free trial lesson with the proposed tutor before any commitment. The trial is a real lesson on a real piece of work rather than a sales call, and the useful question afterwards is not whether your child enjoyed it but whether they can now do something they could not do before it. If the answer is no, the match is wrong and it should be changed rather than persevered with.

The limit worth stating up front is availability. Mathematics, the three sciences, English A and Economics at both levels are covered reliably. Narrower options are not always covered immediately: a Higher Level language B, Visual Arts, Music, Global Politics or a less common ab initio language can take longer to match, and occasionally the honest answer in a given week is that nobody suitable is free at the time a family needs. When that happens we say so rather than placing a generalist and hoping. A Higher Level Physics student taught by a competent biologist loses time they do not have.

Where a UAE-based specialist is not available, the fallback is a specialist elsewhere teaching in Gulf Standard Time, which is the same delivery model with a different person in it. That is disclosed before anything is booked, because a family discovering it afterwards has been misled, and this market contains providers who conceal non-UAE delivery behind a local-looking contact number. The second fallback is a waiting position with a date, which is a worse answer than a match but a better one than a bad match.

Three last practical points for a household in Umm Suqeim 1, 2 or 3. Book the slot that survives the club schedule rather than the one that looks best in September. Expect the first fortnight to be diagnostic, with the tutor finding out what the student actually cannot do rather than teaching from the first page of the syllabus. And set a review date six to eight weeks out, with a specific question attached to it: has the thing we started this for changed? If it has not, something about the arrangement needs to change rather than continue.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the deadline
process.description: A short conversation covering the exact course, whether it is Higher or Standard Level, which school the student attends and what deadline is driving the request. The school matters because its internal coursework calendar, not the IB's, sets the real timetable for the next few months.

process.title: We propose a named specialist and a slot
process.description: A tutor matched to that course and a specific hour in Gulf Standard Time that fits around the school run and the club schedule for your part of Umm Suqeim. If availability for a narrow Higher Level option is limited, you are told that before anything is booked rather than after.

process.title: A free trial lesson on real work
process.description: The trial uses a past paper, a draft or the topic the student is currently stuck on. There is no obligation afterwards. The question that matters is whether the student can do something at the end of the hour that they could not do at the start of it.

process.title: Agree a block, not an open commitment
process.description: Sessions are agreed as a defined block of weeks with a stated purpose: close a content gap, prepare for mocks, get an internal assessment through its draft stage. A block with a purpose can be evaluated. An indefinite weekly hour cannot.

process.title: Review at six to eight weeks
process.description: A short review against the original reason for starting, using school assessment data rather than impressions. Outcomes are continue, change the tutor, change the frequency, or stop. Stopping is a legitimate outcome and we would rather say it than keep invoicing.

whyPoints.title: The slot is chosen around your school, not ours
whyPoints.description: Session times are set against the school your child actually attends and the club schedule attached to it, which is why this page lists earliest workable slots school by school. A slot that survives the term is worth more than a slot that looked convenient in week one.

whyPoints.title: Specialist by subject and level
whyPoints.description: A Higher Level Chemistry student is matched with somebody who teaches Higher Level Chemistry, not with the nearest available science tutor. Removing the driving radius is what makes that possible, and on Higher Level options it is the difference between useful and ornamental.

whyPoints.title: Rates in the open, with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, and none of them is ours. A family can therefore tell whether a quote they receive from anybody is inside the normal Dubai band or outside it.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Feedback is given on the student's own work, and the student makes every change themselves. Nothing is written for them. That is the IB's requirement and it is also the only kind of help that leaves a student able to do the next piece alone.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed before booking
whyPoints.description: If a narrow option has no UAE-based specialist free, you hear that at the start and you hear what the alternative is. Nothing is concealed behind a local-looking telephone number, and a generalist is not placed into a Higher Level seat to fill a gap.

whyPoints.title: A written record after every session
whyPoints.description: Each session ends with a short note of what was covered and the specific practice task set. That note is what makes a six-week review possible, and it is what turns an hour of teaching into something the student does on the other six days.

faqs.question: Does hiring an IB home tutor in Umm Suqeim mean somebody comes to the villa?
faqs.answer: Not with IB Gram. We deliver one-to-one IB tuition to Umm Suqeim households over live video, booked in Gulf Standard Time, and we do not run visiting tuition anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we offer only in India. The phrase is how parents search, so we target it honestly rather than pretending the search means something else. What you get is the at-home part, the one-to-one part and the subject specialist part, without a car journey inside the hour you are paying for.

faqs.question: What time can a weekday Diploma session realistically start for a family in Umm Suqeim 3?
faqs.answer: For most Umm Suqeim 3 households, 16:30 Gulf Standard Time is the earliest slot that holds through a full term, and Diploma students with laboratory or CAS commitments after the taught day are usually better at 17:00 or 17:30. The deciding factor is not when school ends but when the club finishes and the student has eaten. Booking the ideal-looking 16:00 slot is the commonest reason an arrangement collapses in week three, so pick the certain hour rather than the optimistic one.

faqs.question: My child finishes at Kings' School Dubai and has a club afterwards. Does that rule out tutoring?
faqs.answer: No, it just moves the slot. A club finishing late afternoon still leaves a workable 17:00 or 17:30 session on a school night, and the walkable school run that many Umm Suqeim 3 families have means less time lost to traffic than households collecting from Al Sufouh or Al Barsha. The thing to avoid is a session immediately after a club with no gap, because the student arrives tired and the first fifteen minutes are wasted. Twenty minutes of breathing space is worth more than twenty minutes of teaching.

faqs.question: Which IB schools sit inside Umm Suqeim itself?
faqs.answer: Raffles World Academy runs the full IB continuum in Umm Suqeim 3, and Emirates International School - Jumeirah runs the continuum in Umm Suqeim 1. Kings' School Dubai, also in Umm Suqeim 3, is a British-curriculum school with IGCSE at 16. A few minutes inland and east you reach Jumeirah College, Horizon English School and Jumeira Baccalaureate School. These are named as context for families in the area; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them, and current programme details should be checked on each school's own site or the KHDA listing.

faqs.question: How does the Saturday and Sunday weekend change the tutoring week in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The UAE moved to a Monday-to-Friday working week in 2022 and Dubai private schools follow it, so Saturday and Sunday are the weekend. Practically, Saturday is the best day for a long ninety-minute session because no school follows the next morning, and Sunday morning is the best slot for a full timed past paper because the feedback arrives while the school week ahead can still be changed. Families arriving from a British or Indian week often book Friday evenings expecting a weekend slot and get a school night instead.

faqs.question: Is an online lesson genuinely equivalent for a Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: For Higher Level subjects it is usually better, and the reason is the pool rather than the technology. Within driving distance of Umm Suqeim, the number of people teaching Higher Level Chemistry or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches to the current syllabus and free at 17:30 on a weekday is small. Remove the driving constraint and you choose from everyone who teaches that course in Gulf Standard Time. Screen sharing an annotated past paper works at least as well as sitting beside one. What online loses is the physical presence, which matters more for younger students than for Diploma candidates.

faqs.question: What does the Dubai market charge for an in-home IB tutor, and what does online remove?
faqs.answer: Published figures put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour: Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table gives AED 180 to AED 350, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500. Online qualified subject tutors sit at roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing online IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The gap between those bands is travel, not teaching quality. Those are the providers' own published numbers; IB Gram's rate depends on subject, level and proximity to the session, and is set at consultation.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a permit to teach privately in Dubai, and can we check it?
faqs.answer: Yes. Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page is "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", applied for through its app, website and e-services. Tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Can my child's own teacher at an Umm Suqeim school tutor them privately in the evening?
faqs.answer: It is not something to arrange. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat the detail as press-reported and verify against the current policy document. The underlying principle is a conflict of interest between the person teaching a class and the person paid privately by one family in it, and it holds regardless of emirate.

faqs.question: What exactly may a tutor do with my child's internal assessment?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what each criterion letter rewards and what it is worth, question a research question or method the way a supervisor would, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. The student then makes every change themselves. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite rather than comment, provide data the student did not collect, or hand over a bibliography the student has not read. The IB treats produced work as malpractice and the consequence lands on the candidate, so the boundary protects your child rather than us.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do Umm Suqeim Diploma families usually begin with?
faqs.answer: One, in a fixed weekday evening slot, for a defined block of weeks. That covers the great majority of first bookings. A second session is added when mocks are close or when two Higher Level subjects are simultaneously in trouble, and in that case it is a genuine second hour rather than a split one: thirty minutes each of Physics and Mathematics identifies problems without fixing them. Families here typically place the second session on a Saturday or Sunday morning, because the Dubai weekend is where a ninety-minute block exists without competing with a club.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for my child's Higher Level option?
faqs.answer: You are told before anything is booked. Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, English A and Economics are covered reliably at both levels. Narrower options such as a Higher Level language B, Visual Arts, Music or Global Politics can take longer, and sometimes the honest answer in a given week is that nobody suitable is free when you need them. The fallback is a specialist elsewhere teaching in Gulf Standard Time, disclosed up front, or a waiting position with a date. We do not place a generalist into a Higher Level seat to fill the gap.

faqs.question: Do the KHDA mandatory UAE subjects take timetable space my child needs for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: They occupy real curriculum time. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum is licensed, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a Diploma student this is timetable pressure rather than an assessment problem, and it is worth mapping before adding a tutoring hour to an already full week.

faqs.question: How does the free trial lesson work before we commit to a weekly slot?
faqs.answer: The trial is a full lesson with the proposed tutor on real work: a past paper question, a draft, or whatever the student is currently stuck on. There is no obligation afterwards and no card required to book it. The question to ask your child at the end is not whether they liked the tutor but whether they can now do something they could not do an hour earlier. If the answer is no, the match is wrong, and changing it at that point costs nothing but an email.

faqs.question: Should we plan the Diploma year around the May examination session?
faqs.answer: Dubai schools enter the May session, so yes, but the deadlines that actually constrain the year are set by your school rather than by the IB. Internal assessment drafts, Extended Essay submission and mock windows all come from the school's own calendar, which is why two Umm Suqeim students in the same cohort at different schools have different pressure points. Build the plan from your school's published calendar and confirm every IB date with the IB coordinator or on ibo.org, because the IB sets and revises those dates itself.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-umm-suqeim.closingHeading: Start with the hour that will still be there in March
dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-umm-suqeim.closingBody: The decision in front of an Umm Suqeim family is rarely whether to get help. It is which hour of the week can hold a weekly session once the clubs, the pickups and the Al Wasl Road traffic have taken their share. Pick that hour, book a free trial lesson in it with a tutor matched to the exact subject and level, and give the arrangement a stated purpose and a review date six to eight weeks out. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. Tell us the course, the level and the deadline, and we will tell you honestly whether we have the right person free.

intro.heading: The Villanova school run decides when IB tutoring can happen
paragraphs: Villanova sits in the Dubailand belt off Al Qudra Road, a townhouse and villa community whose children are scattered across a wide arc of schools rather than concentrated in one. That single fact shapes everything about tutoring here. A family in Amaranta may send one child to Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City, ten minutes away, and another to Jumeirah English Speaking School in Arabian Ranches, or to GEMS World Academy in Al Barsha, thirty-five minutes away in the wrong direction at 15:30. The bus that drops at the Villanova gate is rarely the quick option.

So the honest starting point for an IB home tutor in Villanova is not a tutor's CV. It is the clock. A Diploma student who gets home at 16:10 can eat, decompress for forty minutes and start a serious session at 17:00. A student who gets home at 17:05 cannot — not well. Push a Maths AA HL session to 17:15 and you are teaching integration by substitution to someone whose working memory is already spent. That is where tutoring money disappears in this community, and it has nothing to do with the tutor's subject knowledge.

An in-home tutor adds a second clock on top of the first. Villanova is not on the way to anywhere for most of Dubai's tutoring workforce. A tutor who finishes a session in Jumeirah at 16:30 is not at your door before 17:20 on a working Wednesday, and if they are, they have usually priced the drive into the hour. Market rates for in-home visits in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for the same qualified tutor teaching online — and the difference is largely diesel and Sheikh Zayed Road.

IB Gram's position on this is simple and stated on every UAE page. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. For Villanova we match the student to the right IB subject specialist and the lesson runs live over video, one-to-one, in a slot that fits the actual bus timetable. The gain is not only the travel hour. It is that the tutor pool stops being 'who will drive to Dubailand' and becomes 'who teaches Chemistry HL and has read the current subject guide'.

This page is written around that: which schools Villanova feeds, what time each one really releases, when a session fits, what the market charges, what the KHDA and MoHRE rules actually say, and what a tutor may and may not touch on an Internal Assessment. Every figure here is attributed. Where a date matters — a Cambridge or Pearson series, a KHDA requirement — the source is named so you can check it rather than take our word.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-villanova.programmesIntro: Villanova households usually cover two or three IB stages at once — a Year 6 child in PYP, a Year 9 in MYP, a Year 12 starting the Diploma. Each needs a different kind of session, and the differences are concrete rather than philosophical.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external exams, so tutoring here is about the skills that make MYP survivable: reading stamina, number fluency without a calculator, and writing that holds a line of argument for more than three sentences. Sessions are shorter — 40 to 45 minutes is usually the ceiling for a Year 4 child after a full day and a bus ride. The useful measure of progress is a unit of inquiry the child can explain to you unprompted.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the PYP years are also when Arabic begins in earnest. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs — combined classes are prohibited. Villanova parents who assume Arabic is optional on an IB track discover otherwise in Year 2, which is why we run Arabic as a separate stream.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP marks against four criteria per subject, A to D, each on a 0-8 scale, and the criteria descriptors are the whole game. A Villanova student losing marks in MYP Sciences is usually losing them in Criterion B or C — planning an investigation and processing data — while revising content they already know. Tutoring that works here reads the task sheet and the criterion wording first, then the content. MYP Year 5 students may also sit eAssessment.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-Diploma step is the one Dubai families underestimate. MYP has no past papers to drill, so a student arriving in DP1 from MYP 5 meets timed written examinations for the first time at sixteen. For Villanova students moving from a local MYP school to a Diploma school in Al Barsha or Arabian Ranches, we usually plan a bridging block over the summer rather than a rescue in November.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, graded out of 45. Internal Assessments carry 20 to 25 per cent of most subject grades and they land in DP1 and early DP2, often in the same six weeks. The Diploma rarely fails on intelligence; it fails on sequencing. Most Villanova DP students need two subjects supported properly rather than six supported lightly.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session; November exists mainly as a resit and southern-hemisphere route. We do not publish IB exam or results dates on this page: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so confirm every IB date with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly. What we can plan around is your school's own internal IA deadlines, which in Dubai schools typically run several weeks ahead of the IB upload dates.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs at least two DP courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. It is offered by a small number of UAE schools and is a genuine option for a student who wants IB subject rigour without six-subject breadth. Tutoring tends to focus on the DP courses carried into the CP and on the personal and professional skills component, where written reflection is assessed against descriptors most students have never been shown.
programmes.countryNote: Because CP provision in Dubai is thin, a Villanova family considering it is usually comparing it against a British A Level route at a nearer school. For MoE equivalency purposes the comparison matters: the British-track requirements are published and specific, the IB equivalency figure is not something we will quote without a moe.gov.ae source. Verify with the Ministry before choosing on that basis.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-villanova.subjectsIntro: Demand from the Dubailand belt clusters in a predictable set of subjects. Below is what each one actually assesses and where Villanova students most often lose marks — not a list of names.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof-and-calculus route. HL Paper 3 is a 60-minute extended-response paper worth 20 per cent of the grade and it is where unprepared HL students lose most. Marks go missing in sequences, binomial proof and the chain rule under time pressure rather than in topics students have never seen.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-weighted and GDC-heavy. Students who choose AI expecting an easier course meet hypothesis testing, chi-squared and regression instead of calculus. Most lost marks are calculator-process marks: the right answer with no visible method, or a GDC output copied without the test name stated.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The syllabus rewards unit discipline and graph interpretation more than memory. Villanova students typically arrive strong on mechanics and weak on fields and circular motion. Paper 2 extended response punishes answers that describe rather than derive, and the data-based question punishes anyone who has not drawn error bars by hand.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics carry the HL grade. The commonest diagnosable failure is curly-arrow convention — students who understand the reaction but draw the arrow from the wrong electron pair lose the mark every time. Paper 1 multiple choice is where SL students shed points they could have kept with timing practice.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A content-dense course where command terms decide the mark. 'Outline', 'explain' and 'discuss' carry different expectations and different mark ceilings. Genetics and the nerve-and-hormone material produce the widest spread in Dubai schools, and HL students often under-practise the statistics in the data-analysis questions.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the fastest grade gain available. A correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram earns marks that prose cannot recover. The IA commentaries — three of them, each on a different unit, each with a strict word limit — are where organised students separate themselves from capable ones.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-based: Ansoff, BCG, break-even, cash-flow forecasts. Students lose marks by applying a tool without reference to the stimulus case. The HL extension and the pre-released case study for Paper 1 reward early, structured reading rather than last-month cramming.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two of the three assessed components are oral or non-literary analysis, which surprises students who expected essays about novels. The Individual Oral needs a global issue and two extracts chosen months in advance; the commonest failure in Dubai cohorts is a global issue too broad to sustain ten minutes of argument.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Separate from, but running alongside, the KHDA-mandated Arabic provision in school. Assessment is text-handling, writing and two oral components. Non-Arab students on ab initio most often lose marks on register — writing a formal letter in the grammar of a text message — rather than on vocabulary breadth.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode, data structures and the internal assessment solution. HL adds abstract data structures and the case study, which changes annually and requires reading well beyond the textbook. Students who code fluently in Python still lose marks writing IB pseudocode conventions, which are examined as written notation.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by an exhibition of three objects with commentary and a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title. TOK is coachable in a way students do not expect: most low marks come from objects that illustrate rather than evidence a knowledge claim. A tutor may question and challenge the reasoning; the writing must be the student's own.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay with a supervisor in school. Support here is process coaching: narrowing a question that is actually answerable, building a source base, and managing the reflection sessions. We do not draft, rewrite or edit an Extended Essay to completion, and no legitimate tutor should.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-villanova.regionsIntro: Tutoring demand in this belt moves with commute, not postcode prestige. These are the neighbouring communities whose families face the same school-run arithmetic, and what differs between them.

regions.name: Villanova
regions.note: Townhouse and villa clusters off Al Qudra Road, including Amaranta, Casa Dora, La Rosa and Tulipa. Young family profile, so PYP and MYP demand outweighs Diploma demand. Internet is fibre throughout, which is why online sessions are practical here in a way they were not a decade ago.

regions.name: Mudon
regions.note: Immediately adjacent and sharing much of the same school intake. Mudon families often run two different bus routes from one household, which pushes sibling sessions into separate slots rather than back-to-back. A common pattern is 17:00 for the younger child and 19:00 for the DP student.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches 3
regions.note: Newer stock, heavy Year 1 to Year 7 population, and the shortest run to Ranches Primary and JESS Arabian Ranches. Diploma-stage families here are mostly commuting towards Al Barsha, which is the slowest afternoon direction in this part of Dubai.

regions.note: Apartment-dense, so study space is at a premium and a quiet room for a video session has to be scheduled as carefully as the lesson. Demand skews towards IGCSE and MYP. Evening slots after 19:30 are more common here than in the villa communities.

regions.name: Motor City and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: The nearest established school cluster, with GEMS Metropole and Victory Heights Primary drawing from this whole belt. Pick-up congestion around Motor City between 15:00 and 16:00 is the single biggest variable in a Dubailand family's afternoon.

Families here report the latest realistic weekday start times in the belt, which makes an online slot at 19:00 or 20:00 genuinely useful rather than a compromise.

regions.note: Closer to Al Khail Road and therefore to the Al Barsha IB schools. The commute advantage shows up as earlier session starts — 16:30 is achievable here where it is not in Villanova — and a correspondingly higher appetite for two sessions a week in DP2.

regions.note: The far end of the belt for most school routes. Serena in particular shares Villanova's school intake almost exactly, so sibling and neighbour referrals move between the two communities and the same tutor often covers both households in adjacent slots.

schoolClusters.city: Dubailand, Motor City and Arabian Ranches
schoolClusters.note: The nearest cluster to Villanova and the one most children in the community travel to. Bus returns from this group typically land between 15:40 and 16:20, which makes a 17:00 session comfortable and a 16:30 session possible for the closest schools.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha and Jumeirah South
schoolClusters.note: Where several of Dubai's full IB continuum schools sit. The afternoon run back to Villanova from this cluster routinely takes 35 to 50 minutes, which is why Diploma students travelling here start sessions an hour later than their neighbours.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-in-villanova.modesIntro: Three formats make sense for a Villanova family, and the right one usually follows the clock rather than the budget. All teaching is delivered live online, one-to-one or in a small group, with no tutor travelling to a UAE address.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, fixed slot
modes.description: The same tutor, the same time each week, booked around the bus return rather than around a tutor's route. This is what most Villanova families use for a single weak subject through DP1 or MYP. A fixed slot matters more here than elsewhere because the alternative — a floating time negotiated weekly — collides with two different school timetables in the same house.

Same tutor each week, so no re-diagnosis every session

modes.title: Intensive block before a deadline
modes.description: A compressed run of sessions aimed at one dated event: a mock week, an IA submission, a Paper 3 that has gone wrong twice. Typically four to ten sessions over three or four weeks, then it stops. For Diploma families this is often better value than a year of weekly tuition, because it attacks a known failure rather than a general worry.

modes.title: Sibling or neighbour pairs
modes.description: Two students at the same level and in the same subject taught together in one session. Common between Villanova and Serena households where children are in the same year group at the same school. It lowers the per-student cost and works well for content teaching; it works poorly for IA supervision, where the work must be individual and the discussion confidential.

sections.heading: What a Villanova parent is actually asking for
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Villanova, in practice, means one-to-one IB teaching that happens at home rather than at a centre, at a time that survives the Dubailand school run. It almost never means a specific preference for a stranger in the living room. When families describe what they want, they describe outcomes: no extra driving, no 20:00 start, the same tutor each week, and someone who knows the Diploma rather than general maths.

That distinction matters because the two things parents are conflating — location of delivery and quality of teaching — pull in opposite directions in this part of Dubai. Restrict yourself to tutors who will drive to Villanova on a weekday afternoon and you have cut the available pool to a handful, then selected within it by geography. Chemistry HL has perhaps a few dozen genuinely strong teachers in the emirate. The chance that one of them is free at 17:00 and willing to drive to Al Qudra Road is not high.

IB Gram resolves it by separating the two. The teaching is one-to-one and live, with a specialist in the subject and level your child is sitting, and it reaches a Villanova desk over video. There is no tutor at the door, in Villanova or anywhere else in the UAE — that is an India-only service — and we would rather say so on the first screen than after a deposit. What you gain is the specialist and the slot. What you give up is a car in the driveway.

The rest of this page assumes you want the comparison made properly rather than asserted. So: the schools and their real release times, the market rate for both formats, the regulatory position on who may teach your child at all, and the boundaries around coursework that no tutor should cross.

sections.heading: The Villanova school run, hour by hour
paragraphs: This is the table nobody writing about tutoring in Dubai bothers to build, and it is the one that decides whether tuition works. Below are the school clusters Villanova children travel to, what the afternoon return looks like, and the earliest session start we would actually recommend rather than the earliest one technically bookable.

Two patterns are worth naming. First, the nearest schools are not always the fastest return, because Motor City and Sports City pick-up congestion between 15:00 and 16:00 can cost twenty minutes on a four-kilometre drive. Second, the Al Barsha IB schools release early but sit on the wrong side of the afternoon traffic, so an on-paper 15:15 finish arrives in Villanova at 16:15 or later.

Treat the final column as a floor rather than a target. A Diploma student can absolutely work at 20:00, and many do, but a 20:00 session that follows a 19:30 dinner is a different lesson from a 17:30 one. Where a family has a genuine choice, we put the harder subject in the earlier slot and leave the later one for review, past-paper marking and IA discussion, which tolerate tiredness better than new abstract content does.

The table also explains a pattern we see in enquiries from this community. Families with a child at a near school ask for weekly tuition and get it easily; families with a child on the Al Barsha run ask for weekly tuition and then cancel twice a term, because the slot they booked was never realistic. Booking an 18:00 session that happens forty times beats booking a 17:00 session that happens twenty-six times, and the second option is what most families accidentally choose. If you are unsure which row you are in, time the journey once on an ordinary Tuesday rather than on a Friday, then add ten minutes.

sections.heading: Where the IB day breaks down for Dubailand families
paragraphs: The failure mode in this belt is not a weak student. It is a Diploma student whose usable study hours are consumed by transit and whose coursework deadlines arrive in clusters. A DP1 student travelling to Al Barsha loses roughly ninety minutes a day to the road. Across a school week that is seven and a half hours — close to a full day of study — and it is taken from exactly the part of the evening when abstract work is still possible.

The second break point is IA bunching. In most Dubai IB schools the Maths, Physics, Chemistry and Economics internal assessments land within a few weeks of each other in DP1 and early DP2, each worth 20 to 25 per cent of its subject grade. A student who has not planned backwards from those internal deadlines spends the period producing four mediocre pieces of coursework instead of two good ones and two adequate ones. Tutoring that only teaches content during that window is solving the wrong problem.

The third is the mandatory UAE subjects, which sit on top of the six Diploma subjects rather than inside them. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a non-Arab student on ab initio Arabic, those periods are real work in a language they do not use at home, and they are frequently the subject nobody is helping with.

What all three have in common is that they are schedule problems wearing the costume of ability problems. A tutor who starts by asking for the school's assessment calendar and the bus timetable will diagnose them in the first session. A tutor who starts by asking what topic the student finds hard will not.

sections.heading: Online to a Villanova desk versus a tutor at the door
paragraphs: Set the two formats side by side on the things that differ, rather than on the things marketing copy usually compares. Cost, travel, the size of the tutor pool, what happens when a session has to move, and what the record of the lesson looks like afterwards. On most of those, the geography of Villanova decides the answer before pedagogy gets a say.

The tutor-pool line is the one worth dwelling on. An in-home search in Dubailand filters by willingness to drive; an online search filters by subject and level. For a mainstream need — Year 7 maths, IGCSE English — both pools contain someone good. For Chemistry HL organic mechanisms, Maths AA HL Paper 3, or an Economics IA commentary on a specific unit, the in-home pool in this belt may contain nobody at all, and the family ends up with a generalist teaching a specialist paper.

The rescheduling line matters more than parents expect. A missed in-home session is a wasted journey and is usually charged; a missed online session can often be moved the same week because there is no travel to re-plan. Over a two-year Diploma, with mock weeks, travel and illness, that difference compounds into several hours of teaching either kept or lost.

There is one column where the in-home format genuinely wins, and it is worth being straight about it. A child under about ten who needs an adult physically present to stay on task, or a student with a specific need that makes screen work difficult, will often do better with a person in the room. That is a real reason to choose the format, and a family in that position should look at the independent in-home market in Dubailand rather than at us. What is not a real reason is the assumption that presence equals attention: a one-to-one online session with a specialist who has read the subject guide beats an hour in the dining room with a generalist who has not.

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor your child in Dubai
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work, not unregulated work. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states the permit 'is granted free of charge for two years'. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service, through the smart app, website or e-services system, with a two-working-day completion time and no listed fee.

Two things follow for a Villanova parent. First, if a tutor tells you a permit costs money or that it is optional, that is a reason to look elsewhere: u.ae is explicit that individuals offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit 'will be subject to fines and penalties' outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published — Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the amounts — so treat any specific figure you are quoted as unverified. Second, a permit is a lawfulness check, not a teaching-quality check. It tells you nothing about whether someone can teach Paper 3.

The institutional layer is separate again. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific licence with initial approval, completion steps and annual renewal. IB Gram does not hold one and does not claim one, and no phrase on this site should be read as KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation or partnership. KHDA regulates Dubai's private schools and is 'responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate'; that is a fact about KHDA, not an endorsement of us.

One more rule is worth knowing even though it sits in Abu Dhabi. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify against the current policy document — but never arrange for your child's own class teacher to tutor them privately on the assumption it is fine.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an IA, EE or TOK essay
paragraphs: This is the line that separates legitimate tutoring from a service that can get a student's Diploma withdrawn, and it is worth stating in plain words because at least one operator ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what a criterion is asking for, question a research question until it is answerable, read a draft and say where the reasoning fails, and show a worked example on a different topic. That is teaching.

A tutor may not choose the topic and hand it over, write or rewrite any part of the text, produce the data, build the processed tables, edit prose to a finished state, or supply a previous student's work as a model. Every one of those is the student passing off another person's work as their own, which is academic misconduct under IB rules and a malpractice trigger for the school. The student's supervisor in school signs declarations about authenticity; a tutor who crosses this line puts the student's entire Diploma at risk, not just one grade.

Practically, what good IA support looks like is unglamorous. The tutor asks what the criteria strands say and makes the student read them aloud. They check that the research question is narrow enough to answer with the equipment and data actually available. They look at the processing and ask why that uncertainty was chosen. They point at a paragraph and say this does not follow from your evidence. The student then goes away and writes. We do not supply or reproduce IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables either; we cite the official source and link out, because reproducing them is a copyright matter.

sections.heading: The exam calendar, counted backwards from a Villanova dining table
paragraphs: Most tutoring starts too late because families plan forwards from today instead of backwards from the deadline. Count backwards instead, and the plan builds itself. For a Villanova household the relevant anchors are the school's own internal coursework deadlines, the board's entry deadlines, and the exam window — in that order of usefulness, because the first one is always the earliest and is the one you can actually miss.

For Cambridge, UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply to your child, whatever a generic article says. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that 'it is essential that you use the correct version of the timetable for your zone', adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask your school which zone it sits in before you print anything.

For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, exams run in May/June and in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are past dates, cited so you can check the pattern. Because Pearson publishes provisional timetables that can be revised, always open the live official timetable rather than trusting a restated date.

For the IB, UAE schools sit the May session. We deliberately publish no IB exam or results date here: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so every IB date on this page would be unverified. Get the May window and the IA upload deadlines from your child's IB coordinator, then work backwards using the pattern below.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: what a Villanova family should file away now
paragraphs: If there is any chance your child applies to a UAE university, Ministry of Education equivalency is the administrative step families discover too late. For the British track, Gulf Today reported the Ministry's clarification: students must pass 'five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3', plus proof of 'one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E' or 'two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade'. Arabic and Islamic education 'are not included among the five required subjects'.

That last clause is where a ranking competitor gets it wrong, publishing a six-subject requirement. Five is the number in the source, and Arabic and Islamic Education sit outside the count — which has a real planning consequence for a Dubai student whose timetable includes both as mandatory school subjects. For the American track, the same clarification sets English proficiency at IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in SAT reading and writing, with at least 450 in SAT Maths.

For the IB there is no equivalency points figure we will print. The article that sources the British and American tracks states no IB threshold, and no figure has been read on moe.gov.ae, so publishing one would be guesswork on a document a family acts on. Check it with the Ministry or your emirate's attestation authority directly. Equivalency is also not something IB Gram performs, submits or guarantees, and no tutoring is required for it — anyone implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a government process.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor who comes to our villa in Villanova?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We deliver IB tuition to Villanova as live one-to-one online lessons, and home visits are a service we offer only in India — no tutor will arrive at a UAE address. Independent in-home tutors do exist in Dubailand and market rates for them run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor teaching online. If you want the in-home format specifically, that is the market to look at. If what you want is a specialist in your child's exact subject and level at a time that suits the school run, online is the better instrument.

faqs.question: What time can an IB session realistically start after the Villanova school run?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which cluster your child travels to. Children at Dubailand and Sustainable City schools are usually home by 15:50 and can start comfortably at 16:30. The Arabian Ranches run supports a 17:00 start. Students travelling to the Al Barsha IB schools face a 35 to 50 minute return against the traffic, so 18:00 is the earliest start we would actually recommend, even though 17:30 can be booked. Our rule of thumb is to put abstract new content — calculus, organic mechanisms — in the earliest slot available, and keep later slots for past papers, marking and IA discussion.

faqs.question: How much does an IB home tutor in Villanova cost per hour?
faqs.answer: In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are advertised at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the range at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. For Villanova specifically, expect the upper half of that spread, because the drive from most of Dubai's tutoring workforce is long. Online, the same qualified tutor sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. Those are market figures from published sources, not IB Gram's prices, which are quoted per student after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Which IB schools do Villanova families usually drive to?
faqs.answer: Villanova children are spread across a wide arc rather than one catchment. The nearest cluster includes Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City, GEMS Metropole in Motor City, Victory Heights Primary, Jebel Ali School in DAMAC Hills, and the Arabian Ranches schools including Jumeirah English Speaking School and Ranches Primary. Full IB continuum provision mostly sits further out in Al Barsha, at schools such as GEMS World Academy Dubai, Dubai International Academy Al Barsha and Nord Anglia International School Dubai. We name these as local context only; no affiliation with any of them is implied or held.

faqs.question: Does live online tuition work for an IB Diploma student in a Villanova villa?
faqs.answer: For Diploma-level work it works well, and the reasons are practical rather than ideological. DP study is already screen-based — shared documents, graphing software, past-paper PDFs — so a shared screen is a natural working surface rather than a compromise. The tutor can annotate the student's own working in real time and both keep the file. What matters is a quiet room, a wired or strong fibre connection, and a parent who is not in the room narrating. Villanova has fibre throughout, which removes the one genuine technical obstacle. Younger children need more adult presence nearby; a sixteen-year-old usually works better without it.

faqs.question: Do private tutors teaching Villanova children need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so distrust any specific amount quoted at you. Note that a permit confirms lawfulness, not teaching quality — it tells you nothing about whether someone can teach Higher Level Physics.

faqs.question: How far can an IB tutor go in helping with a Villanova student's Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help your child get it done; a tutor cannot do it. Legitimate support means teaching the underlying content, explaining what each criterion strand asks for, pressing on a research question until it is answerable with the available data, and giving honest feedback on a draft the student wrote. It does not mean choosing the topic, writing or rewriting text, supplying processed data, editing to a finished state, or handing over a previous student's work as a model. Those are academic misconduct under IB rules and risk the whole Diploma, not one grade. Operators selling completed IAs exist in this market; avoid them.

faqs.question: Our Villanova commute eats the early evening — can lessons run after 7pm?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for families on the Al Barsha run it is often the only honest option. Evening slots at 19:00 and 20:00 are available because there is no travel to plan around on the tutor's side. The thing worth planning is what goes in them. A late session is a poor place to meet a new abstract topic and a good place to mark a past paper, work through a question the student has already attempted, or talk through an IA structure. Where a family has two children, we usually put the younger one at 17:00 and the Diploma student later, rather than fighting for the same early slot.

faqs.question: How many IB sessions a week do Villanova families usually start with?
faqs.answer: One session a week in one subject is the normal starting point, and it is usually the right one. Two subjects at once dilutes attention and makes it hard to tell what is working. The exception is a dated crisis — an IA due in three weeks, a mock that came back badly — where a short intensive block of four to ten sessions over three or four weeks does more than a year of weekly tuition. Families often step up to two sessions a week in DP2 for one subject, then stop entirely once the gap closes. We would rather tell you to stop than keep a slot running out of habit.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Maths AA and Physics for a Villanova student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth checking rather than assuming. The overlap between Maths AA and Physics is real — calculus in kinematics, vectors in fields, uncertainty handling in both — so a tutor strong in both can save a slot and build useful cross-subject links. But depth beats convenience. If the Physics problem is specifically HL fields and the Maths problem is specifically Paper 3 technique, two specialists will usually outperform one competent generalist. We will tell you which case you are in after the trial lesson rather than selling you the tidier arrangement.

faqs.question: Will the tutor follow my child's own school deadlines rather than a fixed syllabus plan?
faqs.answer: That is the plan we build. School internal deadlines are always earlier than the board's, and they are the ones a student can actually miss, so the sequence works backwards from them: the school's IA submission dates, its mock week, its report cycle. A generic syllabus sweep from topic one is the wrong instrument for a student who has an Economics commentary due in two weeks. Send us the school's assessment calendar at the start and the plan is written against it. When the school moves a date, which happens, the plan is revised rather than quietly continued.

faqs.question: Do Villanova session times change during Ramadan and the Dubai school holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families ask for it. Dubai schools shorten the day during Ramadan, which changes both the return time and the point in the day when concentration is available. We move slots later — commonly to post-Iftar — hold them at the new time for the month, and move them back afterwards. Because nothing depends on a tutor's commute, the change is a diary adjustment rather than a renegotiation. This is also a sensible period to shift from new content to consolidation: past papers and review survive a disrupted routine far better than first exposure to an abstract topic does.

faqs.question: What happens if no IB specialist is free for our preferred Villanova slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you, which sounds obvious and is not standard practice in this market. If the subject and level you need is not covered in the window you want, you get the slots that genuinely exist, an honest estimate of when the preferred window might open, or a recommendation to look elsewhere for that specific combination. What we will not do is put a general maths tutor into a Maths AA HL slot and let you discover the mismatch in week four. Niche Higher Level subjects and coursework supervision are where availability is tightest, so ask early rather than in the week before a deadline.

faqs.question: Does my child need Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the IB Diploma in Dubai?
faqs.answer: In a Dubai private school, yes. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and separate classes organised for Arabs and non-Arabs — combined classes are prohibited. Schools must also ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval. For a non-Arab Diploma student these periods are genuine additional work in a language not used at home, and they are frequently the subject nobody is supporting. We run Arabic as its own stream for exactly that reason.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-near-me.tutorsIntro: The specialists below each teach one or two Diploma or IGCSE subjects at a named level. They work from your child's own marked papers and your school's deadlines, and each writes the session note you receive afterwards. Choose a subject and ask for a trial in it.

intro.heading: The evening is the real problem, and it is solvable
paragraphs: A search for an IB home tutor near me in Dubai is almost never really about the home. It is about a window. A Diploma student is home somewhere between 3.15pm in Mirdif and 4.45pm in Jumeirah Village Circle, has eaten by five, has sport on two evenings, and stops absorbing new content somewhere around eight. Inside that window sits homework, three internal deadlines in the same fortnight, and the hour a parent is trying to buy. The arrangement that wins is the one that loses the fewest minutes to logistics.

The second thing underneath the search is the room. Dubai housing runs from a two-bedroom apartment in Discovery Gardens to a five-bedroom villa in Dubai Hills Estate, and the obstacle is different in each. In the apartment it is noise and a shared surface. In the villa it is distance from the adult who was supposed to be keeping half an ear on things. Neither obstacle is solved by a stranger arriving at the door, and both are solved by a closed door and a pair of headphones.

The third is the one families mention last and worry about most. If the parent is at work or in a meeting at 6.30pm, how do they know the hour did anything? A tutor in the room produces a reassuring impression and no evidence. What produces evidence is a written session note within 24 hours naming the syllabus statements covered, the marked questions, the errors by category and the work set for the week. That note is readable on a phone in a car park, which is where it usually gets read.

On that last point this page takes a position. Progress in a Diploma subject does not show weekly and cannot be judged from mood. It shows as a second marked script on the same component scoring differently from the first, six weeks later. So the record we keep is built to make that comparison possible: a baseline script, a topic checklist, dated coursework drafts held separately from the tutor's feedback, and a six-week review that says what moved and what did not.

Then the plain fact about delivery, early rather than buried. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, or anywhere else in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Every lesson described here is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing and a shared annotation surface so the tutor and the student mark up the same past paper together. The honest trade is that nobody rings the doorbell, and in exchange the match is made on subject and level across the whole pool.

That trade also removes the two costs a visit carries quietly. The journey sits inside the hour you pay for, and the settling-in sits inside the minutes your child can still concentrate for. A 60-minute video session contains sixty minutes of teaching, because the marking happened between sessions and the tutor was already on the call when your child sat down.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: What a programme asks of the household changes with age. The notes below are about the practical side — who needs supervising, who needs a closed door, and what a parent can usefully check between sessions at each stage.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The household requirement is a closed door and no supervision: a 17-year-old does not need an adult in the room and will work worse with one. What a parent should check is the session note and the folder, not the lesson itself.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma students sit the May session, and the pressure point is DP1 term two, when internal assessment work in three or four subjects arrives alongside the Extended Essay question deadline. Households with two Diploma students a year apart should expect that fortnight twice and protect two separate slots rather than one shared one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-marked on A to D bands rather than by percentage. At 11 or 12 a session still benefits from an adult within earshot at the start; by 14 it does not. The useful thing a parent can check between sessions is whether the work set actually got done, because at this age the honest answer is often no.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools running MYP into the Diploma set the personal project in Year 11, which absorbs a term of evenings. Families here often find the project, not the subjects, is what needs the standing slot that year — and the project is the student's own work, so what a tutor provides is process coaching and criterion feedback rather than content.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examinations and no percentages, so the only readable evidence is a repeated task. Sessions at this age are shorter, need an adult nearby for the first few minutes, and work best directly after a snack rather than after 6pm. Thirty to forty minutes is usually the ceiling for genuine attention.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all Dubai private schools, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils and combined classes explicitly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and KHDA advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson, which is a reasonable guide for a primary tuition session too.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses alongside a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Scheduling is the awkward part: the career-related units often involve placement or project hours outside school, so the household calendar is fuller than a Diploma student's and the tutoring slot has to be fixed early.
programmes.countryNote: Only a handful of Dubai schools license the Career-related Programme, so there is rarely a neighbour to compare timetables with. The tutorable part is the Diploma courses taken inside it, which are examined exactly as they are in the full Diploma, and the sensible household rule is to protect one slot for the hardest of those.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: For each subject below, what the household actually needs between sessions. Not a syllabus summary — the materials, the practice and the one thing a parent can check on a Thursday without understanding the content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Needs a graphic display calculator the student owns and uses, squared paper, and a quiet surface. Between sessions, check that written working exists on the page rather than answers alone — a parent can verify that without knowing any calculus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The calculator matters more here, because documented screens earn marks. Check that the student can explain what a statistical test concluded in one plain sentence; if the answer is a number with no sentence attached, that is the gap.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: A data booklet, a printer or a tablet that takes annotation, and the school's own practical write-up. Between sessions the checkable thing is whether the student has attempted the question they find hardest rather than the five they find easiest.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Needs the formula booklet and a willingness to write prose. Check for written explanation in the answers: a page of correct numbers with no sentences is the pattern that costs marks on Paper 2, and it is visible at a glance.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Printed data-based questions work better than screen-only, because the graphs need annotating. A parent can check whether the student is reading the question's command term aloud before answering, which sounds trivial and removes a recurring loss.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams have to be drawn by hand, repeatedly, so plain paper and a ruler are the requirement. The checkable signal is whether each diagram in the student's notes is referenced in the paragraph beside it rather than floating unexplained.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Needs the set texts in the school's own editions and a place to read aloud without being overheard, which in a shared apartment is the real constraint. Check that annotations exist in the margins of the text, not on a separate summary sheet.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Short daily exposure beats long weekly sessions, so audio on a commute helps more than an extra hour. Between sessions, check that written tasks follow a named text type rather than being written as generic prose.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The household requirement is storage: a growing case-study bank of named dates, figures and actors. A parent can check its size without knowing the period, and a bank that has not grown in a month is the problem the sessions should be addressing.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Needs printed case-study material and a highlighter, because the marks come from touching the stimulus. The checkable signal is whether the student's answers quote the case rather than describing the theory in the abstract.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Needs nothing material and one hour of uninterrupted quiet, which is scarcer. The exhibition requires objects the student chooses personally, so a household conversation is genuinely useful here in a way it is not for most subjects.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Script practice needs paper and repetition rather than screens. KHDA requires Arabic in all Dubai private schools and sets the content, so between sessions the useful check is whether the school's own material is being used rather than something improvised.

sections.heading: One Dubai evening, four arrangements, counted in minutes
paragraphs: The usable evening for a Dubai secondary student is roughly three hours long, and it is shorter than most families think. Take a Jumeirah Village Circle household: the bus arrives at 4.45pm, food and a shower take to 5.30pm, and by about 8pm a 17-year-old with three Higher Levels is no longer learning anything new. That is 150 usable minutes, into which homework, a sport commitment and any tuition must all fit.

A visiting tutor consumes some of it before teaching anything. The arrival is rarely exactly on the hour because the journey is at the worst time of day; there is a conversation at the door; the student fetches the folder; and a past paper that should have been marked in advance gets read during the lesson because there was no practical way to send it over first. None of this is anyone's fault. It is simply what travel does to a fixed window.

The table below counts one 60-minute lesson four ways, using the arrangements a Dubai family is actually choosing between. The figures are what families report rather than a measured study, so treat them as a model for comparison. What the model shows consistently is that the gap between formats is not the rate; it is how many of the paid minutes are spent teaching.

The fourth row is the one worth looking at twice. A video session where marking happens between lessons gives back the ten or twelve minutes that a tutor in the room spends reading a script in silence while the student watches. Over a term of weekly sessions, that is an extra three or four hours of teaching at no additional cost.

None of this says a tutor in the room is worthless. For a nine-year-old who needs an adult to keep them in the chair, presence is the service. For a Diploma student with a closed door and a deadline, it is an expensive way to lose twenty minutes.

sections.heading: The study-space audit: villa, townhouse, apartment
paragraphs: Whatever the arrangement, the lesson happens in your house, and the room is the variable nobody discusses in advance. Dubai housing produces three distinct problems, and each has a cheap fix that most families arrive at eventually by accident. Doing the audit in the first week rather than the eighth saves a term of sessions that were quietly worse than they needed to be.

In apartments, the problem is noise and surface. A dining table in a two-bedroom flat in Discovery Gardens with a younger sibling two metres away is not a workable study space for Higher Level Physics, and no tutor can fix it from either side of a screen. Headphones with a microphone, a shorter format and a slot chosen when the flat is at its quietest will fix it. A door that closes, where one exists, beats all three.

In villas, the problem is the opposite. A study room on the first floor of a Dubai Hills villa is quiet, private, and completely unobserved, and a student can spend three hours there producing nothing at all. The fix is not surveillance; it is the written record. A session note listing what was set, read on Thursday, tells a parent more than sitting outside the door ever would.

In townhouses the problem is usually glare and furniture. A laptop facing a west window at 5.30pm in a Jumeirah Park study nook is unusable for reading a scanned script, and the student will adapt by not reading it. Turning the desk ninety degrees solves it. The table below lists the obstacle by home type and the fix that is actually cheap.

One Dubai-specific point: air-conditioning noise matters on a video call more than it does in a room. A unit directly above the desk will force a student to raise their voice for an hour, which they will not do, so they go quiet instead. Move the desk, not the microphone.

sections.heading: Two children, one tutor: when sharing works and when it does not
paragraphs: Almost every Dubai family with two secondary children asks about sharing a session, and the question is entirely reasonable. Two children, one hour, one fee. It works in a narrow set of cases and fails in most, and the difference is not age but whether the two students are stuck in the same place.

Sharing works where the content is identical and the gap is identical: twins in the same Standard Level class who both lost marks on the same equilibrium question, or two siblings a year apart who both need Arabic script practice. It works best in short bursts and for skills rather than for diagnosis. Above all it works where neither child minds being watched getting something wrong, which rules out more teenagers than parents expect.

It fails in the ordinary case, which is two children a year or two apart in different subjects or different levels. An hour split between a DP1 student stuck on calculus and a Year 10 student stuck on quadratics is two half-lessons with a gear change in the middle, and the half-lesson is the part that gets remembered. Our strong preference is two consecutive one-to-one hours in the same room with two specialists, which costs more and produces two usable session notes instead of one vague one.

There is a quieter reason to keep them separate. Sibling comparison is corrosive in exactly the subjects where confidence is already the problem, and a shared lesson makes it unavoidable. A student who will attempt a hard question alone with a tutor will not attempt it in front of a younger brother who finds it easy.

sections.heading: What a parent who was not in the room can actually check
paragraphs: This is the part a tutor in the room is assumed to solve and does not. A parent at the door hears a calm voice and concludes the hour went well; a parent at work hears nothing and concludes nothing. Neither has information. What produces information is a short written record designed to be read by somebody who does not know the subject, in about ninety seconds, on a phone.

Ours names five things: the syllabus statements covered, the questions attempted, the marks earned per question against the published mark scheme, the error category behind each loss, and the work set for the week with a number of items rather than a topic. A parent who cannot do Higher Level calculus can still verify whether four named questions were set and whether four named questions were done.

The error category is the line worth learning to read, because it decides what the next month should cost. A log full of accuracy losses on correct methods means a fortnight of drilling units, significant figures and exact forms — no new content, no extra hours. A log full of method losses means a content gap that will reappear in every paper until it is rebuilt, which is more sessions. Treating the second as the first is the most common wasted month in this market.

Then the six-week comparison, which is the only honest measurement. The baseline script from week one is set beside a week-six script on the same component, both marked against the same scheme. If the marks moved, continue. If they did not, the diagnosis, the hours or the tutor needs to change, and you have a page to argue from rather than an impression.
