sections.heading: The Dubai evening, hour by hour
paragraphs: It helps to write the week down once. Most families discover they have fewer usable slots than they assumed, and that the fight over which evening is free has been happening implicitly for months. Three usable evenings a week is normal for a Dubai Diploma student with any sport or CAS commitment, and two is not unusual in DP2.

The earliest workable start is set entirely by the bus. Mirdif, Al Warqa, Al Qusais and Al Nahda households are frequently home by 3.15pm, which makes a 4pm session genuinely available and means Higher Level work can happen while the student is still fresh. Marina, Jumeirah Village Circle, Business Bay and Downtown households are closer to 4.45pm, which pushes the realistic start to 6pm and makes the quality of the slot matter more.

The latest useful finish is about 8pm, and this is the number families argue with and should not. A session that starts at 8.30pm after homework is a session spent on the tutor's energy rather than the student's, and the written note from it will be thinner than the one before. Where the window genuinely does not exist on weekdays, a Saturday or Sunday morning slot is a better answer than a late one, and in the Gulf weekend those mornings are usually free.

Ramadan reshapes the whole pattern for a month. Dubai school days shorten, meals move, and the usable study window for many households shifts to after Iftar. Sessions can move to a post-Iftar slot for the month and move back afterwards; the sensible approach is to agree it a fortnight in advance rather than improvising week by week, because the good late slots fill first.

School events, exam weeks and travel do the rest of the damage. A video slot can be moved or paused without a travel cost attached to the change, which is the quiet administrative advantage of the format: nobody has driven anywhere, so nobody needs compensating for a cancellation at 4pm.

sections.heading: Who is in the room, and what is kept afterwards
paragraphs: Lessons involve a minor, so the household arrangements matter and should be explicit rather than assumed. Our position is simple: the student works in a room where a member of the household can walk in, with the door left on the latch, and a parent may sit in on any session at any time without arranging it in advance. Nobody needs to ask permission to watch a lesson their child is having.

What we do not do is require supervision. A 16 or 17-year-old works worse with an adult listening, and the evidence of the hour belongs in the written note rather than in a parent's memory of overhearing it. For primary and lower-MYP students the balance tips the other way, and an adult within earshot for the first few minutes is sensible while the routine establishes itself.

On data, lead forms and lesson records involve personal information about a child, and the UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection is the relevant framework. What we collect is what the match needs: name, year group, school, subject, level and the marked work you choose to send. What we do not need is a photograph, a full academic history or a copy of a report card, and you should be cautious of any provider that asks for those before a trial lesson.

You can ask what is held and ask for it to be deleted, and the privacy link on this page sets out how. If a session is recorded at all it is because you asked for it, and the recording belongs to the family rather than being retained for marketing. A provider that records lessons by default and cannot tell you where the files live is a provider to avoid.

One further practical point for Dubai households: if a tutor is working from outside the UAE, the data still concerns a child in Dubai, and the right question is who holds it and how it is deleted rather than where the tutor is sitting.

sections.heading: What a visit costs in the Dubai market, and what it buys
paragraphs: The AED figures below are published by the providers named and were read in October 2026. They are market rates, not IB Gram's prices — our own model starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and what a plan costs depends on subject, level and how many sessions a week it genuinely needs. The reason to publish them at all is that three of the six best-ranking pages for this search publish no price, and the two that do quote US dollars.

The in-home premium is the honest part of the comparison. Bestimate's Dubai figures put in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour with independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online. The difference is broadly the cost of a car in evening traffic, and it buys presence in the room rather than more teaching. For some students presence is worth it. For a Diploma student with a closed door, it is not.

Monthly packages in this market cluster at about AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are not the same product and should not be compared on the monthly figure alone. Eight shorter sessions keep weekly contact and eight separate session notes; four long visits concentrate the teaching and spend part of each visit arriving and settling.

Three questions to ask before agreeing to anything, in writing. Does the quoted figure include VAT. Does it include marking and written feedback outside the lesson. And what is the cancellation window, because a slot lost at 4pm to a school event is a cost that somebody absorbs, and with a visiting tutor it is usually you.

A fourth, specific to in-home arrangements: is there a minimum booking. Several in-home providers in this market price in two-hour blocks, which is a long time for a 15-year-old and a reason the published hourly figure can understate what an evening actually costs.

sections.heading: Why the search says home tutor and the lesson happens on video
paragraphs: Worth stating without hedging. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, and visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Nobody will arrive at a Dubai address. Every lesson on this page is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing and a shared annotation surface so a scanned past paper can be marked up by tutor and student at the same moment.

The phrase in the URL is the phrase parents search, and it describes a real need: a lesson that happens in your house, around your evening, without a journey for the student. Video does that. What it does not do is put an adult physically in the room, and for a few students — younger ones, or those who genuinely will not sit down without a person present — that is the service they need, and this is not it.

For everybody else the trade is favourable. Matching happens on subject and level across the whole pool rather than inside a twenty-minute radius, which matters most for the combinations that are tight: Higher Level Chemistry and Physics in the early-evening Gulf window, Higher Level Computer Science, the less common Language B options. In those subjects the nearest available tutor and the right tutor are rarely the same person.

The second gain is the one this page has been counting all along. The journey is not inside the hour, the settling is not inside the hour, and the marking happened between lessons. A 60-minute session contains sixty minutes, and a Dubai evening that only has 150 usable minutes in it notices the difference immediately.

The honest limitation is physical work. A bench practical or an arts exhibition happens at school and belongs to the school. What a video session does with those components is the design, the data analysis and the write-up against the published criteria, which is where most of their available marks sit in any case.

sections.heading: Coursework at the kitchen table, and the line that does not move
paragraphs: Internal assessment work is the part of the Diploma that happens in your house rather than at school, which makes it the part where household help gets complicated. Parents proofread. Older siblings suggest a better opening sentence. A tutor, asked at 10pm on a Sunday, offers to tidy a paragraph. Every one of those is understandable and every one of them transfers a little authorship away from the candidate.

The line itself is not vague once written down. A tutor may ask whether a research question is answerable with the data available, name the criterion a section is failing, and check that feedback was understood. A tutor may not supply the question, write the method, rewrite sentences or proofread a draft to completion. IB Gram does not write, complete or supply internal assessments, Extended Essays, Theory of Knowledge essays or any other assessed work, at any price.

What makes the line defensible in a household is a filing habit rather than a policy. Dated drafts saved in the student's own folder; every piece of tutor feedback kept as a separate document, written by criterion letter; one round of substantive comment per agreed stage. If a Dubai Diploma coordinator asks what outside support was used, that folder answers in the student's favour, and under IB academic-honesty rules the consequence of the alternative falls on the candidate rather than on anyone else.

Confirm the current criterion weightings, word limits and draft policy with your child's subject guide and Diploma coordinator, because they are revised between cohorts and the school holds the authoritative version. We do not publish or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson subject guides, past papers or mark schemes; the school holds the licence for those and is the right route to them.
One practical household rule covers most of it: the student types, always. If anybody else's hands are on the keyboard, something has gone wrong, whatever the intention was.

process.title: Describe the evening, not just the subject
process.description: Tell us when your child is actually home, which evenings are already committed, and where in the house the lesson would happen. Those three facts shape the slot more than the subject does, and getting them right first time avoids a term of sessions quietly scheduled at the wrong hour.

process.title: Send one marked script
process.description: A mock paper, a unit test, a returned draft with the teacher's comments. One marked page lets the specialist arrive at the trial with a hypothesis rather than an introduction, and it is what makes the written diagnosis afterwards worth reading.

process.title: Do the five-minute room check
process.description: Before the trial, sit where your child will sit. Can a door close, is there glare on the screen after 5pm, is the air-conditioning unit directly overhead, are headphones available. Four questions, five minutes, and it removes most of the reasons a good session underperforms.

process.title: Free trial lesson, with a written diagnosis
process.description: Sixty minutes with the matched specialist, no charge and no card details taken. The student attempts a timed question, the tutor marks it against the published scheme, and you receive a note naming the secure topics, the gaps and what the first three sessions would target. Yours whether you continue or not.

process.title: Fix the slot, then read the notes
process.description: Agree the weekly hour and the week-six review date in the same message. A session note reaches you within 24 hours of each lesson, written to be read in ninety seconds by somebody who does not know the subject. At week six we compare two scripts and say plainly what moved.

whyPoints.title: Evidence for the parent who was out
whyPoints.description: A written note after every session naming statements covered, questions attempted, marks earned and work set, plus a six-week comparison of two marked scripts. Readable in ninety seconds on a phone, without any subject knowledge.

whyPoints.title: The hour is an hour
whyPoints.description: No journey, no arrival, no settling, and marking done between lessons rather than in front of the student. In an evening with roughly 150 usable minutes in it, that recovers ten to twenty of them every single week.

whyPoints.title: Siblings taught separately
whyPoints.description: Two consecutive one-to-one hours in the same room beat one shared hour almost every time, because two children are rarely stuck in the same place. You get two specialists and two usable session notes instead of one split lesson.

whyPoints.title: Slots that move without a penalty
whyPoints.description: School events, exam weeks, travel and Ramadan all reshape a Dubai evening. Because nobody has driven anywhere, a session can move or pause without a travel cost attached to the change, which is the quiet administrative advantage of the format.

whyPoints.title: Clear about data and about the room
whyPoints.description: We collect what the match needs and nothing more, under the UAE's personal data protection framework. A parent may sit in on any lesson without arranging it first, the door is not locked, and recordings happen only if you ask for them.

whyPoints.title: No claim we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No regulator approval, no school partnership, no star rating, no promise about a final grade, and no statistic without its source. Every AED figure on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was read.

faqs.question: What does an IB home tutor near me in Dubai cost once travel is counted?
faqs.answer: Published figures read in October 2026 put in-home one-to-one in Dubai at roughly AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The gap is broadly the cost of a car in evening traffic. The cost that does not appear on the invoice is the ten to fifteen minutes of arrival and settling inside a 60-minute visit. Ask whether there is a minimum booking, because several in-home providers price in two-hour blocks.

faqs.question: How much of a school night does a visiting tutor actually use in Dubai?
faqs.answer: More than the hour on the invoice. A Dubai secondary student has roughly 150 usable evening minutes between getting home and losing concentration. A visit typically takes ten to fifteen of those on arrival and settling, and another ten if a past paper is read during the lesson rather than marked beforehand. That leaves about 35 to 40 minutes of teaching. A video session with marking done between lessons keeps closer to the full sixty, which over a term is several extra hours.

faqs.question: Can two siblings in one Dubai villa share a tutoring slot?
faqs.answer: Only when they are stuck in the same place: twins in the same class who both lost marks on the same question, or two children both needing Arabic script practice. In the ordinary case of siblings a year or two apart, a shared hour becomes two half-lessons with a gear change in the middle, and sibling comparison does real damage in exactly the subjects where confidence is already the issue. Two consecutive one-to-one hours in the same room is the better arrangement and produces two usable session notes.

faqs.question: What does a usable study space look like in a Dubai apartment?
faqs.answer: A surface, a door that closes if one exists, headphones with a microphone, and a screen that is not facing a west-facing window at 5.30pm. In a two-bedroom flat with a younger sibling nearby, headphones do most of the work, because the real failure is that the student stops speaking aloud and a lesson where nobody speaks is not a lesson. A 45-minute format at the quietest hour of the household's day beats a 60-minute one at the noisiest.

faqs.question: Does an online lesson need a separate room, or is the dining table enough?
faqs.answer: The dining table is enough for most students, with two conditions. The student must be willing to talk out loud, which means headphones if anyone else is within earshot, and the surface must be clear enough to write on, because working has to be written down rather than done mentally. A separate room helps most for subjects that involve reading aloud, such as English A Paper 1 practice or Language B orals, where being overheard is the thing that stops a teenager trying.

faqs.question: Who should be in the room while a Dubai student has a live lesson?
faqs.answer: Nobody, for a Diploma student, though a parent may sit in on any session at any time without arranging it in advance and the door should not be locked. A 16 or 17-year-old works worse with an adult listening. For primary and lower-MYP students, an adult within earshot for the first few minutes helps while a routine establishes itself. The evidence of the hour belongs in the written session note, not in what a parent happened to overhear from the hallway.

faqs.question: What is a reasonable evening slot for a Diploma student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Start from when your child is physically home. Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais households are often home by 3.15pm, so 4pm works and the student is still fresh. Marina, Jumeirah Village Circle and Business Bay households are closer to 4.45pm, which makes 6pm or 6.30pm the realistic slot. Finish by about 8pm. Where no weekday window genuinely exists, a weekend morning is a better answer than a late session that runs on the tutor's energy rather than the student's.

faqs.question: How do we know the hour was used well if we were not listening?
faqs.answer: Read the session note, which should be written for somebody who does not know the subject. It should name the syllabus statements covered, the questions attempted, the marks earned per question against the published scheme, the error category behind each loss, and the work set as a numbered list. You can verify the last line without any subject knowledge at all: four named questions set, four named questions done. At week six, a comparison of two marked scripts on the same component is the actual measurement.

faqs.question: Does a Dubai household need to provide anything beyond a laptop?
faqs.answer: Headphones with a microphone, a clear surface, and whatever the subject needs physically: a graphic display calculator the student owns for either maths route, the school's own data or formula booklet for the sciences, plain paper and a ruler for Economics diagrams, and the school's editions of the set texts for English A. A printer helps for Biology data questions, which need annotating by hand, though a tablet that takes a stylus does the same job.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our villa in Dubai Hills Estate?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing and a shared annotation surface. For a villa household the practical upside is real: the journey out to Dubai Hills is one of the longer ones in the city at 5pm, and that journey is otherwise sitting inside both the hourly rate and the usable evening.

faqs.question: How does a tutor handle a chemistry diagram without being in the room?
faqs.answer: On a shared annotation surface, which both people can draw on at the same time. Mechanisms get drawn step by step with the student adding the next arrow rather than watching one appear; the tutor can roll back a step and ask what changed. For the student's own practical write-up, the useful work is the method, the data treatment and the evaluation against the published criteria, and all three are easier to do on a shared screen than leaning over one page.

faqs.question: What happens to a paid slot if our child has a school event?
faqs.answer: It moves, and because nobody has driven anywhere there is no travel cost attached to the change. Agree the notice period in writing at the start so there is nothing to argue about in week nine. This is one of the more practical differences between formats: a visiting tutor cancelled at 4pm has already lost the evening and usually charges for it, which is why in-home cancellation terms in this market tend to be stricter.

faqs.question: Can lessons move later during Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they should. Dubai school days shorten during Ramadan, meals move, and for many households the usable study window shifts to after Iftar. Sessions can run post-Iftar for the month and move back afterwards. Agree the change a fortnight ahead rather than week by week, because the good late slots fill first across the whole Gulf. For a DP2 student this often lands close to the final revision block, so it is worth planning the month rather than improvising it.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week fit around a Dubai school day?
faqs.answer: Honestly, fewer than most plans assume. Three usable evenings a week is normal for a Diploma student with any sport or CAS commitment, and two is common in DP2. One subject at one session a week, done properly with work set and done, beats three subjects at one rushed session each. If more than two subjects genuinely need support, the realistic answer is a weekend morning slot rather than a fourth weekday evening after 8pm.

faqs.question: What does the session record show a parent who was out at work?
faqs.answer: Five lines, all checkable. The syllabus statements covered. The questions attempted and the marks earned against the published scheme. The error category behind each loss, which is the line that tells you whether the next month needs two sessions of drilling or six of rebuilding. The work set, as a numbered list. And at weeks six, twelve and eighteen, a comparison with the baseline script. It is written to be read in ninety seconds on a phone, because that is where it gets read.

faqs.question: What if no specialist is free for our child's subject and level?
faqs.answer: We tell you and give a date rather than filling the slot. Higher Level Chemistry and Physics in the early-evening Gulf Standard Time window are the tightest, along with Higher Level Computer Science and the less common Language B options. A fortnight of waiting costs less than six weeks with somebody meeting the syllabus for the first time alongside your child. We will also say what is worth working on unsupervised in the meantime without consolidating the same errors.

dubai/ib-home-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Start with the evening and one marked paper
dubai/ib-home-tutor-near-me.closingBody: If you have been looking for an IB home tutor near me in Dubai, two pieces of information get you most of the way. The first is when your child is actually home and which evenings are already gone. The second is the last marked script they brought back from school. Send both, book the free trial lesson, and read the written diagnosis that comes out of it. No card details are taken, the note is yours either way, and the room check in this page's process takes five minutes and prevents most of the problems a good tutor cannot fix.

dubai/ib-home-tutors.tutorsIntro: Each profile below states the subject and level taught, because that is what the evidence will be read against. A tutor who has marked Paper 2 extended responses in that subject can tell you which band a script sits in; a generalist can tell you it looks good.

intro.heading: The question a Dubai parent cannot usually answer
paragraphs: Ask a parent four months into a tutoring arrangement what has improved and the answer is almost always about feeling rather than evidence. The pupil seems more confident. The tutor is lovely and never cancels. Homework gets done without an argument. All of that is worth something, and none of it is a mark. The Diploma is scored out of 45 by people who have never met your child, and the only signals that predict what they will award are the ones written on marked work.

This is a solvable problem, and solving it does not require trusting anybody. A tutoring arrangement that is working produces specific artefacts on a predictable schedule: a diagnosis naming the fault in week one, session notes naming the component worked on, an internal assessment draft that moves up against named criteria, and a piece of school-marked work in week six or eight that shows a different pattern of lost marks from the one in week one. If those artefacts are absent after two months, the arrangement is not working, whatever the atmosphere in the room.

The reason this page exists under a home tutors search is that an in-home arrangement makes the evidence harder to collect, not easier. A tutor at a kitchen table for ninety minutes leaves behind whatever is on the paper and a verbal summary at the door. There is no record of which criterion was addressed, no file of worked solutions to revisit before the mock, and frequently no written diagnosis at all, because the conversation substituted for one.

Teaching for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE. Visiting is a service offered only in India. A side effect of the online model is that the evidence is automatic: the shared whiteboard retains every worked solution, annotated scripts exist as files rather than as paper in a bag, and session notes are written because the format invites writing them. The audit trail is not a feature bolted on, it is a by-product.

What follows is the full instrumentation, in order. How to read a marked paper for the fault signature. What the first eight weeks should produce, week by week. How to use the internal assessment criteria as a progress measure rather than a grade. What grade movement is realistic and over what period. And a plain account of what cannot be evidenced, because the fastest way to spot a provider worth avoiding is the confidence of their claims about outcomes. None of this requires a parent to understand Higher Level Chemistry. It requires knowing which document to ask for, and in what order, and that is the whole content of this page.

Session notes name the paper and the criterion, not the topic
Internal assessment progress is measured against criterion descriptors
The next piece of school-marked work is the test, not the tutor's opinion
Four-week reviews state what has not improved as well as what has
Any provider promising a grade is promising something unmeasurable

dubai/ib-home-tutors.programmesIntro: Each programme produces a different kind of evidence, which is why a parent who knows how to read a Diploma mark scheme can still be baffled by a Middle Years report. The notes below explain what to look at in each.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Portfolio and inquiry evidence rather than papers, which is why a parent often cannot tell whether a Year 5 pupil is behind. The measurable things at this stage are mechanical: reading fluency timed, number facts recalled without a calculator, a paragraph written in ten minutes. Those are the only honest progress instruments available, and they move visibly within a few weeks of consistent practice.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP pupils also carry the mandatory UAE subjects, which KHDA requires in every private school regardless of the licensed curriculum. Progress in Arabic as an additional language is frequently invisible on a school report because it is reported separately from the main curriculum, and parents discover a problem only when the Middle Years grades arrive.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The most readable evidence in the continuum, and the most ignored. Every assessment is marked against criteria out of 8, and the criterion descriptors state exactly what a 5 does that a 3 does not. A parent who reads the descriptor for the criterion their child scored lowest on has a precise target. Most do not, because the report shows a number and no descriptor.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools that run MYP to Year 9 and then IGCSE for Years 10 and 11 produce a documented discontinuity in the evidence: criterion marks stop and percentage grades start. Families should expect a visible dip in the first IGCSE term that reflects a change of measurement rather than a change in the pupil.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two independent evidence streams run in parallel. Internal assessment is marked against published criteria, finished months before the exams and effectively banked. Examined components are predicted from mocks and class tests. A pupil can be improving sharply on one stream and flat on the other, and a single predicted grade hides that completely, which is why the underlying marked work matters more than the prediction.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma candidates sit the May session, so the mock window typically falls in the winter term and is the most useful diagnostic of the two years. Confirm session dates, upload deadlines and results timing with your school's Diploma coordinator or the IB itself, since those are set by the IB and revised.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Evidence comes from the DP courses, which are marked identically to any other Diploma course, plus the reflective project and the career-related study. The reflective project is the component parents can most usefully audit, because it has published assessment criteria and a draft history, and progress between drafts is visible without any subject expertise.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools license the Career-related Programme, so there is rarely a peer group against which to calibrate. That makes the published criteria the only available benchmark, and it makes an external reader of a draft more valuable here than in the Diploma, where cohort comparison does some of the work.

dubai/ib-home-tutors.subjectsIntro: The fault signature differs by subject: the same grade of 4 means a different thing in Chemistry than in English. Each entry names what to look for on a marked script in that subject.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Read the Paper 1 losses first. Scattered single marks across topics means content gaps. Clustered losses on questions with stated conditions means the pupil is reading stems too fast. On Paper 2, check whether equations carry state symbols and whether organic mechanisms show arrows originating from a lone pair or a bond.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Look at questions where the final number is right and the mark is not. That signature is a missing causal chain in an explain question, and it is the single commonest loss in this subject. On Paper 3, check whether uncertainties were handled at all, because that section is rarely taught and rarely attempted properly.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Compare answer length against the command term. A discuss-length answer to an outline question is a timing fault disguised as diligence, and it is visible on any script in seconds. On data-based questions, check whether specific values from the figure appear in the answer or whether the pupil described a trend in words only.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Separate Paper 1 from Paper 2 losses before anything else. Paper 1 failure with Paper 2 competence is calculator dependence, which is a four-week drill. Equal failure across both is a genuine content gap. On Paper 3, check whether the pupil attempted the generalisation at the end or stopped at the worked cases.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Check the last line of each answer. Marks in this course sit in the interpretation of a result in the context given, and candidates who stop at a correct number lose them consistently. Regression and chi-squared questions are the clearest diagnostic, because the output is easy and the interpretation is where the marks are.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Audit the diagrams as a separate exercise from the prose. Unlabelled axes, unlabelled curves and diagrams never referenced in the text are three distinct faults with three distinct fixes. On the internal assessment portfolio, check that the three commentaries cover different syllabus sections and that each article falls inside the permitted age window.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: On Paper 1, count how many sentences explain the effect of a choice on a reader rather than restating content. On Paper 2, check whether each paragraph has a comparative spine or whether the essay analyses one text and then the other. Both are structural faults, visible without reading the texts.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Count the named studies and check whether each carries a method, a finding and a limitation. A script asserting theory without evidence has a revision-method fault rather than a writing fault. In essays, look for evaluation woven into the argument instead of parked in a final paragraph.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Test each case study for a place name, a date, a figure and a consequence. Scripts that score poorly almost always fail that four-part test. For the fieldwork internal assessment, the diagnostic is whether the question can be answered with data the pupil can actually collect in the time available.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Progress is measurable between drafts: count the knowledge claims that are stated and then tested against a counterclaim. A draft that describes the objects or paraphrases the prescribed title has not started yet. The thinking and the writing remain the candidate's own; what changes between drafts is the quality of the questions they have been asked.

dubai/ib-home-tutors.regionsIntro: What is available to audit varies by school, and school varies by where a family lives. These notes describe what parents in each cluster typically can and cannot see in the paperwork.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Meadows
regions.note: Long-established Diploma cohorts with detailed internal mark tracking, so school-side evidence here is usually good. The gap is criterion-level feedback on coursework drafts, which large classes cannot supply at the frequency a borderline candidate needs.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Tecom
regions.note: Continuum schools report criterion marks consistently from Middle Years upward, which gives parents an unusually readable record. The common fault is that nobody translates the descriptors, so a 4 looks like a grade rather than a target.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Newer Diploma cohorts with less historical mark data to calibrate against, so a predicted grade here rests on fewer data points. External evidence from marked papers matters more in this cluster than in schools with a decade of cohort history.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Households frequently run one child on A Level and another on the Diploma, producing two incompatible reporting systems on the same kitchen table. Parents here benefit most from a single written progress format applied to both.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Strong reporting cultures in the Indian and British curriculum schools that dominate here, with frequent testing. Diploma families in this cluster often have excellent test data and no criterion-level coursework feedback at all.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Pupils travel out to school, which means parents rarely meet subject teachers informally and depend entirely on formal reporting cycles. A fortnightly written note from a tutor fills a real information gap in this cluster.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Mudon
regions.note: Heavy co-curricular and CAS loads make the timing of evidence as important as its content. A drafting deadline colliding with a fixture week shows up as a sudden drop in draft quality that has nothing to do with understanding.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: DP2 families here are usually assembling evidence for university applications as well as for school, so the predicted grade carries extra weight. That makes the gap between internal assessment marks and examined performance worth auditing early.

schoolClusters.city: Schools with mature Diploma mark tracking
schoolClusters.note: Several years of cohort data behind each predicted grade, and detailed internal assessment records. Families from these schools usually need external criterion-level feedback on drafts rather than more testing.

schoolClusters.note: Fewer historical data points, so predicted grades rest on thinner evidence and shift more between reporting cycles. External marked-paper evidence does more work for these families.

schoolClusters.note: Pupils move from criterion marking to percentage grades, or from IGCSE to the Diploma, and the reported dip often reflects the change of instrument rather than the pupil.

dubai/ib-home-tutors.modesIntro: Each booking shape produces a different evidence trail, and the trail is worth choosing deliberately. A parent who cannot audit an arrangement cannot judge it.

modes.title: Weekly slot with a written record
modes.description: A fixed hour, the same specialist, and a short written note after each session naming the component addressed and what the pupil could not do at the start. Over eight weeks that file becomes a diagnostic history, which is the only thing that lets a four-week review be a judgement rather than an opinion.

Worked solutions retained from the shared whiteboard
Four-week review against the next marked school assessment
An explicit option to change the match or stop

modes.title: Draft review cycle
modes.description: A booked sequence tied to a coursework deadline, where the measurable artefact is the draft itself read against its published criteria. Progress is visible without anybody's opinion: a draft that moves from the middle band to the upper band on a named criterion has moved, and a draft that has not has not.
bullets: Feedback mapped to criterion descriptors by letter
Comments on the candidate's own writing only
No text supplied and no section rewritten for the candidate
Draft history kept so movement between versions is visible

modes.title: Post-mock diagnostic block
modes.description: Three to six sessions immediately after the mock window, while the script is fresh and the lost marks are still mapped. The mock paper is the instrument; the block exists to convert it into a list of faults in priority order and then clear the top two.

Produces a written fault list in priority order
Ends when the top faults are cleared, not on a schedule

sections.heading: What counts as evidence that IB home tutors are working
paragraphs: Four things, and nothing else. A written diagnosis produced before any teaching, naming the specific fault. A record per session naming the component and the criterion addressed. Movement on a coursework draft measured against published criterion descriptors. And a change in the pattern of lost marks on the next piece of work marked by the school rather than by the tutor.

Notice what is not on that list. Confidence is not evidence; a pupil can feel considerably better about a subject they still cannot pass. Attendance is not evidence. Homework completion is not evidence, because completing work consolidates a method that may itself be the fault. The tutor's own assessment of progress is the weakest signal available, for the ordinary reason that they are not a neutral party and their mark scheme is not the one that counts.

The reason the school's marking matters so much is independence. A tutor marking their own pupil's practice paper has every incentive, including entirely unconscious ones, to read generously. The school's marked assessment is produced by someone with no stake in the tutoring arrangement, against the same mark scheme an examiner will use. If the pattern of lost marks on that script has changed between week one and week eight, something real happened.

This is also the test to apply before booking anybody. Ask a prospective provider what artefact you will hold after four weeks and what instrument the review will use. A provider who answers with a progress report they write themselves has described a marketing document. A provider who answers with your child's own school-marked work has described a measurement.
bullets: A written diagnosis before teaching, naming the specific fault
Session records naming the component and criterion, not the topic
Draft movement against published criterion descriptors
A changed pattern of lost marks on school-marked work

sections.heading: Reading a marked paper for the fault signature
paragraphs: A marked script contains more information than a report ever will, and most of it is in where the marks were lost rather than how many. Four fault signatures cover the great majority of Diploma underperformance, and they are distinguishable on a single script in about ten minutes by someone who knows the specification.

Content gaps produce scattered losses that follow the syllabus: whole questions on one topic abandoned, adjacent topics answered well. The fix is teaching, it takes weeks, and it is the only one of the four that genuinely justifies a sustained weekly slot. This is the fault families assume they have, and it is the least common of the four in Dubai cohorts.

Command-term faults produce the opposite pattern: answers present, often long, scoring at the bottom of the band. The pupil knew the content and answered a different question from the one asked. Convention faults are narrower still, and they are maddening because the thinking was right: a missing state symbol, an unlabelled axis, an arrow drawn from an atom instead of a lone pair, a number given without units.

Timing faults are the easiest to see and the most often misread as weakness. The script is strong for the first two thirds and then collapses, or the final question is blank. Nothing is wrong with the pupil's understanding of that topic. They spent eleven minutes on a six-mark question earlier, usually because a command term invited them to write an essay. Each signature has a different repair time, and a tutor who cannot name which one your child has is guessing.

table.caption: FOUR FAULT SIGNATURES ON A MARKED DIPLOMA SCRIPT
columns: How long before it shows in marked work
rows: Whole topics abandoned, neighbouring topics answered well
Sequenced teaching of the missing syllabus content
Long answers scoring at the bottom of the band
Explicit command-term hierarchy drilled per subject
Correct reasoning, marks withheld on presentation rules
A checklist applied to twenty past answers
Strong opening, collapse or blanks at the end
Two patterns present at once, usually timing plus command term
Clear the cheaper fault first and re-measure

sections.heading: The first eight weeks, and the artefact each one produces
paragraphs: A schedule a parent can hold a provider to is more useful than a promise. The following is what the first eight weeks of a single-subject arrangement should produce, and the right response to a missing artefact is a question rather than patience.

Weeks one and two are diagnosis and the first repair. No teaching happens in week one; the session is spent on the pupil's most recent marked script, and it ends with a written fault statement. Week two takes the cheapest fault on that list and starts clearing it, because an early visible win buys the pupil's cooperation for the harder work later.

Weeks three and four move to the internal assessment if the pupil is in DP1, because that is the only deadline in the year that cannot be renegotiated. The artefact is a research question narrow enough to control and a plan, both written by the candidate after being questioned hard about them. Week four closes with the first written review, which must name something that has not improved.

Weeks five to eight are the test. The pupil sits something the school marks. The tutor does not mark it, see it in advance, or coach the specific task. When it comes back, the lost marks are mapped against the week-one fault statement, and either the pattern has changed or it has not. Eight weeks is enough to answer that question honestly for every fault signature except a genuine content gap, which needs ten.

sections.heading: Using internal assessment criteria as a progress instrument
paragraphs: The published assessment criteria for coursework are the most useful progress instrument in the Diploma and the least used by parents, because they look like examiner paperwork. They are not. Each criterion has descriptors that state what distinguishes an upper-band response from a middle-band one, in plain language, and a draft can be placed against them by anyone willing to read two paragraphs.

A Group 4 individual investigation is marked out of 24 across five criteria, representing roughly a fifth of the subject grade for about ten hours of work. A mathematics exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria. The Theory of Knowledge essay runs to a 1,600-word limit on a prescribed title, and the Extended Essay to 4,000 words against subject-specific criteria that differ between a History essay and a Chemistry one.

Measured this way, progress stops being a matter of opinion. A draft that was middle-band on evaluation and is now upper-band on evaluation has moved, and the descriptor says why. A draft where the prose improved and every criterion stayed where it was has not moved at all, which is a common and expensive outcome of unfocused drafting support.

The boundary around this work is strict and we state it rather than leaving it implied. A tutor may teach the criteria, interrogate a research question, identify where an argument or method fails, and comment on a draft the candidate has written. A tutor may not supply text or produce any part of a submission. Under IB academic-honesty rules the consequences of crossing that line fall on the candidate and can end a Diploma. One operator in this market advertises finished Internal Assessments for a fee; that is a risk sold to a child, not a service.

sections.heading: What grade movement is realistic, and over what period
paragraphs: Parents are owed a straight answer here and almost never get one. No tutor can promise a grade, and a provider who does is either naive or dishonest. What can be said is what the common fault signatures typically yield when they are correctly identified and cleared, and how long each takes to appear in marked work.

Convention and timing faults are the fast ones. A pupil losing marks to missing units, unlabelled axes or a collapse in the final third of the paper can show measurable change in one to four weeks, because the repair is a checklist rather than knowledge. These are also the faults most likely to be invisible to the family, because nothing about the pupil's understanding is wrong.

Command-term faults take two to four weeks to repair and longer to become habitual under exam pressure. Content gaps take six to ten weeks at one session per week, and that estimate assumes the pupil does the consolidation between sessions. A content gap spanning two years of missing foundations, which happens after a curriculum switch, is a two-term project and should be described as one at the outset.

What none of this supports is a prediction expressed as a number. A pupil who clears a timing fault may gain marks that do not cross a grade boundary, and a pupil who gains fewer marks may cross one. Grade boundaries are set per session by the board and are not published in advance. Any figure attached to a promise about your child's final grade was invented, and the fact that it was offered tells you what else on that page is worth checking.
bullets: Convention and timing faults: visible movement in one to four weeks
Command-term faults: two to four weeks to repair, longer to automate

sections.heading: What a Dubai school report will not tell you
paragraphs: School reporting in this emirate is generally thorough, and it is built to answer a different question from the one a parent books a tutor to answer. A report tells you where a pupil sits relative to expectation. It rarely tells you which component the marks were lost on, which is the only information that selects an intervention.

Three specific blind spots recur. The first is the aggregated subject grade, which averages a strong internal assessment with weak examined performance, or the reverse, and conceals both. A pupil with a banked upper-band coursework mark and collapsing paper technique looks identical on a report to a pupil with the opposite profile, and they need opposite help.

The second is the predicted grade, which is a professional judgement made for university applications and carries institutional caution in both directions. It is not a measurement, it moves between reporting cycles, and in a newer Diploma cohort it rests on very few historical data points. Treating it as a reading rather than a judgement leads families to relax or to panic at the wrong moments.

The third is the inspection band. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority inspects Dubai private schools annually and publishes a judgement from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and the band is a statement about the school as a whole. It cannot tell you whether this year's Diploma cohort was large enough to timetable Higher Level Economics, or whether one teacher covers both levels of Physics. The subject detail sits inside the full report, and the school's option blocks answer the rest.

sections.heading: Two tutors, one record: keeping a paired plan coherent
paragraphs: Families who book two specialists usually do it for good reasons and then discover a coordination problem nobody warned them about. Two tutors optimising independently will both decide that the fortnight before half-term is the right moment for intensive drafting work, and the pupil will face two coursework deadlines, two sets of feedback and a full school week simultaneously.

The fix is one shared calendar built before either slot is fixed. Every internal assessment deadline across all six subjects goes on it, with the mock window and the co-curricular commitments that actually bind: a CAS project, a sports fixture block, a performance. Then the two slots are placed so that drafting intensity alternates rather than coincides.

The second half of the fix is one record rather than two. A single four-week review covering both subjects lets a parent see something neither tutor can: that the pupil is improving in one subject and flat in the other, which usually means attention is being rationed rather than that one tutor is better. That is a scheduling decision, and it can only be made from a combined view.

This is also where an honest provider says no. Three weekly subject slots plus school plus coursework plus CAS does not fit in a sixteen-year-old's week, and arrangements that do not fit fail quietly, with the pupil absorbing the blame. Two is usually the ceiling for sustained weekly work, with a third subject handled as a short component block when a deadline demands it.

sections.heading: The mock is an instrument, not a verdict
paragraphs: Mock results arrive in Dubai Diploma households in the winter term and cause more poor decisions than any other single document. The grade gets read as a prediction, the household reacts, and the script itself, which is the valuable part, goes into a bag and is never looked at again.

A mock paper is the richest diagnostic a family will see in two years. It is sat under timed conditions, marked against a real scheme, and covers the whole specification. The lost marks on it map directly onto the four fault signatures, and the mapping takes one session. That session is the highest-value hour available in the entire Diploma, and most families spend the equivalent money on general revision instead.

The grade itself deserves much less weight than it gets, for a mechanical reason. Mocks are often marked to boundaries the school chooses, sometimes deliberately harsh to produce urgency. Grade boundaries for the real session are set afterwards by the board and are not published in advance. A mock 4 and a mock 5 can be two marks apart on a script, which means the difference between a household's calm and its panic can be one borderline answer.

The right use of a mock is therefore mechanical. Get the script. Map every lost mark to a fault signature. Rank the faults by how cheaply they can be cleared. Clear the top two before the next assessment, and ignore the grade until something has actually changed. A post-mock block of three to six sessions aimed at exactly that produces more marks than a term of weekly general support started at the same moment.
bullets: Keep the script, not the grade
Map lost marks to fault signatures in one session
Rank faults by repair cost, then clear the cheapest two
Mock boundaries are chosen by the school, not by the board
Three to six post-mock sessions beat a term of general revision

sections.heading: What cannot be evidenced, and how to spot a provider who pretends otherwise
paragraphs: A page about evidence owes the reader the limits of it. Several things parents are routinely told in this market cannot be demonstrated at all, and the willingness of a provider to assert them is itself a useful signal about everything else they say.

No final grade can be promised. Grade boundaries are set per session by the board, a pupil's performance on the day is not controllable, and anybody promising a 7, or an assured jump of a grade, is selling something they cannot deliver. Related claims are equally unfounded: a specific points gain, a top-percentage placement, or a refund tied to an outcome whose terms are nowhere published.

Aggregate statistics about pupil outcomes cannot be published without the underlying data. A satisfaction percentage, a median tutor score or a proportion achieving top grades means nothing without the number of pupils, the date range and the method of collection. Competitor pages in this market carry several such figures, including two different review totals on the same page, and one self-asserted rating attached to a pupil count that does not reconcile. None of those numbers appear here, because the data behind them does not exist in a form that would survive a question.

Regulatory standing cannot be implied either. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no page here will suggest otherwise. A permit for an individual tutor is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation; a licence for a training institute with premises in Dubai is a separate matter handled by KHDA. Neither is a badge a tutoring platform can borrow, and the phrase to be most sceptical of in this market is any tutor described as approved by a regulator.
bullets: No grade, points gain or improvement can be promised honestly
Any statistic without a pupil count, a date range and a method is unusable

process.title: Send the most recent marked script
process.description: Not the report, the script with the annotations on it. One paper per subject of concern is enough. It is read for the fault signature before anyone proposes a tutor, because the signature determines whether you need a term of teaching or three sessions of technique work.

process.title: Get the fault statement in writing
process.description: Before any teaching, you receive a written statement naming the fault, the evidence for it on the script, and the repair time. If that statement is vague, the diagnosis was vague, and you should say so rather than proceed hoping it resolves itself.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full session with the proposed specialist at no cost and with no card required, run as a diagnosis rather than a demonstration. By the end you should hold a fault list in priority order and a plan for the first four weeks, whether or not you book anything.

process.title: Agree the review instrument now
process.description: Decide at the outset which piece of school-marked work the four-week review will be measured against. Agreeing the instrument before the sessions start is what prevents a review from becoming a conversation about how the sessions felt.

process.title: Review, and use the exit if the evidence says so
process.description: Every four weeks, against the agreed instrument, with a written note of what has not improved. If the pattern of lost marks is unchanged after eight weeks on a non-content fault, the match is wrong and should change. That is the point of measuring.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before teaching, always
whyPoints.description: The first session works from the pupil's own marked script and produces a written fault statement. Four fault signatures cover most Diploma underperformance and each has a different repair time, so teaching before identifying which one is present is an expensive guess.

whyPoints.title: The measurement is the school's, not ours
whyPoints.description: Progress is judged against work the school marked, by someone with no stake in the arrangement, against the scheme an examiner uses. A provider's own progress report is a document about itself. We would rather be judged on a script we never saw in advance.

whyPoints.title: A record that survives the session
whyPoints.description: Live video with a shared whiteboard leaves every worked solution and annotated script behind as a file. Session notes name the component and the criterion addressed. Eight weeks in, that file is a diagnostic history rather than a memory of pleasant afternoons.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-level feedback, inside the rules
whyPoints.description: Coursework progress is reported against published criterion descriptors by letter, so movement is visible rather than asserted. Feedback addresses only work the candidate wrote. No text is supplied and no part of a submission is produced for anyone.

whyPoints.title: Reviews that name what failed
whyPoints.description: Every four-week review states what has not improved. An arrangement where nothing is ever reported as unchanged is not being measured, and the family finds out at the mock instead, which is the most expensive possible moment.

whyPoints.title: Limits stated rather than papered over
whyPoints.description: No grade promise, no outcome statistics without the data behind them, and no regulator or board accreditation claimed. Two tutors is the sustainable ceiling for weekly work alongside school and CAS, and we say so instead of selling a third.

faqs.question: How will I know whether IB home tutors are actually improving my child's marks?
faqs.answer: By comparing the pattern of lost marks on school-marked work before and after. Keep the script from before the arrangement started, and the next one the school marks six to eight weeks in. If the losses have moved from the pattern named in the week-one diagnosis, something real changed. If they are in the same places, the arrangement is not working regardless of how the sessions feel. Confidence, attendance and completed homework are not evidence, because a pupil can be diligently consolidating the very method that is costing the marks.

faqs.question: Why should the school mark the work rather than the tutor?
faqs.answer: Independence. A tutor marking their own pupil's practice paper has every incentive, including unconscious ones, to read generously, and their boundaries are not the board's. The school's assessment is produced by someone with no stake in the tutoring arrangement, against the same mark scheme an examiner uses, and under conditions the tutor did not design. That is why the review instrument should be agreed before sessions start: a measurement chosen in advance cannot be selected afterwards to flatter whoever is being measured.

faqs.question: What should a tutor's session note actually say?
faqs.answer: Which component was worked on, which criterion or question type, what the pupil could not do at the start, and what they could do by the end. Four lines is enough. What a session note should not say is the topic covered, because a note reading quadratic equations tells a parent nothing about whether a fault was addressed. Over eight weeks, notes written this way become a diagnostic history that makes a four-week review a judgement on evidence rather than an exchange of impressions about a pleasant hour.

faqs.question: Can progress on an internal assessment draft be measured objectively?
faqs.answer: Yes, more objectively than almost anything else in the Diploma, because the criteria are published with descriptors. A Group 4 investigation is marked out of 24 across five criteria; a mathematics exploration out of 20 across five. Place the draft against the descriptor for each criterion and the band is readable by any careful adult. A draft where the prose improved and every criterion stayed in the same band has not progressed, which is a common and costly outcome of unfocused drafting support.

faqs.question: How long before a technique fix shows up in a marked paper?
faqs.answer: It depends on the fault. Convention faults, such as missing units or unlabelled axes, can show measurable change within one to three weeks, because the repair is a checklist applied to practice answers. Timing faults take two to four weeks. Command-term faults take two to four weeks to repair and longer to hold under exam pressure. A genuine content gap takes six to ten weeks at one session a week, assuming the pupil consolidates between sessions, and a gap left by a curriculum switch can take two terms.

faqs.question: Is a mock grade a reliable prediction of the final result?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a diagnostic rather than a prediction. Mocks are often marked to boundaries the school selects, sometimes deliberately severe to create urgency, while real grade boundaries are set per session by the board afterwards and are not published in advance. A mock 4 and a mock 5 can be two marks apart on the same script. The valuable part of a mock is the script, not the grade: mapping every lost mark to a fault signature takes one session and is the highest-value hour available in the two years.

faqs.question: Why will a tutor not promise my child a 7?
faqs.answer: Because nobody can deliver it and offering it is a straightforward misrepresentation. Grade boundaries are set per session by the board, performance on the day is not controllable, and the same number of extra marks crosses a boundary for one candidate and not another. Any provider promising a final grade, an assured improvement or a refund tied to an outcome has either not thought about it or is relying on the terms never being tested. What can honestly be committed to is a diagnosis, a repair plan, a measurement date and an exit.

faqs.question: What does a four-week review contain if nothing improved?
faqs.answer: A statement that nothing improved, the evidence for it, and a recommendation: change the fault being targeted, change the match, or stop. That is the hardest paragraph in this work and it is the one that makes the rest credible. A review that never reports anything unchanged is not a measurement, and a family relying on one discovers the truth at the mock instead, which is the most expensive possible moment to find out.

faqs.question: Does a predicted grade from a Dubai school tell me how tutoring is going?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. A predicted grade is a professional judgement made primarily for university applications, and it carries institutional caution in both directions. It moves between reporting cycles for reasons unrelated to the pupil, and in a newer Diploma cohort it rests on very few historical data points. The underlying internal mark history is far more informative, because it separates banked coursework performance from examined performance. Ask for that history rather than for an explanation of the prediction.

faqs.question: Can one record cover two subjects with two different tutors?
faqs.answer: It should. Two specialists reporting separately conceal the one thing a parent most needs to see, which is divergent progress: improvement in one subject and none in the other usually means attention is being rationed rather than that one tutor is weaker. A single four-week review covering both subjects, using the same four fault names, makes that visible and turns it into a scheduling decision. The combined deadline calendar belongs in the same document, built before either weekly slot is fixed.

faqs.question: How many weekly sessions can a Dubai Diploma candidate actually sustain?
faqs.answer: Two is the realistic ceiling for sustained weekly work alongside a full school timetable, coursework across six subjects, CAS commitments and transport. A third weekly slot generally displaces the consolidation time that makes the first two effective, and the arrangement then fails quietly with the pupil absorbing the blame. Where a third subject genuinely needs attention, a short component block of three to six sessions timed to a specific deadline works, and it ends. Any provider happy to sell four weekly slots is not thinking about the pupil's week.

faqs.question: What evidence does an online session leave that an in-home visit does not?
faqs.answer: A shared whiteboard retains every worked solution as a reviewable file, annotated scripts exist as documents rather than as paper in a school bag, and the session format invites a written note because there is no doorstep conversation to substitute for one. A visit typically leaves whatever was written on paper plus a verbal summary. IB Gram does not offer in-home visiting in the UAE in any case; teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the audit trail is a by-product of that rather than an added feature.

faqs.question: Why are there no success statistics on this page?
faqs.answer: Because a statistic without a pupil count, a date range and a stated method is not information. Pages competing for this search carry satisfaction percentages, review totals that contradict each other within the same page, and at least one self-asserted rating attached to a pupil figure that does not reconcile. Publishing numbers of that kind would be easy and would tell you nothing about your child. The measurement offered here is specific to one pupil and produced by their own school, which is less impressive and considerably more useful.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram approved or accredited by KHDA to provide tutoring?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody in this market should claim it. KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises in Dubai, which is a specific licence for a specific kind of operation. An individual tutor's permit is a different instrument, issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, free of charge for two years. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and the phrase to be most sceptical of in this market is a tutor described as regulator-approved.

faqs.question: What should I keep from a tutoring arrangement once it ends?
faqs.answer: The written fault statements, the session notes, the draft history of each coursework component with its criterion feedback, and the marked scripts that were used as review instruments. That file is useful twice. It tells a future tutor in six months exactly what has already been tried and what did not work, which saves two sessions of rediscovery. And it tells the pupil, during the May session revision period, which three faults cost them the most marks and in what order to check for them.

dubai/ib-home-tutors.closingHeading: Send one marked script and see what it says
dubai/ib-home-tutors.closingBody: The useful first step in judging IB home tutors in Dubai costs nothing and requires no commitment. Send the subject, the level and one recent marked script. You will get back a written fault statement naming which of the four signatures the script shows, the evidence for it, and an honest repair estimate in weeks. If the signature is a convention or timing fault, that is three sessions rather than a term, and you will be told so. The trial lesson that follows is a full diagnostic hour over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no card required.

dubai/ib-igcse-coaching.tutorsIntro: Each profile below names the board, the level and the subjects the tutor coaches. Coaching cadence is agreed before the first paid session, because a student eight weeks from a series needs a different rhythm from one starting in September.

intro.heading: Coaching is a rhythm, and the rhythm has to match the Dubai year
paragraphs: Parents searching for IB IGCSE coaching in Dubai are rarely asking for a different subject expert from the one a tutoring search would return. They are asking for something structural: a programme with a shape, a schedule and a report, rather than an open-ended weekly hour that drifts until the exams arrive. That is a reasonable thing to want, and it is also where the word coaching does most of its work in this market, because it is used for formats that share nothing except the label.

At one end, a coaching centre runs a batch of eight to twenty students through a syllabus on a fixed timetable. It is cheap per head, it covers content reliably, and it cannot follow one student's mark pattern, because following fifteen mark patterns at once is not a thing a timetable can do. At the other end, one-to-one coaching is a cycle: diagnose from a timed paper, teach what the paper exposed, drill the question types, re-test under identical conditions, report. The second format costs more per hour and usually fewer hours in total. Neither is wrong; buying one while expecting the other is.

The second thing this page does is put the cycle on the actual Dubai calendar. A school year here runs from late August to late June across three terms, with a winter break, a spring break and Ramadan moving through it year by year. That calendar matters more than any generic revision timetable, because the deadlines that decide a Diploma or IGCSE result are set by the school and sit inside it. Internal coursework deadlines cluster in the middle of Term 2. Mock windows land weeks before entry decisions take effect. Ramadan drifts about eleven days earlier each year and currently sits inside the second term, landing on the mock window and the coursework deadlines rather than on the exam series itself, which in the UAE is June or November.

The third thing is reporting. A coaching arrangement that reports nothing is indistinguishable from an arrangement that is not working, and parents in this market are routinely offered reassurance in place of evidence. The reporting standard this page describes is modest and specific: a marked artefact after every session, a short written summary after every fourth, and a comparison of two identical timed papers at the ten-week mark. All of it readable by a parent who does not teach the subject.

Delivery, stated once and plainly. IB Gram coaches one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around Dubai school timetables. IB Gram does not run a centre, holds no premises in the UAE, and does not make home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service offered only in India. No approval, accreditation or partnership is claimed from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and the first session is free and runs as a diagnostic on a real past paper.
