sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with a child's writing
paragraphs: English is where the academic-honesty line gets tested hardest, because the product is text and text is easy to supply. A tutor may teach, model on a different example, question, and mark the pupil's own writing against the criteria. A tutor may not write a paragraph the pupil submits, rewrite a sentence into the pupil's draft, or edit a piece to completion. Where a coursework component exists, the mark has to represent the pupil's own work and the restriction tightens rather than relaxes.

The legitimate loop is simple and it is also the loop that works. The pupil writes. The tutor marks against the objectives and names what is missing without supplying it: 'this paragraph has no effect on a reader stated', not 'try writing it like this'. The pupil rewrites. The tutor marks again. A pupil who goes through that four times owns the skill. A pupil handed improved sentences owns nothing and will not be able to repeat it in June.

Modelling deserves a word, because it is legitimate and often confused with writing for a pupil. A tutor may demonstrate the technique on a completely different passage or question, so the pupil sees the shape and then produces their own. That is teaching. Demonstrating it on the pupil's own assessed task, in words they will submit, is not. The test is whether any sentence the tutor composed ends up in the submission.

One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright, at a published price. That is a malpractice trigger, and the exposure sits with the candidate. On the same principle, nobody should hand over past papers, mark schemes or set-text study guides as files: those belong to Cambridge, Pearson and their publishers, and the right behaviour is to link the official page. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, Cambridge, Pearson or IB approval or partnership and makes no such claim.

sections.heading: The June series counted backwards for an essay subject
paragraphs: English behaves differently from maths in the final stretch, and the calendar should be read accordingly. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask the school which zone applies and work from the live official timetable. As a guide to the lead times involved, the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026 and June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026.

Counted backwards, the English sequence has one unusual feature: the last eight weeks are genuinely productive, more so than in a content subject. Technique changes can still be installed in that window, because the pupil is not learning facts but changing how they answer. A pupil who adopts the quote-technique-effect habit in March will use it in June. A pupil learning twelve new set-text quotations in May is doing something much less reliable.

Where a coursework component is used, the deadlines sit much earlier and are set internally by the school rather than by the board. Those dates are the ones to ask about in September, because a missed internal deadline cannot be rescued by revision. And for a single-subject disappointment, the November series is a reasonable plan for English specifically, since the skills are already developed and the remaining work is technique under timing.

sections.heading: Coverage, scheduling and the first session
paragraphs: First Language English and Literature in English at both Cambridge and Pearson are well covered in this set, and a match is usually quick. Thinner briefs exist: a specific Pearson anthology poem set alongside an unusual text choice, or English as a Second Language at the oral-endorsement end. In a given week the honest answer may be that nobody suitable is free, and saying so is better than placing a generalist at the same rate.

Three outcomes are possible and a family should be told which applies. The brief is covered and a trial lesson is scheduled within days. The brief is covered by a specialist working into Gulf Standard Time from outside the UAE, which is disclosed rather than concealed behind a local-looking telephone number. Or the brief is not currently covered, in which case it is named rather than filled. Rates do not change because a tutor is based outside the UAE.

English scheduling has one requirement the other subjects do not. The pupil has to produce writing, which means a session scheduled when they are already exhausted produces a weaker sample than the pupil is capable of, and the diagnosis suffers accordingly. For families in JVT, JVC and Al Furjan, where pupils are often home by four, an early slot is realistic. For Remraam and Mudon households, a weekend morning is frequently better than a weekday evening.

The first session is free, is one session, and requires no card details. The useful thing to bring to it is a piece of your child's own marked writing - a mock answer, a directed writing task, a literature essay - rather than a description of the problem. Within the hour it should be possible to name which assessment objective is costing the most marks and what the first four weeks would consist of. If that is not possible, the match is wrong.

process.title: Establish the codes and the set text list
process.description: Ask the examinations officer which English codes your child is entered for - 0500 or 0990, 0475 or 0992, 4EA1 or 4ET1 - whether a coursework component applies, and what the literature text list is. Every one of those answers changes what practice is worth doing, and none of them can be guessed from the prospectus.

process.title: Get one marked script of each type
process.description: A reading answer and a piece of directed writing, both marked by the school. Look at where the annotations cluster rather than at the grade. A script with comments about explaining effects is an analysis problem; a script with comments about audience is a form problem, and they are different purchases.

process.title: Name the failing objective
process.description: Sort the lost marks into selection, analysis, form and register, structure, and accuracy. Most pupils are losing heavily in one or two of those while performing well in the rest, which is exactly why the overall grade looks immovable. Aim the work at the largest column and leave the others alone.

process.title: Write, mark, rewrite, repeat
process.description: Every session should produce or respond to a piece of the pupil's own writing. The loop is the pupil writes, the tutor marks against the criteria naming what is missing without supplying it, the pupil rewrites. Four cycles usually installs the habit, and installed habits survive into June.

process.title: Protect the slot the pupil can write in
process.description: English needs a pupil with energy because they have to produce text, not follow along. Pupils in JVT and Al Furjan are home early enough for a 5pm session; households in Remraam and Mudon often do better with a weekend morning. Fix the slot and keep it through mock season rather than renegotiating weekly.

whyPoints.title: Marks traced to objectives
whyPoints.description: The first output is a note saying which assessment objective is costing the marks: selection, analysis, form, structure or accuracy. That is what a stuck grade is made of, and it is information a report comment about strong expression cannot give you.

whyPoints.description: Literature work starts from the text list your child's school actually chose and the components the centre entered. Generic literature tutoring teaches a book they will not be examined on, and every session spent that way is a session not spent on the examined material.

whyPoints.title: Writing produced, not discussed
whyPoints.description: Sessions are built round the pupil writing, being marked against the criteria, and rewriting. A pupil who has been through that loop four times owns the skill; a pupil handed improved sentences owns nothing and cannot reproduce it under timing in June.

faqs.question: Why is my fluent Arcadia School child stuck on a grade 5 in English?
faqs.answer: Because IGCSE English does not award marks for writing well; it awards them against assessment objectives, and fluency satisfies only some of them. A pupil who summarises a passage accurately earns comprehension marks and leaves the analysis marks unclaimed, because analysis wants a short quotation, a named technique and an effect on a reader. In writing, marks split between form and register on one side and accuracy on the other, so a fluent essay written in answer to a speech task loses the form marks entirely. The report says 'strong expression' and the grade does not move.

faqs.question: What exactly does a reading analysis question want from a candidate?
faqs.answer: A sentence with three connected parts, repeated three or four times. A short quotation of two or three words, the name of what the writer is doing with them, and an account of the effect that has on a reader. Quoting a whole sentence usually means the pupil has not identified which word does the work, and the mark scheme is interested in the word. Stating an effect on the writer or the character rather than on a reader also loses the mark. Most pupils write a confident paragraph about the passage and earn two marks out of five.

faqs.question: How many marked essays does it take to shift an English grade?
faqs.answer: Three or four, if they are properly marked and then rewritten, which is usually far fewer than families expect. The loop matters more than the number: the pupil writes under timing, the work is marked against the published objectives with the missing element named rather than supplied, and the pupil rewrites it. Going through that four times installs a habit that survives into the examination. A term of discussion about texts and techniques, with no writing produced and marked, routinely changes nothing at all.

faqs.question: My child writes beautifully but keeps losing marks on directed writing. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly form. A directed writing task names a form, an audience and a purpose, and marks all three. A pupil who writes well has been rewarded for organised argumentative prose for years, so when the task asks for a speech they produce an essay with no direct address, no rhetorical pattern and no acknowledgement that listeners exist. The language marks are earned and the form marks are not. The fix is four tasks in four different forms, written under timing, marked and rewritten with the form features inserted deliberately.

faqs.question: Should literature tutoring cover the texts our school actually chose?
faqs.answer: Yes, exclusively, and this is the single best test of a prospective literature tutor. Set texts are chosen by the school and change over time, so a tutor who starts discussing a novel before asking what your child is studying is about to teach a book they will not be examined on. The first questions should be which board, which components and which texts, and all three answers come from the school. Once the list is known, the trainable elements are quotation economy, argument structure and timed essay production.

faqs.question: Is First Language English the same qualification as English as a Second Language?
faqs.answer: No. They are separate IGCSE qualifications with different codes, different papers, different ceilings and different reception at sixth form. Cambridge First Language English runs as 0500 and 0990; English as a Second Language runs as 0510, 0511 and 0993 depending on the arrangement. A pupil capable of the first should not be entered for the second by default, and a pupil entered for the second should know how the Dubai sixth forms they are considering read it. That is a Year 10 conversation with the school rather than a results-day discovery.

faqs.question: What marks does an EAL pupil lose that are not actually language marks?
faqs.answer: More than most families realise. Cultural reference in unseen passages, where a scene is misread because the social setting is unfamiliar rather than because the vocabulary was difficult. Assessment-objective ignorance, which costs first-language pupils just as much. And question-reading speed under timing, which is a processing issue responding to practice rather than to vocabulary work. The genuine language losses are narrower: idiom and collocation, which improve through correction of the pupil's own writing, and register control, which is learned knowledge teachable in about four tasks.

faqs.question: Does more reading at home fix a stuck English grade?
faqs.answer: It helps slowly and it is rarely the bottleneck. A child who already reads widely and still scores 5 is not short of exposure; they are short of a technique nobody has named for them. Reading builds vocabulary, idiom and stamina, which pay over years. Marks move when the pupil writes an analysis sentence, has it marked, sees which clause earned the mark and writes it again. If reading were the mechanism, the fluent readers in every Dubai English class would already have top grades, and they do not.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0500 and Pearson Edexcel 4EA1?
faqs.answer: Different boards, different paper structures and different question types, so past-paper practice has to match the code on the entry. The structural differences bite in two places. Coursework availability varies, and a portfolio route needs a completely different revision strategy from a wholly examined one. And Pearson's literature route uses a published anthology alongside set texts, which is a defined body of material a pupil can be systematically prepared on. Ask the examinations officer for the code in writing; a prospectus saying 'IGCSE English' does not answer the question.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an English coursework piece?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skills the piece needs, model the technique on a different example, and give feedback on the pupil's own draft naming what is missing. A tutor cannot write a paragraph, rewrite a sentence into the draft, or edit the piece to completion, and no price makes that acceptable. Where a component contributes to an assessed mark the restriction tightens, because the mark must represent the pupil's own work. The test is simple: no sentence a tutor composed should end up in the submission.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting English tutoring eight weeks before the June papers?
faqs.answer: For English, yes, more than for a content subject. Technique changes can still be installed in that window because the pupil is not learning facts but changing how they answer, and a pupil who adopts the quote-technique-effect habit in March will use it in June. What does not work in eight weeks is learning twelve new set-text quotations or covering a text properly for the first time. Where a coursework component is used the deadlines sit much earlier and are set internally by the school, so those dates need asking about in September.

faqs.question: Does improving English reading help in History and Geography too?
faqs.answer: Consistently, and this is the strongest argument for buying English analysis work first. A History source question asks the candidate to select, attribute, infer and evaluate, which is the same skill as a reading analysis question in different clothing. Geography extended answers reward structure and a stated judgement in the same way directed writing does. Pupils who install the analysis sentence in English usually show improvement in both within weeks, which means one purchase pays across three subjects rather than one.

faqs.question: Do you send English tutors to JVT, JVC or Al Furjan addresses?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service offered only in India. Tutoring for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. For English this works well: the session is spent annotating the pupil's own marked writing on a shared screen and rewriting the paragraphs that lost marks. It also means the tutor is chosen for the board, the component and the set text list rather than for living within a drivable radius.

faqs.question: What should we bring to the first English session?
faqs.answer: A piece of your child's own marked writing rather than a description of the problem. A mock reading answer, a directed writing task, or a literature essay with the school's annotations on it is worth more than any amount of explanation, because it shows where the marks went. Bring the set text list and the specification code too if you have them. Within an hour it should be possible to name which assessment objective is costing the most marks and what the first four weeks would consist of. The first session is free, is one session, and needs no card details.

intro.heading: Price the timetable, not the hour
paragraphs: Almost every conversation about IGCSE tutoring in Dubai starts with an hourly rate and ends with a number nobody budgeted for. The hourly rate is the least useful figure available. A Year 10 pupil at a selective British-curriculum school in Dubai is sitting nine or ten subjects, and at AED 220 an hour, one weekly session in each of them is more than AED 8,000 a month. No family buys that. What families actually buy is two or three subjects, for two or three terms, with a decision at each report about whether to continue. The real question is therefore which subjects, for how long, and what that totals.

So this page is built the other way round. It starts with the market bands in AED, sourced to the providers who published them, because three of the six highest-ranking tutoring pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars. Then it works out the cost of a subject rather than an hour: a term of weekly sessions, including the marking time that may or may not be inside the rate you are quoted. Then it asks which subject on a ten-subject timetable repays that money, which is a different question from which subject your child finds hardest.

The answer is usually counter-intuitive. The subject a pupil hates is rarely the one where an hour buys the most marks. On an Extended-tier timetable, the biggest single return is normally a subject sitting one grade below where the pupil's working is, because the gap is procedural rather than conceptual: a Maths 0580 candidate losing method marks on non-calculator working, or a Physics 0625 candidate who understands circuits and cannot write a six-mark explanation. Those are cheap gaps. A subject where the pupil has not understood the first third of the specification is an expensive gap, and it costs more terms than most budgets contain.

The second thing that moves the number in Dubai specifically is travel. The published in-home band runs from AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, and the top of that band is not buying better teaching. It is buying a car in Dubai traffic at five in the afternoon. A tutor driving from Jumeirah to Al Barsha South for a 5pm session is committing ninety minutes to deliver sixty, and the invoice reflects it. Removing the car from the arrangement is the single largest saving available to a Dubai family, which is why IB Gram delivers to Dubai households as one-to-one live video rather than as a visit. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service offered only in India.

What follows is specific. The AED bands are sourced. The subject triage is set out as a table you can apply to your own child's last report. The Cambridge calendar is counted backwards from the June and November series so you can see when money needs to be spent rather than when it would be comfortable to spend it. And the things a tutor may never be paid to do are stated plainly, because one page ranking in this market sells completed coursework, and a parent should be able to tell the difference.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-brighton-colleg.programmesIntro: A pupil in a British-curriculum school in Dubai moves through three distinct cost phases. The money behaves differently in each one, and knowing which phase your child is in tells you whether to spend now or hold.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE options are chosen. No external examination sits at the end, which is precisely why it is the cheapest place to buy a grade. A Year 8 pupil whose algebra is insecure needs perhaps ten hours of work; the same pupil in Year 11 needs forty, because the insecurity has been built on for three years and now shows up in every Extended-tier paper.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools stream for IGCSE Maths and Science from Year 9 in many cases, and a set allocation made in Year 9 can decide whether a pupil is entered for Core or Extended tier two years later. Spending in Year 8 to protect an Extended-tier entry is cheaper than spending in Year 11 to recover a grade ceiling that a Core entry has already capped.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, nine or ten subjects, one terminal examination series. Costs concentrate in two places: the first term of Year 10, when the specification is new and habits form, and the final two terms of Year 11, when timed practice and marked scripts are the only thing that moves a grade. The middle three terms are where most families overspend on sessions that could have been a monthly paper instead.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit June and November. The June series is the main entry for a Year 11 cohort in Dubai; November is the resit route. That shape means a Dubai family's heaviest tutoring quarter is January to April, which overlaps Ramadan in some years and needs the schedule planned round Iftar rather than abandoned.

programmes.name: International A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects, each with entry requirements expressed as IGCSE grades. The cost consequence is sharp: an IGCSE grade 6 where a department wants a 7 can close a subject, and reopening it in Year 12 means covering the IGCSE gap and the A Level content at once. That is the most expensive form of tutoring there is.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai sixth forms publish subject-specific IGCSE entry grades, and selective schools apply them. Checking those thresholds in Year 10 rather than after results converts a vague worry into a priced decision: one subject, two terms, a known figure, against a sixth-form place.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-brighton-colleg.subjectsIntro: Cost per subject is not uniform. Below, each IGCSE subject is given with its specification code and the kind of gap that typically needs paying for. The code matters because a Cambridge 0580 candidate and a Pearson 4MA1 candidate are not sitting the same paper.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580)
subjects.description: Two written papers, no coursework. Extended tier reaches grade 9; Core caps at grade 5. The commonest paid-for gap is method marks lost on non-calculator working, which is a habit problem and responds to a short block of sessions rather than a long one.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers of equal weight, both calculator-permitted, which changes revision entirely from the Cambridge route. Pupils moving between Dubai schools sometimes change board mid-course; reconciling the two specifications is a defined, finite piece of work.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge IGCSE 0625)
subjects.description: Theory papers plus the Alternative to Practical, which is where marks leak most consistently. Pupils who can do the physics still lose marks describing a method, identifying a control variable, or reading a scale. That is trainable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge IGCSE 0620)
subjects.description: Organic chemistry and moles account for most of the grade movement at the top end. A pupil who has not secured mole calculations by the end of Year 10 is carrying a cost into Year 11, because every later topic assumes them.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge IGCSE 0610)
subjects.description: Content-heavy rather than conceptually hard, which makes it the cheapest science to tutor and the easiest to self-remedy. Marks are usually lost to imprecise terminology and to command terms, not to misunderstanding.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 and 0990)
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading response. The gap is almost never vocabulary; it is structure under timing. Three or four marked scripts with specific rewriting tasks typically move more than a term of discussion.

subjects.name: English Literature (Cambridge 0475 and 0992)
subjects.description: Set texts differ by school, so any tutoring has to start from your child's own text list. Essay structure and quotation economy are the trainable elements; reading the text remains the pupil's work.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge IGCSE 0478)
subjects.description: Paper 2 pseudocode and algorithm tracing is where grades are decided. Pupils strong in practical programming often lose marks because the examination wants Cambridge pseudocode conventions, not working Python.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Both reward data-response discipline over content recall. A pupil who can define every term and still writes four marks of description for a six-mark evaluation question is losing an avoidable grade.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Taken alongside the KHDA-mandated Arabic provision that every Dubai private school must deliver regardless of its licensed curriculum. Reading fluency and script accuracy are the usual targets, and progress is measurable week to week.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-brighton-colleg.regionsTitle: Where the families reading this page actually live
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-brighton-colleg.regionsIntro: Pupils at a school on the Al Barsha South side of Dubai come from a handful of communities, and the commute from each one is what makes an in-home arrangement expensive. These notes are about the logistics of a 5pm session, not about the school itself.

regions.name: Al Barsha South
regions.note: Immediately around the school, so the only community where a tutor's travel time is genuinely short. Even here, the AED 180-500 in-home band applies, because a tutor prices a round trip rather than the nearest leg of it.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: A fifteen-minute drive at noon and considerably longer on the Al Khail Road at school-run time. Families here often want a 4.30pm start, which is the worst possible slot for anyone driving in.

regions.name: Arjan and Al Furjan
regions.note: Both sit off the main arterials, which means a tutor's satnav estimate and the actual journey diverge. An online session starting at 4.45pm, fifteen minutes after the pupil is home, has no such variance.

regions.name: Motor City and Sports City
regions.note: Well served for group tuition centres, which is why the AED 100-150 per-student group rate is widely available here. Group sessions work for content coverage and not for a specific procedural gap.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Triangle
regions.note: Dense, apartment-heavy and full of families on a tighter education budget than the villa communities. This is where the AED 45-65 budget online band gets most of its enquiries, and where the gap between a cheap tutor and a specialist shows up at Extended tier.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Meadows
regions.note: Villa communities where the premium named-tutor band of AED 500-650 an hour finds its market. Paying it only makes sense for a specific, diagnosed, high-stakes gap rather than for general weekly support.

regions.name: Downtown and Business Bay
regions.note: A long commute to the Al Barsha South corridor, so pupils here are typically home late. Sessions after 7pm are routine, and an online tutor can be scheduled into them without a travel surcharge.

schoolClusters.city: The Al Barsha South and Dubai Hills corridor
schoolClusters.note: A cluster of British-curriculum and IB schools within a few kilometres of each other, which means pupils swap between them and arrive mid-course on a different specification. Reconciling two boards' Maths or Science specifications is one of the more common pieces of paid work here.

schoolClusters.city: The Dubailand and Motor City belt
schoolClusters.note: Newer schools with growing secondary phases, where a first IGCSE cohort may be small and subject sets correspondingly thin. Pupils taking a minority subject sometimes have no classmate at the same tier, which is exactly when one-to-one work earns its cost.

modes.description: Three or four sessions with a defined output: a marked paper per subject under consideration, an error taxonomy, and a recommendation about which subjects deserve a term. At market specialist rates that is roughly AED 800-1,800, and it is the only spend that reliably prevents a larger one.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE hour costs in Dubai, and who publishes that figure
paragraphs: An IGCSE tutor in Dubai costs between AED 45 and AED 650 an hour depending on who is teaching and how. That spread is not noise. Each band corresponds to a different kind of person doing a different kind of work, and knowing which band you are being quoted from tells you more than any sales conversation will.

The figures below are market rates published by the providers named, not IB Gram's price list. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52, both drawing largely on university students and overseas graduates. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. The Bestimate rate survey for Dubai puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 and subject specialists at AED 200-450 or above, while BartyED advertises AED 650 for a named premium tutor. Monthly packages circulate at around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Two things follow. First, the cheap end is cheap because the tutor is learning the specification alongside your child, which is survivable for Core tier content coverage and unreliable at Extended tier. Second, the expensive end is not a quality ladder: part of the in-home premium is travel, and part of the premium-named premium is scarcity and reputation rather than measurable outcome. Nobody in this market publishes outcome data with a sample size and a method, including the brands charging the most, so a rate is a claim about positioning and not evidence of effect.

sections.heading: Nine or ten subjects, and the two that repay the spend
paragraphs: Tutoring every subject on an IGCSE timetable is arithmetically impossible for most families, so the real decision is a triage. The useful sorting question is not which subject is hardest. It is how many marks an hour of work buys in each subject, and that depends on what kind of gap the pupil has rather than on how they feel about the lessons.

Four gap types recur. A timing gap means the pupil knows the content and does not finish the paper; it is the cheapest gap there is and often closes in four or five sessions of timed practice. A technique gap means marks are lost to command terms, working, or the shape of an answer; six to ten sessions. A topic gap means a defined block of the specification was never secured; one term. A foundation gap means the pupil cannot access the tier they are entered for; two years of consequence, and the honest answer is sometimes a tier change rather than a tutor.

Apply this to a real report and the triage usually resolves to two subjects. A pupil at grade 6 in Maths with method marks leaking and a pupil at grade 4 in Chemistry who never secured moles are different propositions: the first is worth AED 2,600 for a term and the second is worth a conversation with the school about tier before anyone is paid anything. sections.heading: The marginal grade, and why the hated subject is rarely the right buy
paragraphs: Families almost always nominate the subject their child complains about. It is the wrong starting point, because complaint tracks discomfort rather than distance from the next grade boundary. A pupil two marks below a boundary in a subject they tolerate is a better purchase than a pupil fifteen marks below a boundary in the subject they dread, and the second pupil needs a different intervention anyway.

The way to find the marginal grade is to read the actual script rather than the report grade. A school report compresses a term into a letter. A marked mock paper shows you where the marks went: which questions, which command words, which topics, and whether the back page was attempted. Ask the school for the script, not the grade. Most Dubai schools will release it, and a tutor who cannot tell you what a script says is not worth AED 200 an hour.

This is also where the honest version of the sales pitch lives. If a diagnostic session shows a pupil is three marks off a boundary across two papers, a short technique block is a defensible spend with a measurable target. If it shows the pupil has not understood the first third of the specification, no amount of weekly tutoring in the final term fixes it, and a provider who takes the money anyway is selling you comfort. No tutor, however experienced with 0580 or 0625 papers, can promise a particular grade, and nobody should write that sentence on an invoice.

sections.heading: An in-home visit to the Al Barsha South corridor, priced honestly
paragraphs: A good deal of the in-home premium in Dubai is a traffic charge. A tutor travelling from Jumeirah or Mirdif for a 4.30pm session in Al Barsha South or Dubai Hills spends between forty and seventy minutes on the road each way at that hour, and a round trip of two hours to deliver one is priced into the rate whether the invoice itemises it or not. That is the honest explanation for why the published in-home band starts at AED 180 and reaches AED 500.

The second cost is selection. An in-home tutor has to live within a drivable radius of your villa. The pool of people who both specialise in Extended-tier Chemistry 0620 and happen to live twenty minutes from Arjan is small, and when it is empty the arrangement quietly becomes whoever is available rather than whoever is right. A family in Dubai Hills ends up with a generalist because the specialist lives in Abu Dhabi.

Removing the car changes both. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to Dubai households over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, which means the tutor is selected for the specification and tier rather than for a postcode. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered in India only. That is a limitation worth stating plainly rather than burying, and the table sets out what each format gives and gives up.

There is a third cost that rarely appears in a quote, which is the cancelled session. A tutor caught on a closed Al Khail Road slip or held up by the school-run queue into Dubai Hills either arrives twenty minutes late and teaches forty, or cancels. Over a thirteen-week term, two lost sessions at AED 300 is AED 600 of budget that bought nothing, and the replacement slot competes with homework that has already moved.

sections.heading: Four Dubai-specific things that move the number
paragraphs: Emirate-level facts change this budget in ways a generic tutoring article will not mention. The first is the school fee itself. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family planning two years of IGCSE, the school half of the education budget is fixed, which makes the tutoring half the only variable worth modelling.

The second is market depth. KHDA counted 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools in Dubai in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the UK curriculum the largest by enrolment share and the International Baccalaureate a much smaller slice. Seven more private schools join the 2026-27 intake, four UK curriculum and three IB, adding 16,846 places. A deep market means real competition on rates, which is why the published spread is so wide and why a quoted figure is negotiable in a way it would not be in a thin market.

The third is the calendar. Demand for IGCSE tutoring in Dubai concentrates between January and April ahead of the June series, and rates at the specialist end firm up in that window because the people who can mark an Extended-tier script are already booked. Buying in September is cheaper than buying in February for exactly the same teaching. The fourth is Ramadan: school days shorten, evenings restructure around Iftar, and a family that plans post-Iftar sessions keeps its momentum while a family that pauses loses six weeks of the most valuable quarter in the two-year course.

sections.heading: Is the rate you have been quoted a legal rate?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and a family paying AED 200 an hour is entitled to know whether the person being paid holds one. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services.

Because the permit is free, any tutor who tells you their rate reflects licensing costs is mistaken about their own paperwork. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts has been published, so any figure circulating online should be treated as unverified.

There is a separate position for a teacher at your child's own school. Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct is reported to bar the same arrangement. The practical advice for a Dubai parent is simple: do not arrange paid tutoring with your child's own class teacher, however convenient it looks. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again, needing a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or MoE approval and makes no such claim; it is an online matching platform, not a licensed Dubai institute.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards as a spending plan
paragraphs: A tutoring budget fails when it is spent on the wrong side of a deadline. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered in India only, so a Dubai parent planning round it is planning for the wrong country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. Your child's school knows its zone; you should ask rather than assume, and you should work from the live official timetable rather than any date restated on a tutoring page, including this one. For a sense of how far ahead the machinery runs, the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026.

Read backwards, the money sequence is clear. Entries close months before the paper. Mocks happen before the entry decision is final, which is why a mock script is the cheapest diagnostic available. The heaviest useful spend sits in the eight to twelve weeks before the series, not the fortnight before it, because timed practice needs marking and remarking to change anything. And the November series is a genuine resit route for a Dubai candidate, which means a disappointing June is a plan rather than a catastrophe.

sections.heading: What no invoice should ever cover
paragraphs: One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. That is not a cheaper form of tutoring; it is a malpractice trigger that puts a candidate's whole qualification at risk, and it is the clearest line a parent can use to sort the market. A tutor teaches, explains, questions, models and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not write it.

In practice the boundary is easy to police. Asking a tutor to explain how a six-mark evaluation question is marked is teaching. Asking a tutor to read a draft and say which paragraph does not answer the question is feedback. Asking a tutor to supply paragraphs, rewrite a conclusion, or produce a piece of coursework is work that must be the student's own, and any provider willing to do it has told you exactly how much they care about your child's certificate. The same applies to supplying copyrighted material: syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and the right behaviour is to link the official page rather than to hand over a file.

Nor should an invoice cover claims nobody can substantiate. No provider in this market publishes outcome data with a sample size, a date and a method, so a page quoting a satisfaction percentage or an average improvement is quoting a number it cannot show you. Treat a grade promise as a reason to walk away, and treat 'KHDA-approved tutors' as the single most dangerous phrase in Dubai tutoring advertising: a KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to institutes with premises, and a matching platform does not hold one.

sections.heading: When no specialist is free, and what that costs
paragraphs: Coverage is the thing no competitor in this market discloses, so here it is. Common IGCSE subjects at Extended tier are well covered and a match is usually quick. Minority subjects are not. A pupil needing Extended-tier Computer Science 0478 with Cambridge pseudocode conventions, or Arabic as a first language at IGCSE level, may wait longer, and the honest answer in a given week may be that nobody suitable is free.

When that happens there are three outcomes and a family deserves to be told which one applies. The subject is covered and a trial is scheduled within a few days. The subject is covered by a tutor outside the UAE working into Gulf Standard Time, which is disclosed rather than hidden behind a local-looking telephone number. Or the subject is not currently covered at the tier required, in which case the right answer is to say so instead of placing a generalist and invoicing for it.

Two further points on cost. Rates do not change because a tutor is based outside the UAE; the published band for the subject and tier is what applies either way. And a trial lesson is one session, free, with no card details required, which exists so that a family can test a match before spending anything. If the trial shows the match is wrong, the next step is a different tutor rather than a different payment plan.

Waiting has a price too, and it is worth naming. A pupil who needs Extended-tier Chemistry 0620 in February and waits three weeks for a specialist has lost three weeks of the most valuable quarter in the two-year course. Booking the diagnostic block in the autumn term, when specialist availability is loose, buys the same teaching at the same published band with the scarcity removed.

process.title: Get the script, not the grade
process.description: Ask the school for your child's last marked mock paper in the subjects you are considering. A report grade tells you a position; a script tells you where the marks went, which questions were abandoned, and whether the problem is timing, technique, topic or foundation. This single request changes the budget more than any other step.

process.title: Triage to two subjects
process.description: Apply the gap grid to each script and rank by marks per hour rather than by how much your child dislikes the subject. Two subjects funded properly outperforms five funded thinly on the same money. If a script shows a foundation gap, book a conversation with the school about tier before paying anyone.

process.title: Buy a diagnostic block first
process.description: Three or four sessions with a written output: a timed paper marked against the real mark scheme, an error taxonomy, and a recommendation that may be to stop. At market specialist rates this is roughly AED 800-1,800 and it is the spend that prevents the larger one.

process.title: Fix the weekly slot round the commute
process.description: Pick a start time fifteen minutes after your child is actually home, not fifteen minutes after the bell. Families in Dubai Hills, Arjan and Downtown routinely need a 5.30pm or later start. Online delivery means that slot is available without a travel surcharge or a traffic cancellation.

process.title: Hold a final-term reserve
process.description: Keep roughly a third of the two-year budget for the eight to twelve weeks before the June series, when timed papers and marked rewrites are the only intervention that still moves a grade. Release it against a diagnosed need, not against a vague anxiety, and keep a contingency for a single-subject November resit.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or survey that published it, with the band stated as a market range rather than as our price. Three of the highest-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, which is not a currency a Dubai family transacts in.

whyPoints.title: Cost measured per subject
whyPoints.description: An hourly rate is the least useful figure in a tutoring decision. A term of one subject, with marking included or excluded as the case may be, is the number that decides whether a plan survives Year 11. This page gives you that number for five different kinds of gap.

whyPoints.title: Specification codes, not subject names
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different calculator rules, and a tutor working from the wrong one is wasting your money politely. Matching starts from the code on your child's exam entry and the tier they are sitting at.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and coverage stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are an India-only service. Where a minority subject has no specialist free, that is disclosed rather than filled with a generalist.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line held
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question, model and give feedback on the student's own work. Nobody writes coursework, supplies paragraphs, or hands over a syllabus or mark-scheme file. Official board pages are linked instead, which is both the lawful position and the one that protects the certificate.

whyPoints.title: No claim we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No grade promises, no satisfaction percentages, no self-asserted star ratings, and no suggestion that any regulator has approved, accredited or partnered with IB Gram. Where a figure cannot be sourced, it is left out rather than rounded into something confident.

faqs.question: What will IGCSE tutoring cost a Brighton College Dubai family per subject?
faqs.answer: Budget per subject per term rather than per hour. At the published Dubai specialist band of AED 200-450 an hour, one weekly session across a thirteen-week term is roughly AED 2,600 to AED 5,900 for a single subject. A qualified subject tutor at the AED 150-300 band brings that to about AED 1,950 to AED 3,900. Those are market figures from Unitors, TutorChase and the Bestimate Dubai rate survey, not an IB Gram price list. Most families fund two subjects rather than one or five, and hold roughly a third of the total for the eight to twelve weeks before the June series.

faqs.question: How do we decide which two IGCSE subjects to pay for?
faqs.answer: Rank by marks per hour, not by which subject causes the most friction at home. Ask the school for the last marked mock script in each candidate subject and sort the lost marks into four types. Timing gaps close in four or five sessions. Technique gaps, where content is present but command terms or working lose marks, take six to ten. A topic gap takes a term. A foundation gap, where the pupil cannot access Extended-tier questions at all, is a tier conversation with the school before anyone is paid. The two cheapest gaps usually sit in subjects nobody complained about.

faqs.question: Why do quoted hourly rates in Dubai run from AED 45 to AED 650?
faqs.answer: Because five different kinds of arrangement are being priced. EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from around AED 33-52, largely using university students. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase quotes about AED 270. The Bestimate survey puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 and specialists at AED 200-450 or more. BartyED advertises AED 650 for a named tutor. The spread reflects who is teaching, whether a car is involved, and scarcity. It does not reflect published outcome data, because nobody in this market publishes any with a sample size and method.

faqs.question: Does an in-home visit to Al Barsha South or Dubai Hills justify its premium?
faqs.answer: Decide it as a travel question. A tutor driving from Jumeirah or Mirdif for a 4.30pm session in that corridor spends forty to seventy minutes each way, so a two-hour round trip is priced into the rate. That is most of the gap between the AED 150-300 online band and the AED 180-500 in-home band. The second cost is selection: an in-home tutor must live within driving distance, so a family often gets a generalist rather than the right specialist. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; lessons are one-to-one over live video.

faqs.question: Does the KHDA fee freeze mean tutoring prices will hold too?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That fixes school fees, not tutoring, which is an unregulated private market with rates set provider by provider. The practical benefit is planning: with the school half of your education spend known, the tutoring half becomes the only variable to model over two IGCSE years. Expect specialist rates to firm up from January as the June series approaches, regardless of what school fees do.

faqs.question: Should we take an AED 799 monthly package or keep paying session by session?
faqs.answer: Divide it out before deciding. Packages circulating in Dubai include roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, which is about AED 100 an hour, and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits, which is around AED 200-225 an hour. A package can be good value and it can also hide conditions: ask whether unused sessions roll over, whether marking is inside the rate or billed separately, what notice cancels the arrangement, and whether the price holds if you drop from two subjects to one.

faqs.question: How can we check that a tutor in Dubai is legally permitted to teach?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which lists a two-working-day completion time. Because it costs nothing, a tutor who says their rate covers licensing has misread their own paperwork. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no amounts have been published.

faqs.question: Does the price we are quoted include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider to put it in writing, and get the answer before the first invoice rather than after it. This page does not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because that would need a Federal Tax Authority citation and the question turns on the provider's own registration and the nature of the service. What a parent can reasonably require is a quoted AED figure with a plain statement of whether VAT is included, excluded, or not applicable, plus a tax registration number if the provider holds one. A provider who will not answer that in writing has told you something useful.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start tutoring in September than in February?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes, for the same teaching. Demand for IGCSE tutoring in Dubai concentrates between January and April ahead of the June series, and the people who can mark an Extended-tier script properly are booked out in that window, which firms up rates at the specialist end. Buying the diagnostic block in the autumn also means you discover a foundation gap while there is still time to act on it, rather than discovering it in March when the only honest advice left is to protect the subjects that can still move.

faqs.question: Could a single tutor handle Maths 0580 and Physics 0625 to save a slot and a fee?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking because it saves money and coordination. Cambridge 0580 Maths and 0625 Physics overlap in graph work, rearranging formulae, units and proportionality, so one tutor who genuinely holds both at Extended tier can use a single session to serve two subjects. The test is whether they can talk about the Alternative to Practical paper and non-calculator method marks with equal specificity. If they can only really do one, two specialists beat one generalist, even though it costs more and takes two slots in the week.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to put two siblings in the same session?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per child, and weaker per child. Shared sessions in Dubai are commonly priced around AED 100-150 per pupil in small groups of two to four, against AED 200-450 for one-to-one specialist work. The saving is real. What is lost is diagnosis: a session pitched between two children's gaps addresses neither precisely, and the whole argument for paying specialist rates is that the hour targets one pupil's specific lost marks. Sharing works for content coverage and for siblings genuinely at the same tier in the same subject, and not much else.

faqs.question: Do you send tutors to homes in Al Barsha South, Arjan or Dubai Hills?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service offered only in India. Tutoring for Dubai families is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, which is why a pupil in Arjan can work with a specialist in Extended-tier Chemistry 0620 rather than with whoever lives within a twenty-minute drive. It also removes the traffic charge built into the published AED 180-500 in-home band, and the cancellation risk that comes with a school-run commute.

faqs.question: What should the first paid hour produce before we commit to a term?
faqs.answer: A document, not a feeling. After a diagnostic session you should have a timed piece of your child's work marked against the real mark scheme, a written breakdown of where the marks went by type, and a recommendation naming the subject, the number of sessions and the target. A recommendation to stop, or to speak to the school about tier first, is a legitimate and valuable outcome. If the first hour produces only reassurance and a proposed payment plan, you have bought a sales meeting rather than a diagnosis.

faqs.question: What should we refuse to pay for at any price?
faqs.answer: Written or edited coursework of any kind. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments, which is a malpractice trigger that risks the candidate's whole qualification rather than a shortcut. Also refuse files of past papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents, which belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB and should be linked rather than supplied. Refuse any promise of a specific grade, any claim of KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE or exam-board approval, and any statistic quoted without a sample size, a date and a stated method.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-collegiate-amer.tutorsIntro: These tutors take IB Diploma and IGCSE work for families in Al Barsha South, Dubai Hills and the surrounding American and British curriculum schools. Each teaches one subject at one level, marks the work themselves, and returns the script rather than a summary of it.

intro.heading: Ask for the script, not the update
paragraphs: Most tutoring in Dubai is sold on reassurance. A parent is told the sessions are going well, the student seems more confident, and the grade should come up. Three months later the grade has not come up, and nobody can say what changed because nothing was ever measured. The alternative is not complicated: a marked script every week, a written diagnosis at the start, and a fresh paper at the end to test whether the diagnosis was right. If a provider cannot produce those three things, there is no evidence that anything happened.

This matters in a specific way for Collegiate American School families. The American curriculum reports through a grade point average built from continuous assessment: quizzes, projects, participation, unit tests, often across a semester. That is a reasonable system and it produces a readable transcript, but it smooths over exactly the information a tutor needs. A grade point average of 3.1 in Chemistry does not tell you whether the student cannot balance redox equations or simply missed two quizzes during a family trip. The number is an average of averages.

IB and IGCSE assessment works the other way round. An IGCSE grade comes almost entirely from terminal papers marked against a published scheme with marks allocated question by question. An IB Internal Assessment is marked against lettered criteria with explicit descriptors. Both produce something a parent can actually inspect: a script with marks lost at identifiable points, or a draft with a criterion score and a descriptor explaining it. That is evidence, and it is the reason this page is organised around documents rather than promises.

So the first thing a family here gets is not a lesson. It is a timed past paper, sat under exam conditions, marked against the published mark scheme, and a written diagnosis naming which of four things has gone wrong: content, method, timing or command-word reading. Those four look identical on any report card, including a transcript, and they need four different remedies. Guessing between them is how a term disappears.

A word on delivery, stated once. Tutoring for families in Dubai is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For an evidence-led plan this turns out to help rather than hinder, because scripts, annotated drafts and marked papers accumulate in one shared place instead of in a folder somebody left at school.

What follows is the paperwork. How to read a marked script. What grade movement is realistic over six, twelve and twenty-four weeks. What criterion feedback on an Internal Assessment draft actually says. Where an American-curriculum transcript and an IGCSE grade do and do not line up. And what the Ministry of Education requires from an American-track leaver, which is the one place where the two systems meet formally.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Scripts show marks lost on units, significant figures and incomplete mechanism arrows far more often than on concepts. At Higher Level the energetics and organic sections reward a written reasoning chain; a correct final answer with no visible chain collects a fraction of the available marks.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The diagnostic pattern is that recall questions score well and graph-based or extended-response questions do not. Deriving a relationship from plotted data is a separate skill from knowing the relationship, and it shows up as a cluster of lost marks in the same part of every paper.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Scripts expose command-word failure clearly: a student asked to explain who has described, or asked to evaluate who has listed. The biology is usually right. The answer shape is wrong, which is a four-session fix and one of the most visible before-and-after changes available.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Marked scripts almost always point to algebraic manipulation inside otherwise understood topics rather than to the topics themselves. Paper 3 at Higher Level is an extended investigation marked on reasoning, so the evidence of progress there is the quality of written justification, not the final answer.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: Core entry caps the grade at 5 and Extended reaches 9, so the first piece of evidence a family needs is which tier the student can collect marks at. Two timed papers, one at each tier, answers a question that otherwise gets decided by assumption.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Progress here is read from annotated drafts rather than scripts. The measurable change is usually in the analytical paragraph: whether a quotation is being analysed or merely quoted. Individual Oral preparation is marked on sustained analysis of a global issue, which is coachable and checkable.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: The summary task is marked on selection, so a student who writes fluently and selects poorly plateaus around a grade 6 and stays there regardless of effort. Directed writing is marked on register, audience and form before content. Both are visible on a marked paper in minutes.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the countable thing. An unlabelled axis or a shift drawn the wrong way loses the mark whatever the prose says, and a marked script shows this as a repeated identical error. Higher Level evaluation is a separate taught skill with its own mark allocation.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study papers reward application to the stimulus material. A script where every paragraph is textbook theory with no reference to the company is a specific and fixable failure, not a knowledge gap. Quantitative tools at Higher Level are marked on method shown.

sections.heading: How to read a marked script, and the four things it can tell you
paragraphs: A marked paper is the most underused document in Dubai tutoring. Parents are shown grades constantly and scripts almost never, which is unfortunate, because the script contains the diagnosis and the grade contains nothing. Reading one takes about twenty minutes and does not require subject knowledge. You are looking for patterns in where the marks were lost, not for whether the answers were right.

There are four patterns and they are mutually distinguishable. A content failure looks like whole questions attempted badly or not at all in one topic area, with the rest of the paper sound. A method failure looks like correct final answers with few marks, because the working was not written out and the method marks could not be awarded. A timing failure looks like a strong first half and blank or rushed final questions, which is a fixed loss of marks on every single paper the student sits. A command-word failure looks like good, accurate subject content that answers a different question from the one printed: a description where an explanation was asked for, a list where an evaluation was required.

Each has a different remedy and a different timescale. Content takes the longest and is the only one that genuinely requires re-teaching. Method is usually four to six sessions of enforced habit change. Timing is three or four sessions with a stopwatch and a deliberate question order. Command words are the fastest fix of all and the most frequently misdiagnosed, because a student who writes accurate biology and scores four out of ten is assumed to need more biology.

This is why the first paid hour here is a marked paper rather than a lesson. The diagnosis determines everything after it, and the four remedies are not interchangeable. A parent who has read the script can also challenge a plan that does not match it, which is a useful position to be in.

sections.heading: What a transcript tells you and what an IGCSE script tells you
paragraphs: A Collegiate American School family holds a transcript, which is a reliable record of sustained performance across a semester and a genuinely useful thing for a university admissions office. It is also, for diagnostic purposes, nearly opaque. A grade point average is an average of quizzes, projects, participation and tests, weighted by a school policy, and a dip in it can be produced by a missed assessment, a weak project, or a real conceptual gap. From the outside these are indistinguishable.

An IGCSE or Diploma script is the opposite. It is a single performance under fixed conditions, marked against a published scheme question by question, which makes it a poor record of a year's work and an excellent diagnostic instrument. You can see which topic failed, whether method was written, how far the student got before time ran out, and whether the command words were read. The two documents answer different questions and a family holding only the first is missing the second.

This has a practical consequence for any student moving between the systems, which happens often in this part of Dubai. A student with a strong transcript can arrive in Year 10 IGCSE and score poorly on the first mock, not because the content is harder but because nothing in a semester of unit tests requires you to write method out so that method marks are collectable, or to distinguish between describe and explain under time pressure. That is an assessment-literacy gap, it is highly fixable, and it is routinely misread as a drop in ability.

The reverse is also worth knowing. A student with an average transcript can score well on a terminal paper if the content is secure, because continuous assessment punishes a bad fortnight in a way a single examination does not. Neither system is fairer. They measure different things, and a family moving between them should expect the number to move.

sections.heading: Grade movement: what can realistically change in six, twelve and twenty-four weeks
paragraphs: Nobody can promise a grade, and anyone who does is telling you to look elsewhere. What can be described honestly is what kind of change is available over what period, because the four failure patterns move at very different speeds and the timescale is the thing families most often get wrong. A parent starting six weeks before a paper is buying something different from a parent starting two years out, even if the subject and the tutor are identical.

In six weeks, technique moves and content does not. A student can learn to write method out, to allocate time across a paper, and to read command words properly. Those are real, countable marks and they are often the difference between adjacent grades. What cannot happen in six weeks is the secure learning of a topic that was never understood, and a plan claiming otherwise is going to spend the time on a thin pass over too much material.

In twelve weeks, one or two substantial content areas can be rebuilt alongside technique, provided the diagnosis identified them precisely. This is the most productive block length for most students and the one where returned marked work shows the clearest before-and-after. In twenty-four weeks, a genuine subject-wide rebuild is possible, including the algebraic fluency that underpins mathematics and physics and takes months rather than weeks to become automatic.

The honest sixth row of the table below matters as much as the first five. Sometimes a block ends and the component has not moved. That means the diagnosis was wrong, and the correct response is to change the plan rather than to extend it. Families who have been shown marked work throughout can see this coming; families who have been given verbal updates find out at results.

sections.heading: What criterion feedback on an Internal Assessment draft actually looks like
paragraphs: IB Internal Assessments are marked against lettered criteria, each with a published descriptor and a fixed mark allocation. This is unlike anything in an American grading structure and it is the single most useful thing a Diploma family can learn to read, because it converts vague essay advice into a specific instruction. A student told their Internal Assessment needs more analysis has been given nothing. A student told that criterion C scores at the lower band because the data is presented but its uncertainty is never discussed has been given a task.

Legitimate draft feedback therefore has a fixed shape. The tutor reads the draft the student wrote, assigns an honest indicative score against each criterion, quotes the descriptor that justifies it, and asks the questions an examiner would ask: does this graph show what the sentence claims, is this limitation weighed or merely listed, is the research question answerable within the word limit. The student then does the writing. Nothing is inserted, nothing is rewritten, and no sentence in the submitted work belongs to anyone but the student.

The word limit is itself a criterion issue rather than an administrative one, because an over-long piece usually indicates a question too broad to answer rather than a trimming problem. Narrowing a research question early is the highest-value intervention available in the whole Internal Assessment process and costs an hour. Doing it late means discarding collected data, which is why the research question conversation belongs weeks before the drafting one.

Timing follows the school rather than the board. Collegiate American School and every Diploma school in Dubai set internal deadlines ahead of the IB's, and those are the real dates. This page publishes no IB submission or results date, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified deadline on a page a parent plans around is worse than silence. Confirm each one with the school's Diploma coordinator.

sections.heading: The exam calendar, counted backwards from the evidence you need
paragraphs: An evidence-led plan needs fixed points to measure against, and the examination calendar supplies them. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai candidate sits June or November, and a page telling a UAE parent otherwise is handing them a date they cannot use.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are past dates and are cited precisely because a parent can verify them. For a future series, read the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than any restated date, since provisional timetables are revised.

There is one administrative trap worth knowing. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. A parent who downloads a timetable from a search result rather than from the school's exams officer has a real chance of reading someone else's dates.

Counted backwards, the evidence schedule writes itself. A baseline timed paper two terms out. A marked mock, properly diagnosed rather than merely graded, one term out. A re-test six weeks out to confirm the technique work landed. Entry and tier decisions sit months before the papers, so the evidence that informs them has to be generated earlier still.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: the one place the two systems meet formally
paragraphs: A student leaving an American-curriculum school in Dubai for a UAE university needs their certificate equivalated by the Ministry of Education, and the requirements differ by track. For the American track, English proficiency is met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test, to be held before applying. Those are published figures and they are the thresholds a Collegiate American School family should plan against.

For the British track, the published requirement is passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among the five. That five-subject figure is worth stating plainly, because a page currently ranking in this market says six, and a family acting on the wrong number may add a subject and lose the hours it consumes.

No IB points threshold is published in the source behind these figures, so none appears on this page. A Diploma family needing that number should read it on moe.gov.ae or confirm it with the emirate's attestation authority directly rather than accepting a figure from any tutoring site, including this one. The absence is deliberate.

Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs. IB Gram does not perform it, does not guarantee it and cannot accelerate it, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. What tutoring can do is help a student reach a threshold that is published, which for an American-track student usually means SAT Math and English preparation with a measurable baseline and a measurable re-test, which is exactly the shape of the rest of this page.

sections.heading: KHDA, inspection evidence, and what it does and does not tell a parent
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described by the UAE government as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually across six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education.

For a parent reading inspection evidence, the headline band is the least useful part of the report. A school rated Very Good still has a bottom set, and a school rated Acceptable still produces strong individual results. The valuable part is the subject-level and phase-level commentary, which usually names attainment and progress by subject. If the report says attainment in secondary mathematics is below expectations, that is direct evidence about where support is likely to be needed, written by inspectors rather than by a tutoring company.

Two regulatory points sit alongside. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and combined classes strictly prohibited. And a tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit, issued to training institutes. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE centre, and no tutor here is described as KHDA-approved.

Dubai's market context is worth one line, because it explains the pressure families feel. The emirate had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen curricula, with UK provision at 37 per cent of students, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7. A fourteen per cent share means American-curriculum families are a substantial minority rather than the default, which is part of why cross-system advice is so thin on the ground.
