sections.heading: The line between feedback and malpractice
paragraphs: An evidence-led page has to be explicit about this, because the evidence in question is a student's own work and at least one provider competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright. The transaction looks like a shortcut and functions as a risk transfer: the fee is paid once and the academic-honesty finding, if it comes, attaches to the student's record rather than to the seller's.

The legitimate boundary is specific enough to hold any tutor to it. A tutor may teach the content an assessment rests on, explain what each published criterion rewards, assign an indicative criterion score to a draft, quote the descriptor behind it, help narrow a research question until it fits the word limit, confirm a data collection plan is viable, ask the questions an examiner would ask, and teach referencing conventions properly. All of that is teaching and all of it leaves the student as the author.

A tutor may not write, rewrite, restructure or supply any text for submission, choose the research question, provide data the student did not collect, or edit a draft until the sentences are no longer recognisably the student's. A tutor should also not supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; those are linked and cited at source, both because reproducing them is a copyright matter and because unreleased material is a malpractice exposure.

A reasonable test for a parent: if the feedback could be shown to the school's Diploma coordinator without anybody being uncomfortable, it is on the right side of the line. Annotated criterion feedback passes that test easily. A returned draft with new paragraphs in it does not. Ask prospective tutors where their line sits before the first session, and treat a vague answer as the answer.

sections.heading: Availability, and the evidence you should get before paying
paragraphs: No provider in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is worth noticing. Specialist supply is finite, and the combinations most often needed urgently are the scarcest: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level Paper 3, Chemistry Higher Level mechanisms, a less commonly taught Diploma language, IGCSE Computer Science pseudocode to the specification style. A platform that answers every request with an immediate yes is either guessing or sending a generalist.

The position here is that a family is told the realistic timescale and the alternatives instead. Where a UAE-based specialist is not available, the tutor may be based elsewhere and working to Gulf Standard Time, and that is disclosed rather than hidden behind a contact number. It makes no practical difference to an online lesson, but a parent is entitled to know before booking.

Before any money changes hands, there are three documents worth asking any provider for. First, who specifically will teach each session, by name, and whether that person marks the work. Second, what the first session produces: a lesson, or a diagnosis you can read. Third, what happens if the block ends and nothing moved. A provider with good answers to those will have them ready; a provider without them will offer reassurance instead, which is the thing this page started by distrusting.

The free trial lesson exists so that a mismatch costs one hour rather than a term. It is free with no card required and the condition is simply that it is a single session, with the specialist who would actually teach the subject. If the fit is wrong, say so and a different specialist is proposed. If nobody suitable exists for the component, that is said plainly.

process.title: Send the most recent marked work
process.description: Not the report card and not the grade point average. The actual script, test or returned assignment with the marks on it. If the school has not returned one, ask for it; most will. Twenty minutes with a real script tells a tutor more than an hour of conversation about how the student feels about the subject.

process.title: Sit a timed paper under exam conditions
process.description: A past paper from the correct board and syllabus code, timed properly, marked against the published scheme. This is the baseline against which every later claim of progress is measured. Without it, a block of tutoring ends with nothing to compare, and the only available evidence is whether everyone felt it went well.

process.title: Read the written diagnosis before agreeing a plan
process.description: The diagnosis names which of the four failure patterns is present, which topics are affected and which command words are being misread. It does not contain a predicted grade. If the proposed plan does not visibly follow from the diagnosis, ask why before the sessions start rather than after six of them.

process.title: Take the free trial with the specialist who will mark the work
process.description: One session, free, no card required, with the person who would actually teach and mark. A trial with a different tutor from the one assigned tells you nothing useful. Ask during the trial how the student's last script was read, and listen for specifics rather than encouragement.

process.title: Collect the weekly scripts and re-test at the end
process.description: Marked work comes back each week and accumulates. At the end of the block the student sits a fresh unseen paper under the same conditions as the baseline. Either the component moved or it did not, and both answers are useful. If it did not, the plan changes rather than extends.

whyPoints.title: Marked scripts, returned
whyPoints.description: The work is marked by the tutor who taught the session and the script comes back to the family rather than being summarised in a message. A parent can read where the marks went without knowing the subject, because mark schemes allocate marks to identifiable points and a script shows which ones were missed.

whyPoints.title: A diagnosis you can argue with
whyPoints.description: The written diagnosis names components, topics and command words, which means it can be checked against the script and challenged if it does not fit. A plan nobody can argue with is a plan nobody can verify, and that is the normal state of tutoring in this market.

whyPoints.title: No predicted grades
whyPoints.description: Nobody here will tell you what grade your child will get, because nobody knows and the claim would be worth nothing. What is offered instead is a statement of what kind of change is available over what period, which is checkable at the end of the block against a fresh paper.

whyPoints.title: Criterion feedback for Diploma work
whyPoints.description: Internal Assessment and Extended Essay feedback is given criterion by criterion with the published descriptor quoted, which converts general essay advice into a specific task. The student writes every word; the feedback is a set of questions and an honest indicative score.

whyPoints.title: Cross-system translation
whyPoints.description: For families holding an American transcript and facing IGCSE or Diploma assessment, the gap is usually assessment literacy rather than ability. Naming that distinction early prevents a predictable first-mock shock from being read as a drop in capability, which is a common and expensive misreading in this part of Dubai.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and coverage stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. Where a UAE-based specialist is unavailable, the tutor's location is disclosed rather than concealed, and there is no UAE office or centre.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work from my child's Collegiate American School report, or do you need something else?
faqs.answer: A report is useful for trend and almost useless for diagnosis. A grade point average is a weighted average of quizzes, projects, participation and tests, so a dip can be produced by a missed assessment, a weak project or a genuine conceptual gap, and from outside those look identical. What is needed is a piece of marked work with the marks visible: a returned test, an annotated essay or a script. Twenty minutes with that document identifies whether the problem is content, method, timing or command-word reading, which is the information a plan has to be built on.

faqs.question: How will I know whether the tutoring is actually working?
faqs.answer: By comparing two timed papers sat under the same conditions, one at the start of the block and one at the end, and by reading the marked scripts that come back each week in between. That is the whole mechanism. If a provider cannot produce a baseline document and a closing document, there is nothing to compare and the only available evidence is whether everybody felt positive about it. Ask at sign-up what the first paid hour produces and what the last one produces. Those two answers tell you whether you are buying a measurable service or a reassuring one.

faqs.question: My child's grades dropped after moving from the American programme into IGCSE. Is that an ability problem?
faqs.answer: Usually not. It is most often an assessment-literacy gap, and it is predictable enough to plan for. Nothing in a semester of unit tests and projects requires a student to write method out so that method marks can be awarded, to allocate time across a long terminal paper, or to distinguish between describe, explain and evaluate under pressure. All three are needed from the first IGCSE mock. The content is usually fine. The fix is four to six sessions of enforced habit change plus timed practice, and it shows up clearly on a marked paper, which is why the baseline paper matters so much here.

faqs.question: What does criterion feedback on an IB Internal Assessment look like in practice?
faqs.answer: An indicative score against each lettered criterion, the published descriptor that justifies that score, and the questions an examiner would ask about the student's own claims. For example: criterion C sits in the lower band because the data is presented but its uncertainty is never discussed, so what is the uncertainty in that measurement and how does it affect the conclusion. The student then writes the answer. Nothing is inserted into the draft, nothing is rewritten, and no sentence in the submitted work belongs to anyone but the student. A reasonable test is whether the feedback could be shown to the school's coordinator comfortably.

faqs.question: How much can realistically change in six weeks before an exam?
faqs.answer: Technique, not content. In six weeks a student can learn to write working out so method marks are collectable, to allocate time so the last questions are not blank, and to read command words so accurate subject knowledge answers the question printed. Those are countable marks and frequently the gap between adjacent grades. What cannot happen in six weeks is the secure learning of a topic never properly understood. A plan promising a full content rebuild in that window will spread itself thinly across too much material and move nothing. Evidence to ask for is two timed papers, first and last, same conditions.

faqs.question: What if the block ends and nothing has moved?
faqs.answer: Then the diagnosis was wrong, and the right response is to change the plan rather than extend it. This happens, and a family that has been reading marked scripts throughout can usually see it coming by week four rather than discovering it at results. The common causes are a misread failure pattern, a content gap larger than the block length allowed for, or an underlying reading or processing issue that needs the school rather than a subject tutor. Extending an unchanged plan because the sessions feel productive is the single most expensive mistake available in this market.

faqs.question: Does my child need IGCSE at all if they are on the American track in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not for Ministry of Education equivalency on the American track, which is met through SAT and English-proficiency thresholds rather than IGCSE subject counts. The published American-track requirements are at least 450 in SAT Math, and for English either 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section. Some families still take individual IGCSEs privately to strengthen an application to a UK or international university, which is a strategic choice rather than a requirement. Confirm current requirements with the Ministry before planning around either route.

faqs.question: Which SAT thresholds does the UAE Ministry of Education publish for equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the American track, mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test, and that must be held before applying. English proficiency can be met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. The published source for these figures does not mention EmSAT and states no IB points threshold, which is why no IB figure appears on this page. Equivalency is a Ministry process; no tutoring provider performs it, guarantees it or speeds it up, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor support Advanced Placement and IB Higher Level in the same subject?
faqs.answer: Often yes in the sciences and mathematics, where content overlap is substantial, but only if the tutor teaches the two assessment styles as distinct. An Advanced Placement examination and an IB Higher Level paper reward different things: the Diploma paper expects a written reasoning chain and penalises an unjustified answer heavily, and Internal Assessment work has no Advanced Placement equivalent at all. A tutor who treats them as interchangeable will prepare a student well for one and adequately for neither. Ask directly which of the two they have taught to final assessment, and how recently.

faqs.question: Why do you refuse to give a predicted grade?
faqs.answer: Because it would be a guess dressed as information, and because the prediction tends to replace the measurement. Once a family has been told to expect a 6, every later conversation is about whether the 6 is on track rather than about which component is leaking marks. What can be stated honestly is what sort of change is available over a given period, and what the evidence at the end of the block will be. If a provider leads with a grade promise, or promises a specific improvement in writing, that is a commercial claim rather than a professional judgement, and no tutor can honour it.

faqs.question: How do I read my child's KHDA inspection report usefully?
faqs.answer: Skip the headline band and read the subject and phase commentary. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually across six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak, but a band describes a school, not a child, and a strong school still has a weak set in some subject. The useful lines are the ones naming attainment and progress by subject and phase, because those are inspectors' judgements about where students in that school are strong and where they are not. If the report says secondary mathematics attainment is below expectations, that is independent evidence about where support may be needed.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education required at an American-curriculum school in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education must hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. For tutoring, a parent needs to confirm which stream the child sits in first, because the content and expectations are not interchangeable.

faqs.question: Who will actually teach and mark each session?
faqs.answer: One named specialist, who teaches the subject at that level, marks the work personally and returns the script. This is worth confirming in writing with any provider, because a named match at sign-up that quietly becomes a rota is the most common version of this problem in the Dubai market, and it destroys the evidence trail: a different marker each week means the marking is not comparable. Where a UAE-based specialist is unavailable for a component, the tutor may be based elsewhere and working to Gulf Standard Time, and that is disclosed before booking rather than left to be inferred.

faqs.question: Do you deliver sessions at our home in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Lessons for Dubai families are delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For an evidence-led plan this is a practical advantage rather than a compromise, because marked scripts, annotated drafts and timed papers accumulate in one shared place instead of in a folder at home or at school. It also means the tutor is selected for subject and level rather than for willingness to drive through Al Barsha at 4pm, which matters most for the scarcest components.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-collegiate-amer.closingBody: If a grade at Collegiate American School is not where you expected, the fastest useful step costs one hour: a timed past paper from the correct board and syllabus code, marked against the published scheme, and a written diagnosis naming which of the four failure patterns is present. That document tells you whether you are looking at six sessions of technique work or two terms of content rebuilding, and it gives you something to measure the end of the block against. Book the free trial with the specialist who would teach and mark the work, read the diagnosis, and decide from evidence rather than impression.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-deira-internati.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors who most often take IGCSE and IB Diploma work for students at Deira International School and the other Festival City and Mirdif schools. Each one teaches a named subject at a named level rather than covering everything, and each session is booked against a specific paper or assessment component.

intro.heading: Start with the paper, not the subject
paragraphs: A parent at Deira International School rarely needs help with "Maths". They need help with Paper 4 of Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, where the extended-response questions carry method marks the student is not collecting, or with Paper 6 of Chemistry 0620, where an alternative-to-practical answer loses marks for naming a control variable instead of describing how it was kept constant. Those are different problems with different fixes, and a tutor who cannot tell them apart will spend eight weeks re-teaching content the student already knows.

So the opening question on this page is narrow on purpose: which component, which code, which topic. Deira International School runs the IB continuum alongside a British secondary route, which means a single family can be holding a Year 10 IGCSE timetable for one child and an MYP report for another. The two are assessed by completely different machinery. IGCSE grades come from terminal written papers sat in a single series. MYP and IB Diploma grades come from a mix of internally assessed coursework and externally marked examinations, with criterion-referenced descriptors doing the work that a mark scheme does at IGCSE.

This page is built around that distinction. It names the syllabus codes a Deira International School student is likely to be entered for, sets out where the marks actually go in each component, and says what a one-to-one session can change in six weeks versus six months. It also publishes what the Dubai tutoring market charges in AED, because three of the six strongest pages ranking for this search publish no price at all and two quote United States dollars, a currency no UAE family transacts in.

The delivery model is stated once, plainly, and it does not change anywhere on this page. Tutoring for families in Dubai is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. A Festival City family therefore chooses from specialists in a particular subject and level rather than from whoever happens to drive to Al Badia in under twenty-five minutes, and the session time is set by the student's timetable rather than by Al Rebat Street at 5pm.

One more thing is worth saying before the detail. A grade that has slipped is almost never a sign that a student has stopped being able to do the subject. It is usually a sign that one specific thing has gone unaddressed long enough to compound: an algebraic technique that was shaky in Year 9, a habit of answering the question the student expected rather than the one printed, a reading speed that makes the last twenty marks unreachable. Each of those is identifiable from a marked script in under an hour, and each has a different remedy. Guessing costs a term.

What follows is organised the way a diagnostic conversation runs. First the components and codes. Then the tiering decision that quietly sets the grade ceiling. Then the market rate in AED with its source. Then the calendar counted backwards from the June and November series, the regulator, the academic-honesty boundary, and finally what a Deira International School leaver needs for a UAE university.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-deira-internati.programmesIntro: Deira International School families usually need one of three things: MYP support that will matter at Diploma, an IGCSE route through Years 10 and 11, or Diploma Programme work where the Internal Assessment and the final papers are running in parallel. Each is listed with what it actually assesses.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP reports arrive as criterion scores out of eight, grouped under letters: A for knowing and understanding, B for investigating patterns or inquiring, C for communicating, D for applying mathematics or science in real-life contexts. A student can be strong on A and weak on D and still look average overall, which is why a parent reading a single 1-7 summary grade cannot tell what to fix. A tutor starts by separating the criteria.
programmes.countryNote: At Deira International School the MYP sits upstream of both the Diploma and the British route, so MYP Year 9 work is the last point at which a student can change direction cheaply. Dubai parents often discover the gap in the first Diploma term instead, when Maths Analysis and Approaches assumes an algebraic fluency the MYP criterion descriptors never explicitly demanded.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, terminal papers, no coursework in most subjects. A student sits between six and ten subjects, each graded 9-1 or A*-G depending on the syllabus. The grade comes almost entirely from papers written in one series, which makes IGCSE unusually responsive to tutoring: paper technique, timing and command-word reading move marks within weeks because they are the same skills in every question.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai candidates sit the June series as the main window and the November series as the resit route. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and the correct zone timetable must be used; Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. A Festival City family should confirm the school's zone with the exams officer rather than reading a generic timetable online.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The six subject grades total 42 points and the core adds up to three more. The pressure point is rarely the final paper; it is the Internal Assessment deadline landing in the same fortnight as a mock series and an Extended Essay draft.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-deira-internati.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects most often requested by families at Deira International School and neighbouring Festival City, Mirdif and Nadd Al Hamar schools. Each entry says what the assessment actually rewards, because that is where a session earns its fee.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580)
subjects.description: Extended Paper 2 and Paper 4 reward written method. Students who calculate correctly on a calculator and write only the answer lose the method marks that separate a 7 from a 9. The fix is mechanical: set out working in lines, label each step, and show the substitution before the result.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The HL course expects algebraic manipulation to be automatic so that the calculus and proof content has room to breathe. Most Diploma students arriving from MYP can do the calculus and stumble on the algebra inside it. Paper 3 at HL is the extended investigation and is marked on reasoning, not speed.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge IGCSE 0625)
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism produce the widest mark spread. Circuit questions fail when a student cannot read a series-parallel diagram under time pressure. Paper 6 asks for experimental description: sources of error, how a variable was controlled, how a reading was made more reliable. That paper is learnable in four sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge IGCSE 0620)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry are where Extended candidates lose the most, followed by organic reaction pathways. Marks go to the units and the significant figures almost as often as the arithmetic. Qualitative analysis tables are pure recall and are worth drilling because they are free marks for the student who learned them.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge IGCSE 0610)
subjects.description: The command words decide the grade. Describe, explain, compare and suggest demand different answer shapes, and a student who writes a description when asked to explain scores nothing for correct biology. Transport in plants and human physiology diagrams repay drawing practice over reading.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge IGCSE 0500 and 0990)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the composition paper reward register control: audience, purpose and form before content. Reading questions on the summary task are marked on selection, not on fluency, so a student who writes beautifully and selects badly plateaus around a 6.

subjects.name: Economics (IB DP and IGCSE 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries the marks. An axis unlabelled or a shift drawn in the wrong direction costs the point no matter how good the prose is. At HL the evaluation paragraph is a separate skill from the explanation and must be taught as one.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study papers reward application to the stimulus rather than textbook recall. Students quote theory correctly and never touch the company in front of them. Quantitative tools at HL, including break-even and investment appraisal, are marked on method shown.

subjects.name: Computer Science (IGCSE 0478)
subjects.description: Paper 1 is theory and Paper 2 is problem solving with pseudocode and flowcharts. Students who can write Python and cannot write the specification's pseudocode style lose marks for syntax that would run perfectly in an editor. Trace tables are the single highest-yield drill.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, so a tutor must know which stream the student sits in before planning a single lesson.

sections.heading: What an IB IGCSE tutor for Deira International School students actually does
paragraphs: An IB IGCSE tutor for Deira International School students in Dubai teaches one named subject at one named level against a specific assessment component, online and one-to-one. The first session is diagnostic: a past paper or a marked school assessment, read against the published mark scheme, to establish whether the problem is content, method, timing or command-word reading. Those four failures look identical on a report card and need entirely different work.

The reason this matters at Deira International School in particular is that the school runs both the IB continuum and a British secondary pathway. A Year 11 student may be sitting Cambridge IGCSE papers while a sibling two years above is managing Diploma Internal Assessments. A tutor who treats both as "IB tutoring" will apply criterion-referenced feedback to a paper that is marked by a point-based scheme, which wastes sessions. The honest version is that these are two separate skill sets and a family should ask which one a tutor actually holds.

What a session does not do is promise an outcome. No tutor can commit to a grade, and any page that does is telling you something about itself. What a session can commit to is a diagnosis you can read, a plan written against syllabus codes and component weightings, and marked work coming back each week so the parent can see movement or the absence of it. Lessons are delivered online over live video; IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE.

paragraphs: Before any revision plan is useful, a parent needs to know which syllabus the school entered the child for. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both offer International GCSEs in the same subjects with different codes, different paper structures and different tiering rules. A revision guide bought for the wrong board teaches content that will not be examined. The exams officer at the school can confirm every code in one email, and that email is worth more than a term of guesswork.

The table below sets out the codes most often seen in Dubai British-route cohorts, with what each paper actually tests. Note that the science practical is assessed by a written alternative-to-practical paper in most centres, not by a lab examination. That single fact changes how a student should revise: the marks come from describing method, identifying variables and spotting sources of error, which can be practised at a desk.

A tutor working with a Deira International School student should be able to name the paper number and its weighting in the first conversation. If the answer is a general statement about covering the syllabus, the plan has not been built yet. Always read the live official syllabus document on the board's own site rather than relying on a summary, because specifications are revised and a two-year-old PDF is a liability. The same applies to past papers and mark schemes: use the official source, and treat any tutor who offers to send you a folder of board material as a copyright and malpractice risk rather than a convenience. Exactly one syllabus code appears across the entire seven-page Dubai area cluster that competes for these searches, which is the gap this page is filling.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the grade ceiling
paragraphs: In tiered Cambridge IGCSE subjects, the entry tier decides the highest grade available before the student writes a word. Core entry in Mathematics 0580 caps the result at grade 5; Extended entry reaches grade 9 but asks harder questions across the whole paper. Schools make this decision in Year 10 or early Year 11, usually on the evidence of internal assessments, and parents frequently do not realise a decision has been taken until the grade arrives.

This is the single most consequential conversation a Dubai parent can have with a subject teacher, and it is worth having early. A student placed on Core who is genuinely a borderline 5 or 6 has their ceiling lowered for the sake of a safer floor. A student pushed onto Extended who cannot yet handle the algebra may score lower than they would have on Core. Neither error is recoverable once entries are submitted, and entry deadlines sit months before the exam window.

What tutoring changes here is the evidence base. Six weeks of timed Extended papers, marked honestly, tells a family and a teacher more than a predicted grade does. If the student is collecting marks on the Extended paper, the case for Extended entry writes itself. If they are not, the family has made an informed choice rather than a hopeful one. Tiering exists in several Cambridge subjects beyond Mathematics, and the equivalent decision in the separate sciences is which paper route the centre enters the candidate for, so ask about each subject rather than assuming one answer covers the timetable. sections.heading: What IB and IGCSE tutoring costs in the Dubai market
paragraphs: Start from the monthly number, because that is the one a family actually budgets. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 for a mid-market qualified tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are market figures from a published source, not an IB Gram price list.

Hourly, the Dubai market sorts into recognisable bands. EdFlik publishes online rates from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget end. Unitors publishes IGCSE tutoring from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level provision at AED 200 to 450 and above, with in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500. BartyED sits at AED 650 at the examiner-led end. Monthly packages seen in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Two things are worth noticing. First, the in-home premium is largely travel: a tutor crossing Dubai at 4pm can teach three sessions in an evening instead of four or five, and the rate carries that. Second, the cheapest hour is not the cheapest outcome. A student who needs Paper 6 method language fixed and gets generic content revision has bought twelve hours that changed nothing. sections.heading: Online versus a tutor at the door in Festival City
paragraphs: The honest comparison starts by taking home tutoring seriously. A tutor in the room has real advantages: a younger student stays on task more easily, handwriting and working-out are visible without a document camera, and some families simply prefer it. Those are genuine reasons and the market prices them accordingly, at AED 180 to 350 an hour by Bestimate's figures and up to AED 500 from independent home tutors.

What a Festival City family is buying at that premium is mostly travel. The eastern Dubai catchment is spread across Mirdif, Al Warqa, Nadd Al Hamar and Al Qusais, and a tutor who lives in one of them is not a realistic weekday proposition for a family in another. The practical consequence is a narrower choice: not the best Chemistry 0620 teacher available, but the best one who can reach your address by 5pm. For a mainstream subject that may be fine. For IGCSE Computer Science 0478 pseudocode or Diploma Maths Analysis and Approaches HL Paper 3, the local pool may be one person or none.

IB Gram's answer is to drop the travel constraint entirely. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and no page here will tell you otherwise; home visits are an India-only service. sections.heading: The exam calendar counted backwards from the June series
paragraphs: Almost nobody writing about Dubai tutoring mentions an exam session at all, which is strange, because the session is the only fixed point in the year. Everything else is negotiable. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only; a UAE candidate sits June or November, and any page telling a Dubai parent otherwise is giving them a date they cannot act on.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are past dates, cited so a parent can check them. For any future series, read the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than a restated date, because provisional timetables are revised.

Counted backwards, the useful fact is that the final entry deadline sits months before the paper. A tiering decision therefore has to be made while the student still has most of the course left to learn, which is exactly why the diagnostic work belongs in Year 10 rather than the spring of Year 11. For IB Diploma dates, work from the school's internal deadlines: Deira International School sets its own Internal Assessment and Extended Essay dates ahead of the IB's, and those are the ones that govern a student's term.

sections.heading: KHDA, the regulator, and what an inspection band actually tells you
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which the UAE government describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. ADEK is named by none of the competing pages in this market and SPEA by one, which tells you how shallow the regulatory coverage is elsewhere.

An inspection band is a judgement about a school, not about a child. A Very Good school still has a bottom set in Chemistry, and an Acceptable school still produces grade 9s. What the report is genuinely useful for is the subject-level commentary: the inspection text usually names attainment and progress by subject and phase, which tells a parent where the school's own data says students are strong and where they are not. That is the paragraph to read before deciding what to tutor.

Two regulatory facts are worth holding. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, and combined classes strictly prohibited. And a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific licence issued to training institutes. IB Gram does not hold one and does not claim one; no tutor anywhere should be described as KHDA-approved unless that permit can be shown.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may touch and what they may not
paragraphs: This matters more in the Dubai market than it should, because at least one page competing for this search sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is an academic-integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger, and the student carries the consequence, not the seller. The boundary is not subtle and it is worth stating in plain words so a family can hold any tutor to it.

A tutor may teach the subject content an assessment rests on. They may explain the published criteria and what each letter rewards. They may help narrow a research question until it is answerable within the word limit. They may read a draft the student wrote and ask the questions an examiner would ask: is this claim supported, does this graph show what you say it shows, where is the evaluation. They may teach referencing conventions and check that a bibliography is complete. All of that is teaching.

A tutor may not write, rewrite, restructure or supply text for submission. They may not provide a dataset the student did not collect, choose the research question themselves, or edit a draft to the point where the sentences are no longer the student's. They may not supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; those are cited and linked to the official source, not reproduced. Ask any prospective tutor where their line sits before the first session, and be wary of an answer that sounds flexible.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency for a Deira International School leaver
paragraphs: A student finishing the British route at a Dubai school and applying to a UAE university needs their certificate equivalated by the Ministry of Education. The published British-track requirement is specific: proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, plus passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects.

That five-subject count is worth repeating because a page currently ranking in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. It is five, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education, from the Ministry's own clarification. Getting this wrong has a practical cost: a family that believes six are required may push a child into a subject they do not need and lose the revision hours it consumes.

For the American track, English proficiency is met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test. No IB points threshold is published in the source behind these figures, so this page does not state one; a Diploma family should confirm the IB requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs. IB Gram does not perform it, guarantee it, or speed it up, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

faqs.question: How do I find out which exam board my child at Deira International School is entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's exams officer directly and ask for the syllabus codes, not just the board name. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both offer International GCSEs in the same subjects with different paper structures, so a revision guide bought for the wrong board teaches content that will not be examined. Once you have the codes you can read the official specification on the board's own site and check that any tutor's plan matches it. faqs.question: What is the difference between Core and Extended entry in IGCSE Maths?
faqs.answer: The tier decides the grade ceiling before the exam is written. Core entry in Cambridge Mathematics 0580 caps the result at grade 5. Extended entry reaches grade 9 but covers the supplement content and asks longer, less scaffolded questions. Schools normally decide in Year 10 or early Year 11 on internal evidence, and the choice is locked once entries are submitted, which happens months before the papers. Extended is normally expected for progression to A Level or IB Higher Level, so the tier also constrains sixth-form options two years later. Timed papers at both tiers, marked honestly, are the evidence that should drive the decision.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP at Deira International School and the report is hard to read. What do the criteria mean?
faqs.answer: MYP reports give criterion scores out of eight under letters rather than a single mark. Criterion A covers knowing and understanding, B covers investigating patterns or inquiring, C covers communicating, and D covers applying the subject in real-life contexts. A student can be strong on A and weak on D and still average out to a middling summary grade, which is why one number tells a parent almost nothing about what to fix. Ask the subject teacher for the criterion breakdown, then target the weakest letter. Criterion D in maths and science is the one most often neglected and the one that matters most at Diploma.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science paper assesses practical work if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: In most Dubai centres the practical component is assessed by a written alternative-to-practical paper, Paper 6 in the Cambridge sciences, rather than by a laboratory examination. That paper is marked on experimental method: identifying independent and controlled variables, describing how a reading was taken, naming sources of error, and explaining how a result could be made more reliable. All of that can be taught and practised at a desk, which means online delivery costs nothing on this component. Confirm with the school which paper your child is entered for, because a centre running a different route would change the plan entirely.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE tutor cost per hour in Dubai in the current market?
faqs.answer: The market sorts into bands. Budget online provision runs from roughly AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online is around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level provision runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 because travel is priced in. Premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650, as BartyED publishes. These are published market rates read in October 2026, not IB Gram's own price list.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor in Mirdif better value than a specialist online?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what is wrong. If a student needs content re-covered and supervision while they do it, budget provision at AED 45 to 150 an hour may be sufficient and good value. If the problem is that extended-response method marks in Maths 0580 Paper 4 are not being collected, or that Paper 6 answers describe the wrong thing, a generalist will not diagnose it and twelve hours will change nothing. The cheapest hour is not the cheapest outcome. Sit one timed paper, have it marked against the published scheme, and let the diagnosis decide which tier of provision the problem actually needs.

faqs.question: Can sessions start right after the Festival City school run?
faqs.answer: Yes. A 4.30pm start is realistic for families in Festival City and Nadd Al Hamar, where the drive home is short. Mirdif and Al Warqa families more often take a 6pm or 7pm slot, because the afternoon run east is unpredictable and a session that starts late loses its first ten minutes to settling down. Because lessons are online there is no travel on the tutor's side, so a slot can be held at the same time every week and moved at short notice during mock weeks. During Ramadan, sessions can shift to post-Iftar timing without changing tutor.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's IB Internal Assessment at Deira International School?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the subject content the Internal Assessment rests on, explain what each published criterion rewards, help narrow a research question until it is answerable within the word limit, check that a data collection plan is viable, and read a draft the student has written and ask the questions an examiner would ask. What a tutor cannot do is write, rewrite or supply any part of it, choose the research question, or provide data the student did not collect. The work carries the student's name, so the words must be the student's. Any service offering a completed Internal Assessment is exposing the student to a malpractice finding.

faqs.question: Which papers generate the most tutoring requests from Festival City families?
faqs.answer: Mathematics and the separate sciences generate the most requests, and within them the pattern is consistent. In Maths 0580 Extended the losses cluster in algebraic manipulation and in writing out method so the marks are collectable. In Physics 0625 it is electricity and circuit reading. In Chemistry 0620 it is moles and stoichiometry, followed by organic pathways. In Biology 0610 the problem is usually command words rather than content: describe, explain and suggest demand different answer shapes. English First Language plateaus around a grade 6 when a student writes fluently but selects badly for the summary task.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE exams actually held for a student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. UAE candidates sit those two; the February and March series is offered to India only, so any Dubai page quoting a March window is giving you a date you cannot act on. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and the correct zone timetable must be used, with Cambridge stating it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. Confirm your school's zone with the exams officer.

faqs.question: Does my child need a permit check before hiring a private tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education required alongside the British curriculum in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic must hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. For tutoring, this means a parent has to know which stream the child sits in, because the two streams are not interchangeable and the content is set by the Ministry.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes will a Deira International School leaver need for MoE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. The published requirement for the British track is passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects. One page currently ranking in this market states six are required, which is wrong and has a practical cost if a family adds a subject they do not need. Verify against the Ministry before making an entry decision.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is available for the component we need?
faqs.answer: You are told, with the timescale and the options, rather than matched to a generalist who will be learning the specification alongside the student. Niche components are where this happens: Computer Science 0478 pseudocode to the specification style, Maths Analysis and Approaches HL Paper 3, a less commonly taught language. The free trial lesson exists for exactly this reason, so that an unsuitable match costs one hour rather than a term. If a specialist becomes free later, the conversation reopens. A platform that always says yes immediately is either guessing or sending someone who does not teach that level.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-deira-internati.closingHeading: Start with the paper that is costing the marks
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-deira-internati.closingBody: If your child is at Deira International School and the grade is not where it should be, the useful first step is narrow: name the subject, the syllabus code and the paper, then sit one timed past paper and have it marked against the published scheme. That single piece of evidence tells you whether you are looking at a content gap, a method problem, a timing problem or a command-word problem, and those need four different plans. Book the free trial lesson with a specialist in that component, read the written diagnosis, and decide from there. Lessons run one-to-one online in Gulf Standard Time, and the marked work comes back to you each week.

intro.heading: A transcript and a 45-point score are not the same measurement
paragraphs: Dubai American Academy runs an American high-school programme with the International Baccalaureate Diploma available alongside it, which means many households here are tracking two assessment systems in parallel. One produces a transcript: course grades accumulated semester by semester, weighted into a grade point average, with Advanced Placement examinations sitting on top as separate single-subject results scored from one to five. The other produces a single number out of 45, built from six subject grades of one to seven plus up to three bonus points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix.

Those two machines reward different behaviour, and that is the practical point rather than a philosophical one. A grade point average rewards consistency across every semester: a weak month in a single course leaves a permanent mark on the transcript, because grades accumulate rather than being superseded. The IB Diploma rewards performance at the end: a weak term in Year 12 is largely invisible if the final papers and internal assessments go well. A student who is strong but erratic does better in the second system; one who is steady but peaks poorly under examination pressure does better in the first.

That difference should shape where tutoring goes. On the American track the highest-value intervention is often early and preventive, because a semester grade once recorded cannot be improved, only averaged down by the next one. On the IB track the highest-value intervention is usually a component with a published weighting, because the final score is assembled from identifiable pieces and the untimed criteria-marked ones move fastest. Families routinely apply the logic of one system to the other and wonder why the hours produced less than expected.

IB Gram supports Dubai American Academy families with one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time. It does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service that exists only in India, and that statement appears on every country page this site publishes. Dubai's in-home market publishes roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, read in October 2026. For a course-specific problem, the question that matters is whether the tutor has taught that course, which is narrower than who will drive to Al Barsha.

Two cautions. No IB session or results date appears here, because none could be verified from the International Baccalaureate's own site for this project; Diploma candidates in the UAE sit the May session and dates should come from the school. And the equivalency figures below are quoted only where a published source exists: the American-track and British-track numbers are sourced, and no IB points threshold is published anywhere this project could verify, so none appears.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-dubai-american-.programmesIntro: Four tracks a household at this school might be managing. Each is assessed differently enough that a tutor matched to the wrong one will teach the right content in the wrong shape.

programmes.name: American high-school diploma courses
programmes.description: Credit-bearing courses graded per semester and accumulated into a transcript with a weighted grade point average. Assessment is continuous: tests, projects, participation and finals, with the balance set by the course rather than by an external board.
programmes.countryNote: Because grades accumulate, the cheapest and most effective tutoring on this track is early and preventive within a semester, not remedial after it. A grade once recorded stays on the transcript, so the useful question in week four of a semester is not whether the student is struggling but whether anything is drifting.

programmes.name: Advanced Placement examinations
programmes.description: Single-subject external examinations scored from one to five, sat in May, independent of the transcript grade for the same course. A student can hold a strong course grade and a weak examination score, or the reverse, because the two measure different things.
programmes.countryNote: That independence is the planning fact families miss. Preparation for the examination is a separate activity from doing well in the class, and it is largely a question of past-paper technique and the specific rubric of the free-response sections. A short targeted block before May is usually better value than a year of general support.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher and three Standard, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, scored out of 45 with 24 as the diploma minimum. Internal assessment carries real weight in every subject, typically twenty to thirty per cent.
programmes.countryNote: A student arriving from an American middle school has usually never been marked against published criteria or written an independent research piece to a word cap. Those are the gaps, not content. The first term of support should therefore be weighted towards criteria and research process rather than towards subject coverage.

programmes.name: IGCSE, for students crossing from a British school
programmes.description: Terminal written papers with tiering into Core and Extended on Cambridge or Foundation and Higher on Pearson Edexcel, and a board-dependent practical arrangement in the sciences. A different system again from both the transcript and the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum at thirty-seven per cent of enrolment and American at fourteen, so crossings between the two are common. A student moving from IGCSE into an American high school meets continuous assessment for the first time and often underestimates how much a weak early semester costs.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches

sections.heading: Advanced Placement and the IB Diploma, compared assessment by assessment
paragraphs: The comparison usually happens on reputation and should happen on structure. Advanced Placement is a set of independent single-subject examinations, sat in May and scored from one to five, with no compulsory core and no requirement to take a particular combination. A student takes as many as they wish, in whatever mix suits them, and each result stands alone. The IB Diploma is a package: six subjects across six groups, three Higher and three Standard, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, assembled into one score out of 45 with 24 as the minimum for the award.

That structural difference produces three practical consequences. First, flexibility. A student with one very strong area and several weak ones can take three Advanced Placement examinations in that area and nothing else; the Diploma requires breadth by design. Second, the core. Advanced Placement has no equivalent of an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge course or a CAS requirement, which means it generates far fewer internally set deadlines and demands much less project management. Third, internal assessment: Diploma subjects carry it, typically at twenty to thirty per cent, so a portion of every grade is produced away from the examination hall.

For tutoring this means the work differs rather than the difficulty. Advanced Placement preparation is almost entirely external-examination technique: past papers, the free-response rubric, pacing, and the recognition that a strong course grade does not predict a strong score because the two measure different things. Diploma support is split across timed papers and criteria-marked internal assessment, and the second usually offers faster returns because the criteria are published and there is no clock.

Neither route is harder. A student who misses deadlines will find the Diploma core punishing in a way that no amount of subject tutoring repairs, and that is the strongest single signal against it. A student who needs breadth imposed on them, or who wants the single score and the core on a university application, has a strong argument for it. The table sets the structures side by side so the choice can be made on something checkable.

sections.heading: Grade point average and 45 points: two different machines
paragraphs: A grade point average is cumulative. Semester grades are recorded, weighted and averaged, and once a semester closes its grade is permanent: it can be diluted by later semesters but never replaced. That gives the transcript a particular property that families underestimate. The cost of a bad month in Grade 10 is not that term's report; it is a small permanent reduction in the number a university eventually reads, and the only remedy is a larger volume of good semesters afterwards.

An IB score is assembled at the end. Six subject grades of one to seven, produced by a mix of timed papers and internal assessment, plus up to three bonus points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix, totalling a maximum of 45 with 24 required for the award. Nothing about a weak term in the first Diploma year appears in that number, provided the final components go well. The system is forgiving of a bad patch and unforgiving of a bad fortnight in May.

The behavioural implication runs in both directions. On the transcript track the discipline that pays is consistency: homework submitted, tests prepared for, nothing drifting for three weeks unnoticed. On the Diploma track the discipline that pays is deadline management on internal assessment plus examination performance at the end. Students are rarely equally good at both, and knowing which one your child is better at is more useful than any comparison of the two systems' prestige.

Where tutoring fits therefore differs. On the transcript, support bought in week two of a semester prevents a grade from being set; support bought in week twelve can only influence the final assessment of a grade that is largely already determined. On the Diploma, support can usefully arrive later, because the components that produce the score are still ahead. Families routinely buy transcript support late and Diploma support early, which is precisely backwards.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency on the American track
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process by which a school certificate earned on an international curriculum is recognised in the UAE, and it is absent from most of this search result: four of the ten query clusters researched for this market contain no mention of it, and one page that does mention it publishes an incorrect figure. For a family on the American track it matters because the requirements are different in kind from the British ones, and they involve test scores rather than a subject count.

On the American track the sourced position is specific. English proficiency is shown through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. That is a testing requirement, and it means a student can hold a perfectly respectable transcript and still have a documentation gap if no qualifying test score exists. The article this was read from names no EmSAT requirement and states no IB points threshold.

By contrast the British track is a subject count: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education specifically excluded from those five, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor states six IGCSE subjects. Five is what the published clarification reported.

For the IB there is no figure on this page, deliberately. No official source for an IB points threshold could be verified for this project, and publishing an invented number would be worse than publishing nothing because a family might plan around it. Two things follow. Describe the process, cite the authority, and go to the Ministry of Education's own channel for your own case. And treat any claim that tutoring is required for equivalency as a false-urgency pitch about a regulatory process; it is a documentation matter, not an academic hurdle a tutor clears.

sections.heading: Moving from an American middle school into the IB Diploma
paragraphs: A student making this move inside one school changes assessment system without changing building, which is exactly why it gets under-planned. The content overlap is usually reasonable; what is missing is specific and consistent. Three things: being marked against published criteria rather than a teacher's rubric, producing an independent research piece to a hard word cap, and sitting long papers in which a full subject's worth of material can appear in any order.

The criteria point is the one that bites first. A Diploma internal assessment is marked against named criteria with published descriptors, and a student used to a classroom rubric often writes something good that satisfies none of them. In the sciences the investigation is capped at 3,000 words and marked out of twenty-four across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each. Research design covers the question and the controlled variables, and it cannot be repaired once the data has been collected, which makes a planning session before any practical work the single highest-value hour available.

The independent research point follows. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words, the Theory of Knowledge essay 1,600 and the exhibition commentary 950. For a student whose longest previous piece was a class paper of a few pages, the step is in project management rather than writing ability: choosing a question the available sources can actually support, keeping a process record, and working to internally set deadlines that arrive in clusters in the autumn of the final year.

The examination point is the slowest to fix and the easiest to start on. Diploma papers are longer than most high-school finals, draw on a whole course rather than a unit, and reward sustained multi-step explanation. Timed sections from the first term, marked against the official scheme with losses attributed to causes rather than topics, closes that gap faster than additional content teaching. For a student coming from a continuous-assessment background it is the most important single piece of preparation.

sections.heading: Where standardised-test preparation actually fits
paragraphs: SAT preparation sits oddly in a tutoring plan because it is not a subject. It is a set of techniques: recognising question types quickly, pacing across a timed section, deciding what to skip, and handling an adaptive format where the test responds to performance. Those are learnable and they are separate from coursework ability. A student with strong mathematics grades can lose points to pacing, and a student with modest grades can gain points from technique alone.

It also has a second relevance in the UAE that families outside the region do not have to think about. The sourced equivalency requirements on the American track cite at least 450 in the SAT Math test, and allow 450 in the reading and writing section as one of three routes to the English requirement alongside IELTS 5 and TOEFL iBT 61. That makes a qualifying score a documentation matter as well as an admissions one, and it is worth checking early rather than in the final semester of Grade 12.

On timing, the practical constraint in this catchment is a full-length sitting. Practice has to include complete timed papers, and a three-hour sitting after a Dubai afternoon commute measures fatigue rather than ability. Weekend mornings are the right home for them for almost every community on this page except those immediately around the school. Midweek sessions then handle technique, review and question-type work, which are short-format activities that survive a late arrival.

One thing this page will not do is promise a score. No tutor can guarantee a specific result on any examination, and anybody who offers a target score as a commitment is making a claim they cannot support. What is honest is that technique and pacing are teachable, that practice under genuine timing produces the only reliable evidence of where points are going, and that a block of focused work before a sitting is better value than a year of general support.

sections.heading: Materials, authorship and what a tutor should refuse
paragraphs: Subject guides, specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge, Pearson and the examination bodies that publish them. A provider distributing them as downloads is reproducing copyrighted material, and for unreleased papers it is a malpractice exposure as well. Reference and link so that a parent reads the authoritative document rather than somebody's summary of it. Everything factual on this page should be confirmed that way through the school.

On assessed work the line is authorship and it is not a matter of degree. A tutor may teach content, explain each criterion in the board's published wording, show how a comparable piece is built, read a draft the student has written and name which criterion it misses, and teach them to fix it themselves. A tutor may not write the internal assessment, draft the Extended Essay, or edit a piece to completion so that the words become theirs. On the transcript track the same applies to coursework, projects and lab reports that carry a grade.

A page in this search result sells completed internal assessment work at a fixed price. Submitting work that is not the candidate's own is malpractice under the board's rules, and the consequence lands on the student's qualification rather than the seller's business. A useful test for anybody offering coursework help is to ask what they would do if your child requested one written paragraph. A refusal with a description of the alternative is the right answer.

On permits, the relevant fact is that the cost is zero. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service with a stated two working days to complete. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's school.

sections.heading: Getting started, and the position of this site
paragraphs: Three pieces of information make a sensible start possible, and all are free. Which track the problem sits on: a transcript course, an Advanced Placement examination, or an IB Diploma subject. For the Diploma, the level and which component is carrying the lowest marks. And for a transcript course, how the semester grade is composed, because the balance between tests, projects and finals varies by course and determines whether intervention now can still change anything.

Then test the tutor on the track rather than the subject. Ask what the free-response rubric rewards in an Advanced Placement paper, or which Diploma investigation criterion cannot be repaired after data collection, or how a semester grade is weighted in the course your child is taking. A specialist answers in a sentence. Somebody whose experience sits in a different system will answer in general terms, which is itself the information.

Run the trial lesson in the slot you actually intend to use rather than a convenient demonstration hour, because a Dubai afternoon commute is the real constraint on whether an arrangement survives a term. Then insist on a diagnostic in the first fortnight — a timed paper or a marked draft, returned with losses attributed by cause — and a written risk list reviewed monthly with the marked work attached.

And position, stated plainly. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International, Pearson, the College Board, the Ministry of Education, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge, the Sharjah Private Education Authority or the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It holds no such relationship, claims none, operates no premises in the UAE, has no arrangement with any school named on this page, publishes no star rating, promises no examination score, and quotes no statistic without its source and date.

process.description: A transcript course, an Advanced Placement examination, or an IB Diploma subject. They are assessed so differently that a tutor matched to the wrong track will teach the right content in the wrong shape, and naming it removes two sessions of discovery from the start.

process.title: For a transcript course, ask how the grade is composed
process.description: The balance between tests, projects, participation and finals varies by course and determines whether intervention now can still change anything. A semester already two-thirds assessed is largely set, and that is worth knowing before buying twelve weeks of support for it.

process.title: Buy transcript support early and AP support in a block
process.description: A recorded semester grade cannot be improved, only averaged, so preventive support in weeks one to four is where the value is. An Advanced Placement score is independent of the course grade, so a six to eight week block of past-paper work before May is better value than a year of general help.

process.title: Test the tutor on the track, not the subject
process.description: Ask what the free-response rubric rewards, or which Diploma investigation criterion cannot be repaired after data collection, or how the semester grade is weighted. A specialist answers in a sentence; an answer in general terms tells you their experience sits in a different system.

process.title: Check the equivalency documentation early
process.description: The American track cites at least 450 in SAT Math and English through IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT reading and writing 450. A strong transcript with no qualifying test score is a documentation gap. Verify your own case through the Ministry of Education's own channel rather than any tutoring site.

process.title: Keep full-length practice at the weekend
process.description: A three-hour sitting after a Dubai afternoon commute measures fatigue rather than ability. Midweek sessions handle technique, review and question-type work; weekend mornings carry the full timed papers that produce the only reliable evidence of where points are going.

whyPoints.title: Two measurement systems explained as different machines
whyPoints.description: A grade point average accumulates and cannot be unwound; an IB score is assembled at the end from identifiable components. That single difference decides when tutoring should arrive, and most families get it backwards by buying transcript support late and Diploma support early.

whyPoints.title: AP and IB compared on structure
whyPoints.description: Independent single-subject examinations against a package with a compulsory core and internal assessment in every subject. Neither is harder; they suit different students, and a student who misses deadlines will find the Diploma core punishing in a way subject tutoring cannot fix.

whyPoints.title: The American-track equivalency rules published
whyPoints.description: SAT Math 450, and English via IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT reading and writing 450. A respectable transcript with no qualifying test score is a documentation gap, and four of the ten query clusters researched for this market do not mention equivalency at all.

whyPoints.title: The crossing into the Diploma named precisely
whyPoints.description: Published criteria instead of a classroom rubric, an independent research piece to a hard word cap, and long papers drawing on a whole course. Those are the three gaps, and research design in the sciences investigation cannot be repaired once data has been collected.
