whyPoints.description: Technique and pacing are teachable and practice under genuine timing produces real evidence, but no tutor can guarantee a specific result on any examination. Anybody offering a target score as a commitment is making a claim they cannot support.

faqs.question: How does a grade point average differ from an IB score out of 45?
faqs.answer: A grade point average accumulates: semester grades are recorded, weighted and averaged, and once a semester closes its grade is permanent and can only be diluted by later ones. An IB score is assembled at the end from six subject grades of one to seven plus up to three core points, with 24 the minimum for the diploma. The transcript rewards consistency across years; the Diploma rewards end performance plus deadline management on internal assessment.

faqs.question: Does a strong class grade predict a strong Advanced Placement score?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, because the two measure different things. The Advanced Placement score comes from a single external examination in May, reported from one to five, and is independent of the transcript grade for the same course. A student can hold a strong course grade and a weak score, or the reverse. Preparation for the examination is a separate activity from doing well in class, centred on past papers and the free-response rubric rather than on classroom study.

faqs.question: Does a tutor visit homes in Al Barsha?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service that exists only in India. Lessons are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Dubai's in-home market publishes roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, read in October 2026. For a course-specific problem the relevant question is whether the tutor has taught that course.

faqs.question: When is the best time to buy support for a transcript course?
faqs.answer: Weeks one to four of a semester, before a grade is substantially set. Because semester grades accumulate and cannot be improved once recorded, the value here is preventive rather than remedial: a bad month in Grade 10 produces a small permanent reduction in the number a university eventually reads. Support bought in week twelve can only influence whatever assessment remains, which is usually a minority of the grade.

faqs.question: What do UAE equivalency rules require on the American track?
faqs.answer: The sourced position cites English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. That is a testing requirement rather than a subject count, so a strong transcript with no qualifying test score is a documentation gap. Verify your own case through the Ministry of Education's own channel.

faqs.question: Where can a Dubai American Academy family get the IB equivalency threshold?
faqs.answer: Because no official source for one could be verified for this project. The published clarification that was read states requirements for the British and American tracks and names no IB points threshold, and the International Baccalaureate's own site returns an error to automated checking. Publishing an invented figure would be worse than publishing nothing, because a family might plan around it. One competitor page already publishes an incorrect IGCSE subject count.

faqs.question: What does a student from an American middle school find hardest in the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Three things, and none is content. Being marked against published criteria with named descriptors rather than a classroom rubric, so good work can satisfy none of them. Producing an independent research piece to a hard word cap, which is project management rather than writing ability. And sitting long papers drawing on a whole course in any order, which rewards sustained multi-step explanation and is the slowest of the three to fix.

faqs.question: Which IB internal assessment criterion is most urgent?
faqs.answer: Research design in the sciences investigation, because it is the only one of the four that cannot be repaired once the data has been collected. It covers the research question, the controlled variables and whether enough data was planned. The investigation is capped at 3,000 words and marked out of twenty-four, with research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation each carrying six marks. A planning session before any practical work is the highest-value hour in the subject.

faqs.question: Is Advanced Placement or the IB Diploma better for a Dubai American Academy student?
faqs.answer: Neither is harder; they suit different students. Advanced Placement lets a student concentrate on their strongest area with no breadth requirement and no core, and each result stands alone. The Diploma requires six subjects, an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, and produces one number out of 45. A student who misses deadlines will find the Diploma core punishing in a way that subject tutoring cannot repair, and that is the strongest single signal.

faqs.question: Where does SAT preparation belong in a tutoring plan?
faqs.answer: As a separate block rather than inside subject support, because it is technique rather than content: question-type recognition, pacing, strategic omission and handling the format. It has a second relevance in the UAE, since the sourced equivalency requirements cite at least 450 in SAT Math and allow 450 in reading and writing as one route to the English requirement. Full-length timed practice belongs at the weekend, not after a Dubai afternoon commute.

faqs.question: Can a tutor guarantee an Advanced Placement or SAT score?
faqs.answer: No, and anybody offering a target score as a commitment is making a claim they cannot support. What is honest is that technique and pacing are teachable, that practice under genuine timing is the only reliable way to find where points are going, and that a focused block before a sitting generally produces more than a year of unfocused support. Ask for the baseline from a full timed paper and the comparison after four weeks instead of a promise.

faqs.question: How many full practice papers should my child sit before May?
faqs.answer: Fewer than families imagine, used properly. One paper sat under genuine timing, marked against the published rubric and analysed for where points went is worth more than several worked through casually, because the casual version produces familiarity rather than improvement. In the final six to eight weeks, one full timed paper a week with the losses compared against the previous week is a realistic and effective pattern, with nothing new added in the last fortnight.

faqs.question: My child is moving from an IGCSE school into an American high school. What changes?
faqs.answer: Continuous assessment, for the first time. At IGCSE almost everything is decided by terminal papers, so a weak autumn can be recovered. On a transcript, grades accumulate from week three of every semester and a recorded grade is permanent. Students from a British background routinely underestimate how much an early weak semester costs, because nothing in their previous system behaved that way. Preventive support from the start of a semester is the appropriate response.

faqs.question: Do tutors working with Dubai students need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it costs nothing. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service with a stated two working days to complete. Eligible applicants include school-registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one brings fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-dubai-american-.closingHeading: Name the track, then pick the moment
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-dubai-american-.closingBody: For a Dubai American Academy family the useful first step is naming which measurement is in play. A transcript course, where grades accumulate and support belongs in week two rather than week twelve. An Advanced Placement examination, where the score is independent of the class grade and a block before May is the efficient purchase. Or an IB Diploma subject, where a named component with a published weighting is the target. Then test the tutor on that track specifically and insist on a diagnostic in the first fortnight. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Price the two years, because that is what you are buying
paragraphs: An IGCSE course is two years long and most tutoring decisions are made as though the commitment were a term. A family agrees a weekly session in the spring of Year 10 because a mock went badly, and twenty-two months later they have spent a sum nobody projected, in a pattern nobody chose. The arithmetic is not complicated and almost nobody does it before starting, which is the single most expensive habit in this market.

Here is the projection, using published market figures. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimate for one weekly hour with a mid-market qualified tutor is AED 600 to 1,200 a month. Sustained across two academic years, allowing for holidays, that is roughly AED 12,000 to 24,000 for one subject. Two subjects doubles it. Add an exam-term intensive in the final spring at the specialist band of AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more a month and the total moves again.

A fixed budget allocated deliberately across those two years buys far more than the same money spent reactively. The principle is unglamorous: spend early on habits, spend little in the middle, and reserve a block for the final term. Habits such as writing method out and reading command words precisely are cheap to install in Year 10 and expensive in Year 11, because by then they compete with revision for the same hours. Reserving money for the final term matters because that is when a specific, diagnosed need usually appears.

The second thing to get right before spending anything is the difference between an advertised rate and an effective one. A package at AED 799 for eight online sessions is advertised as a monthly figure and works out at roughly AED 100 an hour, which places it in the budget band however it is described. A rate of AED 180 an hour with sessions regularly lost to traffic and billed has an effective rate well above AED 180. Both numbers are honest; only one of them is the price.

Dubai British School families in Jumeirah Park sit in a part of the city where in-home arrangements are workable but journeys are long enough to matter. That bears directly on the effective rate, because a session billed and lost is the most common leak in a two-year plan and it happens where drives are long. Removing the journey removes the leak, which is worth more over two years than a discount on the hourly rate.

Delivery, stated once: tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every AED figure below belongs to whoever published it, read in October 2026, and none is an IB Gram price list.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3, Years 7 to 9

programmes.countryNote: A cheaper alternative to weekly sessions for a Dubai family at this stage is one timed paper a term from the board the student will eventually sit, marked honestly against the published scheme. programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Eight or nine subjects over two years with grades coming from terminal papers marked against a published scheme. This is where the main commitment sits, and the budget question is as much about allocation across the four terms as it is about which subject or which rate.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-dubai-british-s.subjectsIntro: Where the two-year money goes, and in which phase each subject is cheapest to support. These are the courses most often requested across Jumeirah Park and the surrounding communities.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580)
subjects.description: Cheapest to support in Year 10, when the method habit can be installed before revision competes for the hours. The commonest loss is correct answers with unwritten working, which costs real marks and is a habit rather than a knowledge gap. Tier choice is worth two timed papers on its own.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Pearson Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Same content territory, different paper structure and tier names from Cambridge, so revision material has to match the code the school entered. A family working from the wrong board's past papers is spending money on content that will not be examined in that form.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge IGCSE 0625)
subjects.description: Electricity and circuit reading generate the widest mark spread, and the alternative-to-practical paper rewards a specific vocabulary of method and error. Both respond to short blocks, which makes this a subject to buy in focused bursts rather than weekly for two years.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge IGCSE 0620)
subjects.description: Quantitative work is where paid hours earn their cost: moles, stoichiometry, units and significant figures. Qualitative test recall is memorisation the student can do alone, and paying an hourly rate to supervise it is the clearest waste available in the subject.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge IGCSE 0610)
subjects.description: Command-word discipline is the usual failure and three to five sessions settles it, which makes this a cheap subject to fix and an expensive one to tutor continuously. The content volume is learning the student must supply themselves.

subjects.name: English Language (IGCSE 0500 and 0990)
subjects.description: A short block on the summary task and directed writing is good value, because marks there go to selection and register rather than fluency. Long weekly arrangements are poor value, since composition improves with reading and writing volume rather than discussion.

subjects.name: Computer Science (IGCSE 0478)
subjects.description: Under-tutored relative to how well it responds. Pseudocode to the specification style and trace tables are narrow and learnable, and students who write good working code routinely lose marks by answering in it. Four sessions can be transformative here.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Case-study recall is the student's own work; data-response and source technique are teachable. Buy the technique in a short block before mocks, and leave the recall to revision, which is the split most families get the wrong way round.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, case-study application and the evaluation paragraph each carry their own marks and each is teachable in a focused block. Content coverage at an hourly rate is the expensive way to do something a textbook does adequately.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because expectations and the language of instruction differ. Responds to frequency rather than length; confirm the stream before buying.

sections.heading: Allocating a fixed budget across two IGCSE years
paragraphs: Suppose a family decides it can spend a fixed amount on tutoring across Years 10 and 11. The default pattern is to spend it as the anxiety arrives, which means roughly nothing in the first year and everything in the last two terms. That ordering is close to the worst available, because the cheapest work is the early work and the most expensive is the late work, and spending reactively guarantees paying the higher price.

A deliberate allocation inverts it. Roughly a quarter of the budget goes to a habit block early in Year 10, when method and command-word discipline can be installed in six to eight sessions. Very little goes to the middle terms, which are covered by one timed paper a term rather than a weekly slot. The remaining half is held in reserve for Year 11, released only against a diagnosed need, with a final block in the spring for technique and timing.

The reason the middle terms can be left largely alone is that the school is teaching the course. Weekly tutoring through a period when nothing specific is failing is supervision, and it consumes a budget that would be more useful later. The termly paper is what makes this safe rather than negligent: it catches a new problem while it is still small, at the cost of one hour rather than a term of sessions.

The table below sets the allocation out term by term. It is a shape rather than a prescription, and a student with a genuine content gap in Year 10 should obviously have it addressed then. But the default of spending nothing early and everything late is a pattern worth breaking deliberately, because it is produced by how worry accumulates rather than by anything about how learning works.

sections.heading: Advertised rate against effective rate
paragraphs: Every provider quotes an advertised rate and a family pays an effective one, and the gap between them is where two-year plans go wrong. The effective rate is the total paid divided by the hours of teaching actually received. Three things drive them apart: packaging, sessions billed but not taught, and work that is charged separately or simply not done.

Packaging usually works in the family's favour and should still be checked. AED 799 for eight online sessions is an advertised monthly figure with an effective rate of roughly AED 100 an hour, which places it in the budget band however the package is described. AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions is roughly AED 200 to 225 an hour including travel. Neither is deceptive. Both need dividing out before comparison.

Lost sessions work the other way. A session billed because a tutor was stuck in traffic, or because a family cancelled inside a notice period, is money paid for no teaching, and it raises the effective rate directly. Over two years, one lost session a month at AED 200 is AED 4,000. This is the largest avoidable leak in a long plan and it is entirely a function of the terms agreed at the start.

The third driver is marking. Marking a full past paper properly against the published scheme takes time, and if it is charged separately the advertised rate understates the cost, while if it is not done at all the plan has no evidence base. Ask which it is. The table below sets out the arithmetic on each.

sections.heading: Commitment terms over two years, and the leaks they create
paragraphs: Over a two-year arrangement, contractual terms matter more than the hourly rate, and they are rarely on a pricing page. Four questions cover most of the exposure: what is the notice period, what happens to a session cancelled inside it, does the slot persist through school holidays and mock weeks, and what happens if the tutor becomes unavailable mid-course.

The notice period is the first leak. A four-week notice period on a weekly arrangement means a family deciding in the first week of a month to stop is paying for four more sessions they have already concluded are not working. Over two years with one change of plan, that is a month of fees for nothing. A block with a defined end has no notice period, which is a practical reason to prefer blocks over standing arrangements.

Holidays and mock weeks are the second. A standing slot that runs through the school's own mock series competes with the thing it is meant to support, and a slot billed through a three-week school holiday when the family is abroad is pure leakage. Both are avoidable by agreeing in advance that the arrangement pauses, which online delivery makes costless because no journey has been committed.

The third and largest is tutor continuity. If the person teaching changes mid-course, the new tutor spends several sessions learning the student and the specification, which is money for no teaching and a break in the evidence trail. Ask who teaches each session by name, and what happens if they leave. A named match that quietly becomes a rota is the commonest version of this problem in Dubai and the hardest to see from an invoice.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home visit from Jumeirah Park
paragraphs: In-home tutoring has genuine merits and the western communities have a reasonable local market. A tutor in the room holds a younger or more distractible student's attention more easily, written working is visible without a camera, and some families prefer it as a preference rather than an argument. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500.

From Jumeirah Park the complication is the drive. The communities west of Al Khail Road are spread out and the afternoon run from the better-supplied areas is long, which has two effects on a two-year plan. The advertised rate carries the tutor's lost capacity, and the effective rate carries the sessions that go wrong. A tutor delayed in traffic once a month over two years is a material number, and it is the leak that most often ends arrangements badly.

The second effect is the shortlist. Even where the local market is reasonable for mainstream subjects, it thins at the top of a subject: A Level Further Mathematics, IGCSE Computer Science pseudocode to the specification style, Higher Level Paper 3 investigation work. For those, the question is not the rate but whether anybody within range teaches it at all.

IB Gram's position does not depend on how that comparison falls. Lessons are delivered one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and nothing on this page suggests otherwise; home visits are a service offered only in India. Over two years the gain is mostly cost certainty rather than a lower headline rate.

sections.heading: The resit decision, and what a second series costs
paragraphs: A two-year budget should account for the possibility of a resit, because it is a real cost and it is better anticipated than discovered. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with the November series functioning as the resit route for UAE candidates. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai family should disregard any page quoting it.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Verifiable dates: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are past and checkable; for any future series, read the live official timetable on the board's own site.

The cost of a resit is an entry fee plus a term of preparation plus, usually, a block of tutoring at the point in the year when a student is also starting sixth form. That combination is what makes it expensive out of proportion to the single grade involved. It is also why the tier decision in Year 10 matters so much: an entry made at the wrong tier is the commonest route to a resit, and the decision is taken months before the papers.

One administrative risk dwarfs all of this. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. A missed paper means a full resit for no academic reason at all. Get the zone in writing from the exams officer.

sections.heading: School fees, tutoring and the context nobody mentions
paragraphs: Tutoring is the discretionary part of a Dubai family's education budget, and it is worth placing against the part that is not. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. The largest education line in the household budget is therefore flat.

The market around those families keeps growing. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. In 2024-25 the emirate had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula, with UK provision at 37 per cent of students, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7.

Two consequences follow for a tutoring budget. More schools and more students means more competition for the same specialist tutors in the 4pm to 6pm weekday window, which is a supply story rather than a quality one and argues for booking a slot early in the year rather than in the mock term. And a flat fee environment means the tutoring line is the one that moves, which is a reason to plan it rather than let it accumulate.

None of this is a reason to spend more. It is a reason to spend deliberately, because in a flat-fee year the tutoring decision is the main education decision a family makes with its own money, and it is the one least likely to have been projected over the full two years it will actually run.

sections.heading: Permits, premises and what a rate cannot include
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and knowing this prevents one specific overcharge. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Because the permit costs nothing, no part of an hourly rate can honestly be attributed to licensing. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, but no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to a parent by anybody, and a figure circulating in this market could not be verified against an official source.

Premises require a different licence. A tutoring operation with staff and a location in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit issued to training institutes, beginning with initial approval, allowing a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and requiring annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE office or centre, and describes no tutor as KHDA-approved.

Dubai private schools themselves are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, inspecting annually across six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak, with ADEK covering Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority covering Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge covering Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education covering Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. KHDA also requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs and combined classes strictly prohibited.

sections.heading: What no budget should include
paragraphs: One line belongs in no two-year plan at any price. At least one provider competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments. The fee is real and the mechanism is a risk transfer: the academic-honesty finding, if it comes, attaches to the student's record while the seller keeps the money. Against a withdrawn result and a lost university place, it is the most expensive purchase in this market.

The legitimate version is specific enough to hold any tutor to. A tutor may teach the content an assessment rests on, explain what each published criterion rewards, assign an honest indicative score to a draft and quote the descriptor behind it, help narrow a research question until it is answerable within the word limit, confirm a method is viable, read the student's own draft and ask the questions an examiner would ask, and teach referencing conventions properly.

A tutor may not write, rewrite, restructure or supply text for submission, choose the research question, provide data the student did not collect, or edit until the sentences stop being the student's. A tutor should also not distribute syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; those are linked and cited at source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and unreleased material is a malpractice exposure.

Nor should any budget include a promised grade. No tutor can honour a guaranteed score or a specific improvement, and a provider leading with one is making a commercial claim rather than a professional judgement. What can be offered honestly is a measurement against a published scheme and a statement of what kind of change is available over a given period.

sections.heading: Availability across a two-year plan
paragraphs: A two-year plan has a supply problem a one-term plan does not. The slot that suits a family in Year 10 has to still exist in Year 11, and the specialist who taught the habit block has to be available for the final intensive. Specialist supply is finite, and the scarcest combinations are the ones needed most urgently: A Level Further Mathematics, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level Paper 3, Chemistry Higher Level mechanisms, IGCSE Computer Science pseudocode to the specification style.

No provider in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is worth noticing when every enquiry gets an immediate yes. The honest version is a realistic timescale and the alternatives. Where a UAE-based specialist is unavailable, the tutor may be based elsewhere and working to Gulf Standard Time, which is disclosed before booking rather than left to be inferred from a contact number.

For a long plan there are two extra questions worth asking at the start. Can this slot be held across the academic year, or is it rebooked each term? And if we pause for two terms, can we return to the same specialist? A provider who cannot answer either is not offering a two-year arrangement, whatever the pricing page says, and a family planning around one should know that before Year 10 ends.

The free trial is one session, free with no card required, with the specialist who would actually teach. It exists so a mismatch costs an hour rather than a term, which matters more in a long plan than a short one. If the fit is wrong, say so and a different specialist is proposed; if nobody suitable exists for the component, that is said plainly. Lessons are one-to-one online, and IB Gram offers no home visits anywhere in the UAE.

process.title: Project the two years before agreeing a term
process.description: Multiply the monthly band by the number of months the arrangement will actually run, not by the term you are currently worried about. One mid-market subject across two IGCSE years is roughly AED 12,000 to 24,000. Seeing that number before starting changes which shape a family chooses, and it is rarely calculated.

process.title: Divide every advertised rate out to an effective one
process.description: Take the package price, divide by the hours of teaching actually received, and add anything charged separately. AED 799 for eight sessions is about AED 100 an hour. Then ask what a cancelled session costs and whether marking is included, because both move the effective rate.

process.title: Buy the habit block in Year 10
process.description: Six to eight sessions on written method and command-word discipline, early, when nothing is urgent. This is the cheapest work in the two years and the first thing cut when a family spends reactively. It is also what makes the Year 11 intervention smaller when it comes.

process.title: Keep the middle terms dormant with a termly paper
process.description: One timed paper a term from the correct board and syllabus code, marked against the published scheme and filed. It keeps the external reference point alive, catches a new problem while it is small, and leaves most of the budget unspent and available for when it is needed.

process.title: Release the reserve against a diagnosed need
process.description: In Year 11, spend from the reserve only when a marked script names something specific. Build the final block from the mock script rather than from the syllabus, and end it at the exam window. Money held back is what makes a targeted late intervention possible rather than a panicked broad one.

faqs.question: What will tutoring cost a Dubai British School family across both IGCSE years?
faqs.answer: On published bands, one subject with a mid-market qualified tutor at one weekly hour runs AED 600 to 1,200 a month, which across two academic years allowing for holidays is roughly AED 12,000 to 24,000. Two subjects doubles it. Adding an exam-term intensive at the specialist band of AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above a month moves it again. These are Bestimate's Dubai figures read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. The point of the projection is that most families agree a weekly slot while thinking about one term and then run it for twenty-two months.

faqs.question: How should a fixed tutoring budget be spread across Years 10 and 11?
faqs.answer: Roughly a quarter on a habit block early in Year 10, very little through the middle terms, and half held in reserve for Year 11 and released against a diagnosed need. The default is the reverse: nothing early and everything in the final two terms, which is close to the worst ordering, because habits are cheapest to install before revision competes for the hours and late help can only move technique. Keep the middle terms covered by one timed paper a term rather than a standing weekly slot.

faqs.question: What is the difference between an advertised rate and the effective one?
faqs.answer: The effective rate is the total paid divided by the hours of teaching actually received. A package at AED 799 for eight online sessions is advertised monthly and works out at roughly AED 100 an hour. AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions is about AED 200 to 225 an hour including travel. Lost sessions push the other way: one billed session a month that is not taught raises a term's effective rate by roughly a quarter. Marking charged separately raises it further, and marking not done at all leaves the plan with no evidence base.

faqs.question: What notice period should we accept on a weekly arrangement?
faqs.answer: Ideally none, which is one practical reason to buy blocks with a defined end rather than standing slots. A four-week notice period means that a family deciding in the first week of a month to stop still pays for four further sessions they have already concluded are not working. Over a two-year plan with one change of direction, that is a month of fees for nothing. Ask the question before signing, along with what a cancelled session costs and whether the slot pauses through school holidays and mock weeks.

faqs.question: Should we keep paying for sessions during school holidays?
faqs.answer: Only if the holiday is being used deliberately, for example as a concentrated content block when the term is not competing for hours. Paying for a standing slot through a three-week break while the family is abroad is straightforward leakage. Because lessons are online, a pause costs nothing on either side and the same tutor and slot can resume afterwards, so there is no reason to buy continuity you cannot use. Agree the holiday position at the start rather than negotiating it each term, which is when it usually gets conceded.

faqs.question: What does a resit actually cost a Dubai family?
faqs.answer: An entry fee for the November series, a term of preparation falling in the autumn of sixth form while new courses are starting, and usually a tutoring block at specialist rates. That combination is what makes a resit expensive out of proportion to the single grade. The commonest route to one is an entry made at the wrong tier, and in tiered Cambridge subjects a Core entry caps the grade at 5 regardless of performance. Two timed papers at each tier in Year 10 is a very small purchase against that.

faqs.question: Does the KHDA fee freeze change what we should budget for tutoring?
faqs.answer: It fixes the larger number, not the smaller one. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Tutoring is an unregulated private market and is the education line that actually moves year to year. The practical effect is that in a flat-fee year the tutoring decision is the main education spending decision a family makes, which is a reason to plan it across two years rather than accumulate it.

faqs.question: Is in-home tutoring viable from Jumeirah Park?
faqs.answer: Viable, with a cost that shows up in the effective rate rather than the advertised one. The communities west of Al Khail Road are spread out and the afternoon drive from better-supplied areas is long, so a tutor's lost capacity sits inside the AED 180 to 500 published in-home band, and sessions that go wrong are usually billed. Over two years, one delayed or lost session a month is a material number. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE in any case; lessons are one-to-one online in Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor stay with my child for two years?
faqs.answer: Ask directly, because it matters more in a long plan than anything about the rate. If the person teaching changes mid-course, the replacement spends several sessions learning both the student and the specification, which is money for no teaching and a break in the evidence trail. Two further questions are worth asking at the start: can the slot be held across the academic year rather than rebooked each term, and if we pause for two terms, can we return to the same specialist. A provider who cannot answer is not offering a two-year arrangement.

faqs.question: Is a package cheaper than paying per session?
faqs.answer: Usually a little, and the way to tell is to divide. AED 799 for eight online sessions is roughly AED 100 an hour, which is budget tier regardless of how it is presented. The questions that decide whether a package is actually cheaper are whether unused sessions carry over, whether a cancelled session is credited, and whether the named tutor teaches all eight. A package that expires monthly and does not credit cancellations can have a higher effective rate than paying per session at a higher advertised figure.

faqs.question: When is the latest useful point to start tutoring before IGCSEs?
faqs.answer: Six weeks out is still useful, but only for a narrow purpose: timing, paper order, written method and command-word reading. Those are real marks and often worth a grade boundary. What cannot happen in that window is the secure learning of a topic never properly understood, and a plan that tries to cover everything thinly will move nothing. Work from the student's own most recent marked mock rather than starting new content. It is also the most expensive point at which to start, which is the argument for one cheap diagnostic paper each term.

faqs.question: Do you send tutors to Jumeirah Park or Al Furjan?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Lessons for Dubai families are delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The practical gain over a two-year plan is cost certainty rather than a lower headline rate: no session is billed and lost to traffic, a pause for holidays costs nothing, and the choice of tutor is not limited to whoever will drive west of Al Khail Road on a weekday afternoon. There is also no UAE office or centre to attend.

faqs.question: How much should we hold back for the final term?
faqs.answer: About half of a two-year budget, released only against a diagnosed need. The reason is that the useful late intervention is narrow and specific, built from the student's own marked mock, and a family that has already spent the money cannot buy it. Holding a reserve also removes the pressure to keep a weekly slot running through quiet terms simply because it exists. If the reserve is not needed, it is not spent, which is a better outcome than having bought supervision through a year when nothing was failing.

faqs.question: What should the first paid hour produce?
faqs.answer: A document, not a lesson. A timed past paper from the correct board and syllabus code, sat under exam conditions, marked against the published scheme, and a written diagnosis naming which topic, which method and which command words are costing marks. That document determines every hour after it and frequently shortens the plan, because it rules out whole categories of work. A first session that produces only a friendly impression of the subject has told you nothing you can budget against.

intro.heading: The gap that opens after results, not before them
paragraphs: At a selective British-curriculum school in Dubai, tutoring enquiries rarely begin with a crisis. They begin with a 6. The pupil is doing fine, the school is pleased, and a sixth-form department has published an entry grade of 7 for the subject the child wants to carry forward. That is not a failing grade problem. It is an admissions problem with a two-year fuse, and it is the single most common reason a family at this kind of school reaches for a tutor.

The second reason arrives twelve months later, after the certificate is already printed. A pupil who has met every entry requirement starts Year 12 and finds the first term of A Level Chemistry or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches considerably steeper than anything IGCSE asked. This is not a failure of teaching at either end. It is a genuine discontinuity: IGCSE assesses whether a pupil can apply taught procedures, and sixth-form courses assess whether they can reason with ideas they have only just met.

Both problems are solvable and both are cheaper to solve early, which is why this page is built as a map rather than as a sales argument. It sets out what a sixth form actually reads on an IGCSE certificate, which specific pieces of content each sixth-form subject assumes, how the A Level route and the IB Diploma route differ in what they want from a Year 11 pupil, and what the UAE Ministry of Education requires from a British-track certificate for recognition purposes.

That last point matters in Dubai and appears almost nowhere else. The MoE equivalency rules for the British track are published and specific: students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor ranking for these queries publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong, and a family planning a timetable on that figure is planning badly.

There is no published IB points threshold for equivalency that can be cited from an official source, so none is quoted here. The honest position is to describe the process, point to moe.gov.ae and the emirate attestation authority, and leave the IB figure to be confirmed there. Tutoring itself is not required for equivalency, admission or progression, and anyone suggesting otherwise is making a false claim about a regulatory process. Tuition for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, and home visits are a service offered only in India.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-dubai-college-s.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is given with the specific content a sixth-form course assumes, which is a narrower and more useful statement than saying the subject gets harder. The specification code is the starting point in every case.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580, Extended)
subjects.description: Sixth-form mathematics assumes instant algebraic manipulation: factorising, rearranging, indices, surds and functions handled without pause. A pupil who can do these slowly will be left behind in the first six weeks, because the new content arrives on top rather than afterwards.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: The best available bridge where a school offers it. Introduces calculus and extended trigonometry, so Year 12 begins with recognition rather than first contact. A pupil heading for Higher Level Analysis and Approaches or A Level Mathematics benefits disproportionately.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge IGCSE 0625, Extended)
subjects.description: A Level and Higher Level physics assume algebraic fluency more than physics knowledge. Pupils who passed IGCSE Physics by remembering equations and failed to develop rearranging and unit discipline struggle in Year 12 for mathematical reasons rather than physical ones.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge IGCSE 0620, Extended)
subjects.description: Moles are the gatekeeper. Sixth-form chemistry begins with quantitative work that assumes mole calculations are automatic, and a pupil who guessed their way through them at IGCSE meets the consequence in the first month rather than the first year.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge IGCSE 0610, Extended)
subjects.description: The step up is in precision of language and in volume rather than in difficulty. Sixth-form biology rewards exact terminology and extended written explanation, which makes IGCSE command-term discipline the most transferable preparation available.

subjects.name: English Literature (Cambridge 0475 and 0992)
subjects.description: Both A Level English and IB Language A assume independent argument rather than taught readings. The IGCSE habit worth carrying forward is answering the question in the first sentence and proving it, rather than arriving at a view on the last page.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 and 0990)
subjects.description: Relevant beyond English itself, because every sixth-form essay subject and every IB internal assessment is written. A pupil who cannot structure an argument under timing at 16 will meet that limitation in history, economics and the Extended Essay.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Sixth-form economics assumes comfort with graphs, percentage change and evaluation writing. Pupils who learned definitions at IGCSE and avoided the data-response questions find the first term harder than those who did the reverse.

subjects.name: History (Cambridge IGCSE 0470)
subjects.description: Source evaluation at IGCSE is a direct rehearsal for both A Level history and the IB history internal assessment. The skill transfers almost intact, which makes it one of the few subjects where IGCSE work pays forward without adaptation.

subjects.name: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are required in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum. Worth noting for equivalency planning: Arabic and Islamic Education are excluded from the MoE's five-subject IGCSE count, so they cannot be used to make the number up.

sections.heading: What a sixth form actually reads on an IGCSE certificate
paragraphs: A sixth-form department reads three things, and families usually attend to only the first. The grade in the subject itself, against a published threshold. The grade in the subjects that underpin it, which is why a physics department looks at the mathematics grade. And the shape of the timetable, because a certificate without separate sciences, or without a second language, or without Extended-tier mathematics, has closed certain routes whatever the grades say.

The thresholds are real and they are applied. A department publishing a 7 for its A Level course is not opening with a negotiating position; selective schools in Dubai hold the line because their results depend on it. Internal progression requirements can differ from the published external ones, so a pupil moving up within their own school may face a different number from an external applicant, and the only way to know is to ask the school directly.

The underpinning grades are the part that surprises people. A pupil with a 7 in Chemistry and a 5 in Extended-tier Mathematics is a weaker A Level Chemistry candidate than the grades suggest, because the quantitative work in Year 12 assumes the mathematics rather than the chemistry. Departments know this. Some publish a mathematics requirement for their science courses explicitly, and some simply decline the application without explaining why.

The practical instruction is to do the lookup in Year 10, while there is still time for the answer to change anything. Find the published entry grades for the sixth forms you are considering, for the specific courses your child wants, including any underpinning subject requirements. Compare them with a marked script rather than with a report grade. That exercise takes an afternoon, costs nothing, and determines everything that follows.

sections.heading: The IGCSE-to-A-Level gap, subject by subject
paragraphs: The step from IGCSE to A Level is not a general increase in difficulty. It is a specific set of assumptions made in the first weeks of each course, and naming them turns an intimidating transition into a short list of jobs. In mathematics the assumption is instant algebraic manipulation. In physics it is the same algebra plus unit discipline. In chemistry it is mole calculations as reflex. In biology it is precise terminology and extended written explanation.

What makes these assumptions costly is that they are not revisited. A Level courses have content to deliver and they deliver it from the first week on the understanding that the IGCSE foundation is secure. A pupil whose algebra is correct but slow is not wrong; they are simply unable to keep up while also absorbing differentiation for the first time. The gap then widens, because each new topic assumes the previous one.

The essay subjects assume something different and no less specific: independent argument. An IGCSE answer can be built from taught readings and a structure the teacher provided. An A Level answer is expected to take a position and sustain it against alternatives. Pupils who were rewarded at IGCSE for comprehensive coverage find that coverage scores poorly at A Level, where selectivity and judgement carry the marks.

All of this is fixable in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12, and that is when it is cheapest. Six to ten sessions on the specific assumption each chosen subject makes, working from the actual sixth-form specification rather than from IGCSE revision, converts the first term from first contact into recognition. Families almost never book it, which is why the first-term wobble at competitive Dubai sixth forms is so predictable.

sections.heading: The IGCSE-to-Diploma gap, which is a different gap
paragraphs: The IB Diploma makes a different demand, and families who assume it is simply harder or simply broader misread it. The Diploma requires six subjects across groups, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The constraint is not depth in one place; it is sustained competence everywhere at once, with internal deadlines that begin generating in the first term.

For an IGCSE pupil, the practical consequences are three. Breadth must be maintained rather than narrowed, so a subject the pupil hoped to drop at 16 may need carrying for two more years. Writing becomes load-bearing across every subject, because internal assessments are written in all six. And time management becomes an assessed skill in effect, since the internal deadlines overlap and nobody sequences them for the student.

The subject-level assumptions still exist. Higher Level sciences assume Extended-tier IGCSE content securely. The mathematics routes divide: Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented, Applications and Interpretation is modelling and data-oriented, each available at Higher and Standard Level, and they are genuinely different courses rather than two difficulty settings. Choosing between them on the basis of which looks easier is the most consequential error available at this point.

The honest preparation for a Diploma-bound pupil is therefore less about content and more about capacity. Writing fluently and quickly under a deadline, managing several overlapping pieces of work, and sustaining six subjects rather than three. A pupil who meets those demands and has a content gap will cope; a pupil with perfect content and no writing stamina will struggle through Year 12 in a way nobody predicted from their IGCSE grades.

sections.heading: The two mathematics routes and the degrees that gate on them
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject where a choice made at 16 most reliably closes a door at 18, and the Diploma's structure makes this sharper than the A Level system does. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and proof-oriented course. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling, statistics and technology-oriented course. Each runs at Higher and Standard Level, giving four distinct options, and university requirements distinguish between them.

Competitive engineering, physics, mathematics and economics courses generally expect Analysis and Approaches, usually at Higher Level. Business, social sciences, design and several health-science routes are well served by Applications and Interpretation, and in some cases prefer it, because the statistical reasoning is more relevant. The mistake is not choosing one or the other; the mistake is choosing on perceived difficulty and discovering the requirement two years later.

On the A Level side the equivalent decision is whether to take Mathematics at all, and whether to add Further Mathematics. A pupil heading for engineering at a competitive university who takes no mathematics has closed the route entirely. A pupil taking Mathematics without Further Mathematics is still viable for most courses and disadvantaged for a few. These requirements are published by universities and are easy to look up, and almost nobody looks them up in Year 11.

The preparation implication is the same in both systems. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches and A Level Mathematics both assume Extended-tier algebraic fluency on day one, and Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 is the designed bridge where a school offers it. Where it is not offered, a summer block covering calculus, harder trigonometry and algebraic stamina does much of the same work, and it is substantially cheaper than catching up during Year 12.

sections.heading: Subject combinations that close doors quietly
paragraphs: Some decisions made at the IGCSE options stage remove routes without anyone saying so. Taking Combined Science rather than separate sciences is the clearest example: it is a reasonable choice for a pupil whose strengths are elsewhere, and it constrains A Level science options at several Dubai sixth forms. Checking the entry rules before the choice is locked is a ten-minute job that almost nobody does at the right time.

Core-tier entry is the second. A Core-tier mathematics or science grade sits below most published sixth-form thresholds by construction, because the tier caps the scale. A pupil entered at Core tier who later wants A Level Chemistry is not in a slightly weaker position; they are outside the published requirement with no route to change it after the entry closes. That is why the tier conversation belongs in Year 10.

Dropping the second language is the third, and it matters more for Diploma-bound pupils than for A Level ones, because the Diploma requires a language and a pupil who abandoned theirs at 14 may be entering a Group 2 course from a weaker base than their peers. It also interacts with equivalency: Arabic and Islamic Education cannot be counted among the five IGCSE subjects the MoE British track requires, so a thin timetable can create an arithmetic problem.

None of this is an argument for taking everything. It is an argument for reading the consequences before the choice rather than after it. The useful exercise at options evening is to name the two or three degree routes the pupil might plausibly want, look up what each requires at sixth form, and work backwards to the IGCSE subjects and tiers that keep those routes open. Everything else is genuinely free choice.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: what a British-track certificate must show
paragraphs: This is the section no competitor in this market writes, and it matters for any family intending a UAE university or any process requiring certificate recognition. The Ministry of Education's published requirements for the British track are specific. A student must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Separately, they must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3.

Two details inside that are frequently got wrong. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which means a pupil whose timetable relies on them to reach five has not reached five. And one competitor currently ranking for UAE tutoring queries states that candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published rule. A family planning a timetable on a wrong number is planning badly, and the fix costs nothing but a check against the source.

For the American track the published requirements are different again: English proficiency via a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in the source material available here, so none is quoted. That figure must be confirmed on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before anyone relies on it.

Two cautions to state plainly. IB Gram does not perform, process or guarantee equivalency or attestation; the process belongs to the Ministry and the emirate authority, and the right action is to use the official channel. And tutoring is not required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. Any page implying that it is has made a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process, which is both inaccurate and a reason to distrust everything else on the page.

sections.heading: Academic honesty at the transition, and what a tutor may not do
paragraphs: The transition year is where academic-honesty pressure spikes, because sixth-form courses introduce extended independent work almost immediately. The IB Diploma's internal assessments, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay all begin generating deadlines while a pupil is still adjusting, and that is exactly when an offer to help with the writing becomes tempting. It should be refused.

The rule is the same in both systems and it is not negotiable. A tutor teaches, questions, models the technique on a different example, and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not write, co-write, or edit to completion any piece that will be submitted. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price; that is a malpractice trigger and the exposure falls on the candidate, whose whole qualification is at stake.

The legitimate version is more useful anyway. A tutor reading a draft and saying which paragraph fails to answer the research question is giving feedback the student can act on and repeat. A tutor supplying the paragraph has produced a document the student cannot defend in a viva and cannot reproduce in an examination. Parents are entitled to ask a prospective tutor directly what they would do if asked to write a section, and the answer is informative.

Material matters too. Cambridge, Pearson and the IB own their syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides, and the right behaviour is to link the official page rather than hand over files. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or IB approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership and makes no such claim. It has no office or centre in the UAE.

sections.heading: Coverage, timing and getting started
paragraphs: Extended-tier IGCSE across mathematics, the sciences and English is well covered in this set, as is bridging work into A Level and Diploma mathematics and sciences. Thinner briefs exist: Further Mathematics preparation, Additional Mathematics 0606 where a school does not teach it, and the combination of a specific Higher Level science with a named internal assessment brief. In a given week the honest answer may be that nobody suitable is free.

Three outcomes are possible and a family should be told which applies. The brief is covered and a trial lesson is scheduled within days. The brief is covered by a specialist working into Gulf Standard Time from outside the UAE, which is disclosed rather than hidden behind a local-looking telephone number. Or the brief is not currently covered, in which case it is named. Rates do not change because a tutor is based outside the UAE.

On timing: the two high-value windows for a transition are the autumn of Year 10, when a threshold gap can still be closed cheaply, and the summer between Year 11 and Year 12, when bridging work costs least and achieves most. The low-value window is the spring of Year 12, when the pupil is already behind and the course is still accelerating. Availability is also loosest in August and tightest from January, which is a second reason the summer block is good value.

Starting is deliberately low-commitment. A free trial lesson is one session, with no card details required. The useful things to bring are the published entry grades for the sixth forms you are considering, your child's last marked scripts in the relevant subjects, and the specification codes from the examinations officer. With those three, the gap can be stated as a number of marks and a number of sessions within the hour.

process.title: Look up the thresholds in Year 10
process.description: Find the published IGCSE entry grades for the specific sixth-form courses your child wants, at every school you would consider, including any underpinning subject requirement. Ask your own school what its internal progression rule is, because it can differ from the external one. This afternoon of work determines everything that follows.

process.title: Measure the gap with a marked script
process.description: Compare the threshold against a timed paper marked properly, not against a report grade. A report gives a position; a script shows which marks are available and which are not. The difference between those two instruments is frequently a whole grade in either direction.

process.title: Decide the sixth-form route on evidence
process.description: Depth in three subjects against breadth in six, terminal examinations against overlapping internal deadlines, and one mathematics decision that gates specific degrees. Match the pattern to how your child actually performs rather than to the school's reputation, and look up the degree requirements before the choice is made.

process.title: Close the threshold gap, then stop
process.description: Aim the weekly work at the named entry grade rather than at the subject in general, and end the arrangement when the target is met. A tutoring arrangement with no stated finish continues by default long after it has stopped being a repair, which is how a budget quietly doubles.

process.title: Book the summer bridging block
process.description: Six to ten sessions in August on the first term of the actual sixth-form specification, not on IGCSE revision. For mathematics and the sciences this converts first contact into recognition and is the single highest-value purchase in the sequence. Availability is loose in August and tight from January, so the timing pays twice.

whyPoints.title: Thresholds named, not implied
whyPoints.description: Work is aimed at a published entry grade for a specific course at a specific sixth form, with the gap stated in marks from a marked script. That gives the arrangement a target and an end point, which a general offer of subject support cannot.

whyPoints.title: The first-term assumption, subject by subject
whyPoints.description: Each sixth-form subject assumes something precise in week one: instant algebra, mole fluency, terminology precision, independent argument. Naming the assumption turns an intimidating transition into a short list of jobs that can be done in a summer rather than survived in a term.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency quoted from the source
whyPoints.description: The MoE British-track rules are stated as published - five IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, Arabic and Islamic Education excluded, plus one A Level at E or two AS at E - with the IB figure left to be verified on moe.gov.ae rather than invented.

whyPoints.title: The mathematics decision taken seriously
whyPoints.description: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are different courses at two levels each, and universities distinguish between them. The route is chosen against the degree requirement rather than against which option looks more manageable in Year 11.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and coverage stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are an India-only service. Where a brief such as Further Mathematics preparation has no specialist free, it is named rather than filled with a generalist.

whyPoints.title: No claim about a regulatory process
whyPoints.description: Tutoring is not required for equivalency, admission or progression, and IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees attestation. No grade promises, no unsourced statistics, and no suggestion that any UAE regulator or exam board has approved or partnered with the platform.

faqs.question: My Dubai College child has a 6 where the sixth form wants a 7. What now?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a measurable gap rather than a verdict. Get the last marked script in that subject and sort the lost marks into content, method, precision and timing. A pupil losing marks to method and precision has considerable headroom and may close the gap in six to ten sessions, because nothing new has to be taught. A pupil losing marks across a third of the specification is in a different position and the conversation should include whether this is the right subject to carry forward. Also ask the school whether its internal progression rule differs from the published external one.

faqs.question: Why does an A Level science department care about the mathematics grade?
faqs.answer: Because the quantitative work in Year 12 assumes mathematics rather than science. A pupil with a 7 in Chemistry and a 5 in Extended-tier Mathematics is a weaker A Level Chemistry candidate than the grades suggest, since mole calculations, rearranging and unit discipline are all mathematical skills examined inside chemistry questions. Some Dubai departments publish a mathematics requirement for their science courses explicitly and some simply decline the application without explaining. Ask the department directly in Year 10, because the mathematics gap is usually the cheaper of the two to close.

faqs.question: What does the first term of A Level Mathematics actually assume?
faqs.answer: Instant algebraic manipulation. Factorising, rearranging, indices, surds and functions handled without pausing to think, because new content arrives on top of them rather than afterwards. A pupil whose algebra is correct but slow is not wrong; they simply cannot keep pace while meeting differentiation for the first time. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 is the designed bridge where a school offers it. Where it is not offered, six to ten summer sessions on algebraic fluency plus an introduction to calculus does much of the same work at a fraction of the cost of catching up mid-year.

faqs.question: Is the IB Diploma harder than A Levels for an IGCSE pupil?
faqs.answer: It is differently demanding rather than uniformly harder. The Diploma requires six subjects across groups with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, and its internal deadlines start overlapping in the first term. A Levels concentrate depth into three or four subjects examined largely terminally. A pupil with one dominant strength and weak writing stamina usually does better on the A Level route; a pupil who is competent across the board and manages deadlines well often does better on the Diploma.

faqs.question: Which IB mathematics route should my child take?
faqs.answer: Decide it against the degree, not against perceived difficulty. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented, and competitive engineering, physics, mathematics and economics courses generally expect it, often at Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation is modelling, statistics and technology-oriented, and suits business, social sciences, design and several health-science routes, sometimes being preferred there. Each runs at Higher and Standard Level, so there are four options and universities distinguish between them. Look up the published requirement for two or three plausible degrees in Year 11 and work backwards from that.

faqs.question: Does taking Combined Science close off A Level sciences?
faqs.answer: At several Dubai sixth forms, effectively yes, and the rule is usually published rather than hidden. Combined Science covers reduced content from all three sciences for one grade, which is a reasonable choice for a pupil whose strengths lie elsewhere and a constraint if they later want A Level Chemistry or Physics. The decision is made at the options stage in Year 9, so the useful action is to check the entry rules of the sixth forms you would consider before the choice is locked. It is a ten-minute lookup that almost nobody does at the right moment.

faqs.question: Is the five-subject MoE rule or the six-subject figure the correct one?
faqs.answer: Five, on the British track, at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among them. One competitor currently ranking for UAE tutoring queries states six, which does not match the published rule, and a family planning a timetable on the wrong number is planning badly. Alongside the five, the published requirement is one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Verify the current position on moe.gov.ae before relying on it.

faqs.question: What does the Ministry of Education require on the American curriculum track?
faqs.answer: Different evidence entirely. English proficiency is met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test before applying. Those are the published figures in the guidance available here. No IB points threshold appears in that guidance, so none is quoted on this page; that figure must be confirmed on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority. IB Gram does not perform, process or guarantee equivalency.

faqs.question: Can Arabic count towards the five subjects for equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. The published rule excludes Arabic and Islamic education from the five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects required on the British track. That has a practical consequence for a thin timetable: a pupil relying on those subjects to reach five has not reached five, and the shortfall only becomes visible at the point of attestation. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies remain mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum under KHDA's requirements, so the subjects are studied either way - they simply cannot be counted in that particular total.

faqs.question: Is the summer between Year 11 and Year 12 worth spending money on?
faqs.answer: For mathematics and the sciences it is the best-value block in the whole sequence. Six to ten sessions built on the first term of the actual sixth-form specification, rather than on IGCSE revision, converts the opening weeks of Year 12 from first contact into recognition. Algebraic fluency, calculus introduction and mole work are the usual content. Availability is also loosest in August and tightest from January, so the timing pays twice. Almost no family books it, which is why the first-term wobble at competitive Dubai sixth forms is so predictable.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an Extended Essay or an Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: With the thinking, the method and the feedback, yes. With the writing, no. A tutor may teach the research skills, model the technique on a different example, and read a draft and say which paragraph fails to answer the research question. A tutor may not write, co-write or edit any submitted piece to completion, and no price makes that acceptable. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright, which is a malpractice trigger whose exposure falls on the candidate rather than on the provider taking the fee.

faqs.question: Do sixth forms in Dubai treat Core-tier grades differently?
faqs.answer: They sit below most published thresholds by construction, because Core tier caps the grade scale. A Core-tier mathematics or science grade is therefore not a slightly weaker version of an Extended-tier one; it is usually outside the stated entry requirement with no mechanism to change it once the entry has closed. That is the strongest argument for having the tier conversation in Year 10, backed by a timed Extended-tier script marked against the real mark scheme rather than by classroom assessment evidence alone.

faqs.question: Do you send tutors to Al Sufouh, Umm Suqeim or Emirates Hills addresses?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service offered only in India. Tutoring for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. For bridging work this is an advantage, because the right specialist for a named sixth-form specification is chosen on subject expertise rather than on living within driving distance of your community. It also removes the travel premium built into the published AED 180-500 in-home band and the cancellation risk of a peak-hour journey.

faqs.question: What should we bring to a first conversation about the transition?
faqs.answer: Three things. The published IGCSE entry grades for the specific sixth-form courses your child wants, at each school you would consider. Their last marked scripts in the relevant subjects, not the report grades. And the specification codes and tiers from the examinations officer. With those, the gap can be stated as a number of marks and a number of sessions inside an hour, and the conversation can be about a plan rather than about reassurance. The first session is free, is one session, and requires no card details.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-dubai-college-s.closingBody: Find the published IGCSE entry grades for the sixth-form courses your child actually wants, at every school you would consider, and ask your own school whether its internal progression rule differs. Then compare those numbers against a marked script rather than a report grade. If the gap is method and precision, it is six to ten sessions. If it is content across a third of the specification, the conversation should be about the subject plan instead. A free trial lesson is one session with no card details required, and the useful things to bring are those thresholds and those scripts. Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.
