sections.heading: What a school will change, and what a tutor may not do
paragraphs: Schools will often change more than parents assume, if asked specifically and early. Set placements are reviewed in most Dubai departments at stated points. Tier entries can be revisited before the centre's deadline. Additional feedback on a specific component can usually be arranged. Predicted grades can move before they are fixed. What rarely changes is anything requested after a deadline, or anything requested in general terms without evidence attached.

What a school will not do is run a parallel curriculum for one pupil, and it should not be asked to. A department has a scheme of work and a cohort, and the right question is not for different teaching but for specific information: which component, which question type, what to practise. That information is free, authoritative and usually precise, and it is the brief any outside support should work from.

On the limits of outside support, the rules are not negotiable. A tutor teaches, questions, models on a different example and marks the pupil's own work. A tutor does not write, co-write or edit any submitted piece, including a school assessment or an Internal Assessment, and no price makes that acceptable. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright, which is a malpractice trigger whose exposure falls on the candidate.

Nor should anybody hand over board material as files. Cambridge, Pearson and the IB own their syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables, and the right behaviour is to link the official page. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or IB approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership and makes no such claim. It has no office or centre in the UAE, and nobody should describe its tutors as regulator-approved, because a KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to institutes with premises.

sections.heading: Coverage, permits and the first session
paragraphs: Mathematics, the sciences and the essay subjects at both Cambridge and Pearson tiers are well covered in this set, and a match is usually quick. Thinner briefs exist: Computer Science 0478 with Cambridge pseudocode conventions, Additional Mathematics 0606, Arabic as a first language, or an unusual literature text list. In a given week the honest answer may be that nobody suitable is free, and that is better stated than filled with a generalist at the same rate.

Which of three answers a Dubai Heights request gets usually turns on how precisely the brief is written. Name the syllabus and the tier and the common outcome is the first: covered, with a trial lesson scheduled within days. The second outcome is that the brief is covered by a specialist teaching into Gulf Standard Time from outside the UAE — an Additional Mathematics 0606 or Computer Science 0478 request often resolves this way — and we state that rather than concealing it behind a local-looking telephone number. The rate is identical either way, because a tutor's postcode is not a pricing input. The third outcome is that nobody suitable is currently free, and the only decent thing to do with it is to say so with the subject and tier named, so that a family can look elsewhere this term rather than next.

Parents are entitled to check the one credential that exists. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. One further point worth knowing: the permit's code of conduct is reported to bar a teacher from tutoring pupils affiliated with their own school, so your child's own class teacher is not the right private arrangement however convenient it looks.

The first session is free, is one session, and requires no card details. The useful thing to bring is the paperwork you already have: the last two reports, the predicted grade, the mock script and the specification codes if you have them. Within that hour it should be possible to say which sources agree, which do not, what the single highest-value target is, and which questions to put to the subject teacher. If the recommendation is to ask the school three questions and spend nothing, that is a legitimate outcome.

process.title: Assemble what you already hold
process.description: The last two reports, the predicted grade and what it was made for, the set placement, the mock script rather than the mock grade, and the specification codes from the examinations officer. All of this exists, most of it is free, and very few families read it side by side before buying anything new.

process.title: Add one independent measurement
process.description: A board past paper from the official Cambridge or Pearson site, sat under timing and marked against the published scheme. This is the only genuinely external instrument available, and it is what makes a report grade interpretable rather than merely reassuring or alarming.

process.title: Triangulate before deciding
process.description: Where the school's data, your measurement and the pupil's own account all agree, act on it immediately. Where two agree and one does not, find the explanation. Where all three disagree, one instrument is faulty and finding out which costs an hour and saves a term.

process.title: Ask the six specific questions
process.description: Which component is costing marks, what the method-against-content split was, which tier is provisionally entered, which specification code applies, whether the practical paper is stronger or weaker, and what one thing the pupil should practise. The last answer is a free tutoring brief from the best-informed person available.

process.title: Require a monthly note in the school's language
process.description: Not a summary of how sessions went, but marks on named question types and the component where movement is happening. A note a head of department can read in two minutes is worth more than a longer one written in a tutor's own vocabulary, because it enables a conversation rather than a parallel account.

whyPoints.title: The school's data read properly first
whyPoints.description: Reports, predicted grades, set placements and inspection bands measure four different things, and most families read them as one noisy signal. Separating them is free, takes an evening, and frequently removes the need to buy anything at all.

whyPoints.title: One external instrument, used consistently
whyPoints.description: A board past paper from the official site, sat under timing and marked to the published scheme, is the only measurement that is not internal to a school. Repeating the same instrument is what makes movement visible, and switching to easier papers destroys the comparison.

whyPoints.title: Reporting in the school's vocabulary
whyPoints.description: Monthly notes use working-at grades, named components and marks on question types, because that is the language a department can act on. A note written in a provider's own terms produces a parallel account rather than a shared one.

whyPoints.title: Questions that produce facts
whyPoints.description: Asking which component is costing marks, or what one thing the pupil should practise, gets a precise answer from a teacher who sees them several times a week. Asking how they are doing in a five-minute slot gets a positive summary, which is all the question allows.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and coverage stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are an India-only service. Where a minority subject or tier has no specialist free, that is named rather than filled with a generalist.

whyPoints.title: No claim that cannot be interrogated
whyPoints.description: No grade promises, no satisfaction percentages, no self-asserted ratings, and no suggestion that KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB has approved or partnered with IB Gram. Board documents are linked at source rather than supplied as files.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA inspection band tell us about our own child's progress?
faqs.answer: Very little, in either direction. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the judgement describes institutional provision averaged across the whole school: teaching, leadership, curriculum, inclusion, cohort progress. One department can be weaker than the band suggests and another stronger. The band is genuinely useful when choosing between schools and useless for diagnosing one pupil's stuck grade. What is worth reading is the narrative commentary by subject and phase, which is specific enough to raise in a conversation.

faqs.question: What is each report in the school year actually for?
faqs.answer: They answer different questions. A baseline or settling report rests on limited evidence and is good for spotting an obvious mismatch. A mid-year full report carries the most considered teacher judgement, after a term of work and usually an internal assessment series, and is the right document for identifying the one subject worth working on. A mock report reports one paper under particular conditions and its value is the script behind it. An end-of-year Year 10 report is the most actionable of all, because a whole year and a summer remain available.

faqs.question: Who decides a predicted grade and on what evidence?
faqs.answer: A teacher or department, for a stated purpose, using evidence you are entitled to ask about. The method changes the meaning: a prediction built from board past papers marked to the published scheme is a measurement, while one built from classwork, effort and experience of similar pupils is a judgement calibrated against that department's own cohort history. A secondary phase running its second or third IGCSE cohort has less history to calibrate against, which is structural rather than a failing. Ask what evidence built it and what would move it.

faqs.question: Can a predicted grade be changed once it has been given?
faqs.answer: Before its fixing point, usually yes, on new evidence. After it, particularly once it has gone into an application, it is effectively settled. Very few parents know when that date falls, and it changes what is worth doing: evidence produced a fortnight before the fixing point can move a number, and the same evidence a fortnight after cannot. Ask for the date, ask what demonstration would move the prediction, and then aim any work at exactly that rather than at the subject generally.

faqs.question: What should we ask at a Dubai Heights Academy parents' evening?
faqs.answer: Questions that name a component, a question type or an evidence source. Which component is costing the most marks. What the method-against-content split was on the mock. Which tier the pupil is provisionally entered for, and what would change it. Which specification code applies. Whether the practical paper is stronger or weaker than the theory papers. And what the one thing is that the pupil should practise this term. That last answer is a precise tutoring brief, given free, by the person with the most information.

faqs.question: The report says 'on track' but the mock was poor. Which one is right?
faqs.answer: Both, probably, because they measure different things. An internal assessment is written to test what has just been taught, under classroom conditions. A board paper tests the whole specification with unfamiliar contexts and tighter timing. A pupil can be genuinely good at the first and genuinely weaker at the second, and the gap is usually explained by specification coverage, timing pressure or unfamiliar question styles. Each of those suggests different work. Read the mock script rather than the mock grade and the explanation is normally visible.

faqs.question: How often should a school review a set placement?
faqs.answer: Ask, because Dubai schools vary considerably and the answer matters more than it sounds. In most departments there is a stated review point each term, and the useful follow-up is what triggers a review: a particular assessment, a teacher referral, or a request. A pupil who had one poor term should not carry a set placement for three years on that basis, and a pupil who transferred into the emirate mid-Key Stage 3 may have been placed on another school's evidence with no reconciliation at all.

faqs.question: What do we do when our own measurement disagrees with the school's?
faqs.answer: Treat it as information rather than as a dispute, and bring it as evidence. A timed board past paper, marked against the published scheme with lost marks categorised, speaks the department's own language and asks nothing to be taken on trust - a head of department can read it in five minutes. A substantially lower independent result usually points to coverage, timing or question style. A higher one usually means the pupil performs better under pressure than in class. Raise it a full term before the decision it should influence.

faqs.question: Is it reasonable to ask a teacher for a mark-scheme breakdown?
faqs.answer: Entirely reasonable, and most Dubai teachers will give it, because it is a factual question with a factual answer. What you are asking for is which questions lost marks and in what category - content, method, precision, timing - rather than a judgement about the pupil. The request is easier to grant than a general conversation about potential, and far more useful. If a full breakdown is not practical, the marked script itself contains the same information in the margin annotations.

faqs.question: How much progress should show between two school reports?
faqs.answer: Enough to be visible, and not necessarily a changed grade. Reports arrive roughly a term apart, which is too long to wait for a signal, so something has to be produced deliberately in between. At four weeks the targeted habit should be visible in the pupil's written work. At eight weeks the marks on the specific question types being worked on should have moved against a baseline under the same conditions. By the next report, the school's judgement should reflect the same movement, and if it does not, the discrepancy is worth raising.

faqs.question: Does a school's inspection band affect IGCSE results for an individual?
faqs.answer: Not in any way a family can use. A band is an aggregate across an institution, and results are produced by individual pupils sitting individual papers marked by Cambridge or Pearson against published criteria. A pupil can be under-served in one subject at a strongly rated school, or very well taught at a school rated lower overall. The things that do affect an individual result are the tier of entry, the specification code, the component profile and the pupil's own preparation, and all four can be checked directly.

faqs.question: Will a Dubai school talk to a private tutor?
faqs.answer: Some will and many prefer to talk to the parent, which is reasonable. The more productive route is usually for a tutor to produce a note the parent can take to the department - marks on named question types, the component where movement is happening, in the school's own vocabulary. That enables a conversation without asking a teacher to coordinate with an outside party. What no school should be asked to do is run a parallel curriculum for one pupil, and the useful request is information rather than different teaching.

faqs.question: Do you send tutors to Al Barsha South or Arjan addresses?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service offered only in India. Tutoring for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. For work built round reading a marked script that suits the method, since the session is spent annotating the script on a shared screen and re-answering the questions where marks were lost. It also removes the travel premium inside the published AED 180-500 in-home band and the cancellation risk of a peak-hour journey.

faqs.question: What should a tutor's monthly note contain?
faqs.answer: Marks on named question types, compared against a dated baseline, and the component where movement is or is not happening - written in the vocabulary the school uses rather than the tutor's own. It should name the current target, state whether it has been met, and say what the next four weeks will consist of. What it should not contain is a narrative about how sessions went, or adjectives like 'engaging well', because neither can be checked in June and both tend to appear where nothing measurable was produced.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-dubai-heights-a.closingHeading: Read what you already hold before buying anything
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-dubai-heights-a.closingBody: Put the last two reports, the predicted grade, the set placement and the mock script on one table, and ask what each of them actually measures. Then add one board past paper, sat under timing and marked to the published scheme, and see whether the three sources agree. Where they do, the target is obvious and narrow. Where they do not, an hour spent finding the faulty instrument saves a term of misdirected work. A free trial lesson is one session with no card details required, and the right thing to bring is that paperwork. Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-dubai-internati.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are matched to one subject in one programme: a Middle Years subject group, or a Diploma subject at Higher or Standard Level. The two are assessed so differently that experience in one does not transfer automatically to the other.

intro.heading: A report full of criterion letters, and nobody explaining them
paragraphs: Dubai International Academy Al Barsha runs the International Baccalaureate as a continuum, which means a student can pass through the Primary Years Programme, the Middle Years Programme and the Diploma without ever sitting a conventional terminal examination until the final two years. That is a genuine strength and it produces a specific problem for parents: the reports do not look like anything they recognise. A Middle Years report arrives as four criterion letters per subject, each with a mark out of eight, and a converted grade from one to seven. It is unfamiliar, and it is far more informative than a percentage, if somebody tells you how to read it.

Nobody usually does, which is why so many families at continuum schools arrive at the Diploma with a vague sense that one subject has been weak for three years without ever knowing which part of it. A student scoring well on criterion A and poorly on criterion C in mathematics does not have a mathematics problem; they have a communication problem, and the remedy is completely different. The same report read as a single grade of four hides that distinction entirely.

So this page is written around the assessment system rather than around the neighbourhood. What the four criteria are in each subject group, what each one actually rewards, where the marks go, what the Personal Project is marked on, and how the Middle Years system maps onto the Diploma's internal assessments. The IGCSE half of this search matters too and is dealt with honestly: Al Barsha families move in and out of British-curriculum schools regularly, and a student arriving from or leaving to IGCSE faces a real crossing in both directions.

IB Gram supports students in Al Barsha and across Dubai with one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time. It does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service that exists only in India, and that position appears on every country page this site publishes. The in-home market in Dubai is large and publishes roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. On a continuum school's criterion problem, what you need is somebody who has marked against those criteria, which is a narrower pool than the set of people who will drive to Al Barsha.

A note on dates before the detail. No IB session or results date appears on this page, because none could be verified from the International Baccalaureate's own site for this project. Diploma students in the UAE sit the May session and Middle Years on-screen examinations sit in May where a school enters them; confirm every date through the school rather than through any tutoring site, this one included.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-dubai-internati.programmesIntro: Three programmes, one continuum, and three entirely different assessment languages. Knowing which one your child is inside determines what a tutor should be doing.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with no external examinations, ending in the Exhibition in the final year. Assessment is continuous and teacher-led, so there is no paper to practise and no mark scheme to work from. Reporting describes what a child can do rather than ranking them against a cohort.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Barsha family the useful tutoring at this stage is narrow and unglamorous: reading fluency, number confidence and the ability to explain an answer in writing. Inquiry-based assessment rewards a child who can justify a conclusion in prose, and that capacity is what later carries the Middle Years criteria on communication.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked out of eight, converted into a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. The Personal Project in the final year is marked out of 24 across planning, applying skills and reflecting. Some schools enter on-screen examinations and ePortfolios in the final year.
programmes.countryNote: This is the programme where a continuum student's weakness either gets identified or gets carried into the Diploma. The single most useful request a parent can make of the school is the criterion breakdown behind a reported grade, not the grade itself, because the four criteria are diagnosed and remedied differently from one another.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher and three Standard, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, scored out of 45 with 24 as the minimum for the diploma and up to three bonus points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix. Internal assessment carries real weight in every subject.
programmes.countryNote: A student arriving from the Middle Years Programme is comfortable with criterion-based marking and less practised at timed papers, which is the opposite of an IGCSE arrival. The first term of Diploma support for a continuum student should therefore be weighted towards examination technique rather than towards content, and that is a deliberate choice rather than an accident.

programmes.name: IGCSE, for students crossing in or out
programmes.description: Terminal written papers, tiering into Core and Extended on Cambridge or Foundation and Higher on Pearson Edexcel, with a board-dependent practical arrangement in the sciences. Nothing in it resembles criterion-based marking, which is why the crossing in either direction is a real adjustment.
programmes.countryNote: Al Barsha has a dense mix of curricula within a few kilometres, so families move between IB and British schools more often here than the national average. A student moving from the Middle Years Programme into Year 10 IGCSE needs examination technique urgently; a student moving the other way needs to learn to write against criteria, which nobody teaches explicitly.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-dubai-internati.subjectsIntro: Middle Years subject groups first, with the four criteria named, because those names are what a parent needs in order to read a report. Criterion letters are consistent within a subject group and differ between groups.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics
subjects.description: Criterion A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, D applying mathematics in real-life contexts, each out of eight. Most students lose marks on C and D rather than A: they can do the mathematics and cannot set it out or apply it to an unfamiliar context.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: Criterion A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, D reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion B is the one that prepares a student for the Diploma investigation, and it is the one most often weak because designing is harder than performing.

subjects.name: MYP Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criterion A analysing, B organising, C producing text, D using language. A student can write fluently and still score poorly on A, because analysing an effect is a different act from describing a technique. That distinction carries straight into Diploma Paper 1.

subjects.name: MYP Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criterion A knowing and understanding, B investigating, C communicating, D thinking critically. Criterion D is where grades are made, and it rewards a judgement supported by evidence rather than a balanced account with no position taken.

subjects.name: MYP Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Assessed in four communicative skills: listening, reading, speaking and writing, each out of eight, with phase placement rather than year group determining expectations. Being in the wrong phase is a common and fixable source of apparent underperformance.

subjects.name: MYP Design
subjects.description: Criterion A inquiring and analysing, B developing ideas, C creating the solution, D evaluating. Students who make an excellent product and document it thinly score below students who make a modest one and document it properly, which feels unfair and is exactly what the criteria say.

subjects.name: DP Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Standard Level: Papers 1 and 2 at forty per cent each, Exploration at twenty. Higher Level: Papers 1 and 2 at thirty per cent each, Paper 3 at twenty, Exploration at twenty. Paper 3 is an extended-response problem paper and the least practised component in the Diploma.

subjects.name: DP Sciences: Physics, Chemistry, Biology
subjects.description: Paper 1 at thirty-six per cent including a data-analysis section, Paper 2 at forty-four, and the scientific investigation at twenty. The investigation is capped at 3,000 words and marked across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each.

subjects.name: DP English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Standard Level: Paper 1 at thirty-five per cent, Paper 2 at thirty-five, Individual Oral at thirty. Higher Level adds the HL Essay at twenty per cent. The Individual Oral requires a global issue traced through two texts and is rehearsable in a way the papers are not.

subjects.name: DP Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Economics at Standard Level runs Paper 1 at thirty per cent, Paper 2 at forty and the portfolio at thirty; the portfolio is three commentaries of no more than 800 words each. Business Management adds a pre-released case at Higher Level, which can be worked on months ahead.

sections.heading: How to read a Middle Years report in five minutes
paragraphs: Four letters, four marks out of eight, one grade from one to seven. That is the whole structure, and the grade at the end is the least useful number on the page because it averages away the information. What a parent should do is ignore the grade for a moment and look at the spread between the four criterion marks. A student with sixes across all four has a different problem from a student with a seven, a six, a three and a six, even though the converted grades may be identical.

The spread is the diagnosis. In mathematics, criterion A is knowing and understanding, B is investigating patterns, C is communicating and D is applying mathematics in real-life contexts. A student strong on A and weak on C can do the mathematics and cannot set it out: no working shown, notation inconsistent, reasoning implied rather than stated. That is a habit, it is highly fixable, and it is not addressed by more content teaching. A student weak on D cannot transfer a known method to an unfamiliar context, which needs practice on unfamiliar contexts rather than on the method.

The same logic runs through every subject group with different letters. In the sciences, criterion B inquiring and designing is the one that predicts how a student will handle the Diploma investigation, and it is often the weakest because designing an experiment is harder than performing one. In language and literature, criterion A analysing is where fluent writers lose marks, because analysing an effect is a different act from identifying a technique. In individuals and societies, criterion D thinking critically rewards a judgement supported by evidence rather than an even-handed summary.

Ask the school for the criterion breakdown behind the reported grade if it is not already on the report, and ask which specific descriptor band each mark sat in. Those two questions turn a report from a verdict into a plan, and they cost nothing. They are also the first thing a tutor who knows the programme will ask you for.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and where its 24 marks go
paragraphs: The Personal Project in the final Middle Years year is marked out of 24 across three criteria — planning, applying skills, and reflecting, each out of eight — and it is the first genuinely independent piece of work a continuum student produces. It is also the clearest early signal of how they will handle the Extended Essay two years later, which makes it worth taking seriously for reasons beyond its own grade.

The failure mode is almost always the same and it is not laziness. A student chooses a goal that is interesting rather than one that can be evidenced, spends most of the available time making or doing the thing, and then discovers that the marks are substantially for the process journal and the reflection rather than for the product. A beautiful outcome with a thin journal scores below a modest outcome with a thorough one, and students find that genuinely counterintuitive until somebody shows them the criteria.

What legitimate support looks like here is narrow. Explaining the three criteria in the guide's own wording. Helping turn a broad goal into one that the available time and evidence can support, which is the single highest-value intervention and takes one session. Reading journal entries the student has written and saying where the evidence of a skill being applied is absent. Explaining how the report should be structured against the marks. None of that involves producing anything.

What a tutor must not do is write the report, draft the reflections or produce the product. The project is the student's own work and a breach is a malpractice matter whose consequence falls on the student. The test to apply to anybody offering help with it is simple: ask what they would do if your child asked them to write a reflection. A refusal with an explanation of the alternative is the right answer.

sections.heading: From criteria to papers: what the Diploma asks that the Middle Years did not
paragraphs: A continuum student arrives at the Diploma with an unusual profile. They are fluent in criterion-based assessment, comfortable with extended independent work, and used to being marked on process as well as product. What they have often never done is sit a two-hour paper under timed conditions with a clock running and no opportunity to redraft. That is the gap, and it is a technique gap rather than a knowledge one, which means it responds quickly to the right work.

The shape of the first Diploma term should reflect that. For a student from an IGCSE background the priority is content depth and the new independence of internal assessment. For a continuum student it is the opposite: the internal assessments feel familiar and the papers do not. Timed sections from week one, marked against the official scheme, with losses attributed to causes rather than topics, closes the gap faster than any amount of additional teaching.

The good news is that the continuum background pays off precisely where other students struggle. The Diploma sciences investigation, capped at 3,000 words and marked across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each, is recognisably a grown-up version of criterion B and C work. The Extended Essay at 4,000 words is recognisably a grown-up Personal Project. A student who took criterion B seriously in Year 9 has a real advantage in Year 12, and a student who did not has a predictable problem.

The mapping below is the one to plan against. It is also the argument for not waiting until the Diploma to fix a criterion weakness: the same weakness reappears two years later attached to twenty per cent of a subject grade rather than to a school report.

sections.heading: What progress evidence looks like when there is no exam percentage
paragraphs: At a continuum school there is no convenient percentage to track, which means progress has to be demonstrated differently and is therefore easier to fudge. A tutor reporting that a student is more confident, more engaged and attempting harder questions has said nothing measurable. At a school where the assessment is criterion-based, measurable means criterion movement with the marked work attached.

A closed criterion looks like this: two pieces of work from two different weeks, marked against the same criterion, scoring in a higher descriptor band than the baseline, with the specific change visible in the text. For communicating in mathematics, that is working shown where it previously was not and notation consistent where it previously drifted. For analysing in language and literature, it is a sentence about effect where previously there was a sentence about technique. These are visible in the script, which is the point.

The baseline matters and should be established in the first fortnight rather than assumed. Ask for a piece of work marked against the criteria by the tutor in the first two sessions, with the descriptor band named. That document is the baseline, it is comparable to the school's own marking, and if the tutor's marking and the school's disagree significantly that is itself worth investigating early rather than at the end of a term.

Review monthly. A term is long enough for an arrangement to drift entirely, and at a continuum school the absence of exam results means drift is harder to notice. The question to ask is specific: which criterion were we working on, what band was it in four weeks ago, what band is it in now, and show me the two pieces of work. A tutor working properly answers in two minutes with documents.

sections.heading: Crossing between the continuum and a British-curriculum school
paragraphs: Al Barsha holds an unusually dense mix of curricula within a few kilometres, and families move between them more often here than the national picture suggests. Dubai's private-school sector had 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum at thirty-seven per cent of enrolment, Indian at twenty-six, American at fourteen and the International Baccalaureate at seven. A family moving between those systems mid-stream is doing something common and under-supported.

Moving from the Middle Years Programme into Year 10 or 11 IGCSE is a technique shock. The content overlap is reasonable; what is missing is terminal examination practice, tiering awareness, and the habit of writing for a mark scheme rather than a descriptor band. The urgent work is timed papers from the first week, plus establishing the syllabus code, because Cambridge sciences carry a practical component worth twenty per cent while Pearson Edexcel sciences have no separate practical exam at all.

Moving the other way, from IGCSE into the Diploma, is the reverse. The student can sit a paper and has never been marked against a published criterion, has never kept a process journal, and has never had to design an investigation rather than follow a method. Those are teachable in a six to ten session block over a summer, and a student who does that block starts the Diploma ahead rather than catching up from week one.

For a student who stays in the continuum but whose siblings do not, the practical point is that a single tutor rarely covers both well. A Middle Years criterion specialist and an IGCSE specification specialist are different professionals, and asking one person to do both usually produces one good arrangement and one adequate one at the same cost as two good ones.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with the Diploma core and internal assessments
paragraphs: At a continuum school the internal assessment load feels normal, which is both an advantage and a risk, because familiarity makes it easier to slide across the authorship line without noticing. The boundary should be stated in the terms a tutor can repeat. A tutor may teach content, explain each criterion in the board's published wording, show how a comparable piece is built, read a draft the student has written and name which criterion it misses, and teach them to fix it themselves. A tutor may not write the internal assessment, draft the Extended Essay, or edit a piece to completion so the words become theirs.

The limits are part of the same competence and function as verification questions. The Extended Essay is capped at 4,000 words, the Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,600, the exhibition commentary at 950, the Diploma sciences investigation at 3,000, and each Economics commentary at 800. The Personal Project is marked out of 24. A tutor who does not know those figures is not working from the guide, and a draft over a cap loses marks for a reason unrelated to its quality.

There is also a materials rule. Subject guides, specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge and Pearson. A provider distributing them as downloads is reproducing copyrighted material, and for unreleased papers it is a malpractice exposure as well. Reference and link; do not redistribute. Everything factual on this page should be confirmed against the current official document through the school.

Finally, position. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International, Pearson, the Ministry of Education, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge or the Sharjah Private Education Authority. It holds no such relationship, claims none, operates no premises in the UAE, and has no arrangement with Dubai International Academy Al Barsha or any other school named on this page.

sections.heading: The practical frame: regulator, mandatory subjects and the Dubai week
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are licensed by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. That is where inspection reports and curriculum approvals live, and it is worth reading the real document rather than a third party's summary of it. Inspection frameworks apply bands aspect by aspect rather than only to a school as a whole, so the band for teaching in your child's phase matters more than a headline.

Separately, the authority's mandatory-subject requirements shape every school week in the emirate regardless of the licensed curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are required in all Dubai private schools, with requirements that had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Classes must be organised separately for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

The language rules are specific. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, with schools able to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met and a recommendation that no mandatory-subject lesson runs under twenty-five minutes.

One rule limits what any tutor can honestly offer. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which means Arabic and Islamic Education tutoring works from the school's own material rather than from a parallel scheme. Anyone selling a separate curriculum for those subjects is describing something the regulations do not permit.

sections.heading: Getting started, including what can go wrong
paragraphs: The first step is a document request rather than a shortlist. Ask the school for the criterion breakdown behind the most recent reported grade in the subject that worries you, and for the descriptor band each criterion mark sat in. For a Diploma student, ask the coordinator for the internal deadline calendar, because those dates are set by the school, arrive in clusters and land hardest in the autumn of the final year.

Then book a trial lesson and treat it as a test of whether the tutor speaks the right language. Ask what criterion C rewards in Middle Years mathematics, or what research design means in the Diploma investigation and why it cannot be repaired after data collection. A specialist answers in a sentence. Somebody whose experience is examination-based will answer in terms of papers, which tells you they will teach content where the marks are being lost on communication.

The failures are predictable. A criterion problem treated as a content problem, which means three months of teaching a student who already knew the material. A continuum student given more content in the first Diploma term when the actual gap is timed paper technique. A Personal Project where the product is finished and the journal is empty. An arrangement that drifts because there is no examination percentage to make the drift visible. Every one of those is caught by a criterion baseline in the first fortnight and a monthly review with the scripts.

And the honest limit, stated once more. No tutor is sent to an Al Barsha address or anywhere else in the UAE. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which in a city with heavy afternoon traffic also means the slot is a slot rather than an arrival window. The reason to choose it is not convenience; it is that criterion-level diagnosis needs somebody who has marked against those criteria, and that is a narrower pool than a radius.

process.title: Ask for the criterion breakdown, not the grade
process.description: The reported grade averages away the information. What you need is the four criterion marks out of eight and the descriptor band each one sat in. Those two facts turn a report into a diagnosis, cost nothing, and are the first thing a tutor who knows the programme will request from you.

process.title: Name the programme and the subject group precisely
process.description: Middle Years or Diploma, which subject, and for the Diploma which level. The two programmes use different assessment languages entirely, and a tutor whose experience is in one does not automatically transfer to the other. Stating it removes two sessions of discovery from the start.

process.title: Test the language in the trial lesson
process.description: Ask what criterion C rewards in Middle Years mathematics, or why research design cannot be repaired after data collection. A specialist answers in a sentence. An examination-trained tutor answers in terms of papers, which signals they will teach content where the loss is in communication.

process.title: Establish a criterion baseline in the first fortnight
process.description: A piece of work marked against the criteria by the tutor, with the descriptor band named, in the first two sessions. That is the comparison point for everything afterwards. If the tutor's marking and the school's disagree significantly, find out why in week two rather than in June.

process.title: Get the internal deadline calendar for Diploma students
process.description: Set by the school, arriving in clusters, and heaviest in the autumn of the final year when internal assessment finals collide with the Extended Essay and mocks. Ask for the whole calendar at the start of the first Diploma year rather than when it is being enforced.

process.title: Review monthly with two scripts, not a report
process.description: Which criterion were we working on, what band was it in four weeks ago, what band now, and show me both pieces of work. A tutor working properly answers in two minutes with documents. At a continuum school there is no exam percentage to catch drift, so the cadence has to be short.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-level diagnosis rather than subject-level guessing
whyPoints.description: A student weak on communicating in mathematics can already do the mathematics, and more teaching will not help. The four criteria are diagnosed and remedied differently, which is why the breakdown behind a grade is the document that matters and the grade itself is the least useful number on the report.

whyPoints.title: The Middle Years and the Diploma treated as different systems
whyPoints.description: A continuum student arrives at the Diploma fluent in criteria and unpractised at timed papers, which is the reverse of an IGCSE arrival. The first Diploma term should be weighted accordingly, and that is a deliberate choice rather than something to discover in February.

whyPoints.title: The Personal Project taken seriously early
whyPoints.description: Twenty-four marks across planning, applying skills and reflecting, and the clearest early signal of how a student will handle a 4,000-word Extended Essay. The usual failure is a strong product with a thin process journal, which the criteria penalise and students find counterintuitive.

whyPoints.title: Progress shown as criterion movement with scripts attached
whyPoints.description: Two pieces of work from two different weeks in a higher descriptor band, with the change visible in the text. Improved confidence is not evidence. At a school with no exam percentage, a tutor who cannot produce the scripts cannot demonstrate anything at all.

whyPoints.title: Both crossings handled, in both directions
whyPoints.description: Into IGCSE the missing skill is timed paper technique; out of IGCSE into the Diploma it is writing against published criteria. Al Barsha families move between systems more often than most, and a six to ten session block before term beats catching up from week one.

whyPoints.title: No claim this site cannot support
whyPoints.description: No regulator or board accreditation, no arrangement with any school named here, no UAE premises, no star rating, no statistic without its source and date, and no IB examination date at all, because none could be verified from the organisation's own site.

faqs.question: How do I read a Dubai International Academy Al Barsha Middle Years report?
faqs.answer: Ignore the converted grade first and look at the spread between the four criterion marks out of eight. A student with a seven, a six, a three and a six has a specific, locatable problem that a grade of four conceals entirely. In mathematics the criteria are knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Ask the school for the breakdown and the descriptor band behind each mark; both are free and both turn a report into a plan.

faqs.question: On a DIA Al Barsha report, criterion A is strong and criterion C is weak. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: In mathematics it means they can do the mathematics and cannot set it out: working not shown, notation inconsistent, reasoning implied rather than stated. That is a habit rather than a knowledge gap, it is highly fixable, and more content teaching will not touch it. In language and literature a low criterion A means techniques are identified but their effect is not analysed. The remedies for those two are completely different, which is why the letter matters more than the grade.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to Al Barsha?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service that exists only in India. Lessons are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Dubai has a large in-home market publishing roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and in heavy afternoon traffic the practical difference is that an online slot is a start time rather than an arrival window.

faqs.question: Why does the Personal Project matter beyond its own grade?
faqs.answer: Because it is marked out of 24 across planning, applying skills and reflecting, and it is the clearest early signal of how a student will handle a 4,000-word Extended Essay two years later. The usual failure is choosing a goal that is interesting rather than one that can be evidenced, then spending the time on the product while the process journal stays thin. The criteria reward the journal and the reflection, which students find counterintuitive until somebody shows them.

faqs.question: What does a continuum student struggle with most in the first Diploma term?
faqs.answer: Timed papers. A student who has come through the Middle Years Programme is fluent in criterion-based marking, comfortable with extended independent work and used to being assessed on process, but may never have sat a two-hour paper with a clock running and no chance to redraft. That is a technique gap rather than a knowledge gap, so it responds quickly: timed sections from week one, marked against the official scheme, with losses attributed to causes rather than topics.

faqs.question: How does criterion B in MYP sciences relate to the Diploma investigation?
faqs.answer: Directly. Criterion B is inquiring and designing, and it becomes research design in the Diploma scientific investigation, worth six of that piece's 24 marks. It is also the only one of the four Diploma investigation criteria that cannot be repaired after the data has been collected. A student who took criterion B seriously in Year 9 has a real advantage in Year 12; one who treated it as a formality has a predictable and expensive problem.

faqs.question: What should I ask for after a month of criterion-focused sessions?
faqs.answer: Which criterion was being worked on, what descriptor band it was in four weeks ago, what band it is in now, and both pieces of marked work so you can see the change in the text. For communicating in mathematics that means working shown where it previously was not. A tutor working properly answers in two minutes with documents. Improved confidence and better engagement are pleasant and are not evidence that a band has moved.

faqs.question: My child is moving from DIA Al Barsha to a British-curriculum school. What changes?
faqs.answer: The assessment language changes completely. IGCSE is terminal written papers with tiering, marked against a mark scheme rather than descriptor bands, and the urgent missing skill is timed examination practice. Establish the syllabus code immediately, because Cambridge sciences carry a practical component worth twenty per cent while Pearson Edexcel sciences have no separate practical exam. A six to ten session block before the new term starts is more effective than catching up alongside it.

faqs.question: Is one tutor enough for a Middle Years child and an IGCSE sibling?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and the reason is that a criterion specialist and a specification specialist are different professionals. One person asked to do both tends to produce one strong arrangement and one adequate one, at the same cost as two strong ones. The scheduling convenience is real and small. Al Barsha households with children in different systems are common, and two specialists on two evenings is generally the better configuration.

faqs.question: Where should an Al Barsha family get IB session and results dates from?
faqs.answer: Because none could be verified from the International Baccalaureate's own site for this project, and an unverified date that a parent plans around is worse than no date at all. Diploma students in the UAE sit the May session, and Middle Years on-screen examinations sit in May where a school enters them. Every specific date should come from the school's own calendar and its coordinator rather than from any tutoring site, including this one.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with a Diploma internal assessment at a continuum school?
faqs.answer: Teach the content, explain each criterion in the board's published wording, show how a comparable piece is constructed, read a draft the student has written and name which criterion it misses, and teach them to fix it themselves. A tutor may not write the internal assessment, draft the Extended Essay, or edit a piece to completion so the words become theirs. The caps are 3,000 words for the sciences investigation, 4,000 for the Extended Essay, 1,600 for the Theory of Knowledge essay and 950 for the exhibition commentary.

faqs.question: What does KHDA actually do, and should I read an inspection report?
faqs.answer: The Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, which is where inspection reports and curriculum approvals live. Reading the real report is worth an hour: bands are applied aspect by aspect rather than only overall, so the band for teaching in your child's phase matters more than a headline word. Check the date too, because an inspection is a snapshot and leadership changes between visits.

faqs.question: How do mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons fit around an IB timetable?
faqs.answer: They run alongside it rather than instead of anything, which is why the Dubai school week is fuller than the programme's own timetable implies. Classes must be organised separately for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. Tutoring in those subjects must work from the school's own material, because additional content without ministry permission is prohibited.

faqs.question: What is the fastest criterion to improve at Middle Years level?
faqs.answer: Communicating, in almost every subject group where it appears. It is a presentation and reasoning habit rather than a knowledge gap: showing working, keeping notation consistent, stating the reasoning instead of implying it, and labelling what is being done. Two or three sessions produce visible change in the script, which is why it is the sensible first target when the criterion spread shows it low. Criteria about content take longer because content takes longer.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-dubai-internati.closingHeading: Get the criterion breakdown, then book one trial lesson
dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-dubai-internati.closingBody: For a family at a continuum school the first move is a document, not a shortlist. Ask the school for the four criterion marks behind the grade that worries you and the descriptor band each one sat in. For a Diploma student, ask the coordinator for the internal deadline calendar. Then book a free trial lesson and ask the tutor what criterion C rewards, or why research design cannot be repaired after data collection, and listen for a sentence rather than a paragraph. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; nobody is sent to an Al Barsha address.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-dubai-internati.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are chosen on the same basis as the rest of this page: specialists who work from your child's marked papers and drafts rather than from a syllabus checklist, across the Diploma subject groups and both IGCSE boards.

intro.heading: Progress you can read, not progress you are told about
paragraphs: Ask most tutoring providers how a parent will know whether the money is working, and the answer arrives as adjectives: confidence, engagement, momentum. Those are real things and none of them is evidence. A parent paying for weekly hours is entitled to something they can read — a document, a mark, a draft with comments on it — and to a point in the calendar at which somebody says plainly whether the plan is working.

There are four artefacts that count, and they are the same whether your child is in the Middle Years Programme, sitting IGCSEs or in the Diploma. The first is a marked past paper with every lost mark attributed to a cause: content not known, method not shown, command term misread, units or notation, time ran out. The second is successive drafts of a piece of coursework with criterion-referenced feedback on each, written by the tutor and acted on by the student. The third is the school's own marks over time, from assessments and reports, which is the only independent measurement in the system. The fourth is a session record: what was covered each week and what was set.

Assembled, those four tell you something a conversation cannot. A student whose paper scores are rising but whose school marks are flat is probably improving on question types the school is not yet assessing. A student whose lost marks were 70% method-not-shown in September and 20% in November has had a specific, visible intervention. A student on their third Internal Assessment draft with the same criterion still weak has a tutor who is giving comfortable feedback rather than useful feedback, and you can see that from the drafts without knowing the subject.

The reason this matters more in a Dubai IB school than in many systems is that the Middle Years Programme produces no external benchmark at all until the optional eAssessment. Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, converted to a 1-7 grade through subject-specific boundaries. A student can go several years with reassuring reports and no externally comparable mark. Diploma internal assessments are marked by teachers and externally moderated, which is better but still arrives too late to steer. So the evidence has to be constructed deliberately, by somebody, and if a tutor is not doing it then nobody is.

What follows is the evidence system rather than a sales argument. There is a table of the artefacts and what each one proves, a breakdown of lost marks by cause with how fast each responds, the six-week review cycle set out step by step, a comparison of what progress looks like in criterion-marked and paper-marked systems, the legitimate feedback boundary at each coursework draft stage, the assessment calendar read as a sequence of evidence points, how to read your school's KHDA report as data, and a plain list of things that are presented as evidence in this market and are not. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, and all UAE tuition runs over live video.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-dubai-internati.programmesIntro: Each programme produces a different kind of evidence, and a parent reading the wrong kind draws the wrong conclusion. These are the three a Dubai IB family will meet.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary and inquiry-led, reported against learner-profile attributes rather than percentages. The evidence problem here is the sharpest in the whole continuum: a report can be warm and uninformative at the same time, and a parent genuinely cannot tell whether a child is behind.
programmes.countryNote: The three measurable things worth checking at this stage are number fluency, reading stamina and written structure, assessed against age expectations rather than against the class. Those three predict Middle Years performance. A short diagnostic that produces numbers on each is more useful to a Dubai primary parent than a term of weekly sessions bought on worry.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, converted to a 1-7 grade through subject-specific boundaries. The criteria are named and the marks are awarded against them, which means a criterion score is the most precise piece of evidence available in the programme and the one least often explained to parents.
programmes.countryNote: The practical evidence task in the MYP is to find out which criterion is dragging the grade. A student scoring 7 of 8 on knowledge and understanding and 3 of 8 on the analytical criterion has a specific, teachable problem that looks like a general weakness on a report. Ask the teacher for the criterion breakdown rather than the summary grade.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Terminal written papers with published mark schemes, which makes IGCSE the most evidence-rich stage in a student's school career. Cambridge tiers most subjects into Core, capped at grade C, and Extended, reaching A*. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is untiered in most subjects and awards 9 to 1.
programmes.countryNote: Because the schemes are published, every lost mark on an IGCSE past paper can be attributed to a cause, which is why the first thing we ask a Dubai family for is marked papers rather than a description of the problem. The Core or Extended decision should also be made on timed evidence rather than on classwork impressions.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Grades run 1-7 with up to three bonus points from the TOK and EE matrix. Higher Level carries 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and the HL extension usually sits on its own paper.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma produces two evidence streams that must be read separately: paper performance, which is diagnosable from past papers, and coursework quality, which is readable from successive drafts against the criteria. Conflating them is how a family concludes that a student is improving when only one stream has moved.

dubai/ib-igcse-tutor-for-dubai-internati.subjectsIntro: Subjects Dubai IB families most often bring to us, with the specific, observable place marks go. Every description below is something a parent can verify on a marked paper rather than take on trust.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Look at Paper 3 first: a two-problem investigation worth 20% of the HL grade, where lost marks cluster in the later parts because students have rarely worked sustained unfamiliar mathematics without a scaffold. On Papers 1 and 2 the visible pattern is correct answers with unwritten working.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The readable signature is a correct regression or calculation followed by no sentence interpreting it, which collects the calculation marks and none of the interpretation marks. Count those on a marked paper and the fix is obvious. HL adds graph theory, Voronoi diagrams and matrices.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: On Paper 2 extended response, look for numerically right answers that scored under half marks: that is a missing reasoning chain, not a missing fact. Paper 1 losses cluster at the end, which is timing. The two causes need different responses and look identical on a report.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and equilibrium carry the weight in Paper 2, and organic mechanism notation is the most frequent hidden gap: students who can describe a reaction lose marks on the arrows. On the IA, read the uncertainty treatment before anything else, because that is where mid-band work is distinguishable from top-band.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Sort the lost marks by command term and the pattern appears immediately: pages of correct content answering the wrong verb. Outline, explain, describe, suggest and evaluate each want a different answer shape, and a student who writes everything they know scores for one of them.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The IA is three 800-word commentaries on articles the student finds, and the readable failure is an article with no usable diagram, visible from the first draft. On papers, evaluation questions lose marks when a judgement is asserted at the end rather than built from the analysis above it.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen analysis against a guiding question, and the diagnosable fault is answering the text rather than the question. On the Individual Oral, weak performances are weak on the global issue rather than on the extracts, which is visible in a plan before the recording.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Read a marked case-study answer for named references to the stimulus business. Where there are none, the candidate has written a generic answer, which is a habit rather than a knowledge gap and among the fastest things to change in the Diploma.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: Published mark schemes make the evidence unusually clean. Count the method marks available on questions where your child wrote only an answer: that total is usually the single largest recoverable block on the paper, and it responds within a few sessions.

subjects.name: Sciences (IGCSE)
subjects.description: Compare theory-paper scores against the practical or alternative-to-practical paper. A gap between them is apparatus and method imprecision rather than subject weakness, and Cambridge Paper 6 in particular rewards precision that theory revision never supplies.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Support here means working with the school's own prescribed material rather than introducing other content.

sections.heading: The four artefacts, and what each one actually proves
paragraphs: Evidence in tutoring is not scarce. It is unassembled. Every piece listed below already exists or can be produced in a single session, and a family that collects all four has a clearer picture of their child's position than most schools assemble for a parent meeting.

A marked past paper with losses attributed by cause is the most powerful of the four, because it converts a vague worry into a sorted list. It proves what is going wrong and, by implication, how fast it can be fixed. Successive coursework drafts with criterion-referenced comments prove whether feedback is being acted on, and they do so in a way a non-specialist parent can read: if the same criterion is weak on draft three, something is not working. The school's own marks over time are the only independent measurement available, and they are the check against a tutor's self-report. A weekly session record proves what was actually taught, which sounds trivial until a review meeting where nobody can remember.

What each artefact does not prove matters just as much. A rising past-paper score does not prove school marks will rise, because the school may not yet be assessing those question types. A good draft does not prove the final submission will score well, because moderation happens elsewhere. A single school assessment proves very little, because one test has a wide margin. And a session record proves delivery, not learning.

The discipline is to look at all four together on a fixed schedule rather than reacting to whichever one arrives most recently. That is what the six-week review exists for, and it is the part of this arrangement we would most like to be held to.

sections.heading: Sorting lost marks by cause, and how fast each responds
paragraphs: Most underperformance in both IGCSE and the Diploma is not a content gap. It is a mark-scheme gap, and mark schemes are specific enough that the diagnosis can be done precisely rather than impressionistically. That precision is the difference between six useful sessions and six comfortable ones.

The method is mechanical. Take four or five marked past papers at the right level and board. Go through every lost mark and assign it to one of five causes: content not known, method not shown, command term misread, units or notation, or time ran out. Add them up. The distribution is almost always lopsided, and the shape of it determines what the next block of sessions should contain. A student losing 40% of their marks to unwritten working needs a habit changed, not a topic retaught.

The reason this is worth doing before buying hours is that the five causes respond at wildly different speeds. Units and significant figures respond in one session. Showing working and reading command terms respond in a few. Timing responds over a term with disciplined timed practice. Genuine content gaps respond over months. A plan that treats all five the same wastes the fast wins and under-resources the slow ones.

It also gives a parent a baseline that later evidence can be compared against. If the September distribution was dominated by method-not-shown and the November distribution is not, something specific has happened and it is visible on paper. That is a different kind of conversation from being told a child is more confident.

sections.heading: The six-week review cycle, step by step
paragraphs: A weekly arrangement without a review date drifts, and drift is where tutoring budgets go to die. So the cycle is fixed in advance: every six weeks, a written review that compares the plan against the evidence and ends in one of three decisions — continue, change the plan, or change the tutor.

What goes into it is specific. The baseline distribution of lost marks from the diagnostic block. The current distribution from a fresh timed paper. The school's assessment marks since the last review. Coursework drafts and the criterion comments on them. The session notes, which say what was actually covered against what was planned. Those five items produce a one-page answer to a one-line question: has the thing we targeted moved?

The uncomfortable part is what happens when the answer is no. Six weeks of a plan that has not moved the targeted measure means either the diagnosis was wrong, the plan was wrong, the student is not doing the work between sessions, or the match is wrong. All four are fixable and none of them is fixed by continuing. We would rather say so at week six than discover it at week twenty, and a rematch at week six costs six weeks rather than a term.

For a Dubai family the review also has a calendar function. It forces a check against the school's assessment and coursework dates, which is where the real deadlines live: the IB coordinator's internal Internal Assessment deadlines bind before any exam does, and a review that ignores them can report progress on paper technique while a coursework deadline passes unmet.

sections.heading: Progress looks different in a criterion-marked system
paragraphs: A parent whose child moves from the Middle Years Programme into the Diploma, or from an MYP school into an IGCSE cohort, has to change what they read. The same amount of real progress produces completely different-looking evidence in each system, and misreading it is the commonest source of unnecessary worry and unnecessary spending in Dubai IB households.

In the Middle Years Programme the unit of evidence is the criterion score: four criteria per subject, each out of eight, converted to a 1-7 grade through subject-specific boundaries. A grade can sit still for a year while one criterion climbs from 3 to 6, because the boundary has not been crossed. That is real progress invisible on a report, and the only way to see it is to ask for the criterion breakdown. The reverse is also true: a grade can move for boundary reasons without anything much changing.

In IGCSE the unit is the mark, against a published scheme, so the evidence is granular and comparable. This is the easiest system in which to demonstrate progress and the one where a tutor has least excuse for vagueness. In the Diploma there are two units running in parallel — paper marks, which behave like IGCSE, and internal assessment criteria, which behave like the MYP but are externally moderated. They move independently, and a report that shows one must not be read as covering both.

The practical rule is to match the evidence to the system before judging it. Ask for criterion breakdowns in the MYP, mark-scheme-level analysis at IGCSE, and both separately in the Diploma. A tutor who offers the same progress report shape in all three has not thought about it.

sections.heading: Draft by draft: what feedback is legitimate at each stage
paragraphs: Coursework drafts are the clearest evidence a parent gets of whether coaching is working, and they are also where this market most often crosses a line. Both facts are worth setting out together, because the same document is the proof and the temptation.

At the research-question stage a tutor may legitimately explain what the assessment criteria reward, say whether a question can be answered inside the word limit, and point out that a proposed investigation has no measurable variable or a proposed essay has no arguable position. That conversation saves weeks and it is entirely the student's decision at the end of it. At the first-draft stage a tutor may read what the student wrote and say where it falls short of specific criterion descriptors, name the missing element, and explain what a stronger version would contain. At the later-draft stage the same applies, with the addition that a tutor should be saying plainly if a weak criterion has not moved.

What a tutor may not do at any stage is write, draft, complete, ghost-produce or edit to submission standard any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, TOK essay, Personal Project or coursework. IB Gram does not and declines the request when it arrives. Nor should a tutor supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads, because those belong to the IB, Cambridge or Pearson; we cite and link to the official source instead. One page examined for this project sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price, and the student rather than the seller carries the consequence.

The parent's test is free and works at every stage: a legitimate session ends with your child holding a list of changes to make. If a cleaner document arrives instead, the evidence trail has been replaced by a purchase, and the thing at risk is the Diploma.

sections.heading: The assessment calendar read as a sequence of evidence points
paragraphs: A calendar is usually published as a list of dates. Read instead as a sequence of evidence points, it becomes a plan: each date is a moment when something measurable becomes available, and the gaps between them are where a tutoring arrangement either produces its own evidence or produces none.

For Cambridge candidates in the UAE the external points are the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so any page quoting a March window to a Dubai family is quoting another country's calendar. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The zone belongs to the centre, so ask your school's exams officer.

For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, exams run in May/June and in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those past dates establish the shape, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables that get revised, so take exact dates from the live official timetable rather than from any page restating them.

For the IB, UAE schools sit the May session, and this page publishes no specific IB exam or results date: the IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Get the session dates from your school's IB coordinator. More importantly, get the internal deadlines, because those are the evidence points that bind first and the ones a tutoring plan is most often blind to.

sections.heading: Reading your school's inspection report as data
paragraphs: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, inspects private schools annually on a six-band scale running from Outstanding to Very Weak, and publishes the reports. For a family assembling evidence, that report is free data and almost nobody uses it as such.

The headline band is the least useful part. What matters is the breakdown: attainment and progress reported by subject and by phase. That names the year groups and subjects in which the school's own students are doing least well, which is a targeting signal no tutoring provider can match, because it is based on the whole cohort rather than on one marketing claim. If secondary mathematics shows weaker progress than the rest of the school, that is where outside help is most likely to add something. If attainment is strong everywhere, the honest reading may be that paid tutoring is not the first purchase.

Two cautions on how these reports are used in this market. A band is a school-level judgement across hundreds of students and tells you nothing specific about your child, so it is a targeting tool rather than a diagnosis. And no provider should present a school's rating as a reason to buy or imply any relationship with the school: several competitor pages examined for this project list twenty or more schools as though they were clients, and one lists a school that appears not to exist.

Used properly, the report and your child's marked work answer the targeting question between them, at no cost and in an evening. That is why we ask for marked papers before quoting anything, and why the first recommendation on this page is to read a document you already have access to.
